body.text:
1.
(prakṛti-)(īśa-)(ubhaya-)(ātma-)(ādi-)(vyāpāra-)(rahitam, 2nd s.)(calam, 2nd s.)
(karma-)(tat-)(phala-)(sambandha-)(vyavasthā)(ādi-)(samāśrayam, 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 1. [That which is] devoid of the activity of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), <s>Īśvara</s> (God), both, <s>Ātman</s> (Self), and so forth, [yet which is] unstable, and the basis for the establishment of <s>karma</s> (action), its fruit, their connection, and so forth,

body.text:
2.
(guṇa-)(dravya-)(kriyā-)(jāti-)(samavāya-)(ādi-)(upādhibhiḥ, 3rd pl.)(śūnyam, 2nd s.)(āropita-)(ākāra-)(śabda-)(pratyaya-)(gocaram, 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 2. [That which is] empty of the superimpositions of quality, substance, activity, universal, inherence, and so forth, [yet] within the range of words and cognitions whose forms are superimposed,

body.text:
3.
(spaṣṭa-)(lakṣaṇa-)(saṃyukta-)(pramā-)(dvitaya-)(niścitam, 2nd s.)(aṇīyasā, 3rd s.)(api*)(na*)(aṃśena, 3rd s.)(miśrībhūta-)(aparā-ātmakam, 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 3. [That which is] ascertained by the two valid cognitions endowed with clear characteristics, not mixed in its own nature with even the slightest part,

body.text:
4.
(a-saṃkrāntim, 2nd s.) (an-ādi-antam, 2nd s.)(pratibimba-)(ādi-)(sannibha, 2nd s. [adj.])
(sarva-)(prapañca)(sandoha-)(nirmuktam, 2nd s.)(a-gatam, 2nd s.)(paraiḥ, 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 4. [That which is] without transference, without beginning or end, resembling a reflection and the like, free from the entire mass of conceptual proliferation, not reached by others —

body.text:
5.
(svatantra-)(śruti-)(nissaṅgaḥ)(jagat-)(hita-)(vidhitsayā, 3rd s.)(an-alpa-)(kalpa-)(a-saṃkhyeya-)(sa-ātmībhūta-)(mahā-dayaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 5. He who, independent, unattached to scripture, out of desire for the welfare of the world, through innumerable eons of no small number, became one with great compassion,

body.text:
6.
(yaḥ)(pratītya-)(samutpādam, 2nd s.)(jagāda ”gad Perf. III p. s.)(gadatāṃvaraḥ, m. 1st s.)(tam, m. 2nd s.)(sarvajñam, m. 2nd s.)(praṇamya* ”nam)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(kriyate ”kṛ pass.)(tattva-)(saṃgrahaḥ)
body.translated_text: 6. He who taught <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), the best of speakers — having bowed to that omniscient one, this <s>Tattvasaṃgraha</s> (Compendium of Reality) is composed.

body.text:
7.
(pradhānāt, 5th s.)(kevalāt, 5th s.)(eva*)(pracitāt, 5th s.)(a-śeṣa-)(śakti-)(bhedāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(kārya-)(pravarttante, pra”vṛt Pr. III p. pl.), (bhāvataḥ* [-tas suff.])(rūpāḥ, 1st pl.)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 7. From <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter) alone, which is undifferentiated, [yet] endowed with the distinctions of all powers, effects proceed, being of its nature —

body.text:
8.
(yadi*)(kāryam, n. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū Opt.)(a-sat, n. 1st s.)(śaktitaḥ* [-tas suff.])(ātmani, n. 7th s.)(kāraṇa-)(na*)(eva*)(śakyeta ”śak pass. Opt. III p. s.)(kartum*)(nairūpyāt, 5th s.)(-vat*)(viyat-abja- [ap-ja > `born in the water' = lotus])
body.translated_text: 8. If the effect were non-existent [in the cause], it could not be produced from its power, since it would have no form — like a sky-lotus.

body.text:
9.
(ca*)(kasmāt, 5th s.)(gṛhṇanti ”grah Pr. III p. pl.)(eva*)(niyatāni, 2nd pl.)(upādānāni, n. 2nd pl.)(bhedataḥ* [-tas suff.])(śāli-bīja-)(ādi-)(tu*)(na*)(param, 2nd s.)(loc. abs.)(a-sattve, 7th s.)(tulye, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 9. And why then do [causes] take only determinate material causes in a differentiated manner? When the non-existence is equal, a rice-seed and so forth [should produce anything], but it does not.

body.text:
10.
(ca*)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(dharmakam, 1st s.)(utpatti-)(bhavet ”bhū Opt.)(sarvatas*)(bhāvāt, 5th s.)(a-viśeṣataḥ* [-tas suff.])(vigamasya, 6th s.)(tādātmya-)(sarvasmin, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 10. And everything would be productive of everything, arising from everything, since there is no distinction — because of the identity of non-existence in all.

body.text:
11.
(śaktīnām, 6th pl.)(eṣām, 6th pl.)(niyamāt, 5th s.)(na*)(evam*)(iti*)(an-uttaram, 1st s.)(yataḥ*)(śaktāḥ, 1st pl.)(hetavaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(kurvanti ”kṛ Pr. III p. pl.)(eva*)(kāryam, 2nd s.)(śakyam, 2nd s.)."
body.translated_text: 11. [If one says] 'Not so, because of the restriction of these powers' — that is no answer, because causes that are capable simply produce the effect that can [be produced].

body.text:
12.
(a-)(atiśayam, n. 1st s.)(kārya-)(nīrūpam [> nir-rūpam])(ca*)(a-vikāri, n. 1st s.)(katham* nu*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(kriyeta ”kṛ pass. Opt.)(taiḥ, 3rd pl.)(vikṛtau, 7th s.)(āpteḥ, 6th s.)(hāni-)(ātma-)
body.translated_text: 12. The effect being without surplus, formless, and unchanging — how could it be produced by those? For upon transformation, there would be loss of the nature [of the cause].

body.text:
13.
(ca*)(evam*)(kāryasya, 6th s.)(a-yogāt, 5th s.)(kim*)(kurvat, 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū Opt.)(kāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(tataḥ*)(kāraṇa-)(bhāvaḥ)(api*)(ādeḥ, 6th s.)(bīja-)
body.translated_text: 13. And thus, since there is no connection with the effect, what would the cause be doing? Then even the causal nature of the seed and so forth [is lost].

body.text:
14.
(vyaktam vyaktam, 1st s.)(samīkṣyate ”īkṣ pass.)(anvitam, 2nd s.)(sukha-)(ādi-)(upalabdhitaḥ* [-tas suff.])(iha*)(kāryasya, 6th s.)(prasāda-)(tāpa-)(dainya-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 14. The manifest is clearly observed to be accompanied [by pleasure and so forth], from the apprehension of pleasure and so forth herein — the effect's clarity, heat, dejection, and so forth.

body.text:
15.
(tataḥ*)(kāpilāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(iti*)(darśanāt, 5th s.)(anvaya-)(tat-)(jāti-),
(-sambhūtam)(-maya-)(tat- [= pleasure, etc.])(ca*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(-vat*)(bheda-)(kuta-)(-ādi)(pradhānam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 15. Therefore the <s>Kāpilas</s> (followers of Kapila) [say]: from observation, [being] born of that class through connection, and being made of that, and like that — [this is] <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter), with its distinctions and origins.

body.text:
16.
(tad atra*)(sudhiyaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(prāhuḥ pra-āhuḥ ”ah)(codanā, f. 1st s.)(api*)(tulyā, 1st s.)(sattve, 7th s.)(uttaram, 1st s.)(tasyām, f. 7th s.)(yat, 1st s.)(vaḥ, 6th pl.)(tat)(tulyam)(sudhiyām, m. 6th pl.)(api*)
body.translated_text: 16. To this the wise say: the objection is equally [applicable]; whatever is your answer to that, that same [answer] is equally [available] to the wise.

body.text:
17.
(yadi*)(dadhi-)(ādayaḥ)(santi ”as Pr. III p. pl.)(sarvathā*)(ātmasu, n. 7th pl.)(dugdha)(ādi-)(satām)(-ātmanām)(sadṛśa-)(hetu-)(-ādi-)(kim)(teṣām)(utpādyam)
body.translated_text: 17. If curds and so forth exist in all respects within milk and so forth — [since they already] exist, having similar causes and so forth, what of them remains to be produced?

body.text:
18.
(tat kāryam)(na*)(janyam)(hetu)(sattātaḥ* [-tas suff.])(-vat*)(hetu)(vitti)
(ataḥ)(abhimataḥ)(a-)(sādhya)(-vat*)(parātma-)
body.translated_text: 18. That effect is not producible, because of its [already] existing in the cause — just as the cause [already] exists. Therefore, the desired [conclusion] is unestablished — like the other's self.

body.text:
19.
(atha)(kaścit)(asti)(vilakṣaṇa)(-ādi-)(hetavaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(yānti ”yā P. III p. pl.)(-tām)(vācya-)
body.translated_text: 19. Now, if there exists some [effect] that is of a different character and so forth — the causes go to that [state]; [this remains] to be stated —

body.text:
20.
(yadi*)(asau, m. 1st s.)(āsīt ”as Imperf. III p. s.)(prāk*)(uttaram, 1st s.)(dattam, 1st s.)(na* kiṃcit*)(cet*)(saḥ)(no*)(cet*)(a-sat, 1st s.)(katham*)(samaśnute ”aś V C. Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(prādurbhāvam, 2nd s.)(tebhyaḥ, 5th pl.)
body.translated_text: 20. If it existed before, the answer has been given; if not, and if it is non-existent, how does it attain manifestation from them?

body.text: 21. (ataḥ*)(iti*)(samasti ”as)(na*)(sādhyaṃ, n. 1st s.)(parigrahaḥ)(upādāna-)(no*)(janma)(api*)(niyatāt, 5th s.)(na*)(ca*)(śaktir, f. 1st s.)(na*)(ca*)(kriyā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 21. Therefore, the argument 'it exists' is not established; there is no apprehension of a material cause, nor is there birth; and from what is determined, there is neither power nor action.

body.text:
22.
(niṣpatteḥ, 5th s.)(sarva-)(ātmanā, n. 3rd s.)(iha*)(kāryam, 1st s.)(tasmāt, 5th s.)(api*)(vyapadeśaḥ)(kāraṇa-)(na*)(upapadyate ”pad Āt. Pr. 3rd s.)(eva*)
body.translated_text: 22. Since the effect is produced entirely here, therefore even the designation 'cause' is not appropriate.

body.text:
23.
(sarvam, 1st s.)(sādhanam, n. 1st. s.)(vṛttam, n. 1st s.)(nivartakam, 1st s.)(viparyāsa-)(ca*)(utpādakam, 1st s.)(niścaya-)(idam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(-saṅgatam)(yukti-)(tathā*)
body.translated_text: 23. All [this] — the means of accomplishment being completed, the reversal of error, and the production of certainty — this is not coherent. Likewise,

body.text:
24.
(sandeha-)(-viparyāsau, m. 1st d.)(na*)(nivarttyau, m. 1st d.)(sthiteḥ, 5th s.)(sarvadā*)(na* api*)(asti ”as)(janma)(niścaya-)(eva*)(tataḥ*)(akhilam, 1st s.)(vṛthā*)
body.translated_text: 24. Doubt and error are not removable since [they are already] always present; nor is there birth; certainty alone — therefore all [effort] is in vain.

body.text:
25.
(atha*)(api*)(niścayaḥ)(a-bhūtaḥ)(samutpadyeta ”pad pass. Opt. 3rd s.)(sādhanāt, 5th s.)(nanu*)(eva*)(tena, 3rd s.)(sarve, m. 1st pl.)(amī, m. 1st pl.)(bhaveyuḥ ”bhū Opt. 3rd pl.)(vyabhicāriṇaḥ m. 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 25. Moreover, if certainty, [previously] non-existent, were to arise from a means of proof, then surely by that [reasoning] all of these would be deviant.

body.text: 26. (iti*)(cet*)(avyaktaḥ)(bhāktebhyaḥ, 5th pl.)(kā, f. 1st s.)(vyaktir, f. 1st s.)(asya, 6th s.)(na*)(utpattiḥ, f. 1st s.)(atiśaya-)(a-vibhāgāt, 5th s.)(a-saṅgateḥ, 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 26. If so, [then <s>Pradhāna</s> being] unmanifest — what manifestation is there of it from the secondary [sources]? There is no origination, because of the absence of distinction and because of incoherence.

body.text:
27.
(na*)(tat-)(viṣaya-)(na*)(-kṣayaḥ)(āvṛti-)(upalambha-)(-tvāt, 5th s.)(nitya-)(api*)(a-sambhavāt, 5th s.)(dvitīyasya, 6th s.)(upalambhasya, 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 27. There is no cessation of that domain, because of its being perceived; also because of the impossibility of the eternal, [and] because of the impossibility of a second perception.

body.text:
28.
(tadvat*)(api*)(a-)(vibhede, m. 7th s.)(trai-guṇyasya, n. 6th s.)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(kārakam, n. 1st s.)(sarva-)(tadvat*)(a-satve, 7th s.)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(kārakam, n. 1st s.)(sarva-)
body.translated_text: 28. Likewise, even when there is no differentiation of the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), nothing is a cause of everything — just as when [something is] non-existent, nothing is a cause of everything.

body.text:
29.
(niṣpatteḥ, f. 5th s.)(avadhīnām, 6th pl.)(na*)(te, 6th s.)(śaktayaḥ, f. 1st pl.)(na*)(niyatāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(sattve, 7th s.)(niyamaḥ)(tāsām, f. 6th pl.)(nanu*)(yuktaḥ)(sa-avadhikaḥ)
body.translated_text: 29. The powers [of <s>Pradhāna</s>] are not determined, since there are no limits to production; the restriction of those [powers] is indeed proper [only] when [they are] limited.

body.text:
30.
(na* evam*)(utpattyā, 3rd s.)(teṣām, 6th pl.)(mā-abhūt ”bhū Aor. III s.)(tathā* aparam)(śabdaḥ)(na*)(kṣatiḥ, 1st s.)(-rūpasya, 6th s.)(vastu-)(viviktasya, 6th s.)(sarva-)(upādhi-)
body.translated_text: 30. Not so — through their production [the restriction] would not have been thus, and furthermore: sound does not damage the nature of a thing that is devoid of all superimpositions.

body.text:
31.
(nāma*)(vastūnām, n. 6th s.)(na*)(rūpam, n. 1st s.)(yat, 1st s.)(vikalpāḥ)(ca*)(vācakāḥ)(viśva-kalpāḥ)(pravarttante, pra”vṛt Pr. III p. pl.)(yathā*)(abhyāsam, 2nd s.)(a-bhedini, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 31. Indeed, the name is not the form of things; and concepts and expressions — manifold constructions — operate according to habit, even in what is undifferentiated.

body.text:
32.
(utpādaḥ)(tu*)(-bhāvaḥ)(vastu-, n.)(saḥ)(na*)(satā, f.)(tathā*)(a-satā, f.)(tu)(sambadhyate, sam-”badh, pass. P. III s.)(kevalam*)(a-satā)(dhiyā, f. 3rd s.)(kalpikayā, f. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 32. But the arising of a thing — that [thing] is not connected with [something] existent in that way, nor with [something] non-existent; it is connected only with a non-existent, constructive cognition.

body.text:
33.
(rūpa, n. 1st s.)(vastunaḥ, 6th s.)(īkṣyate ”īkṣ, Pass. P. III s.)(anantaram*)(eka-)(na*)(āsīt ”as, Imperf. III p. s.)(prāk*)(na*)(tad-bīja)(tu*)(asti ”as)(na*)
body.translated_text: 33. The form of a thing is seen immediately after [its cause]; it was not one [with the cause] before; nor does its seed exist [in the cause].

body.text:
34.
(yan-matam, n. 1st s.)(dadhi-, n.)(-ādi, n. 1st s.)(kṣīra-)(-ādiṣu, m. 7th s.)(-rūpeṇa, n. 3rd s.)(śakti-)(kā, f. 1st s.)(śaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(dadhi-, n.)(-ādi, n. 1st s.)(dṛśyeta ”dṛś Opt. III s.)(-vat)(dugdha-)
body.translated_text: 34. As for the view that curds and so forth [exist] in milk and so forth in the form of a power — what power? If curds and so forth were seen [in milk], as [they are seen in] milk —

body.text:
35.
(cet*)(anyat, n. 1st s.)(katham*)(sad-bhāvaḥ)(satvasya, 6th s.)(ucyate ”vac pass. Pr. III s.)(a-bhaktyā, f. 3rd s.)(sad-bhāvaḥ)(satvasya, 6th s.)(sad-bhāvaḥ)(duḥkha-)(mohayoḥ, 6th d.)
body.translated_text: 35. If [the power is] something different, how can the existence of what exists be asserted? Without devotion, the existence of what exists [is asserted to be] the existence of suffering and delusion.

body.text:
36.
(vyaktam, n. 1st s.)(siddham, n. 1st s.)(naḥ, 6th pl.)(kathaṃcana*)(anugatam, n. 1st s.)(satvādi-)(sukha-)(ādīnām, m. 6th pl.)(āntaratvāt n. 5th s.)(sva-saṃvidaḥ, f. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 36. [You say] the manifest is somehow established for us, accompanied by <s>sattva</s> (existence) and so forth — [this is] because of the internality of pleasure and so forth, from one's own experience.

body.text:
37.
(bhedataḥ*, [-tas suff.])(bhāvanā-)(jāti-)(saṅga-)(-ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(lakṣyante ”lakṣ pass. Pr. III p. pl.)(niyatāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(eva*)(ekatra*)(śabda-)(ādau, m. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 37. From the distinctions of cultivation, birth, association, and so forth, [things] are observed to be determined only in one [thing] — in sound and so forth.

body.text:
38.
(anupātitve, n. 7th s.)(eka-vastu-)(saṃvit, f. 1st s.)(prasajyate ”sañj pass. Pr. III p. s.)(citrā)
(cet*)(na)(-vaśāt, 5th s.)(adṛṣṭa-)(-ādi-)(na*)(syāt)(anuyāyinī)(vastu-)
body.translated_text: 38. If one thing were to follow [another], variegated cognition of a single object would result. If not, through the force of unseen [karma] and so forth, [cognition] would not follow the object.

body.text:
39.
(rūpam, n. 1st s.)(vastunaḥ, n. 6th s.)(tri-ākāraṃ)(ca*)(vidaḥ, f. 1st pl.)(tat-)(eka-ākārāḥ)
(katham*)(tāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(bhāvinyaḥ, f. 1st pl.)(yujyante ”yuj pass. Pr. III pl.)(tatra)(vilakṣaṇāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 39. And the form of a thing is triple, and cognitions of it are of one form — how then could those [cognitions], being of a different character, be rightly [applied] there?

body.text:
40.
(yoginām, m. 6th pl.)(prasāda-)(udvega-)(varaṇāni)(jāyante ”jan Pr. III p. pl.)(ekasmin, 7th s.)(puṃsi, 7th s.)(pumān, m. 1st s.)(abhimataḥ)(na*)(ca*)(rūpaḥ)(tat-)(paraiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 40. For <s>yogins</s>, feelings of serenity, agitation, and obscuration arise toward a single person — yet a person is not considered to have that form by others.

body.text:
41.
(api*)(vyakte, n. 7th s.)(siddhe, n. 7th s.)(tri-guṇe, m. 7th s.)(pradhānam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(prasidhyati ”sidh IV C. Pr. III p. s.)(ekam, n. 2nd s.)(nityam, n. 2nd s.)(-kāraṇam, n. 2nd s.)(tat-)(tat, n. 1st s.)(na*)(-anvitam)(eka-)(jāti-)
body.translated_text: 41. Even when the manifest, [which is] established [as having] three <s>guṇas</s>, [is accepted], <s>Pradhāna</s> is not established — [for] a single, permanent cause is not accompanied by a single universal.

body.text:
42.
(sarvāḥ, f., 1st pl.)(vyaktayaḥ, f. 1st pl.)(dṛśyante ”dṛś/paśy pass.)(kalpāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(ayaḥ-śalākā-)(mūrttayaḥ, f. 1st pl.)(saṅgata-)(krama-)(ātmikāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(miśrita-)(kalpanā-)
body.translated_text: 42. All manifest [things] are seen to be fabricated, having the form of iron rods, possessed of the nature of sequential combination — mixed fabrication.

body.text:
43.
(tathā*)(vikāra-)(bhedāḥ)(mṛd-)(-ādayaḥ)(na*)(dṛśyante ”dṛś pass.)(-anvitam)(eka-)(jāti-)(eka-)(nimittāḥ)(vibhedataḥ* [-tas suff.])(-ādeḥ, 6th s.)(mṛt-)(piṇḍā-)
body.translated_text: 43. Likewise, the varieties of transformation — clay and so forth — are not seen to be accompanied by a single universal, [produced from] a single cause; from the differentiation of the source, lumps of clay —

body.text:
44.
(puruṣāṇām, m. 6th s.)(api*)(anvitatve, 7th s. [-tva suff.])(caintya-)(ādi-)(-tvam)(pūrva-)(eka-)(cet*)(amukhyaṃ, n. 1st s.)(kim*)(na*)(samam, n. 1st s.)(iha*)(api*)
body.translated_text: 44. Even when the connection of <s>Puruṣas</s> (souls) [with <s>Pradhāna</s> is accepted], [their] inconceivability and so forth — if not primary, is it not the same here as well?

body.text:
45.
(tataḥ*)(api*)(a-bhāve, m. 7th s.)(hetu-)(pradhāna-)(sarvam, 1st s.)(vaicitryam, n. 1st s.)(kārya-)(karaṇa-)(-ādikam)(bhedena, 3rd s.)(śakteḥ, 6th s.)
body.translated_text: [Verse 45] Even in the absence of that [Īśvara], all the diversity of effects, instruments, and so forth is [explained] through the differentiation of <s>śakti</s> (power).

body.text:
46.
(anye, 1st pl.)(pracakṣate ”cakṣ Pr. III p. pl. Āt.)(īśam, m. 2nd s.)(hetum, m. 2nd s.)(sarva-)(-matām, n. 6th pl.)(utpatti-)(kila*)(a-cetanam, n. 1st s.)(svayam)(prārabhate, pra-ā”rabh)(sva-kāraṇam)
body.translated_text: [Verse 46] Others declare <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) as the cause; according to all doctrines, the non-conscious [matter] itself initiates its own cause.

body.text:
47-48.

body.translated_text: 178. All these — desire and the rest — are dependent on something; when there is some real entity, because of being an effect, like form, that is our <s>puruṣa</s> (person/self).

body.translated_text: 179. From apprehension, its being a real entity is not deviant; because even at the time of destruction, since destruction has a cause, there is indeed reality.

III p. s.)(a-nibandhanam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 180-181. All cognitions — those having single or multiple causes such as form and so forth — their reconnection by means of a cognition, thus by me, as it were: cognitions of many, in the movement of the eyebrow-creeper of a dancer — otherwise, reconnection would arise without a basis.

body.text:
182.
(vacanam, n. 1st s.)(ātmā, n. 1st s.)(abhidhāyakam, n. 1st s.)(vyatirikta-)(saṃghāta-)(buddhi-)(indriya-)(ādi-)(yasmāt, n. 5th s.)(matam, n. 1st s.)(eka-)(padam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 182. The word '<s>ātman</s>' (self) is that which denotes [something] distinct from the aggregate, cognition, sense-faculties, and so forth; since it is held [to be] a single term.

body.text:
183.
(bhinnatve, n. 7th s.)(siddha-)(paryāya-)(yat, n. 1st s.)(pariniścitam, n. 1st s.)(evam*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(uktam, n. 1st s.)(dharmeṇa, m. 3rd s.)(yathā*)(nirdiṣṭa-)(-vat*)(śabda-)(paṭa-)
body.translated_text: 183. In the case of difference, what is established as a synonym and ascertained — thus that is stated; by the principle, as has been indicated — [like] word and cloth.

body.text:

(ca*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(jīvat, m. 1st s.)(dehaḥ)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(viyuktaḥ)(prāṇa-)(ādibhiḥ, m. 3r pl.)(nairātmyāt, n. 5th s.)(-vat*)(ghaṭa-)(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(asya, m. 6th s.)(na*)(eva*)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(nirātmatā, f.)
body.translated_text: 184. And this living body would exist, separated from <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) and the rest, due to selflessness — like a pot. Therefore, there is indeed no selflessness of it.

body.text:
185.
(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(uttara-)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(vedyate ”vid caus. pass.)(eva*)(vedakena, m. 3rd s.)(jāta-)(ādya-vijñāna- [b.v. cpd.])(sadyas*)(-tvāt, n. 5th s.)(maj>mat-)(jñāna-)(-vat*)(ādya-)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 185. All subsequent cognition is indeed experienced by an experiencer; because of the simultaneity of the consciousness in which the first cognition arises — like my cognition; the first, that —

body.text:
186.
(api*)(nivartti, n. 1st s.)(deśa-)(dūra-)(yuktam, n. 1st s.)(madīyena, n. 3rd s.)(ātmanā, n. 3rd s.)(-mattvāt, 5th s.)(mūrtti-)(ādi-)(kṣiti-)(-vat*)(asmadīya-)(śarīra-)
body.translated_text: 186. Even what is remote in place, is connected with my own self — because of being mine; like earth with form and so forth — [this is] our body.

body.text:

body.translated_text: 187. And thus, in the determination of the existence, permanence, and all-pervasiveness of the <s>ātman</s> (self), it is established that all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) are not without a self.

body.text:

(prathame, m. 7th s.)(atra*)(-tā, f. 1st s.)(sādhya-)(siddha-)(yataḥ*)(pravedyatvam, n. 1st. s.)(tvat-jñānasya)(sarva-jña-)(ādi-)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass. Pr. III p. s.)
body.translated_text: 188. In the first [argument], here the state of being the thing to be proved is [already] established as what is to be proved; since the experienceability of your knowledge is desired by the omniscient and others.

body.text:
189.
(cit-)(prajāyate ”jan pass. Pr. III p. s.)(sva-cit-rūpam, 1st s.)(an-apekṣam)(prakāśaka-)(evam*)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(anya-)(api*)(nidarśanam, n. 1st s.)(śūnyam, n. 1st s.)(sādhya-)
body.translated_text: 189. Consciousness arises in the form of its own consciousness, independent, illuminating; thus cognition too — even another example is devoid of what is to be proved.

190.
(api*)(tasya, 6th s.)(udāharaṇatve, n. 7th s.)(yad, 1st s.)(pravedyate ”vid caus. pass.)(uparaktena, 3rd s.)(ākāra-)(tat-)(saṃśayaḥ)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(anyena, 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 190. Even if it were taken as an example of that, what is experienced by one affected by a [particular] form — there would be doubt about that; by another [it is experienced differently].

body.text:

(yadi*)(pra-sādhyate ”sādh caus. pass. Pr. III p. s.)(icchā)(ādeḥ, m. 6th s.)(samāśritatvam, n. 1st s.)(kvacit*)(cet*)(tatra*)(parikalpyate ”kḷp pass.)(āśrayaḥ)(mātram, n. 2nd s.)(kāraṇa-)
body.translated_text: 191. If the dependence of desire and the rest on something is to be proved, and if a substratum is imagined there — a mere cause,

body.text:

body.translated_text: 192. If then your desired conclusion is established: the container is the substratum [of desire and so forth] — that imagination, devoid of any ground or destination, is fruitless.

body.translated_text: 193. A basin and the like serve as a substratum for jujube fruits and the like; [but is this] because of obstruction of motion, or because of the production of a distinction?

body.text:

(na* eva*)(yukti-mat, n. 1st s.)(nāśasya)(nīrūpasya > nir-rūpasya)(kārya-tvam, n. 1st s.)(ataḥ*)(viśeṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(uktam, n. 1st s.)(paraiḥ, 3rd s.)(hetau, 7th s.)(vyartham)(iha*)
body.translated_text: 194. It is not at all reasonable that formless destruction has the nature of an effect; therefore, the qualification stated by others regarding the cause is pointless here.

(idam)(pratisandhānam, n.)(iti*)(mayā, 3rd s.)(upa-plavāt, 5th s.)(a-vidyā-)(-ādi-)(bhāsataḥ* [-tas suff.])(eka-tva-)(or perceiver)(kartṛ-)(sarveṣu, 7th pl.)(kṣaṇikeṣu, 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 195. 'This is the reconnection' — thus, by me: from the disruption of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and the rest, appearing as unity, or as a doer — in all momentary [things].

body.text:
196.
(ca*)(asmāt, 5th s.)(mithyā-)(vikalpataḥ* [-tas suff.])(na yuktā)(saṃsthithiḥ, f.)(tattva-)(api*)(bhinnaḥ)(bhedāt, 5th s.)(sāmarthya-)(bhavati)(nibandhanam, n.)(eka-)
body.translated_text: 196. And from this, from false conceptualization, the establishment of reality is not justified; moreover, what is different, from differentiation, becomes the basis of capability — as one.

body.text:
197.
(cittānām, 6th s.) (rūpa-)(śabda-)(ādi-)(kāryatve, 7th s.)(eka-)(anugāmika-)(paurvāparyam, n. 1st s.)(viruddhyate ”rudh, pass.)(sannidheḥ, 5th s.)(kāraṇa-)(śakta-)
body.translated_text: 197. When forms, sounds, and the rest are effects of minds, the sequential order following a single [mind] is contradicted; [this is] because of the proximity of a capable cause.

body.text:
198.
(samudbhavaḥ)(ṣaḍ-vijñāna-)(eka-)(anantara-)(vijñānāt)(vyaktam, 2nd s.)(vedyate ”vid caus. pass.)(yugapat*)(ataḥ*)(prasādhanam, n. 1st s.)(iṣṭa-)
body.translated_text: 198. The arising of the six consciousnesses from a single immediately preceding consciousness — [each] is clearly experienced; simultaneously. Therefore, the desired proof [is established].

body.text:
199.
(tu*)(kramiṇām, m. 6th pl.)(anantaram, 1st s.)(na*)(eka-hetutvam, 1st s.)(yuktam)(ataḥ*)(vyāpteḥ, 5th s.)(asmin, 7th s.)(samīkṣyate ”īkṣ pass.)(vyaktam, 2nd s.)(bādhā-)(anumāna-)
body.translated_text: 199. But for those that are sequential, the having of a single cause is not appropriate; therefore, in this, an inferential obstruction is clearly observed.

body.text:
200.

body.translated_text: 200. The movement of the eyebrow-creeper of a dancer is not one — because of being a collection of many atoms; the unity of that is imagined.

body.text:

body.translated_text: 201. Because of being useful for a single effect, even a single [entity] is within the range of the word; if thus desired — what is to be proved [is already in] the means of proof; [it is already] established.

body.text:
202.
(śabdānām, m. 6th pl.)(buddhi-)(citta-)(ādi-)(api*)(bhāve, 7th s.)(eka-pada-)(abhidhāyitā, f. 1st s.)(vyatirikta-)
body.translated_text: 202. Even when mind, cognition, and the rest exist, the denotation by a single term of words [such as '<s>ātman</s>'] that is distinct [from them] —

body.text:
203.
(ataḥ*)(hetuḥ, m. 1st s.)(anaikāntikaḥ)(nanu*)(viśeṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(tat-)(uktam)(ucyate ”vac pass. Pr. III p. s.)(na*)(eva*)(siddham)(-sthiteḥ, 5th s.)(paryāyatā-)
(cetaḥ-)
body.translated_text: 203. Therefore, the reason is inconclusive. Indeed, that qualification stated — is it not the case that it is not at all established? From the position of being a synonym — of mind.

body.text:
204.
(cittam)(āśrayatvena, n. 3rd s.)(ahaṅkāra-)(gīyate ”gai, pass.)(iti*)(ātmā, n. 1st s.)(tu*)(viṣayaḥ)(asya, n. 6th s.)(na*)(vedyate ”vid caus. pass.)(saṃvṛttyā, f. 3rd s.)(vṛttyā, f. 3rd s.)(vastu-)
body.translated_text: 204. The mind is sung of as '<s>ātman</s>' (self) by way of being a substratum of the sense of 'I' (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>). But its object is not experienced as a real entity — by convention, by function.

body.text:

body.translated_text: 205. By that, deviation is observed; moreover, what is one — the active agent — is placed first [as] a term. Like a lotus on the surface of the sky.

body.text:
206.
(vācaḥ, f. 1st pl.)(bhāvinyaḥ, 1st pl.)(mātra-)(saṅketa-)(kutra*)(na* saṅgatāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(padānām, m. 6th pl.)(ādi-)(ātma-)(ca*)(na*)(eva*)(prakṛtyā, f. 3rd s.)(prakāśanam)(artha-)
body.translated_text: 206. Expressions that are future, of mere convention — where are they not applicable? And the first [term] is not by nature an illumination of the meaning of words.

body.text:
207.
(yadi*)(sambandhaḥ)(prāṇa-)(ādīnām)(saha*)(ātmanā, n. 3rd s.)(bhavet,, Opt. III p. s.)(siddhaḥ)(prasaṅgaḥ)(ayam)(yujyate ”yuj pass.)(tadā*)(anyathā*)(a-saṅgataḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 207. If the connection of <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) and the rest with the <s>ātman</s> (self) were established, this consequence would be justified; otherwise, it is incoherent.

body.text:
208.
(śūnya-tve, 7th s.)(suta-)(vandhyā-)(na*)(prasajyate ”sañj pass.)(jīvad-)(dehaḥ)(virahe, 7th s.)(prāṇa-ādi-)(evam*)(hi*)(etat)(prasañjanam)(tava)(api*)
body.translated_text: 208. In the case of voidness [of the self], [the consequence is like] the son of a barren woman — it does not follow. A living body, in separation from <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest — for this consequence is [applicable] to you as well.

body.text:
209.
(iha*)(tāvat*)(tādātmyam, n. 1st s.)(aṅgīkaraṇāt, 5th s.)(bheda-)(tayoḥ, 6th s.)(na* api*)(kārya-kāraṇa-tā, f.)(prasaṅgataḥ* [-tas suff.])(yaugapadya-)
body.translated_text: 209. Here, first: identity — from [your own] acceptance, there is no differentiation of the two; nor is there a cause-effect relationship, from the consequence of simultaneity.

body.text:
210.
(tad*)(hi*)(nivṛttau, 7th s.)(ātmanaḥ, n. 6th s.)(tat-)(vivarjitāḥ)(sambandha-)(kim*)(amī, m. 1st pl.)(prāṇa-)(apāna-)(ādayaḥ, 1st pl.)(vinivartante, III p. pl.)(tanoḥ, 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 210. For if, upon the cessation of the <s>ātman</s> (self), those — <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, and the rest — deprived of that connection, do they cease from the body?

body.text:
211.
(evam*)(ca*)(satva-)(ātma-)(a-prasiddhitaḥ* [-tas suff.])(sarvaiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(sādhanaiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(nidarśanam, n. 1st s.)(uktam, n. 1st s.)(nitya-)(vyāpitvayoḥ, n. 6th d.)(sādhya-hīnam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 211. And thus, from the non-establishment of the existence of the <s>ātman</s> (self), [the argument] with all its means of proof and examples is stated to be devoid of what is to be proved — regarding permanence and pervasiveness.

body.text:
212.

body.translated_text: 212. The establishment of the <s>ātman</s> (self) as imagined by others — through direct perception: the <s>ātman</s> is held to be self-cognized, the object of the sense of 'I' (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>).

body.text:
213.

body.translated_text: 213. That is not right, because the form of permanence, pervasiveness, and so forth does not appear in the sense of 'I'; for indeed, that appearance is not perceived there.

body.text:
214.
(vyaktam)(nirbhāsaḥ)(tatra*)(tu*)(gaura-)(varṇa-)(ādi-)(ca*)(ātmā, 1st s.)(na*)(iṣṭaḥ)(sva-bhāvaḥ)(tat-)(tataḥ*)(ayam, 1st s.)(na*)(viṣayaḥ)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 214. Clearly, the appearance there is of fair complexion and so forth; and the <s>ātman</s> is not desired [to have] that nature. Therefore, this is not its object.

body.text:
215.
(yadi*)(puruṣaḥ)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(satyataḥ* [-tas suff.])(gamyaḥ)(pratyakṣa-)(tat)(kim*) (artham*)(vivādaḥ ayam)(pravarttate ”vṛt)(tat-sattva-)(ādau, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 215. If the <s>puruṣa</s> (person) were truly apprehended by direct perception, then for what purpose does this debate proceed regarding the existence and so forth of that?

body.text:
216.
(hi*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(ahaṅkāra-)(pra-varttate ”vṛt Pr. III p. s.)(ātmā)(niścaya-)(āropa-)(buddhyoḥ, 6th d.)(sthitā, f.)(-tā suff.)(bādhaka-, f.)(bādhya-)
body.translated_text: 216. For this sense of 'I' (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>) operates; the <s>ātman</s> — between the cognitions of ascertainment and superimposition, the state of being the refuter and the refuted is established.

body.text:
217.
