body.translated_text: 217. Therefore, desire and all the rest are not at all inherent in the <s>ātman</s> (self); because they arise sequentially — like the seed, sprout, and creeper.

body.text:
218.
(atha vā*)(sarve, m. 1st pl.)(ādhyātmikāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(mūrttayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(ākrānta-)(nairātmya-)(hetubhyaḥ, m. 5th pl.)(vastu-)(sattva-)(ādi-)(yathā*)(ghaṭa-)(ādayaḥ)(bāhyāḥ, 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 218. Or rather, all internal forms [of the body] — since they are assailed by the proofs of selflessness, [they are] like external things such as pots, regarding the existence of a real entity and so forth.

body.text:
219.
(hi*)(sa-)(ātmakatve, 7th s.)(hetūnām, 6th pl.)(tad- = soul)(prasajyate ”sañj pass.)(nityatvam, n. 2nd s.)(ca*)(nityāḥ)(a-śaktāḥ)(artha-kriyā-)(ataḥ*)(na*)(a-sambhavaḥ)(sattva-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 219. For if the causes had a self, permanence of that [self] would follow; and what is permanent is incapable of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) — therefore the existence and so forth [of a self] is impossible.

body.text:
220.
(nairātmyam, n. 1st s.)(yad)(paraiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(niṣidhyate ”sad, pass.)(ghaṭa-)(ādiṣu, 7th pl.)(tat)(samānam)(prasādhyate ”sādh caus. pass.)(asmābhiḥ, 3 pl.)(asmin, 7th s.)(jīvad-)(śarīre, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 220. The selflessness that is rejected by others regarding pots and the like — that same [selflessness] is equally established by us in this living body.

body.text:
221.
(ca*)(ittham*)(ātma-)(a-prasiddhau, f. 7th s.)(sā, f. 1st s.)(sarvā, f. 1st s.)(prakriyā, f. 1st s.)(yā, f.)(kṛtā, f. 1st s.)(tatra*)(sthitā, f. 1st s.)(eva*)(nirāspadā, f. 1st s.)(iva*)(putra-)(vandhyā-)
body.translated_text: 221. And thus, when the <s>ātman</s> (self) is not established, all that procedure which was performed [to prove it] remains there itself, groundless — like the son of a barren woman.

body.text:
222.
(apare, m. 1st s.)(punaḥ*)(icchanti ”iṣ Pr. III p. pl.)(ātmānam, n. 2nd s.)(rūpam)(caitanya-)(vyāvṛtti-)(anugama-)(ātmānam, n. 2nd s.)(caitanya, n. 2nd s.)(lakṣaṇam, 2nd s.)(buddhi-)
body.translated_text: 222. Others, however, maintain that the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) has the form of consciousness — [that is,] the <s>Ātman</s> characterized by <s>caitanya</s> (consciousness) that persists through the exclusion [of other properties]; it has the nature of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) —

body.text:
223.
(yathā*)(aheḥ, m. 6th s.)(kundala-)(avasthā, f. 1st s.)(vyapaiti; vi-apa-”i II C. Pr. III p. s.)(tad-anantaram)(sambhavati ”bhū Pr. III p. s.)(arjava-)(avasthā)(tu*)(sarpatvam)(anu-varttate ”vṛt)
body.translated_text: 223. Just as a serpent's coiled state departs, and immediately thereafter the straightened state arises, while the serpenthood continues,

body.text:
224.
(tathā* eva*)(api*)(na*)(niḥśeṣa-)(rūpa-vigamaḥ, 1st s.)(ātmanaḥ, n. 6th s.)(sva-bhāvasya)(nitya-)(caitanya-)(api*)( vā*)(anugamaḥ)(sarvasya, 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 224. Even so, there is no complete departure of the form of the <s>Ātman</s>'s own nature — or rather, the <s>caitanya</s> (consciousness) of everything, being eternal, continues.

body.text:
225.
(kintu*)(vi-ni-varttante ”vṛt)(avasthāḥ)(lakṣaṇāḥ)(sukha-)(duḥkha-)(ādi-)(ca*)(tāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(jāyante ”jan)(tu*)(caitanyam)(anu-varttate ”vṛt)
body.translated_text: 225. Rather, the states characterized by pleasure, pain, and so forth cease, and those [new states] arise, while <s>caitanya</s> (consciousness) continues.

body.text:
226.
(hi*)(atyanta-)(nāśe, m. 7th s.)(syātām ”as Opt. III p. d.)(nāśa-)(kṛta-)(āgamau, 1st d.)(a-kṛta-)(eka-)(rūpiṇaḥ, n. 6th s.)(na*)(syāt ”as Opt. III p. s.)(eva*)(bhogaḥ)(sukha-)(duḥkha-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 226. For if there were absolute destruction, destruction and acquisition would result; and for [something] of a single, uncreated form, there would be no experience of pleasure, pain, and so forth.

body.text:
227.
(puṃsaḥ, m. 6th s.)(kartṛ-)(-tve n. 1st d.)(bhoktṛ-)(na*)(samāśrite, n. 1st d.)(avasthām, m. 2nd s.)(tataḥ*)(-tattvāt)(tat-)(avasthāsu, f. 7th pl.)(kartā, m. 1st s.)(āpnoti ”āp, =experiences)(phalam, n. 2nd s.)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 227. When agency and enjoyership are not dependent on the <s>Puruṣa</s> (soul), [but rather] because of having the nature of those states, the agent experiences the fruit in those states.

body.text:
228.
(pumān, m. 1st s.)(evaṃvidhaḥ)(pramīyate ”mā, pass.)(bhāvataḥ* [-tas suff.])(pratyabhijñāna-)(ca*)(hi*)(nairātmyasya, 6th s.)(prabādhā, f. 1st s.)(amunā, m. 3rd s.)(eva*)
body.translated_text: 228. Such a <s>Puruṣa</s> (soul) is ascertained from its actual existence; and indeed, through recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>), the objection of selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) is refuted by this very [argument].

body.text:
229.
(ahaṃ-buddhiḥ, 1st s.)(vedmi ”vid II C. Pr. I p. s.)(pratipadyate ”pad IV C. Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(jñātāram, m. 2nd s.)(ca*)(yadi*)(saḥ)(syāt ”as Opt. III p. s.)(vā*)(ātmā, n. 1st s.)(again: vā*)(ekānta-vinaśvaram)(-jñānam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 229. The I-cognition (<s>ahaṃ-buddhi</s>) apprehends a knower, [thinking] 'I know.' And if it were the <s>Ātman</s>, or if knowledge were entirely momentary,

body.text:
230.
(yadi*)(ātmā)(viṣayaḥ)(tasyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(tadā*)(akhilam, n. 1st s.)(caturasram, n. 1st s.)(tu*)(kṣaṇika-)(jñāna-)(pakṣe, 7th s.)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(ati-)(durghaṭam)
body.translated_text: 230. If the <s>Ātman</s> were the object of that [I-cognition], then all would be settled. But on the thesis of momentary cognition, everything is extremely difficult [to explain].

body.text:
231-232.
(tathā*)(hi*)(aham, 1st s.)(jñātavān, m. 1st s.)(pūrvam eva*)(ca*)(pravedmi ”vid II C. Pr. I p. s.)(samprati*)(iti*)(tasyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(buddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(yā, f. 1st s.)(upajāyate ”jan pass.)(kaḥ)(jñāna-kṣaṇaḥ)(nu*)(parikalpyate ”kḷp pass.)(viṣayaḥ)(kiṃ vā*)(atītaḥ)(kim vā*)(sāmprataḥ)(atha*)(asau, m. 1st s.)(santatiḥ, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 231-232. For when the cognition arises: 'I knew before and I know now' — which moment of cognition is conceived as the object? Is it the past [moment], or the present one, or is it the [entire] continuum?

body.text:
233.
(ādye, 7th s.)(tatra*)(yujyate ”yuj)(iti*)(jñātvān, m. 1st s.)(viṣaye, 7th s.)(jñāte, 7th s.)(ca*)(na*)(yuktam, 1st s.)(iti*)(jānāmi ”jñā IX C. Pr. I p. s.)(asau, 1st s.)(na*)(vetti ”vid II C. Pr. III p. s.)(idānīm*)
body.translated_text: 233. In the first [case], 'one who has known' is appropriate regarding the object that has been known; but 'I know [now]' is not appropriate, [for] that [past knower] does not know now.

body.text:
234.
(viṣaye, 7th s.)(varttamāne, 7th s.)(upapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(iti*)(pravedmi ”vid II C. Pr. I p. s.)(tu*)(a-satyam)(jñātavān m. 1st s.)(yataḥ*)(idam, 1st s.)(na*)(eva*)(āsīt ”as)(prāk*)
body.translated_text: 234. When the object is present, 'I know [now]' is appropriate; but 'I have known' is untrue, since this [present cognition] did not exist before.

body.text:
235.
(eva*)(ataḥ*)(dvayam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(eva*)(prakalpyate ”kḷp pass.)(grāhyam, n. 1st s.)(tasyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(na*)(vā*)(hi*)(ubhau, m. 1st d.)(jñātavantau, m. 1st d.)(vā*...punaḥ)(jānītaḥ ”jñā IX C. Pr. III p. d.)(adhunā*)
body.translated_text: 235. Therefore, neither of the two can be conceived as the object of that [I-cognition]; nor indeed [can] both — [that] they have known before and know now —

body.text:
236.
(api*)(na*)(santānaḥ)(bāhyaḥ)(tat-)(a-sambhavāt, 5th s.)(dvitīyasya)(api*)(asau, m. 1st s.)(hi*)(na*)(jñātvān)(pūrvam)(a-vastu-tvāt, 5th s.)(adhunā*)
body.translated_text: 236. Nor is the continuum [a viable option], since that [continuum] is external [to each moment]; moreover, that [continuum] too did not know before, since it has no [real] existence now.

body.text:
237.
(tasmāt, 5th s.)(siddhaḥ)(yatra*)(gocare, 7th s.)(ahaṅkāraḥ)(varttate ”vṛt)(asau, 1st s.)(ātmā, 1st s.)(-vat- suff.)(śāśvata-)(rūpa-)(anyatra*)(uktād, 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 237. Therefore it is established: that in whose domain the sense of 'I' (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>) operates — that is like the <s>Ātman</s>, of an eternal form, as stated elsewhere.

body.text:
238.
(ca*)(ahaṅkṛtiḥ, f. 1st s.)(vyatīta [vi-ati-”i])(ca*)(jñātā, f. 1st s.)(ādyaḥ, 1st s.)(anuvarttate ”vṛt Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(adya*)(api*)(gamyatvāt, n. 5th s.)(aham-pratyaya-)(-vat* suff.)(boddhṛ-)(idānīntana-)
body.translated_text: 238. And the I-function, [relating to] the past, and [relating to] the knower — the first continues even today, since it is apprehended as having the nature of the I-cognition, [relating to] the present knower.

body.text:
239.
(vā*)(eṣaḥ)(jñātā, m. 1st s. [-tṛ suff.])(hyastanaḥ)(-tvāt suff.)(jñātṛ-)(vā*)(tataḥ*)(eva*)(-vat* suff.)(jñātṛ-)(hyastana-)(ca*)(teṣām, 6th pl.)(pratyayānām, 6th pl.)(sādhyatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 239. Or this [is] the knower, because of being yesterday's, or [he is] a knower therefore — like yesterday's knower; and the validity of those cognitions [must be established].

body.text:
240.
(sarve, 1st pl.)(hyastana-)(adyatanāḥ, 1st pl.)(tulya-)(arthāḥ, 1st pl.)(-tas suff.)(aham-pratyaya-tva-)(jñātṛ-)(sambandha-)(eka-)(santāna-)(-vat* suff.)(eka-)(buddhi-)
body.translated_text: 240. All [cognitions], whether of yesterday or today, are of equal meaning — from the fact of being I-cognitions, having the nature of a single continuum of knower-connection, of a single cognition.

body.text:
241.
(tad*)(atra*)(cintyate ”cint pass.)(yadi*)(caitanyam, 1st s.)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(nityam, 1st s.)(ekam, 1st s.)(tathā sati, 7th s.)(buddhiḥ, f.)(api*)(prāptā, f. 1st s.)(tat-)(eva*)(rūpā, f.)
body.translated_text: 241. Here it is to be considered: if <s>caitanya</s> (consciousness) is held to be eternal and one, then <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) too would be obtained as having that very form.

body.text:
242.
(buddhīnām, 6th pl.)(puruṣasya, 6th s.)(ca*)(ceṣṭā, f.)(nityatvam, n.)(ekatā, f.)(svābhāvyāt, 5th s.)(caitanya-)(cet*)(bhedaḥ)(āśrayaḥ)(viṣaya-)
body.translated_text: 242. Of the <s>buddhis</s> (cognitions) and of the <s>Puruṣa</s> (soul): [their] activity, eternality, and oneness — [all follow] from the intrinsic nature of <s>caitanya</s> (consciousness). If [one objects that] the difference [arises from] the basis and the object —

body.text:
243.
(tathā*)(sva-rūpeṇa, 3rd s.)(vahniḥ, f. 1st s.)(nityam)(dharmakaḥ)(dahana-)(dahati ”dah)(artham, 2nd s.)(upanītam)(dāhyam, 2nd s.)(na*)(anyat, 2nd s.)(na*)(anyadā*)
body.translated_text: 243. Then, just as fire, being eternally possessed of the nature of burning, burns the combustible object brought [near it], and not another object, and not at another time —

body.text:
244.
(yathā vā*)(svacchaḥ)(darpaṇaḥ)(yathā* vā*)(sphaṭikopalaḥ)(pratipadyate ”pad IV C. Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(chāyām, f. 2nd s.)(eva*)(tad, 2nd s.)(yad, 2nd s.)(ādhīyate ”dhā pass.)(tatra*)
body.translated_text: 244. Or just as a clear mirror or a crystal reflects precisely that image which is placed before it —

body.text:
245.
(eva*)(tathā*)(pumāṃsaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(nitya-)(caitanyāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(gṛhṇanti ”grah Pr. III p. pl.)(rūpa-ādīn, 2nd pl.)(vṛttayaḥ, f. 1st. pl.)(deha-)(ānītān, 2nd pl.)(karaṇa-)(ca*)(asau, f. 1st s.)(dhīḥ, f. 1st s.)(naḥ, 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 245. Even so, the <s>Puruṣas</s> (souls), [being] eternally conscious, apprehend forms and so forth brought [to them] through the body and the sense organs — and this cognition is our [view].

body.text:
246.
(tena*)(bhaṅgitvāt, n. 5th s.)(saṃrambha-)(upanetṛ-)(matiḥ, f.)(bhaṅginī, f.)(yathā*)(vahniḥ, m.)(na*)(nityam)(dāhakaḥ)(a-sannidhinā, 3rd s.)(dāhyā, f.)
body.translated_text: 246. By that [reasoning], because of [cognition's] perishability, the cognition that brings forth activity is perishable; just as fire does not burn permanently, when the combustible is not proximate.

body.text:
247.
(tatra*)(matiḥ)(pratyabhijñāyate; prati-abhi-”jñā pass.)(-tvena suff. 3rd s.)(ātmaka-)(bodha-)(-tvam suff.)(buddhi-)(ghaṭa-)(hasti-)(ādi-)(sammatam, 1st s.)(loka-)(bhedāt, 5th s.)(tat-)."
body.translated_text: 247. Therein, cognition is recognized as having the nature of awareness — the cognition of a pot, an elephant, and so forth; that is commonly accepted. From [their] difference —

body.text:
248.
(buddhiḥ, f.)(na*)(ucyate ”vac pass. Pr. III p. s.)(sā, f.)(eva*)(anusāribhiḥ, 3rd pl.)(bheda-)(artha-) [cognized](na*)(ca*)(asti ”as)(a-pratyabhijñānam)(upāśrite, 7th s.)(bhede, 7th s.)(artha-)
body.translated_text: 248. That very [cognition] is not said [to be identical] by those who follow [it]; nor is there non-recognition when a difference in the cognized object is resorted to.

body.text:
249.
(nanu*)(tatra*)(pratyayāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(ye, m. 1st pl.)(āropa-kāriṇaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(hasti-)(ādi-)(bhūmau, f. 7th s.)(śūnyāyām, f. 7th s.)(pravarttante; pra-”vṛt Āt. Pr. III p. pl.)(kim*)(āśrayaḥ)(bhedaḥ)
body.translated_text: 249. Indeed, when the ground of elephants and so forth is empty [of them], what basis is there for the cognitions that superimpose [them] to operate? Is [the basis] a difference?

body.text:
250.
(cet*)(vyaktayaḥ, 1st pl.)(bhāvinyaḥ, 1st pl.)(anya-)(deśa-)(ādi-)(nibandhanam)(yasmāt, 5th s.)(sarvatra*)(ālambanam, n. 1st s.)(deśa-)(kāla-)(anyathā*)
body.translated_text: 250. If [cognitions] are manifest and existent — the restriction [of cognition] depends on [factors like] another place and so forth; since everywhere the support [of cognition varies] according to place, time, and other [conditions].

body.text:
251.
(nanu*)(asti ”as)(na*)(tathā*)(sambandhaḥ)(eva*)(tat-)(deśa-)(tāsām, f. 6th pl.)(tat*)(kim* iti*)(pratibhāsante ”bhās Pr. III p. pl.)(tena rūpeṇa, 3rd s.)(ca*)(tatra*)
body.translated_text: 251. Indeed, there is no such connection of those [cognitions] with that [particular] place. Then why do they appear in that form there?

body.text:
252.
(hi*)(bhavan-)(mate, 7th s.)(bāhyaḥ)(ākāraḥ)(na*)(varṇyate ”varṇ pass. Pr. III p. s.)(buddheḥ, 6th s.)(na* ... ca*)(gaja-)(yaṣṭi-)(ādayaḥ, 1st pl.)(sthitāḥ, 1st pl.)(vivakṣita-)(deśe, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 252. For in your view, the external form of cognition is not described; and elephants, posts, and so forth do not exist in the intended place.

body.text:
253.
(yadi*)(buddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(sthitā)(sadā*)(rūpā)(bodha-)(sarva-)(artha-)(tat*)(kim* artham*)(saṃvittiḥ, f.)(sarva-)(na*)(vidyate ”vid IV C. Pr. III p. s.)(sarvadā*)
body.translated_text: 253. If <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) is always established [as having] the form of awareness of all objects, then why is cognition of everything not found at all times?

body.text:
254.
(buddhiḥ)(śabda-)(upadhānā, f.)(gocarā, f.)(rasa-)(rūpa-)(ādi-)
(cet*)(na*)(hi*)(tvayā, 3rd s.)(upapāditāḥ, 1st pl.)(bhedāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(iti*)(sā, f.)(eva*)
body.translated_text: 254. [If you say] <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) has sound as its basis and has taste, form, and so forth as its domain — [the objection is:] the differences have not been established by you; that very [problem remains].

body.text:
255.
(api*)(kṛśānuḥ, 1st s.)(na*)(nityam)(ātmakaḥ)(dahana-)(samasta-)(dāhya-)(rūpāṇām, 6th pl.)(anyathā*)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. Pr. III p. s.)(niḥśeṣam, 2nd s. [adv.])(bhasmasān, 2nd pl.)
body.translated_text: 255. Moreover, fire is not eternally possessed of the nature of burning all combustibles; otherwise, it would reduce everything to ashes completely.

body.text:
256.
(eva*)(loc. abs.)(sannidhau, 7th s.)(dāhya-)(artha-)(tasya, 6th s.)(yuktā, f. 1st s.)(hi*)(na*)(sajyate ”sajj pass.)(dāhaḥ, 1st s.)(sarva-artha-)(sakṛt*)(evam*)
body.translated_text: 256. Indeed, the burning of fire is appropriate [only] in the proximity of a combustible object; it does not ignite all objects at once in this way.

body.text:
257.
(darpaṇa-)(sphuṭika-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(kṣaṇa-bhaṅginaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(sambandhāt, m. 5th s.)(nīla-utpala-)(ādi-)(hetavaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(utpāda-)(vibhrama-)(tat-)(chāyā-)
body.translated_text: 257. Mirrors, crystals, and the like are momentarily perishable; through their connection with blue lotuses and so forth, the cause of the illusion of [reflected] images —

body.text:
258.
(itara-)(avasthaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(sa-)(upadhāna-)(sarvadā*)(iti*)(ekaḥ, 1st s.)(eva*)(vā*)(chāyaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(tat-)(viyuktaḥ)(tat-)(punaḥ*)(dṛśyeta ”dṛś pass. Opt. III p. s.)(anyathā*)
body.translated_text: 258. [If the mirror] always has one condition, with the same basis — then either it would have only one image, or, separated from that, it would again appear otherwise.

body.text:
259.
(darpaṇa-talam, n. 1st s.)(na* kadācana*)(eva*)(bibhartti ”bhṛ III C., Pr. III p. s.)(chāyām, f. 2nd s.)(sthiratvāt, n. 5th s.)(nirvibhāgatvāt, n. 5th s.)(mūrttānām, m. 6th pl.)(a-saha-sthiteḥ, f. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 259. A mirror surface never bears a [real] image, because of its rigidity, because of its partlessness, and because solid [objects] cannot co-exist [in the same location].

body.text:
260.
(-saṃsthāḥ, 1st pl.)(dvitaya-)(pārśva-)(samīkṣyante; sam-”īkṣ 4th c., Pr. III p. pl.)(su-śuklam, m. 2nd s.)(sphaṭikopalam, m. 2nd s.)(tat*)(eṣaḥ)(api*)(na*)(pratipannavān, m. 1st s.)(chāyām, f. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 260. [Reflections with] two-sided configurations are observed; [but if] a very white crystal has not [truly] received an image —

body.text:
261.
(prasajyate ”sañj pass.)(sphuṭikā-)(ādeḥ, 6th s.)(bhedaḥ)(prati*)(upadhānam, n. 2nd s.)(cet*)(pratipattiḥ, f. 1st s.)(tasya, 6th s.)(chāyā-)(vidyeta ”vid IV C. Opt. III p. s.)(tāttvikī, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 261. If, for a crystal and the like, the basis [of reflection] is per each difference, then the apprehension of its image would be [ultimately] real.

body.text:
262.
(tasmāt, 5th s.)(iyam, f. 1st s.)(bhrāntiḥ, f. 1st s.)(teṣu, 7th pl.)(vicitra-)(acintya-)(śaktiṣu, f. 7th pl.)(buddhau, 7th s.)(api*)(bhāvaḥ)(bhrāntiḥ, f. 1st s.)(na*)(yuktaḥ)(viyogataḥ* [-tas suff.])(bheda-)
body.translated_text: 262. Therefore, this is an error — [arising] in those [mirrors and crystals] of diverse and inconceivable powers; in cognition too, error is not appropriate, because of the separation of differences.

body.text:
263.
(tu*)(bhedam, m. 2nd s.)(a-bodha-)(samānam, m. 2nd s.)(sarva-)(buddhiṣu, f. 7th pl.)(pratyabhijñānam)(pravarttate ”vṛt Pr. III p. s.)(āropya*)(api*)(nānātve, n. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 263. But recognition operates in all cognitions, superimposing a sameness equal to non-awareness, even regarding diversity.

body.text:
264.
(bheda-)(avasthā-)(bhedena, 3rd s.)(śūnyaḥ)(api*)(eka-)(antataḥ* [-tas suff.])(sthite, 7th s.)(sthira-)(ātmani, n. 7th s.)(ātmani, n. 7th s.)(idam, 1st s.)(parikalpyate ”kḷp pass.)
body.translated_text: 264. Even though devoid of difference through the distinction of states (<s>avasthā</s>), this is imagined with respect to the unchanging <s>Ātman</s> in an absolute sense.

body.text:
265.
(avastāḥ, f. 2nd pl.)(sukha-)(duḥkha-)(ādi-)(ca*)(gacchan, m 1st s. [gacchat (>-an)], m. 1st s.)(api*)(naraḥ)(mama, 6th s.)(na*)(eva*)(vimuñcati ”muñc Pr. III p. s.)(rūpam, n. 2nd s.)(caitanya-)(dravya-)(sattva-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 265. A person, even while undergoing states of pleasure, pain, and so forth, never relinquishes his form — [this is maintained] because of the reality of the substance of consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>).

body.text:
266.
(utpāde, 7th s.)(avasthā-antara-)(pūrvā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(vinaśyati ”naś 4th C. Pr. III p. s.)(līyate ”lī pass.)(sāmānya-)(ātmani, n. 7th s.)(artham*)(anuguṇa-)(uttara-)
body.translated_text: 266. Upon the arising of a subsequent state, the previous one does not perish; it merges into the universal nature (<s>sāmānya-ātman</s>) in accordance with [its] purpose.

body.text:
267.
(hi*)(anyonyasya)(virodhitā, f.)(avasthānām, 6th pl.)(sva-rūpeṇa, 3rd s.)(tu*)(sāmānya-)(ātmā, 1st s.)(pratīyate, prati-”i, pass. Pr. III p. s.)(sarvāsu, f. 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 267. For there is mutual opposition among the states; but the universal nature (<s>sāmānya-ātman</s>) is perceived by its own form in all [states].

body.text:
268.
(tatra*)(cet*)(avasthānām 6th pl.)(no*)(ekāntena, 3rd s.)(vibhinnatā, f.)(puruṣāt, 5th s.)(vyaya-)(utpāde, 7th s.)(tat-)(tau, 1st d.)(syātām ”as Opt. III p. dual)(asya)(api*)
body.translated_text: 268. If, in that case, the states are not absolutely distinct from <s>Puruṣa</s>, then upon [their] arising and perishing, those two [arising and perishing] would belong to him as well.

body.text:
269.
(tu*)(saṅge, 7th s.)(viruddha-)(dharma-)(bhedaḥ)(bhavet ”bhū Opt.)(ekāntikaḥ)(iva*)(te, 6th s.)(puṃsām, m. 6th pl.)(niyatena, 3rd s.)(svabhāvena, m. 3rd s.)(pratisvam, 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 269. But in [their] connection, the distinction of contradictory properties would be absolute, as it were; for [you hold that] among persons (<s>puṃs</s>), each one has a fixed nature.

body.text:
270.
(ca*)(yadi*)(vaḥ, 6th pl.)(avasthāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(līyante ”lī)(puṃsi, 7th s.)(eva*)(svarūpeṇa, 3rd s.)(sam-ud-bhave, m. 7th s.)(sudha-)(ādi-)(duḥkha-)(ādi)(api*)(anubhūyeta ”bhū pass. Opt. III p. s.)
body.translated_text: 270. And if your states merge into <s>Puruṣa</s> alone in their own form, then upon [their] arising, pleasure and the like as well as pain and the like would [all] be experienced [simultaneously].

body.text:
271.
(ca*)(saṅkrāntau, f. 7th s.)(anya-)(rūpa-)(na*)(saṅkrānti-)(anya-)(ca*)(saṅkrāntiḥ, 1st s.)(tādātmyena, 3rd s.)(ātmā, 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū Opt.)(udaya-vān, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 271. And in the case of transference (<s>saṅkrānti</s>), the form is not other [than the self]; and the transference being other [than the self], the <s>Ātman</s> would become one that possesses arising through identity [with the states].

body.text:
272.
(yadi*)(kartṛtva-)(bhoktṛtve, n. 1st d.)(samāśrite, 1st d.)(avasthām, 2nd s.)(tad*)(na*)(saṃbhavaḥ)(kartṛtva-)(ādi-)(tatvāt, n. 5th s.)(avasthāvataḥ, m. 6th s. [-vat suff.])
body.translated_text: 272. If agentship (<s>kartṛtva</s>) and enjoyership (<s>bhoktṛtva</s>) are dependent on a state, then that is not possible, because agentship and the like belong to the possessor of states.

body.text:
273.
(tad*)(vācyatvam, n. 1st s.)(śabda-)(nitya-)(na*)(vinivāryate; vi-ni”vṛ pass.)(-tvāt [suff.] n. 5th s.)(sva-rūpa-)(vikriyāvat-)(asya, 6th s.)(vyuchedaḥ)(vidyate ”vid IV C. Pr. III p. s.)
body.translated_text: 273. That expressibility [of the self] cannot be denied, because words are eternal; [and yet] for this [self] which possesses modification of its own nature, cessation exists.

body.text:
274.
(sarpaḥ)(api*)(prapadyate ”pad pass.)(kauṭilya-)(ādīn, m. 2nd pl.)(kṣaṇa-)(bhaṅgitvāt, n. 5th s.)(tu*)(sthira-rūpe, 7th s.)(iva*)(saṅgatiḥ, 1st s.)(antara-)(avasthā-)(na*)
body.translated_text: 274. Even a serpent assumes coiling and other [forms]; but due to momentariness, there is no connection with a stable form — [nor with] an intervening state.

body.text:
275.
(ayam, m. 1st s.)(ahaṅkāraḥ)(pravarttate)(eva*)(nirālambanaḥ, m. 1st s.)(prabhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(an-ādi-)(bīja-)(dṛk-)(sattva-)(hi*)(eva*)(kvacit*)
body.translated_text: 275. This <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (I-notion) operates indeed without any support (<s>nirālambana</s>); for it arises from the power of beginningless seeds of perception (<s>dṛk</s>) and existence (<s>sattva</s>) in some [cases].

body.text:
276.
(eva*)(kecid*)(saṃskārāḥ)(prapadyante ”pad pass. Pr. III p. pl.)(ādhipatyam, 2nd s.)(adhyavasāyini, n. 7th s.)(tat-)(rūpa-)(hi*)(tad, 1st s.)(na*)(varttate ”vṛt Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(sarvatra*)
body.translated_text: 276. Indeed, certain <s>saṃskāras</s> (impressions) attain predominance in the determining [mind]; for that [I-notion] of that form does not operate everywhere.

body.text:
277.
(anyathā*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(paryanuyogaḥ)(tulyaḥ)(vaḥ, 6th pl.)(puruṣe, m. 7th s.)(api*)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(nirākulam, n. 1st s.)(sadbhāvāt, 5th s.)(bheda-)(tat-)(śakti-)
body.translated_text: 277. Otherwise, this objection applies equally to your [doctrine regarding] <s>Puruṣa</s> as well; [for if] everything is unconfused because of the existence of the power of differentiation in that [Puruṣa] —

body.text:
278.
(pakṣe, m. 7th s.)(nitya-)(ālambana-)(sarva-)(ahaṃkṛtayaḥ, f. 1st pl.)(prasūyeran ”sū Āt. Opt. III p. pl.)(sakṛt* eva*)(śakti-hetu-)(vyavasthiteḥ, 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 278. In the position [where the I-notion has] a permanent support, all I-cognitions would arise simultaneously, because the causal determination through [its] power is fixed.

body.text:
279.
(a-nitya-)(ālambane, 7th s.)(syuḥ ”as Opt. III p. pl.)(spaṣṭābhāḥ, 1st pl.)(tataḥ*)(pare, m. 1st pl.)(vyartham, 2nd s.)(paryanuyuñjate; pari-anu-”yuj, VII C. Āt. Pr. III p. pl.)(sad-bhāvam, 2nd s.)(artha-)(ālambana-)
body.translated_text: 279. If [the support is] impermanent, then we others are clearly [in agreement]; [you] pointlessly object to the existence of an object-support — the reality [of such a support].

body.text:
280.
(vāsanā, f. 1st s.)(arhati ”arh Pr. III p. s.)(kartum* ”kṛ)(pratyabhijñānam, n. 2nd s.)(jñātari, m. 7th s.)(saḥ)(prajñām, f. 2nd s.)(a-tasmin, 7th s.)(hi*)(asau, f. 1st s.)(na*)(kāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(bhrānti-)
body.translated_text: 280. <s>Vāsanā</s> (latent impression) is capable of producing recognition in the knower; that [I-notion] in the absence of that [object] is indeed not a cause — [it is] an error (<s>bhrānti</s>).

body.text:
281.
(tad*)(ahaṃ-pratyayaḥ)(na*)(iṣṭaḥ)(bhrāntiḥ, f. 1st s.)(varjanāt, n. 5th s.)(bādha-)(cet*)(na*)(yuktyā, 3rd s.)(uktayā, 3rd s.)(anantara-)(upadarśanāt, n. 5th s.)(bādha-)(tasya, 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 281. If [you say] the I-notion is not accepted [as] an error, because of the avoidance of sublation (<s>bādha</s>) — no, because by the reasoning stated immediately [above], the sublation of that [I-notion] has been demonstrated.

body.text:
282.
(ca*)(katham*)(bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(mātra-)(vāsanā-)(bhaktānām, m. 6th pl.)(jāyante ”jan pass. Pr. III p. pl.)(vividhāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(vibhramāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(īśvara-)(ādiṣu, 7th pl.)(hetutva-)(tat-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 282. And how do various delusions arise among those devoted merely to <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impressions), such as [attributing] causality to <s>Īśvara</s> (God) and so forth?

body.text:
283.
(evam*)(ca*)(nir-ālambana-tā, f. 1st s.)(sthitā, f. 1st s.)(ahaṅkāre, 7th s.)(tad*)(vidyate ”vid IV C. Pr. III p. s.)(na*)(jñātā, -tṛ stem, m. 1st s.)(grāhye, 7th s.)(ahaṃ-pratyaya-)
body.translated_text: 283. Thus, the groundlessness (<s>nirālambanatā</s>) of the <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (I-notion) is established; there is no knower [to be found] in the object of the I-cognition.

body.text:
284.
(tataḥ*)(sarva-)(pramāṇeṣu, m./n. 7th pl.)(asti ”as)(na*)(dṛṣṭāntaḥ)(bhāk, m. 1st s.)(siddhi-)(ca*)(hetavaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(udāhṛtāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(yathāyogam, 2nd s.)(a-siddhāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(āśraya-)
body.translated_text: 284. Therefore, among all <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge), there is no corroborating example; and the reasons cited as establishing [the self] are, as appropriate, unestablished due to the fallacy of unestablished locus (<s>āśraya-asiddha</s>).

body.text:
285.
(anye, 1st m. pl.)(manyante ”man Pr. III p. pl.)(caitanyam, n. 2nd s.)(bhinnam, n. 2nd s.)(svarūpataḥ* [-tas suff.])(buddhi-)(te, 1st pl.)(kalpayanti ”kḷp caus. Pr. III p. pl.)(caitanyam, n. 2nd s.)(nijam, n. 2nd s.)(rūpam, n. 2nd s.)(ātmanaḥ, n. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 285. Others consider consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>) as distinct from <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) in its own nature; they postulate consciousness as the inherent nature (<s>nija rūpa</s>) of the <s>Ātman</s>.

body.text:
286.
(ca*)(saḥ)(kevalam*)(bhuṅkte ”bhuj Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(phalam, n. 2nd s.)(upanītam, n 2nd s.)(pradhānena, n. 3rd s.)(tasya, 6th s.)(asti ”as)(na* eva*)(kartṛtvaṃ)(tan-)(matam, n. 1st s.)(prakṛteḥ, f. 6th s.)(eva*)
body.translated_text: 286. And he merely enjoys the fruit brought forth by <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter); agentship does not belong to him at all — that is the doctrine; [agentship belongs] to <s>Prakṛti</s> alone.

body.text:
287.
(tatra* api*)(cet*)(cetanā, f. 1st s.)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(ekā, f. 1st s.)(katham*)(cetasām, n. 6th pl.)(rūpa-)(śabda-)(ādi-)(su-vyaktam, n. 1st s.)(rūpam, n. 1st s.)(-vat suff.)(bheda-)(vedyate ”vid caus. pass.)
body.translated_text: 287. Even there, if consciousness (<s>cetanā</s>) is held to be single, how is it clearly perceived as manifold, possessing forms of color, sound, and so forth, like [objects] possessing form?

body.text:
288.
(caitanye, n. 7th s.)(eka-rūpe, n. 7th s.)(ca*)(avasthite, n. 7th s.)(sarva-)(kālam, n. 2nd s.)(katham* nāma*)(upapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(-tvam suff. n. 1st s.)(bhoktṛ-)(artha-)(nānāvidha-)
body.translated_text: 288. And when consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>) is of a single nature and exists at all times, how indeed can the status of being an enjoyer (<s>bhoktṛtva</s>) of manifold objects be justified?

body.text:
289.
(didṛkṣā- [des. noun, ”dṛś])(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(bhinnāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(na*)(bhavanti ”bhū Pr. III p. pl.)(nibandhanam, n. 2nd s.)(tasya)(bhoga-)(hi*)(tathā*)(pumān, 1st s.)(bhavet, Opt.)(utpattimān, 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 289. The desire to see (<s>didṛkṣā</s>) and other [mental states], being different, do not constitute the basis of his enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>); for if so, <s>Puruṣa</s> would become one who has origination.

body.text:
290.
(di*)(didṛkṣā-)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(vidyate ”vid IV C. Pr. III p. s.)(na*)(vyatiriktam, n. 2nd s.)(caitanaya-)(asau, m. 1st s.)(āveśe, 7th s.)(udaya-)(vyaya-)(asau, m. 1st s.)(durvāraḥ, m. 1st s.)(puruṣe, m. 7th s.)(api*)
body.translated_text: 290. If the desire to see (<s>didṛkṣā</s>) and so forth exist as not separate from consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>), that [Puruṣa] would be subject to arising and perishing — an inescapable [consequence] even for <s>Puruṣa</s>.

body.text:
291.
(cet*)(śubha-)(a-śubha-)(karma, n. 1st s.)(na*)(eva*)(kṛtam)(ātmanā, n. 3rd s.)(tad*)(kutaḥ*)(bhedaḥ)(asya, m. 6th s.)(bhoga-)(samupajāyate ”jan pass.)
body.translated_text: 291. If meritorious and non-meritorious <s>karma</s> is not performed by the <s>Ātman</s>, then whence does the differentiation of his enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) arise?

body.text:
292.
(cet*)(prakṛtiḥ, f. 1st s.)(prayacchati ”yacch)(anurūpeṇa, 3rd s.)(abhilāṣa-)(eṣaḥ)(sambandhaḥ)(tayoḥ, 6th d.)(vyavasthitaḥ)
(hi*)(-vat* [suff.])(paṅgu-)(andha-)
body.translated_text: 292. If <s>Prakṛti</s> provides [enjoyment] in accordance with [his] desire — this relationship between those two is established like [that of] the lame and the blind.

body.text:
293.
(yadi*)(evam*)(kim* iti*)(api*)(vāñchāyām, f. 7th s.)(iṣṭa-)(satyām, f. 7th s.)(na*)(siddhyati ”sidh IV C. Pr. III p. s.)(prakṛtiḥ, f. 1st s.)(na* eva*)(apekṣate, apa-”īkṣ Pr. III p. s. Āt.)(kiñcit*)(anyat, n. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 293. If this is so, why then, even when a desire for something wished-for is present, does it not succeed? <s>Prakṛti</s> does not depend on anything else whatsoever.

body.text:
294.
(atha*)(yadi*)(kāle, 7th s.)(upabhoga-)(na* eva*)(vikriyā, f. 1st s.)(asya, n. 6th s.)(syāt ”as Opt. III p. s.)(-tvam suff.)(bhoktṛ-)(asya, n. 6th s.)(ca*)(prakṛtiḥ, f.)(upakāriṇī, f.)
body.translated_text: 294. Now, if at the time of enjoyment there is indeed no modification of this [Puruṣa], then his enjoyership (<s>bhoktṛtva</s>) [is questionable]; and [if] <s>Prakṛti</s> is the benefactress —

body.text:
295.
(ca*)(vikriyāyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(sad-bhāve, m. 7th s.)(nityatvam, n. 1st s.)(avahīyate ”hā pass. Pr. III p. s.)(hi*)(vikāraḥ)(anyathātvam, n. 1st s.)(katham*)(tādavastye, n. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 295. And when modification exists [in Puruṣa], [his] eternality is undermined; for transformation is becoming-otherwise — how [can that be] in that [unchanging] state?

body.text:
296.
(matam, n. 1st s.)(syāt ”as Opt. III p. s.)(ādau, m. 7th s.)(buddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(ākārā, f. 1st s.)(viṣaya-)(vivarttate ”vṛt)(puruṣaḥ)(pratipadyate ”pad IV C. Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(artham, m. 2nd s.)(vyavasitam, m. 2nd s.)(tayā, f. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 296. The doctrine would be: first, <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), having the form [of objects], transforms [in accordance with] sense objects; [then] <s>Puruṣa</s> apprehends the object determined by her.

body.text:
297.
(ca*)(evam*)(asya, m. 6th s.)(-tā suff.)(upabhoktṛ-)(dvārā, f. 1st s.)(udaya-)(pratibimba-)(tu*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(puruṣaḥ)(na*)(kadācana*)(jahāti ”hā 3rd C. Pr. III p. s.)(svarūpam, 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 297. And thus, his status as enjoyer (<s>upabhoktṛtā</s>) is through the door of reflection (<s>pratibimba</s>) arising [in buddhi]; but this <s>Puruṣa</s> never abandons his own nature.

body.text:
298.
(ucyate ”vac pass. Pr. III p. s.)(pratibimbasya, n. 6th s.)(samudbhave, 7th s.)(tādātmyena, 3rd s.)(tu*)(vibhede, 7th s.)(na*)(-tā suff.)(bhoktṛ-)
body.translated_text: 298. [We] reply: upon the arising of a reflection, [if Puruṣa is identical with it] through identity (<s>tādātmya</s>), then enjoyership [follows]; but if [there is] difference [between Puruṣa and the reflection], then enjoyership does not [follow].

body.text:
299.
(pradhānam, n. 1st s.)(sampravarttate; sam-pra-”vṛt Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(bhede, m. 7th s.)(vicitra-)(racanā-)(ānukūlyena, n. 3rd s.)(didṛkṣā-)(ādi-)(katham*)(vā*)(ātmakam, n. 1st s.)(a-cetanā-)
body.translated_text: 299. How does <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter), being non-conscious (<s>acetana</s>), set forth [its products] with variegated arrangement favorable to the desire to see (<s>didṛkṣā</s>) and so forth?

body.text:
300.
(nāma*)(pradhanam, n. 1st s.)(prajānāti ”jñā)(kartum* ”kṛ)(vyañjana-)(ādikam, m. 2nd s.)(ca*)(na*)(vijānāti ”jñā)(bhoktum* ”bhuj)(ataḥ*)(kim, n. 1st s.)(a-yuktam, n. 1st s.)(param, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 300. Can <s>Pradhāna</s> indeed know how to prepare condiments and the like? And [it] does not know [how] to enjoy [them]. Therefore, what greater absurdity [could there be]?

body.text:
301.
(cet*)(-tvāt suff.)(pradhānasya, n. 6th s.)(-mat- suff.)(buddhi-)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(a-viroddhi, n. 1st s.)(asya, n. 6th s.)(tu*)(-mat-tvena, n. 3rd s.)(buddhi-)(caitanyam, n. 1st s.)(prāptam, n. 1st s.)(iva*)(caitanyam, n. 1st s.)(puruṣu, m. 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 301. If, because <s>Pradhāna</s> possesses <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), all [this] is non-contradictory — but by [its] possessing <s>buddhi</s>, consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>) is as if obtained [by Pradhāna], [just as] consciousness [is held to exist] in <s>Puruṣas</s>.

body.text:
302.
(hi*)(buddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(adhyavasāyaḥ)(saṃvit, f. 1st s.)(saṃvedanam, n. 1st s.)(saṃvittiḥ, f. 1st s.)(ca*)(cetanā, f. 1st s.)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(vācakam, n. 1st s.)(caitanya-)
body.translated_text: 302. For <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>adhyavasāya</s> (determination), <s>saṃvit</s> (cognition), <s>saṃvedana</s> (awareness), <s>saṃvitti</s> (perception), and <s>cetanā</s> (consciousness) — all these are designations of <s>caitanya</s> (consciousness).

body.text:
303.
(buddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(a-cetanā-)(ātmikā, f. 1st s.)(-vat* suff.)(śabda-)(gandha-)(rasa-)(ādi-)(hetubhyām, m. 5th d.)(utpattimattva-)(nāśitva-)(iti*)(cet*)(matam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 303. If [you say] <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) is of non-conscious nature, like sound, smell, taste, and so forth — because it possesses origination and destruction as [its] two causes — [then we reply]:

body.text:
304.
(etau, m. 1st d.)(hetū, m. 1st d.)(sva-tantre, 1st d.)(na*)(siddhau, 1st d.)(dvayoḥ, 6th d.)(mate, n. 1st d.)(sādhane, n. 1st d.)(na*)(bādhā)(viparya-)(prasaṅgaḥ)(abhidhitsate; abhi-”dhā desid. Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(api*)
body.translated_text: 304. These two reasons are not established in your own system; [and] if the two proofs are accepted, there is no obstruction — [but] the undesirable consequence of the reverse also arises [for you].

body.text:
305.
(ca*)(na*)(kṣatiḥ, f.)(naḥ, 6th pl.)(api*)(niveśe, 7th s.)(śabdasya, m. 6th s.)(ātma-)(caitanye, n. 7th s.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(nityatvam, n. 1st s.)(duḥsādhyam, n. 1st s.)(-tva-taḥ* [-tas suff.])(akṣi-)(ādeḥ, m. 6th s.)(sa-phala-)
body.translated_text: 305. And there is no loss for us even in the attribution to sound of the nature of consciousness; its permanence is difficult to establish, because of its nature — like the eye and so forth, which are fruitful.

body.text:
306.
(yadi*)(caitanyam, n. 1st s.)(śāśvatam, n. 1st s.)(artha-)(akṣi-)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(a-phalam, n. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū Opt.)(na*)(arthaḥ)(indhanena, n. 3rd s.)(yadi*)(analaḥ)(syāt ”as Opt. III p. s.)(śāśvataḥ)
body.translated_text: 306. If consciousness were eternal, the eye and so forth, along with objects, would be fruitless; there would be no purpose — just as if fire were eternal, there would be no [need for] fuel.

body.text:
307.
(punaḥ*)(cakṣus-)(ādīnām, 6th pl.)(pārārthyam, n. 1st s.)(pratipādyate; prati-”pad caus. pass.)(tena ... hetunā, m. 3rd s.)(-tvena, n. 3rd s. [-tva suff.])(saṃghāta-)(-vat* suff.)(śayyā-)(āśana-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 307. Furthermore, the other-directedness of the eye and so forth is established; by that very reason, as being of the nature of an assemblage — like a bed, seat, and so forth.

body.text:
308.
(upapādyate ”pad IV C. pass. Pr. III p. s.)(eṣām, 6th pl.)(atiśaya-)(arthatvam, n. 1st s.)(ādheya-)(yat, n. 1st s.)(iṣṭa-siddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(te, m. 1st pl.)(iṣṭāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(asmābhiḥ, 3rd pl.)(upakāriṇaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(jñāna-)
body.translated_text: 308. It is demonstrated that these have a surplus purpose; that which is to be established — the desired accomplishment — [is this]: those are acknowledged by us as auxiliaries in the production of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge).

body.text:
309.
(sādhane, 7th s.)(upakāritva-)(a-vikāri-)(sādhya-)(śunyatā, f. 1st s.)(te, m. 1st pl.)(yuktāḥ, m. 1st s.)(dṛṣṭāntasya, m. 6th s.)(upakāriṇaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(calasya, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 309. In the production [of knowledge], their being auxiliaries, being unchanging — the emptiness of the object to be established: they are fitting as auxiliaries; of the example that is unstable.

body.text:
310.
However (tu*)(yadi*)(samprasādhyate sam-pra-”sādh caus. pass. Pr. III p. s.)(sāmānyena, 3rd s.)(eṣām, 6th pl.)(pārārthyam)(tathā* api*)(sādhanam, n. 1st s.)(vyartham, n. 1st s.)(siddhāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(upayoginaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(citta-)
body.translated_text: 310. However, if their other-directedness is established merely in general, even so the proof is futile; [for] the auxiliaries of <s>citta</s> (mind) are [already] established.

body.text: The Doctrine of the `Soul' according to the Digambara Jainas
body.translated_text: The Doctrine of the 'Soul' according to the Digambara Jainas

body.text:
311.
(jaināḥ, m. 1st pl.)(iva*)(jaiminīyāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(prāhuḥ ”ah Pr. III p. pl.)(naram, m. 2nd s.)(lakṣaṇam, m. 2nd s.)(cit-)(rūpeṇa, 3rd s.)(paryāya-)(dravya-)(anugama-)(-ātmakam, n. 1st s.)(rūpeṇa, 3rd s.)(paryāya-)(vyāvṛtti-)(-ātmakam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 311. The <s>Jainas</s>, like the <s>Jaiminīyas</s>, declare the person to have the characteristic of being in its nature one of continuity in <s>dravya</s> (substance) with the form of consciousness, and in its nature one of exclusion in <s>paryāya</s> (mode).

body.text:
312.
(tatra*)(api*)(yadi*)(a-vikṛtam)(dravyam, n. 1st s.)(saṅgatam, n. 1st s.)(paryāyaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(asti)(na*)(viśeṣaḥ)(iti*)(na*)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(parināmi, n. 1st s. [-in suff.])
body.translated_text: 312. In that case too, if the <s>dravya</s> (substance) is unmodified and conjoined with <s>paryāyas</s> (modes), there would be no distinction, and it would not be transforming (<s>parināmin</s>).

body.text:
313.
(ucyate ”vac pass. Pr. III p. s.)(ekatā, f. 1st s.)(a-bhedāt, m. 5th s.)(deśa-)(kāla-)(śvabhāvānām, m. 6th pl.)(tu*)(bhedaḥ)(bhedāt, m. 5th s.)(saṅkhyā-)(lakṣaṇa-)(saṃjñā-)(artha-)
body.translated_text: 313. It is said [that there is] oneness because of non-difference of place, time, and nature; but difference because of the difference of number, characteristic, designation, and purpose.

body.text:
314.
(iti*)(ghataḥ, m. 1st s.)(rūpa-)(ādayaḥ, 1st pl.)(vibheditā, f. 1st s.)(saṅkhyā-)(saṃjñā-)(vibheditā, f. 1st s.)(lakṣaṇa-)(anuvṛtti-)(kārya-)(artha-)(vyāvṛtti-)
body.translated_text: 314. Thus a pot, color, and so forth — differentiated by number and designation, differentiated by characteristic — [have] continuity of function and exclusion of purpose.

body.text:
315.
(evam*)(dravya-)(paryāyayoḥ, m. 6th d.)(dravyam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(ekāntena, n. 3rd s.)(a-viśeṣa-vat, n. 1st s.)(svayam*)(yāti ”yā Pr. III p. s.)(viśeṣam, m. 2nd s.)(rūpeṇa, n. 3rd s.)(paryāya-)
body.translated_text: 315. Thus, regarding <s>dravya</s> (substance) and <s>paryāya</s> (mode): the substance is not absolutely without distinction; it itself goes to distinction in the form of <s>paryāya</s> (mode).

body.text:
316.
(ca*)(tasmin, 7th s.)(ekatvam)(a-bhede, m. 7th s.)(svabhāva-)(sati, 7th s.)(bhinnatā, f. 1st s.)(duḥsādhyā, f. 1st s.)(kathamcit* api*)(-vat* suff.)(rūpa-)(paryāya-)(ātma-)
body.translated_text: 316. And in that [case], oneness in non-difference of nature being granted, [yet] differentiation is difficult to establish — even in some manner — like color in the form of the <s>paryāya</s> (mode) of the self.

body.text:
317.
(ca*)(ekatve, n. 7th s.)(evam*)(dravya-)(paryāyayoḥ, m. 6th d.)(a-gauṇe, n. 7th s.)(dravyam, n. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(-mat, n. 1st s.)(vyāvṛtti-)(-vat suff.)(svarūpa-)(paryāyāṇām, m. 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 317. And if there is oneness of <s>dravya</s> (substance) and <s>paryāya</s> (mode) in a non-figurative sense, the substance would possess exclusion — like the own-nature of <s>paryāyas</s> (modes).

body.text:
318.
(vā*)(yadi*)(te, m. 1st pl.)(paryāyāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(api*)(anugata-)(ātmakāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(-vat* suff.)(dravya-)(eka-ātma-tā, f. 1st s.)(eṣām, m. 6th pl.)(dravyeṇa, n. 3rd s.)(prāpnuvanti; pra-”āp Pr. III p. pl.)
body.translated_text: 318. Or, if those <s>paryāyas</s> (modes) are also of the nature of continuity — like the oneness of <s>dravya</s> (substance) in self — they would attain [identity] with the substance.

body.text:
319.
(tataḥ*)(vidyate ”vid IV C. Pr. III p. s.)(avasthitam, n. 1st s.)(dravyam, n. 1st s.)(ātmā-)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(-tvāt suff.)(a-vyatirikta-)(paryāya-)(-vat* suff.)(sva-rūpa-)(paryāyāṇām, m. 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 319. Therefore, the permanent <s>dravya</s> (substance) exists — being the self and so forth — like <s>paryāyas</s> (modes) that are non-different, with the own-nature of the <s>paryāyas</s>.

body.text:
320.
(ca*)(na*)(kecana*)(paryāyāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(api*)(ākrāntāḥm. 1st pl.)(udaya-)(vyaya-)(-tvāt suff.)(a-vyatirikta-)(dravyāt, n. 5th s.)(-vat* suff.)(niyata-)(dravya-)
body.translated_text: 320. And no <s>paryāyas</s> (modes) whatsoever are [truly] attained, because of [their] nature of arising and perishing — like [being] non-different from the substance, with a fixed substance.

body.text:
321.
(tataḥ*)(vā*)(dhvaṃsaḥ)(vā* [trans. twice])(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(sthiram, n. 1st s.)(tu*)(imau, m. 1st d.)(vyāvṛtti-)(anugamau, m. 1st d.)(na* eva*)(staḥ ”as Pr. III p. d.)(eka-ātmani, n. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 321. Therefore, either everything is destroyed, or everything is permanent; these two — exclusion and continuity — do not exist in a single self.

body.text:
322.
(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(na*)(pratibhāsaḥ)(dravyasya, n. 6th s.)(rūpasya, n. 6th s.)(upalabhya-)(ātmanaḥ, n. 6th s.)(anugata-)(paryāya-)(tat*)(na*)(asti ”as)(-vat* suff.)(gagana-)(abja-)
body.translated_text: 322. There is no appearance of substance in the form of something apprehensible; the continuous <s>paryāya</s> (mode) — that does not exist — like a sky-lotus.

body.text:
323.
(yogyāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(vividha-)(artha-kriyā)(hetavaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(jñāna-)(tulya-)(ādi-)(gocarāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(pratyaya-)(saṅketa-)(śabda-)(tathā*)(artha-)
body.translated_text: 323. [Things are] capable of various purposeful activities, being causes; having the same scope as cognition and so forth — designation, convention, word, and likewise object.

body.text:
324.
(eva*)(paryāyāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(kevalāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(samvedyante ”vid caus. pass. Pr. III p. pl.)(dharmāṇaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(udaya-)(vyaya-)(tataḥ*)(atinirmalam, n. 1st s.)(nairātmyam, n. 1st s.)(spaṣṭam, 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 324. Only the <s>paryāyas</s> (modes) alone are experienced as <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) of arising and perishing; therefore <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness) is supremely pure and evident.

body.text:
325.
(atha*)(sat, n. 1st s.)(mūrchitam, n. 1st s.)(rūpam, n. 1st s.)(dravya-)(paryāyayoḥ, m. 6th d.)(hi*)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(dvi-rūpam, n. 1st s.)(nirbhāgam, n. 1st s.)(narasiṃha-vat*)
body.translated_text: 325. Now, if the form is maintained as real in both <s>dravya</s> (substance) and <s>paryāya</s> (mode) — it is desired as having two forms, indivisible — like a man-lion (<s>narasiṃha</s>).

body.text:
326.
(nanu*)(eva*)(iti*)(dvi-rūpam, n. 1st s.)(vinibandhanaḥ, m. 1st s.)(nānā-)(artha-)(nirdeśaḥ)(śabdena, m. 3rd s.)(rūpa-)(svabhāvasya, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 326. Indeed, thus the two-formed [nature] is the basis; the explanation of diverse meanings is through words — of that which has the nature of form.

body.text:
327.
(narasiṃhaḥ)(api*)(na* eva*)(ekaḥ)(dvi-ātmakaḥ)(hi*)(saḥ)(pratīyate, prati-”i, pass. Pr. III p. s.)(tathā*)(ātmā, m. 1st s.)(samūha-)(aneka-)(aṇu-)
body.translated_text: 327. Even a <s>Narasiṃha</s> (man-lion) is not truly one, for he is of dual nature; likewise the <s>ātman</s> (self) is apprehended [as] an aggregate of many atoms.

body.text: The Advaita Doctrine of the Soul
body.translated_text: The Advaita Doctrine of the Soul

body.text:
328.
(apare, m. 1st pl.)(punaḥ*)(iti*)(kṣiti-)(tejas-)(jala-)(ādikaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vivarttaḥ)(nitya-)(jñāna-)(ātmā, 1st s.)(tad-)(ātmakaḥ)(ātmakaḥ)
body.translated_text: 328. Others again [say] thus: earth, fire, water, and so forth are transformations; [the self is] of the nature of eternal consciousness — composed of that.

body.text:
329.
(na* kiñcit*)(iha*)(saṃyuktam)(lakṣaṇa-)(grāhya-)(tasmāt, 5th s.)(sarvaḥ)(samīkṣyate ”īkṣ pass.)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(parināmaḥ)(vijñāna-)
body.translated_text: 329. Nothing here is connected; it is apprehensible by its characteristics; therefore all this is regarded as a transformation of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness).

body.text:
330.
(tu*)(darśanam, n. 1st s.)(teṣām, m. 6th pl.)(alpa-)(aparādham, n. 1st s.)(uktitaḥ* [-tas suff.])(nityatā, f. 1st s. [-tā suff.])(upalakṣaṇāt, n. 5th s.)(bheda-)(vyaktam [adv.])(vijñāne, n. 7th s.)(rūpa-)(śabda-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 330. But their view has a small fault: from [their own] statement, permanence — since from the characteristic, clearly in consciousness — form, sound, and so forth.

body.text:
331.
(tu*)(ātmakatve, n. 7th s.)(eka-)(jñāna-)(rūpa-)(śabda-)(rasa-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(prasajyate ”sañj pass.)(vedyāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(sakṛt*)(ca*)(nitye, m. 7th s.)(na*)(antaram, n. 1st s.)(avasthā-)
body.translated_text: 331. But if [they are] of the nature of a single consciousness — form, sound, taste, and so forth would be apprehensible simultaneously; and in what is permanent, there would be no interval of states.

body.text:
332.
(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(upalabhyate ”labh pass.)(bhinnam, n. 2nd s.)(vittitaḥ* [-tas suff.])(rūpa-)(ādi-)(bhede, 7th s.)(tasyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(prati-kṣaṇam, n. 2nd s.)(kim, n. 1st s.)(vyavasthitam, n. 1st s.)(a-bhinnam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 332. <s>Jñāna</s> (knowledge) is not apprehended as different from awareness; [yet] in the difference of form and so forth, is that [knowledge] established moment by moment, or is it undifferentiated?

body.text:
333.
(vidyate ”vid IV C. Pr. III p. s.)(na*)(bhedaḥ)(jñāna-)(viparyasta-)(a-viparyasta-)(puṃsi, 7th s.)(eka-)(jñāna-)(katham*)(tataḥ*)(bandha-)(mokṣau, m. 1st d.)
body.translated_text: 333. There is no difference in knowledge — in one who is deluded or undeluded; with a single knowledge, how then [can there be] bondage and liberation?

body.text:
334.
(vā*)(kim*)(yogī, m. 1st s.)(nivartayet ”vṛt Opt. III p. s.)(sādhayet ”siddh, caus. Opt. III p. s.)(abhyāsena, m. 3rd s.)(vā*)(na*)(śakyaḥ)(hātum* ”hā)(hi*)(viparyāsa-)(ātmakaḥ)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 334. Or what — should the <s>yogin</s> turn away [from delusion], or accomplish [liberation] through practice? Or is it not possible to abandon [that which is] of the nature of delusion? In that case —

body.text:
335.
(ca*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(tattva-)(na*)(utpādyam [gerundive])(sarvadā*)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(abhyāsaḥ, m. 1st s.)(yoga-)(api*)(a-phalaḥ)(ca*)(sarvaḥ)(eva*)
body.translated_text: 335. And knowledge of reality is not producible at any time; therefore this practice, and <s>yoga</s> as well, is entirely fruitless.

body.text: The Doctrine of the `Soul' according to the Vātsīyaputrīyas
body.translated_text: The Doctrine of the 'Soul' according to the <s>Vātsīputrīyas</s>

body.text:
336.
(tu*)(kecit*)(api*)(manyāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(saugatam, m. 2nd s.)(pracakṣate ”cakṣ Pr. III p. pl. Āt.)(ātmānam, n. 2nd s.)(vyapadeśena, m. 3rd s.)(pudgala-)(varjitam, n. 2nd s.)(tattva-)(anyatva-)
body.translated_text: 336. But some, though claiming to be Buddhist, declare the self by the designation '<s>pudgala</s>' (person) — devoid of identity and difference with [the <s>skandhas</s>].

body.text:
337.
(pudgalaḥ)(skandhebhyaḥ, m. 5th pl.)(prasaṅgataḥ* [-tas suff.])(dṛṣṭi-)(na*)(an-anyaḥ = non-different)(prāpteḥ, f. 5th s.)(an-ekatā, f. 1st s. [ `being not-one'])(ādya-)(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(sādhvī, f. 1st s.)(avācyatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 337. The <s>pudgala</s> (person), because of the consequence of the view of [substantial] reality, is not different from the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates); from the impossibility [of real identity], there is non-oneness; therefore the first [option — identity] is valid: inexpressibility.

body.text:
338.
(te, m. 1st pl.)(vācyāḥ, m. 1st pl. [gerundive])(pudgalaḥ)(na* eva*)(vidyate ”vid IV C. Pr. III p. s.)(pāramārthikaḥ)(-tvāt suff.n. 5th s.)(a-vācya-)(tattva-)(anyatvāt, n. 5th s.)(-vat* suff.)(nabhas- `sky'; kokanada- `lotus')(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 338. They should be told: the <s>pudgala</s> (person) does not ultimately exist, because of its being inexpressible in terms of identity or difference — like the sky, a red lotus, and so forth.

body.text:
339.
(na* eva*)(ativarttate ”vṛt)(vā*)(an-anyatvam)(vā*-api*)(anyatvam, n. 1st s.)(vastu, n. 1st s.)(vastutaḥ*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(yat, n. 1st s.)(nir-rūpam = nīrūpam, n. 1st s.)(prakalpyate ”kḷp)(a-vācyam, n. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 339. It neither transcends non-identity nor identity either; a thing, in reality, that which has no form — what is imagined as inexpressible,

body.text:
340.
(bhāvataḥ* [-tas suff.])(adhiṣṭhāna-)(vastu-)(vikalpasya, m. 6th s.)(bheda-)(abheda-)(yujyate ”yuj pass. Pr. III p. s.)(a-nirdeśaḥ)(anyatva-)(tattva-)(niḥsvabhāveṣu, m. 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 340. From the point of view of reality, the non-expression of difference and non-difference is fitting [only] in those that are devoid of intrinsic nature — with respect to the substratum, the real thing, and conceptual construction.

body.text:
341.
(na*)(vastuni, n. 7th s.)(yat, n. 1st s.)(pratiṣedhanam, n. 1st s.)(etat, n. 1st s.)(hi*)(na*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(vastu, n. 1st s.)(-vat*)(antara-)(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(anyatvam, n. 1st s.)(vyaktam, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(ucyate ”vac pass. Pr. III p. s.)
body.translated_text: 341. [When] something that is not a real thing is negated — that indeed is not [of the nature of] a real thing; like another [entity]; therefore its otherness is clearly stated.

body.text:
342.
(ca*)(niṣedhaḥ)(a-tad-bhāva-)(tattvam, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(abhidhīyate ”dhā pass.)(tat*)(vastu, n. 1st s.)(na*)(atikrāmati ”kram I C. Pr. III p. s.)(bhedam, 2nd s.)(ca*)(tattvam, n. 2nd s.)(vastunaḥ, n. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 342. And the negation of the state of being 'not that' is declared to be its very reality; that real thing does not go beyond difference; and [difference is] the reality of the thing.

body.text:
343.
(eṣā, f. 1st s.)(iti*)(pudgalaḥ)(na*)(anyaḥ)(skandhebhyaḥ, m. 5th pl.)(sūcanā, f. 1st s.)(an-anya-)(iyam, f. 1st s.)(iti*)(skandhaḥ)(na*)(pudgalaḥ)(vyaktā, f. 1st s.)(tasya, m 6th s.)(anyatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 343. This [is the position]: the <s>pudgala</s> (person) is not different from the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) — [that is] the indication; and this: the <s>skandha</s> (aggregate) is not the <s>pudgala</s> (person) — its otherness is manifest.

body.text:
344.
(saṅgaḥ)(viruddha-)(dharma-)(ucyate ”vac pass. Pr. III p. s.)(bhedaḥ)(vastūnām, n. 6th pl.)(ca*)(kim*)(na*)(bhinnatā, f. 1st s.)(vidyate ”vid IV C.)(pudgalayoḥ, m. 6th d.)(skandha-)(eva*)
body.translated_text: [Verse 344] The connection of contradictory properties is called differentiation of things. Is there no difference between the <s>pudgala</s> (person) and the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates)?

body.text:
345.
(tathā* hi*)(pudgalaḥ)(ucyate ”vac)(avācyaḥ)(anyatvena, n. 3rd s)(tattva-)(vedana-)(ādibhyaḥ, m. 5th pl.)(rūpa-)(saṃjñā-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(vācyāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(tataḥ*)
body.translated_text: [Verse 345] For the <s>pudgala</s> is said to be inexpressible as identical with the reality of <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) and the rest; <s>rūpa</s> (form), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), and the rest are expressible. Therefore,

body.text:
346.
(rūpa-skandha-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(matāḥ, 1st pl.)(vācyāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(a-nityatvena, n. 3rd s.)(tu*)(pudgalaḥ)(na*)(tathā*)(iti* tataḥ*)(anyatā, f. 1st s.)(vispaṣṭam, n. 2nd s. [adv.])
body.translated_text: [Verse 346] the aggregate of <s>rūpa</s> (form) and the rest are held to be expressible as impermanent; but the <s>pudgala</s> is not so — thus the difference is manifest.

body.text:
347.
(śaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(lakṣaṇam, 1st s.)(vidyamānatva-)(niyatā, f. 1st s.)(kṣaṇikeṣu, 7th pl.)(eva*)(tathā*)(a-vācye, m. 7th s.)(na*)(vastutā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: [Verse 347] <s>Śakti</s> (capacity) is the defining characteristic, determined [only] in existing things, only in momentary [entities]. In what is inexpressible, there is no real existence.

body.text:
348.
(tu*)(virodhe, m. 7th s.)(āgama-)(artha-)(parākrāntam, n. 1st s.)(mahātmabhiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(citrāḥ, 1st pl.)(vācaḥ, f. 1st pl.)(dayāvataḥ, m. 6th s.)(pratiṣedhāya, m. 4th s.)(nāstikya-)
body.translated_text: [Verse 348] But in [the face of] contradiction, the great souls, out of compassion, have exerted themselves upon the meaning of scripture, [speaking] variegated words for the prohibition of nihilism.

body.text:
349.
(deśanā, f. 1st s.)(hāra-)(bhāra-)(ādi-)(samudāya-)(ādi-)(cittena, m. 3rd s.)(ca*)(viśeṣa-)(pratiṣedhaḥ)(rājate ”rāj Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(prati*)(dṛṣṭīn, f. 2nd pl.)(tat-)
body.translated_text: [Verse 349] The teaching shines forth as a prohibition of specific [wrong] views through the mind [contemplating] aggregates of necklaces, burdens, and the like regarding those [views].

body.text:
350.
(athavā*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(āyāsaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kriyate ”kṛ pass.)(eva*)(asthānaḥ)(yataḥ*)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(prakṛti-)(nirākṛtam, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(prasiddhyā, f. 3rd s.)(kṣaṇa-bhaṅga-)
body.translated_text: [Verse 350] Or rather, this effort is simply misplaced, since <s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s> (momentary destruction) has already been refuted from the beginning by [its] own nature through established [convention].

body.text:
351.
(tataḥ)(kṣaṇa-bhaṅgaḥ)(spaṣṭam*)(prasādhyate ”sādh caus. pass.)(niṣedhāya, m. 4th s.)(uktasya, m. 6th s.)(ca*)(jāti-)(ādeḥ, m. 6th s.)(vakṣyamāṇasya)(a-viśeṣataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: [Verse 351] Therefore, <s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s> (momentary destruction) is clearly established. And for the refutation of the stated [objections of] universal counter-argument (<s>jāti</s>) and the like, what will be said [later] applies without distinction.

396.

body.translated_text: 396. But even if the permanent [entity] has sequential co-operative conditions, depending on which it produces the collection of effects in sequence —

body.text:
397.
(etat, n. 1st s.)(sādhu, n. 1st s.)(kiṃtu*)(te, m. 1st pl.)(bhavanti ”bhū Pr. III p. pl.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(sahakāriṇaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(kim*)(hetutvāt, n. 5th s.)(yogya-rūpa-)(vā*)(karaṇena, n. 3rd s.)(ekārtha-)
body.translated_text: 397. This is well [argued], but do those become its co-operative conditions because of their being causes, or by making it assume a suitable form for a single purpose?

body.text:
398.
(hetutve, 7th s.)(yogya-rūpasya, 6th s.)(saḥ)(bhāvaḥ)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(kṛtaḥ)(taiḥ, 3rd pl.)(ca*)(saḥ)(aśakya-)(kriyaḥ)(yasmāt, n. 5th s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(tadā*)(sthitam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 398. If [they contribute] a suitable form for being a cause, that state would be produced by them; and since that [form] cannot be produced [in what is permanent], the [permanent entity] then remains [unchanged].

body.text:
399.
(vā*)(svarūpasya, 6th s.)(tat-)(kṛtau, f. 7th s.)(asya, m. 6th s.)(nityatā, f. 1st s.)(avahīyate ”hā pass.)(yadi*)(atiśayaḥ)(vibhinnaḥ)(tasmāt, m. 5th s.)(katham*)(asau, n. 1st s.)(kārakaḥ)
body.translated_text: 399. Or, if its intrinsic nature is produced by those, its permanence is lost; and if a distinction is different from it, how can it be an agent?

body.text:
400.
(hi*)(utpādaḥ)(kāryāṇām, n. 6th pl.)(tasmin, m. 7th s.)(sati, m. 7th s.)(an-utpādāt, 5th s.)(tat-)(a-bhāvataḥ* [-tas suff.])(evam*)(saḥ)(eva*)(vyavasthitaḥ, 1st s.)(hetutvena, m. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 400. For the production of effects [occurs] when that [cause] is present; when it is absent, there is non-production. Thus, it is established in its causality in this very way.

body.text:
401-402.
(atha* api*)(sambandhāt, m. 5th s.)(hetutā, f. 1st s.)(asti ”as)(eva*)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(eva*)(api*)(kaḥ)(sambandhaḥ)(iṣṭaḥ)(tayaḥ, n. 6th d.)(tādātmyena, n. 3rd s.)(vibhedataḥ* [-tas suff.])(na*)(ca*)(utpattiḥ)(tat-)(prasaṅgataḥ* [-tas suff.])(yaugapadyam, n. 1st s.)(tataḥ*)(ca*)(udayaḥ)(kāryāṇām, n. 6th pl.)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(yaugapadyena, 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 401-402. But even if causality exists through connection — what connection is desired between those two? Not through identity, nor through difference — for there is no origination; from that consequence, simultaneity [would follow]; and then the arising of effects would be simultaneous.

body.text:
403.
(tatra*)(vyapekṣāyām, f. 7th s.)(api*)(anya-)(prasajyate ”sañj pass.)(anavashtā, f. 1st s.)(tataḥ*)(a-sambandhāt, m. 5th s.)(kāryam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(prakalpyate ”kḷp pass.)(ekadā*)
body.translated_text: 403. Even in the case of mutual dependence there, another infinite regress follows; therefore, from the absence of connection, an effect is not constructed [from a permanent cause] at once.

body.text:
404-405.
(cet*)(sambandhaḥ)(cet*)(samavāyaḥ)(api*)(vicintyate ”cint pass.)(evam*)(tatra*)(kim*)(saḥ)(samavāyī, m. 1st s.)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass. Pr. III p. s.)(upakārībhavan, m. 1st s.)(na* vā*)(tathā*)(yadi*)(prathamaḥ)(vikalpaḥ)(gṛhyate ”grah pass.)(prāptā, f. 1st s.)(sā eva*)(utpattiḥ, f. 1st s.)(tat-)(sā, f. 1st s.)(api* anantaram*)(vyapāstā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 404-405. If <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) is considered as the connection — then what is considered there? Is the inherer [i.e., samavāya] a contributor or not? If the first alternative is accepted, that same origination [follows]; and that too has been subsequently refuted.

body.text:
406.
(yadi*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(mataḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(upakārī, m. 1st s.)(tasya, 6th s.)(anye, 1st pl.)(sarva-bhāvāḥ, 1st pl.)(syuḥ ”as Opt. III p. pl.)(samavāyinaḥ, 1st pl.)(api*)(a-viśeṣāt, 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 406. If this [samavāya] is held to be not a contributor, then all entities would be its inherents too, because of the absence of distinction.

body.text:
407.
(pratyekam*)(vikalpasya, 6th s.)(bheda-)(abheda-)(tasya, 6th s.)(vastunaḥ, 6th s.)(atiśayaḥ)(dvi-rūpaḥ)(bhavati ”bhū)(vyastaḥ)
body.translated_text: 407. The distinction of that real thing — of difference and non-difference — the surplus is of two forms, in each alternative, analyzed separately.

body.text:
408.
(parīkṣāsu, f. 7th s.)(ādi-)(dvairāśya-)(pratiṣedhanāt, 5th s.)(atiśayaḥ)(na* asti ”as)(dvi-rūpaḥ)(ātmakaḥ)(an-ubhaya-)(ubhaya-)
body.translated_text: 408. From the negation of dual nature in the investigations, the surplus that is of two forms does not exist — neither as both nor as neither.

body.text:
409.
(atha*)(nityaḥ)(na*)(apekṣate, apa-”īkṣ Pr. III p. s. Āt.)(sahakāriṇaḥ, 1st pl.)(pratyayān, 2nd pl.)(tathā* api*)(viyuktaḥ)(tat-)(na*)(kārakaḥ)(-vat suff.)(antya-hetu-)
body.translated_text: 409. But if the permanent [entity] does not depend on co-operative conditions — even so, separated from those, it is not an agent; like the final cause.

body.text:
410.
(tasya, 6th s.)(nijaḥ)(svabhāvaḥ)(kārakatva-mataḥ, 6th s.)(eva*)(sannidhau, 7th s.)(teṣām, 6th pl.)(hi*)(api*)(tat-)(sadbhāve, 7th s.)(na*)(sarvadā*)
body.translated_text: 410. Its own intrinsic nature — the causality of which is held — even in the presence of those, indeed, not always [does it produce].

body.text:
411.
(astu ”as Imperative III p. s.)(evam*)(kimtu*)(cet*)(prakṛtiḥ, f. 1st s.)(tasya)(sākalye, 7th s.; sakala -ya)(matā, f. 1st s.)(eva*)(sā, f. 1st s.)(yā, f. 1st s.)(vaikalye, 7th s.)(sahakāriṇaḥ, 1st pl.)(syuḥ ”as Opt. III p pl.)(iṣṭāḥ, 1st pl.)(nityāḥ, 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 411. Let it be so; but if its nature is held as complete, then that very [nature] which [exists] in the absence [of co-operative conditions] — the co-operative conditions would [need to be] permanent [too, and thus] desired.

body.text:
412.
(teṣām, 6th pl.)(api*)(bhāve, 7th s.)(sthiteḥ, 6th s.)(svabhāvasya, 6th s.)(sambandha-)(tat-)(cet*)(anyat, 1st s.)(vikalam, 1st s.)(ekatvam, n. 1st s.)(avahīyate ”hā pass.)
body.translated_text: 412. Even when they are present, if the intrinsic nature remains [unchanged], that connection [is questionable]; if another [factor] is deficient, the unity [of the permanent entity] is lost.

body.text:
413.
(evam*)(krama-)(udayaḥ)(kāryāṇām, 6th pl.)(na*)(api*)(vyapekṣayā, 3rd s.)(ca*)(yaugapadyam, 1st s.)(na*)(iṣṭam, 1st s.)(eva*)(krama-)(īkṣaṇāt, 5th s.)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 413. Thus, the sequential arising of effects is not [explained] by dependence [on co-operative conditions]; and simultaneity is not desired, from the observation of sequence.

body.text:
414.
(cet*)(arthaḥ)(ātma, m. 1st s.)(sāmarthya-)(nivarttate ”vṛt Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(kṛtvā*)(niḥśeṣāṇi, 2nd pl.)(kāryāṇi, 2nd pl.)(sakṛt*)(asya, 6th s.)(kṣaṇabhaṅgitā, f. 1st s.)(siddhā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 414. If the self, having produced all effects at once, withdraws from causal efficacy — then its momentariness is established.

body.text:
415.
(tu*)(rūpasya, 6th s.)(tat-)(anuvṛtau, 7th s.)(utpādayet ”pad Opt. III p. s.)(kāryam, 2nd s.)(punaḥ*)(katham*)(sāmarthyam, 1st s.)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass. Pr. III p. s.)(rūpasya, 6th s.)(a-)(a-kiñcit-kara-)
body.translated_text: 415. But if that form persists, how can it produce an effect again? A capacity that produces nothing is desired for a form —

body.text:
416.
(sarve, 1st pl.)(asantaḥ, 1st pl.)(a-kṣaṇikāḥ, 1st pl.)(-vat*)(tārā-patha-)(saroja-)(-tvāt, 5th s.)(śūnya-)(sarva-sāmarthya-)(yad)(śaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(lakṣaṇam, 2nd s.)(vastu-)
body.translated_text: 416. All non-momentary [things] are non-existent, like a sky-lotus; being devoid of all power — that which has power as its characteristic is a real thing.

body.text:
417.
(atha*)(lakṣaṇam, 1st s.)(śakti-)(aṅgīkriyate ”kṛ pass. [cvi cpd.])(vastu-tvam, n. 1st s.)(yad evam*)(paraiḥ, 3rd pl.)(nirdiśyam)(anyat, n. 1st s.)(lakṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(vastūnām, 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 417. But if the characteristic of power is accepted as constituting real-thingness — then some other characteristic of real things should be indicated by others.

body.text:
418.
(cet*)(lakṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(vastūnām, 6th pl.)(iṣṭaḥ)(sambandhaḥ)(sattā, f. 1st s.)(tat, 1st s.)(na*)(asiddheḥ, 5th s.)(ādeḥ, 6th s.)(samavāya-)(katham* vā*)(anyaḥ)(lakṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(anya-)
body.translated_text: 418. If the desired connection is that existence (<s>sattā</s>) is the characteristic of real things — that is not [established], because of its non-establishment; of <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) and the rest — how? Or else another characteristic —

body.text:
419.
(ca*)(sarvaḥ)(vyāpāraḥ)(ādi-)(vicāra-)(artha-)(yuktaḥ, 1st s.)(dhiyaḥ)(nirākulu-)(arthinaḥ)(arthakriyā-)(punaḥ*)(na*)(unmattakatayā, f. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 419. And all activity of investigation of meaning and so forth is appropriate for the mind that is unconfused, purposeful; but again, not through the state of being insane.

body.text:
420.
(tatra*)(eva*)(yuktaḥ)(vyavasthitiḥ, f. 1st s.)(sattā, f. 1st s.)(nāma*)(yat, n. 1st s.)(upayujyate ”yuj pass.)(keṣāṃcit*)(kvacit*)(kadācit*)(kathaṃcit*)
body.translated_text: 420. There itself it is appropriate: what is called existence (<s>sattā</s>) is the establishment [of something] that is useful for some [persons], somewhere, at some time, and in some way.

body.text:
421.
(ca*)(eva*)(tad-rūpasya, 6th s.)(arthasya, 6th s.)(prasādhyate ”sādh caus. pass.)(kṣaṇikatvam, 1st s.)(eva*)(eva*)(tasmin, 7th s.)(vyāptiḥ, 1st s.)(upasaṃhārā, f. 1st s.)(sarva-)(abhidhīyate ”dhā pass.)
body.translated_text: 421. And the momentariness of such a real thing is established; for the pervasion in that [is shown]; the universal induction is stated.

body.text:
422.
(śūnyam, 1st s.)(niḥśeṣa-)(śakti-)(sannibham*)(suta-)(vandhyā-)(na* kadācana*)(eti ”i Pr. III p. s.)(hetutvam, n. 1st s.)(api*)(cetasaḥ, 6th s.)(sarva-jña-)
body.translated_text: 422. What is devoid of all power, resembling [the son of] a barren woman, never attains causality — not even for the cognition of the omniscient.

body.text:
423.
(tatra*)(vicakṣaṇaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(a-dṛṣṭitaḥ* [-tas suff.])(kārya-)(rūpa-)(ādi-)(na*)(eva*)(kriyate ”kṛ pass.)(idam, n. 1st s.)(vyavasthānam, n. 1st s.)(astitva-)(nirnibandhanam, 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 423. There, by the discerning, from the non-observation of [any] effect — form and the like — this determination of existence is not made without a basis.

body.text:
424.
(na*)(kaścana*)(arthaḥ)(sādhitena, 3rd s.)(kṣaṇikatvena, 3rd s.)(tasmin, 7th s.)(ca*)(tatra*)(paryanuyogaḥ)(kriyamāṇaḥ)(api*)(niṣphalaḥ)
body.translated_text: 424. No purpose is served by the established momentariness; and in that [context], the objection being raised there is also fruitless.

body.text:
425.
(nanu*)(ādyayaḥ, 1st pl.)(nabhas-tāmarasa-)(śaktā, f. 1st s.)(arthakriyā-)(bhāvena, 3rd s.)(hetu-)(sva-)(jñāna-)(ca*)(ete, m. 1stpl.)(santi ”as Pr. III p. pl.)(na*)(bhāvikāḥ, 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 425. But surely, these first [entities] — sky-lotuses and the like — are incapable of <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy); and by their nature, as causes of their own cognition, these [momentary things] exist and are future.
