470.
(ādeḥ, 6th s.)(jāti-)(niḥsvabhāvatvāt, 5th s.)(na* eva*)(iṣṭāḥ, 1st pl.)(tad*)(sādhanam, n. 1st s.)(nirdiṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(artham, 2nd s.)(prasiddhi-)(abhāva-)(vṛthā*)
body.translated_text: 470. Since the universals and so forth are devoid of intrinsic nature, they are not accepted [by us]; that proof, being directed at an object whose establishment is absent, is futile.

body.text:
471.
(vācyatvam, n. 1st s.)(samāna-)(śabda-)(varttate ”vṛt Pr. III p. s. Āt.)(pratyayeṣu, 7th pl.)(ādi-)(dīpa-)(api*)(tena, 3rd s.)(ataḥ*)(eṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(hetuḥ, m. 1st s.)(bhavati ”bhū)(vyabhicārī, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 471. Expressibility pertains equally to cognitions of lamps and so forth that share the same word; therefore this reason is deviant.

body.text:
472.
(cet*)(sāmānādhikaraṇyam, n. 1st s.)(bādhitam, 1st s.)(kim*)(na*)(vīkṣyate, vi-”īkṣ)(vispaṣṭā, f. 1st s.)(bādhā, f. 1st s.)(eṣā, f. 1st s.)(vivakṣite, 7th s.)(api*)
body.translated_text: 472. If [you say] co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) is not seen to be refuted — this refutation is clear, even regarding what is intended [by the opponent].

body.text:
473.
(dhiyaḥ, 1st pl.)(ārūḍhāḥ, 1st pl.)(padam, 2nd s.)(vivāda-)(na*)(viṣayāḥ, 1st pl.)(eka-artha-)(-tvāt, 5th s.)(utpadyamāna-)(krameṇa, 3rd s.)(-vat*)(buddhi-)(vidyut-)(dīpa-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 473. Cognitions that have reached the stage of dispute are not [concerned with] objects of a single meaning; [they are] like lightning, lamps, and so forth — cognitions arising in sequence.

body.text:
474.
(hi*)(jñāneṣu, 7th pl.)(eka-)(arthabhāviṣu, 7th pl.)(bhāva-)(krama-)(virodhaḥ)(anyaiḥ, 3rd pl.)(a-)(bhedasya, m. 6th s.)(kārya-)(apekṣā-)(tat-)(virodhataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 474. For among cognitions that pertain to a single object, there is a contradiction of the sequence of existence; the contradiction of non-difference, by others, [arises from] the dependence on the effect of that [non-difference].

body.text:
475.
(sarveṣu, 7th pl.)(eteṣu, 7th pl.)(hetuṣu, m. 7th pl.)(sandigdha-)(vyatirekatvam, n. 1st s.)(anupadarśanāt, 5th s.)(bādhaka-)(vipakṣe, 7th s.)(varttamānānām, 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 475. In all these reasons, there is doubtful negative concomitance, from the non-observation of [reasons] that are counterevidence, present in the opposing side.

body.text: Examination of the Relation between Actions and their Results: Action and Reaction
body.translated_text: Examination of the Relation between Actions and their Results: Action and Reaction

body.text:
476.
(cet*)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(vastu, n. 1st s.)(līḍham, 1st s.)(a-nityatā-)(kṣaṇika-)(tat*)(katham*)(sambandha-)(karma-)(tat-phalam, 2nd s.)(-tā suff.)(kāraṇa-)(kārya-)(ādayaḥ, 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 476. If everything is momentary, consumed by impermanence — then how [can there be] the connection of <s>karma</s> (action) and its fruit, [or] the relations of cause and effect and so forth?

body.text:
477.
(kuśala-ādīnām, 6th pl.)(asau, m. 1st s.)(kṣaṇaḥ)(yaḥ)(avakalpyate ”kḷp pass.)(kartṛtvena, 3rd s.)(na* eva*)(anuvarttate ”vṛt Pr. III p. s. Āt.)(kāle, 7th s.)(prasava-)(phala-)
body.translated_text: 477. That moment of wholesome [action] and so forth which is conceived as the agent does not continue until the time of the ripening of the fruit.

body.text:
478.
(ca*)(karma, n. 1st s.)(na* eva*)(kṛtam, 1st s.)(tena, 3rd s.)(kṣaṇaḥ, m. 1st s.)(yaḥ)(saṃvarṇyate ”varṇ pass. Pr. III p. s.)(bhoktā, m. 1st s. [bhaktṛ stem])(phalasya, 6th s.)(prasūtau, 7th s.)(tasya, 6th s.)(asambhavāt, 5th s.)(pūrvam, 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 478. And the <s>karma</s> (action) was not performed by that moment which is described as the experiencer of the fruit, since at the time of ripening, [the original moment] does not exist, [having perished] before.

body.text:
479.
(evam*)([a-])(eka-)(kartṛ-)(a-parigrahāt, 5th s.)(karma-)(tat-phalayoh, 6th d.)(āsaktā, f. 1st s.)(nāśa-)(kṛta-)(prāptiḥ, 1st s.)(akṛta-)(ati-)(virodhinī, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 479. Thus, since there is no apprehension of a single agent [for both action and result], the connection of <s>karma</s> (action) and its fruit involves the attainment of what is destroyed and [the fruit of] what was not done — which is extremely contradictory.

body.text:
480.
(tu*)(pakṣe, 7th s.)(vāda-)(nairātmya-)(avabudhyate ”budh pass.)(eva*)(pūrvam, 2nd s.)(vināśāt, 5th s.)(syāt ”as)(na*)(phalam, 1st s.)(vā*)(api*)(bhavet ”bhū Opt.)(anyasya, 6th s.)(mattaḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 480. But on the thesis of <s>nairātmyavāda</s> (the doctrine of selflessness), it is understood that: either the fruit would not exist because of the prior destruction [of the cause], or it would belong to another — [produced] from me.

body.text:
481.
(iti*)(prekṣāvān, m. 1st s.)(na* eva*)(pravartteta ”vṛt Opt. III p. s. Āt.)(ārambhe, 7th s.)(kriyā-)(śubha-)(aśubha-)(lipsayā, f. 3rd s.)(phala-)(phalam, n. 1st s.)(sthitam, 1st s.)(dūrataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 481. Therefore, a discerning person would not engage in wholesome or unwholesome actions out of desire for the fruit; the fruit, being distant, stands [as if unreachable].

body.text:
482.
(anāgataḥ, m. 1st s.)(na* vā*)(atītaḥ)(bhāvaḥ)(kṣamaḥ)(kriyā-)(kārya-)(varttamānaḥ)(api*)(na*)(eva*)(avatiṣṭhate ”sthā Āt.)(tāvantam, 2nd s.)(kālam, 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 482. Neither a future nor a past entity is capable of being the effect of an action; and even a present [entity] does not remain for that [sufficient] length of time.

body.text:
483.
(hi*)(vastu, n. 1st s.)(a-)(labdha-)(ātmakam, n. 1st s.)(kalpyate ”kḷp pass.)(aṅgatva-)(para-)(na*)(vinaṣṭam)(na*)(ca*)(sthānam, 1st s.)(tasya, 6th s.)(kṣamam, n. 1st s.)(kṛti-)(kārya-)
body.translated_text: 483. For a thing that has not attained its own nature is conceived as subsidiary to another; and what has perished — the station of [performing] the effect of action is not possible for it.

body.text:
484.
(ca*)(vināśe, 7th s.)(pūrva-)(kṣaṇa-)(kalpyamane, 7th s.)(niranvaye, 7th s.)(upapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(na*)(utpattiḥ, f. 1st s.)(paścāt*)(tasya, 6th s.)(a-nimittatvāt, 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 484. And when the prior moment is conceived as destroyed, with no continuity, the subsequent arising [of the effect] is not possible, because of the absence of a cause for it.

body.text:
485.
(api*)(nāśa-)(utpāda-)(samatve, 7th s.)(na* eva*)(parasparam*)(apekṣā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(staḥ ”as Pr. III p. d.)(-tve, 1st d.)(kāraṇa-)(kārya-)(an-anugrahāt, 5th s.)(tasya, 6th s.)(vyāpāra-)
body.translated_text: 485. Moreover, when destruction and origination are equal [in status], there is no mutual dependence; [if] there is no cause-effect [relation], because of the absence of the operation of that [cause], the two [would not be related].

body.text:
486.
(gandha-)(ādiḥ, 1st s.)(jāyamānaḥ, 1st s.)(vinaśyati ”naś)(rūpe, 7th s.)(ghaṭa-)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass. Pr. III p. s.)(kāryam, 2nd s.)(tat-)(yadvat*)(antarāṇi, 1st pl.)(rūpa-)(tathā*)
body.translated_text: 486. Smell and so forth, arising, perish in [the domain of] form; just as a pot is held to be the effect of that — so too the intermediate forms.

body.text:
487.
(tasmāt, 5th s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(kāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(yasya, 6th s.)(vyāpāraḥ)(dṛśyate ”paś-dṛś pass.)(prāk-)(niṣpatteḥ, 5th s.)(kārya-)(tu*)(na*)(mātrakam, 2nd s.)(ānantarya-)
body.translated_text: 487. Therefore, that alone is the cause whose operation is seen before the production [of the effect]; but mere immediate succession is not [sufficient to establish causation].

body.text:
488.
(ayam, m 1st s.)(saṃkṣepaḥ)(cet*)(kārya-)(sambhavaḥ)(kāraṇāt, 5th s.)(vinaṣṭāt, 5th s.)(idam, 1st s.)(niṣkāraṇam)(-tvāt suff.)(pradhvastasya, 6th s.)(anupākhyatvāt, 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 488. In brief: if the effect arises from a destroyed cause, this [would be] without a cause — because what has been annihilated has no describable [existence].

body.text:
489.
(ca*)(jātau, 7th s.)(avinaṣṭāt, 5th s.)(tadā*)(sambhavāt, m. 5th s.)(aneka-)(kṣaṇa-)(katham*)(kṣaṇikatvam, n. 1st s.)(bhāvānām, m. 6th pl.)(na*)(vyāhanyeta ”han Opt. III p. s. Āt.)
body.translated_text: 489. And if [the effect arises] from an undestroyed [cause] at the time of production, then since [the cause persists through] multiple moments, how would the momentariness of entities not be contradicted?

body.text:
490.
(cet*)(ghaṭa-)(ādiḥ, 1st s.)(sthāyī, m. 1st s.)(kṣaṇa-)(na*)(upalabhyeta ”labh Opt. III p. s. Āt.)(cakṣusā, 3rd s.)(naṣṭāḥ, 1st pl.)(na*)(pratīyante ”i pass.)(-vat*)(padārtha-)(cira-)(atīta-)
body.translated_text: 490. If a pot and so forth were enduring [for more than] a moment, [they] would not be perceived by the eye; just as long-past objects are not cognized — [so too would persistent objects not be perceived].

body.text:
491.
(api*)(bhāvaḥ)(kāraṇa-)(kārya-)(an-upalambhataḥ* [-tas suff.])(pratyakṣa-)(svabhāva-)(bhāvānām, 6th pl.)(anupalambhanāt, 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 491. Moreover, the causal-effect relation of entities [is established] from the non-apprehension of [their] intrinsic nature by direct perception — from the non-apprehension of entities.

body.text:
492.
(vyavasthitaḥ, 1st s.)(karttā, m. 1st s.)(saṃdhatte ”dhā Pr. III p. s. Āt.)(gatim, 2nd s.)(-vat suff.)(krama-)(asya, 6th s.)(dṛṣṭau, 7th s.)(idam, 1st s.)(dṛṣṭam, 1st s.)(tu*)(asya, 6th s.)(a-dṛṣṭau, 7th s.)(na*)(lakṣyate ”lakṣ pass.)
body.translated_text: 492. An established agent produces a course [of action] — like a sequence; this is seen when [the agent] is observed; but when it is not observed, it is not perceived.

body.text:
493.
(bhāveṣu, 7th pl.)(kṣaṇabhaṅgiṣu, 7th pl.)(pratyabhijñā, f. 1st s.)(ca*)(durghaṭā, f. 1st s.)(hi*)(arthaḥ)(dṛṣṭaḥ)(anya-)(nara-)(na*)(pratyabhijñāyate; prati-abhi-”jñā pass.)(paraiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 493. And recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) is difficult [to explain] regarding momentarily perishing entities; for an object seen [by one person] is not recognized by another person.

body.text:
494.
(keśa-)(ādike, 7th s.)(bhinne, 7th s.)(pratyabhijñānam, n. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(sādṛśyāt, 5th s.)(sadbhāvāt, 5th s.)(ekasya, m. 6th s.)(jñātuḥ, m. 6th s.)(tu*)(bhede, m. 7th s.)(dvi-)(anibandhanam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 494. Recognition would arise regarding [things like] hair and so forth that are distinct, because of similarity; but for a single knower, when there is difference, the restriction [of recognition] to two [moments] is without basis.

body.text:
495.
(ca*)(yadi*)(vidyate ”vid IV C.)(na*)(ekaḥ)(arthaḥ)(kārī, m. 1st s.)(pratisandhāna-)(tat*)(katham*)(dṛṣṭe, 7th s.)(rūpe, 7th s.)(syāt ”as Opt. III p. s.)(ādiḥ, m. 1st s.)(abhilāṣa-)(rasa-)(ādiṣu, m. 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 495. And if there is no single object that performs the connecting [function], then how, upon seeing a form, would there arise a desire for taste and so forth?

body.text:
496.
(baddhaḥ)(nigadaiḥ, 3rd pl.)(rāga-)(ādi-)(vārake, 7th s.)(bhava-)(anyaḥ)(kṣaṇaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ca*)(mucyate ”muc pass.)(anyaḥ)(abaddhaḥ)(iti*)(idam, 1st s.)(na* avabudhyate ”budh pass.)
body.translated_text: 496. One moment is bound by the fetters of <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and so forth, and another is released — [yet the latter is] unbound; this is not understood.

body.text:
497.
(hi*)(baddhasya, 6th s.)(mokṣaḥ)(na* )(kadācit*)(sambhavī, m. 1st s.)(eva*)(ekānta-)(nāśataḥ* [-tas suff.])(tena, 3rd s.)(kṣamaḥ)(arthinām, m. 6th pl.)(mukti-)(vyarthaḥ)
body.translated_text: 497. For the liberation of one who is bound is never possible, since [the bound one] is absolutely destroyed; therefore, the <s>mukti</s> (liberation) desired by aspirants is futile.

body.text:
498.
(saḥ)(āsādayat, 1st s.)(mokṣa-)(dṛṣṭaḥ)(baddhaḥ)(nigaḍādibhiḥ, 3rd pl.)(īdṛśam, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(baddhaḥ)(eti ”i Pr. III p. s.)(muktim, 2nd s.)(vyāhatam, 1st s.)(dṛṣṭam, 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 498. One who is seen bound by fetters and the like [is said to] attain <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) — [but] such [a claim that] the bound one goes to liberation is seen to be contradictory.

body.text:
499.
(bandha-mokṣau, 1st d.)(eka-)(adhikaraṇau, 1st d.)(etau, m. 1st d.)(tathā*)(sthiteḥ, 6th s.)(iva*)(tau, m. 1st d.)(laukikau, 1st d.)(tena, 3rd s.)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(cārutaram, n. 1st s.)(sthitam, 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 499. These two — bondage and liberation — have the same substratum; since [worldly usage] is established in that way, they are [treated as] conventional. By that, everything is well established.

body.text:
500.
(etena, 3rd s.)(eva*)(prakāreṇa, 3rd s.)(vastuṣu, n. 7th pl.)(kṣaṇakṣayiṣu, n. 7th pl.)(smṛti-)(ādīnām, 6th pl.)(asambhavaḥ)(a-bhāvāt, 5th s.)(eka-adhikaraṇa-)
body.translated_text: 500. By this very method, regarding things that perish momentarily, the impossibility of memory and so forth [is raised] — because of the absence of a single substratum.

body.text:
501.
(atra*)(abhidhīyate ”dhā pass.)(kāryakāraṇatā, f. 1st s.)(satyām, 7th s.)(sthitau, 7th s.)(sarva-)(ete, 1st pl.)(a-vyāhatāḥ, 1st pl.)(sidhyanti ”siddh pass.)(nirātmasu, n. 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 501. To this it is said: when the cause-effect relation is real and established, all these [functions] — being uncontradicted — are accomplished even in [entities] without a [permanent] self.

body.text:
502.
(yathā*)(śaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(bīja-)(ādeḥ, 6th s.)(niyatā, f. 1st s.)(aṅkura-)(ādiṣu, 7th pl.)(api*)(viyoge, 7th s.)(anvayi-)(ātma-)(eva*)(tathā*)(sthitiḥ, 1st s.)(adhyātmike, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 502. Just as the power of a seed and so forth is determined with respect to sprouts and so forth, even in [their] separation — having a continuous self — so too is the situation in the personal [domain].

body.text:
503.
(vā*)(pāramparyeṇa, 3rd s.)(sākṣāt*)(kiṃcit*)(hi*)(kvacit*)(śaktimat, n. 1st s.)(tataḥ*)(sambandhaḥ)(ādīnām, 6th pl.)(karma-)(phala-)(upapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)
body.translated_text: 503. Or, directly or through a succession, something somewhere has power; from that, the connection of <s>karma</s> (action) and fruit and so forth is established.

body.text:
504.
(tu*)(vyavasthā, f. 1st s.)(kartṛtva-)(ādi-)(vivakṣayā, f. 3rd s.)(aikya-)(santāna-)(iṣṭā, f. 1st s.)(eva*)(āropitā, f. 1st s.)(kalpanā-)(sā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(aṅgam, n. 1st s.)(tattva-saṃsthiteḥ, 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 504. But the determination of agency and so forth — through the desire [to speak of] the unity of the continuum — that [determination], being a superimposed construction, is not a component of the establishment of reality.

body.text:
505.
(a-sambhave, 7th s.)(anvaya-)(karya-kāraṇatā, f. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū)(viśiṣṭā, f. 1st s.)(sā)(eva*)(yujyate ”yuj pass.)(yadvat*)(bhāvibhiḥ, 3rd pl.)(antara-)(santāna-)
body.translated_text: 505. When continuity [of a self] is impossible, there would be a distinguished cause-effect relation; that very [relation] within the continuum is appropriate — just as [it is] with future [members of the continuum].

body.text:
506.
(bīja-)(aṅkura-)(ādīnām, 6th pl.)(karya-)(kāraṇatā, f. 1st s.)(īkṣyate ”īkṣ pass.)(niyatā, f. 1st s.)(api*)(na*)(sūkṣmaḥ)(aṃśaḥ, 1st s.)(anugama-)(ātmakaḥ)
body.translated_text: 506. The cause-effect relation of seeds, sprouts, and so forth is observed as determined; yet not even a subtle part of a continuing nature [persists through them].

body.text:
507.
(kṣiti-)(ādīnām, 6th pl.)(bīja-)(aṅkura-)(latā-)(ādiṣu, 7th pl.)(avaiśiṣṭye, 7th s.)(na* yuktaḥ, 1st s.)(bhedaḥ)(aikātmyāt, n. 5th s.)(tadā*)(siddhā, f. 1st s.)(niranvayā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 507. Of earth and so forth, in seeds, sprouts, vines, and so forth — when there is no distinction, a difference is not appropriate, because of [their] identity; then [the relation] is established as without continuity.

body.text:
508.
(tasmāt, 5th s.)(prasiddhaye, 4th s.)(bhāva-)(abhāva-)(karma-)(phalādīnām, 6th pl.)(kāraḥ)(yatnaḥ)(siddhau, 7th s.)(karya-kāraṇatā-)(alam*)(paraiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 508. Therefore, for the establishment of the existence and non-existence of entities, <s>karma</s> (action), fruit, and so forth — the cause-effect relation is sufficient [as an explanation]; enough with others [i.e., a permanent self]!

body.text:
509.
(ucyate ”vac)(atra*)(hi*)(kāryam)(prajāyate ”jan pass.)(dvitīye, 7th s.)(kṣaṇe, 7th s.)(kāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(jātam, 1st s.)(pratheme, 7th s.)(ca*)(tadā*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(avinaṣṭam)
body.translated_text: 509. Here it is said: the effect is produced in the second moment; the cause arose in the first [moment]; and at that time, that [cause] was undestroyed.

body.text:
510.
(tu*)(kṣaṇikatvāt, 5th s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(kāle, 7th s.)(kṣaṇa-)(kārya-)(vā*)(vṛtau, 7th s.)(viphalam, n. 1st s.)(yatas*)(tadā*)(tat, 1st s.)(kāryam, 1st s.)(nirvṛttam, 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 510. But because of momentariness, at the time of the effect-moment — or at the time of [its] functioning — it [the cause] is fruitless, since the effect has [already] been accomplished.

body.text:
511.
(ca*)(jātam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(śakyam, 1st s.)(janayitum*)(tena, 3rd s.)(punaḥ*)(-tvāt, 5th s.)(vastunaḥ, n. 6th s.)(bhāva-)(a-bhūta-)(na*)(anyathā*)(sthitiḥ, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 511. And what has [already] been produced cannot be produced again by that [cause], because of [its] being [already] existent; nor is there any other status of the thing.

body.text:
512.
(tasmāt, 5th s.)(eva*)(dvitīya-kṣane, 7th s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(kāryam, n. 1st s.)(utpadyate ”pad)(śaktāt, 5th s.)(hetoḥ, 5th s.)(bhāvinaḥ, 5th s.)(prathama-kṣaṇa-)(tu*)(a-naṣṭāt, 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 512. Therefore, in the second moment, the effect arises from the cause that is endowed with power — that is, from the first moment [of the cause] which has not [yet] perished.

body.text:
513.
(yadi*)(kāryam, 1st s.)(tṛtīya-kṣaṇe, 7th s.)(bhavet ”bhū)(vinaṣṭāt, 5th s.)(hetoḥ, 5th s.)(vipāka-)(pradhvastāt, 5th s.)(yathā*)(kāryam, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(vakṣyate ”vac F. III p. s.)
body.translated_text: 513. If the effect were to arise in the third moment from a cause that has perished — as [one says] an effect [arises] from a ripened and destroyed [cause] — that will be explained.

body.text:
514.
(bhavet ”bhū)(prasaṅgaḥ)(yaugapadya-)(yadi*)(tat, 1st s.)(pratheme, 7th s.)(ca*)(punaḥ*)(tat, 1st s.)(na*)(yujyate ”yuj)(yuktyā, 3rd s.)(-vat*)(saha-bhū-hetu-)
body.translated_text: 514. There would be the consequence of simultaneity if it [arose] in the first [moment]; and again, that is not logically proper — like a co-existent cause.

body.text:
515.
(a-sataḥ, 6th s.)(a-sāmārthyāt, 5th s.)(sāmārthye, 7th s/)(kārya-)(saṃbhavāt, 5th s.)(yaugapadyam, 1st s.)(kārya-kāraṇayoḥ, 6th d.)(spaṣṭam*)(virudhyate ”rudh)
body.translated_text: 515. Because of the incapacity of what is non-existent, and because when there is capacity, the effect [already] occurs — the simultaneity of cause and effect is clearly contradicted.

body.text:
516.
(hi*)(kāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(janayati ”jan caus.)(ātmīyam, 2nd s.)(kāryam, 2nd s.)(na*)(gṛhītvā*)(tat, 2nd s.)(iva*)(saṃdaṃśena, 3rd s.)(yataḥ*)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(yaugapadyam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 516. For the cause generates its own effect — not by seizing it, as if with tongs, whereby there would be simultaneity.

body.text:
517.
(na* api*)(gāḍham, 2nd s.)(sam-ā-liṅgya*)(iva*)(kāmī, 1st s.)(dayitā, f. 1st s.)(yena, 3rd s.)(tayoḥ, 6th d.)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(bhāvaḥ)(sakṛt*)
body.translated_text: 517. Nor does [the cause cling] tightly, as a lover embracing a beloved, whereby there would be simultaneous existence of the two.

body.text:
518-519.
(api*)(vastuni, 7th s.)(avyāpāre, 7th s.)(niyamāt, 5th s.)(utthāt, 5th s.)(ātma-)(hetu-)(yad, 1st s.)(bhāvinaḥ, 6th s.)(prathama-)(kṣaṇa-)(jātam, n. 1st s.)(anantaram*)(ataḥ*)(sannidheḥ, 6th s.)(dvitīya-kṣaṇa-)(iti*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(āhuḥ ”ah)(janayati ”jan caus.)(tat, n. 2nd s.)(anuvidhāyinaḥ, 1st pl.)(saṅketa-)(mātra-)(sambhūta-)(vivakṣā-)
body.translated_text: 518-519. Moreover, since [there is] no activity in [any] real thing — because of the restriction that what arises from one's own cause arises immediately after the first moment [of the cause]; therefore 'in the second moment' — thus those who follow [the tradition] say: it [the cause] produces that [effect]; [this is said] on the basis of a mere convention and the desire to express [it].

body.text:
520.
(atra*)(kim*)(vyāpāreṇa, 3rd s.)(kālena, 3rd s.)(atirikta-)(janma-)(eva*)(sattā, f. 1st s.)(vyāpṛtiḥ, f. 1st s.)(yataḥ*)(tasyām, f. 7th s.)(satyām, f. 7th s.)(kārya-)(udayaḥ)
body.translated_text: 520. Here, what [need is there] for activity beyond time? Existence alone is the activity; since when that [existence] obtains, the effect arises.

body.text:
521.
(sā, f. 1st s.)(niyamaḥ)(ānantarya-)(abhidhīyate ”dhā pass.)(apekṣā, f. 1st s.)(ca*)(udaye, 7th s.)(kārya-)(vyāpāra-)(kāraṇasya, 6th s.)(sadā*)(bhāvaḥ)
body.translated_text: 521. That restriction is called 'immediate succession'; and the dependence [of the effect] upon the arising — [this is] the activity of the cause with respect to the effect; [the cause's] existence is constant.

body.text:
522.
(vyāpāraḥ)(api*)(avakalpitaḥ)(eti ”i Pr. III p. s.)(-tvam, n. 2nd s.)(hetu-)(mātrāt, 5th s.)(bhāvita-)(tat-)(bhāva-)(tataḥ* varam*)(vā*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(tad-vān, m. 1st s.)(astu ”as)(hetutvam, n. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 522. Activity too is merely imagined; [for the effect] attains [its] nature of being a cause from the cause alone, conditioned by the existence of that; or rather, let that alone which possesses that [power] be the causality.

body.text:
523.
(hi*)(sati, 7th s. [sat stem])(bhāve, 7th s.)(bījāt, 5th s.)(eva*)(aṅkura-)(dṛśyante ”dṛś/paśy pass.)(udayāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(tu*)(na*)(kiṃcit*)(samīkṣyate ”īkṣ pass.)(bhavat, n. 1st s.)(sadbhāve, 7th s.)(vyāpāra-)
body.translated_text: 523. For when [the seed] exists, sprouts are seen to arise from the seed alone; but nothing whatsoever that is an activity is observed when existence obtains.

body.text:
524.
(kalpyamāne, 7th s.)(hetutve, 7th s.)(śakteḥ, 6th s.)(adṛṣṭa-)(kim*)(na*)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass. Pr. III p. s.)(anyasya, 6th s.)(api*)(vā*)(kaḥ)(hetutvam, n. 1st s.)(asya, 6th s.)(viśeṣaḥ)(tataḥ*)
body.translated_text: 524. When causality is being imagined — what is the unseen [element] of the power [that is not already admitted]? Or of another as well — what distinction is there of this [from any other cause]?

body.text:
525.
(ca*)(vinā*)(anyena, 3rd s.)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(hetuḥ, 1st s.)(kāryasya, 6th s.)(vā*)(api*)(kim*)(na*)(anye, 1st pl.)(tad-vat*)(bhavet ”bhū)(hetavaḥ, m. 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 525. And if the cause is admitted without anything else [beyond mere existence], or — why should not others likewise be causes?

body.text:
526. [missing verse]
[Verse 526 is missing in the printed Text; the commentary upon it however is available.]
body.translated_text: 526. [Verse 526 is missing in the printed text; the commentary upon it, however, is available.]

body.text:
527.
(ca*)(abhimatam, n. 1st s.)(dṛśyatva-)(vayam, 1st pl.)(upalabhāmahe ”labh Pr. I p. pl. Āt.)(evam*)(tat-katham*)(aṅgīkurmaḥ, Pr. I p. pl.)(sambandham, 2nd s.)(tasya, 6th s.)(nibandhanam, 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 527. And [if] the accepted [position is that] perceptibility — we apprehend [things] in this way; how then do we accept the relation, the basis of that?

body.text:
528.
(ca*)(yathā*)(buddheḥ, 6th s.)(janma, 1st s.)(eva*)(pramāṇatvam, n. 2nd s.)(tat*... kim*)(na*)(hetutvam, n. 1st s.)(sarva-)(bhāveṣu, 7th pl.)(matam, 1st s.)(eva*)(tathā*)
body.translated_text: 528. And just as the very arising of cognition is its validity as a means of knowledge — why is not causality likewise accepted in all entities?

body.text:
529.
(hi*)(yathā*)(buddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(kṣaṇikā, f. 1st s.)(eva*)(tathā*)(anye, 1st pl.)(janminaḥ, 1st pl.)(sādhitāḥ, 1st pl.)(ataḥ*)(eva*)(tad-vat*)(idam, n. 1st s.)(jagat, n. 1st s.)(nir-vyāpāram, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 529. For just as cognition is momentary, so all other things that arise are established [as momentary]; therefore, likewise, this world is devoid of [real] activity.

body.text:
530.
(gandha-)(ādeḥ, 6th s.)(hetutā, f. 1st s.)(anyonya-)(vṛttyā, 3rd s.)(prabandha-)(eva*)(iṣṭā, f. 1st s.)(idam, 1st s.)(abādhakam, 1st s.)(prasañjanam, 1st s.)(-tva-)(hetu-)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 530. The causality of odor and so forth, through mutual succession — only the continuum is accepted; this is an unobjectionable consequence — because of its being the cause of that nature.

body.text:
531.
(api*)(bhāve, 7th s.)(anantara-)(anya-)(eva*)(kiṃcit*)(kāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(niyamāt, 5th s.)(iṣṭam, 1st s.)(tathā* eva*)(ca*)(etat, n. 1st s.)(tulyam, 1st s.)(sthireṣu, 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 531. Moreover, when [the cause] exists, something other [than the cause] — just the immediately subsequent — is accepted as the cause, because of the restriction; and this is equally [applicable] to permanent [entities].

body.text:
532.
(yatra*)(yaḥ)(vyāpṛtaḥ)(kārye, 7th s.)(na*)(mataḥ)(hetuḥ, m. 1st s.)(tasya, 6th s.)(saḥ)(iṣyatām ”iṣ Imp. III p. s. Āt,)(hetuḥ, 1st s.)(yasmin, 7th s.)(sadbhāvaḥ)(niyata-)
body.translated_text: 532. Wherever one is deemed to be active with respect to an effect, [that one is] not considered the cause of that [effect]; let that be accepted as the cause in whose [presence] the existence [of the effect] is determined.

body.text:
533.
(bhāva-)(abhāva-)(pratyakṣa-)(anupalambhataḥ* [-tas suff.])(yadi*)(matam, 1st s.)(vastu, n. 1st s.)(vijñeyam, n. 1st s.)(vijñāna-)(sa-ākāra-)
body.translated_text: 533. If it is held that a real thing is to be known through perception and non-apprehension of existence and non-existence — having the form of consciousness,

body.text:
534.
(yuṣmābhiḥ, 3rd pl.)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass. Pr. III p. s.)(vastu, n. 1st s.)(vedyam, n. 1st s.)(dhī-)(an-ākāra-)(samānam, 1st s.)(upalabhyate ”labh pass.)(pakṣe, 7th s.)(kṣaṇatva-)(tat-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 534. If the real thing that is knowable is accepted by you as being without the form of cognition — then on the thesis [that cognition is] formless, momentariness and so forth [of things would follow equally].

body.text:
535.
(hi*)(sarvam, 1st s.; eva*)(vijñānam, 1st s.)(prajāyate ”jan pass. Pr. III p. s.)(sva-)(pūrvakebhyaḥ, 5th s.)(hetubhyaḥ, 5th s.)(rūpam, 1st s.)(bodha-)(sama-)(rūpa-)(ādi-)(aṃśa-)(kāla-)
body.translated_text: 535. For indeed all cognition arises from its own prior causes; form, cognition, similar form and so forth — [all are determined by] portions and time.

body.text:
536.
(vijñāne, 7th s.)(sākāre, 7th s.)(bhavet ”bhū Opt.)(vaicitryam, 1st s.)(cetasaḥ, n. 6th s.)(asti ”as)(an-aṅkitatve, 7th s.)(ākāra-)(na*)(nibandhanam, 1st s.)(pratyāsatti-)
body.translated_text: 536. If cognition has form, there would be variety of mind; [but] if it is unimprinted by form, there is no basis for proximity.

body.text:
537.
(bhavadbhiḥ, 3rd pl.)(api*)(kiṃcit*)(vaktavye, 7th s.)(uttare, 7th s.)(yat, n. 1st s.; ca*)(samādhānam, n. 1st s.)(vaḥ, 6th pl.)(atra*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū)(asmākam, 6th pl.)(api*)
body.translated_text: 537. By you also, when something is to be said in reply — whatever resolution you have here, that would be ours too.

body.text:
538.
(evam*)(bhavet ”bhū)(nāśaḥ)(kṛta-)(yadi*)(hetuḥ, 1st s.)(na*)(janayet ”jan Opt. III p. s.)(kāryam, 2nd s.)(ca*)(na*)(evam*)(iṣṭam, 1st s.)(yat, 1st s.)(asti ”as)(na*)(hetutā, f. 1st s.)(prabandhe, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 538. Thus there would be destruction of what has been done, if the cause were not to produce the effect; and this is not accepted — namely, that there is no causality in the continuum.

body.text:
539.
(abhyāgamaḥ)(a-kṛta-)(api*)(syāt ”as)(yadi*)(kvacit*)(kāryam, n. 1st s.)(jāyeta ”jan Opt. III p. s.)(vinā*)(hetunā, m. 3rd s.)(etad, n. 1st s.)(na*)(śaktitaḥ* [-tas suff.])(niyata-)
body.translated_text: 539. [If] something done [by one who has not done it] were to arrive — if an effect were to arise somewhere without a cause — this is not [possible], because of the restriction based on power.

body.text:
540.
(codyate ”cud pass.)(vikalpena, 3rd s.)(bheda-)(kṣaṇa-)(nāśa-)(kṣaṇa-)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(āpāditam, 1st s.)(eva*)(yat, 1st s.)(paraiḥ, 3rd pl.)(na*)(eva*)(kiṃcit*)(an-iṣṭam, 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 540. [It is] objected through conceptual construction — the moment of difference, the moment of destruction, and so forth; but whatever has been produced by others — nothing [of it] is unacceptable.

body.text:
541.
(vikalpanā, f. 1st s.)(bheda-)(kṣaṇa-)(na*)(pravarttate ”vṛt)(dṛṣṭīnām, 6th pl.)(sattva-)(ahīna-)(abhimānena, 3rd s.)(aikya-)(santāna-)
body.translated_text: 541. The conceptual construction of the moment of difference does not operate; through the pride of unity in the continuum — [which is ascribed] to beings without [real] selfhood.

body.text:
542.
(tu*)(abhisaṃbuddha-)(tattvāḥ, 1st pl.)(buddhvā*)(niyamam, 2nd s.)(hetūnām, 6th pl.)(vināśinām, 6th pl.)(pratikṣaṇa-)(prārabhante ”rabh Pr. III p. pl. Āt.)(śubhāḥ, f. 2nd pl.)(kriyāḥ, 2nd pl.)
body.translated_text: 542. But those who have realized the truth, having understood the restriction that causes are destructible moment by moment, undertake auspicious actions.

body.text:
543.
(viśiṣṭā, f. 1st s.)(-tā suff.)(kārya-kāryi-[tā])(niyatā, f. 1st s.)(keṣāṃcit*)(cittānām, 6th pl.)(eva*)(tena, 3rd s.)(smaraṇa-ādayaḥ, 1st pl.)(sarvatra*)(nirbādhāḥ, 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 543. The specificity of cause-and-effect relation is restricted to certain minds alone; therefore, memory and so forth are unobstructed everywhere.

body.text:
544.
(avidyādayaḥ, 1st pl.)(bhūtāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(kārya-kāraṇa-)(matāḥ, 1st pl.)(bandhaḥ)(vigamāt, 5th s.)(tat-)(nirmalatā, f. 1st s.)(iṣtaḥ)(muktiḥ, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 544. <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance) and so forth, being real, are considered as cause and effect; bondage [exists]; from its cessation, purity — [that] is accepted as <s>mukti</s> (liberation).

body.text:
545.
(api*)(laukikau, 7th s.)(etau, 1st d.)(bandha-)(mokṣau, 1st d.)(siddhau, 1st d.)(ekādhikaraṇau, 1st d.)(hi*)(eva*)(sarvam, 1st s.)(prasiddham, 1st s.)(kṣaṇikam, 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 545. Moreover, even in the worldly [sense], these two — bondage and liberation — are established; sharing the same substratum, indeed everything is well-known [as] momentary.

body.text:
546.
(tu*)(sarvathā*)(asattvāt, 5th s.)(atiśaya-)(īdṛśī, f. 1st s.)(-tva suff.)(kartṛ-)(bhoktṛ-[tva])(bandha-)(ādi-)(ātmani, n. 7th s.)(vyāhatā, f. 1st s.)(anyathā*)(anityatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 546. But because of the complete non-existence [of a permanent self] in every way — such features as agency, enjoyership, bondage, and so forth in the self are contradicted; otherwise, impermanence [would follow].

body.text:
547-548.
(prāhuḥ ”ah)(mātrakāḥ, 1st pl.)(āgama-)(iti*)(jāti-)(ādeḥ, 6th s.)(niḥsvabhāvatvam, n. 1st s.)(prakāśitam, 1st s.)(prāk*)(ayuktam, 1st s.)(ṣaḍ-arthāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(dravya-)(ādi-)(vidyante ”vid IV C. Pr. III p. pl.)(pāramārthikāḥ, 1st pl.)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(pratiṣedhaḥ)(saṅkṣepeṇa, 3rd s.)(ucyate ”vac pass.)
body.translated_text: 547-548. Those who rely merely on scripture say thus: the essencelessness of <s>jāti</s> (universal) and so forth has been previously demonstrated; the six categories — <s>dravya</s> (substance) and so forth — are not ultimately real; [now] this refutation is stated in brief.

body.text:
549.
(dravyam, n. 1st s.)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass. Pr. III p. s.)(navadhā*)(bhinnam, 1st s.)(bheda-taḥ* [-tas suff.])(kṣiti-)(ādi-)(catus-saṅkhyam)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(pṛthivī-)(dvidhā)(nitya-)(anityatayā, f. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 549. <s>Dravya</s> (substance) is accepted as ninefold, differentiated by kind — earth and so forth, fourfold in number; the first, earth, is twofold: permanent and impermanent.

body.text:
550.
(te, m. 1st pl.)(parama-aṇavaḥ, 1st pl.)(iṣṭāḥ, 1st pl.)(ātmakāḥ, 1st pl.)(pṛthivī-)(ādi-)(nityāḥ, 1st pl.)(tu*)(te, m. 1st pl.)(ye, m. 1st pl.)(prārabdhāḥ, 1st pl. [”rabh])(tat-)(ādyaiḥ, 3rd pl.)(vināśinaḥ, 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 550. Those that are <s>paramāṇus</s> (ultimate atoms) are accepted as having the nature of earth and so forth, and as permanent; but those which are compounded from those [atoms] and so forth are perishable.

body.text:
551.
(tatra*)(asattvam, n. 1st s.)(rūpānām, 6th pl.)(nitya-)(aṇu-)(upapāditam, 1st s.)(prasādhanāt, 5th s.)(niḥśeṣa-)(vastu-)(viṣaya-)(kṣaṇa-bhaṅga-)
body.translated_text: 551. Therein, the non-existence of permanent atoms in the form [category] is demonstrated — from the establishment of the momentary destruction of all real things without remainder.

body.text:
552.
(hi*)(nityatve, 7th s.)(sakalāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(sthūlāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(jāyeran ”jan Opt. III p. pl.)(eva*)(sakṛt*)(teṣām, 6th pl.)(aviśeṣataḥ* [-tas suff.])(asti ”as)(na*)(apekṣyam, 1st s.)(saṃyoga-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 552. For if [atoms were] permanent, all gross [objects] would arise simultaneously, just once — because of the absence of any distinction among them; there is nothing to be awaited, such as conjunction and so forth.

body.text:
553.
(cet*)(utpādakam, n. 1st s.)(aṇu-)(na*)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass. Pr. III p. s.)(upagatam, 1st s.)(dharma-)(sad-)(viṣayatvataḥ* [-tas suff.])(pramāṇa-)(upalambha-)(vidyamāna-)(artha-)

body.translated_text: 641. If cognition of a single object is imagined regarding one quality and the rest, through the <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) with a single substance, from the oneness of that [substance] —

body.translated_text: 643. And this cognition of a single object, through <s>samavāya</s> (inherence), is secondary [i.e., figurative], and thus defective — since, like fire in a boy, it is a [mere] cognition.

body.translated_text: 644. The numerical cognition is established from the distinctness of cognitions arising from elephants and the like, which are other [than the substance] — like the cognition of blue cloth and the like.

body.translated_text: 645. The desired conclusion: therein, number in cognition and the like would arise from this very [process] — [from] convention constructed by attention, desire, and so forth.

body.translated_text: 646. If the production of number is described as dependent on cognition, is not that cognition held [to be sufficient] merely through the convention of mental engagement?

body.translated_text: 647. Measure — such as great, long, and so forth — is spoken of through differentiation; why then is it not held [to be] likewise in the case of form and meaning, from differentiation?

body.translated_text: 648. A garland is [said to be] long; a palace is known to be great — but measurement, as such a form, is imagined there.

body.translated_text: 650. And the palace is accepted [as having those qualities through] connection; that quality — he who is without measure — there is no other garland that is the basis of the figurative usage.

body.translated_text: 651. The usage that is imagined as analytical extraction, on account of its being a cause, its separateness — is not that [usage] held as the conclusion [pertaining to] things of differentiated nature?

body.translated_text: 652. For just as cognition, pleasure, and the like are differentiated, [and are] mutually expressible as distinct — and [each] is a part without another — so too others.

body.translated_text: 653. <s>Saṃyoga</s> (conjunction) and <s>vibhāga</s> (disjunction) are determined [to exist] in substances, as imagined by others; those two, being the causes of cognitions such as 'conjoined' and the like, are purposeless.
