body.text:
659.
(ca*)(iyam, f. 1st s.)(yā, 1st s.)(sāntare, 7th s.)(avasāyinī, f. 1st s.)(nairantarya-)(yā, 1st s.)(api*)(nirantare, 7th s.)(anyā, f. 1st s.)(iyam, f. 1st s.)(dvidhā*)(mithyābuddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 659. And this cognition which determines [something] as 'with an interval,' and the other which [determines it] as 'without an interval' — both are false cognitions.

body.text:
660.
(ca*)(mithyābuddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(sarvā, f. 1st s.)(prādhāna-)(artha-)(anukāriṇī, f. 1st s.)(ca*)(pradhānam, n. 1st s.)(vaktavyam, 1st s.)(iha*)(tat-)(uktau, 7th s.)(tau, 1st d.)(siddhyataḥ ”sidh IV C. Pr. III p. d.)
body.translated_text: 660. And every false cognition imitates the principal meaning; and the principal [object] is to be stated here — in its statement, those two are established.

body.text:
661.
(ca*)(kim*)(nimittaḥ)(iyam, f. 1st s.)(matiḥ, 1st s.)(iti*)(kuṇḍalī, m. 1st s.)(upajāyate ”jan pass.)(no*)(bhāvāt, 5th s.)(nara-)(kuṇḍala-)(tat, 1st s.)(prasaṅgataḥ* [-tas suff.])(sarvadā*)
body.translated_text: 661. And what is the cause of this cognition 'one wearing earrings'? It arises from the existence of the man and the earring — otherwise, from the consequence, [it would arise] always.

body.text:
662.
(bhāvasya, 6th s.)(dṛṣṭa-)(anyatra*)(niṣedhaḥ)(anyatra*)(ca*)(saṃyogaḥ)(bhavet ”bhū Opt.)(dṛṣṭaḥ)(katham*)(pratiṣidhyate ”sidh pass.)
body.translated_text: 662. The negation of an entity seen elsewhere, and conjunction seen elsewhere — how is it negated?

body.text:
663.
(iti*)(caitraḥ)(akuṇḍalaḥ)(evam*)(tasmāt, 5th s.)(asti ”as)(vāstavaḥ)(yat, 1st s.)(vidhāna-)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(niṣedha-)(pravarttate ”vṛt Pr. III p. s. Āt.)(vibhāgena, 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 663. [One can say] 'This <s>Caitra</s> is without earrings' — therefore, that which operates through the division of injunction and negation exists as real.

body.text:
664.
(ucyate ”vac)(jala-)(ādayaḥ, 1st pl.)(na*)(a-viśeṣāḥ, 1st pl.)(kṣaṇikatvena, 3rd s.)(api*)(sattve, 7th s.)(te, m. 1st pl.)(apekṣante ”īkṣ Pr. III p. pl. Āt.)(daśāntaram, n. 2nd s.)(a-vyavadhāna-)(ādi, n. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 664. It is said: water and the like are not without distinction, even through momentariness; those, being [real], depend on another state such as non-interruption and the like.

body.text:
665.
(tu*)(yadi*)(jala-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(syuḥ ”as Opt.)(sa-)(apekṣā, 1st s.)(mātra-)(saṃyoga-)(kāryam, n. 1st s.)(syāt ”as Opt.)(eva*)(anantaram, 2nd s.)(yoga-)(vā*)(ete, m. 1st pl.)(na*)(bhavet ”bhū)
body.translated_text: 665. But if water and the like have dependence, the effect of mere conjunction would be immediate; or else these [entities] would not [arise from] conjunction.

body.text:
666.
(hi*)(paśyati ”dṛś/paśy)(ye, n. 2nd d.)(prāpta-)(avasthā-)(nairantaryeṇa, 3rd s.)(jāti-taḥ* [-tas suff.])(āharati; ā”hṛ)(te, n. 2nd d.)(vastunī, n. 1st d.)(tathāvidhe, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 666. For one sees those two things that have reached the [requisite] state — [one] brings [them together] in succession from [their] class; in such a [state],

body.text:
667.
(jātam, n. 1st s.)(vicchinnam, 1st s.)(eti ”i Pr. III p. s.)(nimittatām, f. 2nd s.)(jñāne, 7th s.)(sa-antaram, 2nd s.)(ca* eva*)(anyathā*)(anantara-)(-vat*)(geha-)(vindhya-)(himādri-)
body.translated_text: 667. That which, having arisen and been interrupted, goes to the status of a cause in cognition — as 'with an interval'; and otherwise, like 'without an interval' — [the examples of] a house, <s>Vindhya</s>, and the <s>Himālaya</s>.

body.text:
668-669.
(mithyābuddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(na*)(eva*)(sarvā, f. 1st s.)(anusāriṇī, f. 1st s.)(pradhāna-)(artha-)(yathā*)(ādi-)(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(dvi-candra-)(nirapekṣā, 1st s.)(sādharmya-)(kācit*)(upaplavāt, 5th s.)(antar*)(cittasya, 6th s.)(gata-)(anyatra*)(vā*)(pradhānam, 1st s.)(iha*)(vidyate ”vid IV C.)(jātam, 1st s.)(avacchinna-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 668-669. Not every false cognition follows the principal meaning — as in the cognition of a double moon and the like, which is independent [of the object]; some [errors arise] from the disruption of the internal [faculty] of the mind or from elsewhere; but here the principal [cognition], having arisen, is determined by exclusion and the like.

body.text:
670.
(matiḥ)(iti*)(kuṇḍalī, m. 1st s.)(eva*)(caitra-)(kuṇḍalayoḥ, 7th d.)(viśeṣayoḥ, 6th d.)(avasthā-)(jāta-)(jāyate ”jan pass.)(iva*)(saṃyogaḥ)
body.translated_text: 670. The cognition 'one wearing earrings' — regarding the particular states of <s>Caitra</s> and the earring, arising [from their conjunction] — it is as if conjunction of states.

body.text:
671.
(saḥ)(tādṛk*)(atiśayaḥ)(avasthā-)(dṛṣṭaḥ)(niṣidhyate ”sidh pass.)(anyatra*)(ādau, 7th s.)(iti*)(caitre)(a-kuṇḍalaḥ)(na*)(saṃyogaḥ)(a-dṛṣṭitaḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 671. Such a surplus is seen in states; it is negated elsewhere; thus 'in <s>Caitra</s>, there is no earring' — the non-observation of conjunction.

body.text:
672.
(dhīḥ, f. 1st s.)(vastu-)(yukta-)(na*)(jāyate ”jan pass.)(yogāt, 5th s.)(abhimatāt, 5th s.)(para-)(buddhitayā, f. 3rd s.)(yukta-)(yat, n. 1st s.)(-vat*)(dhīḥ, f. 1st s.)(yukta-)(prāsāda-)(ādiṣu, 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 672. A cognition that is conjoined with a real thing does not arise from the connection as intended by others — like a cognition conjoined [with the real thing] in palaces and the like, through the nature of cognition.

body.text:
673.
(athavā*)(jāyamānatayā, f. 3rd s.)(sadbhāve, 7th s.)(aneka-)(vastu-)(iva*)(buddhayaḥ, 1st pl.)(viṣayāḥ, 1st pl.)(aneka-)(vibhakta-)(tantu-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 673. Or, when there is the existence of many things through their arising, cognitions [are] like the objects — multiple, differentiated — threads and the like.

body.text:
674.
(dvayam, n. 1st s.)(pramā-)(vācyam, n. 1st s.)(yathāyogam*)(vibhāge, 7th s.)(api*)(ca*)(prabādhakam, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(na*)(yuktā, 1st s.)(ekasya, 6th s.)(vṛttiḥ, f. 1st s.)(aneka-)
body.translated_text: 674. Both the valid cognition and the expressible are spoken of according to their applicability; and even in disjunction, it is refuting — therefore, the function of one with many [objects] is not justified.

body.text:
675.
(abhidhāna-)(paratvam, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(aparatvam, n. 1st s.)(kalpyate ”kḷp)(nimittam, 1st s.)(para-)(apara-)(tat, n. 1st s.)(na*)(avadhikam, 1st s.)(dik-)(kāla-)
body.translated_text: 675. And priority (<s>paratva</s>) and posteriority (<s>aparatva</s>) — [considered as] the cause of designating prior and posterior — that is not delimited by direction or time.

body.text:
676.
(yathā*)(rūpāṇi, 1st pl.)(ādi-)(nīla-)(ucyante ”vac pass.)(tathā*)(api*)(viveke, 7th s.)(anya-)(upādhi-)(tathā*)(apare, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 676. Just as colors such as blue and the like are spoken of, so too, upon analysis, [they are] the qualification of something else; so too the others.

body.text:
677.
(matam, n. 1st s.)(cet*)(sarve, 1st pl.)(saṃkhya-)(yoga-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(na*)(a-vyatirekiṇaḥ, 1st pl.)(dravya-)(vyavacchedakatvena, n. 3rd s.)(tat-)(iva*)(daṇḍa-)(ādiḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 677. If it is held that all — number, conjunction, and the like — are not non-different from substance, [then] by way of being delimiters of substance — like a staff and the like.

body.text:
678.
(sādhanam, n. 1st s.)(iṣṭa-)(varṇanāt, 5th s.)(saṃvṛtti-)(sattvena, 3rd s.)(sadyataḥ* [-tas suff.])(saṃvṛtti-)(na* eva*)(nirvācyam)(-tvena, 3rd s.)(tattva-)(anya-)(sat-)
body.translated_text: 678. The description of the desired proof: through conventional reality and actual existence — [it is] not indeed to be expressed by convention alone, [as] the reality of a different entity.

body.text:
679.
(atha*)(samūha-)(ādeḥ, 6th s.)(-tvam, n. 1st s.)(a-nirvacanīya-)(niṣidhyate ”sidh pass.)(yasmāt, 5th s.)(dharmatvam, 1st s.)(niyata-)(-vat*)(rūpa-)(śabda-)(rasa-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 679. Now, the inexpressible nature of a collection and the like is negated, since [the property of being] a <s>dharma</s> is determined — like form, sound, taste, and the like.

body.text:
680.
(tattva-taḥ* [-tas suff.])(tasya, 6th s.)(niḥsvabhāvatayā, 3rd s.)(-vat*)(ambara-padma-)(na*)(niyatāḥ, 1st pl.)(dharmāḥ, 1st pl.)(siddhāḥ, 1st pl.)(te, 1st pl.)(kalpanā-āropitāḥ, 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 680. In reality, since that is of no intrinsic nature — like a sky-lotus — those <s>dharmas</s> (properties) are not established as determined; they are superimposed by conceptual construction.

body.text:
681.
(eva*)(uktau, 7th s.)(tathā)(anekāntaḥ)(yataḥ*)(ādibhiḥ, 3rd pl.)(viyat-padma-)(ca*)(abhedaḥ)(vyatirekaḥ)(vyavasthitaḥ)(eva*)(vastuni, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 681. Thus, in the statement — since from 'and so forth' and the like, both non-difference and difference are established in the real thing — [it is called] <s>anekānta</s> (many-sidedness), like a sky-lotus.

body.text:
682.
(evam*)(cet*)(pratipādyate; prati-”pad caus. pass.)(saṃkhyā-)(ādeḥ, 6th s.)(anyatvam, n. 1st s.)(dravyataḥ* [-tas suff.])(hetoḥ, 6th s.)(āśraya-asiddhatā, 1st s.)(saṃkhyā-)(ādīnām, 6th pl.)(a-siddhitaḥ*)
body.translated_text: 682. Thus, if the otherness of number and the like from substance is demonstrated — from the non-establishment of the basis, [there is] the non-establishment of the reason, since number and the like are not established.

body.text:
683.
(tu*)(dravyam, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(bhinnam, 1st s.)(samuccaya-)(ādi-)(tathā*)(ucyate ”vac pass.)(bhedaḥ)(eva*)(svarūpāt, 5th s.)(vyāhataḥ)(bhavet ”bhū Opt.)(sādhitaḥ)
body.translated_text: 683. But substance itself, being differentiated, is spoken of as collection and the like; the difference from its own nature — if established, would be contradictory.

body.text:
684.
(saṃskāraḥ)(proktaḥ)(trividhaḥ*)(ākhyaḥ)(vega)(saṃjñaḥ)(bhāvanā-)(lakṣaṇaḥ)(sthitasthāpaka-)(akhilaḥ)(asau, m. 1st s.)(na*)(saṃgacchate ”gam/gacch Pr. III p. s. Āt.)
body.translated_text: 684. <s>Saṃskāra</s> (latent impression) is said to be threefold, called by the designation of velocity, <s>bhāvanā</s> (cultivation), and having the characteristic of restoring to the original position; all of that does not hold.

body.text:
685.
(padārthānām, 6th pl.)(kṣaṇikatvāt, 5th s.)(na*)(kriyā, f. 1st s.)(vidyate ”vid IV C.)(prabandhasya, 6th s.)(yat-)(saṃskāraḥ)(saṃjñakaḥ)(vega-)(syāt ”as)(hetuḥ, 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 685. Since entities are momentary, no [real] action (<s>kriyā</s>) exists; that which is designated as <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression), the cause of the momentum of the continuum, would be —

body.text:
686.
(yuktaḥ)(saṃskāraḥ)(ākyaḥ)(bhāvanā-)(ātmakaḥ)(vāsanā-)(cetasaḥ, n. 6th s.)(ca*)(idam, 1st s.)(na*)(yujyate ”yuj)(guṇaḥ)(ātma-)(tat-)(nirākṛteḥ, 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 686. The <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression) called <s>bhāvanā</s> (cultivation), having the nature of <s>vāsanā</s> (latent tendency), is appropriate — and this [applies] to the mind; but [to posit it as] a quality of the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) is not appropriate, since that [Self] has been refuted.

body.text:
687.
(tu*)(na*)(yuktaḥ)(rūpaḥ)(sthitasthāpaka-)(kṣaṇabhaṅgataḥ* [-tas suff.])(a-sambhavāt, 5th s.)(artha-)(sthita-)(bhāve, 7th s.)(saṃsthitiḥ, f. 1st s.)(eva*)(tādrūpyāt, 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 687. But the form of a stabilizing [force] is not appropriate, since momentary destruction makes [permanent stability] impossible; when the object remains in existence, stability [follows] simply from [its] having that nature.

body.text:
688.
(ekam, 1st s.)(kṣaṇam, 1st s.)(avasthānam, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(sva-hetoḥ, 5th s.)(ca*)(na*)(anuvarttanam, n. 1st s.)(prabandhe, 7th s.)(prabhāvāt, 5th s.)(pūrva-pūrva-)
body.translated_text: 688. Abiding for a single moment is [simply] from one's own cause; and there is no continuation [beyond that moment] in the continuum, through the power of each preceding [moment].

body.text:
689.
(eṣaḥ)(na*)(udayavāt, m. 1st s.)(anyathā*)(kasya, m. 6th s.)(tataḥ*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(sthāpakaḥ)(na*)(ca*)(hetutvam, n. 1st s.)(dṛṣṭam, 1st s.)(saṃskāraḥ)(vā*)(anyaḥ)(bhavet ”bhū Opt.)
body.translated_text: 689. This [stabilizing force] does not arise otherwise — of what, then, is this a stabilizer? Nor is causality observed [for it]; or [else] the <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression) would be something different.

body.text:
690.
(iṣṭaḥ)(sthāpakaḥ)(utpannasya, 6th s.)(ādeḥ, 6th s.)(vastra-)(nāma, n. 1st s.)(guṇa-)(saṃskāra-)(na*)(sambhavī, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 690. [If] a stabilizer of what has [already] arisen is accepted — [such as] the quality-<s>saṃskāra</s> of cloth and so forth, beginning [from the moment of production] — it is not possible.

body.text:
691.
(nibandhanāt, 5th s.)(vistareṇa, 3rd s.)(pūrvam*)(manas-)(yoga-)(ātmanām, 6th pl.)(upapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(na*)(adṛṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(upetam, 1st s.)(lakṣaṇa-)(ukta-)(para-)
body.translated_text: 691. Because of the extensive prior explanation regarding those [entities] connected with mind and <s>yoga</s> — the unseen [force] (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>), endowed with the characteristics stated by the opponent, is not established.

body.text:
692.
(karma, n. 1st s.)(utkṣepa-)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(a-sambhavi, n. 1st s.)(bhāveṣu, 7th s.)(kṣaṇa-kṣayiṣu, 7th pl.)(cyuteḥ, 5th s.)(eva*)(deśe, 7th s.)(jāta-)(tat, n. 1st s.)(a-sambhavāt, 5th s.)(prāpti-)(anya-)
body.translated_text: 692. <s>Karma</s> (action) such as throwing upward and so forth is not possible in entities that perish momentarily; since [what is produced] arises only at the place of cessation [of the prior moment], and the attainment of another place is not possible.

body.text:
693.
(hi*)(pare, 1st pl.)(jaguḥ ”gai I C. Perf. III p. pl.)(kālam, 1st s.)(kriyā-)(kālam, 1st s.)(atirikta-)(janma-)(api*)(ādiṣu, 7th pl.)(vastuṣu, 7th pl.)(dīpa-)(iṣṭa-)(nāśa-)(āśutara-)
body.translated_text: 693. For others have declared that time — the time of action — is also a surplus [entity] arising; regarding things such as lamps and so forth, the accepted [view is that their] destruction [is] extremely rapid.

body.text:
694-695.
(āśleṣaḥ)(kāraṇa-)(abhivyañjanam, n. 1st s.)(sāmānyasya, 6th s.)(tataḥ*)(karma, n. 1st s.)(sva-)(avayave, 7th s.)(tad-anantaram, 2nd s.)(vibhāgaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ca*)(vināśaḥ)(saṃyogasya, 6th s.)(tataḥ*)(saṃkṣayaḥ)(dravyasya, 6th s.)(api*)(dīpa-)(ādau, 7th s.)(vastuni, 7th s.)(iṣṭā, f. 1st s.)(āyitā, f. 1st s.)(ṣaṭ-)(kṣaṇasya, 6th s.)(eva*)
body.translated_text: 694-695. Contact with the cause, manifestation of the universal — then <s>karma</s> (action) in one's own part, immediately after that separation, and destruction of conjunction, then destruction even of the substance — regarding things such as lamps and so forth, only a six-moment duration is accepted.

body.text:
696.
(viśleṣa-)(paścima-)(āśleṣa-)(agrima-)(deśābhyām, 3rd d.)(sarvaḥ)(prakalpitaḥ)(aparaḥ)(gantā, m. 1st s.)(vā* )(ca*)(ādhāraḥ)(karma-)
body.translated_text: 696. Through the locations of the final contact and the initial separation — all others are conceived as goers; or alternatively, the basis of <s>karma</s> (action) —

body.text:
697.
(yaḥ)(cala-ātmakaḥ)(janaḥ)(na*)(āste, ”as Āt.)(jātu*)(api*)(tasya, 6th s.)(antara-mātre, 7th s.)(aṇu-)(a-sambhavaḥ)(saṃkrānti-)(deśa-)
body.translated_text: 697. The person who is of a moving nature never remains [still]; there is no possibility of transference to another place even in the interval [between moments] of an atom.

body.text:
698.
(sthairye, 7th s.)(vastunaḥ, 6th s.)(tu*)(gamana-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(sarve, 1st pl.)(durghaṭāḥ, 1st pl.)(asya, 6th s.)(a-viśeṣataḥ* [-tas suff.])(sarvāsu, f. 7th pl.)(daśāsu, 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 698. But if a thing were stable, motion and so forth would all be difficult [to explain], since there would be no distinction in all its states.

body.text:
699.
(yadi*)(gamana-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(prakṛtyāḥ, 1st pl.)(tat-)(syuḥ ”as Opt.)(sadā*)(rūpam)(gantṛ-)(evam*)(na*)(avatiṣṭheta ”sthā Pot. III p. s. Āt.)(niścalam, 2nd s.)(api*)(kṣaṇam, 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 699. If motion and so forth were of [the thing's] nature, then the thing would always have the form of a mover; thus it would not remain still even for a single moment.

body.text:
700.
(yasmāt, 5th s.)(gati-)(ādi-)(a-sattve, 7th s.)(te, 1stpl.)(dhruvam*)(prāpnuvanti ”āp Pr. III p. pl.)(a-tyakta-)(pūrva-)(rūpatvāt, 5th s.)(-vat*)(kāla-)(udaya-)(gati-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 700. Since, when motion and so forth are absent, they [the things] certainly obtain [stillness] — because of not having relinquished their previous form — like time, arising, motion, and so forth.

body.text:
701.
(atha*)(tat-prakṛtyā, 3rd s.)(a-gantṛ-)(a-gamana-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(syuḥ ”as)(sadā*)(bhavet ”bhū Opt.)(na*)(eva*)(api*)(ekam, 2nd s.)(kṣaṇam, 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 701. If, on the other hand, [the thing] is by nature a non-mover, then non-motion and so forth would always [obtain]; it would not [move] even for a single moment.

body.text:
702.
(yasmāt, 5th s.)(api*)(gati-)(ādi-)(bhāve, 7th s.)(tat, 1st s.)(ātmakam, 1st s.)(niścala-)(a-tyakta-)(pūrva-)(rūpatvāt, 5th .s)(-vat*)(kāla-)(ātmaka-)(niścala-)
body.translated_text: 702. Since, even when motion and so forth exist, that [thing] would have the nature of stillness — because of not having relinquished its previous form — like [something that has] the nature of being still and timeless.

body.text:
703.
(tu*)(yadi*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(syāt ”as)(a-gantā, m. 1st s.)(ekadā*)(ca*)(punaḥ*)(anyathā*)(saṃgateḥ, 5th s.)(paraspara-)(vibhinna-)(ātma-)(bhavet ”bhū)(bhinnatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 703. But if this [thing] were sometimes a non-mover and at other times otherwise, then, because of the mutual incompatibility, there would be a differentiation of [its] nature — [it would be] split [into two].

body.text:
704.
(vyavasīyate; vi-ava-”so pass. Pr. III p. s.)(iti*)(tau, 1st d.)(atyanta-)(bhinnau, 1st d.)(vṛttitvāt, 5th s.)(viruddha-)(dharma-)(-vat*)(vastu-)(cala-)(niścala-)
body.translated_text: 704. Those two are thus determined to be absolutely different, because of having contradictory properties — [namely,] the moving and the still thing.

body.text:
705.
(ca*)(karma, n. 1st s.)(abhimatam, 1st s.)(dṛśyatva-)(na*)(vyatireki, n. 1st s.)(vastu-)(sattā, f. 1st s.)(asya, 6th s.)(anupātinī, f. 1st s.)(yukti-)(nā*)(eva*)(dṛśyate ”dṛś / paśy pass.)
body.translated_text: 705. And <s>karma</s> (action), [which is] accepted [as having] the nature of perceptibility — is not different from the thing; the existence of this [action] does not follow [from the thing]; nor indeed is it seen through reasoning.

body.text:
706.
(evam*)(gati-)(ādīnām, 6th pl.)(a-sambhavaḥ)(vā*)(sthire, 7th s.)(vā*)(asthire, 7th s.)(a-yogataḥ* [-tas suff.])(vibhāga-)(prāktana-)(apara-)(deśābhyām, 3rd d.)
body.translated_text: 706. Thus, the impossibility of motion and so forth — whether in what is stable or in what is unstable — because of the impossibility [in both cases]; through the locations of the former and the subsequent, and through separation —

body.text:
707.
(gatiḥ-)(bhrāntiḥ, f. 1st s.)(-vat*)(pradīpa-)(janmanaḥ, 5th s.)(apara-)(samāna-)(vastūnām, 6th pl.)(upalabdheh, 5th s.)(nairantaryeṇa, 3rd s.)(antara-)(deśa-)
body.translated_text: 707. Motion is an illusion — like [the apparent movement of] a lamp flame; through the uninterrupted apprehension of similar things arising at different locations.

body.text:
708.
(dravya-)(ādiṣu, 7th pl.)(niṣiddheṣu, 7th pl.)(jātayaḥ, 1st pl.)(api*)(nirākṛtāḥ, 1st pl.)(hi*)(tāḥ, 1st pl.)(sarvāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(parikalpitāḥ, 1st pl.)(vṛttāḥ, 1st pl.)(traya-)(padārtha-)
body.translated_text: 708. When substances and so forth have been refuted, universals (<s>jātis</s>) are also refuted; for all those are conceived as operating [only] within the three categories of <s>padārtha</s> (ontological category).

body.text:
709.
(tatra*)(jātiḥ, 1st s.)(abhyupagamyate ”gam / gacch pass.)(paraiḥ, 3rd pl.)(iyam, 1st s.)(dvi-vidhā*)(eva*)(sāmānyam, 1st s.)(ākhyam, 1st s.)(sattā-)(anuvṛttitaḥ* [-tas suff.])(samasteṣu, 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 709. Therein, <s>jāti</s> (universal) is accepted by the opponents as being of two kinds: [first,] the universal called <s>sattā</s> (being), from [its] recurrence in all [entities];

body.text:
710.
(dravyatva-)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(tu*)(sāmānyam, 1st s.)(abhidhīyate ”dhā pass.)(sat, 1st s.)(viśeṣaḥ)(sva-)(āśrayeṣu, 7th pl.)(bhāvataḥ* [-tas suff.])(hetu-)(cetasaḥ, 6th s.)(anuvṛttasya, 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 710. But <s>dravyatva</s> (substancehood) and so forth are called the [specific] universal (<s>sāmānya</s>), being the existing particular — from [its] recurrence in its own substrata; [it is] the cause of the mind [that apprehends it].

body.text:
711.
(ca*)(viśeṣaṇāt, 5th s.)(sva-āśrayasya, 6th s.)(sarvebhyaḥ, 5th pl.)(vijātibhyaḥ, 5th pl.)(tataḥ*)(teṣām, 6th pl.)(eva*)(sthitam, n. 1st s.)(hetutvam, n. 1st s.)(vyāvṛtti-)(buddhi-)
body.translated_text: 711. And because of differentiating its own substratum from all those of a different class — therefore, the causal status of the cognition of exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) is established for those alone.

body.text:
712.
(kecit*)(viśeṣāḥ, 1st pl.)(hetavaḥ, 1st pl.)(vyāvṛtteḥ, 6th s.)(eva*)(ye, 1st pl.)(varṇitāḥ, 1st pl.)(antyāḥ, 1st pl.)(viśeṣāḥ, 1st pl.)(sthitāḥ, 1st pl.)(nitya-)(dravya-)
body.translated_text: 712. Some [say] that the causes of exclusion are [these] particulars (<s>viśeṣas</s>) — those that have been described; the ultimate <s>viśeṣas</s> (particularities) reside in permanent substances.

body.text:
713.
(yad-balāt, 5th s.)(dhiyaḥ, 1st pl.)(jāyante ”jan pass.)(yoginām, 6th pl.)(paramāṇu-)(ādau, 7th s.)(iti*)(ayam, 1st s.)(vilakṣaṇaḥ)(āśritāḥ, 1st pl.)(pratyakem, 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 713. By the power of which, cognitions arise for <s>yogins</s> regarding atoms and so forth — this [particular] is of a different character; [they are] dependent individually.

body.text:
714.
(jātayaḥ, 1st pl.)(sattva-)(gotva-)(ādi, 1st s.)(prasiddhāḥ, 1st pl.)(pratyakṣataḥ* [-tas suff.])(udayāt, 5th s.)(pratyaya-)(sat-)(ādi-)(bhāve, 7th s.)(akṣa-)(vyāpāra-)
body.translated_text: 714. The universals <s>sattva</s> (being), <s>gotva</s> (cowness), and so forth are established through direct perception — from the arising of cognitions of 'existent' and so forth upon the operation of the senses.

body.text:
715.
(sattvam, n. 1st s.)(āsām, 6th pl.)(pratīyate, prati-”i, pass. Pr. III p. s.)(balena, 3rd s.)(anumāna-)(api*)(viśeṣa-)(pratyayaḥ)(bhāvikaḥ)(antara-)(nimitta-)
body.translated_text: 715. The existence (<s>sattva</s>) of these [universals] is cognized through the force of inference as well; the particular cognition is natural, [arising from] an internal cause.

body.text:
716.
(go-)(gaja-)(ādiṣu, m. 7th pl.)(viśeṣāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(śabda-)(go- [gav])(ādi-)(prajñāna-)(hetavaḥ, 1st pl.)(artha-)(vyatirikta-)(samaya-)(ākṛti-)(piṇḍa-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 716. In cows, elephants, and so forth, the particulars (<s>viśeṣas</s>) are the causes of the cognition of 'cow' and so forth — [these particulars are] distinct from the object, from convention, from configuration, from the aggregate, and so forth.

body.text:
717.
(hi*)(viṣayatve, 7th s.)(go- [gav])(ādi-)(anyatvāt, 5th s.)(śabda-)(buddhitaḥ* [-tas suff.])(tat-)(dhvanī, m. 1st d.)(dhī-)(sa-vatsā-)(aṅkuśa-)(yathā*)(eṣu, 7th pl.)(eva*)
body.translated_text: 717. For [when something is] in the domain of 'cow' and so forth, [it is] different [from the universal]; from the cognition of the word — [the universal and the particular] are a pair; like [the cognition of] a cow with a calf and a goad — in those very [instances].

body.text:
718.
(viśeṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(vyabhicārāt, 5th s.)(vijñānaiḥ, 3rd pl.)(śaśa-śṛṅga-)(ādi-)(abhidhānam, 1st s.)(svarūpa-)(tat-)(nidarśanam)(vaidharmyeṇa, 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 718. The qualifier is deviant; by cognitions of hare's horns and so forth — their designation, that very [thing], is an illustration by means of dissimilarity of properties.

body.text:
719.
(vijñānam, 1st s.)(anuvṛttam)(go- [gav])(ādiṣu, 7th pl.)(jāyate ”jan pass.)(anyataḥ* [-tas suff.])(piṇḍataḥ* [-tas suff.])(viśeṣakatvāt, 5th s.)(iva*)(vijñānam, 1st s.)(nīla-)(ādi, 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 719. A recurring cognition arises in cows and so forth, from one [cow] to another — from the aggregate; [just as] a differentiating [cognition], like the cognition of blue and so forth, [arises from particular features].

body.text:
720.
(gotvam, n. 1st s.)(artha-antaram, 1st s.)(gotaḥ* [-tas suff.])(viṣayatva-taḥ* [-tas suff.])(bhinna-)(dhī-)(-vat*)(rūpa-)(sparśa-)(ādi-)(tasya, 6th s.)(-vat*)(caitra-)(ukteḥ, 5th s.)(iti*)(tasya, 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 720. <s>Gotva</s> (cowness) is something other than the cow; from [its] being a [different] object — like the cognition of form, touch, and so forth, which is different — like that of <s>Caitra</s>; because of his statement, it is like that.

body.text:
721.
(tat, n. 1st s.; idam, n. 1st s.)(asāram, 1st s.)(kāryam, 1st s.)(varṇanam, 1st s.)(mātra-)(prakriyā-)(ca*)(iha*)(na*)(pramāṇam, 1st s.)(vidyate ”vid IV C.)(jñāpakam, 1st s.)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 721. That [argument] is without substance; [it is merely] a description of the effect — a mere procedure; and here no means of valid cognition is found that would indicate that [universal].

body.text:
722.
(hi*)(pratyayāḥ, 1st pl.)(sat-)(ādi-)(na*)(anantara-bhāvinaḥ, 1st pl.)(vyāpāra-)(akṣa-)(te, 1st pl.)(ābhoga-taḥ* [-tas suff.])(saṅketa-)
body.translated_text: 722. For the cognitions of 'existent' and so forth do not arise immediately after the operation of the senses — [they arise] from convention and mental engagement.

body.text:
723.
(yathā*)(ādīnām, 6th pl.)(dhātrī-)(abhaya-)(upalabhyate ”labh pass.)(pratyekam*)(vā*)(-tve, 7th s.)(saha*)(nānā-)(api*)(śaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(nivartane, 7th s.)(nānā-)(roga-)
body.translated_text: 723. Just as the individual powers of <s>dhātrī</s> (emblic myrobalan) and <s>abhaya</s> (terminalia) are apprehended, whether individually or together — multiple powers [are found] in the removal of multiple diseases.

body.text:
724.
(vidyate ”vid IV C.)(na*...kiṃcit*)(teṣu, 7th pl.)(sāmānyam, 1st s.)(-mat*)(śakti-)(upalambhataḥ* [-tas suff.])(śānti-)(roga-)(bhedena, 3rd s.)(kṣipra-)(cira-)
body.translated_text: 724. No universal endowed with power is found in those [substances]; from the apprehension of the curing of diseases, through the distinction of quick and slow [cures].

body.text:
725.
(na*)(hi*)(kaścit*)(atiśayaḥ)(sāmānye, 7th s.)(bhedataḥ* [-tas suff.])(kṣetra-)(ādi-)(nityam, 2nd s.)(eka-)(rūpatayā, 3rd s.)(saḥ)(vidyate ”vid IV C.)(dhātrī-)(ādeḥ, 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 725. For there is no surplus [entity] — a universal — [arising] from the distinctions of field and so forth; it [the universal] would always exist in a single form, [being] eternal, from <s>dhātrī</s> and so forth.

body.text:
726.
(evam*)(api*)(atyanta-)(bhede, 7th s.)(kecit*)(niyata-)(śaktitaḥ* [-tas suff.])(yānti ”yā Pr. III p. pl.)(hetutvam, 2nd s.)(pratyavamarśa-)(tulya-)(ādeḥ, 6th s.)(apare, 1st pl.)(na*)
body.translated_text: 726. Even so, when there is absolute difference, some [things], through their determinate powers, go to [the status of] causality — like [others having] equal reflection and so forth; but others do not.

body.text:
727.
(śruteḥ, 5th s.)(sat-)(vivakṣāyām, 7th s.)(mātra-)(upayogitva-)(kārya-)(samayaḥ)(kriyate, ”kṛ pass.)(teṣu, 7th pl.)(yad-vā*)(anyasyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(yathā*)(ruci, 1st s.)
728.
(saṅketaḥ)(śruti-)(go- [gav])(kriyate, ”kṛ pass.)(vyavahartṛbhiḥ, 3rd pl.)(upayogini, 1st s.)(bheda-)(kārya-)(rūpeṇa, 3rd s.)(vāha-)(doha-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 727-728. When the [conventional] expression of 'existent' is intended, by the use of mere words — a convention regarding them is made for the purpose of [particular] effects; or, according to another [interpretation], as one pleases. The convention of the word 'cow' is made by users of language — in the form of a useful distinction of effect — in the form of milking, carrying, and so forth.

body.text:
729.
(tat*)(ime, 1st pl.)(pratyayāḥ, 1st pl.)(sat-)(ādi-)(lakṣyante ”lakṣ pass.)(jāyamānāḥ, 1st pl.)(manaskārāt, 5th s.)(saṅketa-)(na*)(anantaram, 2nd s.)(vyapṛti-)(akṣa-)
body.translated_text: 729. Therefore, these cognitions of 'existent' and so forth are observed to arise from conventional mental engagement, not immediately after the operation of the senses.

body.text:
730.
(ādau, 7th s.)(vijñanam, 1st s.)(prajāyate ”jan pass.)(eva*)(ākāram, 1st s.)(ajalpa-)(tataḥ*)(ābhogaḥ)(samaya-)(tasmāt, 5th s.)(te, 1st pl.)(smārttam, 1st s.)(tataḥ*)(api*)
body.translated_text: 730. At first, cognition arises without verbalization of form; then there is intentional engagement by convention; therefore that [cognition] of theirs is memorial, and thereafter also,

body.text:
731.
(tataḥ* eva*)(cittasya, 6th s.)(gata-)(anyatra*)(pravarttate ”vṛt)(upalambhanam, 2nd s.)(mātra-)(vastu-)(vivekena, 3rd s.)(sarva-)(upādhi-)
body.translated_text: 731. From that very [conventional engagement], the apprehension of the mind, having gone elsewhere, proceeds — by the discrimination of the mere object from all qualifying conditions (<s>upādhis</s>).

body.text:
732.
(ādye, 7th s.)(hetau, 7th s.)(vaiphalyam, 1st s.)(teṣām, 6th pl.)(bhāvitā, 1st s.)(ābhoga-)(samaya-)(eva*)(iṣṭā, 1st s.)(saḥ)(saṃsargī, m. 1st s.)(-vān, 1st s. [-vat suff.])(anvaya-)(vyatireka-)
body.translated_text: 732. In the first reason, there is futility for those [universals]; the disposition toward conventional engagement alone is accepted; that [reason] possesses positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) and negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>).

body.text:
733.
(tasya, 6th s.)(a-bahir-bhāve, 7th s.)(pakṣa-)(nidarśanam, 1st s.)(śūnyam, 1st s.)(sādhya-)(bāhya-)(vatsā-)(aṅkuśa-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(na*)(sākṣāt*)(hetavaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 733. When that [universal] has no external existence, the example is devoid of the property to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>); external [things such as] calves, goads, and so forth are not direct causes of that.

body.text:
734.
(asti ”as)(na*)(vṛttiḥ, f. 1st s.)(vikalpānām, 6th pl.)(abhidhāna-)(sva-lakṣaṇe, 7th s.)(yena, 3rd. s.)(sva-lakṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(mūrttiḥ, 1st s.)(atīta-)(gocara-)(vāg-)
body.translated_text: 734. There is no operation of conceptual constructions (<s>vikalpas</s>) upon the unique particular (<s>sva-lakṣaṇa</s>) — the particular is not within the domain of verbal designation; whereby the unique particular is the form of speech directed toward the past.

body.text:
735.
(te, m. 1st s.)(pravarttante ”vṛt Pr. III p. pl. Āt.)(avalambya ”lamb)(ādi-kam, m. 2nd s.)(aṅkuśa-)(samārūḍham)(antar-mātrā-)(sāṃvṛtam, m. 2nd s.)(bahir-rūpam)(adhyavasitam)
body.translated_text: 735. They proceed by grasping the initial [object such as] a goad — [which is] mounted [upon something]; the external form, determined [by conceptual construction], is concealed by merely internal [representation].

body.text:
736.
(a-bhāvaḥ)(kriyā-)(guṇa-)(vyapadeśa-)(varṇyate ”varṇ pass. Pr. III p. s.)(hetuḥ, m. 1st s.)(pratyayasya, 6th s.)(abhāva-)(iti*)(viśeṣaṇam, 1st s.)(an-arthakam, 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 736. The absence of action, quality, and designation is described as the cause of the cognition of [mere] absence — thus, the qualifier is meaningless.

body.text:
737.
(tat, 1st s.)(api*)(a-yuktam, 1st s.)(hetutve, 7th s.)(vastutā, f. 1st s.)(śakti-taḥ* [-tas suff.])(api*)(ca*)(pratyayaḥ)(abhāva-)(prāptaḥ)(a-viśeṣa-taḥ* [-tas suff.])(sattā-)(ādiṣu, 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 737. That too is unjustified; if [something] has the nature of being a cause, its reality [derives] from [its] capacity; and moreover, the cognition of absence would follow without distinction in <s>sattā</s> (existence) and so forth.

body.text:
738.
(vailakṣaṇyam, n. 1st s. [vilakṣaṇa - ya])(taj-)(jñānānām, 6th pl.)(buddhi-taḥ* [-tas suff.])(piṇḍa-)(ākṛti-)(ādi-)(asiddham)(ataḥ*)(eṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(hetuḥ, m. 1st s.)(bhavati ”bhū)(asiddhaḥ)(api*)
body.translated_text: 738. The difference of those cognitions — from cognition of mass (<s>piṇḍa</s>), configuration (<s>ākṛti</s>), and so forth — is unestablished; therefore this reason is also unestablished.

body.text:
739.
(anvayī, m. 1st s.)(pratyayaḥ)(avabhāsavān, m. 1st s.)(śabda-)(vyakti-)(tu*)(jātiḥ, f. 1st s.)(varṇyate ”varṇ pass. Pr. III p. s.)(śūnyā, f. 1st s.)(ākāra-)(varṇa-)(ākṛti-)(akṣara-)
body.translated_text: 739. The recurring cognition possesses the appearance of word-instances; but <s>jāti</s> (universal) is described as devoid of form, color (<s>varṇa</s>), configuration (<s>ākṛti</s>), and syllable (<s>akṣara</s>).

body.text:
740.
(sāmānyasya, 6th s.)(rūpatve, 7th s.)(nīla-)(ādi-)(api*)(kaḥ, m. 1st s.)(asya, 6th s.)(bhedaḥ)(guṇataḥ* [-tas suff.])(ekaḥ)(anugataḥ)(nīla-ādiḥ, m. 1st s.)(upalabhyate ”labh pass.)
body.translated_text: 740. If [the universal] has the nature of the general (<s>sāmānya</s>), what distinction does it have from blue and so forth in terms of qualities? One recurring [entity such as] blue and so forth is apprehended.

body.text:
741.
(api*)(cet*)(bhāsamānaḥ)(eṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(lakṣyate ”lakṣ pass.)(vivekena, 3rd s.)(katham*)(tau, m. 1st d.)(dhī-)(dhvanī, m. 1st d.)(vartete ”vṛt Pr. III p. d.)(vyaktau, 1st d.)(balena, 3rd s.)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 741. Even if this [universal] is appearing, it is not perceived with distinction; how then do those two — the cognition and the word — operate as two distinct [entities] in the particular, by the force of that [universal]?

body.text:
742.
(paraiḥ, 3rd pl.)(iṣṭaḥ)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(pratyayaḥ)(sāmānya-)(eva*)(ātmakaḥ)(niścaya-)(ca*)(a-grahaṇe, 7th s.)(prāpte, 7th s.)(an-upalakṣaṇam, 1st s.)(na*)(yuktam, 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 742. This cognition is accepted by the opponents as having the nature of the universal alone, and as a determination; when apprehension has not occurred, the absence of characterization is not justified.

body.text:
743.
(api*)(siddhe, 7th s.)(anya-)(nimittatve, 7th s.)(anugāmī, 1st s.)(viviktam, n. 1st s.)(a-drauvyam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(prasiddhyati ”sidh IV C. Pr. III p. s.)(udayāt, 5th s.)(krama-)
body.translated_text: 743. Even when another cause is established, the recurring [universal], being distinct, non-substantial, is not established — because of successive arising.

body.text:
744.
(kam, 2nd s.)(hetum, m. 2nd s.)(śabdaḥ)(padārtha-)(apekṣate ”īkṣ Pr. III p. s. Āt.)(ṣatsu, 7th pl.)(ca*)(pratyayaḥ)(asti ”as)(iti*)(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(anuvarttate ”vṛt)(sattā-)(ādiṣu, 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 744. What cause does the word require for [designating] a category (<s>padārtha</s>)? And in the six [categories], there is a cognition — so it is said — that follows in <s>sattā</s> (existence) and so forth.

body.text:
745.
(cet*)(tatra*)(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(astitā-)(asti ”as)(nimittaḥ)(anya-)(dharma-)(tad*)(an-iṣṭa-)(āsakteḥ, 5th s.)(hetutve, 7th s.)(anya-)(dharma-)(a-)([-tā suff.])([-in suff.])(dharmitā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 745. If there is a cognition of existence there, [and] another property is the cause — that [leads to] the undesired consequence of attachment [to an infinite regress]; when another property has the status of being a cause, [there is] the property of being a locus of [yet another] property.

body.text:
746.
(tataḥ*)(amībhiḥ, 3rd pl.)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(hetuḥ, m. 1st s.)(iṣyate ”iṣ)(vyabhicārī, m. 1st s.)(na*)(ca*)(sarva-upasaṃhārasya, 6th s.)(vyaptiḥ, f. 1st s.)(asya, 6th s.)(prasādhitā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 746. Therefore, by these [arguments], this reason is held to be deviant (<s>vyabhicārī</s>); and the pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) of this [reason] covering all instances has not been established.

body.text:
747.
(sādhanam, n. 1st s.)(sāmānya-)(uddiṣṭam, 1st s.)(tad-anantaram)(nirākṛtam, 1st s.)(anena, 3rd s.)(eva*)(iṣṭa-siddhi-)(ādayaḥ, 1st pl.)(samāḥ, 1st pl.)(tasmin, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 747. The proof that has been set forth for the universal — it has been refuted by this very [argument] immediately after; [objections such as] establishment of the desired conclusion (<s>iṣṭa-siddhi</s>) and so forth apply equally to that [proof].

body.text:
748.
(vinā*)(ekena, 3rd s.)(anugaminā, 3rd s.)(upajāyate ”jan pass.)(viśiṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(pācaka-)(buddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(abhāva-)(abhāve, 7th s.)(ca*)
body.translated_text: 748. Without a single recurring [entity], a qualified cognition arises — [such as] the cognition of 'cook' and so forth; and in the absence of [that universal's] absence,

body.text:
749.
(rūpeṣu, 7th pl.)(racita-)(icchā-)(vā*)(naṣṭa-)(a-jāteṣu, 7th pl.)(sarvaiḥ, 3rd pl.)(ebhiḥ, 3rd pl.)(yathā*)(uditaiḥ, 3rd pl.)(hetoḥ, 6th s.)(anaikāntikatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 749. Or, regarding forms — whether fashioned by desire, destroyed, or not yet arisen — by all these [arguments] as stated, the reason has the fault of being inconclusive (<s>anaikāntikatā</s>).

body.text:
750.
(asti ”as)(na*...kiñcit*)(nibandhanam, n. 1st s.)(buddhīnām, 6th pl.)(pācaka-)(ādi-)(cet*)(karma, n. 1st s.)(asti ”as)(nanu*)(tad, n. 1st s.)(bhidyate ”bhid pass.)(tathā*)(prativyakti, n. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 750. If there is no basis whatsoever for cognitions [such as] 'cook' and so forth — but surely action exists! — [we reply:] that [action] too differs in each individual instance.

body.text:
751.
(iṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(sāmānyam, n. 1st s.)(-mat*)(anuvṛtti-)(sarva-)(vyakti-)(iti*)(a-satve, 7th s.)(anvayinaḥ, 6th s.)(na*)(yuktā, f. 1st s.)(anvayinī, f. 1st s.)(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(bhinneṣu, 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 751. The universal, possessing recurrence in all individuals, is what is accepted [by the opponent]; [but] when the recurring [entity] is non-existent, a recurring cognition among distinct [individuals] is not justified.

body.text:
752.
(ca*)(yadi*)(hetuḥ, m. 1st s.)(prakalpyate ”kḷp pass.)(daridram)(anvaya-)(karma-)(tadā*)(kim* iti*)(vyaktayaḥ, f. 1st pl.)(eva*)(na*)(hetavaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(asyāḥ, f. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 752. And if action is postulated as the meager basis for recurrence — then why are the individuals themselves not the causes of this [cognition]?

body.text:
753.
(ca*)(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(pācaka-)(na*)(syāt ”as Opt.)(tatra*)(kriye, 7th s.)(uparata-)(hi*)(paraiḥ, 3rd pl.)(na*)(iṣṭam, 1st s.)(karma, 1st s.)(sannidhānam, 1st s.)(sadā*)(jāti-vat*)
body.translated_text: 753. And the cognition of 'cook' would not arise there when the action has ceased; for action is not accepted by the opponents as always being present, like <s>jāti</s> (universal).

body.text:
754.
(cet*)(dhī-)(śabdaḥ)(teṣu, 7th pl.)(pācaka-)(ādiṣu, 7th pl.)(nimittī-kṛtya* [cvi cpd.])(atīta-)(an-āgatam, 2nd s.)(karma, 2nd s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(na*)(hetuḥ)(a-sattva-taḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 754. If the word-cognition regarding those [individuals] such as 'cook' and so forth is produced by taking past and future action [as its basis] — that [action] is not a [valid] cause, because of its non-existence [at the time of cognition].

body.text:
755.
(yadi*)(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(yogāt, 5th s.)(kriyā-)(sambandha-)(jāti-)(kriyātva-)(ca*)(upalakṣaṇāt, 5th s.)(dhruva-)(hetu-)(tayā, 3rd s.)(api*)(kriye, 7th s.)(naṣṭa-)
body.translated_text: 755. If the cognition [arises] from the connection with the <s>jāti</s> (universal) of action-ness (<s>kriyātva</s>), and from the characterization [of the individual by that universal] — even so, by being a permanent cause, when the action has ceased,

body.text:
756.
(tatra*)(tu*)(kriye, 7th s.)(naṣṭa-)(jātiḥ, f. 1st s.)(yā, f. 1st s.)(gṛhyate ”grah pass.)(dhruvā, 1st s.)(na*)(vidyate ”vid IV C.)(api*)(lakṣitā, f. 1st s.)(sva-)(ādhāra-)(vinivṛtti-taḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 756. That <s>jāti</s> (universal) which is apprehended as permanent even when the action has ceased — [such a permanent universal] is not found, even when characterized [as such], because of the cessation of its own substratum.

body.text:
757.
(jātīnām, 6th pl.)(daṇḍa-)(aṅgada-)(ādi-)(lakṣaṇe, 7th s.)(ekadā*)(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(daṇḍī-)(ādi- [= `the man with the armlet'])(na*)(pravarttate ”vṛt)(viyoge, 7th s.)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 757. Regarding the defining characteristics of <s>jātis</s> (universals) [such as] stick-ness, armlet-ness, and so forth — the cognition of 'one with a stick,' 'one with an armlet,' and so forth does not arise when there is separation from that [stick or armlet].

body.text:
758.
(atha*)(pācakatva-)(ādi-)(varttate ”vṛt)(eva*)(anyā, f. 1st s.)(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū)(sadyas*)(jāte, 7th s.)(api*)(yogāt, 5th s.)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 758. Now, [if you say] the cognition of 'cook-ness' and so forth persists [regardless] — [then] another cognition would arise immediately even upon [newly] arisen [action], from the connection with that [universal].

body.text:
759.
(cet*)(-vat*)(mati-)(sat-)(ādi-)(no*)(samavāyinī, f. 1st s.)(tadā*)(paścāt*)(api*)(na*)(tatra*)(tathā*)(syāt ”as Opt.)(a-viśeṣataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 759. If [the cognition is] like [the cognition of] existence (<s>sat</s>) and so forth, possessing [an inherent universal] — no, [it is] not inherent [in that way]; then even afterwards it should not be there [in that manner], since there is no difference.

body.text:
760.
(na*)(tayoḥ, 6th d.)(vaiguṇyāt, 5th s.)(svabhāva-)(sambaddha-)(tat-)(katham*)(bhavet ”bhū)(asau, m. 1st s.)(samavāyaḥ)(paścāt*)(tādātmye, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 760. Because of the deficiency of those two — [when the universal is] connected with the intrinsic nature of that [substratum] — how could that <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) arise afterwards, when there is identity [between them]?

body.text:
761.
(yadi*)(vyaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(a-dhruvā, 1st s.)(tadā*)(labheta ”labh Opt.)(atiśayam, 2nd s.)(viguṇam, 1st s.)(rūpam, n. 1st s.)(jāteḥ, f. 6th s.)(na* kadācit*)(nivarttate ”vṛt Āt. Pr. III p. s.)
body.translated_text: 761. If the individual (<s>vyakti</s>) is impermanent, then the form of <s>jāti</s> (universal), [being] defective, would obtain a surplus [character]; [yet the universal] never ceases.

body.text:
762.
(ca*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(pācaka-)(iti*)(ādi, 1st s.)(pradhānam, n. 1st s.)(sādhanam, 1st s.)(kriyāyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(pacana-)(ādi-)(ca*)(prādhānyam, n. 1st s.)(asti ”as)(antare, 7th s.)(pācaka-)
body.translated_text: 762. And [the designation] 'cook' and so forth — that is the principal means of establishing the action; and the primacy [lies] in the cooking and so forth — it exists within [the individual as] 'cook.'

body.text:
763.
(idam, n. 1st s.)(nāma*)(prādhānyam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(śaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(a-samanvayāt, 5th s.)(eva*)(ataḥ*)(avakalpyate ”kḷp pass.)(ātma-)(dravya-)(kriyā-)(guṇa-)(ādi, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 763. This so-called primacy is not a [real] power, because of the lack of connection; therefore, from this alone, substance, action, quality, and so forth — [as well as] self — are postulated [without universals].

body.text:
764.
(tat*)(śemuṣī, f. 1st s.)(pācaka-)(ādiṣu, 7th pl.)(sāpekṣā, f. 1st s.)(bheda-)(saṅketa-)(avasāyinī, f. 1st s.)(mātra-)(rūpa-)(viśleṣi-)(vijātīya-)
body.translated_text: 764. That cognition regarding 'cook' and so forth is dependent on convention regarding distinctions, discerning [mere] form, separating from what is of a different kind.

body.text:
765.
(ataḥ*)(eva*)(śabdāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(ca*)(buddhayaḥ, 1st pl.)(pravartante ”vṛt)(vibhāge, 7th s.)(eva*)(yathā*)(saṅketam, 2nd s.)(vinā*)(ekena, 3rd s.)(anugāminā, 3rd s.)(na*)
body.translated_text: 765. Therefore, words and cognitions indeed operate in [the domain of] division, according to convention; not without a single recurring [entity] —

body.text:
766.
(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(abhāva-)(abhāveṣu, 7th pl.)(na*)(virudhyate ”rudh)(vā*)(anugataḥ)(dhvaniḥ, m. 1st s.)(tayoḥ, 6th d.)(anugamāt, 5th s.)(saṅketa-)(an-)(artha-)
body.translated_text: 766. The cognition of absence is not contradicted in cases of non-absence; or, the recurring word — from the recurrence of those two [cognition and word], [the recurrence derives] from convention, not from a [real] object.

body.text:
767.
(ayam, f. 1st s.)(dhīḥ, f. 1st s.)(prāk-)(a-bhāvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ghaṭasya, 6th s.)(pradhvaṃsaḥ)(ghaṭa-)(iti*)(prapadyate ”pad pass.)(abhāvān, 2nd pl.)(vastu-)(upādhikān, 2nd pl.)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 767. This cognition — 'the prior absence of the pot,' 'the destruction of the pot' — thus it apprehends absences qualified by real things (<s>vastu-upādhikān</s>).

body.text:
768.
(anuvṛttatā, f. 1st s.)(tasyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(sarvatra*)(eva*)(vaśāt, 5th s.)(sāmānya-)(gata-)(upādhi-)(cet*)(na*)(evam*)(vailakṣaṇya-)(a-)(tat-)(āśrayāt, 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 768. The recurrence of that [cognition of absence] everywhere [derives] from the force of the qualifying condition (<s>upādhi</s>) pertaining to the universal; if [you say] not so — [that is refuted] because of depending on [something] not different from that [universal].

body.text:
769.
(a)(anugāminī, f. 1st s.)(buddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(ādika, f. 1st s.)(ghaṭaḥ)(yuktā, 1st s.)(tebhyaḥ, 5th pl.)(na*)(a-bhāvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(eṣā, f. 1st s.)(bhāvaḥ)(tu*)(vilakṣaṇā, 1st s.)(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(tan-)
body.translated_text: 769. The cognition of absence and so forth that follows [its objects] — such as 'pot' — is justified; but this cognition regarding [positive] existence is different from those [cognitions of absence] and is of a distinct character.

body.text:
770.
(ca*)(buddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(gauḥ, f. 1st s.)(aśvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(hi*)(na*)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(vaśāt, 5th s.)(sattā-)(anyathā*)(eva*)(ekam, n. 1st s.)(sāmānyam, n. 1st s.)(kalpyam, 1st s.)(sādhanam, n. 1st s.)(sarva-)
body.translated_text: 770. And the cognition 'cow,' 'horse' — for [this cognition] is not accepted [as arising] from the force of <s>sattā</s> (existence) [alone]; otherwise, one single universal alone would have to be postulated as the means of establishing everything.

body.text:
771.
(cet*)(tasmin, 7th s.)(buddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(na*)(anurūpā, f. 1st s.)(nimitta-)(yataḥ*)(buddhīnām, 6th pl.)(senā-)(ādi-)(iṣṭam, 1st s.)(nibandhanam, n. 1st s.)(sāṅkhyā-)(ādi, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 771. If the cognition [of 'cow' etc.] is not proportionate to the cause in that [<s>sattā</s>] — since for cognitions [such as] 'army' and so forth, the basis that is accepted [by you] is [mere] enumeration (<s>sāṅkhya</s>) and so forth,

body.text:
772.
(yadi*)(iyam, f. 1st s.)(evam*)(kim*)(na*)(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(eṣu, 7th pl.)(bhedeṣu, 7th pl.)(iṣṭā, f. 1st s.)(anusāriṇī, f. 1st s.)(ābhoga-)(bheda-)(saṅketa-)(racita-)(icchā-)
body.translated_text: 772. If this cognition is thus accepted as following the distinctions in these [individuals] — [produced by] convention regarding distinctions, fashioned by desire and intentional engagement — then why is it not [simply accepted as such for all cases]?

body.text:
773.
(sati, 7th s. [loc. abs.])(jñāne, 7th s.)(bheda-)(tataḥ*)(icchā, f. 1st s.)(karaṇe, 7th s.)(saṅketa-)(kṛtiḥ, 1st s.)(tat-)(śrutiḥ, f. 1st s.)(tat-)(ca*)(ābhogaḥ)(asyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(tataḥ*)(matiḥ, 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 773. When there is cognition, [there arises] a desire for distinction; in [using] an instrument, there is the act of convention; the hearing of that [convention]; and the mental engagement with it; from that arises understanding.

body.text:
774.
(idam, n. 1st s.)(samartham, 1st s.)(kāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(tasyām, f. 7th s.)(viniścitam, 1st s.)(eva*)(anvaya-)(vyatirekābhyām, 3rd d.)(anyeṣām, 7th pl.)(an-avasthitiḥ, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 774. This is the competent cause, determined with certainty in that [cognition] — through [the methods of] agreement and difference (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>); for others, there is no [such] stability.

body.text:
775.
(kalpanā, f. 1st s.)(anya-artha-)(iti*)(saṃsargī, 1st s.)(syāt ”as Opt.)(anurūpī, 1st s.)(tu*)(buddhīnam, 6th pl.)(vailakṣaṇye, 7th s.)(eva*)(varam, 1st s.)(āśritam, 1st s.)(iyat, 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 775. [If one says] 'conceptual construction concerns another object' — [then] what is conjoined would be [merely] conforming; but given the dissimilarity of cognitions, it is better to take recourse in just this much.

body.text:
776.
(atra*)(niyamaḥ)(hi*)(sāmārthya-)(kalpanīyaḥ)(ca*)(varam, 2nd s.)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(kalpitaḥ, 1st s.)(śaktiṣu, f. 7th pl.)(jñāta-)(anvaya-)(vyatirekābhyām, 3rd d.)
body.translated_text: 776. Here, a restriction based on capacity must be postulated; and it is better that it be postulated with respect to the powers [of things], known through agreement and difference.

body.text:
777.
(ca*)(vidyate ”vid IV C.)(na*)(anvaya-)(anuvidhānam, n. 1st s.)(sāmānyeṣu, n. 7th pl.)(sadā*)(a-sattvāt, n. 5th s.)(tu*)(vyatirekaḥ)(na*)(sambhavī, m. 1st s.)(nityānām, m. 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 777. And there is no conformance of agreement in universals, because they always do not exist [in all cases]; but [there is] no difference [either], since permanence is impossible [for them].

body.text:
778.
(ādi, 1st s.)(-tva-)(guṇa-)(hetuḥ, m. 1st s.)(dhiyaḥ, 6th s.)(a-dravya-)(ādi-)(na*)(yuktimat, n. 1st s.)(tataḥ*)(ca*)(na*)(samavāyaḥ)(aneka-)(dhiyaḥ, f. 6th s.)(sāmānya-)
body.translated_text: 778. [The argument that] the universal and so forth [is] a non-substantial cause of cognition is not logically sound; and therefore <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) [does not follow] either — from the cognition of a multiplicity of universals.

body.text:
779.
(samavāyaḥ)(aneka-)(vidyate ”vid IV C.)(saṅkhyā-)(ādi-)(api*)(iva*)(sāmānyeṣu, 7th pl.)(iti*)(buddhayaḥ, 1st pl.)(sāmānyam, n. 1st s.)(syuḥ ”as Opt.)(teṣu, 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 779. <s>Samavāya</s> (inherence) is manifold — as is number and so forth — [existing] in universals; thus the cognitions [of universals] would themselves be universals in those [things].

body.text:
780.
(sāmānyam, n. 1st s.)(ghaṭatva-)(ādi, 1st s.)(vartate ”vṛt)(eva*)(ghaṭa-)(ādau, 7th s.)(tu*)(vṛttiḥ, f. 1st s.)(abhāveṣu, 7th pl.)(na*)(tasmāt, 5th s.)(katham*)(dhīḥ, f. 1st s.)(nu*)(teṣu, 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 780. The universal '<s>ghaṭatva</s>' (potness) and so forth exists in pots and so forth; but its occurrence in non-existences is not [the case]; therefore, how [can there be] a cognition in those?

body.text:
781.
(dhī-)(dhvanī, m. 1st d.)(na*)(hi*)(yuktau, 7th s.)(anyatra*)(vṛttāt, 5th s.)(āśraya-)(antara-)(ādau, 7th s.)(karka-)(na*)(hastitva-)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(api*)(āśrayaḥ)(eka-)(artha-)(na*)(atra*)
body.translated_text: 781. For cognition and word are not proper [when applied] to something that exists elsewhere — in another substratum and so forth; [the universal] 'elephanthood' and the like — [there is] no single-object substratum here.

body.text:
782.
(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(rasaḥ)(śītaḥ)(ca*)(guruḥ, m. 1st s.)(syāt ”as Opt.)(āśrayaḥ)(eka-)(artha-)(iha*)(api*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(na* eva*)(a-bhāvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(vartate ”vṛt)(kvacit*)
body.translated_text: 782. [Objection:] Understanding, taste, coldness, and heaviness would have a single-object substratum here too; [reply:] this indeed is not non-existence — it does not occur anywhere.

body.text:
783.
(cet*)(iha*)(asti ”as)(sambandhaḥ)(viśeṣaṇa-)(viśeṣya-)(nanu*)(asau, m. 1st s.)(prakalpyate ”kḷp pass.)(sambandha-antara-)(sad-bhāve, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 783. [Objection:] 'If there is here a relation of qualifier and qualified — [reply:] indeed, that [relation] is to be postulated [only] when the existence of another relation [is established].'

body.text:
784.
(-tā suff.)(viśeṣaṇa-)(viśeṣya-)(kalpyate ”kḷp pass.)(āśritya*)(āsattim, 2nd s.)(tayoḥ, 6th d.)(tu*)(abhāve, 7th s.)(tat-)(sā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(siddhyati ”sidh IV C. Pr. III p. s.)(a-nimittā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 784. The qualifier-qualified relation is postulated by relying on proximity of the two; but in its absence, that [relation] is not established — it would be without a basis.

body.text:
785.
(ayam, m. 1st s.)(vacanam, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(prāg-)(a-bhāvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ghaṭasya, 6th s.)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(nirmāṇam, 1st s.)(mātra-)(kalpanā-)(-vat*)(śūratā-)(ādi-)(kalpite, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 785. This statement: 'the prior non-existence of a pot and so forth is a construction,' [is] like the imagining of a mere fabrication — as in the case of imagined valor and the like.

body.text:
786.
(yatra*)(-tvam, n. 1st s.)(viśeṣaṇa-)(viśeṣya-)(samāśrayam, 1st s.)(vastu-)(avaśyam*)(sad-bhāvaḥ)(antara-)(sambandha-)(prakalpyate ”kḷp)(tathā*)
body.translated_text: 786. Wherever the qualifier-qualified [relation has] a real entity as its basis — necessarily [there must be] the existence of another relation; thus it is postulated.

body.text:
787.
(avacoditam, 1st s.)(atra*)(eva*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(abhāvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(abhāvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(iti*)(ca*)(sāmānyam, n. 1st s.)(-stham)(upādhi-)(vartate ”vṛt)(eva*)(sva-)(āśrayeṣu, 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 787. What has been objected to here is just this: the cognition 'non-existence is non-existence' — the universal, abiding in a limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>), exists only in its own substrata.

body.text:
788.
(na*)(ca*)(iṣṭam, 1st s.)(anuyāyi, n. 1st s.)(sattvam, n. 1st s.)(teṣu, 7th pl.)(buddhayaḥ, 1st pl.)(abhāva-)(na*)(jāyante ”jan pass.)(atirekeṇa, 3rd s.)(ṣaḍ-)(artha-)
body.translated_text: 788. And the existence that follows [things] in those [substrata] is not accepted; the cognitions of non-existence do not arise — beyond the six categories.

body.text:
789.
(ādau, 7th s.)(arthe, 7th s.)(rūpa-)(racita-)(icchā-)(na*)(jātiḥ, f. 1st s.)(vidyate ”vid IV C.)(eva*)(a-sambhavāt, 5th s.)(vyakteḥ, 6th s.)(vyabhicāritā, f. 1st s.)(tat-)(sthitā, 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 789. In the first [of the categories] — an object fashioned with the desire for form — <s>jāti</s> (universal) does not exist at all, because of the impossibility of manifestation; its deviation is thereby established.

body.text:
790.
(atīta-)(anupajāteṣu, 7th pl.)(cet*)(jñānam, 1st s.)(gocaram, 1st s.)(nitya-)(sāmānya-)(tu*)(idam, 1st s.)(kevalam, 1st s.)(sāmānyam, 1st s.)(na*)(gṛhyate ”grah pass.)
body.translated_text: 790. If cognition [takes as its] object things past and unarisen — [but] this universal is merely permanent; [then] the universal alone is not apprehended.

body.text:
791.
(vā*)(kevalasya, 6th s.)(upalambhe, 7th s.)(idam, 1st s.)(na*)(bhavet ”bhū)(sāmānyam, 1st s.)(vyaktīnām, 6th pl.)(na*)(ca*)(vyaṅgyam, 1st s.)(tat-)(iva*)(himālayaḥ)(vindhyasya, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 791. Or, if only the isolated [universal] were apprehended, this would not be a universal; the particulars are not [thereby] manifested — just as <s>Himālaya</s> [is not manifested] from <s>Vindhya</s>.

body.text:
792.
(na*)(hi*)(idam, n. 1st s.)(pratibaddham, 1st s.)(utpatti-)(pāratantryeṇa, 3rd s.)(tāsu, 7th pl.)(pāratantryam, n. 1st s.)(jñāna-)(nityatvāt, 5th s.)(grahāt, 5th s.)(kevala-)
body.translated_text: 792. For this [universal] is not bound by dependence on origination in those [particulars]; [there is] dependence [only] on cognition — because of the permanence [of the universal], from the apprehension of the isolated alone.

body.text:
793.
(a-sambhavāt, 5th s.)(vyapekṣāyāḥ, 6th s.)(ādi-)(yoga-)(sva-)(āśraya-)(indriya-)(vā*)(upalabhyeta ”labh Āt. Opt. III p. s.)(sadā* eva*)(yadi* vā*)(na*)(kadācana*)
body.translated_text: 793. Because of the impossibility of dependence — of one's own substratum, sense faculty, and initial connection — either it would always be apprehended, or never at all.

body.text:
794.
(yogyam, n. 1st s.)(janane, 7th s.)(jñāna-)(ātmani, 7th s.)(sva-)(vā*)(vā*)(eva*)(a-yogyam, n. 1st s.)(ekadā*)(tadā*)(hi*)(bhavet ”bhū Opt.)(sarvadā*)
body.translated_text: 794. [If the universal is] suitable or unsuitable for producing cognition in its own self — if [suitable] at one time, then it would be [suitable] at all times.

body.text:
795.
(rūpam, n. 1st s.)(yogyam, 1st s.)(vā*)(ayogyam, 1st s.)(tasya, 6th s.)(sthitam, 1st s.)(prakṛti-)(tat-)(drauvyāt, 5th s.)(kaḥ nāma*)(calayiṣyati ”cal Fut. III p. s.)(a-prakampyam, 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 795. Whether its form is suitable or unsuitable, it remains established in its own nature; through substantiality, who indeed will set in motion what is immovable?

body.text:
796.
(gotvam, n. 1st s.)(antaram, 1st s.)(artha-)(go-taḥ* [-tas suff.])(viṣayatva-taḥ* [-tas suff.])(bhinna-)(dhīḥ, f. 1st s.)(-vat*)(rūpa-)(sparśa-)(ādi-)(ukteḥ, 5th s.)(tasya, 6th s.)(-vat*)(turaṅga-)(caitra-)
body.translated_text: 796. 'Cowness' (<s>gotva</s>) is different from a cow, in terms of objecthood — just as cognition is differentiated [by its object]; like form, touch, and so forth — as stated regarding that — like a horse and <s>Caitra</s>.

body.text:
797.
(iti*)(uktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(vyabhicāra-)(tathā*)(ādibhiḥ, 3rd pl.)(ca*)(anayā, 3rd s.)(diśā, f. 3rd s.)(sarve, m. 1st pl.)(anye, 1st pl.)(ku-hetavaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(api*)(dūṣyāḥ, m. 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 797. Thus: the statement of deviation and so forth — by this direction, all other fallacious reasons too are to be refuted.

body.text:
798.
(api*)(ca*)(yad, n. 1st s.)(ucyate ”vac pass.)(sāmānyasya, 6th s.)(aneka-vṛttitvam, n. 1st s.)(tatra*)(kā, 1st s.)(iyam, f. 1st s.)(vṛttiḥ, f. 1st s.)(matā, f. 1st s.)(kim*)(sthitiḥ, f. 1st s.)(vā*)(eva*)(vyaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 798. Moreover, regarding what is said about the multiple occurrence (<s>anekavṛttitva</s>) of the universal — what is this 'occurrence' that is accepted? Is it mere abiding, or [is it] manifestation?

body.text:
799.
(tāvat*)(sthitiḥ, f. 1st s.)(a-pracyutiḥ, f. 1st s.)(sva-)(rūpa-)(asya, 6th s.)(svabhāvataḥ* [-tas suff.])(ādhāraḥ)(śaktaḥ)(kṛtau, f. 7th s.)(tat-)(yena, 3rd s.)(bhavet, ”bhū)(sthāpakatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 799. First, abiding is the non-departure from one's own form — by its very nature; [something is] a substratum [only if it is] capable of effecting that; whereby there would be the [status of] establishing [the universal].

body.text:
800.
(api*)(pratibandhaḥ)(gamana-)(na*)(tasya, 6th s.)(-vat*)(badara-)(vidyate ”vid IV C.)(niṣkriya-)(-tvena, 3rd s.)(ataḥ*)(ādhāraḥ)(na*)(prakalpyate ”kḷp pass.)
body.translated_text: 800. Moreover, there is no obstruction of movement for it — like a berry-fruit — because of its being actionless; therefore, a substratum is not to be postulated.

body.text:
801.
(cet*)(sthitiḥ, f. 1st s.)(samavāyaḥ)(tat-)(na*)(tat, 1st s.)(eva*)(vicāryate ”car pass.)(ātmakaḥ)(-tā-)(āśraya-)(āśrayi-)(a-yuta-siddhānām, 6th pl.)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(abhīṣṭaḥ)
body.translated_text: 801. If abiding is [itself] <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) — that very [inherence] is [now] being examined: [whether it is] of the nature of substratum-and-substrate; that [inherence] is desired [to hold] among inseparably-existing things.

body.text:
802.
(jala-)(ādīnam, 6th pl.)(syāt ”as Opt.)(ādhāraḥ)(pratibandhakaḥ)(gamana-)(sāmānyānām, 6th pl.)(a-gatīnām, 6th pl.)(kim*)(ādhāraiḥ, 3rd pl.)(prakalpitaiḥ, 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 802. Water and so forth would have a substratum that obstructs movement; [but] for universals that have no motion — what [need is there] for postulated substrata?

body.text:
803.
(yogyatve, 7th s.)(utpatti-)(sva-)(jñāna-)(kim*)(kāraṇaiḥ, 3rd pl.)(abhivyakti-)(a-yogyatve, 7th s.)(utpatti-)(sva-)(jñāna-)(kim*)(kāraṇaiḥ, 3rd pl.)(abhivyakti-)
body.translated_text: 803. If [the universal] is suitable for the production of its own cognition — what [need is there] for causes of manifestation? If unsuitable for the production of its own cognition — what [use are] causes of manifestation?

body.text:
804.
(yadi*)(samarthaḥ)(hyaḥ*)(kriyate ”kṛ pass.)(samartha-ātmā, m. 1st s.)(vyañjakaiḥ, 3rd pl.)(bhāvaḥ)(bhavet ”bhū Opt.)(a-sthiraḥ)(-vat*)(ghaṭa-)(ādi-)(dīpa-)
body.translated_text: 804. If a powerful [entity] is made powerful by its manifestors — then the [supposedly permanent] entity would be impermanent — like a pot and so forth [made visible by] a lamp.

body.text:
805.
(bhedāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(jāti-)(ghaṭa-)(ādi-)(vṛtti-bhājaḥ, 1st pl. [bhāj- stem])(vā*)(sva-)(eva*)(āśrayeṣu, 7th pl.)(bhaveyuḥ ”bhū Opt. III p. pl.)(sarvatra*)(-vat*)(para-)(jāti-)
body.translated_text: 805. The varieties of <s>jāti</s> (universal), having their occurrence in pots and the like — would either exist only in their own substrata, or everywhere — like another <s>jāti</s>.

body.text:
806.
(vastu-)(prādurbhāve, 7th s.)(antare, 7th s.)(deśa-)(iti*)(na*)(gamyate ”gacch / gam pass.)(katham*)(te, m. 1st pl.)(nu*)(dṛśyante ”paśy / dṛś pass.)(vā*)(vṛttibhājaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(tasmin, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 806. How [the universal] is understood [to occur] in another place-entity — [when] it arises [there] — is not comprehended; and how are they seen to occur in that [place]?

body.text:
807.
(hi*)(na*)(utpannāḥ, m. 1st s.)(saha*)(tena, 3rd s.)(nityatvāt, 5th s.)(na* api*)(avasthitāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(tatra*)(prāk*)(a-vibhutvena, 3rd s.)(na*)(ca*)(āyānti ”yā Pr. III p. pl.)(anyataḥ* [-tas suff.])(a-kriyāḥ, m. 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 807. For they are not born together with that [entity], because of [their] permanence; nor are they stationed there beforehand, because of [their] non-pervasiveness; and they do not come from elsewhere, being actionless.

body.text:
808.
(sati, 7th s. [loc. abs.])(yoga-)(sva-āśraya-)(indriya-)(ādeḥ, 6th s.)(ekasmin, 7th s.)(grahe, 7th s.)(tat-)(upalabhyeran ”labh Opt. III p. pl. Āt.)(sarvatra* eva*)(a-vibhāgataḥ* [-tas suff.])(tat-)(svarūpa-)
body.translated_text: 808. When one's own substratum, sense faculty, and initial connection obtain — in a single apprehension, they [the universals] would be apprehended everywhere without distinction — because of their own nature.

body.text:
809.
(cet*)(a-vyatiriktam, 1st s.)(jñātāt, 5th s.)(bhavet ”bhū Opt.)(grahaṇam, 1st s.)(tasya, 6th s.)(api*)(vā*)(tasya, 6th s.)(na*)(grahaṇam, 1st s.)(eva*)(tad-vat*)(vā*)(eva*)(bhedaḥ)
body.translated_text: 809. If the apprehension is not different from the knower — it would [follow that] its apprehension too [is identical]; or there would be no apprehension of it at all; or likewise there would be [real] difference.

body.text:
810.
(ime, m. 1st pl.)(pratyayāḥ, 1st pl.)(vṛka-)(ādi-)(na*)(jātibhyaḥ, 5th pl.)(kalpita-)(anya-)(ādibhyaḥ, 5th pl.)(tva-)(krami-)(anugama-)(yathā*)(dhiyah, 1st pl.)(pācaka-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 810. These cognitions — of wolves and so forth — are not [derived] from <s>jātis</s> (universals); they are from other imagined [concepts] and so forth — just as cognitions of 'cook' and the like [are derived] from convention and continuous practice.

body.text:
811.
(nityasya, 6th s.)(a-janakatvam, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(bādhakam, n. 1st s.)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(yat, 1st s.)(eva*)(uktam, 1st s.)(dūṣaṇe, 7th s.)(saṃyoga-)(pratibādhakam, 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 811. And the non-productivity of what is permanent is an objection [that] overturns everything; whatever was stated in the refutation — [it] also blocks conjunction.

body.text:
812.
(evam*)(eṣā, f. 1st s.)(jātiḥ, f. 1st s.)(nirākṛtā, f. 1st s.)(ekāntataḥ* [-tas suff.])(bhinna-)(tu*)(abhyupetā, f. 1st s.)(jaiminīya-)(pratiṣetsyate ”sidh II C. Fut. III p. s. Āt.)(syādvāde, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 812. Thus this <s>jāti</s> (universal) is absolutely refuted; but [the <s>jāti</s> that is] accepted as differentiated — that of the <s>Jaiminīyas</s> — will be refuted in [the context of] <s>syādvāda</s> (the doctrine of conditional predication).

body.text:
813.
(punaḥ*)(ete, m. 1st pl.)(viśeṣāḥ, 1st pl.)(ye, 1st pl.)(kalpitāḥ, 1st pl.)(bhāvinaḥ, 1st pl.)(antya-)(api*)(a-sambhavitāḥ, 1st pl.)(vyapohena, 3rd s.)(te, 1st pl.)(kṣaṇāḥ, 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 813. Furthermore, these <s>viśeṣas</s> (particularities) that are postulated — [as] existing in the final [atoms] — are also impossible; by [the method of] exclusion (<s>apoha</s>), those moments [are established].

body.text:
814-816.
(aṇu-)(ākāśa-)(dik-)(ādīnām, 6th pl.)(yadā*)(svarūpam, n. 1st s.)(a-saṅkīrṇam, 1st s.)(tadā*)(upalakṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(vailakṣaṇya-)(etasmāt, 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 814-816. When the own-nature of atoms, space, directions, and so forth is unmixed, then the distinguishing characteristic, [because of] the distinctiveness from this [nature] —

body.text:
815.
(yadi*)(punaḥ*)(te, 1st pl.)(bhaveyuḥ ”bhū Opt. III p. pl.)(miśrībhūta-)(apara-ātmānaḥ, 1st pl.)(api*)(bhāve, 7th s.)(anya-)(upalakṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(vailakṣaṇya-)(na*)(a-vibhrāntam, 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 815. If, on the other hand, they [the particularities] were to have their natures mixed with others — even when [the particular] exists, the distinguishing characteristic [would] not [be] unconfused.

body.text:
816.
(katham*)(upalakṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(vailakṣaṇya-)(teṣu, 7th pl.)(viśeṣu, 7th pl.)(iti*)(cet*)(eva*)(svataḥ* [-tas suff.])(kim*)(na*)(evam*)(matam, 1st s.)(aṇu-)(ādau, 7th s.)(api*)
body.translated_text: [Verse 816] How is [impurity] an indicator among those particulars that are dissimilar? If [you say]: is it not so accepted of its own nature in atoms and the like as well?

body.text:
817.
(yathā*)(a-śucitvam, n. 1st s.)(hi*)(sthitam, 1st s.)(śva-)(māṃsa-)(ādeḥ, 6th s.)(eva*)(svataḥ*)(tu*)(apareṣām, 6th pl.)(yogāt, 5th s.)(tat-)(iha* [lit: `here')(api*)(yadi*)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)
body.translated_text: [Verse 817] Just as the impurity of dog-flesh and the like is inherent in its own nature, but [extends] to others through connection — if that is accepted here as well,

body.text:
818.
(yathā*)(dīpaḥ)(svataḥ*)(sthitaḥ)(prakāśakaḥ)(ghaṭa-)(ādeḥ, 6th s.)(ca*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(niyataḥ)([-tā suff.])(ātmatāyām, f. 7th s.)(prakāśa-)(tat-)(idam, 1st s.)(tathā*)
body.translated_text: [Verse 818] Just as a lamp is self-luminous by its own nature and also illuminates a pot and the like — this is fixed in its own nature as illuminating — this too is likewise.

body.text:
819.
(nanu*)(ca*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(a-śuci-bhāvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sāṃvṛtaḥ)(tu*)(na*)(tāttvikaḥ)(tat*)(katham* nāma*)(bhaviṣyate ”bhū Fut. III p. s.)(svayam*)(vā*)(parataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: [Verse 819] Objection: But this impurity is conventional, not ultimate. Then how can it exist either intrinsically or extrinsically?

body.text:
820.
(athavā*)(api*)(bhāvikatve, 7th s.)(ime, 1st pl.)(bhāvāḥ, 1st pl.)(jāyante ”jan pass.)(aśucayaḥ, 1st pl.)(vaśāt, 5th s.)(śva-)(māṃsa-)(ādi)(nityāḥ, 1st pl.)(na* eva*)(a-janmataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: [Verse 820] Or even granting its [conventional] reality, these entities arise as impure by the force of dog-flesh and the like; they are certainly not permanent, since they are born.

body.text:
821.
(ca*)(prabhāvāt, 5th s.)(pradīpa-)(ādi-)(kṣaṇikāḥ, 1st pl.)(kalaśa-)(ābharaṇa-)(ādayaḥ, 1st pl.)(labhante ”labh Pr. III p. pl. Āt.)(svarūpatām, f. 2nd s.)(utpāda-)(jñāna-)
body.translated_text: [Verse 821] And through the power of lamps and the like, momentary pots, ornaments, and the like attain their own form — through the arising of cognition.

body.text:
822.
(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(vailakṣaṇya-)(na*)(bhāvinī, f. 1st s.)(bala-)(viśeṣa-)(āspadībhūta- [cvi cpd.])(vivāda-)(utpatteḥ, 5th s.)(krama-)(-vat*)(sukha-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: [Verse 822] The cognition of dissimilarity does not arise without the ground of a specific force [causing it] — just as the arising of dispute [occurs only when] a ground of specific difference [exists], like [the cognition of] pleasure and the like [arising] in sequence.

body.text:
823.
(samavāyaḥ)(avagamyate ”gam pass.)(bhāvāt, 5th s.)(mateḥ, 6th s.)(iti* ādi, n. 1st s.)(iha*)(paṭaḥ)(amīṣu, 7th pl.)(tantuṣu, 7th pl.)(punaḥ*)(kaṭaḥ)(vīraṇeṣu, 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: [Verse 823] <s>Samavāya</s> (inherence) is cognized from the existence of the cognition [that says] 'and so on' — here again, [the cognition] 'cloth in these threads', 'mat in these grasses.'

body.text:
824.
(cet*)(saḥ, 1st s.)(a-bhāve, 7th s.)(nibandhanam, n. 1st s.)(asyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(mateḥ, f. 6th s.)(na*)(viśeṣa-)(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(dṛṣṭā, f. 1st s.)(varjitā, f. 1st s.)(antara-)(nimitta-)
body.translated_text: [Verse 824] If, in its absence, the basis of this cognition [is sought] — no specific cognition is seen that is devoid of another cause.

body.text:
825.
(ca*)(a-viśeṣāt, 5th s.)(buddhi-)(iha*)(na*)(vibhidyate ”bhid pass.)(-vat*)(yoga-)(tu* [-vat-tu-eṣa...])(pratīyate, prati-”i, pass. Pr. III p. s.)(sarvasmin, 7th s.)(ekaḥ)(eva*)(-vat*)(bhāva-)
body.translated_text: [Verse 825] And because of no difference, the cognition here is not differentiated — like the connection of [a universal]; but a single entity is perceived in everything — like existence.

body.text:
826.
(ca*)(kāraṇa-)(an-upalabheḥ, 5th s.)(saḥ)(nityaḥ)(eva*)(-vat*)(bhāva-)(hi*)(na*)(kāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(asya, 6th s.)(upalabhyate ”labh pass.)(pramāṇena, 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: [Verse 826] And because of the non-perception of a cause, it would be permanent — like existence. For no cause of this [inherence] is perceived by any means of valid cognition.

body.text:
827.
(tad*)(etad, n. 1st s.)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(iha*)(vartate ”vṛt)(pareṣām, 6th pl.)(eva*)(anurāgeṇa, 3rd s.)(sva-)(siddhānta-)(tu*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(na*)(dṛṣṭam, 1st s.)(laukikam)
body.translated_text: [Verse 827] This cognition operates here [only] through the attachment of the opponents to their own doctrine; but that [cognition] is not seen [to be] worldly [i.e., commonly accepted].

body.text:
828.
(bhūtayoḥ, 7th d.)(ādhāra-)(ādheya-)(hi*)(syāt ”as Opt.)(nānātva-)(lakṣaṇe, 7th s.)(vijñānam, 1st s.)(iti*)(idam, 1st s.)(atra*)(śrīphala-)(ādi-)(ādi-)(kuṇḍa-)(ādau, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: [Verse 828] For in [two] elements [related as] container and contained, there would be cognition in terms of the defining characteristic of multiplicity — this here, in a basin and the like, [with regard to] a wood-apple and the like.

body.text:
829.
(ādīnām, 6th pl.)(paṭa-)(tantu-)(vidyate ”vid IV C.)(na* eva*)(upalakṣaṇam, 1st s.)(nānātvena, 3rd s.)(yena, 3rd s.)(syuḥ ”as Opt. III p. pl.)(buddhayaḥ, 1st pl.)(teṣu, 7th pl.)(iti*)(idam, 1st s.)(atra*)
body.translated_text: [Verse 829] The indicator of multiplicity of cloth and threads, and the like, simply does not exist — by which there would be [distinct] cognitions regarding those. This [is the point] here.

body.translated_text: [Verse 830] In this [matter], fabricated as if by one's own will, the cause [of assuming inherence] does not properly apply to real things; furthermore,

831.
(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(laukikī, f. 1st s.)(eṣā, 1st s.)(śākhāḥ, 1st pl.)(vṛkṣe, 7th s.)(ca*)(śilāḥ, 1st pl.)(age, 7th s.)(upalambhanāt, 5th s.)(nairantarya-)(aṅganaiḥ, 3rd pl.)(pariśiṣṭa-)(ākya-)
body.translated_text: [Verse 831] This is a worldly cognition: 'branches in the tree' and 'rocks in the mountain' — from the continuous perception, through limbs, of the remaining [parts identified by] designation.

832.
(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(tau, 1st d.)(tāsu, 7th pl.)(punaḥ*)(atikrāntam, n. 1st s.)(loka-)(tu*)(iti*)(rūpam, 1st s.)(kriyā-)(ghaṭe, 7th s.)(avagacchati ”gam / gacch)(tādātmyam, 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: [Verse 832] [The statement] 'cognition' — those two [are perceived] in those [threads] — again, has surpassed common [experience]. But the world understands the identity of form and action in a pot.

833.
(hi*)(śabdāḥ, 1st pl.)(rūpa-)(kumbha-)(ādi-)(abhidhāyakāḥ, 1st pl.)(avasthā-)(sarva-)(abhidhānāya, 4th s.)(tat-)(viśeṣa-)(te, 1st pl.)(viniveśita-)(tathā*)
body.translated_text: [Verse 833] For words like 'pot' and 'form' are designators [of the same thing]; they are assigned to those specific [aspects] for the designation of all states.

body.translated_text: [Verse 834] Depending on those [designations], cognition operates with that form — not from <s>samavāya</s> (inherence); since the difference of all [things] is not observed.

body.translated_text: 887. Some say: 'The object exists' — this is the characteristic of what is to be conveyed; it is the same for all words [applied] to cows and the like, [as well as to] <s>apūrva</s> (the unprecedented [Vedic result]), deities, and heaven,

body.translated_text: 890. When the form of the word has been unified with the object through association — thus they declare that word to be <s>abhijalpa</s> (verbal expression),

body.translated_text: 891. By some, the meaning of a word is held to be: the object is the domain of cognition, and external reality is its basis; thus external reality is the known [object]. [For them,] the meaning of a word is external substance,

(samāsataḥ* [-tas suff.])(sarvaḥ)(śabdaḥ)(hetuḥ, 1st s.)(pratibhā-)(abhyāsāt, 5th s.)(yathā*)(artha-)(pratipādane, 7th s.)(bālānām, 6th pl.)(ca*...ca*)(tiraścām, 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 892. In brief, every word is the cause of <s>pratibhā</s> (verbal intuition) through repeated practice, as in the case of children and animals in comprehending meaning,

body.translated_text: 893. In that regard, if 'the object exists' is held to be the expressible meaning — is this [object] a <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular), or a <s>jāti</s> (universal), or a connection [of the two], or something else — a reflection, [or] a cognition?

body.translated_text: 894. The defects of each [of these options] have been stated previously; moreover, usage through differentiation does not obtain when the object alone [is posited], nor is there [anything] to be conveyed,

body.translated_text: 895. From mere existence, [the word] would apply [to everything]; but the view [of the opponent] is that the word 'cow' [refers to what is] qualified by <s>gotva</s> (cowness) and particular object. body.translated_text: 896. If so, there would be denotation of [both] the object and that which possesses those [qualities], and also of the differences; but in the presence of those [qualities in the meaning], the defect [already stated applies], and no other object is seen,

body.translated_text: 897. Even in the denotation of the aggregate, the denotation is clear [only] through the denotation of <s>jāti</s> (universal) and differentia, [which applies to] <s>tapas</s> (austerity), <s>jāti</s> (caste/universal), <s>kriyā</s> (action), and the rest taken collectively,

body.translated_text: 898. But the connection of substance and the rest with their own natures is established through a determined connection; and that real universal has been previously refuted,

body.translated_text: 899. Due to the impossibility [of positing] <s>jāti</s> (universal) and differentia in the form of word and meaning, the form of the word unified with the object is not tenable,

body.translated_text: 900. This <s>jalpa</s> (verbal expression) exists only in cognition, through differentiation; what external connection [could there be]? What difference is there between this [view] and the immediately preceding position of the mental image [as word-meaning]?

body.translated_text: 901. Moreover, the mental image as the meaning of a word has been previously refuted, due to the impossibility of separation from cognition, [and] due to the separation of the pervader,

body.translated_text: 902. And if <s>pratibhā</s> (verbal intuition) has an external object as its domain — [if] the meaning of a word is external — then how, when a single [external object] is fixed, are there varied <s>pratibhās</s> (verbal intuitions)?

body.translated_text: 903. Now if these [intuitions] are objectless, arising merely from <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impressions), then how could there be cognition or activity with respect to external objects?

body.translated_text: 904. If those two [cognition and verbal intuition] are held [to operate] through conviction regarding an external form [projected upon] one's own mental image — [then] the meaning of a word is obtained [as] non-ultimate, because activity [proceeds] thus through error,

body.translated_text: 905. That [error] is not proper if it is without a seed, for it would [then] apply everywhere. If [you say] there is a seed for this — this differentiation [between cases of error] is precisely our position.

body.translated_text: 909. If the activity of the two [speaker and hearer] is [directed at] a coherent form, the intention to speak is from the existence of inference [of meaning] — if external, that is precisely our view.

body.translated_text: 910. But how is it said by you that a word is the maker of the <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) of another? Here only a mere negation is not apprehended in the appearance [of cognition].

body.translated_text: 911. Rather, from a word, the verbal cognition operates with a positive form — [producing] the determinate cognition of 'cow,' 'gavaya' (wild ox), 'elephant,' 'tree,' and so forth.

body.translated_text: 918. Therefore, the form that is determined in [the cognition of] 'cow' — that which is individually [present] in all —

body.translated_text: 919. And if the meaning of a word is imagined as having the form of mere negation — it would be emptiness devoid of any positive character; the expressible would be the non-existence of words.

body.translated_text: 924. In cognition, there is no exclusion [apprehended] from an internal cognition; and from the mere arising of its own nature, that [cognition] bears no other part.
