body.text:
932.
(ca*)(na*...kaścit*)(śaktaḥ)(jñātum*)(go-)(ādīn, 2nd pl.)(sārūpyam, 2nd s.)(a-prasiddha-)(viṣaya-)(apoha-)
body.translated_text: 932. And no one is able to know the similarity of cows and the like — when the domain of <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) is not established.

body.text:
933.
(api*)(ca*)(ṛte*)(anvaya-)(eka-)(dharma-)(na*)(śaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(nirūpayitum*)(apohyān, 2nd pl.)(ādīn, 2nd pl.)(aśva-)(tad*)(apohaḥ)(siddhyate ”sidh)
body.translated_text: 933. Moreover, without the [positive] property of a single co-occurrence (<s>anvaya</s>), there is no capacity to determine the things to be excluded — horses and the like; therefore <s>apoha</s> is established [only with positive content].

body.text:
934.
(pravṛttiḥ)(śabda-)(liṅgayoḥ, 6th s.)(na*)(vinirmuktā, f. 1st s.)(anvaya-)(ca*)(vinā*)(tābhyām, 3rd d.)(na*)(apohaḥ)(na*)(ca*)(anvayaḥ)(a-sādhāraṇe, 7th s.) [i.e., for what is unique or specific)
body.translated_text: 934. The operation of word and inference is not free from co-occurrence (<s>anvaya</s>); and without those two, there is no <s>apoha</s>; and there is no co-occurrence in what is non-common.

body.text:
935.
(apohaḥ)(a-niṣpannaḥ)(kva*)(sāhacaryam, 2nd s.)(kathyatām ”kath Imp. III p. s.)(ca*)(tasmin, 7th s.)(a-dṛśyamāne, 7th s.)(syāt ”as Opt.)(na*)(pramāṇatā, f. 1st s.)(tayoḥ, 6th d.)
body.translated_text: 935. Where <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) is not accomplished — let the concomitance be stated; and in the case of that [concomitance] not being observed, there would be no validity of those two [word and inference].

body.text:
936.
(ca*)(bhavet ”bhū Opt.)(na*)(pratyāyanam, 1st s.)(mātreṇa, 3rd s.)(a-darśana-)(hi*)(a-dṛṣṭatvāt, 5th s.)(sarvatra* eva*)(pratyayaḥ)(na*)(viśiṣyate ”śās pass.)
body.translated_text: 936. And there would be no [valid] communication merely through non-observation; for because of the non-observation [being universal], the cognition [would not be distinguished] anywhere at all.

body.text:
937.
(atha*)(a-sati, 7th s.)(sārūpye, 7th s.)(syāt ”as Opt.)(kalpanā, 1st s.)(apohasya, 6th s.)(kasmāt, 5th s.)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(apohaḥ)(a-go-)(na*)(kalpyate ”kḷp pass.)(go-)(aśvayoḥ, 6th d.)
body.translated_text: 937. Now, when there is no similarity, would the construction of <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) arise? Why then is the <s>apoha</s> of non-cow not constructed between cow and horse?

body.text:
938.
(ca*)(bhinnatvam, n. 1st s.)(śābaleyāt, 5th s.)(samam, 1st s.)(bahuleya-)(aśvayoḥ, 6th d.)(cet*)(na*)(anyat, 1st s.)(sāmānyam, n. 1st s.)(iṣṭam, 1st s.)(kva*)(apohaḥ)(a-go-)(pravarttatām ”vṛt Imp. III p. s.)
body.translated_text: 938. And the difference from a <s>Śāvaleya</s> (particular breed of cow) is equal for a <s>Bahuleya</s> (another breed) and a horse; if no other universal is desired — where should the <s>apoha</s> of non-cow operate?

body.text:
939.
(api*)(apohaḥ)(a-go-)(na*)(prathamam*)(vyavasīyate; vi-ava-”so pass.)(indriyaiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(ca*)(vṛttiḥ, f. 1st s.)(śabda-)(na*)(anyatra*)(dṛṣṭvā*)(kim, 2nd s.)(saḥ)(prayujyatām ”yuj pass. Imperative III p. s.)
body.translated_text: 939. Moreover, the <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) of non-cow is not first ascertained by the senses; and the function of words is not [operative] elsewhere — having seen what, should it be applied?

body.text:
940.
(uktena, 3rd s.)(pūrva-)(vidyate ”vid IV C.)(na*)(anumā, f. 1st s.)(api*)(atra*)(tena, 3rd s.)(api*)(na* eva*)(anubhavaḥ)(sambandha-)(asya, 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 940. By what was said before, there is no inference here either; therefore, indeed, there is no experience of its connection.

body.text:
941.
(katham* punaḥ*)(gamyatām ”gam/gacch pass. Imperative III p. s.)(-tvam, n. 2nd s.)(a-)(abhidheya-)(śabda-)(go-)(śabdaḥ)(go-)(na*)(dṛṣṭaḥ)(kṣaṇe, 7th s.)(yatra*)(anubhava-)(sambandha-)
body.translated_text: 941. How, then, should one proceed — regarding the non-denotability of words for 'cow'? The word 'cow' is not observed at that moment of experiential connection.

body.text:
942.
(tarhi*)(sarvam, 1st s.)(eva*)(yat, 1st s.)(piṇḍāt, 5th s.)(go-)(bhavet ”bhū Opt.)(apohyam, 1st s.)(iti* etena, 3rd s.)(na*)(sāmānyasya 6th s.)(vācyatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 942. Then, whatever would be excludable from the individual cow — thereby the denotability of the universal is [not established].

body.text:
943.
(ca*)(siddhaḥ)(a-gauḥ, m. 1st s.)(apohyeta ”ūh Āt. Opt. III p. s.)(ca*)(saḥ)(ātmakaḥ)(niṣedha-)(go-)(tatra*)(gauḥ, 1st s.)(eva*)(vaktavyaḥ)(yaḥ)(pratiṣidhyate ”sidh pass.)(nañā, 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 943. And the non-cow is established [as] that which would be excluded; and that whose nature is negation — there the cow alone is to be stated as what is negated by the negative particle.

body.text:
944.
(cet*)(saḥ)(bhavet ”bhū Opt.)(ātmā, m. 1st s.)(nivṛtti-)(a-go-)(saṃśrayaḥ)(anyonya-)(cet*)(gauḥ, 1st s.)(siddhaḥ)(artham*)(apoha-)(prakalpanam, n. 1st s.)(apoha-)(vṛthā*)
body.translated_text: 944. If the <s>ātman</s> (self) of the non-cow were the basis of the mutual exclusion [between cow and non-cow] — if the cow were [thereby] established — the imagining of <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) would be in vain, purposeless.

body.text:
945.
(tu*)(go-)(a-siddhe, 7th s.)(asti ”as)(na*)(a-gauḥ, 1st s.)(tu*)(tat-)(a-bhāve, 7th s.)(kutaḥ*)(gauḥ, 1st s.)(a-bhāvayoḥ, 6th d.)(na*)(sambandhaḥ)(ādheya-)(ādhāra-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 945. But when the cow is not established, there is no non-cow; and in the absence of that, whence the cow? In the case of the non-existence of both, there is no relation of container and contained and the like.

body.text:
946.
(ca*)(vastu, n. 1st s.)(a-sādhāraṇam, 1st s.)(na*)(gamyate ”gam /gacch pass.)(-vattayā, f. 3rd s.)(apoha-)(katham* vā*)(sambandhaḥ)(parikalpyeta ”kḷp pass.)(vastu-)(a-vastunoḥ, 6th d.)
body.translated_text: 946. And a non-common real thing is not understood through the nature of <s>apoha</s>; how then can a connection between a real thing and a non-real thing be imagined?

body.text:
947.
(na*)(kiṃcit*)(viśeṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(mātreṇa, 3rd s.)(sattva-)(svarūpa-)(tat, n. 1st s.)(yena, 3rd s.)(viśeṣyam, 1st s.)(rajyate ”raj pass.)(sva-buddhyā, 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 947. No qualifier — by the mere nature of being — by which the qualificand is colored by one's own cognition —

body.text:
948.
(śabdena, 3rd s.)(aśva-)(ādi-)(na*)(jāyate ”jan pass.)(bodhanam, 1st s.)(apoha-)(ca*)(buddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(viśeṣya-)(iṣṭā, f. 1st s.)(iha*)(na*)(viśeṣaṇā, f. 1st s.)(a-jñāta-)
body.translated_text: 948. The cognition of <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) of horse and the like does not arise from the word; and the cognition of the qualificand is desired [by you] here — not the cognition of the unknown qualifier.

body.text:
949.
(ca*)(viśeṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(kuryāt ”kṛ Opt.)(jñānam, 2nd s.)(-dṛś, 2nd s.)(anyā-)(rūpam, 2nd s.)(katham*)(ca*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(ucyate ”vac pass.)(viśeṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(jñāne, 7th s.)(anyādṛśe, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 949. And the qualifier would not produce a cognition of a different form; and how can that be called a qualifier in a cognition of a different kind?

body.text:
950.
(atha*)(sati, 7th s. [loc. abs.])(kalpanā, f. 1st s.)(viśeṣaṇa-)(syāt ”as Opt.)(tathā*)(api*)(viśeṣye, 7th s.)(anyathā*)(hi*)(yat, 1st s.; kiṃcit*)(prapadyeta ”pad pass. Opt. III p. s.)(viśeṣaṇam, 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 950. If, when [the qualifier] exists, the construction would be a qualifier — even so, regarding the qualificand, [it is] otherwise; for whatever becomes a qualifier [must be related to] the qualificand.

body.text:
951.
(viśeṣye, 7th s.)(rūpe, 7th s.)(gamya-)(a-bhāva-)(na*)(vastutā, f. 1st s.)(ataḥ*)(te, 6th s.)(asti ”as)(na*)(vastu, n. 1st s.)(vācyam, n. 1st s.)(viśeṣitam, n. 1st s.)(apohena, 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 951. Since there is no reality of [something] apprehensible in the form of the qualificand, therefore there is no real entity expressible [by it]; [what is] qualified by <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) [has no real referent].

body.text:
952.
(yadi* api*)(vṛttiḥ, f. 1st s.)(śabda-)(liṅgayoḥ, 6th d.)(na*)(nirmukte, 7th s.)(apoha-)(tathāpi*)(bodhaḥ)(avalambate ”lamb Āt.)(jñātum*)(vastu, n. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 952. Even though the operation of word and inferential mark is not [directed] toward [something] free from <s>apoha</s> (exclusion), nevertheless, awareness relies [on apoha] in order to know a [real] thing.

body.text:
953.
(ca*)(a-sādhāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(vastu, n. 1st s.)(na*)(viparivarttate ”vṛ Āt.)(buddhau, 7th s.)(na*)(ca*)(yuktā, f. 1st s.)(adhigamyatā, f. 1st s.)(tasya, 6th s.)(nirvikalpatvāt, 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 953. And a unique particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) does not transform itself in cognition; nor is its apprehensibility appropriate, because of its being free from conceptual construction (<s>nirvikalpa</s>).

body.text:
954.
(śabena, m. 3rd s.)(a-gamyamānam, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(iti*)(sāhasam*)(tena, 3rd s.)(viśeṣyam, n. 1st s.) (sāmānyam, n. 1st s.)(eṣṭavyam, n. 1st s.)(viṣayaḥ)(buddhi-)(śabdayoḥ, 6th d.)
body.translated_text: 954. And [to say] that [the particular is] not apprehended by words — that is rash; therefore the qualificand must be accepted as a universal — the object of both cognition and word.

body.text:
955.
(yadā*)(vyaktīnām, 6th pl,)(apohyatā, f. 1st s.)(a-)(vācyatvāt, 5th s.)(śabda-)(tadā*)(sāmāmyam, n. 1st s.)(apohyeta ”ūh Āt. Opt. III p. s.)(ca*)(tasya, 6th s.)(apohāt, 5th s.)(vastutā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 955. When the individuals are excludable by words — because of their inexpressibility — then the universal too would be excluded; and from its exclusion, it would have the status of a [real] thing.

body.text: 956. "Mere negations (a-bhāvānām, 6th pl.)(na*)(apohyatvam, n. 1st s.)(varjanāt, 5th s.)(a-bhāva-)(a-bhāva-)(tasmāt, 5th s.)(vyaktaḥ)(apoha-)(antara-)(apoha)(vastunaḥ, n. 6th s.)(sāmānya-)
body.translated_text: 956. Non-existences are not excludable, because of the exclusion of non-existence from non-existence; therefore, the <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) of the universal — the inner exclusion — [applies to] the [real] thing.

body.text:
957.
(cet*)(a-bhavaḥ)(a-bhāvasya, 6th s.)(vilakṣaṇaḥ)(tasmāt, 5th s.)(bhavet ”bhū)(bhāvaḥ)(eva*)(no*)(cet*)(gauḥ, m. 1st s.)(prasajyate ”sajj)(a-gauḥ, m. 1st s.)(te, 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 957. If the non-existence of non-existence is of a different character from that [non-existence], then it would be an existent entity; if not, then for you, a cow would absurdly become a non-cow.

body.text:
958.
(anyeṣu, m. 7th s.)(śabdeṣu, m. 7th s.)(vastunaḥ, 6th s.)(syāt ”as)(apohyatā, f. 1st s.)(yu*)(sat-)(na*)(bhinnam, n. 1st s.)(ākhyāt, 5th s.)(a-bhāva-)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(apohyam, 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 958. In other words, the thing would be excludable — [which is] indeed a real existent; what is different from the designation of non-existence is accepted as excludable.

body.text:
959.
(tatra*)(api*)(a-sataḥ, 6th s.)(bhāvatvam, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(mahān, m. 1st s.)(kleṣaḥ)(tat-)(a-siddhau, 7th s.)(asti ”as)(sattā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(ca*)(a-sattā, f. 1st s.)(prasiddhyati ”siddh IV C. Pr. III p. s.)
body.translated_text: 959. In that case too, there would be the great difficulty [that] a non-existent has the status of an existent; when that is not established, there is existence [of the universal]; and non-existence is not established.

body.text:
960.
(api*)(na*)(ca*)(bhedaḥ)(api* vā*)(sadrūpatā, f. 1st s.)(apohānām, 6th pl.)(prakalpyeta ”kḷp Opt. III p. s.)(bhedāt, 5th s.)(vāsanā-)(hi*)(sā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(matā, f. 1st s.)(a-vastuni, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 960. Moreover, neither a difference nor an identity of form among the <s>apohas</s> (exclusions) can be conceived; for from [their] difference, that <s>vāsanā</s> (latent tendency) is not accepted in a non-entity.

body.text:
961.
(bhavadbhiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(na*)(api*)(labhyate ”labh pass.)(bhedaḥ)(śabda-)(nimittaḥ)(tat-)(hi*)(na*)(a-sādhāraṇaḥ)(vācakaḥ)(śabdaḥ)(a-dṛṣṭitaḥ* [-tas suff.])(prāk*)
body.translated_text: 961. Nor is a word-occasioned difference obtained by you; for a word is not an exclusive designator, since [such a function is] not seen previously.

body.text:
962.
(tatra*)(sāmānye, 7th s.)(parikalpite, 7th s.)(apohe, 7th s.)(antara-)(śabda-)(a-vasturūpatvāt, 5th s.)(eva*)(tathā*)(bhedaḥ)(śabda-)(na*)(kalpyate ”kḷp pass.)
body.translated_text: 962. Therein, when a word-internal <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) is conceived as the universal — since it is of the nature of a non-real-entity — a word-[occasioned] difference is not conceived.

body.text:
963.
(yathā*)(vācakānām, 6th pl.)(evam*)(vācya-)(vācakayoḥ, 6th d.)(ca*)(mithaḥ)(ca* api*)(iti*)(asti ”as)(na*)(bhedaḥ)(bhedena, 3rd s.)(apohya-)(upapāditam, 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 963. Just as among the designators, so too between the designatum and designator, and mutually — there is no difference; it has been demonstrated through the difference of what is to be excluded.

body.text:
964.
(syāt ”as Opt.)(na*)(gamya-)(gamakatvam, 1st s.)(apohayoḥ, 6th d.)(a-vastutvāt, 5th s.)(bhavat-pakṣe, 7th s.)(yathā*)(kha-puṣpa-)(śaśa-śṛṅgayoḥ, 6th d.)(loke, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 964. There would be no relation of signified and signifier between the two <s>apohas</s> (exclusions), since [they are] non-entities — on your thesis — just as between a sky-flower and a hare's horn in the world.

body.text:
965.
(yad*)(dṛṣṭvā*)(vṛṣṭi-)(megha-)(a-satoḥ, 6th d.)(vadet ”vad Opt. III p. s.)(an-aikāntikam, 2nd s.)(mat-pakṣe, 7th s.)(eva*)(astu ”as Imperative III p. s.)(vastu, 1st s.)(atra*)(kutaḥ*)(api*)(adaḥ*)
body.translated_text: 965. Whatever one might say upon seeing a rain-cloud — [that] for [a pair of] non-existents [the relation] is non-invariable — on our thesis, let the thing here [be established] from some [source] or other.

body.text:
966.
(ca*)(yena, 3rd s.)(na*)(abhupagamyate ”gam / gacch pass.)(arthaḥ)(śabda-)(vidhi-)(rūpaḥ)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(na*)(vyatirekaḥ)(tasya, 6th s.)(api*)(asau, m. 1st s.)(pūrvakaḥ)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 966. And by whom the positive meaning of words is not accepted — for him there would be no negative concomitance either; for that [negative concomitance] too presupposes that [positive meaning].

children.translated_text: What is accepted here as the expressibility of mere <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) — [there is] no establishment of the qualifier-qualificand [relation] and co-reference; in words such as 'blue lotus' that designate [complex objects],

body.text: (śabala-)(artha-)(hi*)(vyudāse, 7th s.)(a-nīlatva-)(cyutiḥ, f. 1st s.)(an-utpala-)(na* api*)(itarataḥ* [-tas suff.])(tatra*)(tasmāt, 5th s.)(na*)(viśeṣya-)(viśeṣaṇe, n. 1st d.)
body.translated_text: when the variegated object is excluded — there is [neither] the exclusion of non-blueness nor of non-lotusness from the other [side]; therefore, [there is] no qualifier-qualificand [relation].

body.text: (na* api*)(te, n. 1st d.)(syātām ”as Opt. III p. d.)(śabdayoḥ, 6th d.)(an-apekṣayoḥ, 6th d.)(abhidheya-)
body.translated_text: Nor would the two be the denotata of the two words, which are independent of each other.

970.
(ca*)(sāmānādhikaraṇyam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(bhinnatvāt, 5th s.)(apohayoḥ, 6th d.)(cet*)(iṣyeta ”iṣ Opt.)(tat, 1st s.)(arthataḥ* [-tas suff.])(kīdṛśyā, f. 1st s.)(adheyatā, f. 1st s.)(tayoḥ, 6th d.)
body.translated_text: 970. And there is no co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>), because of the difference of the two <s>apohas</s> (exclusions); if that [co-reference] is desired — in what manner would the two [have] a common substratum?

body.text:
971.
(na*)(asādhāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(gamyate ”gam / gacch pass.)(ca*)(anyat, n. 1st s.)(na*)(asti ”as)(te, 6th s.)(kva*)(upayujyate ”yuj pass.)(ekārthyam, n. 1st s.)(śabdayoḥ, 6th d.)(a-gamyamānam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 971. The unique particular is not apprehended; and there is nothing else belonging to it; where is the co-referentiality of the two words applied — [when it is] not apprehended?

body.text:
972.
(atha*)(abhidhīyate ”dhā pass.)(iti*)(vācyam, n. 1st s.)(vastu, n. 1st s.)(-vat, n. 1st s.)(apoha-)(tatra*)(api*)(vyāptiḥ, f. 1st s.)(śabdena, 3rd s.)(durlabhā, f. 1st s.)(tantratvāt, 5th s.)(para-)
body.translated_text: 972. If [one says] that the thing expressed is like an <s>apoha</s> (exclusion)-entity — even there, the pervasion by the word is hard to obtain, because of [its] dependence on the other [system].

body.text:
973.

body.translated_text: 973. There is no connection of <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) with gender, number, and the like — the manifestation [of these in apoha] is inexpressible; that [apoha] does not exist through that channel either.

body.text:
974.
(ākhyāteṣu, 7th pl.)(nivṛttiḥ, f. 1st s.)(anyasya, 6th s.)(na*)(sampratīyate; prati-”i, pass. Pr. III p. s.)(hi*)(tatra*)(vidyate ”vid IV C.)(na*)(niṣedhyam)(paryudāsa-rūpam, 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 974. In verbs, the cessation of the other is not cognized; for therein there is nothing to be negated — [no] exclusionary form is found.

body.text:
975.
(hi*)(api*)(iti*)(na* na*)(ucyamāne, 7th s.)(niṣedhanam, 1st s.)(niṣedhasya, 6th s.)(iti*)(a-niṣiddham, n. 1st s.)(pacati ”pac)(tiṣṭhati ”sthā III C. Pr. III p. s.)(very*)(svarūpeṇe, 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 975. For even when 'not-not' is being uttered, the negation of the negation — [that which is] not negated — [such as] 'he cooks' — remains in its own form.

body.text:
976.
(ca*)(tatra*)(pratyayaḥ)(sādhyatva-)(tathā*)(rūpaṇam, 1st s.)(bhūta-)(ādi-)(apohasya, 6th s.)(niṣpannatvāt, 5th s.)(prasajyate ”sañj pass.)(nirnimittam, 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 976. And therein the cognition [requires] the status of something to be established; the depiction of the <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) of past [entities] and so forth would then be without a basis.

977.

body.translated_text: 977. In the aggregate of objects, the depiction of the positive [meaning] and so forth — and what kind of <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) would there be of the other, [when it is] in reasoning, by a negation particle of a negation particle?

body.translated_text: 978. And there is no connection of the negation particle [with the meanings] and so forth; therefore the non-exclusion in the meaning of the sentence — the cessation of the other — cannot be designated.

body.translated_text: 979. The non-exclusion-of-the-other in the initial word — from where is it established as expressible? But the excludable — of the word, of the knowable, of the object of valid cognition — from the initial word.

(kalpanāyām, f. 7th s.)(apohya-)(varam*)(kalpitam)(vastu, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(niṣedhāt, 5th s.)(ākāra-)(jñāna-)(arthaḥ)(abhidhīyate ”dhā pass.)(na*)(antara-)
body.translated_text: 980. In the construction of what is to be excluded — it is better to accept a constructed real thing itself; the object [referred to] is not expressed from the negation of the form of cognition — [there is] no intermediary.

body.text:

body.translated_text: 981. And there is no excludability from that; therefore the excludable is not established — of words and so forth, in those [entities]; thus the excludable is not established.

982.

body.translated_text: 982. What object of all words is to be conceived? For the one whose exclusion of non-everything [is intended] — of what [would there be] no negation?

body.text:

(cet*)(iti*)(eka-)(ādi-)(a-sarvam, n. 1st s.)(prasajyate ”sañj pass.)(apohaḥ)(artha-)(aṅgānām, 6th pl.)(pratiṣiddhatvāt, 5th s.)(ca*)(an-iṣṭaḥ)(aṅginaḥ, 6th s.)(pṛthak*)
body.translated_text: 983. If 'non-all' [is the meaning] of 'one' and so forth — [then] the <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) of the meaning would follow absurdly; and since the parts are negated, the undesired [consequence follows] — [namely,] the whole [is negated] separately.

body.text:
984.
(evam*)(arthe, 7th s.)(śabda-)(samūha-)(vyapohataḥ* [-tas suff.])(samudāyi-)(ca*)(sarve, 7th s.)(prāpnuvanti ”āp Pr. III p. pl.)(nir-)(arthakāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(anya-)(an-iṣṭeḥ, 5th s.)."
body.translated_text: 984. Thus, when the aggregate meaning of words is excluded, all collective [terms] would obtain meaninglessness — because of the undesired [consequence involving] the other.

body.text:

(ca*)(śabdāḥ, 1st pl.)(dvi-)(ādi-)(ye, 1st pl.)(gocarāḥ, 1st pl.)(samuccaya-)(pratiṣedhena, 3rd s.)(eka-)(ādi-)(na*)(bhaveyuḥ ”bhū Opt. III p. pl.)(tathāvidhāḥ, 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 985. And words that have 'two' and so forth as their domain — through the negation of the aggregate — [words like] 'one' and so forth would not be of such a kind.

body.text:
986.
(arthaḥ)(śabdasya, 6th s.)(go-)(ucyate ”vac pass.)(na*)(a-gauḥ, m. 1st s.)(iti*)(kim*)(saḥ)(bhāvaḥ)(athavā*)(a-bhāvaḥ)(vā*)(bhāvaḥ)(gauḥ, m. 1st s.)(athavā* api*)(a-gauḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 986. The meaning of the word 'cow' is said to be 'not a non-cow' — is that a positive entity or a non-entity? Or [is] the positive entity a cow, or else a non-cow?

body.translated_text: 987. If [the meaning is] 'cow' — there is no dispute; but let the meaning be of a positive character. If [the meaning is] 'non-cow' — [that is] expressible by the word 'cow' — [then] the skill in the meaning of words [is lost].

body.translated_text: 988. Moreover, this [meaning as] non-entity is not appropriate, because of the impossibility of injunctions and so forth; for no one apprehends a non-entity from the word 'cow'.

989.
(ca*)(kasmāt, 5th s.)(arthaḥ)(śabda-)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(apohaḥ)(iti*)(gauḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(a-gauḥ)(hi*)(kena, 3rd s.)(āsaktam, 1st s.)(a-gotvam, n. 1st s.)(gauḥ, m. 1st s.)(etat, m. 1st s.)(apohyate ”ūh pass.)
body.translated_text: 989. And why is <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) accepted as the meaning of words? [When one says] 'cow,' by whom is non-cowness attached [to it]? This [cow] — 'cow' — is excluded from [being] a non-cow.

body.translated_text: 990. Is the <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) of a non-cow in a cow the meaning of the word? Is that [apoha] accepted as different from the cow, or as non-different?

body.translated_text: 991. Would [the apoha] be different, or dependent [on the cow], or independent? If dependent, the attribute [of being a quality] is obtained; then the statement of [it being a] substance [is contradicted].

body.translated_text: 992. Therefore, by the word 'cow' — the [denotation] would be merely a quality of designation; there is no co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>); 'the cow moves, the cow stands' —

body.text:

body.translated_text: 993. Now, if no object whatsoever, without being referred [to a universal], would exist — by what could it be designated? [You say] 'for the negation of non-cow' —

(atha*)(ca*)(apohaḥ)(anya-)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(tvayā, 3rd s.)(a-vyatiriktaḥ)(ayam, 1st s.)(ataḥ*)(prāptaḥ)(gauh, m. 1st s.)(eva*)(kim, 1st s.)(adhikam, 1st s.)(tataḥ*)(uktam, 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 994. Now, if the exclusion of the other (<s>anyāpoha</s>) is accepted by you as non-different [from the object] — then what has been arrived at is just the cow [itself]; what more has been said?

995.

body.translated_text: 995. Is this exclusion (<s>apoha</s>) one per each entity, or is it many? If one — then with many cows, it would simply be cowness (<s>gotva</s>) [i.e., a universal].

body.translated_text: 996. Moreover, if [the exclusions are] many, [there follows] infinitude — like [that of] lumps [of matter]; therefore, through that very [difference], its expressibility [in speech] is not useful.

body.translated_text: 997. Is this exclusion of the other (<s>anyāpoha</s>) accepted as expressible or as inexpressible? If expressible — is it through a positive assertion or through the negation of the other?

body.translated_text: 998. If it is expressible through its own positive nature — then the one-sided [negative] view must be abandoned; [for] what has been described everywhere — this meaning is [merely] the rejection of the other by the word.

body.translated_text: 999. If, however, <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) is expressed through the elimination of [another] <s>apoha</s> — then there would be an infinite regress, since at each point [one needs another exclusion].

1000.

body.translated_text: 1000. If, on the other hand, this <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) is accepted by you as inexpressible — then your statement 'words effect exclusion of the other' would be contradicted.

body.translated_text: 1001. Moreover, [if you maintain] oneness, permanence, and inherence — [while] making [exclusions] individual — in exclusions that are without designation, [your position is like] cloth without thread.

body.translated_text: 1002. Therefore, the portion of the negation of the other would exist in those words in which only the negative particle (<s>nañ</s>) is conjoined; elsewhere, the [word's] own meaning alone is understood.

body.translated_text: 1003. These fallacious views regarding the exclusion of the other (<s>anyāpoha</s>) — [held by] evil-natured [opponents] — [who are] themselves destroyed, they destroy others too.

body.text:
1004.
(tathā*)(hi*)(apohaḥ)(dvi-vidhaḥ)(paryudāsa)(niṣedhataḥ* [-tas suff.])(paryudāsaḥ)(api*)(dvi-vidhaḥ)(bhedataḥ* [-tas suff.])(ātma-)(buddhi-)(ātma-)
body.translated_text: 1004. Thus, <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) is twofold — from [the distinction of] <s>paryudāsa</s> (implicative negation) and <s>niṣedha</s> (absolute negation); and <s>paryudāsa</s> too is twofold — in terms of the object-self and the cognition-self.

body.translated_text: 1005. The objects previously stated — equal [in status], differentiated [as] fearlessness and the like — are the causes of the other [type of exclusion]; [they are causes] of a single reflective awareness.

(a-bhāve, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 1006. Depending on those [objects], a reflection (<s>pratibimba</s>) appears in constructive cognition; what is determined thus — [these are] objects too — in the absence of real object-nature.

body.translated_text: 1007-1009. Because of difference, by virtue of being the cause of an internal appearance — through the access to the real thing that is excluded from others — through the avenue of the real, even though not [directly] connected with the real — through determination, the result [is obtained] in that [real object]; the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) is turned away from what is different in kind; through [mistaken] identification of it with that — therein, this designation '<s>anyāpoha</s>' (exclusion of the other) is said to have a basis; even in the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>, the cause — because of its being of that nature, the separation from others.

body.translated_text: 1010. And this <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s> (absolute negation): 'a cow is, it is not a non-cow' — the exclusion of the other is apprehended very clearly.

body.translated_text: 1011. This first [type of] <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) is conveyed by words; because of the arising of cognition — by words [directed to] the external object, through determination.

1012.

body.translated_text: 1012. And in the arising of cognition, the reflection (<s>pratibimba</s>) [has] the nature of word and referent (<s>vācya-vācaka</s>), born from the word — [it has] the form of cause and effect.

body.translated_text: 1013-1014. When this form is directly conveyed — thus the <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s> (absolute negation) too is understood through [its] capacity; thus — it is of the nature of that, not of the nature of the other; when there is a connection with real things, the comprehension of the real thing that is excluded [from others follows] even indirectly.

body.translated_text: 1015. Therefore this too is figuratively applied — [as] 'the meaning of the word'; but this is twofold: the verbal <s>apoha</s> — it is not directly stated.

body.translated_text: 1016. The verbal expression, effecting exclusion of the other's meaning — expresses its own meaning; this is non-contradictory.

body.translated_text: 1017. This [word] produces the reflection (<s>pratibimba</s>) [which is] engaged through determination with the external object.

body.translated_text: 1018. But this [reflection] does not touch the differentiated self, the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) — beyond [its own] portion; there is no action of it [beyond that].

body.translated_text: 1019. In the movement of that reflection, the separation from others is followed — through [its own] capacity; since the nature of being other does not [truly] belong to it.

body.translated_text: 1023. And through determination, the real thing is called 'real thing'; for that is indeed a mistaken cognition, arising instantly from its own seed.

body.text:
1024.
(saḥ)(eva*)(ucyate ”vac pass.)(apohaḥ)(arthaḥ)(śabda-)(ākāra-)(tat-)(sāmānyam, 1st s.)(rūpam, 1st s.)(vastu-)(avasāyataḥ* [-tas suff.])(tathā*)(bhrāntyā, f. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 1024. That alone is called the <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) — the meaning of the word — having the form of the word; the universal is the form [projected] through the determination of the real — thus through error.

body.text:
1025.
(na*)(yuktam, 1st s.)(asya, 6th s.)(rūpatvam, 1st s.)(sāmānya-)(vastu-)(bhāvikam, 1st s.)(hi*)(an-anyarūpam, 1st s.)(buddheḥ, 5th s.)(katham*)(yāyāt ”yā Opt. III p. s.)(antaram, 2nd s.)(artha-)
body.translated_text: 1025. The nature of being a real universal is not proper for it; for, being of no other form [than cognition], how could it go [i.e., apply] to another object, from cognition?

body.text:
1026.
(yadi* api*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(ākāraḥ)(a-vyatiriktaḥ)(rūpataḥ* [-tas suff.])(buddhi-)(tathā* api*)(tasya, 6th s.)(bāhya-)(rūpatvam, 1st s.)(avasīyate ”so pass.)(bhrāntaiḥ, 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 1026. Even though this form (<s>ākāra</s>) is non-different from cognition in terms of form, nevertheless its external-object-nature is determined by those who are mistaken.

body.text:
1027.
(tasya, 6th s.)(na*)(an-apekṣatvam, 1st s.)(artha-)(tat-)(āgateḥ, 5th s.)(pārampāryāt, 5th s.)(ca*)(tena, 3rd s.)(ātmanā, n. 3rd s.)(vastutvam, n. 1st s.)(na* eva*)(asti ”as)(iti*)(upapāditam, 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1027. [The cognition's form] is not independent of the object, because it arrives [i.e., arises] from that [object], and through a continuous succession; therefore — it has been demonstrated that its [form's] reality is not [that of] a real thing in itself.

body.text:
1028.

body.translated_text: 1028. The <s>apoha</s> (exclusion), having the nature of a reflection (<s>pratibimba</s>) — called 'appearance' (<s>pratibhā</s>) — arises from a word; for us, this alone is the meaning of the word.

body.translated_text: 1029. It [the appearance] does not bear any portion other than its own nature of arising; therefore, the exclusion of [what is] other than cognition is understood from the cognition itself.

body.translated_text: 1030. Just as the difference of what does not [really] exist is not ultimate — so too even the difference [that is posited]; thereby there would be synonymy.

body.text:
1031.
(hi*)(a-bhedaḥ)(eka-rūpatvam, n. 1st s.)(kutaḥ*)(tat, 1st s.)(nīrūpeṣu, 7th pl.)(ca*)(vācakāḥ)(prāpnuvanti ”āp Pr. III p. pl.)(paryāyāḥ, 1st pl.)(ekatve, 7th s.)(arthasya, 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 1031. For non-difference means single-formedness; whence [would] that [arise] in things without form? And [if they have the same form,] synonyms would apply; in the oneness of the object —

body.text:
1032.
(yathā*)(api*)(a-bhāve, 7th s.)(rūpa-)(aikatvam, n. 1st s.)(nirmitam, 1st s.)(kalpanā-)(eva*)(tathā*)(vibhedaḥ)(api*)(kutaḥ*)(paryāyatā, f. 1st s.)(tataḥ*)
body.translated_text: 1032. Just as in the absence of form, the oneness [of form] is fabricated — it is conceptual construction alone; so too is the distinction; whence then [would] synonymy [arise]?

body.translated_text: 1033. But from the standpoint of reality, [words] are neither synonyms nor non-synonyms; for it has been described [that] the external [object] is neither one nor many for them.

body.translated_text: 1034. However, if a maker of many [effects] is seen — then, through the superimposition of single effect and single property, a single verbal expression is applied there.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1078] And the thinkers of reality have said [this]: the meaning is [merely] the appearance of the word; but the world, not knowing the distinction, imagines the visible [mental construction] to be external.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1079] Therefore, the denotability of that [meaning] belongs only to particulars, through determination. And in reality, the denotable does not exist for words — this has been established.

body.text:
1080.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1080] Thus there is the excludability (<s>apohyatā</s>) of particulars, because of being the denotable of words. But for the universal, there is no <s>apoha</s> (exclusion), nor is there any real existence in exclusion.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1081] For a non-entity is not excluded — non-entity [has] no excludability. Thus its nature is accepted as [merely] an entity — not the self of that.

body.text:
1082.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1082] That which is not the self of something — that is called its <s>apoha</s> (exclusion). And the entity is not of the form of non-existence — in [the realm of] exclusion, there is no real existence of that.

body.translated_text: 1130. And in the case of duration — by whom is it said [to be] 'duration' (feminine) or 'intrinsic nature' (masculine)? Or, if the form of these is indeed undivided — there would be [only] one grammatical gender.

body.text:
1131.

body.translated_text: 1131. If these — femininity and the like — are held to be like cowness and the like, those very [universals] have been refuted by the refutation of universals.

body.text:
1132.

body.translated_text: 1132. [If it is said that] 'universal' (feminine), 'existence' (masculine), and 'universal' (neuter) are accepted in those — indeed, other universals are not justified in [existing in] universals.

body.text:
1133.

body.translated_text: 1133. How, moreover, [can there be] the [triple gender of] 'non-existence' (masculine), 'state of being without designation' (neuter), and 'emptiness' (feminine)? Therefore, this fixity of the three genders is itself conventional.

body.text:
1134.

body.translated_text: 1134. Number too is indeed conventional, imagined through the intention [of the speaker]; [for example] 'wives' and so forth, 'forests' and so forth — [spoken of] as if there is division and non-division, upon analysis.

body.text:
1135.
(nanu*)(cet*)(dārā-)(prayujyate ”yuj pass.)(vyaktau, 7th s.)(ca*)(ca*)(jātau, 7th s.)(varttate ”vṛt Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(ādāya*)(saṃkhyām, f. 2nd s.)(vyakteḥ, 6th s.)(vā*)(avayavānām, 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 1135. Surely, 'wives' is used [both] for the individual and for the class, taking the number from the individual or from its parts.

body.text:
1136.

body.translated_text: 1136. Or rather, the word 'forest' [may] denote many individuals qualified by a number-class — a class dependent on many individuals.

body.text:

body.translated_text: 1137. Surely, by this method, all speech would be one — annihilated. If the intention to speak does not lie elsewhere — then let that very [intention] be the basis of this.

body.text:

(na*)(saṃkhyā, 1st s.)(jāteḥ, f. 6th s.)(api*)(vā*)(yadi*)(bhāve, 7th s.)(katham*)(viśeṣitāḥ, 1st pl.)(tat-)(sambandhāt, 5th s.)(sambaddha-)(vā*)(api*)(sambandhataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 1138. If number does not [really] belong to the class, or if in its existence, [the individuals] qualified [by it] are [so] from that connection — or from the connection of what is connected —

body.text:
1139.

body.translated_text: 1139. Even so, a single tree is called 'forest' — and many too are spoken of — from that connection; and that exists.

body.translated_text: 1140. That [class] which is dependent on many individuals — even if established in a single one, from the equality of the cause — the cognition of 'forest' would arise there too.

body.translated_text: 1141. Therefore, this restriction of speech to 'one' and so forth [is determined] from the intention to speak, through agreement and difference — not from the object, through deviation.

body.text:
1142.

body.translated_text: 1142. The conjunction of action, time, and the like has also been refuted previously; therefore, these [categories] are conventional and are not real entities — not even in individuals.

body.text:

body.translated_text: 1143. Or, if <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) is spoken of, through determination in the form of the individual — the connection of that [apoha] with gender and the like is through the avenue of the individual.

body.text:
1144.

body.translated_text: 1144. A word is employed [to convey] the meaning of what is intended by the cognition of the speaker; therefore, the exclusion of what is not desired is accomplished by its capacity alone.

body.text:
1145.

body.translated_text: 1145. And not everything that is attained [by a word's capacity] is desired [by the speaker] — because of the absence of restriction to all meanings of all words; 'he cooks' and the like [are] perfectly clear — that which is to be excluded.

body.text:
1146.

body.translated_text: 1146. For when 'he cooks' is said, [the person] does not remain idle, nor does he eat or play — [this] exclusion is understood through propriety.

body.translated_text: 1147. Thus, whatever is accepted as determinate — that which is of the nature of <s>paryudāsa</s> (implicative negation) — is what is to be excluded; and the interval between [this and] the indifference of action [is understood].

body.translated_text: 1148. But this statement: 'he cooks, he stands' — [these are] not negated; each in its own nature is mutually exclusive.

body.translated_text: 1152. Therefore, the cognition of what is to be proved, and likewise the characterization as a real entity and the like — from the similarity of form with real things — it follows that it is caused by that.

body.translated_text: 1153. And in the collection of meanings — in the positive statement and the like — existence and so forth are not negated; that which is not intended [is excluded] through capacity, not by the word [directly].

body.translated_text: 1158. But in the fourth [negation], it is determined that he is distinct from that; thus 'he cooks' — thereby, the exclusion of the other is equivalent to the positive statement.

body.translated_text: 1161. Those that are to be excluded — what is of a different kind — are perfectly clear; and those [excluded things] of the sentence meaning too — for there is indeed nothing other than those.

body.translated_text: 1164. Rather, a conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) arises from this utterance, which determines the positive meaning; afterward, cognition arises regarding the exclusion — the <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) of the word's meaning.

body.translated_text: 1165. But that [construction] is non-veridical, because of the loss of connection with such a [real] thing; all verbal cognitions are not determinative of real, existing objects.

(śabda-)(ādeḥ, 5th s.)(premeya-)(jñeya-)(nimittatām, f. 2nd s.)(pratipatti-)(dṛṣṭvā*)(eva*)(sthitasya, 6th s.)(vākya-)(api*)(antareṣu, 7th pl.)(kāla-)(upalambhe, 7th s.)(kevalasya, 6th s.)(sā, f. 1st s.)(pratipattiḥ, f. 1st s.)(yā, f. 1st s.)(upajāyate ”jan pass.)(bhedeṣu, 7th pl.)(artha-)(plavamāna-)(anusārataḥ* [-tas suff.])(vākya-)(tat-)(ca*)(śabdebhyaḥ, 5th pl.)(ādibhyaḥ, 5th pl.)(ghaṭa-)(api*)(sā, f. 1st s.)(asti ”as)(eva*)(tathāvidhā*)(tasmāt, 5th s.)(dhvanayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(jñeya-)(ādi-)(samāḥ, 1st pl.)(śabdena, m. 3rd s.)(ghaṭa-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 1176-1178. Having seen the status of the knowable, the object of valid cognition, and the cause — from the word and so forth — even in intervening times, the apprehension of the isolated [object] — that apprehension which arises following the word-meaning that floats among [various] object-distinctions — that too exists from words, pots, and so forth — being of that kind; therefore, utterances and so forth are equal to the knowable — like pots and so forth [expressed] by words.

body.text:
1179.
(etat, n. 1st s.)(proktam, 1st s.)(iti*)(kalpanāyām, f. 7th s.)(apohya-)(varam, 2nd s.)(kalpitam, 2nd s.)(vastu, 2nd s.)(eva*)(vyāhatam, 1st s.)(varjanāt, 5th s.)(anya-)(niyamena, 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 1179. This was stated: 'In the construction of what is to be excluded, it is better to accept a constructed real thing itself' — [this is] contradicted, by the restriction of the exclusion of the other.

body.text:
1180.
(vastu, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(kalpyate ”kḷp pass.)(yat, n. 1st s.)(vivakṣitam, n. 1st s.)(ataḥ*)(kṣepaḥ)(vivakṣitasya, n. 6th s.)(tu*)(sarvam, 1st s.)(na*)(vivakṣitam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1180. When the intended real thing itself is constructed — the rejection of the intended [meaning follows]; but not everything [that is] not intended [is rejected].

body.text:
1181.
(tu*)(niṣedhaḥ)(ākāra-)(jñāna-)(na*)(śakyate ”śak pass.)(sva-vedyatvāt, 5th s.)(hi*)(an-ekadhā*)(āropakam, n. 1st s.)(nirālambam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1181. But the negation of the form of cognition is not possible, since [cognition] is self-luminous; for [cognition], being without support, superimposes in many ways.

body.text:
1182.
(avaśya-)(abhyupagantavyaḥ)(kaścit*)(gataḥ)(ātma-)(jñānasya, 6th s.)(niyataḥ)(pratigocaram, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(saḥ)(eva*)(svabhāvaḥ)(ca*)
body.translated_text: 1182. Some [element] that has gone to the self of cognition must necessarily be accepted — determinate with respect to each [particular] domain; and that alone is [its] intrinsic nature.

body.text:
1183.
(uktaḥ)(asmābhiḥ, 3rd pl.)(ākāraḥ)(pratibimbam, n. 1st s.)(tad-ābhatā, f. 1st s.)(ullekhaḥ)(ca*)(pratibhāsaḥ)(bhedaḥ)(saṃjñā-)(tu*)(a-)(kāraṇam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1183. What we have called the 'form' (<s>ākāra</s>) — the reflection (<s>pratibimba</s>), the appearance of that — the 'delineation' and the 'manifestation' — the difference is [merely] in designation; it is not a [real] cause.

body.text:
1184.
(śabdānām, m. 6th pl.)(ādi-)(evam*)(vidyate ”vid IV C.)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(na* evam*)(iti* = quotes)(vispaṣṭam, 1st s.)(apohyam, 1st s.)(iti* = quotes)(lakṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(antara-)(prakāra-)
body.translated_text: 1184. Thus the [nature] of words and so forth exists; [the view] that 'it is not thus' — the clearly excludable — [this is] the characteristic of the other type.

body.text:
1185.
(ca*)(śabde, m. 7th s.)(sarva-)(api*)(upanīte, 7th s.)(vyavahāra-)(vidyate ”vid IV C.)(vyudāsyam, 1st s.)(tasya, 6th s.)(arthaḥ)(abhidhitsitaḥ)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(apohaḥ)(anya-)
body.translated_text: 1185. And when all words are brought into use — the intended meaning of that [word] is the <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) of the other — what is to be excluded in practice.

body.text:
1186.
(sarve, m. 1st pl.)(dharmāḥ, 1st pl.)(nirātmanaḥ, 1st pl.)(vā*)(sarve, m. 1st pl.)(puruṣāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(gatāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(tatra*)(gamyate ”gam / gacch pass.)(sāmastyam, n. 1st s.)(apohyate ”ūh pass.)(kaścit*)(aṃśaḥ)
body.translated_text: 1186. 'All <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) are without self' or 'all persons have gone [to liberation]' — therein, the totality is understood, [and] some portion is excluded.

body.text:
1187.
(bhrāntiḥ, f. 1st s.)(eva*)(kecit*)(bāhyāḥ, 1st pl.)(ghaṭa-ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(iṣṭāḥ, 1st pl.)(nirātmānaḥ, 1st pl.)(gamanam, 1st s.)(eva*)(kasyacit*)(tat, 1st s.)(vinivarttate ”vṛt Āt. Pr. III p. s.)
body.translated_text: 1187. [Some say] that external [things like] pots and so forth are merely an illusion — [they are] accepted as without self; the going of anyone — that [statement merely] turns back [the opponent].

body.text:
1188.
(pratiṣedhaḥ)(sarva-)(aṅga-)(na*)(eva*)(vivakṣitaḥ)(tasmin, 7th s.)(tasmāt, 5th s.)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(prasaṅgaḥ)(apoha-)(svārtha-)(ucyate ”vac pass.)(a-jñatayā, f. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 1188. The negation of all parts [of the meaning] is not at all intended in that [statement]; therefore, this objection is [raised merely] out of ignorance of the <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) of one's own meaning.

body.text:
1189.
(ca*)(apohaḥ)(na* api*)(bhāvaḥ)(na*)(a-bhāvaḥ)(a-)(lakṣaṇaḥ)(pṛthak-)(ekatva-)(ca*)(na*)(āśrita-)(an-āśritaḥ)(vastutaḥ* [-tas suff.])(na*)(eka-)(na-ekaḥ)
body.translated_text: 1189. And <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) is neither a positive entity nor a non-entity; it has no separate characteristic; it is neither one nor many in reality; it is neither dependent nor independent.

body.text:
1190.
(tathā*)(asau, m. 1st s.)(na*)(tattvena, n. 3rd s.)(asti ”as)(tathā*)(vyavasīyate; vi-ava-”so pass.)(tat*)(na*)(bhāvaḥ)(na*)(ca*)(a-bhāvaḥ)(avasāyataḥ* [-tas suff.])(vastutvena, n. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 1190. Thus, that [apoha] does not exist in its true nature; yet thus it is determined; therefore it is neither a positive entity nor a non-entity — [it is determined] from the standpoint of [being a] real thing.

body.text:
1191.
(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(bheda-)(a-bheda-)(pariniṣṭhitāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(sat-)(vastu-)(ca*)(arthaḥ)(śabda-)(niḥsvabhāvaḥ)(tasmāt, 5th s.)(ete, 1st pl.)(nirāspadāḥ, 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 1191. Difference, non-difference, and so forth — [as] established in a real, existent thing — and the meaning of words is without intrinsic nature; therefore these [objections] are without basis.

body.text:
1192-1194.
(naḥ, 6th pl.)(śabdaḥ)(karoti ”kṛ VIII C.)(vinivṛttim, f. 2nd s.)(anya-)(artha-)(sākṣāt*)(tu*)(kṛte, m. 7th s.)(abhidhāne, m. 7th s.)(svārtha-)(sā, f. 1st s.)(avagamyate ”gam / gacch pass.)(sāmarthyāt, n. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 1192-1194. The word effects the exclusion of the other's meaning for us; but when [the word's] own meaning is directly expressed, that [other-exclusion] is understood through [its] capacity.

body.text:
1193-1194.
(iti*)(tat-)(ātmā, n. 1st s.)(na*)(ātmā, n. 1st s.)(para-)(upapāditam, n. 1st s.)(vistareṇa, 3rd s.)(tasmāt, 5th s.)(ucyate ”vac pass.)(iha*)-- ...
"Who (kena, 3rd s.)(hi*)(āsaktam, 1st s.)(a-gotvam, n. 1st s.)(goḥ, 6th s.)(yena, 3rd s.)(etat, n. 1st s.)(apohyate ”ūh pass.)(iti*)(an-abhijñena, 3rd s.)(pakṣa-)(para-)(etat, n. 1st s.)(na* eva*)(apohyate ”ūh pass.)(śabdena, m. 3rd s.)(abhimukhena, 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 1193-1194. Thus — [the apoha] is not the self of another — this has been demonstrated at length; therefore it is said here: 'By whom indeed is non-cowness attached to a cow, by which this [cow] is excluded?' — by one who is ignorant of the opponent's thesis; this is not at all excluded by the word [when it is] directed [toward its own meaning].

body.text:
1195-1199.
(ca*)(vācyatvam, n. 1st s.)(paripṛcchyate ”pṛcch pass.)(katamena, m. 3rd s.)(śabdena, m. 3rd s.)(kim*)(etena, 3rd s.)(apohasya, m. 6th s.)(yadi* vā*)(kim*)(ghaṭa-)(ādinā, 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 1195-1199. And the expressibility [of apoha] is questioned: by which word? Is it by this [word] of <s>apoha</s> (exclusion), or by [the word] 'pot' and so forth?

body.text:
1196.
(nirūpaṇe, 7th s.)(kim*)(apohaḥ)(arthaḥ)(śabda-)(vā*)(vā*)(vidhiḥ, m. 1st s.)(evam*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(yat, n. 1st s.)(bhāti ”bhā Pr. III p. s.)(pratīyate, prati-”i, pass. Pr. III p. s.)(apohaḥ)
body.translated_text: 1196. In the examination: is <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) the meaning of the word, or is it the positive meaning? Thus, that which appears — [that which] is cognized — is the <s>apoha</s>.

body.text:
1197.
(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(iti*)(arthaḥ)(śabda-)(sākṣāt*)(pratibimbam, n. 1st s.)(tu*)(hāniḥ, f. 1st s.)(vidhi-)(ādi-)(jāti-)(avagamyate ”gam / gacch pass.)(sāmarthyāt, 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 1197. This cognition is the direct meaning of the word — [it is] a reflection (<s>pratibimba</s>); but the loss of <s>jāti</s> (universal) and so forth — the positive [meaning] — is understood through [its] capacity.

body.text:
1198.
(ca*)(śabdāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(ghaṭa-)(vrkṣa-)(ādi-)(bruvanti ”brū Pr. III p. pl.)(tat, 2nd s.)(eva*)(pratibimbakam, n. 2nd s.)(arthāt, 5th s.)(jananāt, 5th s.)(sākṣāt*)(tu*)(anyat, n. 2nd s.)(kṣipanti ”kṣip Pr. III p. pl.)
body.translated_text: 1198. And the words 'pot,' 'tree,' and so forth express precisely that reflection; directly, from the production of the meaning; but they cast aside the other.

body.text:
1199.
(tasmāt, 5th s.)(asti ”as)(na*)(doṣaḥ)(vidhi-)(na*)(ca*)(an-iṣṭā, f. 1st s.)(prasajyate ”sañj pass.)(tu*)(an-aṅgīkṛteḥ, f. 5th s.)(tat-)(doṣaḥ)(pakṣa-)(a-vācya-)(na*)(naḥ, 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 1199. Therefore, there is no fault in the positive [account]; nor does the undesired [consequence] follow; but because of the non-acceptance of that [real universal], the fault belongs to the opponent's thesis — not to ours.

body.text:
1200.
(ekatva-)(nityatā-)(ādiḥ, m. 1st s.)(kalpitaḥ)(tu*)(na*)(tāttvikaḥ)(tat*)(hāsa-karaṇam, 1st s.)(atra*)(sūcakam, 1st s.)(mahā-)(vidvattva-)
body.translated_text: 1200. Oneness, permanence, and so forth are [merely] imagined — not real; therefore, [raising] that [objection] here is laughable — a sign of great [supposed] learning.

body.text:
1201.
(yatra*)(eva*)(svātmā, n. 1st s.)(gamyate ”gam / gacch pass.)(apohaḥ)(anya-)(api*)(gamyate ”gam / gacch pass.)(sāmarthyāt, 5th s.)(avadhāraṇa-)(anyathā*)(niyamaḥ)(viphalaḥ)
body.translated_text: 1201. Wherever one's own meaning is understood, the <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) of the other is also understood through [its] capacity; otherwise, the restriction of determination would be fruitless.

body.text:
1202.
(tarhi*)(śabdasya, m. 6th s.)(ādi-)(suta-)(vandhyā-)(yasya, 6th s.)(na*)(bāhyaḥ)(arthaḥ)(anyathāvṛttaḥ)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(api*)(kva*)(apohaḥ)(ucyate ”vac pass.)(tena, 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 1202. Then, of a word and so forth — like the son of a barren woman — for which there is no external object that exists in a different manner — where is <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) said to apply by that [word]?

body.text:
1203.
(a-bhāvānām, 6th pl.)(a-bhāvāt, 5th s.)(rūpa-)(śabdāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(a-)(eva*)(śaṅkyā, 3rd s.)(vācakāḥ, 1st pl.)(jāti-)(ādi-)(siddhāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(te, m. 1st p.)(eva*)(sūcakāḥ, m. 1stpl.)(nirbhāsasya, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 1203. Since non-existences have no form, words are not to be suspected [of denoting] non-entities as such; [words] are established as designators of <s>jāti</s> (universal) and so forth — they are indicative of [their] appearance.

body.text:
1204.
(tat, 1st s.)(pratipādyate ”pad caus. pass.)(śabdaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(pratibimbam, n. 1st s.)(yat, n. 1st s.)(ābhāti ”bhā Pr. III p. s.)(nirmitam, n. 1st s.)(mātra-)(vāsanā-)(uttha-)(abhijalpa-)(śūnya-)(artha-)
body.translated_text: 1204. That which is conveyed by words — the reflection (<s>pratibimba</s>) that appears, fabricated — arising from latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) [and] inner verbalization (<s>abhijalpa</s>), empty of [real] object.

body.text:
1205.
(śabdāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(ime, m. 1st pl.)(dyotakāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(sākṣāt*)(tat-)(mātra-)(sa-saṃśayāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(sa-vyapekṣatvāt, n. 5th s.)(saṅketa-)(-vat*)(abhidhāna-)(kalpita-)(artha-)
body.translated_text: 1205. These words are directly illuminators of that alone — [though] accompanied by doubt; because of their dependence [on convention] — like convention — the designated meaning is imagined.

body.text:
1206.
(ca*)(ete, m. 1st pl.)(dhvanayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(na*)(pratipādakāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(vidhāna-)(bheda-)(ādi-)(upagata-)(para-)(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(gamyatām ”gam / gacch pass. Imp. III p. s.)(eva*)(-vat*)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 1206. And these sounds are not conveyors of the arrangement of distinctions and so forth — [which are] taken up by others; therefore, let that alone be understood — like that [convention].

body.text:
1207.
(atra*)(hi*)(sādhitaḥ)(purā*)(saṅketa-)(a-sambhavaḥ)(bheda-)(ādau, 7th s.)(ca*)(tat*)(na*)(vaiphalyam, n. 1st s.)(hetvoḥ, m. 6th d.)(sandigdha-)(vyatirekitā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1207. Here indeed, the impossibility of convention has been previously established with regard to distinctions and so forth; and that [objection] is not futile; of the two proofs, the uncertainty of the negative concomitance —

body.text:
1208-1209.
(pakṣe, 7th s.)(apoha-)(api*)(katham*)(saṅketa-)(sambhavaḥ)(katham*)(ca*)(tasya, 6th s.)(sāphalyam, n. 1st s.)(hi*)(saḥ)(na*)(siddhyati ”sidh IV C. Pr. III p. s.)(dvayoḥ, 6th d.)(vaktṛ-)(śrotroḥ, 6th d.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(vedyate ”vid caus. pass.)(parasparam, 2nd s.)(ca*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(dṛṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(saṅkete, m. 7th s.)(na*)(samīkṣyate ”īkṣ pass.)(vyavahāre, m. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 1208-1209. On the <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) thesis too, how [is] convention possible? And how [is there] efficacy of it? For that [convention] is not established — the cognition of the two, speaker and hearer, is not known to each other; and that [convention], as observed, is not found [operative] in [actual] linguistic usage.

body.text:
1210.
(api*)(svasya, m. 6th s.)(jñāne, 7th s.)(avabhāsasya, m. 6th s.)(svasya, m. 6th s.)(varttate ”vṛt Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(adhyavasāye, m. 7th s.)(bāhya-)(artha-)(yataḥ*)(api*)(samaḥ)(dvayoḥ, m. 6th d.)
body.translated_text: 1210. Moreover, one's own appearance in one's own cognition operates through the determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>) of the external object; since it is also the same for both [speaker and hearer].

body.text:
1211.
(hi*)(yathā*)(akṣaḥ)(upahata-)(timira-)(prāha ”ah Pr. III p. s.)(sva-samāya, m. 4th s.)(dvayam, 2nd s.)(śaśi-)(tathā*)(sarvā, f. 1st s.)(śābdī, f. 1st s.)(vyavahṛtiḥ, f. 1st s.)(matā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1211. For just as an eye afflicted by timira (an eye-disease) reports two moons to its own assembly — so too all verbal usage is considered [to operate].

body.text:
1212.
(idam, 1st s.)(vyāpakatvam, n. 1st s.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(iṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(adhyavasāyikam, n. 1st s.)(hi*)(ete, m. 1st pl.)(pratyayāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(nirmitāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(śabda-)(avabhāsinaḥ, m. 1st pl. [-in suff.])(mithyā-)
body.translated_text: 1212. This pervasiveness of it [the <s>apoha</s>] is accepted [to work] through determination; for these cognitions, illuminated by words, are falsely fabricated.

body.text:
1213.
(pratyakṣam, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(anumānam, n. 1st s.)(yat, 1st s.)(uktam, 1st s.)(paraiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(prasiddhaye, f. 4th s.)(upādhi-)(na*)(siddham, n. 1st s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(hi*)(lakṣaṇakam, n. 1st s.)(evam*)
body.translated_text: 1213. And <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and <s>anumāna</s> (inference) — whatever has been stated by others for [their] establishment — that, characterized by a limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>), is not established; thus —

body.text:
1214.
(pratyakṣam, n. 1st s.)(apoḍham, n. 1st s.)(kalpanā-)(a-bhrāntam, 1st s.)(kalpanā, f. 1st s.)(pratītiḥ, f. 1st s.)(abhilāpinī, f. 1st s.)(tu*)(na*)(ātmikā, f. 1st .s)(hetutva-)(kḷpti-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 1214. <s>Pratyakṣa</s> (perception) is defined as free from conceptual construction (<s>kalpanā</s>) and non-erroneous; conceptual construction is an apprehension that has the capacity for verbalization; but [perception] is not of the nature of causality, construction, and so forth.

body.text:
1215.
(yā, f. 1st .s)(yogyā, f. 1st s.)(ghaṭanā-)(artha-)(śabda-)(jāyate ”jan pass.)(sa-abhilāpaḥ)(api*)(vācām, f. 6th pl.)(rūpatas*)(iti*)(vṛkṣaḥ)(ādi-)(a-prayoge, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 1215. That [conceptual construction] which, being capable of connecting with the object of words, arises — even with verbalization — in terms of the form of words — as in [the case of the concept] 'tree' and so forth, when [such words are] not [actually] employed.

body.text:
1216.
(anvayāt, 5th s.)(vāsanā-)(bhāvanā-)(artha-)(nāma-)(atīta-)(bhava-)(api*)(sadyas*-jātaḥ)(paṭuḥ, m. 1st s.)(itikartavyatā-)(yogāt, 5th s.)(yat-)
body.translated_text: 1216. Through the continuity of the cultivation of latent impressions of names — even from a past existence — one who is just born [and] alert — through the connection with [knowing] what is to be done —

body.text:
1217.
(sā, f. 1st s.)(yā, f. 1st s.)(vispaṣṭam, 2nd s.)(pravedyate ”vid caus. pass.)(kāle, 7th s.)(cintā-)(utprekṣa-)(iva*)(anuviddhā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(śakyate ”śak pass.)(apahnotum* ”hnu)(śabdaiḥ, 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 1217. That [conceptual construction] which is clearly experienced at the time of deliberation and imagination — [being] pervaded [by verbalization] — cannot be denied by [mere] words.

body.text:
1218.
(sthitiḥ, f. 1st s.)(śabda-)(arthayoḥ, 6th d.)(adhyavasāyena, 3rd s.)(bhrāntā, f. 1st s.)(a-sattve, 7th s.)(asyāḥ, 6th s.)(api*)(īdṛśī, f. 1st s.)(sā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(sambhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(tasyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(a-yogāt, 5th s.)(anya-)
body.translated_text: 1218. The stability of word and meaning through determination is erroneous; if that [determination] is absent, such [stability] would not be possible — because of the lack of connection with the other.

body.text:
1219.
(anye, m. 1st pl.)(viduḥ ”vid II C. Perf. III p. pl.)(kalpanām, f. 2nd s.)(yogyām, f. 7th s.)(yojanā-)(jāti-)(ādi-)(sā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(saṅgatā, f. 1st s.)(jāti-)(ādi-)(apāstatvāt, 5th s.)(ca*)(a-dṛṣṭeḥ, 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 1219. Others understand conceptual construction as [being] suitable [for] connection with <s>jāti</s> (universal) and so forth; that is not coherent — because <s>jāti</s> and so forth have been rejected, and because they are not observed.

body.text:
1220.
(jāti-)(ādīnām, 6th pl.)(a-dṛṣṭatvāt, 5th s.)(tat-)(yoga-)(a-pratibhāsanāt, 5th s.)(ca*)(katham*)(ghaṭanā, f. 1st s.)(arthe, 7th s.)(ghaṭate ”ghaṭ Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(-vat*)(kṣīra-)(udaka-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 1220. Because <s>jāti</s> (universals) and so forth are not observed, and because the connection with them does not appear [in cognition] — how does the connection with the object occur? — like milk and water and so forth.

body.text:
1221.
(iyam, f. 1st s.)(kalpanā, f. 1st s.)(uditā, f. 1st s.)(dvividha-)(prasiddhā, f. 1st s.)(para-)(apara-)(dvaya-)(uktitas*)(kathanāya, 4th s.)(viṣaya-)(heya-)(upādeya-)
body.translated_text: 1221. This conceptual construction is said to be twofold — well-known as higher and lower; [it is stated] in terms of the two — for the purpose of explaining the object [to be abandoned and the object] to be adopted.

body.text:
1222.
(ca*)(iyam, f. 1st s.)(yojanā, f. 1st s.)(nāma*)(ādi-)(varttate ”vṛt Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(ākṣipya* ”kṣip)(sva-)(anantaram, 2nd s.)(nimitam, 2nd s.)(tena, 3rd s.)(abhidhā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(a-prastutā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1222. And this [connection] called '<s>yojanā</s>' (joining) — of names and so forth — operates by drawing upon its own immediate referent; therefore, designation is not irrelevant.

body.text:
1223.
(vā*)(nāma-)(jāti-)(sarve, m. 1st pl.)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(yojyante ”yuj cause. pass. Pr. III p. pl.)(anayā, f. 3rd s.)(uktā, f. 1st .s)(tathā*)(sā, f. 1st s.)(kalpanā, f. 1st s.)(proktā, f. 1st s.)(pratītiḥ, f. 1st s.)(abhilāpinī, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1223. Or [else], all — names, <s>jātis</s> (universals), and so forth — are joined by this [conceptual construction]; thus that conceptual construction is said to be an apprehension capable of verbalization.

body.text:
1224.
(yat* vā*)(uditā, f. 1st s.)(kevalā, f. 1st s.)(kalpanā, f. 1st s.)(siddhā, f. 1st s.)(eva*)(sva-)(mata-)(yojanāt, 5th s.)(iti*)(sarvatra*)(yuktaḥ)(arthaḥ)(ucyate ”vac pass.)(nāmna, 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 1224. Or alternatively, the isolated conceptual construction is [already] established — from the connection with one's own accepted [position]; thus everywhere, the meaning is properly stated by the name.

body.text:
1225.
(taiḥ, 3rd pl.)(karaṇa-)(vibhāktyā, 3rd s.)(sāphalyam, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(arthaḥ)(iyam, f. 1st s.)(sā, f. 1st s.)(adhyavatiṣṭhate ”sthā Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(nāmnaḥ, 6th s.)(jāti-)(ādibhiḥ, 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 1225. By those [names], through the instrument of case-endings — efficacy [is achieved]; thus the meaning: this [conceptual construction] determines [the relation] of name with <s>jāti</s> (universal) and so forth.

body.text:
1226.
(ca*)(sadbhāvatas*)(jāteḥ, f. 6th s.)(vācyāyāḥ, 6th s.)(yadṛcchā-śabda-)(na*)(mantavyā, f. 1st s.)(a-vyāptiḥ, f. 1st s.)(asya, 6th s.)(tu*)(śrutiḥ, f. 1st s.)(pṛthak*)(prasiddheḥ, 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 1226. And from the standpoint of the reality of <s>jāti</s> (universal), which is to be expressed — what is merely a conventional word is not to be considered [a proof of] non-pervasion; but the verbal expression [is valid] separately — from [its own] establishment.

body.text:
1227.
(tu*)(nanu*)(śabdaḥ)(jāti-)(kevalaḥ)(-tvāt, 5th s.)(vācya-)(apoha-)(anya-)(vā*)(-tvāt, 5th s.)(paratantra-)(vivakṣā-)(śabdaḥ)(vivakṣā-)(eva*)
body.translated_text: 1227. Now, [the question]: is the word [denoting] only <s>jāti</s> (universal), because of [its] expressible nature; or [denoting] the <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) of the other, because of [its] dependent nature? The word is [dependent on] the intention to speak — [it is] intention alone.

body.text:
1228.
(satyam, 1st s.)(idam, n . 1st s.)(īdṛśam, 1st s.)(uktam, n. 1st s.)(nyāya-vidā, 3rd s.)(anuvṛttyā, 3rd s.)(loka-)(hi*)(eva*)(iyān, m 1st s.)(śabdaḥ)(gataḥ)(padam, 2nd s.)(vyavahāra-)(asmin, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 1228. True — this is said in such a manner by the knower of logic; for following worldly [convention] — this much the word has reached its foothold in usage.

body.text:
1229.
(te, m. 1st pl.)(ādayaḥ, 1st pl.)(jāti-)(na*)(vyatirekinaḥ, 1st pl.)(vid-)(loka-)(iha*)(iti*)(artham, 2nd s.)(pratipatti-)(etat-)(iti*)(tu*)(anye, 1st pl.)(ādi-)(varṇitam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1229. <s>Jāti</s> (universals) and so forth are not [things] different [from what is] known in the world; this [is the meaning]: the apprehension of this meaning [is sufficient]; but others have described it [differently] and so forth.

body.text:
1230.
(api*)(taiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(samupāśritāḥ, sam-upa-ā-”śri m. 1st pl.)(kalpanām, 2nd s.)(yojanām, 2nd s.)(jāti-)(ādi-)(niyatam, 2nd s.)(abhyyupeyā, f. 1st s.)(pratītiḥ, f. 1st s.)(abhilāpinī, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1230. Moreover, those [who] have resorted to conceptual construction [as] the connection with <s>jāti</s> (universal) and so forth — must necessarily accept [it as] an apprehension capable of verbalization, [which is] determinate.

body.text:
1231.
(anyathā*)(iva*)(yuktayoḥ, 6th d.)(bhāvayoḥ, 6th d.)(yojanā-)(a-bhāvāt, 5th s.)(paricchedāt, 5th s.)(svātantryeṇa, 3rd s.)(kalpanā, f. 1st s.)(na* eva*)(kalpyate ”kḷp pass.)
body.translated_text: 1231. Otherwise — as with two things that are [actually] proper — because of the absence of [the need for] connection, and because of [the capacity for] independent determination — conceptual construction alone is not to be postulated.

body.text:
1232.
(evam* vā*)(syāt ”as Opt. III p. s.)(a-vyavahāryam, 1st s.)(idam, 1st s.)(sarvam, 1st s.)(viśvam, 1st s.)(tataḥ)(idam, 1st s.)(vyavahāryam, 1st s.)(matam, 1st s.)(saṃsṛṣṭam, 1st s.)(rūpa-)(jāti-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 1232. Or thus: all this entire universe would be non-expressible; [but] since this [universe] is considered expressible, [it follows that it is] mixed with form, <s>jāti</s> (universal), and so forth.

body.text:
1233.
(yojanā, f. 1st s.)(jāti-)(ādi-)(a-vyabhicārinī, f. 1st s.)(yojanā-)(śabda-)(ca*)(evam*)(etat, n. 1st s.)(vacas, n. 1st s.)(ucyate ”vac pass.)(iti*)(jāyate ”jan pass.)(phalavat, 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1233. The connection with <s>jāti</s> (universal) and so forth is unfailing; and the word-connection thus — this statement is said: it arises as fruitful.

body.text:
1234.
(tasmāt, 5th s.)(iyam, f. 1st .s)(kalpanā, f. 1st s.)(matā, f. 1st s.)(sādhyā, f. 1st s.)(a-yatnena, 3rd s.)(a-vivādāt, 5th s.)(pravādinām, 6th pl.)(saṃsthitānām, 6th pl.)(samasta-)(siddhānta-)
body.translated_text: 1234. Therefore, this conceptual construction is considered [to be] established without effort — because of the non-dispute among those who abide in [their] complete doctrinal positions.

body.text:
1235.
(āgūrya* ”gṝ)(sakalam, 2nd s.)(etat, 2nd s.)(varṇanam, 1st s.)(nāma-)(jāti-)(ādi-)(ittham*)(iha*)(akarot ”kṛ P. Imp. III p. s.)(upādanam, 2nd s.)(matayoḥ, 6th d.)(sva-)(anyayoḥ, 6th d.)
body.translated_text: 1235. Having encompassed all this description of name, <s>jāti</s> (universal), and so forth — thus [the author] has here made the exposition of both one's own and others' views.

body.text:
1236.
(a-bruvan, 1st s.)(evam*)(iti*)(bhedaḥ)(asmākam, 6th pl.)(tebhyaḥ, 5th pl.)(eva*)(iyān, m. 1st s.)(anantaram*)(jagau ”gai I C. Perf. III p. s.)(vākyam, 1st s.)(ādikam, 1st s.)(tu*)(anye, 1st pl.)(iti* )
body.translated_text: 1236. 'Not saying thus' — this is our difference from them, just this much; but [<s>Dignāga</s>] then stated the initial statement: 'but others [say]...'

body.text:
1237.
(evam*)(granthe, 7th s.)(nyāyamukhe, 7th s.)(vyākhyātavyaḥ)(ananyā, f. 3rd s.)(diśā, f. 3rd s.)(pratītiḥ, f. 1st s.)(coditā, f. 1st s. [”cud])(tatra*)(abhisambandhāt, 5th s.)(iti*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1237. Thus, in the text <s>Nyāyamukha</s>, what is to be explained — in no other direction: the apprehension is prompted therein, because of its connection — [this is the] cognition.

body.text:
1238.
(yad* vā*)(viśeṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(yena, 3rd s.)(śrutiḥ, f. 1st s.)(kṛt-)(apoha-)(anya-)(ca*)(anena, 3rd s.)(karoti ”kṛ VIII C.)(vyavacchedam, 2nd s.)(or: `it differentiates')(jāti-)(ādīnām, 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 1238. Or, that which is the qualifier — and by which the verbal expression effects the <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) of the other — and by this [qualifier], it differentiates <s>jātis</s> (universals) and so forth.

body.text:
1239-1242.
(kalpanā, f. 1st s.)(matā, f. 1st s.)(eva*)(pratīti-rūpā, f. 1st s.)(ca*)(evam*)(pratiṣedhaḥ)(tādātmya-)(pratyakṣasya, 6th s.)(upavarṇyate ”varṇ pass. Pr. III p. s.)(ca*)
body.translated_text: 1239-1242. The conceptual construction is considered [to be] of the nature of apprehension — and thus the negation of identity [with perception] — of <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) — is described.

body.text:
1240.
(na*)(bādhyate ”bādh pass.)(śabdena, 3rd s.)(adhyakṣa-)(ādi-)(adhyakṣe, 7th s.)(virahaḥ)(kalpanā-)(sā, f. 1st s.)(hi*)(na*)(vācyatā, f. 1st s.)(śabda-)
body.translated_text: 1240. [Perception] is not contradicted by a word; perception and so forth — [when] there is absence of conceptual construction in perception — that indeed is not verbal expressibility.

body.text:
1241.
(anyathā*)(rūpa-)(gandha-)(ādeḥ, 6th s.)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(sa-vikalpakatā, f. 1st s.)(ataḥ*)(na*)(āspadam, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(idam, 1st s.)(yat, n. 1st s.)(kudhiyaḥ, 1st pl.)(āhuḥ ”ah Pr. III p. s.)
body.translated_text: 1241. Otherwise, form, smell, and so forth would have the nature of conceptual determination; therefore, this is not at all a ground — what those of poor understanding say.

body.text:
1242.
(yadi*)(śabdena, 3rd s.)(pratyakṣa-)(abhidhīyate ”dhā pass.)(pratyakṣam, 1st s.)(katham*...katham*)(tat-)(apoḍham, 1st s.)(kalpanā-)(gamyate ”gam / gacch pass.)(a-yuktam, 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1242. If <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) is expressed by a word — how then is that [perception] free from conceptual construction? It is understood — [this objection is] unreasonable.

body.text:
1243.
(pratyakṣam, 1st s.)(apoḍham, 1st s.)(kalpanā-)(vedyate ”vid caus. pass.)(atiparisphuṭam*)(vedanāt, 5th s.)(nīla-)(api*)(manasā, n. 3rd s.)(āsakta-)(anyatra*)
body.translated_text: 1243. <s>Pratyakṣa</s> (perception), free from conceptual construction, is cognized very clearly; even blue [color] is cognized by the mind — attached elsewhere.

body.text:
1244.
(asau, m. 1st s.)(eva*)(vikalpaḥ)(na*)(pratipadyate ”pad IV C. Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(tam, m. 2nd s.)(artham, m. 2nd s.)(tyāgāt, 5th s.)(abhidhā-)(atīta-)(ādi-)(āptitas*)(ghaṭanā-)(nāma-)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 1244. That very conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) does not apprehend that object — because of the abandonment of verbal designation; [designations regarding] the past and so forth, [arising] from authoritative [convention], are mere nominal constructions.

body.text:
1245.
(ca*)(tadā*)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(na*)(aparaḥ)(vikalpaḥ)(saṃsargī, m. 1st s.)(nāma-)(tat-)(a-pratisaṃvitteḥ, f. 5th s.)(dṛśyasya, 6th s.)(sakṛt*)(dvayoḥ, 6th d.)(an-iṣṭeḥ, 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 1245. And at that time there is no other conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) connected with that name — because of the non-awareness of the visible [object]; [this follows] from the undesirability of [simultaneous awareness of] the two occurring at once.

body.text:
1246.
(ataḥ*)(bhāvi-)(vikalpakam, n. 1st s.)(anubhūyate ”bhū pass.)(saha-)(jñāna-)(tasmāt, 5th s.)(idam, n. 1st s.)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(indriya-)(sphuṭam*)(a-kalpanam, 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1246. Therefore, that which is experienced together with cognition as conducive to future conceptual construction — this cognition, [arising] from the sense faculties, is clearly non-conceptual (<s>a-kalpana</s>).

body.text:
1247.
(cet*)(matam, 1st s.)(iti*)(vijñānāni, 1st pl.)(upajāyante ”jan pass. Pr. III p. pl.)(eva*)(krameṇa, 3rd s.)(tu*)(abhimānaḥ)(sakṛt*)(bhāva-)(vṛtteḥ, 5th s.)(śīghra-)(-vat*)(alāta-)
body.translated_text: 1247. If it is held that cognitions arise in sequence, but that the impression of simultaneity [arises] from the rapidity of their occurrence — like a firebrand [appearing as a circle],

children.text: (na*)(tadā*)(abhimukhī-)(bhūta-)(bhāvānām, m. 6th pl.)(anuṣaṅgavān, m. 1st s. [-vat suff.])(vikalpaḥ)(vidyate ”vid IV C.)(dṛśyaḥ)(iti*)(eva*)(uktam, 1st s.)(nāma-)
children.translated_text: [we reply:] at that time, no conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) is found that is connected with [objects that have] come into view and that is attached to [their] name — this very [point] has been stated, and nothing [further remains to be said].
