body.text:
1249.
(ca*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(nirantaram, n. 1st s.)(bhrāntiḥ, f. 1st s.)(vyaktam, 1st s.)(ca*)(ataḥ*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(yaugapadyam, n. 1st s.)(artha-)(vijñāna-)(sphuṭam*)
body.translated_text: 1249. And that [impression of simultaneity] is clearly an error; and therefore that very simultaneity of object and cognition is evident.

body.text:
1250.
(avasthādau, 7th s.)(dṛṣṭi-)(narttakī, f. 1st s.)(akhilam, 1st s.)(vedyate ”vid caus. pass.)(sakṛt*)(api*)(bahubhiḥ, 3rd pl.)(vyavadhāne, 7th s.)(cet*)(bhrāntiḥ, f. 1st s.)(vṛttitas*)(āśu-)
body.translated_text: 1250. In the initial state, the dancer of vision [i.e., perception] — the entire [object] — is cognized at once even by many [sense faculties]; if [there is] an intervening [obstruction], the error [arises] from the rapidity of occurrence.

body.text:
1251.
(buddhīnām, 6th pl.)(ādi-)(varttanam, 1st s.)(laghu-)(atyartham*)(ataḥ*)(kim* artham*)(varttate ”vṛt Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(na*)(abhimānaḥ)(sakṛt-bhāva)(atra*)(api*)
body.translated_text: 1251. The initial operation of cognitions is exceedingly swift; therefore, why does the impression of simultaneity not arise here as well?

body.text:
1252.
(ca*)(mānase, 7th s.)(śuddhe, 7th s.)(na*)(kramaḥ)(vyavasīyeta ”so pass. Opt. III p. s.)(ca*)(a-sthiteḥ, 5th s.)(cirā*)(sarva-)(buddhīnām, 6th pl.)(āśu-)(vṛttiḥ, f. 1st s.)(alpā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1252. And in a pure mental [cognition], succession would not be ascertained; and because of the instability of all cognitions, [their] rapid operation is slight.

body.text:
1253.
(ataḥ*)(sarvatra*)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(grahaṇam, n. 1st s.)(krama-)(bhāsaḥ)(sakṛt-)(grahaṇa-)(tu*)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(-vat*)(bodha-)(śabda-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 1253. Therefore, everywhere there would be apprehension of succession; but apprehension [occurring] at once — like the cognition of words and so forth — would [also] occur.

body.text:
1254-1256.
(api*)(alāte, 7th s.)(bhrāntiḥ, f. 1st s.)(sakṛt*)(pravarttate ”vṛt Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(ābhāsā, f. 1st s.)(cakra-)(na*)(pratisandhānāt, 5th s.)(dṛśām, f. 2nd s.)(vispaṣṭam*)(pratibhāsanāt, 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 1254-1256. Even in a firebrand, the error [of seeing a circle] does not arise at once; the appearance of a circle [arises] from the reconnection of the perceptions, from the clear appearance [of each successive point].

body.text:
1255.
(tathā* hi*)(pratisandhānam, n. 1st s.)(kriyate ”kṛ pass.)(eva*)(smṛtyā, f. 3rd s.)(tu*)(na*)(darśanena, 3rd s.)(an-avagrahāt, 5th s.)(viṣayasya, 6th s.)(vyatītasya, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 1255. For indeed, the reconnection is made by memory, not by perception — because of the non-apprehension of the object that has passed.

body.text:
1256.
(ca*)(asau, m. 1st s.)(viṣayaḥ)(asyā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(parisphuṭaḥ)(vinaṣṭatvāt, 5th s.)(tataḥ*)(prasajyate ”sajj pass.)(ābhāsaḥ)(cakra-)(na*)(parisphuṭaḥ)
body.translated_text: 1256. And this [past] object of this [memory] is not clearly manifest, because of [its] having perished; therefore, the appearance of a circle does not arise clearly.

body.text:
1257-1260.
(yadi*)(ca*)(kāraṇam, 1st s.)(upasthiti-)(bhāvasya, 6th s.)(yat-)(rūpa-)(na*)(vidyate ”vid IV C.)(saḥ)(vyavasthāpyate ”sthā pass. Pr. III p. s.)(tattvena, 3rd s.)(buddhaiḥ, 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 1257-1260. And if the cause — whatever form constitutes the presence of [something in cognition] — is not found, that [cognition] is established in its true nature by the wise.

body.text:
1258.
(a-vidyamāna-)(sāsnā-)(ādiḥ, m. 1st s.)(yathā*)(karkaḥ)(go-)(ātmanā, n. 3rd s.)(viśeṣaṇa-)(viśiṣṭa-)(artham, 2nd s.)(grahaṇam, n. 1st s.)
(na*)(ca*)(vidyate ”vid IV C.)
body.translated_text: 1258. Just as [something] lacking a dewlap and so forth [is not a real cow but] is [mistakenly identified as a] cow by [its superficial] nature — so too, the apprehension of an object qualified by a qualifier does not [truly] exist.

body.text:
1259.
(sa-vikalpaka-)(bhāvasya, 6th s.)(sthiteḥ, 6th s.)(ākṣe, 7th s.)(nibandhanam, n. 1st s.)(vipakṣaḥ)(śābaleya-)(ādiḥ, 1st s.)(anyathā*)(atiprasajyate ”sajj pass.)
body.translated_text: 1259. The basis for the existence of conceptual cognition (<s>sa-vikalpaka</s>) [lies] in the axle [of the argument]; the counter-example [is] a spotted [dog] and so forth; otherwise, overextension would follow.

body.text:
1260.
(na* ca*)(hetoḥ, 6th s.)(a-prasiddhatā, f. 1st s.)(jāti-)(ādeḥ, 5th s.)(pratiṣedhataḥ*)(ca*)(a-paricchedāt, m. 5th s.)(bhedena, 3rd s.)(ca*)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(na*)(evam*)(viśeṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1260. And the reason is not unestablished — from the negation of <s>jāti</s> (universal) and so forth; and because of non-determination by distinction, there is no qualifier of this kind.

body.text:
1261.
(nāma*)(api*)(yat, 1st s.)(śabdasya, 6th s.)(svalakṣaṇam, 1st s.)(na* eva*)(vācakam, 1st s.)(hi*)(svalakṣaṇasya, 6th s.)(vācyatva-)(vācakatve, 7th s.)(dūṣite, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 1261. Even what is the word's own unique particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) is indeed not an expresser; for the expressibility and expressive capacity of the unique particular have been refuted.

body.text:
1262.
(ataḥ*)(vācakam, n. 1st s.)(vācya-)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(eva*)(adhyāropitam, 1st s.)(ca*)(pratyakṣam, 1st s.)(pratipadyate ”pad IV C. Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(artham, 1st s.)(an-āropitam, 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1262. Therefore, what is accepted as the expresser is only [something] superimposed upon the expressible; and direct perception apprehends an object that is non-superimposed.

body.text:
1263.
(sadbhāvāt, 5th s.)(svalakṣaṇasya, 6th s.)(sadbhāve, 7th s.)(ca*)(tasya, 6th s.)(api*)(vyatirekatas*)(bhāve, 7th s.)(vyavadhāna-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 1263. Because of the real existence of the unique particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), and also because of its real existence [as perceived] — through its distinctness [from conceptual construction]; when there is the existence of an intervening [obstruction] and so forth,

body.text:
1264.
(hi*)(ātmā, m. 1st s.)(nīla-)(ādīnām, 6th s.)(bhāk, 1st s.)(an-anya-)(a-śakya-)(samayaḥ)(ca*)(saṃvittiḥ, f. 1st s.)(teṣām, 6th pl.)(ataḥ*)(na*)(anuṣaṅgiṇī, f. 1st s.)(abhijalpa-)
body.translated_text: 1264. For the self of blue and so forth partakes of no other [nature]; and the awareness of them is a convention that cannot be [otherwise]; therefore [it is] not accompanied by verbal designation.

body.text:
1265.
(nanu*)(nāma- [=universal])(ādikam, 1st s.)(mā*)(/a/-bhūt ”bhū Aor. III p. s.)(viśeṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(grahyam, 1st s.)(tasya, 6th s.)(tathā* api*)(hetoḥ, m. 6th s.)(na* eva*)(vyāvarttate ”vṛt Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(a-siddhatā, f. 1st s.)(yataḥ*)
body.translated_text: 1265. But suppose [the opponent says]: let the universal and so forth not be the apprehensible qualifier; even so, the unestablishedness of the reason does not turn away, because —

body.text:
1266.
(yadi*)(a-grahaṇam, n. 1st s.)(rupeṇa, 3rd s.)(vyavacchinna-)(antara-)(artha-)(syāt ”as Opt. III p. s.)(vā*)(grahaḥ)(artha-)(eva*)(vā*)(a-grahaḥ)(yathā*)(ghaṭe, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 1266. If non-apprehension is [understood] in the form of an object whose interior is excluded — or [if there is] apprehension of [just] the object — or non-apprehension [of the qualifier], as in [the case of] a pot,

body.text:
1267.
(yadi*)(a-grahaṇam, n. 1st s.)(rūpeṇa, 3rd s.)(vyavacchinna-)(antara-)(ghaṭa-)(vā*)(grahaḥ)(ghaṭasya, 6th s.)(mātra-)(vā*)(vai*)(a-grahaḥ)(ghaṭasya, 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 1267. If non-apprehension is [understood] in the form of a pot whose interior is excluded — or [if there is] apprehension of the pot merely — or indeed non-apprehension of the pot [as qualified],

body.text:
1268.
(cet*)(matam, n. 1st s.)(grāhi, n. 1st s.)(bhāvena, 3rd s.)(vyavacchinnam, n. 1st s.)(antara-)(grāhya-)(vijñānam, n. 1st.)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(sa-vikalpaka-)(-vat*)(bodha-)(vṛkṣa-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 1268. If it is held that [non-conceptual] cognition apprehends [an object] whose interior is excluded by [its own] nature — [then] it would be like conceptual cognition (<s>sa-vikalpaka</s>), [which apprehends] trees and so forth.

body.text:
1269.
(ca*)(vidyate ”vid IV C.)(na*)(viśeṣaḥ)(a-spṛṣṭa-)(sāmānyaḥ)(cet*)(tat-)(a-spaṣṭa-)(grahaṇe, 7th s.)(vibhāvatvāt, 5th s.)(na*)(gṛhyate ”grah pass.)
body.translated_text: 1269. And there is no particular [that is] untouched by the universal; if [you say that] in the unclear apprehension of that [universal], because of [the universal's] being a qualifying condition — [we reply:] it is not apprehended.

body.text:
1270.
(iti*)(bodhaḥ)(viśiṣṭa-)(viṣayaḥ)(na*)(kalpanā, f. 1st s.)(iti*)(sāhasam*)(na*)(sambhavaḥ)(vaiśiṣṭya-)(ṛte*)(sambandhāt, m. 5th s.)(viśeṣaṇa-)
body.translated_text: 1270. Thus [to say] that cognition has a qualified object [and yet] is not conceptual construction — this is rash; for qualification is impossible without the connection with a qualifier.

body.text:
1271.
(bodhaḥ)(mataḥ)(viśiṣṭa-)(viṣayaḥ)(grahāt, 5th s.)(artha-)(vyāvṛtta-)(sajātīya-)(vijātīya-)(na*)(saṅgateḥ, 6th s.)(viśeṣaṇa-)
body.translated_text: 1271. [If] cognition is held to have a qualified object — from the apprehension of an object excluded from what is of the same kind and of different kind — [this is] not tenable, [because of the absence of] connection with the qualifier.

body.text:
1272.
(hi*)(vaiśiṣṭyam, n. 1st s.)(bhedaḥ)(na*)(saṅgatiḥ, f. 1st s.)(viśeṣaṇa-)(tat, n. 1st s.)(api*)(iti*)(bhinnam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(pratīyate, prati-”i, pass. Pr. III p. s.)(anuviddham, n. 1st s.)(vācā, f. 3rd s.).
body.translated_text: 1272. For qualification is not [mere] distinction; and the connection with the qualifier — that too is not cognized as distinct [from the qualified]; [it is] not apprehended as pervaded by speech.

body.text:
1273.
(tu*)(sati, 7th s.)(tasmin, 7th s.)(gṛhīte, 7th s.)(vyatirekiṇi, 7th s.)(niḥśeṣa-)(padārtha-)(apara-)(svabhāva-)(jāyate ”jan pass.)(vikalpaḥ)(tathā*)
body.translated_text: 1273. But when that [qualifier], being apprehended as distinct [from the qualified], [is grasped], then a conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) arises that [posits] another nature — the entirety of the category (<s>padārtha</s>) — accordingly.

body.text:
1274.
(sāmānyam, n. 1st s.)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(paraiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(an-avacchinnam, n. 1st s.)(viśeṣaṇa-)(grāhyam, n. 1st s.)(nirvikalpaka-)(vijñāna-)(ataḥ*)(samam, n. 1st s.)(tatra*)(api*)
body.translated_text: 1274. The universal is accepted by the opponents as undivided by qualifiers, [and as] apprehensible by non-conceptual cognition (<s>nirvikalpaka vijñāna</s>); therefore the same [objection applies] there as well.

body.text:
1275.
(sāmānyam, n. 1st s.)(avagamyate ”gam / gacch pass.)(viśiṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(viśeṣāt, m. 5th s.)(ataḥ*)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(grāhakam, n. 1st s.)(tat-)(prāptam, n. 1st s.)(sa-vikalpakam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1275. The universal is cognized as qualified — [i.e., distinguished] from the particular; therefore the cognition that apprehends it is consequently conceptual (<s>sa-vikalpaka</s>).

body.text:
1276.
(cet*)(gṛhītaḥ)(nirviśeṣam, n. 1st s.)(ucyate ”vac pass.)(sāmānyam, n. 1st s.)(tataḥ*)(na*)(yujyate ”yuj pass.)(sāmānya-)(viśiṣṭatvam, n. 1st s.)(viśeṣāt, n. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 1276. If the universal is said to be apprehended without qualification — then the qualification of the universal by [its] distinction from the particular is not tenable.

body.text:
1277.
(kila*)(ime, m. 1st pl.)(jñāyamānāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(bhāvena, 3rd s.)(sama-)(vaiṣamya-)(prakalpayanti ”kḷp caus. Pr. III p. pl.)(ātmani, n. 7th s.)(sthitim, 2nd s.)(sāmānya-)(viśeṣa-)
body.translated_text: 1277. Indeed, these [entities], being cognized in [their] nature of sameness and difference, project upon themselves the status of universal and particular.

body.text:
1278.
(yadi*)(bhavaḥ)(sama-)(vaiṣamya-)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(pravibhaktaḥ)(tat*)(-tvam, n. 1st s.)(sāmānyasya, 6th s.)(viśeṣṭa-)(viśeṣatas*)(avastham, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1278. If existence is accepted as divided into sameness and difference — [then] the nature of the universal, [which should be] without stages, [would be] qualified by particulars.

body.text:
1279.
(atha*)(ayam, f. 1st s.)(sthitiḥ, f. 1st s.)(a-saṅkīrnā, f. 1st s.)(katham*)(eva*)(a-vibhakaḥ)(a-parihāreṇa, 3rd s.)(anyonya-)(na*)(antaram, n. 1st s.)(gati-)(sthiteḥ, 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 1279. Now, if this [universal's] mode of being is unmixed — how [can it be] undivided? Without the removal of the mutual [distinction], there is no [way to establish] the distinction of [its] mode of being.

body.text:
1280.
(na*)(aparam, n. 1st s.)(lakṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(bheda-)(atirekeṇa, m. 3rd s.)(ātma-)(viśeṣa-)(katham*)(grahaṇam, n. 1st s.)(teṣu, 7th pl.)(ucyate ”vac pass.)(a-sparśane, 7th s.)(tat-)(rūpa-)
body.translated_text: 1280. There is no other defining mark beyond distinction of self and particular; how is apprehension in those [cases] to be described, when that form [of the universal] is not touched [by cognition]?

body.text:
1281.
(ca*)(api*)(tat-)(rūpa-)(sparśane, 7th s.)(gṛhītāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(vibhedinaḥ, f. 1st s.)(antara-)(bheda-)(iti*)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(teṣu, 7th pl.)(prāptam, n. 1st s.)(vikalpakam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1281. And even upon touching that form, [things are] apprehended as having internal distinctions; therefore the cognition regarding those [entities] is consequently conceptual (<s>vikalpaka</s>).

body.text:
1282.
(ca*)(sāmānyam, n. 1st s.)(sampratīyate; sam-prati-”i, pass. Pr. III p. s.)(viśeṣam, n. 1st s. [or: `distinct'] from the featureless thing (nirupākhyāt, 5th s.)(ataḥ*)(te, 6th s.)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(grāhyam, n. 1st s.)(vikalpaka-)(jñāna-)
body.translated_text: 1282. And the universal is cognized as distinct from the featureless [particular] (<s>nirupākhya</s>); therefore [the cognition] of it would be apprehensible by conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpaka jñāna</s>).

body.text:

body.translated_text: 1283. If that [universal] is not qualified — [then] of what nature is [the cognition arising] from the non-existent? If not [of any nature], then why is qualification not accepted? Therefore,

body.text:
1284.
(hi*)(vastunaḥ, 6th s.)(api*)(idam, n. 1st s.)(vaiśiṣṭyam, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(ātmakam, 1st s.)(a-tat-)(ca*)(sāmānyam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(rūpam, 1s. s.)(a-sat-)(katham*)(te, 6th s.)(na*)(viśiṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 1284. For even this qualification of a real thing is of the nature of that [very thing]; and the universal — [which is] not of that [nature] — has no form of non-existence. How is that [universal] not qualified for you?

body.text:
1285.
(tasmāt, 5th s.)(yat, n. 1st s.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(sampravarttate ”vṛt Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(svalakṣaṇe, 7th s.)(viṣayam, n. 1st s.)(atīta-)(patha-)(vak-)(tat*)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(nirvikalpakam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1285. Therefore, whatever cognition arises regarding the unique particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) — having as its object [something] beyond the path of speech — all that is non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>).

body.text:
1286.
(hi*)(ādyam*)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(ālocana-jñānam, n. 1st s.)(nirvikalpakam, n. 1st s.)(sadṛśam, n. 1st s.)(vijñāna-)(bāla-)(mūka-)(ādi-)(-jam, n. 1st s.)(śuddha-)(vastu-)
body.translated_text: [Verse 1286] For initially there exists a bare perceptual cognition (<s>ālocana-jñāna</s>), non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>), similar to the consciousness of infants, mutes, and the like — [born from] a pure object.

body.text:

body.translated_text: [Verse 1287] At that time, neither the universal nor the particular is experienced; but only the individual (<s>vyakti</s>), which is the substratum of those two, is determined.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1288] Thereafter, the object is further determined through properties such as universals and the like, by a cognition which is also accepted as [a form of] direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>).

body.translated_text: [Verse 1289] Again and again, even in conceptual cognition, whatever is apprehended in accordance with the connection [with the object] — all of that is held to be direct perception.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1290] For the objects of the senses, when they have entered a heated interior chamber and the like, do not appear [directly]; yet they are not [therefore] unknown to the senses.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1291] Just as having previously known [them] through the mere appearance, [people] later recognize them in their own nature — so too with regard to [their] properties of universal and the like.

1292.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1292] But if someone, having perceived [an object], were to close his eyes and conceptualize [it], that [conceptualization] would not have the status of direct perception, because of the absence of connection [with the object].

body.text:
1293.
(tat, n. 1st s.)(a-yuktam, n. 1st s.)(yadi*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(pravṛttam, n. 1st s.)(tat-)(svalakṣaṇe, 7th s.)(hi*)(api*)(grahaṇe, 7th s.)(jāti-)(ādi-)(tat, n. 1st s.)(an-āviṣṭa-)(abhilāpam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: [Verse 1293] That is not correct. If the cognition has arisen regarding that <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (unique particular), then even in the apprehension of universals and the like, that [cognition] is free from verbal designation.

body.text:
1294.
(tathā* ca*)(idam, n. 1st s.)(sādhitam, n. 1st s.)(prāk*)(svalakṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(a-vācyam, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(vṛttam, n. 1st s.)(tasmin, 7th s.)(niyatam, n. 1st s.)(nirvikalpakam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: [Verse 1294] And thus this has been previously established: the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (unique particular) is inexpressible. The consciousness that occurs with respect to it is necessarily non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>).

body.translated_text: [Verse 1296] If the qualifier were absolutely different from the qualified, then how could it generate a cognition conforming to its own [nature] in the qualified?

body.translated_text: [Verse 1297] And a single cognition knowing both its own [nature] and the universal is not justified. For in the conceptual [cognition], [there is] no knowledge of the previous [non-conceptual moment]; in the alteration of the subsequent [moment],

body.text:
1298.
(ekāntena, 3rd s.)(a-bhāvāt, 5th s.)(anyatā-)(cet*)(jāti-)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(gatam, n. 1st s.)(ādyena, 3rd s.)(adhigantṛtvāt, 5th s.)(artha-)(vijñāta-)(param, n. 1st s.)(samam, n. 1st s.)(smārtta-jñāna-)
body.translated_text: [Verse 1298] if [you say that] because of the absolute absence of otherness, the universal and the like has been reached by the first [cognition] — then, because of the cognizer having comprehended the object, the subsequent [cognition] would be equal to a memory-cognition.

body.text:

body.translated_text: [Verses 1299-1300] If the apprehension is confused by the universal having multiple forms — then the object is certainly not ascertained. But [each] successive determination [refines the understanding].

body.text:
1300.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1300] Just as inference [operates through] the ascertainment of the exclusion and superimposition of the object-domain, so too is the determination of the exclusion and superimposition of the object.

body.text:
1301.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1301] The validity of inference is not through being an object, [but through] exclusion and superimposition. Even memory would have the absurd consequence of being a valid means of cognition.

body.text:
1302.
(tu*)(laiṅgikam, n. 1st s.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(iṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(pramāṇam, n. 1st s.)(vāraṇāt, 5th s.)(samāropana-)(udbhūta-)(anantara-)(pratyakṣa-)(tat, n. 1st s.)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(na*)(te, 6th s.)
body.translated_text: [Verse 1302] But inferential cognition is accepted as a valid means of cognition because of the prevention of superimposition — that [cognition] arisen immediately after direct perception does not exist for that [opponent].

1303.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1303] For initially [one perceives]: 'this is a white cow moving.' Immediately after direct perception, no superimposition is known. In this cognition, what is being negated?

body.translated_text: [Verse 1306] Even non-conceptual cognition, possessing the power of generating conceptual cognition — through that door, it becomes the basis of all practical activity without remainder.

body.translated_text: 1396. There would be uncommonness (<s>asādhāraṇatā</s>) in the reason [and] in the proof of moon-ness; and in the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>), when the well-known [example] is resorted to — the form of the real thing.

body.text:
1397.
(na*)(viśeṣaḥ)(samīkṣyate ”īkṣ pass.)(kṛtatvasya, n. 6th s.)(patat-)(kīṭa-)(ca*)(udayasya, m. 6th s.)(pratilabdha-)(saṃsparśa-)(patat-)(kīṭaka-)
body.translated_text: 1397. No distinction is observed between [the property of] being made and the arising of a falling insect — and the contact obtained from a falling insect.

body.text:
1398.
(hi*)(kāryam, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(patataḥ)(asya, m. 6th s.)(viśeṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(hetoḥ, m. 6th s.)(anyathā*)(vyabhicāritvam, n. 1st s.)(prasajyate ”sajj pass.)(durnivāram, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1398. For the qualifier [that says] 'this [sensation] is the effect of that [insect] which has fallen' — otherwise, the deviancy [of the reason] would follow, [and it would be] difficult to prevent.

body.text:
1399.
(yadi*)(sādhyaḥ)(vyavahāraḥ)(kāryatā-)(sati, n. 7th s.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(vismaraṇe, n. 7th s.)(syāt ”as Opt. III p. s.)(tri-rūpaḥ)(nidarśanāt, n. 5th s.)(siddha-)(pūrva-)
body.translated_text: 1399. If the [property] to be proved is conventional usage — when there is effecthood, when there is forgetfulness of that — [the reason] would be triple-characterized from a previously established example.

body.text:
1400.
(sattā, f. 1st s.)(cakṣuṣaḥ, n. 6th s.)(dharmi-rūpasya, n. 6th s.)(tāvat*)(a-niścitā, f. 1st s.)(ca*)(sādhanam, n. 1st s.)(tasyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(na*)(yuktam, n. 1st s.)(prasaṅgataḥ* [-tas suff.])(a-siddhi-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 1400. The existence of the eye in the form of the subject is, to begin with, not ascertained; and the proof of that [existence] is not appropriate — because of the consequence of non-establishment and so forth.

body.text:
1401.
(kintu*)(rūpa-)(ādi-)(bhāve, m. 7th s.)(cakṣur-)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(jāyate ”jan pass.)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(gamyate ”gam / gacch pass. Pr. III p. s.)(iti*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(mātram, n. 1st s.)(na*)(hetuḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1401. Rather, when form and so forth are absent, visual cognition does not arise; by that alone [the eye's role] is understood; that much alone — not the [formal] reason.

body.text:
1402.
(aṅkura-)(ādiḥ, m. 1st s.)(vidyate ”vid IV C.)(udbhūtiḥ, f. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(niyata-)(sva-)(hetu-)(ca*)(evam*)(tasmin, m 7th s.)(dṛṣṭānte, m. 7th s.)(vailakṣaṇyam, n. 1st s.)(atisphuṭam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1402. A sprout and so forth exists, having the nature of emergence — with a determinate cause; and thus, in that example, the dissimilarity [from the subject] is very clear.

body.text:
1403.
(sādhane, n. 7th s.)(ghaṭa-)(ādiṣu, m. 7th pl.)(kathaṃcit*)(ātmatva-)(a-sat-)(hetu-)(dṛśyate ”dṛś / paśy pass.)(-vat*)(pūrva-)(vaiphalyam, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(a-prasiddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1403. In the proof — regarding pots and so forth — somehow [having] the nature of a self, [which is] non-existent — the reason is seen; and there is also the futility of the previous [argument], and its non-establishment.

body.text:
1404.
(ca*)(atra*)(api*)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(vispaṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(nidarśanam, n. 1st s.)(vaidharmyeṇa, n. 3rd s.)(hi*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(rūpam, n. 1st s.)(teṣām, m. 6th pl.)(prayāti ”yā II C. Pr. III p. s.)(vipakṣatām, f. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 1404. And here too there is a clear example by dissimilarity; for that very form of those [entities] goes to the status of the dissimilar instance (<s>vipakṣa</s>).

body.text:
1405.
(-tva-)(ātma-)(kathaṃcana*)(sat-)(nirātmasu, n. 7th pl.)(siddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(iṣṭa-)(ca*)(a-siddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(ca*)(āptiḥ, f. 1st s.)(vaidharma-)(eva*)(tathā*)
body.translated_text: 1405. The establishment of somehow-existent selfhood in what is without self — the desired [conclusion]; and [its] non-establishment — the attainment [of the conclusion] by dissimilarity alone; likewise.

body.text:
1406.
(sambandhitā, f. 1st s.)(pitṛ-)(veśmanaḥ, n. 6th s.)(pratipādyate ”pad caus. pass.)(śruteḥ, f. 5th s.)(pitṛ-)(śabda-)(hetuḥ, m. 1st s.)(tatra*)(vyaktaḥ)(tri-lakṣaṇaḥ)
body.translated_text: 1406. The connection with the father's house is demonstrated from hearing the word 'father'; the reason is clearly triple-characterized there.

body.text:
1407.
(kvacit*)(prāk*)(svaraḥ)(upalakṣitaḥ)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(an-anubhave, m. 7th s.)(pūrvam, 2nd s. [adv.])(a-siddhatā, f. 1st s.)(hetu-)(durddharā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1407. [If] a [particular] tone is observed somewhere before — when that [tone] is not [previously] experienced — the non-establishment of the reason would be insuperable.

body.text:
1408.
(yasmin, n. 7th s.)(saḥ)(upalabdhaḥ)(prāk*)(ca*)(yatra*)(na*)(upalabdhaḥ)(anvayaḥ)(vā*)(vyatirekaḥ)(vispaṣṭam, 2nd s. [adv.])(dṛśyate ”dṛś / paśy pass.)
body.translated_text: 1408. Wherever it [the mark] has been observed, and wherever it has not been observed — the positive concomitance or the negative concomitance is clearly seen.

body.text:
1409.
(tu*)(śabdaḥ)(na* eva*)(jñāpayati ”jñā caus. Pr. III p. s.)(bāhyam*)(kathaṃcana*)(anyathā*)(a-sambhava-)(a-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(tu*)(asau, m. 1st s.)(gamakaḥ)(vivakṣā-)
body.translated_text: 1409. But the word does not inform [us] of the external [object] in any way whatsoever; because of the impossibility of [its being] otherwise — rather, that [word] is indicative [only] of the intention to speak.

body.text:
1410.
(tasyām, f. 7th s.)(pratipādyāyām, f. 7th s.)(vailakṣaṇyam, n. 1st s.)(atisphuṭam, n. 1st s.)(bhāve, m. 7th s.)(vivakṣā, f. 1st s.)(a-saṃmukhī-)(śabdaḥ)(na*)(prayujyate ”yuj pass. Pr. III p. s.)
body.translated_text: 1410. When that [intention] is being conveyed, the distinctiveness is extremely clear; when [the intention to speak of] a [particular] entity is not directed [at an object] — the word is not employed.

body.text:
1411.
(tu*)(dīpaḥ)(na* eva*)(jñāpakaḥ)(nīla-)(ādeḥ, m. 6th s.)(bhāvataḥ* [-tas suff.])(liṅga-)(jananāt, n. 5th s.)(yogyasya, m. 6th s.)(utpādana-)(jñāna-)(tu*)(ucyate ”vac pass.)(tathā*)
body.translated_text: 1411. But a lamp is not an informer of blue and so forth in terms of reality; from the production of the cognition that is suitable — [the lamp is] called [merely] the cause of [that] cognition; so too [with the word].

body.text:
1412.
(ca*)(jñāpake, m. 7th s.)(liṅga-rūpe, m. 7th s.)(dharma-)(pakṣa-)(ādi, ns. 1st s.)(cintyate ”cint X C. pass.)(anyathā*)(kasmāt, n. 5th s.)(codyate ”cud pass.)(cakṣur-)(ādīnām, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 1412. And when the mark has the form of a logical sign — the property of the thesis (<s>pakṣadharmatā</s>) and so forth is examined; otherwise, why should [the marks] of the eye and so forth be questioned?

body.text:
1413.
(api*)(anyathā*)(an-upapattyā, f. 3rd s.)(cākṣaṣatvam, n. 1st s.)(sādhakam, n. 1st s.)(viyogena, m. 3rd s.)(dharma-)(pakṣa-)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(eka-lakṣaṇāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(klībāḥ, m. 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 1413. Moreover, through the impossibility of [it being] otherwise — the [mark's] being perceptual (<s>cākṣuṣatva</s>) serves as a proof; through separation from the property of the thesis — those of single-character are neuter [i.e., inconclusive].

body.text:
1414.
(uktānām, n. 6th pl.)(eka-rūpatayā, f. 3rd s.)(dvairūpyam, n. 1st s.)(upalakṣitam, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(uktānām, n. 6th pl.)(dvi-rupatvena, n. 3rd s.)(trairūpyam, n. 1st s.)(dharmataḥ* [-tas suff.])(pakṣa-)
body.translated_text: 1414. What has been stated to have single-formedness is observed to have dual-formedness; and what has been stated to have dual-formedness [is observed to have] triple-formedness — by the nature of the thesis-property.

body.text:
1415.
(ca*)(cet*)(ākṣepāt, m. 5th s.)(iti*)(eva*)(anyathā*)(an-upapattyā, f. 3rd s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(na*)(ādau, m. 7th s.)(śabda-)(api*)(cākṣaṣatve, n. 7th s.)(anyathā*)(iṣṭe, n. 7th s.)(asau, n. 1st s.)(atha*)(na*)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)
body.translated_text: 1415. And if [one says] 'through implication' — thus through the impossibility of [it being] otherwise — that is not [valid]; in the case of the word at the outset — even when the perceptual [character] is accepted as [being] otherwise — then [if] that does not exist [either] —

body.text:
1416.
(ādi-)(hetūnām, m. 6th pl.)(putratva-)(tat-)(vyatirekataḥ* [-tas suff.])(sandigdha-)(trailakṣaṇya-)(na*)(sadbhāve, m. 7th s.)(a-virodhataḥ* [-tas suff.])(vijātīya-)
body.translated_text: 1416. Of the initial causes — the sonship of that [cause] — the triple-characterization through the exclusion of what is different in kind — is doubtful when [the thing] exists, because of non-contradiction.

body.text:
1417.
(api*)(putratve, n. 7th s.)(tat-)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(anyathā*-bhāvaḥ)(hi*)(sambhāvyate ”bhū caus. pass.)(viśeṣataḥ* [-tas suff.])(hetūnām, m. 6th pl.)(karma-)(āhāra-)(ādi-).
body.translated_text: 1417. Moreover, even in [the case of] sonship — the alteration of that [cause] is conceivable, especially because of [the variety of] causes such as <s>karma</s> (action), food, and so forth.

body.text:
1418.
(ayam, m. 1st s.)(na*)(sva-bhāvaḥ)(vā* [na])(kāryam, n. 1st s.)(vā* [na])(eva*)(a-dṛṣṭiḥ, f. 1st s.)(dṛśyasya, n. 6th s.)(ca*)(vyatiriktasya, m. 6th s.)(tat-)(bhavati ”bhū Pr. III p. s.)(na*)(a-vyabhicāritā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1418. This is neither an own-nature [proof] nor an effect [proof]; [there is] non-perception of what is perceptible; and of what is excluded [from the perceptible] — that [proof] does not have unfailing [concomitance].

body.text:
1419-1420.
(a-vyabhicāritvam, n. 1st s.)(dṛśyate ”dṛś / paśy pass.)(anyeṣam, m. 6th p..)(api*)(yathā*)(udayaḥ)(candra-)(dṛṣṭaḥ)(liṅgam, n. 1st s.)(vikāsasya, m. 6th s.)(kumudānām, n. 6th s.)(ca*)(vṛddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(jaladheḥ, m. 6th s.)(ca*)(sadbhāvataḥ* [-tas suff.])(ātapasya, m. 6th s.)(sadbhāvaḥ)(chāyāyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(para-bhāgeṣu, m. 7th pl.)(sampratīyate, prati-”i, pass. Pr. III p. s.)
body.translated_text: 1419-1420. [Yet] unfailing [concomitance] is seen of others too — just as the rising of the moon is observed [as] the mark for the blossoming of <s>kumuda</s> (white water-lilies); and the swelling of the ocean; and [just as] from the existence of sunshine, the existence of shadow is understood in the further regions.

body.text:
1421.
(ulmuka-)(dṛṣṭau, f. 7th s.)(tamasi, n. 7th s.)(ārāt*)(dhūmaḥ)(pratīyate, prati-”i, pass. Pr. III p. s.)(ca*)(udayataḥ* [-tas suff.])(kṛttikā-)(kalpanā, f. 1st s.)(āsatti-)(rohiṇī-)
body.translated_text: 1421. When a firebrand is seen, smoke is inferred from afar in the darkness; and from the rising of <s>Kṛttikā</s> (the Pleiades constellation), the proximity of <s>Rohiṇī</s> is inferred.

body.text:
1422-1423.
(sarve, m. 1st pl.)(te, m. 1st pl.)(apare, m. 1st pl.)(bodha-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(jātāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(eka-)(kālataḥ* [-tas suff.])(tat-)(matāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(anumitaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(tādṛśaḥ)(hetuḥ, m. 1st s.)(dharmasya, m. 6th s.)(tat*)(atra*)(iyam, f. 1st s.)(saṃsiddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(kāraṇa-)(kāryāt, n. 5th s.)(evam*)(vidhānataḥ* [-tas suff.])(ca*)(an-upapattau, f. 7th s.)(sambandha-)(gatiḥ, f. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(api*)(sarvasya, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 1422-1423. All those others — cognition and so forth — born at a single time — are considered [to be valid] through inferred [marks]; such a mark of the property — therein lies this establishment: from the effect and the cause, through such arrangement; and when there is impossibility [of it being otherwise], there would be the understanding of the connection of everything.

body.text:
1424.
(ca*)(viśeṣaḥ)(prabhañjana-)(kāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(udaya-)(kṛttikā-)(hi*)(saḥ)(eva*)(yaḥ)(santatyā, f. 3rd s.)(kāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(āsatti-)(rohiṇī-)
body.translated_text: 1424. And the particular [mark]: the wind is the cause of the rising of <s>Kṛttikā</s> (the Pleiades); for that same [wind], through a continuum, is the cause of the proximity of <s>Rohiṇī</s>.

body.text:
1425.
(ca*)(ataḥ*)(tat-)(pratītiḥ, f. 1st s.)(matā, f. 1st s.)(pratītiḥ, f. 1st s.)(dharma-)(hetu-)(iha*)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(na*)(kācit*)(pratītiḥ, f. 1st s.)(tat-)(svatantrā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1425. And therefore, [such] understanding is accepted; the understanding of the property of the inferential mark — there is no understanding here that is independent of that [mark].

body.text:
1426.
(ca*)(anumānam, n. 1st s.)(yat, n. 1st s.)(viṣayam, n. 1st s.)(bimba-)(pravarttate ”vṛt Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(liṅgāt, n. 5th s.)(ākhyāt, n. 5th s.)(pratibimba-)(yuktam, n. 1st s.)(tatra*)(liṅga-)(-jāt, n. 5th s. [-ja suff.])(kārya-)(anyat-)
body.translated_text: 1426. And <s>anumāna</s> (inference), whose object is the original (<s>bimba</s>), operates from the mark — from the stated [sign]; the reflection (<s>pratibimba</s>) is proper therein — born from the mark; the effect-mark and the other [marks].

body.text:
1427.
(pratibimbakam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(vastu-)(dvaya-)(a-sattvāt, n. 5th s.)(saha*)(ekatra*)(tat*)(katham*)(tasya, n. 1st s.)(kāryatā, f. 1st s.)(pāramārthikī, f. 1st s.)(cet*)
body.translated_text: 1427. The reflection (<s>pratibimba</s>) is not a [real] thing — because of the non-existence of two [things] simultaneously in one place; how then [would there be] its real effect-nature?

body.text:
1428.
(yadi* api*)(vastutā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(asya, n. 1st s.)(pratibimbasya, n. 6th s.)(mūrttasya, n. 6th s.)(kena, n. 3rd s.)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(ābhāsam, n. 1st s.)(tat-)(bhaviṣyati ”bhū Fut. III p. s.)(a-vastu, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1428. Even if this reflection (<s>pratibimba</s>) does not have reality — of that embodied [thing], by what [means] will the cognition, having that appearance, become non-real?

body.text:
1429.
(ca*)(liṅgatvam, n. 1st s.)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(hi*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(iṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(atra*)(kāryam, n. 1st s.)(niralambanam, n. 1st s.)(etat, n. 1st s.)(pravarttate ”vṛt Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(ādhipatyāt, n. 5th s.)(bimba-)
body.translated_text: 1429. And its mark-nature is precisely what is accepted here; this effect is without [external] support; it operates [merely] through the dominance of the original (<s>bimba</s>).

body.text:
1430.
(parārtham, n. 1st s.)(varṇyate ”varṇ pass.)(anyaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(vacas, n. 1st s.)(pratijñā-)(ādi-)(bhūtatvāt, n. 5th s.)(aṅga-)(a-sādhana-)(pratijñā, f. 1st s.)(an-upayoginī, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1430. The <s>parārthānumāna</s> (inference for others) is described by others [as including] the statement of the thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>) and so forth; being a component of the proof-method — the thesis, [when] not useful —

body.text:
1431.
(a-sambandhāt, m. 5th s.)(sā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(yuktā, f. 1st s.)(upapādikā, f. 1st s.)(artha-)(na* api*)(yujyate ”yuj pass. Pr. III p. s.)(pārampayena, 3rd s.)(sūcanāt, n. 5th s.)(a-sakta-)
body.translated_text: 1431. Because of [its] lack of connection [with the proof], that [thesis] is not proper as a demonstrator of the meaning; nor is it justified through a successive [chain of reasons] — because of [its merely] indirect indication.

body.text:
1432.
(yadi*)(tu*)(eṣaḥ)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(aṅgam, n. 1st s.)(sādhana-)(upadarśanāt, n. 5th s.)(viṣayasya, m. 6th s.)(sādhana-)(sādhya-)(-vat*)(pada-)(dṛṣṭānta-)
body.translated_text: 1432. If, however, this is accepted as a component of the proof-method — from the demonstration of the subject — then the <s>sādhana</s> (proof) and <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved) [are established] — like a statement and an example.

body.text:
1433.
(nanu*)(vākyena, n. 3rd s.)(abhyanujñā-)(ādi-)(atra*)(vyabhicāritā, f. 1st s.)(ca*)(viṣayasya, m. 6th s.)(upadarśanam, n. 1st s.)(yatra*)(tadā*)(niṣphalam, n. 1st s.)(ca*)
body.translated_text: 1433. [Objection:] 'Indeed, through [the thesis] statement and permission and so forth — here there is deviation [of the mark]'; and the demonstration of the subject — where that [thesis is stated separately] — is then fruitless.

body.text:
1434.
(katham*)(vyavasthā, f. 1st s.)(sapakṣa-)(ādi-)(cet*)(a-prayogataḥ* [-tas suff.])(pakṣa-)(ataḥ*)(trairūpyam, n. 1st s. [tri-rūpa-ya-])(api*)(na*)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(nibandhanam, n. 1st s.)(apekṣā-)(tat-)(cet*)
body.translated_text: 1434. How [then is] the determination of the similar instance (<s>sapakṣa</s>) and so forth? [Answer:] Because of the non-employment of the thesis [separately]; therefore the triple-characterization (<s>trairūpya</s>) too has no basis — if [there is] a dependence on that [thesis] —

body.text:
1435.
(abhidhāne, n. 7th s.)(sādhana-)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(kalpanā, f. 1st s.)(sapakṣa-)(ādi-)(tu*)(śāstre, n. 7th s.)(te, m. 1st pl.)(pravibhajyante ”bhaj pass. Pr. III p. pl.)(tathā*)(vyavahārāya, m. 4th s.)
body.translated_text: 1435. In the statement of the proof-method, there is the conceptual construction of the similar instance and so forth; but in the treatise, they are distinguished — for the purpose of [facilitating] practical usage.

body.text:
1436.
(yadi* vā*)(sā, f. 1st s.)(āśrayā, f. 1st s.)(artha-)(prakṛta-)(na*)(virudhyate ”rudh pass.)(hi*)(vādī, m. 1st s.)(na*)(āha ”ah Pr. III p. s.)(sādhanam, 2nd s.)(api*)(parasya, m. 6th s.)(eva*)(a-kāṇḍe, m. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 1436. Or, if that [statement] has the object at hand as its basis — [then] it is not contradicted; for the proponent does not state the proof [only] for the other — [and] not at an improper occasion.

body.text:
1437.
(dharmatā, f. 1st s.)(pakṣa-)(varttanāt, n. 5th s.)(viśeṣe, m. 7th s.)(jijñāsita-)(samānatvāt, n. 5th s.)(tat-)(tat-)(a-bhāvataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 1437. The thesis-property — from its occurrence in the particular — that is to be investigated; because of the sameness with that, [and] because of the absence of that [property in the dissimilar instance].

body.text:
1438.
(ca*)(an-abhidhāne, n. 7th s.)(pratijñā-)(an-abhidhānataḥ* [-tas suff.])(kāraṇa-)(na*)(karttavyā, f. 1st s.)(uktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(upanayaḥ)(prasiddhaye, f. 4th s.)(sadbhāva-)
body.translated_text: 1438. And when the thesis is not stated — because of the non-statement of the cause — the statement of the <s>upanaya</s> (application) is not to be made; for the establishment of the existence [of the thesis-property].

body.text:
1439.
(mātre, m. 7th s.)(bhāva-)(ukte, m. 7th s.)(prāk*)(ca* paścāt*)(vyapteḥ, f. 6th s.)(prakāśanāt, n. 5th s.)(pratibimbakam, n. 1st s.)(viphalam, n. 1st s.)(saṃsiddheḥ, f. 5th s.)(vivakṣita-)(artha-)
body.translated_text: 1439. When merely the existence of the entity has been previously stated — from the illumination of the pervasion, both before and after — the reflection (<s>pratibimba</s>) is fruitless, because of the establishment of the intended meaning.

body.text:
1440.
(siddhataḥ* [-tas suff.])(eva*)(sāmarthyāt, n. 5th s.)(nirdeśa-)(tri-rūpa-)(hetu-)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(na*)(śaṅkāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(viparyaya-)(tataḥ*)(nigamanam, n. 1st s.)(vyartham, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1440. From the establishment alone, through the capacity of the triple-formed inferential mark — there are no doubts of the contrary; therefore, the conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>) is superfluous.

body.text:
1441.
(eva*)(sambaddhaiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(vacanaiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(ekaḥ)(arthaḥ)(pratipādyate ”pad caus. pass.)(ataḥ*)(artham, 2nd s.)(siddhi-)(sambandha-)(na*)(vācyam, n. 1st s.)(nigamanam, n. 1st s.)(pṛthak*)
body.translated_text: 1441. For, through connected statements, a single meaning is conveyed; therefore, the meaning — the establishment of connection — the conclusion is not to be stated separately.

body.text:
1442.
(evam*)(kecit*)(pracakṣate ”cakṣ Pr. III p. pl.)(dvaividhyam, 2nd s.)(anumānasya, n. 6th s.)(bhedataḥ* [-tas suff.])(paridṛṣṭatva-)(ḍṛṣṭa-)(viśeṣa-)(sāmānya-)
body.translated_text: 1442. Thus, some declare the twofold nature of <s>anumāna</s> (inference) — by the distinction of [what is] generally observed and [what is] particularly observed.

body.text:
1443-1445.
(A)(sambandham, n. 1st s.)(dṛṣṭa-)(pratyakṣa-)(yayoḥ, m. 6th d.)(viśeṣayoḥ, m. 6th d.)(ādi-)(indhana-)(gomaya-)(viśeṣa-)(tat-)(deśa-)(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(kṛtā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1443-1445. (A) The connection of two particular [things] that is directly perceived — such as the particular [connection] of fuel, cow-dung, and so forth — the cognition is made in that place.

body.text:
1444.
(tena, m. 3rd s.)(eva*)(sthena, m. 3rd s.)(tat-)(deśa-)(api*)(gatvā* ”gam / gacch)(yadā*)(punaḥ* punaḥ*)(budhyate ”budh pass. Pr. III p. s.)(kāla-antare, n. 7th s.)(tam, m. 2nd s.)(agnim, m. 2nd s.)(bodhāt, m. 5th s.)(pūrva-)
body.translated_text: 1444. By that very [person, acting as] a thief — having gone to that place — when he cognizes repeatedly at another time — that fire — from the prior cognition,

body.text:
1445.
(tasya, m. 6th s.)(pramāṇatā, f. 1st s.)(bodhāt, m. 5th s.)(vastu-)(sadbhāva-)(sandihyamāna-)(etat, n. 1st s.)(likhitam, n. 1st s.)(vindhyavāsinā, m. 3rd s.)(dṛṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(viśeṣa-)
body.translated_text: 1445. Its validity [as a means of knowledge comes] from the cognition of the real existence [of the thing] that was in doubt; this [inference] is what is observed as particular — [so] <s>Vindhyavāsin</s> has written.

body.text:
1446.
(tu*)(mitau, f. 7th s.)(sāmānyataḥ* [-tas suff.])(vācye, n. 7th s.)(antaratve, n. 7th s.)(agni-)(dhūma-)(iti*)(ādityaḥ, m. 1st s.)(gantā, m. 1st s. [gantṛ- stem])(ekāntāt, n. 5th s.)(dṛṣṭam, 2nd s.)(sāmānya-)
body.translated_text: 1446. But in [the inference] from the general — when what is to be expressed is the otherness of fire and smoke — [such as inferring that] 'the sun is a goer' — from what is observed as general, necessarily.

body.text:
1447.
(tat*)(atra*)(pratisādhanāt, n. 5th s.)(kṣaṇa-bhaṅgasya, m. 6th s.)(vyāpinaḥ, m. 6th s.)(na*)(sambhavaḥ)(anumānasya, n. 6th s.)(eva*)(prāktanasya, n. 6th s.)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(eva*)
body.translated_text: 1447. In that regard — from the establishment of momentary destruction, which is pervasive — [the inference] of this very previous [inference] is not possible; thereby alone.

body.text:
1448.
(cet*)(ekatvam, n. 1st s.)(kalpitam, n. 1st s.)(vivakṣayā, f. 3rd s.)(aikya-)(prabandha-)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(na*)(kācit*)(avasthitiḥ, f. 1st s.)(ca*)(bhāvikam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(vastutvam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1448. If the unity [of the continuum] is fabricated by the desire to express — [being merely] a continuum of oneness — its reality is not actual; and there is no stability whatsoever of that [fabricated unity].

body.text:
1449.
(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(nirviṣayam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(anumanyate ”man pass. Pr. III p. s.)(yuṣmābhiḥ, 3rd pl.)(ca*)(vikalpita-)(arthatāyām, f. 7th s.)(vyaktam, 2nd s. [adv.])(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(nirviṣayam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1449. A cognition without an object is not admitted by you; and when the object-hood is [merely] conceptually constructed, it would clearly be without [a real] object.

body.text:
1450.
(yadi*)(api*)(nāśe, m. 7th s.)(vyakti-)(rūpasya, n. 6th s.)(tayoḥ, n. 6th d.)(ākṛtiḥ, f. 1st s.)(tiṣṭhati ”sthā III C. Pr. III p. s. [975, 992, 1148-49])(eva*)(na*)(bhāve, m. 7th s.)(tasyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(api*)(dhruvam*)(āpteḥ, f. 5th s.)(kṣaṇa-bhaṅga-)
body.translated_text: 1450. Even if, upon the destruction of the form of the individual (<s>vyakti</s>), the configuration (<s>ākṛti</s>) of those two persists — even so, because of [the doctrine of] momentary destruction (<s>kṣaṇa-bhaṅga</s>), the permanence of that [configuration] is certainly not obtained.

body.text:
1451.
(ca*)(kena, m. 3rd s.)(hetunā, m. 3rd s.)(yuṣmābhiḥ, 3rd pl.)(uktaḥ)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(niyamaḥ)(iti*)(eva*)(viśeṣayoḥ, m. 6th d.)(yayoḥ, m. 6th d.)(sambandhaḥ)(dṛṣṭaḥ)(pratyakṣa-)
body.translated_text: 1451. And by what reason has this restriction been stated by you — [namely] that this very [thing] whose connection with the two particulars has been seen by direct perception,

body.text:
1452.
(ekadā*)(dṛṣṭvā*)(anumānena, n. 3rd s.)(anumā, f. 1st s.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(eva*)(punaḥ*)(kasmāt, 5th s.)(na*)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(pramāṇam, n. 1st s.)(hi*)(kaḥ)(viśeṣaḥ)(pūrvake, n. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 1452. Having been seen once, [its inference] by inference again of that very [thing] — why is it not accepted? For what distinction is there in the previous [cognition] as a valid means of cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>)?

body.text:
1453.
(yadi*)(idam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(pramāṇam, n. 1st s.)(adhigantṛtvāt, n. 5th s.)(artha-)(vijñāta-)(-vat*)(smārtta-)(kim*)(na*)(etat, n. 1st s.)(prāktanaḥ)(api*)(vīkṣyate ”īkṣ pass. Pr. III p. s.)(samānam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1453. If this [inference] is not a valid means of cognition because of [merely] apprehending [what is already] known — like a memorial cognition of a [previously] known object — is not the same [objection] seen [to apply] to the earlier [cognition] as well?

body.text:
1454.
(cet*)(tatra*)(ādhikyam, n. 1st s.)(nivarttanāt, n. 5th s.)(sandehasya, m. 6th s.)(pravṛttasya, m. 6th s.)(antarāla-)(kim*)(na*)(sadṛśam, n. 1st s.)(atra*)(api*)
body.translated_text: 1454. If [you say] there is a surplus there — because of the removal of the doubt that had arisen in the interval — is not the same [applicable] here as well?

body.text:
1455.
(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(saḥ)(eva*)(kṛt, n. 1st s.)(vinivṛtti-)(sandeha-)(iti*)(kim*)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(na*)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(iti*)(etat, n. 1st s.)(sāmānya-)(darśanam, n. 1st s.)(nirākāṅkṣam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1455. Therefore, that very [inference] is the remover of doubt — [the question] 'does it exist or not?' — this perception of the universal is free from [further] expectation.

body.text:
1456.
(kecana*)(ku-dṛṣṭayaḥ)(prāhuḥ ”ah Pr. III p. s.)(iti*)(anumanam, n. 1st .s)(na*)(pramānam, n. 1st s.)(api*)(vāgbhiḥ, f. 3rd pl.)(arpayantaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(vivakṣam, f. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 1456. Some with wrong views declare — [expressing their] desire to speak through words — that inference is not a valid means of cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>).

body.text:
1457.
(mānam, n. 1st s. [=pramāṇam])(sva-artham, n. 1st s.)(na*)(yujyate ”yuj pass. Pr. III p. s.)(pūrvatvāt, n. 5th s.)(tri-rūpa-)(liṅga-)(yathā*)(mithyā-)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(janyam, n. 1st s.)(ghāṭa-kṛtā, m. 3rd s.)(iṣṭa-)
body.translated_text: 1457. [They argue:] the valid means of cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) regarding its own object is not tenable — because of the priority of the three-formed inferential mark (<s>trirūpa-liṅga</s>); [or they say] just as erroneous cognition is produced by the effort of the desired [conclusion],

body.text:
1458.
(na*)(ca*)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(trairūpyam, n. 1st s.)(liṅgasya, n. 6th s.)(kāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(anumiti-)(bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(api*)(an-anumāne, n. 7th s.)(iva*)(dvairūpyam, n. 1st s.)(ataḥ*)(anumā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1458. And the triple form (<s>trairūpya</s>) of the inferential mark is not the cause of inferential cognition (<s>anumiti</s>); even in what is not inference, there is double form; therefore inference [would not be valid].

body.text:
1459.
(virodhasya, m. 6th s.)(anumāna-)(ca*)(sambhavāt, m. 5th s.)(sarvatra*)(sādhane, n. 7th s.)(viruddhānām, m. 6th pl.)(kiñca*)(a-vyabhicāriṇaḥ, m. 5th s.)(viruddha-)
body.translated_text: 1459. And because of the possibility everywhere of [finding] a contradiction to inference — since among those that do not deviate from what is contradictory, [there is always the possibility of finding contradictory evidence] in the probandum,

body.text:
1460.
(avasthā-)(deśa-)(kālānām, m. 6th pl.)(bhedāt, n. 5th s.)(bhinnāsu, f. 7th pl.)(śaktiṣu, f. 7th s.)(prasiddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(bhāvānām, m. 6th pl.)(anumānena, n. 3rd s.)(atidurlabhā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1460. Because of the difference of conditions (<s>avasthā</s>), places (<s>deśa</s>), and times (<s>kāla</s>), and because of the different capacities [of things] — the establishment of [the nature of] entities through inference is extremely difficult to obtain.

body.text:
1461.
(sambandhe, m. 7th s.)(viśiṣṭa-)(dravya-)(asya, n. 6th s.)(śakteḥ, f. 6th s.)(vijñāta-)(sā, f. 1st s.)(śaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(pratibadhate ”badh pass. Pr. III p. s.)(prati*)(tām, tām, f. 2nd s.)(artha-kriyām, 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 1461. When the capacity [of a thing] is known in connection with a particular substance — that [very] capacity is obstructed with respect to that [particular] purposeful action.

body.text:
1462.
(api*)(arthaḥ)(anumitaḥ)(yatnena, m. 3rd s.)(upapādyate ”pad IV C. pass. Pr. III p. s.)(eva*)(anyathā*)(abhiyuktataraiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(kuśalaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(anumātṛbhiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 1462. Even an object that has been inferred — through effort — is established otherwise by more skilled and more learned inferrers.

body.text:
1463-1467.
(anumanam, n. 1st s.)(para-artham, n. 1st s.)(tu*)(na*)(mānam, n. 1st s.)(anuvādāt, m. 5th s.)(apekṣayā, f. 3rd s.)(vaktṛ-)(asau, m. 1st s.)(na*)(svayam*)(prapadyate ”pad pass.)(artham, m. 2nd s.)(tena, n. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 1463-1467. But inference-for-others (<s>parārthānumāna</s>) is not a valid means of cognition, because of [merely] restating [what is already known]; from the standpoint of the speaker — he does not himself apprehend the object through that [inference-for-others].

body.text:
1464.
(api*)(vyapekṣayā, f. 3rd s.)(śrotṛ-)(etat, n. 1st s.)(upapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(eva*)(svārtham, m. 2nd s.)(hi*)(kaḥ)(viśeṣaḥ)(saṃvidaḥ, f. 6th s.)(mūlāyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(śrotra-)(darśana-)
1465.
(apekṣayā, f. 3rd s.)(śrotṛ-)(vacasaḥ, n. 6th s.)(na*)(anumanatvam, n. 1st s.)(artha-)(para-)(-taḥ* [-tas suff.])(hetutva-)(santāna-)(vijñāna-)(śrotṛ-)(jñāpakatva-)
body.translated_text:
1464. Even from the standpoint of the listener, this is indeed tenable [as inference]-for-one's-own-sake; for what distinction is there from the root awareness of the listener's auditory perception?
1465. The statement is not [a case of] inference-for-others (<s>parārthānumāna</s>) — from the standpoint of other-directed causality; [it is rather due to] the capacity of informing the listener's cognitive stream, like a sense organ.

body.text:
1466.
(yathā*)(indriyasya, m. 6th s.).
(na*)(sākṣāt*)(prakāśanam, n. 1st s.)(anumeya-)(ca*)(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(-vat*)(jñāna-)(sambandha-)(a-vinābhāva-)(asya, n. 6th s.)(na*)(tat, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1466. [The statement] is not a direct illumination of the inferable [object]; and therefore, [it is] not that [inference-for-others]; the invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>) and the connection of cognition — [these are] not [properties] of that [statement].

body.text:
1467.
(atha*)(ucyate ”vac pass.)(artha-)(para-)(apekṣayā, f. 3rd s.)(vyāvṛtti-)(para-)(tat, n. 1st s.)(api*)(a-yuktam, n. 1st s.)(svārthe, m. 7th s.)(api*)(prasaṅgataḥ* [-tas suff.])(parārthatva-)
body.translated_text: 1467. Now, if it is said [that inference-for-others is defined] from the standpoint of the exclusion of other [meanings] directed toward [another's] object — that too is unjustified, because inference-for-others would follow even in [the case of] one's own object.

body.text:
1468.
(nanu*)(pūrvatvam, n. 1st s.)(tri-rūpa-)(liṅga-)(lakṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(saṃvādi-)(ca*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(mānatvam, n. 1st s.)(kim*)(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(niṣidhyate ”sidh pass.)
body.translated_text: 1468. But surely, the priority of the three-formed inferential mark (<s>trirūpa-liṅga</s>) is [its] defining characteristic; and that [cognition] which is concordant [with reality] has the status of being a valid means of cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) — why is that rejected?

body.text:
1469.
(mithyā-)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(samānam, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(pūrva-)(pakṣa-)(vyapekṣayā, f. 3rd s.)(iṣṭa-)(ghāṭa-)(kṛtā, f. 3rd s.)(janyam, n. 1st s.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(uktam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(vastutaḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 1469. The erroneous cognition [objection] is equal [to our position] — from the standpoint of the prima facie view (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>); the cognition produced by the effort of the desired [conclusion] has been stated [as an objection, but] not [as valid] in reality.

body.text:
1470.
(vastu-)(sthityā, f. 3rd s.)(hi*)(tat-)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(a-visaṃvādi, n. 1st s.)(niścitam, n. 1st s.)(vādi-)(iṣṭa-)(viparītasya, m. 6th s.)(pramāṇam, n. 1st s.)(ataḥ*)(eva*)(tat, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1470. For by the state of affairs of the real thing, that cognition is ascertained as non-discordant; [the cognition] of the opposite of what is intended by the proponent — therefore, that alone is the valid means of cognition.

body.text:
1471.
(ataḥ*)(viruddhatā, f. 1st s.)(hetoḥ, m. 6th s.)(dṛṣṭānte, m. 7th s.)(ca*)(api*)(a-sādhyatā, f. 1st s.)(etena, m. 3rd s.)(eva*)(prakāreṇa, m. 3rd s.)(dvitīye, m. 7th s.)(hetu-)(a-siddhatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1471. Therefore, the contradictoriness of the reason, and in the example too, the unprovability — by this very method, in the second [case as well], there is the unestablishedness of the reason.

body.text:
1472.
(vādinaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(nyāya-)(prāhuḥ ”ah Pr. III p. s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(sādhanam, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(siddhaye, f. 4th s.)(yat, n. 1st s.)(sambandham, n. 1st s.)(pariniścitam, n. 1st s.)(yat, n. 1st s.)(tādātmya-)(utpattyā, f. 3rd s.)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 1472. The <s>Naiyāyikas</s> (logicians) declare that [the inferential mark], the proof for the sake of establishing [the thesis] — whose connection has been ascertained — that [connection is either] through identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) or through origination.

body.text:
1473.
(īdṛśaḥ)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(na*)(virodha-)(anumāna-)(ādiḥ, m. 1st s.)(hi*)(na*)(eva*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(sambhavati ”bhū Pr. III p. s.)(kvacit*)(vinā*)(ātma-)(hetubhyām, m. 3rd d.)
body.translated_text: 1473. There is no such [thing as] contradiction to inference and the like; for that [contradiction] is never possible anywhere without the two — identity and causality.

body.text:
1474.
(ca*)(paraspara-)(viruddhau, m. 1st d.)(dharmau, m. 1st d.)(na*)(yujyete ”yuj VII C. pass. Pr. III p. d.)(ekatra*)(vastuni, n. 7th s.)(ataḥ*)(na*)(sambhavaḥ)(a-vyabhicāriṇaḥ, m. 6th s.)(viruddha-)
body.translated_text: 1474. And two mutually contradictory properties are not possible in one and the same real thing; therefore, the non-deviating contradictory [mark] is not possible.

body.text:
1475.
(ca*)(vṛttiḥ, f. 1st s.)(anumā-)(lakṣaṇānām, n. 6th pl.)(abhyasta-)(liṅga-)(samyak*)(viniścaye, n. 7th s.)(tu*)(anyā, f. 1st s.)(abhidhīyate ”dhā pass.)(iti*)(na*)(anumā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1475. And the operation of those [marks] possessing the characteristics of inference — upon the correct ascertainment of the well-practiced inferential mark — another [cognition] is spoken of [as arising]; that is not [the same as] inference.

body.text:
1476.
(ataḥ*)(śaktiṣu, f. 7th pl.)(bhinnāsu, f. 7th pl.)(bhedāt, m. 5th s.)(avasthā-)(kālānām, m. 6th pl.)(deśa-)(siddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(bhāvānām, m. 6th pl.)(anumānena, n. 3rd s.)(na*)(sudurlabhā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1476. Therefore, even when capacities are different — because of the difference of conditions, times, and places — the establishment of [the nature of] entities through inference is not at all difficult to obtain.

body.text:
1477.
(api*)(arthaḥ)(anumitaḥ)(yatnena, m. 3rd s.)(kuśalaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(anumātṛbhiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(saḥ)(na*)(sādhyate ”sidh caus. pass.)(anyathā*)(api*)(anyaiḥ, m. 3rd s.)(abhiyuktataraiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 1477. Even an object that has been inferred through effort by skilled inferrers — that is not established otherwise even by more skilled [opponents].

body.text:
1478.
(hi*)(na*)(svabhāvaḥ)(ṛte*)(svabhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(vā*)(kāryam, n. 1st s.)(kāraṇāt, n. 5th s.)(prāpteḥ, f. 5th s.)(bheda-)(a-nimittatā, f. 1st s.)(ca*)(vinā*)(te, n. 2nd d.)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(na*)(anumā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1478. For neither does an essential nature [exist] apart from the essential nature, nor does an effect [exist apart] from its cause; the absence of a reason for distinction [between them] — and without those two, there is no inference.

body.text:
1479.
(vacasaḥ, n. 6th s.) (tri-rūpa-)(liṅga-)(yat, n. 1st s.)(uktam, n. 1st s.)(anumānatvam, n. 1st s.)(artha-)(para-)(sūcakatvataḥ* [-tas suff.])(sakta-)tat, n. 1st s.)(apekṣayā, f. 3rd s.)(śrotṛ-)
body.translated_text: 1479. The statement — possessing the three-formed inferential mark (<s>trirūpa-liṅga</s>) — which has been called 'inference-for-others' (<s>parārthānumāna</s>) from the standpoint of indicating the object of another, attached to the listener's expectation —

body.text:
1480.
(evam*)(anumānatvam, n. 1st s.)(āśritam, n . 1st s.)(gauṇam, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(sāṅketikam, n. 1st s.)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(saṃsūcakatvena, n. 3rd s.)(sakta-)(na*)(atiprasajyate ”sajj pass.).
body.translated_text: 1480. Thus, the status of 'inference' [applied to the statement] is secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>) and conventional (<s>sāṅketika</s>); being attached to that [role of] indicating, overextension does not follow.

body.translated_text: 1481. If [you say] that inference is not a valid means of cognition — your contradiction is futile; for no one [who engages in] debate apprehends [your] desire to express [anything without inference].

body.translated_text: 1482. If [you say that] the worldly inferential mark is accepted, but not [the one] fabricated by others — [we reply:] but surely the world too cognizes effects and causes and the like.

body.text:
1483.
(tu*)(tattvataḥ* [-tas suff.])(tat, n. 1st s.)(alum*)(eva*)(vādibhiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(nyāya-)(uktam, n. 1st s.)(api*)(tat*)(laukika-)(abhyanujñāte, n. 7th s.)(kim, n. 1st s.)(svayam*)(bhavati ”bhū Pr. III p. s.)(tyaktam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1483. But in reality, that [worldly inference] is sufficient. What has been said even by the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> (logicians) — when the worldly [inference] is approved, what [more] is [to be gained] by that [formal inference]? Is it abandoned by itself?

body.translated_text: 1484. What does the opponent apprehend through this? And if the conviction produced by this non-valid-means is [itself] produced by a non-valid-means — of what kind would it be?

body.translated_text: 1486. That [statement] is accepted as a non-valid-means because of not illuminating an unknown object — but surely your own [position is the same]; [it is] not [valid merely] through the capacity of indicating, [to which you too are] not attached.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1487] Objection: Why is the defining characteristic stated only for two [valid means of cognition] — the [intervening] means of cognition [between] verbal [testimony] and other means of cognition?

body.translated_text: [Verse 1488] [Reply:] It is said: another means of valid cognition beyond the two [perception and inference] is not possible, because of the impossibility of [its] defining characteristic and because of [its] being included within [the scope of] the [other] means of cognition.

body.translated_text: [Verses 1489-1491] Others have declared verbal cognition [as a separate valid means] — [arising from] a word [revealing] a hidden object. And that [verbal testimony derives] (a) from an authorless sentence, and likewise (b) from one uttered by a trustworthy person.

body.text:

body.translated_text: [Verse 1490] And this [verbal testimony] is admittedly not direct perception, because its object is hidden. Nor does inference fit, because of the separation from the defining characteristic of that [inference].

body.translated_text: [Verse 1491] For as long as the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) is not well ascertained — [that is,] the subject possessing the property (<s>liṅgin</s>) — that [cognition] would not be inference, because its object is that [unascertained subject].

body.translated_text: [Verse 1492] And here, the property-bearer that is postulated for this [verbal cognition] is indeed the object of knowledge. And when that has not been determined, there is no determination of its property-hood.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1493] If [you say] it was grasped prior to [its] being a subject — by what properties and the like would its being an inference be [established]?

body.translated_text: [Verse 1494] And the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) of the word with the object of knowledge cannot be ascertained. For the concomitant nature of all [words with their meanings] is apprehended through activity.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1495] There, where smoke exists, the positive concomitance with fire is manifest. But here [in the case of words], the meaning is not so ascertained: 'wherever there is a word, the object exists there.'

body.translated_text: [Verse 1523] Therefore, wherever the triple-characteristic [has been established] — in external [objects it has been] refuted by the opponents [and] by us — the status of words as valid cognition is simply not accepted.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1524] But there, where the triple-characteristic of these [reasons] is desired — this [has been] clearly [demonstrated] — when the intention to speak is what is to be proven, the triple-characteristic has been illuminated.

body.translated_text: By which the connection with the majority of common parts (<s>sāmānya-avayava</s>) is understood — if in [that] connection the reality (<s>tattva</s>) of all common parts is entailed,

1563.

body.translated_text: Some hold that <s>upamā</s> (analogy) is the cognition of the relation between name (<s>saṃjñā</s>) and referent (<s>sambandha</s>), upon encountering [the object] described by the instructive statement (<s>atideśa-vākya</s>).

body.text:
1564.
(yadi*)(an-ākulā, f. 1st s.)(pratipattiḥ, f. 1st s.)(sambandha-)(saṃjñā-)(eva*)(tadā*)(śravaṇe, n. 7th s.)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(atideśa-)(vākyasya, n. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: If the understanding is unconfused, then it is simply the relation between name (<s>saṃjñā</s>) and referent (<s>sambandha</s>) [established] upon hearing that instructive statement (<s>atideśa-vākya</s>).

body.text:
1565.

body.translated_text: 1565. Since the meaning has been grasped [already] through the apprehension of <s>upamāna</s> (analogy), [analogy] does not [have independent] validity as a means of knowledge — just as memory [does not]; likewise, because of [its] separation from the purpose of the [real] object.

body.text:
1566.
(atha*)(sā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(eva*)(saṃjātā, f. 1st s.)(tathā* api*)(katham*)(tadā*)(pratipadyate ”pad IV C. Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(iti*)(yasya, m. 6th s.)(saṃjñā, f. 1st s.)(saṃśrutā, f. 1st s.)(mayā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1566. Now, if that [cognition of similarity] has not arisen [through analogy] — then how does one apprehend [it] at that time? [The person says:] 'The name of that [animal] whose name I have heard —'

body.text:
1567.
(tathā*)(hi*)(prabhuḥ, m. 1st s.)(tat-)(samjñaḥ, m. 1st s.)(upalambane, n. 7th s.)(gavayasya, m. 6th s.)(na*)(kaścana*)(jñātum* ”jñā)(iti*)(nāma n. 1st s.)(tat-)(saṃśrutā, f. 1st s.)(mayā, 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 1567. For thus, [the person] is capable [of knowing] that [animal] upon the apprehension of a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) [bearing] that name; [there is] no one [else who can] know [it]; [he says:] 'That name was heard by me.'

body.text:
1568.

body.translated_text: 1568. If, when grasping [the gavaya], one who has employed <s>upamāna</s> (analogy) understands the connection — through the [quality of] having a distinguished object — [namely, the relation of] similarity,

body.text:
1569.
(hi*)(saḥ)(vetti ”vid II C. Pr. III p. s.)(sambandham, m. 2nd s.)(āgamāt, m. 5th s.)(sāmānya-)(gocaram, m, 2nd s.)(tu*)(āśrayāt, m. 5th s.)(upamā-)(vijānāti ”jñā IX C. Pr. III p. s.)(tam, m. 2nd s.)(viśeṣṭam, m. 2nd s.)(viṣayam, m. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 1569. For he knows the connection — through tradition (<s>āgama</s>) — [which has] similarity as its domain; but from the basis of <s>upamā</s> (comparison), he recognizes that distinguished object.

body.text:
1570.
(nanu*)(sambandhasya, m. 6th s.)(saṃjñāyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(avabodhane, n. 7th s.)(anyatra*)(hi*)(bodhaḥ)(tasyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(antare, n. 7th s.)(artha-)(na*)(yujyate ”yuj pass. Pr. III p. s.)(atiprasaṅgataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 1570. Indeed, regarding the understanding of the connection of the name, [it is argued:] the awareness of that [name's connection] in another [context] — in a different object — is not appropriate, because of [the fault of] over-extension.

body.text:
1571.
(sati, m. 7th s.)(grahaṇe, n. 7th s.)(kaścit*)(nāma-)(citra-)(aṅgade, m. 7th s.)(na*)(antare, n. 7th s.)(kāla-)(vetti ”vid II C. Pr. III p. s.)(tam, n. 2nd s.)(śabdam, m. 2nd s.)(cāru-)(kirīṭini, m. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 1571. When someone named <s>Citrāṅgada</s> (brightly-ornamented) is apprehended — [but] at a different time, he does not know that word [to apply to another] — one who wears a beautiful diadem.

body.text:
1572.
(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(yatra*)(idam, n. 1st s.)(nāma, n. 1st s.)(jñātam, n. 1st s.)(tena, m. 3rd s.)(vikalpa-)(pratibimbe, n. 7th s.)(buddhyā, f. 3rd s.)(bāhya-)(saṃjñite, n. 7th s.)(iti*)(sāmānyam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1572. Therefore, wherever this name was known by that [person] — in the conceptual reflection (<s>vikalpa-pratibimba</s>), [which is] designated as external by cognition — [the name applies] in general.

body.text:
1573.
(eva*)(tatra*)(api*)(upalambhe, m. 7th s.)(gavayasya, m. 6th s.)(pratipadyate ”pad IV C. Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(a-vibhāga-jñaḥ)(dṛśya-)(kalpā-)(abhimanyate ”man IV C. Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(iti*)(bāhyaḥ)
body.translated_text: 1573. Even in the apprehension of the <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) there too, [the person] apprehends [it]; not knowing the distinction, [he] regards [it as] external — [being] of the nature of what is seen and constructed — [and thus] imagines [the similarity].

body.text:
1574.
(ca*)(evam*)(yat, n. 1st s.)(pratipattavyam, n. 1st s.)(vikalpāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(ca*)(dhvanayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(api*)(gocarāḥ, m. 1st pl. [bv. cpd.])(sva-lakṣaṇa-)(nirākṛtāḥ, m. 1st s.)(vistareṇa, n. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 1574. And thus, what is to be apprehended, and the conceptual constructions, and the utterances — [when these] have <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (the particular) as their domain — are refuted at length.

body.text:
1575.
(vā*)(api*)(gocaractve, n. 7th s.)(teṣām, m. 6th pl.)(eva*)(bhavati ”bhū Pr. III p. s.)(anumā, f. 1st s.)(eva*)(ca*)(janyatvam, n. 1st s.)(tri-rūpa-)(liṅga-)(evam*)(pratīyate, prati-”i, pass. Pr. III p. s.)
body.translated_text: 1575. Or, even if those [particulars] are the domain [of analogy] — [the resulting cognition] would be <s>anumāna</s> (inference) alone; and [its] producibility [is established] through the triple-characterized inferential mark — thus it is understood.

body.text:
1576.

body.translated_text: 1576. That [animal] which is similar to a cow — for [the person] who has heard [the name] '<s>gavaya</s>' — [the person is] in the cognitive state of grasping the convention — situated in [that] cognition, like a <s>gavaya</s>.

body.text:

body.translated_text: 1577. If, in that state, that [person] were not situated in [that] cognition — at what time is this convention made: 'this is similar to a cow'?

body.text:
1578.

body.translated_text: 1578. And [it has been] established that [there is] no connection that is additional [to the relata]; previously, at the time of convention, the word was grasped by the ear and the mind.

body.text:
1579.
(ca*)(asau, m. 1st s.)(paśuḥ, m. 1st s.)(avasthitaḥ)(agrataḥ* [-tas suff.])(dṛśyate ”dṛś / paśy pass.)(cakṣuṣā, n. 3rd s.)(pṛthak*)(vijñātayoḥ, m. 6th d.)(eṣā, f. 1st s.)(ghaṭanā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(yuktā, f. 1st s.)(pramā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1579. And that animal stands before [him] and is seen with the eye; the joining together of the two [— the word and the seen object —] separately cognized is not a valid cognition that is appropriate.

body.text:
1580.

body.translated_text: 1580. Through the connecting together of what has [previously] been grasped — like the sweetness and fragrance [of something tasted before] — that cognition, [being merely] the joining of names, does not go beyond the status of memory.

body.text:
1581.
(ca*)(saṃvidaḥ, f. 1st pl.)(yoga-)(samākhyā-)(janyāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(ananta-)(upāya-)(api*)(an-apekṣayā, f. 3rd s.)(sādharmyam, n. 2nd s. [sa-dharma-ya-])(jāyante ”jan pass. Pr. III p. pl.)(narapa-)(ādiṣu, m. 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 1581. And cognitions that are produced by the joining of designations — through infinite means — [yet] without dependence [on a new source of knowledge] — [cognitions of] similarity arise regarding kings and so forth.

body.translated_text: 1582-1583. Among those kings, [one is said to be] the lord of men — with covered feet, [wearing] a red-and-white parasol; [having been] told thus, when [that king is] seen at another time, [recognized] through the [earlier] instruction — the cognition that [arises] of that [king] — that name [is applied] then; that is another valid cognition — obtained without dependence on similarity and so forth.

body.text:
1584.
(anyaḥ)(sādhayati ”sidh caus. Pr. III p. s.)(astitvam, n. 1st s.)(antara-)(pramāṇa-)(balāt, m. 5th s.)(anumāna-)(pratyakṣam, n. 1st s.)(saṅgatam, n. 1st s.)(pramaṇa-)(antara-)(anumā-)
body.translated_text: 1584. Another [valid cognition] establishes existence through the force of an intervening means of knowledge — [namely,] perception [combined with] inference; the combination of intervening <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of knowledge), [which is] inference —

(na*)(evam*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(hetuḥ, m. 1st s.)(a-pratibandhaḥ)(a-prakāśanāt, n. 5th s.)(bādha-)
body.translated_text: 1585. [Has] the status of a means of knowledge — like inference; and inference too is of this kind. Not so — this reason is unconnected, because of [its] non-illumination of the counterevidence.

1586.

body.translated_text: 1586. And thus your [proposed] fourness of the means of knowledge would be contradicted; whatever is your response there, that will apply here [too].

body.text:
1587.

body.translated_text: 1587. One who has ascertained the object through six <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of knowledge) — being otherwise — does not fabricate another unseen [means]; that [sixth means] is designated <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption).

body.text:
1588.

body.translated_text: 1588. Therein, the burning capacity of fire [is established] from direct perception of the burning; the possession of [burning] power by the sun [is established] from the inferred journey [of the sun].

1589.
(3)(śaktayaḥ, f. 1st pl.)(sarva-bhāvānām, m. 6th pl.)(sādhanāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(arthāpatti-)(kārya-)(ca*)(tāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(gamyante ”gam / gacch pass. Pr. III p. pl.)(a-pūrvāh, f. 1st pl.)(ṛte*)(grahaṇāt, n. 5th s.)(sambandha-)
body.translated_text: 1589. The powers of all entities — [as] proofs — are the effects of <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption); and those are understood as unprecedented — without the apprehension of a [prior] connection.

body.text:
1590.

body.translated_text: 1590. And there is no [prior] connection of those [powers] — neither previously nor [does] another [connection] obtain now; since, together with the effects here, the two — the property-of-the-subject — would [follow from] the connection.

body.text:
1591.
(pakṣe, m. 7th s.)(śakti-)(śrotra-)(ādi-)(hetuḥ, m. 1st s.)(prasajyate ”sajj pass.)(vā*)(sarvaḥ)(asau, m. 1st s.)(a-siddhaḥ)(āśraya-)(dharmi-)(prasajyate ”sajj pass.)(a-siddheḥ, f. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 1591. In the thesis — the reason of [the power of] hearing and so forth would absurdly follow; or that [reason] would be entirely unestablished — because of the unestablishment of the basis of the subject.

body.text:
1592.

body.translated_text: 1592. In scripture thus: 'He who is stout does not eat during the day' — this understanding of nighttime eating [is produced by] speech and so forth; this is called <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) from what is heard.

children.translated_text: And the meaning — nighttime [eating] and so forth — is understood in the sentence; the connection of the word-meanings 'daytime' and so forth — in [the sentence about] nighttime eating,

body.translated_text: 1594. The distinction by which that sentence would be informative — of that [meaning]; and there is no fabrication of a second meaning, because of [its already] being engaged with another meaning.

body.translated_text: 1595. Therefore, this [nighttime eating] is cognized through the intervening sentence; [and] through that [cognition] which is situated in the intellect, even that sentence which is cognized as not forthcoming [is understood].

1596.
(yat, n. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(pratyakṣa-)(ādiṣu, m. 7th pl.)(pramāṇam, n. 1st s.)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(vaktavyam, n. 1st s. [-tavya suff.])(tu*)(vākye, n. 7th s.)(an-uccarite, n. 1st s.)(na*)(pratyakṣam. n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1596. Whichever [means of knowledge] — among perception and so forth — would be the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge) of that [fact]; that must be stated. But when the sentence is not [actually] uttered, [it is] not [established by] perception.

1597.

body.translated_text: 1597. Nor is this inference; nowhere together with an example — but if even when the connection is not apprehended, the status of a mark (<s>liṅgatā</s>) is accepted,

1598.

body.translated_text: 1598. Then that course would [extend to] all sentences — by the mere utterance [of any sentence], because of [its being] devoid of connection; [for] that [sentence] is not distinguished from another [sentence].

body.translated_text: 1599. That cow which is compared — the capacity of the cognition of that [comparison] is understood through [its] capacity — having the power born of comparison.

body.translated_text: 1600. Thus, the designation [of the cow] would not be established — having understood the capacity otherwise; through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) of the expressive [word], again — because of there being no other course.

body.translated_text: 1601. The certainty through the intervening <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) — of the word's permanence: for [the word] is impermanent, not possessing continuity of convention and usage.

body.translated_text: 1602. 1603.
