body.translated_text: 1603. One may cite that other <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) — arising from non-existence; this too is distinct from inference, because of not being a component [involving] the thesis-property and so forth.

body.text:
1604.
(arthe, m. 7th s.)(viśiṣṭe, m. 7th s.)(vā*)(bahir-deśa-)(again: vā)(deśe, m. 7th s.)(viśeṣite, m. 7th s.)(tat-)(katham*)(a-bhāvaḥ)(gṛha-)(yaḥ)(prameyaḥ)(pakṣa-dharmaḥ)
body.translated_text: 1604. [Is it] in a qualified object, or in a place outside? Or in a particular place? How then [is] the non-existence, which is the provable thesis-property, in the house?

body.text:
1605.
(ca*)(kalpyate ”kḷp pass.)(pakṣa-dharmaḥ)(atra*)(a-bhāvaḥ)(gṛha-)(jīvataḥ, m. 6th s. [-at pr. part.])(ca*)(na*)(saṃvittiḥ, f. 1st s.)(tat-)(upajāyate ”jan pass. Pr. III p. s.)(a-buddhā, f. 1st s.)(bhāvam, m. 2nd s.)(bahir*)
body.translated_text: 1605. And the thesis-property here is postulated [as] the non-existence in the house; and the cognition of one who is alive — that [cognition] does not arise [directly]; the existence outside is not cognized.

body.text:
1606.
(varjitaḥ)(vidyamānatva-)(yaḥ)(śuddhaḥ)(a-bhāvaḥ)(geha-)(dṛṣṭatvāt, n. 5th s.)(mṛteṣu, m. 7th pl.)(api*)(na*)(sādhakaḥ)(vṛtteḥ, m. 6th s.)(bahiḥ*)
body.translated_text: 1606. That which is a pure non-existence in the house — devoid of [the quality of] being existent — because of [its] being observed in the dead as well, it does not prove the existence outside.

body.text:
1607.
(atirekeṇa, n. 3rd s.)(śakta-)(na*)(kācana*)(nāma*)(śaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(yā, f. 1st s.)(avagamyeta ”gam/gacch pass. Opt. III p. s.)(arthāpattyā, f. 3rd s.)(ca*)(śaktaḥ)(hi*)(adhyakṣe, m. 7th s.)(eva*)
body.translated_text: 1607. Beyond [mere] capacity, no power whatsoever that might be understood through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) [exists]; for what is capable is [already known] in direct perception alone.

body.text:
1608.
(tu*)(dāha-)(ādīnām, m. 6th pl.)(hetuḥ, m. 1st s.)(samīkṣyate ”īkṣ pass.)(pāvaka-)(ādiḥ, m. 1st s.)(a-viparyāsam, n. 1st s.)(a-saṃśaya-)(kā, f. 1st s.)(tataḥ*)(śaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(anyā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1608. But fire and so forth are observed as the cause of burning and so forth — without error and without doubt; what other power then could there be?

body.text:
1609.
(tu*)(vyatirikte, m. 7th s.)(upayogataḥ* [-tas suff.])(kāryeṣu, n. 7th pl.)(tasyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(bhāvaḥ)(eva*)(syāt ”as Opt. III p. s.)(a-kārakaḥ)(eva*)(upayoge, m. 7th s.)(na*)(bhedinī, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1609. But in the excluded [cases], through utility in effects — the existence of that [power] would obtain; [but] one that is non-productive — in [mere] utility — [that power] is not differentiating.

body.text:
1610.
(hi*)(svarūpam, n. 1st s.)(lakṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(śakti-)(samartham, n. 1st s.)(artha-)(kriyā-)(ca*)(evam*)(ātmā, m. 1st s.)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(bhāvaḥ)(vyavasīyate ”so pass. Pr. III p. s.)(pratyakṣāt, n. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 1610. For the own-nature is the characteristic of the power — capable of purposeful activity; and thus this entity, the self, is determined from direct perception.

body.text:
1611.
(ca*)(na*)(pramāṇam, n. 1st s.)(saṃsiddhau, f. 7th s.)(kiñcana*)(anya-)(lakṣaṇa-)(api*)(jñātena, n. 3rd s.)(na*)(arthaḥ)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(tat-)(kārya-)(siddhitaḥ* [-tas suff.])(rūpāt, n. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 1611. And no other means of knowledge whatsoever [is needed] for the establishment of the other characteristic; for even when that [characteristic] is known, there is no [further] purpose — because of the accomplishment of its effect from that form.

body.text:
1612.
(cet*)(aparam, n. 1st s.)(lakṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(śakti-)(gamyam, n. 1st s.)(arthāpatti-)(kārya-)(na*)(kāryasya, n. 6th s.)(bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(anyathā*)(hi*)(etat, n. 1st s.)(bhavati ”bhū Pr. III p. s.)(bhāvataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 1612. If another characteristic of the power is to be understood through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) — [that is] not [the case]; [the understanding] from the effect — for the existence of the effect [proceeds] otherwise — through the existence of reality.

body.text:
1613.
(pāvakaḥ)(vyatiriktaḥ)(jala-)(ādi-)(hi*)(kṣamaḥ)(ādau, m. 7th s.)(dāha-)(kim*)(tat*)(prayojanam, n. 1st s.)(anyena, n. 3rd s.)(sāmarthyena, n. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 1613. For fire, different from water and so forth, is competent for burning at the outset; what then is the purpose of another capacity?

body.text:
1614.
(cet*)(śaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(na*)(ekāntena, n. 3rd s.)(vibhinnā, f. 1st s.)(sā, f. 1st s.)(ātmikā, f. 1st s.)(ubhaya-)(api*)(sā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(virodhāt, m. 5th s.)(ca*)(yat*)(an-anyatā, f. 1st s.)(pratyakṣa-)(api*)
body.translated_text: 1614. If [it is said that] the power is not absolutely different [from the entity] — that [power] would be of the nature of both; [but] that too would not be [possible], because of contradiction; and if [it is] non-different — [it is established] by direct perception too.

body.text:
1615.
(ca*)(pratyakṣatve, n. 7th s.)(sthite, n. 7th s.)(vāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(tasyām, f. 7th s.)(anumeyatva-)(na*)(kṣataye, f. 4th s.)(eva*)(yena, n. 3rd s.)(na*)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(anumā, f. 1st s.)(asmin, m. 7th s.)(viṣaye, m. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 1615. And when perceptibility is established, the prevention of its inferability [in this case does] not [amount to] the destruction [of inference]; for inference is not thereby accepted [to be invalid] in this domain.

body.text:
1616.
(tu*)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(bhāvaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(śrotṛ-)(ye, m. 1st pl.)(na*)(gocarāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(pratyakṣasya, n. 6th s.)(teṣām, m. 6th pl.)(eva*)(sattā, f. 1st s.)(lakṣaṇā, f. 1st s.)(śakti-)(gamyate ”gam / gacch pass. Pr. III p. s.)(liṅgena, n. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 1616. But those entities — the hearer and so forth — that are not within the scope of direct perception — their existence, characterized by power, is understood through the inferential mark.

body.text:
1617.
(hi*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(vedanam, n. 1st s.)(śabda-)(sa-apekṣam, n. 1st s.)(antara-)(kāraṇa-)(api*)(tat-)(hetoḥ, m. 5th s.)(bhāve, m. 7th s.)(a-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(anyasya, m. 6th s.)(-vat*)(aṅkura-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 1617. For that cognition of sound requires another cause; from the existence of that cause — because of the absence [of sound-cognition] in the absence [of that cause] — like a sprout and so forth.

body.text:
1618.
(raveḥ, m. 6th s.)(vyāptyā, f. 3rd s.)(antara-)(deśa-)(nirantaram, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(jātiḥ, f. 1st s.)(deśe, m. 7th s.)(a-samāne, m. 7th s.)(upādāna-)(iva*)(gamyate ”gam / gacch pass. Pr. III p. s.)(jvāla-)(ādeḥ, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 1618. Through the pervasion of the sun, in another place without interval — the <s>jāti</s> (type) [is inferred]; in a dissimilar place — like the material cause of a flame and so forth — [it] is understood.

body.text:
1619.
(viśeṣatvāt, n. 5th s.)(ātmanaḥ, n. 6th s.)(sthira-)(iyam, f. 1st s.)(prāptiḥ, f. 1st s.)(antara-)(deśa-)(na*)(prasajyate ”sajj pass.)(anyathā*)(tu*)(śaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(nirākṛtā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1619. Because of the particularity of the stable self — this access to another place does not apply; otherwise, the power [theory] is refuted.

body.text:
1620.
(na*)(niścayaḥ)(pīnaḥ)(na*)(bhuṅkte ”bhuj Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(divā, m. 3rd s.)(pumān, m. 1st s.)(vadet ”vad Opt. Pr. III p. s.)(yogāt, m. 5th s.)(dveṣa-)(moha-)(ādibhiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(api*)(anyathā*)
body.translated_text: 1620. [The argument:] 'A fat man does not eat during the day — [therefore he eats at night]'; [but] one might say [this] through the connection with aversion, delusion, and so forth as well; otherwise —

body.text:
1621.
(yadi*)(punaḥ*)(antaram, n. 1st s.)(sa-artham, n. 1st s.)(vākya-)(ākṣipyate ”kṣip pass.)(an-apekṣeṇa, n. 3rd s.)(gati-)(artha-)(syāt ”as Opt. III p. s.)(ākṣepaḥ)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(antare, n. 7th s.)(vacas-)
body.translated_text: 1621. If, on the other hand, [the conclusion about] another [fact] is drawn together with its purpose from the sentence — independently, the understanding of the meaning of the movement would be [merely] an implication from the utterance.

body.text:
1622.
(atha*)(gatiḥ, f. 1st s.)(artha-)(tatra*)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(rūpeṇa, n. 3rd s.)(upagama-)(yat* vā*)(antarataḥ* [-tas suff.])(pramāna-)(gatiḥ, f. 1st s.)(artha-)(bhavatu ”bhū Imperative III p. s.)(tataḥ*)
body.translated_text: 1622. Now, if the understanding of the meaning is accepted there — in the form of an approach — or, let the understanding of the meaning [come] from a means of knowledge other [than presumption], from therein.

body.text:
1623.
(pratīyate; prati-”i pass. Pr. III p. s.)(pumān, m. 1st s.)(iṣṭaḥ)(sambandhī, m. 1st s.)(bhojana-)(kṣapā-)(pīnatvena, n. 3rd s.)(vaikalya-)(bhojana-)(divā-)(-vat*)(anya-)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 1623. The man is understood [as] desired, connected with food [and] night; through fatness and the deficiency of daytime eating — like that other [inference].

body.text:
1624.
(pīnatvam, n. 1st s.)(sati, n. 7th s.)(bhojane, n. 7th s.)(niścitam, n. 1st s.)(anvaya-)(vyatirekataḥ* [-tas suff.])(tena, n. 3rd s.)(gatiḥ, f. 1st s.)(vastunaḥ, n. 6th s.)(vastutaḥ* [-tas suff.])(sambaddhāt, m. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 1624. Fatness, when there is eating, is ascertained through positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>); thereby, the understanding of the real thing — from the [other] real thing that is connected in reality.

body.text:
1625.
(katham*)(hi*)(vākyam, n. 1st s.)(pratīyate; prati-”i pass. Pr. III p. s.)(śūnyam, n. 1st s.)(sarva-)(sambandha-)(punaḥ*)(anyathā*)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(pratīyeta; prati-”i pass. Opt. III p. s.)(ekamāt, n. 5th s.)(vākyataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 1625. For how is a sentence understood [as valid when it is] empty of all connection? Otherwise, everything would be understood from a single sentence.

body.text:
1626.
(a-sati, m. 7th s.)(tathā*)(sambandhe, m. 7th s.)(ca*)(sati, m. 7th s.)(an-avadhārite, m. 7th s.)(idam, n. 1st s.)(vākyam, n. 1st s.)(gamyamānam, n. 1st s.)(prasajyeta ”sajj pass. Opt. III p. s.)(a-pramāṇakam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1626. And when such a connection is absent, and when [the connection that is present] is not ascertained — this sentence, being understood, would result in being without a valid means of knowledge.

body.text:
1627.
(cet*)(no*)(nṛpa-)(ājñayā, f. 3rd s.)(pramāṇatvam, n. 1st s.)(sambaddhasya, m. 6th s.)(katham* vā*)(pramāṇatvam, n. 1st s.)(pratyakṣasya, n. 6th s.)(vinā*)(saṅgatim, f. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 1627. If not — [if] the validity [comes] from the king's command — how then is the validity of perception without [any such] connection?

body.text:
1628.
(nanu*)(a-sambaddha-)(gamyatve, n. 7th s.)(kim*)(no*)(gatiḥ, f. 1st s.)(anyasya, n. 6th s.)(api*)(hi*)(śūnyatve, n. 7th s.)(sambaddha-)(na*)(kaścana*)(viśeṣaḥ)(īkṣyate ”īkṣ pass.)
body.translated_text: 1628. [Objection:] 'Indeed, when what is unconnected is understood — what then? Is there not understanding of another [unconnected thing] too? For when [both] are empty of connection — no distinction whatsoever is observed.'

body.text:
1629.
(adhyakṣe, m. 7th s.)(api*)(mānatvam, n. 1st s.)(vyavasthitam, n. 1st s.)(sambandhāt, m. 5th s.)(eva*)(hi*)(pramāṇatvam, n. 1st s.)(saṃvādaḥ)(ca*)(saḥ)(lābhataḥ* [-tas suff.])(ātma-)(arthāt, m. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 1629. Even in the case of direct perception, validity is determined — for it is from connection alone that the status of valid knowledge [derives]; and that [connection] is concordance, from the attainment of one's own purpose.

body.text:
1630.
(na*)(tat-)(yujyate ”yuj pass. Pr. III p. s.)(niyamena, m. 3rd s.)(a-tat-hetoḥ, m. 6th s.)(ca*)(a-hetoḥ, m. 6th s.)(vā*)(anyathā*)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(saṃvādaḥ)(samastānām, n. 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 1630. That is not proper — by restriction; and [when there is] a cause that is not that [proper cause], or no cause at all — otherwise, there would be concordance of all [things].

body.text:
1631.
(vā*)(anumīyate ”mā III C. pass. Pr. III p. s.)(vivakṣā, f. 1st s.)(nirbhāsā, f. 1st s.)(dvitīya-)(vākya-)(ca*)(etena, n. 3rd s.)(gatiḥ, f. 1st s.)(vyatireka-)(matā, f. 1st s.)(anvaya-)(vākyāt, n. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 1631. Or, the intention to speak is inferred [from the sentence] — an apparent, second sentence; and by this, the understanding from the negative concomitance [and] the positive concomitance of the sentence is accepted.

body.text:
1632.
(pramaṇatve, n. 7th s.)(upamāyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(nirākṛte, n. 7th s.)(vistareṇa, n. 3rd s.)(pramāṇatā, f. 1st s.)(arthāpatteḥ, f. 6th s.)(utthāyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(tat-)(eva*)(vāritā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1632. When the validity of <s>upamāna</s> (analogy) has been refuted at length — the validity of <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), arising from that [refutation] — that alone is also blocked.

body.text:
1633.
(tu*)(gauḥ, f. 1st s.)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(ālambanam, n. 1st s.)(upamāna-)(pramāṇasya, n. 6th s.)(ca*)(matam, n. 1st s.)(ālambyam, n. 1st s.)(janakam, n. 1st s.)(sva-jñāna-)(eva*)(sva-sattayā, f. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 1633. But a cow is accepted as the object of <s>upamāna</s> (analogy) as a means of knowledge; and what is to be grasped — the producer of its own cognition — is accepted [as valid] merely by its own existence.

body.text:
1634.
(atra*)(kim*)(anyayā, f. 3rd s.)(śaktyā, f. 3rd s.)(gati-artham, n. 2nd s.)(yat-)(apekṣate ”īkṣ Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(arthāpatteḥ, f. 6th s.)(samāśrayam, n. 2nd s.)(upamāna-)(pramāṇatvam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1634. Here, what need is there of another power — for the purpose of understanding? The validity of <s>upamāna</s> (analogy) [should be based on] the basis of <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption).

body.text:
1635.
(api*)(viyoge, m. 7th s.)(an-anyatva-)(na*)(virudhyate ”rudh VII C. pass.)(pratyāyanam, n. 1st s.)(artha-)(śabdānām, m. 6th pl.)(yat* -vat*)(kāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(kampa-)(pāṇi-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 1635. Moreover, in separation, non-otherness is not contradicted; the informative capacity of words regarding meaning — like the cause of trembling, hands, and so forth.

body.text:
1636.
(hetutvāt, n. 5th s.)(pratyāyakatvam, n. 1st s.)(śabdānām, m. 6th pl.)(tulya-)(pratyavamarśasya, m. 6th s.)(yathā*)(kampanam, n. 1st s.)(tathā*)(na*)(virudhyate ”rudh VII C. pass.)(eva*)
body.translated_text: 1636. Because of being a cause, the informative capacity of words — just as shaking — is of the same reflective awareness; thus it is not at all contradicted.

body.text:
1637.
(nanu*)(kriyāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(yāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(dṛśyante ”dṛś/paśy pass. Pr. III p. pl.)(varttinyaḥ, f. 1st pl.)(pratyakṣa-)(dravya-)(tāsām, f. 6th pl.)(iṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(nityatvam, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(-vat*)(varṇa-)(pratyabhijñayā, f. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 1637. [Objection:] 'Indeed, those actions which are seen as occurring in perceptible substances — their permanence is accepted — like color — through recognition.'

body.text:
1638.
(ca*)(āsām, f. 6th pl.)(an-upalambhatā, f. 1st s.)(santata-)(a-bhāvataḥ* [-tas suff.])(vyañjaka-)(yat, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(syāt ”as Opt. III p. s.)(utpādakam, n. 1st s.)(vaḥ, 6th pl.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(matam, n. 1st s.)(vyañjakam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1638. And their non-apprehension [is explained] by the absence of the continuum of manifestors; what you consider to be a producer — that alone is accepted [by us] as a manifestor.

body.text:
1639.
(na*)(evam*)(sāmarthye, n. 7th s.)(a-pratibaddhe, m. 7th s.)(tat-)(jñanam, n. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(santatam, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(tu*)(viyoge, m. 7th s.)(tat-)(na* kadācana*)(syāt ”as Opt. III p. s.)(eva*)
body.translated_text: 1639. Not so — when the capacity is unobstructed, that cognition would arise continuously; but in separation from that [capacity], it would never arise at all.

body.text:
1640.
(ca*)(tataḥ*)(vyañjakāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(saṅgacchante ”gam/gacch Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(tāsām, f. 6th pl.)(tu*)(pratyabhijñā, f. 1st s.)(nityatve, n. 7th s.)(pūrvam* eva*)(nirākṛtā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1640. And therefore, the manifestors are consistent [with our position]; but the recognition of those [actions' permanence] — this has been previously refuted in [the discussion of] permanence.

body.text: And (ca*)(tataḥ*)(saṅgacchante ”gam/gacch Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(vyañjakāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(tāsām, f. 6th pl.)(hetavaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(tu*)(pratyabhijñā, f. 1st s.)(nityatve, n. 7th s.)(pūrvam* eva*)(nirākṛtā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1640. And then the manifestors of those [qualities] agree — the causes; but recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>), [as evidence] for permanence, has already been refuted.

body.text:
1641.
(tu*)(na*)(yujyate ”yuj pass. Pr. III p. s.)(bhāvaḥ)(caitrasya, m. 6th s.)(bahiḥ*)(a-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(geha-)(yasmāt, n. 5th s.)(śaṅkayā, f. 3rd s.)(maraṇa-)(upapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(anyathā*)(api*)
body.translated_text: 1641. But the existence of <s>Caitra</s> outside is not justified merely from his non-existence in the house, since by doubt, death and the like are also possible.

body.text:
1642.
(cet*)(a-bhāvaḥ)(jīvataḥ, m. 6th s.)(gṛha-)(āvahaḥ)(arthāpatti-)(prasiddhaye, f. 4th s.)(bhāva-)(bahiḥ-)(etat, n. 1st s.)(hi*)(na* eva*)(tatra*)(api*)(a-niścayāt, m. 5th s.).
body.translated_text: 1642. If the non-existence of the living [<s>Caitra</s>] in the house is to establish <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) — [his] being outside — this is indeed not [justified] even there, because of uncertainty.

body.text:
1643.
(arvāk-darśinaḥ, m. 6th s.)(a-paśyataḥ, m. 6th s.)(caitram, m. 2nd s.)(veśmani, n. 7th s.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(varttate ”vṛt Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(na*)(pramā, f. 1st s.)(kathaṃcit*)(api*)(sambandhe, m. 7th s.)(jīvan-)
body.translated_text: 1643. For one who sees only what is near, not seeing <s>Caitra</s> in the house — there is no valid cognition of him in any way regarding the connection with [his] being alive.

body.text:
1644.
(atha*)(sati, m. 7th s.)(niścaye, m. 7th s.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(jīvattā, f. 1st s.)(śabda-)(ādinā, m. 3rd s.)(ca*)(a-bhāve, m. 7th s.)(sadmani, n. 7th s.)(niścite, n. 7th s.)(a-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(pramāṇatā, f. 1st s. [-tā suff.])(asyāḥ, f. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 1644. Now, when there is certainty of his being alive through words and the like, and when his non-existence in the house is ascertained — the validity of this [<s>arthāpatti</s>] arises from the non-existence [being established by other means].

body.text:
1645.
(tadā*)(api*)(geha-)(a-yuktatvam, n. 1st s.)(a-dṛṣṭeḥ, f. 5th s.)(dṛṣṭyā, f. 3rd s.)(viniścitam, n. 1st s.)(ataḥ*)(tatra*)(bahiḥ-)(bhāvaḥ)(liṅgāt, n. 5th s.)(eva*)(avasīyate ”so pass.)
Textual variant (Baudha Bhāratī): dṛśyādṛṣṭeḥ
body.translated_text: 1645. Even then, the unfittingness of [his] being in the house is ascertained from non-seeing by sight; therefore, his being outside is ascertained there from the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) alone.

body.text:
1646.
(hi*)(asau, m. 1st s.)(a-saṃsṛṣṭaḥ)(sadmanā, n. 3rd s.)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(niyatam, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(bahiḥ*)(iva*)(pumān, m. 1st s.)(sthitaḥ)(geha-aṅgaṇa)(dṛṣṭaḥ)(sthitaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(dvāri, n. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 1646. For he, unconnected with the house, certainly exists outside — just as a man standing in the courtyard of the house is seen by those standing at the door.

body.text:
1647.
(naraḥ)(antar-gataḥ)(sadana-)(bhavati ”bhū Pr. III p. s.)(vipakṣaḥ)(api*)(atra*)(atha*)(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(iyam, f. 1st s.)(arthāpattiḥ, f. 1st s.)(na*)(bhidhyate ”bhid pass. Pr. III p. s.)(anumānāt, n. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 1647. A man who has gone inside the dwelling becomes a counter-example even here; therefore, this <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) is not distinguished from inference (<s>anumāna</s>).

body.text:
1648.
(vastu-rūpe, n. 7th s.)(pañcakam, n. 1st s.)(pramāṇa-)(na*)(jāyate ”jan pass.)(artham n. 2nd s.)(avabodha-)(sattā-)(vastu-)(tatra*)(a-bhāva-)(pramāṇatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1648. A fivefold [system of] valid means of cognition regarding the real nature [of things] does not arise; the apprehension of the object — [regarding] existence and reality — there, the status of non-existence as a valid means of cognition [is not established].

body.text:
1649.
(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(a-bhāvaḥ)(pramāṇa-)(an-utpattiḥ, f. 1st s.)(pratyakṣa-)(ādeḥ, m. 6th s.)(sā, f. 1st s.)(a-pariṇāmaḥ)(ātmanaḥ, n. 6th s.)(vā*)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(anya-)(vastuni, n. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 1649. Non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>) is held to be a [separate] means of valid cognition — [namely,] the non-arising of perception and the like; that is [either] the non-transformation of the self, or consciousness [directed] at another object.

body.text:
1650.
(ca*)(a-bhāvaḥ)(vastunām, n. 6th pl.)(saṃpratīyate; sam-prati-”i, pass. Pr. III p. s.)(a-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(pramā-)(ca*)(asau, m. 1st s.)(vibhinnaḥ)(caturdhā*)(bhedataḥ* [-tas suff.])(prāk-)(a-bhāva-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 1650. And the non-existence of things is apprehended; and from [the object of] non-existence, valid cognition is different — fourfold by division: prior non-existence (<s>prāg-abhāva</s>) and the like.

body.text:
1651.
(dadhi-)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(yat, n. 1st s.)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(na*)(kṣīram, n. 1st s.)(saḥ)(kalpyate ”kḷp pass.)(prāk-)(a-bhāvaḥ)(na* astitā, f. 1st s.)(payasaḥ, n. 6th s.)(dadhni, n. 7th s.)(lakṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(a-bhāva-)(pradhvaṃsa-)
body.translated_text: 1651. Yogurt and the like, which exists when there is no milk — that is conceived as prior non-existence (<s>prāg-abhāva</s>); the non-existence of milk in yogurt has the characteristic of destruction-absence (<s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s>).

body.text:
1652.
(ca*)(a-bhāvaḥ)(aśva-)(ādi-)(gavi, f. 7th s.)(yaḥ)(ucyate ”vac pass.)(a-bhāva-)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(na*)(para-)(rūpam, n. 1st s.)(tataḥ*)(nāstitā, f. 1st s. [na* asti-tā])(asya, m. 6th s.)(ātmanā, n. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 1652. And the non-existence of horse and the like in a cow — which is called [mutual] non-existence (<s>anyonyābhāva</s>) — of that there is no other form; therefore its non-existence [is established] by its own nature.

body.text:
1653.
(4)(nimnāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(avayavāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(śirasaḥ, n. 6th s.)(varjitāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(kāṭhinya-)(vṛddhi-)(rūpeṇa, n. 3rd s.)(śṛṅga-)(śaśa-)(saḥ)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(atyanta-)(a-bhāva-)
body.translated_text: 1653. The concave parts of the head, excluded [from having] the form of hardness and growth [that characterize] horns — the rabbit's [horn] — that is held to be absolute non-existence (<s>atyantābhāva</s>).

body.text:
1654.
(ca*)(yadi*)(na*)(a-bhāva-)(vidyate ”vid IV C.)(bhedena, m. 3rd s.)(prāk-)(a-bhāva-)(ādi-)(syāt ”as Opt. III p. s.)(na*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(vyavahāraḥ)(vibhāgaśaḥ*)(kāraṇa-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 1654. And if non-existence is not found with [these] divisions — prior non-existence and the like — this conventional usage [distinguishing] by divisions, [according to] cause and the like, would not [be possible].

body.text:
1655.
(na* ca*)(syuḥ ”as Opt. III p. pl.)(ete, m. 1st pl.)(bhedāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(a-vastunaḥ, n. 6th s.)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(asya, m. 6th s.)(vatutā, f. 1st s.)(saḥ)(a-bhāvaḥ)(kārya-)(ādīnām, m. 6th pl.)(yaḥ)(bhāvaḥ)(kāraṇa-)(ādinā, m. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 1655. And these divisions would not exist of a non-real thing; therefore its reality [is established]. That non-existence of effects and the like, which is the existence of causes and the like —

body.text:
1656.
(yat* vā*)(svayam*)(gamyatām ”gam/gacch pass. Imperative III p. s.)(vastu, n. 1st s.)(-vat*)(go-)(ādi-)(yataḥ*)(grāhyaḥ)(vyāvṛtti-)(anuvṛtti-)(buddhayoḥ, f. 6th d.)(ca*)(prameyatvāt, n. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 1656. Or rather, let it be understood by itself as a real thing, like cow and the like, since it is apprehensible by the cognitions of exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) and inclusion (<s>anuvṛtti</s>), and because of being cognizable.

body.text:
1657.
(cet*)(katham*)(a-bhāvaḥ)(mānam, n. 1st s.)(kīdṛśam, n. 1st s.)(prameyam, n. 1st s.)(atra*)(yat* -vat*)(meyaḥ)(a-bhāvaḥ)(mānam, n. 1st s.)(api*)(iṣyatām ”iṣ pass. Imperative III p. s.)
body.translated_text: 1657. If [you ask] how is non-existence a valid means of cognition — of what kind is the cognizable here? Whatever is cognizable as non-existence, let the valid means [of cognizing it] also be accepted.

body.text:
1658.
(ca*)(hi*)(a-bhāvaḥ)(pramāṇānām, n. 6th pl.)(bhidhyate ”bhid pass. Pr. III p. s.)(a-pratyakṣa-)(ādeḥ, m. 5th s.)(vācyatvāt, n. 5th s.)(śabda-)(a-bhāva-)(-vat*)(a-bhāva-)(prameyāṇām, m. 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 1658. And indeed, non-existence of the valid means of cognition is distinguished from non-perception and the like, because of being expressible by words — like [other] non-existences — of things cognizable as non-existence.

body.text:
1659.
(vā*)(a-bhāvaḥ)(mīyate ”mā pass. Pr. III p. s.)(pramāṇena, n. 3rd s.)(rūpeṇa, n. 3rd s.)(sva-)(prameyatvāt, n. 5th s.)(yathā*)(bhāvaḥ)(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(pṛthak*)(ātmakāt, m. 5th s.)(bhāva-)
body.translated_text: 1659. Or, non-existence is measured by a valid means of cognition in its own form, because of being cognizable, just as an existent [thing]; therefore [it is] distinct from the nature of existents.

body.text:
1660.
(tat*)(atra*)(pariṇāmaḥ)(nitya-)(sattvasya, n. 6th s.)(nirākṛtaḥ)(sadbhāvaḥ)(viparyayaḥ)(tat-)(na*)(yujyate ”yuj pass. Pr. III p. s.)(kādācitkaḥ)
body.translated_text: 1660. That [claim regarding] transformation of the eternally existent is refuted here; its existence as the contrary — that is not justified [if] it is occasional.

body.text:
1661.
(cet*)(atra*)(vivakṣitaḥ)(ātmā, n. 1st s.)(pratikṣepa-)(tat-)(astitve, n. 7th s.)(vastutā, f. 1st s.)(sarvadā*)(asya, n. 6th s.)(gamyeta ”gam/gacch pass. Opt. III p. s.)(a-nivarttanāt, n. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 1661. If what is intended here is the self — as a counter-rejection — then in the existence of that, the reality of this would always be understood, because of [its] non-cessation.

body.text:
1662.
(vā*)(astu ”as Imperative III p. s.)(a-pariṇāmaḥ)(asya, n. 6th s.)(tathā* api*)(vyabhicāritā, f. 1st s.)(artha-)(sambhavāt, m. 5th s.)(avasthāsu, f. 7th s.)(svāpa-)(mūrcchā-)(ādi-)(api*)(bhave, m. 7th s.)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 1662. Or let the non-transformation of this [self] be [accepted]; even so, there would be deviation — for even in states of sleep, fainting, and the like, because of the possibility of the existence of that [object].

body.text:
1663.
(yadi*)(asau, m. 1st s.)(asya, n. 6th s.)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(ghaṭa-)(ādi-)(antara-)(pratyaya-)(sadbhāve, m. 7th s.)(darśanāt, n. 5th s.)(vivikta-)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 1663. If that [non-existence cognition] is held [to arise] for this [self] in the existence of another cognition — of pot and the like — because it is seen as separate from that —

body.text:
1664.
(tadā*)(kaḥ)(abhihitaḥ)(asya, n. 6th s.)(viśeṣaḥ)(dvitīyāt, m. 5th s.)(pakṣāt, m. 5th s.)(idam, n. 1st s.)(dvayam, n. 1st s.)(pakṣa-)(yat-)(nirdiṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(tvayā, 3rd s.)(vikalpena, m. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 1664. Then what distinction of this [position] has been stated from the second view? This pair of views that has been set forth by you by way of an alternative —

body.text:
1665.
(dvitīya-)(a-bhāva-)(saṃśaye, m. 7th s.)(vijñāne, n. 7th s.)(anya-)(vastuni, n. 7th s.)(vṛtte, n. 7th s.)(nāstitā, f. 1st s. [na* asti-tā])(sarvasya, m. 6th s.)(gamyeta ”gam/gacch pass. Opt. III p. s.)(api*)(a-dṛśyasya, n. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 1665. In the doubt about the second [type of] non-existence — when cognition directed at another object has occurred — the non-existence of everything would be understood, even of what is not seen.

body.text:
1666.
(vijñāne, n. 7th s.)(anya-)(vivikta-)(tat-)(nāstitā, f. 1st s. [na* asti-tā])(rūpasya, n. 6th s.)(yogya-)(tulya-)(tat-)(antara-)(kāraṇa-)(sannidhau, f. 7th s.)(cet*)(pratīyate; prati-”i pass. Pr. III p. s.)
body.translated_text: 1666. When cognition is separate from another [object] — the non-existence of [that] form — if [that non-existence] is apprehended because of the proximity of another equal and suitable cause —

body.text:
1667.
(sati, m. 7th s.)(evam*)(nāstitā, f. 1st s. [na* asti-tā])(eva*)(pratyakṣasya, n. 6th s.)(ābha-)(grāhya-darśana-)(vastu-)(na*)(anyeṣām, m. 6th pl.)(vyabhicāriṇī, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1667. When it is thus, the non-existence of perception alone — the appearance, the seeing of what is to be apprehended as a real thing — is not deviant with regard to the others.

body.text:
1668-1669.
(katham*)(vā*)(jñāyate ”jñā IX C. pass.)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(anya-)(vastuni, n. 7th s.)(jātam, n. 1st s.)(yena, n. 3rd s.)(buddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(matā, f. 1st s.)(a-pratyakṣā, f. 1st s.)(yadi*)(arthāpattitaḥ* [-tas suff.])(sā, f. 1st s.)(api*)(eva*)(ātmikā, f. 1st s.)(jñāna-)(iti*)(kutaḥ*)(tasyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(api*)(gatiḥ, f. 1st s.)(antara-)(arthāpatti-)(prasajyate ”sajj pass.)(an-avasthā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1668-1669. How, or, is it known that consciousness has arisen regarding another object, by which a non-perceptual cognition is held [to establish non-existence]? If [it is known] through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), that too is of the nature of knowledge — whence [is it independently established]? For regarding that [presumption] too, another presumption would be required — an infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>) follows.

body.text:
1670.
(a-bhāvaḥ)(pramā-)(vastu, n. 1st s.)(a-bhāvaḥ)(meya-)(ca*)(eva*)(tathā*)(sati, m. 7th s.)(tathā*)(katham*)(te, 6th s.)(na*)(antaḥ-gataḥ)(a-bhāvaḥ)(pratyakṣe, n. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 1670. Non-existence as valid cognition and as reality, non-existence as the cognizable — that being so, how is non-existence for you not included within perception?

body.text:
1671.
(hi*)(a-bhāvaḥ)(kārya-)(ādīnām, m. 6th pl.)(yaḥ)(bhāvaḥ)(kāraṇa-)(ādinā, m. 3rd s.)(saḥ)(ātmā, m. 1st s.)(vivikta-)(apara-)(gamyate ”gam/gacch pass. Pr. III p. s.)(pratyakṣeṇa, n. 3rd s.)(eva*)
body.translated_text: 1671. For the non-existence of effects and the like, which is the existence of causes and the like — that self, separate from another [form], is apprehended by perception alone.

body.text:
1672.
(vastuni, n. 7th s.)(ātmake, n. 7th s.)(nityam, n. 1st s.)(sat-)(sva-rūpa-)(a-sat-)(para-)(rūpābhyām, n. 3rd d.)(kiṃcit*)(rūpam, n. 1st s.)(jñāyate ”jñā IX C. pass.)(kaiścit*)(kadācana*)
body.translated_text: 1672. Regarding a real thing of permanent nature — existent in its own form and non-existent in the other form — some form is known by some [cognizers] at some time.

body.text:
1673.
(ca*)(yadā*)(bhāva-)(aṃśaḥ)(gṛhyate ”grah IX C. pass. Pr. III p. s.)(pratyakṣa-)(ādi-)(avatāraḥ)(a-bhāvaḥ)(aṃśaḥ)(vyāpāraḥ)(an-utpatteḥ, f. 6th s.)(tat-)(jighṛkṣate ”ghṛṣ desid. Āt. Pr. III p. s.)
body.translated_text: 1673. And when the positive aspect is apprehended — perception and the like enters [into operation]; the non-existence aspect — because of the non-arising of that [perception] — it seeks to grasp [the non-existence].

body.text:
1674.
(eva*)(rūpam, n. 1st s.)(vastūnām, n. 6th pl.)(sva-)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(vyāvṛttam, n. 1st s.)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(ātmanā, n. 3rd s.)(sat, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(pratyakṣam, n. 1st s.)(amunā, n. 3rd s.)(ātmanā, n. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 1674. Indeed, the own form of real things is held to be that which is excluded [from others]; by that nature, being existent, perception [operates] by that very nature.

body.text:
1675.
(ca*)(samartham, n. 1st s.)(artha-kriyā-)(ucyate ”vac pass.)(sat, n. 1st s.)(anyat, n. 1st s.)(a-sat, n. 1st s.)(na* ca*)(samāveśaḥ)(tayoḥ, n. 6th d.)(yuktaḥ)(ekatra*)(virodhataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 1675. And that which is capable of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) is called existent; the other is non-existent. And the inclusion of both in one [locus] is not justified, because of contradiction.

body.text:
1676.
(nanu*)(samartham, n. 1st s.)(sva-)(sādhyāyām. f. 7th s.)(a-kṣamam, n. 1st s.)(asyām, f. 7th s.)(cet*)(hi*)(etat, n. 1st s.)(tat*)(dvirūpatvam, n. 1st s.)(na*) (eva*)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(ekatra*)(vastuni, n. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 1676. Surely, [if something is] capable regarding its own [domain of efficacy] but incapable regarding this [other domain] — if indeed this [is your position], that two-naturedness does not exist in a single real thing.

body.text:
1677.
(yadi*)(tu*)(anyat, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(iti*)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(a-samartham, n. 1st s.)(anyasyām, f. 7th s.)(tadā*)(prāpte, n. 1st d.)(dve, n. 1st d.)(vastunī, n. 1st d.)(tat*)(dvirūpatā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(ekasya, n. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 1677. If, however, it is another thing entirely that is held to be incapable regarding the other [domain], then two real things are arrived at; that two-naturedness is not of one [entity].

body.text:
1678.
(a-bhāva-)(vastutve, n. 7th s.)(sati, n. 7th s.)(pūrvam, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(aṅgīkṛte, n. 7th s.)(kim, n. 1st s.)(artham, n. 1st s.)(upavarṇyate ”varṇ pass.)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(nīrūpatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1678. When the reality of non-existence has been previously accepted, for what purpose is its formlessness described?

body.text:
1679.
(hi*)(prameyasya, m. 6th s.)(nīrūpasya, m. 6th s.)(hānau, f. 7th s.)(rūpa-)(vijñāna-)(na*)(yujyate ”yuj pass. Pr. III p. s.)(pramāṇatā, f. 1st s.)(sā, f. 1st s.)(hi*)(lakṣaṇā, f. 1st s.)(saṃvitti-)
body.translated_text: [Verse 1679] For when the object of knowledge, which is formless, is absent — the valid cognition status of the cognition of form is not justified. For that [valid cognition] is characterized by <s>saṃvitti</s> (self-awareness).

body.text:
1680.
(cet*)(ucyate ”vac pass.)(pramāṇam, n. 1st s.)(hetutvāt, n. 5th s.)(tat-)(-vat*)(cakṣur-)(ādi-)(nīrūpasya, n. 6th s.)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(na*)(kadācana*)(sambhavaḥ)(hetutva-)
body.translated_text: [Verse 1680] If it is said that [it is] a valid means of cognition because of being a cause — like the eye and the like — [we reply:] there is never the possibility of being a cause for what is formless.

body.text:
1681.
(ca*)(viviktaḥ)(rūpa-)(jñāna-)(katham*)(saḥ)(a-bhāvaḥ)(gamyate ”gam/gacch pass. Pr. III p. s.)(evam*)(a-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(pramā-)(gocara-)(tat-)(tarhi*)(an-avasthitiḥ, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: [Verse 1681] And how is that non-existence, separated from the cognition of form, understood? Thus, from [its] non-existence, [there would be] no object of valid cognition; then there is no stability [in the argument].

body.text:
1682.
(yadi*)(gamyeta ”gam/gacch pass. Opt. III p. s.)(a-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(vastu-)(ca*)(nāstitā, f. 1st s. [na* asti-tā])(a-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(pramā-)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(anyonya-)(saṃśrayaḥ)
body.translated_text: [Verse 1682] If [the non-existence of the object] were understood from [its] non-existence, and the non-existence of the thing [were established] from [its] non-existence as [an object of] valid cognition — there would be mutual dependence.

body.text:
1683.
(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(yā, f. 1st s.)(dṛṣṭiḥ, f. 1st s.)(ekasya, n. 6th s.)(sā, f. 1st s.)(eva*)(ucyate ”vac pass.)(a-dṛṣṭiḥ, f. 1st s.)(anya-)(ca*)(sā, f. 1st s.)(saṃsiddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(svatantra-)(a-jaḍatvataḥ* [-tas suff.])(svarūpeṇa, n. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: [Verse 1683] Therefore, the perception of one [thing] is itself declared to be the non-perception of another. And that [cognition's] accomplishment [is established] through its own nature — from being self-luminous and non-inert.

body.text:
1684.
(siddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(buddheḥ, f. 6th s.)(aparataḥ* [-tas suff.])(na*)(sambhavaḥ)(sarvathā*)(vā*)(a)(liṅgāt, n. 5th s.)(b)(antara-)(c)(an-upapatteḥ, f. 5th s.)(anyathā*)
body.translated_text: [Verse 1684] The accomplishment of cognition (<s>buddhi</s>) is not possible from anything else; [or else there would be] in all cases (a) [the need for] a mark [to cognize it], (b) an [additional cognition] in between, (c) the impossibility [of doing so] otherwise.

body.text:
1685.
(sati, m. 7th s.)(sambhave, m. 7th s.)(paryanuyogasya, m. 6th s.)(pratyekam*)(traya-)(syuḥ ”as Opt. III p. pl.)(bahvya, f. 3rd s.)(anavasthitayā, f. 3rd s.)(visarpiṇyaḥ, f. 1st pl.)(te, 6th s.)(atra*)
body.translated_text: [Verse 1685] When [the need for further cognition] is possible, [there would be] many spreading infinite regresses for each [item of] inquiry, regarding the triad [of cognizer, cognized, and cognition] there.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1687] In the self-awareness (<s>saṃvitti</s>) of which one [cognition], the moonless sky is understood — how is the discrimination of all [individual] words ascertained anywhere?

body.translated_text: [Verse 1688] Of the mass of light and darkness, one considers that very [experience to be] space (<s>vyoman</s>). Since the perceiver of the other [cognition] — its existence — is neither [perceived], nor is there [another] perception [of it].

body.translated_text: [Verse 1689] [What is] separated from all words is also perceived — because of the absence of perception [of it through words]. And that [cognition] is established ultimately from self-awareness (<s>sva-vedana</s>) of other consciousnesses.

body.text:

body.translated_text: [Verse 1690] And thus, when non-existence is established by the self, the expressibility of valid cognition by words is uncontradicted by the non-existence — in the case of internal [cognition].

body.translated_text: [Verse 1691] Non-existence is measured by a valid means corresponding to its own [nature] — thus [the charge of] proving what is already proven [arises] here. The correspondence to that [nature is what is at issue].

body.translated_text: [Verse 1692] (A) It exists when this exists; it does not exist when this does not exist — therefore from that very [fact] it exists. Hence this is declared to be the reasoning.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1693] The sage <s>Caraka</s> said: this very [non-perception] is a separate means of valid cognition. This is not inference, since no example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) is obtained.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1694] (B) The object that is known through perception — from the absence of that [perception], its non-existence is understood. This is accepted as <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-perception).

body.translated_text: [Verse 1695] This too is a separate valid means of cognition, because of not depending on an example and the like. For even in the example, non-existence is established by this very [non-perception].

body.translated_text: [Verse 1696] The cognition [here] is not restricted [in the same way as inference] — because of the cause-effect relationship. Since in this [non-perception], there is no difference between what is to be proven and the means of proof.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1697] Apart from the other result-status that has been posited — the conditioning of that nature — non-existence is not perceived. Setting aside the perception of what is visible, [no] other [means exists].

body.translated_text: [Verse 1699] The causes of the arrangement of composite [entities] — the cognition of the composite — arises from hundreds of thousands [of instances] of occurrence and the like, [as] the effect of the logical mark.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1700] The deviating nature of tradition (<s>aitihya</s>), intuition (<s>pratibhā</s>), and the like — for the most part — does not qualify [them] as valid means of cognition. From the absurd consequence of overextension regarding such [alleged means],

body.translated_text: [Verse 1701] or rather, this effort is simply misplaced, since [it is] established that [valid means of cognition are] twofold — direct and indirect — only.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1702] For that other [category] is simply not justified. The self [of cognition] being both and neither [direct and indirect] — [these two] action and non-action are contradictory [when applied] to one [thing] in one [respect].

body.translated_text: [Verse 1703] For an object is called 'directly perceived' [when it is] the immediate generator of cognition. The opposite of that, as stated, is accepted by the wise as 'indirectly known' (<s>parokṣa</s>).

body.translated_text: [Verse 1704] Now, this verbal [cognition], analogy (<s>upamā</s>), and the like is not an [independent] object-domain. From the attainment of the primary meaning — either [it is] included in direct perception, or [it has] the futility [of being equivalent to] memory.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1705] Even if [verbal cognition has] an indirect object-domain — how [can it be] the object of all? If this is not directly [perceived], [it is like something] indirectly [known] — like an object of direct perception.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1706] In the understanding [of meaning], through dependence on another [cognition] — is that [verbal cognition] connected with this [object]? Or [does it come] from the other [direction]? Neither — [that would be merely] an appearance of difference.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1707] When [cognition] arises from what is unconnected [with the object], instability follows. And if there were a difference of appearance, the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) would not hold.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1708] As long as [the cognition is] based on an indirect object, connected with the meaning, without touching the differences [directly] — that clear understanding is inference.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1709] Objection: But is not the object of many natures — like a dark gem (<s>mecaka</s>)? This being so, what contradiction [is there] for existence (<s>sat</s>) and the like [to be multiple by] their own nature?

body.translated_text: [Verses 1711-1713] Even when non-equality is accepted in every way — without a real thing [as its basis], real-thing-ness is necessarily lost. For a thing that has ceased — where is any other possibility seen, apart from non-existence — like a sky-lotus? Therefore, one who desires the non-equality of that thing with [another] thing must accept its being a sky-flower. What is called 'real-thing-ness' — the universal — is [merely] that sameness.

body.text:
1714.
(hi*)(kim*)(iti*)(kṛtam, n. 1st s.)(sā, f. 1st s.)(buddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(na*)(varttate ”vṛt Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(balibhuj-)(daśana-)(ādiṣu, m. 7th pl.)(tu*)(eṣā, f. 1st s.)(niyatā, f. 1st s.)(bhāveṣu, m. 7th pl.)(eva*)
body.translated_text: [Verse 1714] For why does that cognition [of sameness] not arise regarding the teeth of a crow and the like? Rather, this [cognition] is restricted to [certain] entities only.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1715] If [you say] this restriction [arises] from similarity of form — that very [similarity] is our universal. By this very [similarity], the power of [their shared] nature has been described.

body.text:

(atyanta-)(bhinnatā, f. 1st s.)(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(na*)(eva*)(ghaṭate ”ghaṭ Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(kasyacit*)(hi*)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(bhidhyate ”bhid pass. Pr. III p. s.)(parasparam, n. 2nd s.)(vasturūpeṇa, n. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: [Verse 1716] Therefore, absolute difference does not obtain for anything. For everything is not differentiated from everything else in the form of a real thing.

body.translated_text: [Verse 1717] If [an entity], devoid of difference established [by others], [is posited as] different from [other] things — that thing would not be different from those [things]; [there would be] non-difference — like the self of that [thing].

body.text:
1718.
(hi*)(abhidhīyate ”dhā pass.)(vairūpyam, n. 1st s.)(svarūpam, n. 1st s.)(bhinnam, n. 1st s.)(tebhyaḥ, n. 5th pl.)(etat, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(na*)(vairūpyam, n. 1st s.)(ca* ...ca*)(bhinnam, n. 1st s.)(anyonya-)(bādhitam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1718. For it is said: 'the own-form is different from those [others]' — this is [what is meant by] difference of form; and [this] difference of form and distinction are mutually contradictory.

body.text:
1719.
(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(upagacchatā, m. 3rd s.)(bhinnatvam, n. 1st s.)(kathaṃcit*)(arthānām, m. 6th pl.)(upagantavyam, n. 1st s.)(vairūpyam, n. 1st s.)(ataḥ*)(api*)(viśeṣa-)(ātmakatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1719. Therefore, by one who accepts the distinctness of things in some manner, the difference of form must [also] be accepted; hence the nature of being a particular (<s>viśeṣa</s>) [follows].

body.text:
1720.
(idam, n. 1st s.)(vastu, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(ātmakam, n. 1st s.)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(an-eka-)(ākāram, m. 2nd s.)(ca*)(te, m. 1st pl.)(sthitāh, m. 1st pl.)(grāhyatayā, f. 3rd s.)(anuvṛtti-)(vyāvṛtti-)(buddhi-)
body.translated_text: 1720. This reality alone is accepted as having a manifold nature; and they [the cognitions] are established as having the nature of cognitions of recurrence and exclusion, by [their] apprehensibility.

body.text:
1721.
(ete, m. 1st pl.)(ādyāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(anuvṛttatvāt, n. 5th s.)(kīrtitāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(iti*)(sāmānyam, n. 1st s.)(tu*)(apare, m. 1st pl.)(vyāvṛttatvāt, n. 5th s.)(abhidhīyante ”dhā pass. Pr. III p. pl.)(tataḥ*)(viśeṣāh, m. 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 1721. The former [cognitions], because of recurring [across instances], are called 'universal' (<s>sāmānya</s>); but the latter, because of being excluded [from others], are designated 'particulars' (<s>viśeṣas</s>).

body.text:

(sāmānya-)(viśeṣayoḥ, m. 6th d.)(svabhāvatve, n. 7th s.)(paraspara-)(sāṅkāryam, n. 1st s.)(syāt ”as Opt. III p. s.)(idam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(upapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(vastutaḥ* [-tas suff.])(dvairūpyam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1722. If the universal and the particular have [distinct] essential natures, there would be mutual contamination; this dual nature (<s>dvairūpya</s>) is not tenable in reality.

body.text:
1723.

body.translated_text: 1723. Even if [the universal and the particular] have no [distinct] essential nature in relation to each other — even so, their multiplicity is not tenable [as real]; the dual nature is not tenable in [their] existence.

body.text:
1724.
(api*)(sati, m. 7th s.)(eka-)(svabhāvatve, n. 7th s.)(atra*)(siddhyati ”sidh IV C. Pr. III p. s.)(bhedaḥ)(dharma-)(ca*)(a-virodhaḥ)(bheda-)(saṃsthā-)(yathā*)(śaktiṣu, f. 7th pl.)(kāraka-)
body.translated_text: 1724. Even when [there is] a single essential nature, distinction of properties is established here; and there is no contradiction of distinction — just as in the capacities of causal factors (<s>kārakas</s>) arranged in [various] configurations.

body.text:
1725.
(na*)(ca*)(yat, n. 1st s.)(an-upapannam, n. 1st s.)(dṛṣṭe, m. 7th s.)(īkṣyate ”īkṣ pass.)(api*)(sāmānya-)(viśeṣayoḥ, m. 6th d.)(aikātmye, n. 7th s.)(anuvarttanam, n. 1st s.)(loka-yātra-)(bheda-)
body.translated_text: 1725. And what is not untenable [but] is seen in the perceived [world] — the recurrence and the distinction of properties in the identity of the universal and the particular — the conduct of worldly affairs [proceeds accordingly].

body.text:
1726.
(nanu*)(sati, m. 7th s.)(eka-rūpatve, n. 7th s.)(na*)(siddhyati ”sidh IV C. Pr. III p. s.)(bhedaḥ)(dharma-)(hi*)(vibhedaḥ)(a-kalpitaḥ)(abhidhīyate ”dhā pass.)(nānātvam, n. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 1726. But surely, when there is a single form, distinction of properties is not established; for unfabricated distinction is what is called multiplicity.

body.text:
1727.

body.translated_text: 1728. For it is said: that which is declared to be one — that very [thing] which is again declared to be of manifold nature — that [latter declaration] does not hold.

body.text:
1729.
(tat-bhāvaḥ)(ca*)(a-tat-bhāvaḥ)(paraspara-)(virodhataḥ* [-tas suff.])(na*)(eva*)(avakalpyate ”kḷp pass.)(eka-)(vastuni, n. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 1729. And being-that and being-not-that — because of mutual contradiction — cannot be postulated in a single real thing.

body.text:
1730.
(vidhana-)(pratiṣedhau, m. 1st d.)(paraspara-)(virodhinau, m. 1st d.)(no*)(śakyau, m. 1st d.)(kenacit*)(svastha-cetasā, m. 3rd s.)(kartum* ”kṛ)(ekatra*)
body.translated_text: 1730. Affirmation and negation, being mutually contradictory, cannot be performed by anyone of sound mind with respect to one and the same [thing].

body.text:
1731-1732.
(vastunaḥ, n. 6th s.)(an-eka-)(sajātīya-)(vijātīya-)(tataḥ*)(tataḥ*)(kathyate ”kath X C. pass.)(bhedaḥ)(dharma-)(tataḥ*)(api*)(ekasya, n. 6th s.)(yuktā, f. 1st s.)(kalpitā, f. 1st s.)(a-saṅkhya-)(rūpatā, f. 1st s.)(api*)(na*)(saṅgatam, n. 1st s.)(vāstavam, n. 1st s.)(dvairūpyam, n. 1st s.)(eka-)(bhāvasya, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 1731-1732. The distinction of properties of a real thing — [arising] from [what is] of the same kind and of different kind, from one [perspective] and from another — is spoken of; but even so, the postulated innumerable nature of a single [entity] is not coherent; a real dual nature of a single entity [is not tenable].

body.text:
1733.
(hi*)(narasimha-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(ye, m. 1st pl.)(upavarṇitāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(dvairūpyeṇa, n. 3rd s.)(teṣām, m. 6th pl.)(api*)(bhāvikam, n. 1st s.)(dvirūpatvam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(eva*)(vidyate ”vid IV C.)
body.translated_text: 1733. For those that have been described as having a dual nature — <s>Narasiṃha</s> (man-lion) and the like — even for them, a real dual nature does not exist.

body.text:
1734.
(hi*)(saḥ)(svabhāvaḥ)(sandoha-)(an-eka-)(aṇu-)(eka-)(rūpavān, m. 1st s. [-vat suff.])(yat, n. 1st s.)(citram, n. 1st s.)(tat-)(na*)(ekam, n. 1st s.)(-vat*)(nānā-)(jātīya-)(ratna-)
body.translated_text: 1734. For the essential nature of that [entity like Narasiṃha] is an aggregate of many atoms, having a single form; what is variegated — like a jewel of many kinds — is not one.

body.text:
1735.
(aikye, n. 7th s.)(na*)(syāt ”as Opt. III p. s.)(avabhāsanam, n. 1st s.)(nānā-)(ākāra-)(dvirūpatvāt, n. 5th s.)(ca*)(api*)(pihite, m. 7th s.)(pada-)(makṣikā-)(na*)(an-āvṛtiḥ, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1735. In [true] oneness, there would be no appearance of manifold forms; and even because of dual nature, when the foot of a fly is covered [by something larger], there is no non-concealment.

body.text:
1736.
(ca*)(eva*)(prakṛtyā, f. 3rd s.)(te, m. 1st pl.)(aṇavaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(hetavaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(pratyabhijñāna-)(anusyūta-)(bhāga-)(nṛ-)(siṃha-)(udbhavāt, m. 5th s.)(viśiṣṭa-)(pratyaya-)
body.translated_text: 1736. And indeed, by their nature, those atoms are the causes of the recognition-cognition — [being] interwoven with parts; from the arising of the distinct cognition of the man-lion form.

body.text:
1737.
(etena, m. 3rd s.)(eva*)(prakāreṇa, m. 3rd s.)(citra-)(ratna-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(gatāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(hi*)(vaicitryam, n. 1st s.)(nānā-)(ātmanā, n. 3rd s.)(virudhyate ”rudh VII C. pass.)(ekatvena, n. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 1737. By this very method, variegated jewels and the like are [to be understood]; for variegation, [which requires] a manifold nature, is contradicted by oneness.

body.text:
1738.
(vastutvam, n. 1st s.)(abhidhīyate ”dhā pass.)(samarthatvam, n. 1st s.)(arthakriyā-)(yadi*)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(anugāmitvam, n. 1st s.)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(syāt ”as Opt. III p. s.)(kṛt, n. 1st s.)(sarva-)(kārya-)
body.translated_text: 1738. If reality (<s>vastuva</s>) is defined as the capacity for purposeful action (<s>arthakriyā</s>) — [and] if that [capacity] is a recurring [property] of that [entity] — [then] everything would be the producer of every effect.

body.text:
1739.
(ekaḥ)(janakaḥ)(artha-)(yogataḥ* [-tas suff.])(tasya, m. 6th s.)(sāmarthya-)(ca*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(a-viśiṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(anyasmin, n. 7th s.)(iti*)(katham*)(an-utpādakaḥ)
body.translated_text: 1739. [If] a single [entity] is the producer of a [particular] object by [its] connection [with that object] — and [if] its capacity is undifferentiated in another [entity] — then why is [that other entity] not also a producer?

body.text:
1740.
(yadi*)(nīla-)(ādi-)(eva*)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(anugāmi, n. 1st s.)(vastutvam, n. 1st s.)(sita-)(pīta-)(api*)(prāptam, n. 1st s.)(kṛt, n. 1st s.)(kārya-)(saṃsādhya-)(nīla-)
body.translated_text: 1740. If the recurring reality is accepted as [being only] blue and so forth — [then] white, yellow, and so forth too would be obtained [as having the same reality]; [for they are equally] the accomplisher of the effect of blue [as of any other].

body.text:
1741.
(tataḥ*)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(viśvam, n. 1st s.)(jātam, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(ekam, n. 1st s.)(vivarjitam, n. 1st s.)(dvitīya-)(ātma-)(ataḥ*)(na*)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(naḥ, 6th pl.)(ekam, n. 1st s.)(an-eka-)(ākāram, n. 1st s.).
body.translated_text: 1741. Then the entire universe, [being] born as one, would be devoid of a second nature; therefore, for us, [reality] is not one — [it has] a manifold form.

body.text:
1742.
(cet*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(na*)(vastutvam, n. 1st s.)(-vat*)(sattva-)(mata-)(Kaṇāśi-)(na*)(vaḥ, 6th pl.)(ekasya, n. 6th s.)(eva*)(an-eka-)(rūpatvam, n. 1st s.)(syāt ”as Opt. III p. s.)(vibhedataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 1742. If that very [reality] is not held [to be like] <s>sattā</s> (existence) as conceived by <s>Kaṇāda</s> — [then] the manifold form of a single [entity] would not exist for you, because of [its actual] differentiation.

body.text:
1743.
(ca*)(lakṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(bheda-)(vastūnām, n. 6th pl.)(saṅgaḥ)(viruddha-)(dharma-)(na*)(anyathā*)(kathañcit*)(bhedaḥ)(iṣṭaḥ)(nīla-)(pītayoḥ, m. 6th d.)
body.translated_text: 1743. And the defining mark of the distinction of real things is the association of contradictory properties; otherwise, the distinction between blue and yellow, [which is] somehow accepted, [would not hold].

body.text:
1744.
(ca*)(saḥ)(vidyate ”vid IV C. Pr. III p. s.)(sāmānya-)(bhedayoḥ, m. 6th d.)(bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(anugāmi-)(anyathā*)(katham*)(tat*)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(na*)(bhedayoḥ, m. 6th d.)(parisphuṭam, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(tayoḥ, m. 6th d.)
body.translated_text: 1744. And that [association of contradictory properties] exists between the universal and the particular; because of the existence of a recurring [element] — otherwise, how [would it hold]? That [distinction] is clearly not [found] between the two.

body.text:
1745.
(yathā*)(kalmāṣa-)(varṇasya, n. 6th s.)(nigrahaḥ)(varṇa-)(yathā*)(iṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(citratvāt, n. 5th s.)(api*)(evam*)(bheda-)(a-bheda-)(vastunaḥ, n. 6th s.)(avadhāraṇe, n. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 1745. Just as the restriction of [a particular] color in the case of a variegated color — that which is accepted [as restriction] even despite variegation — so too in the ascertainment of a real thing [that is both] distinct and non-distinct.

body.text:
1746.
(tu*)(yadā*)(vastu, n. 1st s.)(śabalam, n. 1st s.)(pratipadyate ”pad IV C. Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(yugapat*)(tadā*)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(bheda-)(anya-)(an-anya-)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(pralīyate ”lī I and IX C. pass.)
body.translated_text: 1746. But when the variegated reality is apprehended simultaneously, then everything — distinction, otherness, non-otherness, and the like — dissolves.

body.text:
1747.
(vastunaḥ, n. 6th s.)(an-eka-)(rūpasya, n. 6th s.)(iṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(vivakṣayā, f. 3rd s.)(vṛttibhyām, f. 3rd d.)(krama-)(yugapat*)(na*)(anyaḥ)(vidhiḥ, m. 1st s.)(vacasām, n. 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 1747. It is accepted [by us] that the reality having manifold forms [is expressed] by the desire to express, through the two modes of successive and simultaneous [predication]; there is no other way for words.

body.text:
1748.
(na*)(evam*)(hi*)(citratvam, n. 1st s.)(pratiṣiddham, n. 1st s.)(ekatvam, n. 1st s.)(anantaram, n. 2nd s.)(vaicitryam, n. 1st s.)(an-eka-)(rūpam, n. 1st s.)(a-sahasthitam, n. 1st s.)(ekatvena, n. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 1748. For thus, variegation has not been negated; immediately after, oneness [is also not negated]; variegation — [having] manifold form — cannot coexist with oneness.

body.text:
1749.
(hi*)(te, m. 1st pl.)(bhāvikāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(ākārāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(yāvantaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(tasmin, n. 7th s.)(vastuni, n. 7th s.)(jātāni, n. 1st pl.)(tāvanti, n. 1st pl.)(vastūni, n. 1st pl.)(iti*)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(na*)(ekatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1749. For however many real aspects exist in that real thing — that many real things there are; thus there is no oneness.

body.text:
1750.
(anyatve, n. 7th s.)(ekasmāt, n. 5th s.)(vastunaḥ, n. 5th s.)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(vikalam, n. 1st s.)(tādātmya-)(na*)(saṃkāśam, n. 1st s. [adj.])(ākāśa-puṣpa-)(tat, n. 1st s.)(hi*)(api*)(kṣamam, n. 1st s.)(arthakriyā-)
body.translated_text: 1750. If [the aspects were] other than one real thing, [the real thing] would be deficient; [such a distinct aspect would have] no identity [with the real thing] — it would be like a sky-flower; for even that [sky-flower] would be capable of purposeful action.

body.text:
1751.
(ca*)(śaktam, n. 1st s.)(rūpam, n. 1st s.)(ekasya, n. 6th s.)(na*)(varttate ”vṛt Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(anyeṣu, n. 7th pl.)(vastuṣu, n. 7th pl.)(kārya-)(nirbhāsa-)(upalambha-)(bheda-)(ādeḥ, m. 5th s.)(iti*)(varṇitam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1751. And the effective form of one [real thing] does not operate in other real things — because of the difference of effect, appearance, apprehension, and so forth; thus it has been described.

body.text:
1752.
(ātmakatvam, n. 1st s.)(vastu-)(a-tat-)(yujyate ”yuj pass. Pr. III p. s.)(a-śleṣeṇa, m. 3rd s.)(tat-)(na*)(bhāvataḥ* [-tas suff.])(lakṣaṇa-)(vastu-)(a-vastutvam, n. 1st s.)(a-viśeṣam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1752. The nature of being a non-real-thing [is arrived at] by the non-connection with that [real thing]; from the standpoint of reality, [there would be] no distinction between the defining mark of a real thing and a non-real-thing.

body.text:
1753.
(kalpane, n. 7th s.)(iti*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(api*)(yogyam, n. 1st s.)(arthakriyā-)(tat, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(vastu, n. 1st s.)(sādṛśyam, n. 1st s.)(parāvṛttiḥ, f. 1st s.)(a-samartha-)
body.translated_text: 1753. Thus, that too [would be] fit for purposeful action (<s>arthakriyā</s>) in [mere] postulation — that is [what constitutes] a real thing; [mere] similarity is the turning away of [what is] incapable.

body.text:
1754.
(ca*)(tataḥ*)(api*)(atyanta-)(bhede, m. 7th s.)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(vikalpitā, f. 1st s.)(tulyatā, f. 1st s.)(tat*)(bhāvaḥ)(tulyaḥ)(antaraiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(bhāva-)(viśiṣyate ”śiṣ VII C. pass. Pr. III p. s.)(kha-puṣpāt, n. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 1754. And therefore, even in absolute difference, there is a postulated equality; that [entity's] existence is equal [to a sky-flower]; [but] it is distinguished from a sky-flower by [its] inner [real] qualities.

body.text:
1755.
(nanu*)(yadi*)(ātmanā, n. 3rd s.)(yena, n. 3rd s.)(vastu, n. 1st s.)(vyāvṛttam, n. 1st s.)(samāna-)(apara-)(vastunaḥ, n. 5th s.)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(eva*)(sadṛśam, n. 1st s.)(sajatīyaiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 1755. But surely, if a real thing is excluded from another real thing by that very nature by which [it is defined] — then by that very [nature] it would be similar to [things of] the same kind.

body.text:
1756.
(tadā*)(vijñāyeta ”jñā IX C. pass. Opt. III p. s.)(tulyatayā, f. 3rd s.)(vijātīyaiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(api*)(a-viśiṣṭatvāt, n. 5th s.)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(ātmanaḥ, n. 6th s.)(ca*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(na*)(tathā*)(jñāyate ”jñā IX C. pass.)
body.translated_text: 1756. Then it would be cognized as equal even to [things of] different kinds, because of the non-distinction of that nature; and that [implication] is not cognized thus.

body.text:
1757.
(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(yena, m. 3rd s.)(bhavati ”bhū Pr. III p. s.)(a-samānaḥ)(sajātīya-)(ca*)(ātmanā, n. 3rd s.)(samānaḥ)(tat-)(bhedaḥ)(svabhāvayoḥ, n. 6th d.)
body.translated_text: 1757. Therefore, that by which this [entity] is dissimilar from what is of the same class, and similar to that [class] by its own nature — [that is] the difference of the two natures.

body.text:
1758.
(tena, n. 3rd s.)(eva*)(asau, m. 1st s.)(avagamyate ”gam/gacch pass. Pr. III p. s.)(iti*)(samānaḥ)(hetutvena, n. 3rd s.)(eka-)(pratyavamarśasya, m. 6th s.)(bhedataḥ* [-tas suff.])(anya-)
body.translated_text: 1758. By that very [nature] it is understood as similar [to its class] — as a cause, because of the difference from others — of a single reflective awareness.

body.text:
1759.
(hi*)(eva*)(kecit, m. 1st pl.)(hetavaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(eka-)(pratyavamarśasya, m. 6th s.)(niyamāt, m. 5th s.)(rūpa-)(samartha-)(api*)(bhede, m. 7th s.)(-vat*)(akṣa-)(amṛtā-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 1759. For certain [things] are indeed causes of a single reflective awareness, through [their] restriction — [yet they are] capable [of producing cognitions] in the form of [a particular thing] — like the eye, <s>amṛta</s> (ambrosia), and so forth, even when there is difference.

body.text:
1760.
(nanu*)(katham*)(locanam, n. 1st s.)(jananam, n. 1st s.)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(nīla-)(ādi-)(yadi*)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(bhāk, n. 1st s. [adj.])(eva*)(vyāvṛtta-)(nīla-)(ādibhyaḥ, m. 5th pl.)
body.translated_text: 1760. Indeed, how is the eye [accepted as] the producer of cognition — of blue and so forth? If [it is] accepted [as such] — [it] is merely excluded from blue and so forth.

body.text:
1761.
(yathā*)(śrotram, n. 1st s.)(bhedavat, n. 1st s.)(nīla-)(ādeḥ, m. 5th s.)(na*)(janakam, n. 1st s.)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(janakāt, n. 5th s.)(jñāna-)(nīla-)(ādi-)(tathā*)(cakṣur, n. 1st s.)(api*)(iṣyatām ”iṣ pass. Imperative III p. s.)
body.translated_text: 1761. Just as the ear, being different from blue and so forth, is not the producer of that [blue-cognition] — from [its being different from] the producer of the cognition of blue and so forth — so too let the eye be accepted [as different].

body.text:
1762.
(hi*)(kaḥ)(aparaḥ)(bhāvaḥ)(parāvṛttaḥ)(janakāt, m. 5th s.)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(niścayaḥ)(iti*)(anvayaḥ)(api*)(padārthānām, m. 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 1762. For what other entity, turned away from the producer, could there be? Therefore, the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) of entities too [is established] — [this is] the certainty.

body.text:
1763.
(anyathā*)(bhedena, m. 3rd s.)(nirviśiṣṭatvāt, n. 5th s.)(kim*)(na*)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(śravaṇa-)(api*)(iṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(janakam, n. 1st s.)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(-vat*)(cakṣus, n. 1st s. [cakṣur - rūpa ḥḥ cakṣū-rūpa-])(rūpa-)(rūpa-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 1763. Otherwise, since there is no distinction in [their] difference — why is the ear and so forth not accepted as the producer of that [visual cognition] — like the eye — of form and so forth?

body.text:
1764-1775.
(iyam, f. 1st s.)(vyāvṛttiḥ, f. 1st s.)(cakṣur-)(ādīnām, m. 6th pl.)(janakāt, m. 5th s.)(na*)(siddhā, f. 1st s.)(a-viśeṣeṇa, m. 3rd s.)(ātmā, n. 1st s.)(teṣām, n. 6th pl.)(api*)(mataḥ)(janakaḥ)
body.translated_text: 1764-1775. This exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) of the eye and so forth from the producer is not established — without distinction, the self of those [entities] is also considered a producer.

body.text:
1765.
(ca*)(vyāvṛttiḥ, f. 1st s.)(bhāvānām, m. 6th pl.)(svabhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(na*)(upapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(hi*)(vyāvṛttau, f. 7th s.)(svabhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(prasajyate ”sajj pass.)(naiḥsvābhāvyam, n. 1st s. [niḥsvabhāva - ya])
body.translated_text: 1765. And the exclusion of entities from [their own] nature is not appropriate; for in [positing] exclusion from one's own nature, essencelessness (<s>niḥsvabhāvatva</s>) would follow absurdly.

body.text:
1766.
(upavarṇyate ”varṇ pass.)(vyāvṛttiḥ, f. 1st s.)(anyasmāt, m. 5th s.)(janakāt, m. 5th s.)(vācyam, n. 1st s.)(a-)(rūpatvam, n. 1st s.)(tat-)(janaka-)(ca*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(iṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(naḥ, 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 1766. [If] exclusion from another producer is described — the non-formness of that [producer] is to be stated; and that very [non-form] is accepted as the producer by us.

body.text:
1767.
(hi*)(na*)(utpādakam, n. 1st s.)(varṇyate ”varṇ pass.)(eva*)(svarūpeṇa, n. 3rd s.)(sarve, m. 1st pl.)(te, m. 1st pl.)(samutthitāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(niyatāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(svahetubhyaḥ, m. 5th pl.)
body.translated_text: 1767. For the producer is not described [merely] by its own form; all of them, arising from their own causes, are determined.

body.text:
1768.
(yadi*)(tu*)(ime, m. 1st pl.)(eka-)(janakāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(anugatatvāt, n. 5th s.)(eka-ātmā-)(saḥ)(ātmā, n. 1st s.)(api*)(ekatra*)(iti*)(kim, n. 1st s.)(anyaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(sahakāribhiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 1768. If, on the other hand, these are of a single producer — because of [their] continuity — [then] that self too [would produce] in a single [instance]; what [need] then of other co-operating causes?

body.text:
1769.
(nanu*)(yadi*)(vaikalpyāt, n. 5th s.)(antara-)(viśeṣa-)(eke, m. 1st pl.)(na*)(janakam, n. 1st s.)(te, m. 1st pl.)(a-śaktāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(bhedāt, m. 5th s.)(vā*)(a-bhede, m. 7th s.)(katham*)(vikalāḥ, m. 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 1769. Indeed, if because of optionality, [things having] a specific difference are not producers — [then] they are incapable because of difference; or, if there is no difference, how are they deficient?

body.text:
1770.
(yathā*)(api*)(viśeṣe, m. 7th s.)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(kāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(sarva-)(eva*)(tathā*)(api*)(a-viśeṣe, n. 7th s.)(nānātvasya, n. 6th s.)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(niyamaḥ)
body.translated_text: 1770. Just as not everything is the cause of everything in a specific [domain] — so too, even when there is no specificity, there would be a restriction of [their] multiplicity.

body.text:
1771.
(api*)(bhede, m. 7th s.)(kaścit*)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(janakaḥ)(niyamāt, m. 5th s.)(svabhāva-)(tu*)(anvaye, m. 7th s.)(kim*)(ekaḥ)(janakaḥ)(ca*)(a-janakaḥ)(ekasya, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 1771. Moreover, in [the case of] difference, some [entity] would be a producer by the restriction of [its own] nature; but in the case of continuity, would a single [entity be] both a producer and a non-producer of a single [effect]?

body.text:
1772.
(cet*)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(bhedaḥ)(atra*)(api*)(saḥ)(astu ”as Imperative III p. s.)(kim*)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(vastunaḥ, n. 6th s.)(eva*)(hi*)(na*)(bhedaḥ)(anyaḥ)(anvayāt, m. 5th s.)(nanu*)(na*)(kārakaḥ)
body.translated_text: 1772. If there is difference here too — let it be so; what [is the purpose] of that real entity? For from [the relation of] continuity, there is no difference; indeed, is it not [the case that it is] not a cause?

body.text:
1773.
(ca*)(saḥ)(eva*)(bhāvikaḥ)(arthaḥ)(yaḥ)(nāma*)(kṣamaḥ)(arthakriyā-)(ca*)(saḥ)(na*)(anveti; anu-”i II C. Pr. III p. s.)(tasmāt, m. 5ths.)(yaḥ)(anveti; anu-”i II C. Pr. III p. s.)(kāryam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(jāyate ”jan pass.)
body.translated_text: 1773. And that very natural object [is the one] which is indeed capable of purposeful activity; and it does not continue; therefore, from what continues, no effect is produced.

body.text:
1774.
(ca*)(bheda-)(a-bheda-)(vidyete ”vid IV C. Pr. III p. d.)(a-kalpitau, m. 1st d.)(eva*)(gatau, m. 1st d.)(tat-)(ātmānam, n. 2nd s.)(abhipretya* [abhi-pra-”i])(yam, n. 2nd s.)(eṣaḥ)(pumān, m. 1st s.)(pravarttate ”vṛt Āt. Pr. III p. s.)
body.translated_text: 1774. And difference and non-difference are obtained as unfabricated alone; [that is,] having understood that self, with respect to which this person acts.

body.text:
1775.
(anyathā*)(bhedaḥ)(hi*)(ātmanā, n. 3rd s.)(samānatā, f. 1st s.)(ca*)(vyāvṛttyā, f. 3rd s.)(vastu, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(na*)(anveti; anu-”i II C. Pr. III p. s.)(prasaṅgataḥ* [-tas suff.])(ādi-)(pravṛtti-)
body.translated_text: 1775. Otherwise, the difference is by [its own] nature, and the sameness is by exclusion; the thing alone exists — and [the thing] does not continue — absurdly, from the initiation of activity and so forth.

body.text:
1776.
(vaicitryasya, n. 6th s.)(upavarṇyate ”varṇ pass.)(racitasya, n. 6th s.)(kalpanā, f. 1st s.)(kaḥ)(nāma*)(atiśayaḥ)(proktaḥ)(vipra-)(nirgrantha-)(kāpilaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 1776. Who indeed — among <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Nigranthas</s> (Jainas), and <s>Kāpilas</s> (Sāṃkhyas) — has declared the surplus [of the fabricated] variety that has been described?

body.text:
1777.
(yadā*)(varddhamānaka-)(bhaṅgena, m. 3rd s.)(rucakaḥ)(kriyate ”kṛ pass.)(tasā*)(arthinaḥ, m. 6th s.)(pūrva-)(śokaḥ)(ca* api*)(arthinaḥ, m. 6th s.)(uttara-)(prītiḥ, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1777. When a bracelet is made by breaking [an ornament called] a <s>vardhamānaka</s> — the prior sorrow of the one who desires [the vardhamānaka], and the subsequent joy [of the one who desires] the bracelet,

body.text:
1778.
(tu*)(arthinaḥ, m. 6th s.)(hema-)(mādhyasthyam, n. 1st s.)(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(vastu, n. 1st s.)(tri-)(ātmakam, n. 1st s.)(trayam, n. 1st s.)(mati-)(na*)(syāt ”as Opt. III p. s.)(a-bhave, m. 7th s.)(utpāda-)(sthiti-)(bhaṅgānām, m. 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 1778. But indifference toward the gold [itself] — therefore, a thing has a threefold nature; the cognition of the three — of arising, persistence, and destruction — would not exist in [their] absence.

body.text:
1779.
(na*)(śokaḥ)(vinā*)(nāśena, m. 3rd s.)(na*)(sukham, n. 1st s.)(vinā*)(utpādena, m. 3rd s.)(na*)(mādhyasthyam, n. 1st s.)(vinā*)(sthityā, f. 3rd s.)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(sāmānya-)(nityatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1779. There is no sorrow without destruction, no happiness without arising, and no indifference without persistence; thereby [the Jainas argue for] the permanence of the universal.

body.text:
1780.
(iti*)(api*)(no*)(yuktam, n. 1st s.)(a-sāmānya-)(āśrayatvataḥ* [-tas suff.])(utpāda-)(hi*)(sthiti-)(bhaṅgānām, m. 6th pl.)(na*)(āśrayatā, f. 1st s.)(eka-)(artha-)
body.translated_text: 1780. This too is not proper, because of [their] not being the substratum of a [single] universal; for arising, persistence, and destruction do not have a single-object substratum.

body.text:
1781.
(prāpteḥ, f. 5th s.)(samāna-)(kālatā-)(paraspara-)(virodhinām, m. 6th pl.)(tu*)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(idam, n. 1st s.)(an-ākulam, n. 1st s.)(sati, m. 7th s.)(kṣanabhaṅgitve, n. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 1781. Because of the attainment of simultaneity — for [they are] mutually contradictory; but all this [becomes] unconfused when momentary destruction is [accepted].

body.text:
1782.
(hi*)(katham*)(śoka-)(sambhavaḥ)(kasyacit*)(an-anvaye, m. 7th s.)(vināśe, m. 7th s.)(kaladhauta-)(bhāvasya, m. 6th s.)(varddhamānaka-)
body.translated_text: 1782. For how would there be sorrow when there is no continuity — when the gold-nature of the <s>vardhamānaka</s> is destroyed?

body.text:
1783.
(sarvathā*)(utpadyate ”pad IV C. Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(prītiḥ, f. 1st s.)(janmani, n. 7th s.)(pūrva-)(rūpasya, n. 6th s.)(rucakasya, m. 6th s.)(tat-)(ātmanaḥ, n. 6th s.)(tu*)(avasthānam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(kasyacit*).
body.translated_text: 1783. Joy arises in every way at the birth of the bracelet, [which is of] the former form; but there is no persistence of anyone whatsoever — [it is] of that nature.

body.text:
1784.
(yadā*)(mūdhadhīḥ, m. 1st s.)(paśyanti ”paś/dṛś Pr. III p. pl.)(bhāvau, m. 2nd d.)(ātmakau, m. 2nd d.)(śātakumbha-)(tadā*)(manyate ”man IV C. Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(sthiratvam, n. 2nd s.)(bhāvena, m. 3rd s.)(samāna-)(apara-)
body.translated_text: 1784. When the deluded see the two golden entities, then [one] imagines stability — through a subsequent entity of similar [appearance].

body.text:
1785.
(hemnaḥ, n. 6th s.)(avasthita-)(rūpatve, n. 7th s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(rūpam, n. 1st s.)(api*)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(rucaka-)(dṛśyeta ”dṛś pass. Opt. III p. s.)(ādi-)(pūrva-)(uttara-)(avasthāsu, f. 7th pl.)(anyathā*)(an-ekatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1785. If the form of gold remained unchanged — then that very form should be seen even in the bracelet and so forth — in the prior and subsequent states; otherwise, [there is] non-oneness.

body.text:
1786.
(anugama-)(sāmyena, n. 3rd s.)(hemnaḥ, n. 6th s.)(manyate ”man IV C. Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(sthiratvam, n. 1st s.)(tadā*)(kaiścit*)(baudhaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(api*)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(bhāvaḥ)(bhedavān, m. 1st s.)(avasthā-)
body.translated_text: 1786. Through the similarity of continuity, the stability of gold is imagined; therefore, by some <s>Bauddhas</s> (Buddhists) too, an entity differentiated by states is accepted.

body.text:
1787.
(yathā*)(hema, n. 1st s.)(na*)(jahāti ”hā 3rd C. Pr. III p. s.)(varṇyam, n. 1st s.)(api*)(bhāve, m. 7th s.)(bheda-)(avasthā-)(tathā*)(adhvasu, n. 7th pl.)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(bhāvaḥ)(na*)(tyajati ”tyaj Pr. III p. s.)(dravyatvam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1787. Just as gold does not abandon [its] describable [character], even when there are state-differences — so too, this entity does not abandon <s>dravyatva</s> (substantiality) in the [three] time-paths.

body.text:
1788.
(anyathā*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(atītā-)(a-jātayoḥ, m. 6th d.)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(a-viṣayam, n. 1st s.)(katham*)(kathitam, n. 1st s.)(tāyinā, m. 3rd s.)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(āśrayam, n. 1st s.)(dvaya-)
body.translated_text: 1788. Otherwise, knowledge of what is past and unarisen would be objectless; how then has the <s>Tāyin</s> (the Protector, i.e., the <s>Jina</s>) declared cognition to have a twofold basis?

body.text:
1789.
(katham*)(ca*)(karma, n. 1st s.)(atītam, n. 1st s.)(niḥsattvam, n. 1st s.)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(phaladam, n. 1st s.)(kim*)(ca*)(yoginām, m. 6th pl.)(vibhaktam, n. 1st s.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(atīta-)(an-āgate, n. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 1789. And how is past <s>karma</s> (action), which is without existence, accepted as fruit-bearing? And how is the cognition of <s>yogins</s> divided with respect to the past and the future?

body.text:
1790.
(tataḥ*)(atīta-)(an-āgatāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(na*)(viṣayāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(apoha-)(dravya-)(rūpāt, m. 5th s.)(saṅgraha-)(adhva-)(vibhāva-)(ādeḥ, m. 6th s.)(-vat*)(varttamāna-)
body.translated_text: 1790. Therefore, past and future [entities] are not [mere] objects — from the form of <s>dravya</s> (substance) [defined as] exclusion; from the collection of time-paths [the distinction arises] — like the present, from the manifestation and so forth.

body.text:
1791.

body.translated_text: 1791. And here one should not think thus: whence [comes] the distinction of the time-paths? For this distinction of the time-paths is conceived through purposeful activity (<s>kāritra</s>).

body.text:
1792.

body.translated_text: 1792. For [what] operates in purposeful activity is called 'present'; [what has] fallen from purposeful activity [is called] 'past'; and [what has] not attained that [purposeful activity is called] 'future.'

body.text:
1793.
(kāritvam, n. 1st s.)(dharmāṇām, m. 6th pl.)(ākṣepaḥ)(phala-)(na* tu*)(janakam, n. 1st s.)(vā*)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(na*)(ākṣepaḥ)(atītānām, n. 6th pl.)(na*)(sambhavaḥ)(kāritra-)
body.translated_text: 1793. The purposeful activity of <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) is the impelling of the fruit, not the producer [itself]; or, there is no impelling of the past [entities], and no possibility of [their] purposeful activity.

body.text:

body.translated_text: 1794. This purposeful activity must be accepted by them [the opponents] as either different from the <s>dharma</s> (phenomenon) or of that very form; [but] there is no other real course.

body.text:
1795.
(anyatve, n. 7th s.)(prāk*)(ūrdhvam*)(varttamānānām, n. 6th pl.)(gamyatām ”gam/gacch pass. Imperative III p. s.)(a-svabhāvatā, f. 1st s.)(hetutva-)(saṃskṛtatva-)(ādeḥ, m. 5th s.)(iva*)(kāritrasya, n. 6th s.).
body.translated_text: 1795. If [purposeful activity is] different — let the essencelessness of present [entities] be understood before and after — like the purposeful activity of causality, conditionedness, and so forth.

body.text:
1796.
(anyathā*)(āpattiḥ, f. 1st s.)(nityatā, f. 1st s.)(avasthiteḥ, f. 5th s.)(svabhāva-)(sadā*)(hi*)(atiriktam, n. 1st s.)(etat-)(rūpa-)(vidyate ”vid IV C. Pr. III p. s.)(na*)(lakṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(nitya-)
body.translated_text: 1796. Otherwise, the consequence [would be] eternality of [what] abides [in its] own nature; for indeed, a permanent characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) that is distinct from this form does not exist.

body.text:
1797.
(nityasya, n. 6th s.)(hetutā, f. 1st s.)(niṣiddhā, f. 1st s.)(pūrvam*)(virodhataḥ* [-tas suff.])(krama-)(a-krama-)(hi*)(saṃskṛtatvam, n. 1st s.)(vyaktam, n. 1st s.)(nirāspadam, n. 1st s.)(nityatve, n. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 1797. The causality of the permanent has been previously refuted on the grounds of contradiction; for <s>saṃskṛtatva</s> (conditionedness) — [whether] sequential or non-sequential — is clearly without basis in the case of eternality.

body.text:
1798.
(kāritrasya, n. 6th s.)(upavarṇane, n. 7th s.)(vyatiriktasya, n. 6th s.)(skandha-)(ādi-)(durnirvāraḥ)(virodhaḥ)(sva-)(siddhānta-)(prasajyate ”sajj pass.)
body.translated_text: 1798. In the description of <s>kāritra</s> (purposeful activity) as distinct [from the <s>dharma</s>], an irrefutable contradiction with one's own established doctrine regarding the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and the like arises.

body.text:
1799.
(api*)(kāritram, n. 1st s.)(an-anyatve, n. 7th s.)(dharmāt, m. 5th s.)(a-vyatirekataḥ* [-tas suff.])(dharmāt, m. 5th s.)(prasaktam, n. 1st s.)(sārvakālikam, n. 1st s.)(iva*)(svarūpam, n. 1st s.)(dharmasya, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 1799. Moreover, if <s>kāritra</s> (purposeful activity) is non-different from the <s>dharma</s> (phenomenon) — because of [its] non-distinction from the <s>dharma</s> — [then] the own-nature of the <s>dharma</s> would be as if present at all times.

body.text:
1800.
(tataḥ* ca*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(vibhāgaḥ)(adhva-)(na*)(prakalpyate ”kḷp pass.)(vaśāt, n. 5th s.)(tat-)(hi*)(vibhāgataḥ* [-tas suff.])(cyutiḥ, f. 1st s.)(prāptiḥ, f. 1st s.)(vā*)(a-prāptiḥ, f. 1st s.)(tasya, n. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 1800. And therefore, this distinction of the time-paths (<s>adhvan</s>) cannot be conceived; for from that [non-distinction], there would be the falling away from the [temporal] division, and either the attainment or non-attainment of that [activity].

body.text:
1801.
(vā*)(a-vyatirekāt, m. 5th s.)(kāritra-)(dharmaḥ)(-vat*)(kāritra-)(bhavet ”bhū Opt. III p. s.)(vyavacchinna-)(pūrva-)(apara-)(sarvavān, m. 1st s. [poss. suff.])(mātraka-)(madhya-)
body.translated_text: 1801. Or, because of non-distinction from the <s>dharma</s>, <s>kāritra</s> (purposeful activity) would become — like the <s>dharma</s> [itself] — possessed of all [temporal aspects]: prior, posterior, intermediate, and merely fragmentary.

body.text:
1802.
(kāritram, n. 1st s.)(asti ”as Pr. III p. s.)(na*)(sarvadā*)(ca*)(dharmaḥ)(varṇyate ”varṇ pass. Pr. III p. s.)(sadā*)(ca*)(kāritram, n. 1st s.)(na* anyat, n. 1st s.)(dharmāt, m. 5th s.)(vyaktam, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(viceṣṭitam, n. 1st s.)(deva-)
body.translated_text: 1802. <s>Kāritra</s> (purposeful activity) does not exist at all times, yet the <s>dharma</s> (phenomenon) is described as [existing] always; and <s>kāritra</s> is not other than the <s>dharma</s> — clearly a divine contortion!

body.text:
1803.
(yadi*)(tatra*)(api*)(sthithiḥ, f. 1st s.)(adhva-)(sāpekṣā-)(antara-)(kāritra-)(nanu*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(paryanuyogaḥ)(tulyaḥ)(dhāvati ”dhā Pr. III p. s.)(sarvatra*)(api*)
body.translated_text: 1803. If there too [you say] the distinction of time-paths depends on another <s>kāritra</s> (activity) — surely this objection runs equally everywhere.

body.text:
1804.
