body.translated_text: 1804. If [you say that] a distinguishing feature, distinct from the own-nature, is observed — as with <s>sapratighatva</s> (impenetrability) — this is not at all helpful for the matter at hand.

body.text:
1805.
(hi*)(sapratighatva-)(ādiḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(anugāminaḥ, m. 6th s.)(padārthasya, m. 6th s.)(kaścit*)(mataḥ)(kādācitkaḥ)(bhavasya, m. 6th s.)(eva*)(udbhavāt, m. 5th s.)(tathā*)
body.translated_text: 1805. For <s>sapratighatva</s> (impenetrability) and the like are not considered to be occasional [properties] of an entity that is permanent; [they arise] only from the arising of [what is] existent, in that manner.

body.text:
1806.
(bhāvaḥ)(eva*)(an-ākṣipta-)(bhedena, m. 3rd s.)(anya-)(tathā*)(ucyate ”vac pass.)(śabdena, m. 3rd s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(rūpasya, n. 6th s.)(iti*)(api* ca*)(vāsanā, f. 1st s.)(cetasaḥ, n. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 1806. An entity itself is spoken of by another word, without [any] difference being implied — thus, that [word designates] the form [of the entity]; and moreover, [there is merely] an impression (<s>vāsanā</s>) of the mind.

body.text:
1807.
(atha*)(kāritram, n. 1st s.)(varṇyate ”varṇ pass. Pr. III p. s.)(a-vācyam, n. 1st s.)(prakārābhyām, m. 3rd d.)(tattva-)(anyatva-)(iva*)(santāna-)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(evam*)(nanu*)(syāt ”as Opt. III p. s.)(sāṃvṛtam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1807. Now, if <s>kāritra</s> (purposeful activity) is described as inexpressible by the two modes — identity and otherness — like a continuum (<s>santāna</s>) and the like — then surely it would be [merely] conventional (<s>sāṃvṛta</s>).

body.text:
1808.
(ca*)(ataḥ*)(kalpitatvena, n. 3rd s.)(-vat*)(santati-)(tat, n. 1st s.)(na*)(upayujyate ”yuj pass. Pr. III p. s.)(kvacit*)(kārye, n. 7th s.)(yasmāt, n. 5th s.)(eva*)(vastu, n. 1st s.)(kṣamam, n. 1st s.)(arthakriyā-)
body.translated_text: 1808. And therefore, like a continuum, being of a fabricated nature, that [kāritra] would not be useful in any [real] effect; because only a real entity (<s>vastu</s>) is capable of efficacious action (<s>arthakriyā</s>).

body.text:
1809.

body.translated_text: 1809. Thus, the establishment of this [kāritra's] presence has not been accomplished; the true arrangement of the three time-paths (<s>tri-adhvan</s>) is not tenable.

body.text:
1810.
(kāritra-)(ākhyā, f. 1st s.)(yā, f. 1st s.)(śaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(ākṣepa-)(phala-)(gocarā, f. 1st s.)(śabda-)(ca*)(eva*)(śakteḥ, f. 6th s.)(vastutvāt, n. 5th s.)(katham*)(sā, f. 1st s.)(prajñaptisatī, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1810. That capacity (<s>śakti</s>) called <s>kāritra</s> (purposeful activity), whose domain is the impelling of the fruit — and because of the reality of [this] capacity [designated by] a word — how could it be [merely] conceptually existent (<s>prajñaptisat</s>)?

body.text:
1811.
(ca*)(yat, n. 1st s.)(rūpam, n. 1st s.)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(kṛt, n. 1st s.)(kārya-)(dāha-)(pāka-)(ādi-)(kim*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(abhyupeyate; abhi-upa-”i pass.)(atīta-)(anāgata-)(avastham, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1811. And as for the form [of activity] that is accepted — producing effects such as burning, cooking, and the like — is that very [form] accepted as existing in the past and future states?

body.text:
1812.
(cet*)(eva*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(katham* nāma*)(kriyā, f. 1st s.)(kriyā, f. 1st s.)(viratiḥ, f. 1st s.)(kriyā-)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(sataḥ, n. 6th s.)(eka-)(ātmanaḥ, n. 6th s.)?
body.translated_text: 1812. If so, how indeed [could there be both] action and cessation of action for that [entity] which is of a single nature, [while] existing [in all three times]?

1897.

body.translated_text: 1897. Therefore, the initial consciousness there [in the embryo] arises through the force of its own material cause — [namely] from [prior] causes [in its own continuum] — like present-day consciousness, by [its] nature of being consciousness and the like.

body.text:
1898.
(ca*)(saṃsthite, n. 7th s.)(a-hetutve, n. 7th s.)(anyathā*)(anya-)(hetu-)(pratikṣepāt, m. 5th s.)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(na*)(prasajyate ”sañj pass.)(niyataḥ, m. 1st s.)(dharmaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1898. And when causelessness is established, otherwise — because of the rejection of other causes — this determinate property would not follow.

body.text:
1899.
(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(kṣaṇa-)(maraṇa-)(kṣamam, n. 1st s.)(udaya-)(sva-)(upādeya-)(rāgiṇaḥ, 6th s.)(a-hīna-)(saṅgatvāt, 5th s.)(vat*)(pūrva-)(vijñāna-)
body.translated_text: 1899. Consciousness, [which is] capable of momentary death and arising — [arises] from its own material [cause which is] to be taken up [in the next moment]; because of the undiminished connection [with its continuum] — like a previous consciousness.

body.text:
1900.
(rūpeṇa, n. 3rd s.)(yena, n. 3rd s.)(janayat ”jan caus., n. 1st s.)(pariniścitam, n. 2nd s.)(vijñānam, n. 2nd s.)(prāk*)(kim*)(na)(tat-bibhrat ”bhṛ III C., n. 1st s.)(akhaṇḍam, n. 1st s.)(kārakam, n. 1st s.)(paścāt*)(api*)
body.translated_text: 1900. [If] a consciousness that generates [the next moment] in a [particular] form has been ascertained previously — does it not bear that [form] intact as a causal agent even afterwards?

body.text:
1901.
(para-)(pakṣe, m. 7th s.)(saṃsthitiḥ, f. 1st s.)(iti*)(tat-jñānam, n. 1st s.)(kāyāt, m. 5th s.)(eva*)(katham*)(tat*)(dṛṣṭāntau, m. 1st d.)(siddhau, m. 1st d.)(sādhya-dharma-)
body.translated_text: 1901. [The opponent says:] 'the establishment [of consciousness] is in the opponent's position' — [but] that cognition [arises] from the body alone — how [can that be]? The two examples are [only] established [for you as] having the property to be proven.

body.text:
1902.
(kāyasya, m. 6th s.)(hetutvam, n. 1st s.)(prāk* eva*)(nivāritam, n. 1st s.)(cetasaḥ, n. 6th s.)(prāpteḥ, f. 5th s.)(yugapat*)(a-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(atirekiṇaḥ, 6th s.)(nanu*)(ca*)
body.translated_text: 1902. The causality of the body for consciousness has already been refuted; because of the non-simultaneous arising [of body and consciousness], and because of [consciousness] being surplus [to the body]. But surely,

body.text:
1903.
(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(smṛti-)(rāga-)(ādi-)(viniścitam, n. 1st s.)(bhāvitvena, n. 3rd s.)(ābhoga-)(śubha-)(citta-)(tat, n. 1st s.)(na* pāryate ”pṛ caus. pass.)(niṣeddhum* ”sidh)
body.translated_text: 1903. Consciousness — [which is] determined [to include] memory, attachment, and the like — possessing the nature of being future, [and being] a virtuous, intentional consciousness — that cannot be denied.

body.text:
1904.
(dṛṣṭau, m. 1st d.)(nirhrāsa-)(atiśayau, m. 1st d.)(pūrva-)(bhāvinām, f. 6th pl.)(buddhīnām, f. 6th pl.)(apakarṣataḥ* [-tas suff.])(samutkarṣa-)(abhyāsa-viśeṣasya, m. 6th s.)(buddhi- ?)
body.translated_text: 1904. Diminution and increase are observed in prior and subsequent cognitions — from the diminution and enhancement [arising] from particular practice and the like of cognitions.

body.text:
1905.
(śakti-)(viguṇe, 7th s.)(a-grahāt, m. 5th s.)(antara-)(jñātavya-artha-)(jñāna-)(hetutvam, n. 1st s.)(jñānasya, n. 6th s.)(na*)(vacanīyatām, f. 2nd s.)(yāti ”yā II C.)
body.translated_text: 1905. Because of the non-apprehension of [any cause] with a deficient capacity within [the series] — the causality of cognition for the cognition of the object to be known — [this] does not reach the status of being [merely] something to be stated.

body.text:
1906.
(vṛttitvam, n. 1st s.)(vibhinna-)(deha-)(na*)(sidhyati ”sidh IV C.)(kā, f. 1st s.)(vṛttiḥ, f. 1st s.)(cetasaḥ, n. 6th s.)(a-pātinaḥ, n. 6th s.)(deheṣu, m. 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 1906. The occurrence [of consciousness] in different bodies is not established; what occurrence of consciousness, which is non-falling, [could there be] in bodies?

body.text:
1907.
(jala-)(ādīnām, m. 6th pl.)(āśrayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(syāt ”as II C. opt.)(pratiṣedhataḥ* [-tas suff.])(patana-)(cetasām, n. 6th pl.)(ca*)(a-gatīnām, n. 6th pl.)(kim, n. 1st s.)(prayojanam, n. 1st s.)(ādhāraiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 1907. [If consciousness were like] water and the like, [it would need] a support; from the negation of falling — and for consciousnesses that have no [physical] movement, what purpose [is served] by supports?

body.text:
1908.
(cet*)(iha*)(vṛttiḥ, f. 1st s.)(parikalpyate ”kḷp caus. pass.)(sthitiḥ, f. 1st s.)(tādātmyena, n. 3rd s.)(sā, f. 1st s.)(api*)(a-yuktā, f. 1st s.)(hi*)(tava, 6th s.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(na* yuktam, n. 1st s.)(ātmakam, n. 1st s.)(kāya-)
body.translated_text: 1908. If occurrence [in the body] is postulated here as abiding through identity [with the body] — that too is unjustified; for cognition is not tenable as having the nature of body, according to you.

body.text:
1909.
(tādātmye, n. 7th s.)(kim*)(cetaḥ, n. 1st s.)(rāga-)(dveṣa-)(ādi-)(na*)(pravedyate ”vid caus. pass.)(paraiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(vispaṣṭam)(yathā*)(kāyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vedyate ”vid caus. pass.)(api*)(tathā*)
body.translated_text: 1909. If [there were] identity [of consciousness and body], why is consciousness — [with its] attachment, aversion, and the like — not clearly perceived by others, just as the body is perceived?

body.text:
1910.
(cetaḥ, n. 1st s.)(vedyate ”vid caus. pass.)(svena, m. 3rd s.)(eva*)(tu*)(dehaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sva-)(paraiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(ca*)(yau, m. 1st d.)(evam*)(tau, m. 1st d.)(vibhidyete ”bhid pass. d.)(iva*)(kukṣi-mūla-)(naṭau, m. 1st d.)
body.translated_text: 1910. Consciousness is perceived by oneself alone; but the body [is perceived] by oneself and by others. These two are thus distinguished — like two dancers, [one] in the belly [and one] on the stage.

body.text:
1911.
(tu*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(hetuḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(prasidhyati ”sidh IV C.)(pakṣe, m. 7th s.)(jñāna-)(advaya-)(vedanāt, 6th s.)(avabhāsasya, m. 6th s.)(svasya, 6th s.)(vat*)(timira-)(ādi-)(svasya, m, 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 1911. But this reason is not established in the thesis of the non-duality of cognition (<s>advaya</s>); because of the [self-]awareness of its own appearance — like [the appearance caused by] an eye-disease (<s>timira</s>) and the like.

body.text:
1912.
(lakṣyate ”lakṣ caus. pass.)(dhvaṃsi, n. 1st s.)(anantara-)(udaya-)(dehasya, m. 6th s.)(cetaḥ-)(tādrūpye, n. 7th s.)(kim*)(na*)(matam, n. 1st s.)(kṣaṇikatvam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1912. [Consciousness,] which is perishable, is observed [to have] an immediately succeeding arising; if the nature of consciousness were [identical with] that of the body — why is momentariness not accepted?

body.text:
1913.
(yadi*)(tatra* ?)(vṛttiḥ, f. 1st s.)(iṣyeta ”iṣ pass. opt.)(sambhūteḥ, f. 5th s.)(tat-)(āśrayeṇa, m. 3rd s.)(vā*)(a-vyabhicāritaḥ* [-tas suff.])(tena, m. 3rd s.)(tahāpi*)(vyabhicāritā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1913. If occurrence [of consciousness] in that [body] were accepted — because of its arising from that [body's] support, or because of its invariable [connection] with that [body] — even so, there would be deviation.

body.text:
1914.
(vinaśvare, 7th s.)(prati-kṣaṇa-)(prāk-avastham, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(karoti ”kṛ VIII C.)(nirantaram, m. 2nd s.)(pratisandhim, m. 2nd s.)(deha-vṛttam, m. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 1914. [Consciousness,] which is of a prior state, produces an uninterrupted reconnection [with the body] — the [re]connection that occurs in the body — in [what is] perishing moment by moment.

body.text:
1915.
(cet*)(tatra*)(bhāvena, m. 3rd s.)(eka-)(santāna-)(na*)(vibhinnatā, f. 1st s.)(anyatra*)(api*)(bhūt ”bhū augmentless aorist)(mā*)(vibhinnatā, f. 1st s.)(bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(eka-)(santāna-)
body.translated_text: 1915. If [you say] there is no difference [between consciousness and body] there, because of belonging to a single continuum — [then we reply:] let there be no difference elsewhere as well, [precisely] because of belonging to a single continuum.

body.text:
1916.
(kutaḥ*)(matam, n. 1st s.)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(kṣīṇa-)(āsravasya, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(a-sandhānam, n. 1st s.)(cet*)(kṛta-antāt, m. 5th s.)(parakīya-)(na*)(prāmāṇya-)(ḥa-parigrahāt, m. 5th s. )
body.translated_text: 1916. How is consciousness of one whose <s>āsravas</s> (influxes) are destroyed known? If there is no continuity, then from the standpoint of the opponent, there is no acceptance of validity.

body.text:
1917.
(iha*)(kecit, m. 1st s.)(su-dhiyaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(ye, m. 1st pl.)(pracakṣate ”cakṣ II C. pl. Āt.)(jinān, m. 2nd pl.)(nirvṛttīn, m. 2nd pl. [bv. cpd.])(a-pratiṣṭhita-)(yānayoḥ, n. 6th d.)(niṣṭhatvam, n. 2nd s.)(tat-)(yāna-)
body.translated_text: 1917. Here, certain wise ones who declare the <s>Jinas</s> to be free from rebirth — for the two vehicles, the <s>apratiṣṭhita-yāna</s> (non-fixed-abode vehicle),

body.text:
1918.
(prati*)(tān, m. 2nd pl.)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(dṛṣṭāntaḥ, m. 1st s.)(asiddhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(samanvitaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sādhya-dharma-)(api*)(te, 6th s.)(āśrayaṇe, n. 7th s.)(siddhānta-)(prativādi-iṣṭa-)
body.translated_text: 1918. Against them, this example is unestablished; it is accompanied by the fallacy of the property to be proved. Moreover, in their taking recourse to the established doctrine desired by the opponent,

body.text:
1919.
(an-abhidhānāt, 5th s.)(bādhaka-)(sandigdha-)(vyatirekitā. f. 1st s.)(śaṅkhyamāna-)(sat-)(bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(vijātīya-)(vyabhicāritā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1919. there is the fault of non-statement of the counter-argument, doubtful differentiation from what is being examined, and deviation with respect to what is heterogeneous, due to the existence of what is being considered.

body.text:
1920.
(na*)(sāhasam, n. 1st s.)(iti* etat, n. 1st s.)(asti ”as II C.)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(kalalādiṣu, 7th pl.)(api*)(indriyatve, n. 7th s.)(a-sañjāta-)(kim*)(na*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. opt.)(tatra*)
body.translated_text: 1920. It is not the case that this is mere boldness — consciousness exists even in the <s>kalala</s> (embryonic) and other stages. If the sense faculties have not yet arisen, would there not be knowledge there?

body.text:
1921.
(sāhasam, n. 1st s.)(iti* adaḥ, n. 1st s.)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(udbhūtam, n. 1st s.)(bala-)(indriya-)(artha-)(yasmāt, 5th s.)(tat, n. 1st s. anyathā* api*)(vedyate ”vid caus. pass.)(svapna)(-ādau, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 1921. All this is boldness — consciousness arises from the strength of sense faculties and objects; since even otherwise it is experienced, as in dreams and such states.

body.text:
1922.
(api*)(rūpam, n. 1st s.)(asya, 6th s.)(vyavasīyate, ”so pass.)(anyat, n. 1st s.)(gateḥ, f. 5th s.)(artha-)(tena, 3rd s.)(api*)(mūrcchā-)(ādau, 7th s.)(sat-bhāvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(asya, 6th s.)(upapadyate ”pad I C. Ā)
body.translated_text: 1922. Moreover, its nature is determined as something other than mere cognition, by reasoning; therefore even in swoon and similar states, the existence of this [consciousness] is established.

body.text:
1923.
(cāpi*)(tathā*)(dhīḥ, f. 1st s.)(na*)(upatiṣṭhate I C. Āt.)(rūpeṇa, n. 3rd s.)(śakti-)(tadā*)(vyavasthānam, n. 1st s.)(matam, n. 1st s.)(buddhīnām, f. 6th pl.)(sva-)(rūpeṇa, n. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 1923. And thus, cognition does not present itself in its own form; at that time, the arrangement of cognitions in the form of potency is accepted, in their own nature.

body.text:
1924.
(kutaḥ*)(te, 6th s.)(iti*)(na*)(cetaḥ, n. 1st s.)(supta-)(mūrcchā-)(ādi-)(avasthāsu, f. 7th pl.)(cet*)(iti*)(niścayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(a-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(vedana-)(kutaḥ*)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(gataḥ)
body.translated_text: 1924. How then? If [you say] the mind does not exist in the states of sleep, swoon, and so forth — from the absence of sensation, whence has that certainty gone?

body.text:
1925.
(yadi*)(bhavataḥ, m. 6th s.)(niścayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tāsu, f. 7th pl.)(sampravarttate ”vṛt Āt. Pr. III p. s.)(ittham*)(vedmi ”vid II C.)(cittam, n. 2nd s.)(evaṃ* sati, 7th s.)(siddhā, f. 1st s.)(sa-cittatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1925. If your certainty operates in those [states] thus — 'I know the mind' — this being so, the state of possessing consciousness is established.

body.text:
1926.
(syāt ”as II C. opt.)(matam, n. 1st s.)(yadi*)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(asti ”as II C.)(āsu, f. 7th pl.)(daśāsu, f. 7th pl.)(tat*)(katham*)(bhavet ”bhū I C. opt.)(na*)(smṛtiḥ, f. 1st s.)(tat-ākārā, f. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(pratibuddhādeḥ,m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 1926. If it is held that consciousness exists in those states, then how would there not be memory having the form of that [consciousness] for one who has awakened and so forth?

body.text:
1927.
(tat, n. 1st s.)(ati-artham, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(a-kāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(na* pravarttate ”vṛt Āt. I C.)(smaraṇam, n. 1st s.)(a-sambhavāt, m. 5th s.)(pāṭava-)(ādeḥ, 6th s.)(vat*)(sadyaḥ-jāta-ādi-)
body.translated_text: 1927. That is entirely without cause; recollection does not operate, due to the impossibility of proficiency and the like, as in the case of the newborn and so forth.

body.text:
1928.
(yadi*)(evam*)(katham*)(vyavasīyate, ”so pass.)(astitvam, n. 1st s.)(asya, n. 6th s.)(āsu, f. 7th pl.)(avagamyate ”gam pass.)(iti*)(hetoḥ, m. 5th s.)(upavarṇitāt, m. 5th s.)(pūrva-)
body.translated_text: 1928. If so, how is the existence of this [consciousness] in those [states] determined? It is understood from the reason previously described.

body.text:
1929.
(yadi*)(cittam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(iṣyate ”iṣ pass.)(avasthāsu, f. 7th pl.)(svapna-)(mūrcchā-)(ādi-)(mṛtiḥ, f. 1st s.)(vā*)(utpattau, f. 7th s.)(a-bhāvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(maraṇa-)(eva*)
body.translated_text: 1929. If the mind is not accepted in the states of sleep, swoon, and so forth, then death itself would be the non-existence at the time of arising.

body.text:
1930.
(mānasī, f. 1st s.)(buddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(sva-tantrā, f. 1st s.)(an-apekṣaṇāt, n. 5th s.)(cakṣuḥ-)(ādi-)(vartate ”vṛt I C. Āt.)(balena, m. 3rd s.)(sva-)(upādāna-)(iva*)(svapna-)(ādau, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 1930. The mental cognition (<s>mānasī buddhi</s>) operates independently, without dependence on the eye and other [sense faculties], by the force of its own material cause, in dreams and similar states.

body.text:
1931.
(tathā* hi*)(vikalpānām, m. 6th pl.)(vyapekṣitā, f. 1st s.)(indriya-)(artha-)(bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(api*)(a-bhāve, m. 7th s.)(vyāpāra-)(tat-)(vyoma-utpala)(ādiṣu, 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 1931. For indeed, the dependence on sense faculties and objects is not required for conceptual cognitions (<s>vikalpas</s>); even in the absence of their activity, [conceptual cognition operates], as with sky-lotuses and the like.

body.text:
1932.
(api*)(bhāve, m. 7th s.)(tayoḥ, 6th d.)(vikalpaḥ, m. 1st s.)(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pravartate ”vṛt I C. Āt.)(atīta-)(ādi-)(avasīyate ”so pass.)(tulyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(uparāgeṇa, 3rd s.)(a-sat-artha-)
body.translated_text: 1932. Moreover, even when those two [sense faculty and object] are present, the conceptual cognition that operates is equal [to one without them], being tinged by unreal objects, as is determined regarding past objects and the like.

body.text:
1933.
(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(upapāditam, n. 1st s.)(vistareṇa, m. 3rd s.)(iti*)(rūpam, n. 1st s.)(vastu-)(na*)(bhāsate ”bhās I C. Āt.)(vikalpeṣu, m. 7th pl.)(pratibhāsitvāt, n. 5th s.)(śabda-artha-)
body.translated_text: 1933. All this has been established in detail — that the nature of real things does not appear in conceptual cognitions, because what appears [in them] is the meaning of words.

body.text:
1934.
(avasthāsu, f. 7th pl.)(prasuptikā-)(ādi-)(api*)(vikṛtau, f. 7th s.)(śarīra-)(na*)(anyathātvam, n. 1st s.)(manaḥ-buddheḥ, f. 6th s.)(tasmāt, 5th s.)(iyam, f. 1st s.)(āśrayā, f. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(tat-)
body.translated_text: 1934. Even in the states of deep sleep and the like, when there is a transformation of the body, there is no alteration of the mental cognition; therefore this [mental cognition] depends on that [body] as its basis.

body.text:
1935.
(timira-ādike, m. 7th s.)(su-alpīyasi, m. 7th s.)(vikāre, m. 7th s.)(netra-ādeḥ, 6th s.)(buddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(āśritā, f. 1st s.)(cakṣuḥ-ādi-)(jāyate ”jan IV C. Āt.)(vikṛtā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1935. When there is a very minor defect of the eye and other [organs], such as <s>timira</s> (visual disorder) and the like, the cognition dependent on the eye and other [organs] arises in a distorted form.

body.text:
1936.
(tat*)(api*)(dehasya, m. 6th s.)(vināśe, m. 7th s.)(manaḥ-dhīḥ, f. 1st s.)(a-)(āśrayā, f. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(tat-)(vartamānā, f. 1st s.)(balena, m. 3rd s.)(sva-)(upādāna-)(a-virodhinī, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1936. Therefore, upon the destruction of the body, the mental cognition, being without that basis, continuing by the force of its own material cause, is not contradicted.

body.text:
1937.
(yat)(a-virodhinī, f. 1st s.)(manaḥ-buddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(kevalā, f. 1st s.)(vayam, 1st pl.)(na*)(yatninaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(siddhaye, f. 4th s.)(sat-bhāva-)(anya-)(deha-)
body.translated_text: 1937. That the mental cognition alone is non-contradictory [i.e., can continue independently] — we do not strive to establish the existence of another body.

body.text:
1938.
(na*)(ca*)(śakya-)(niṣedhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(asau, m. 1st s.)(a-dṛṣṭau, f. 7th s.)(api*)(saṃśayāt, m. 5th s.)(syat ”as Opt. III p. s.)(eṣā, f. 1st s.)(manda-)(netrasya, m. 6th s. [bv. cpd.])(su-alpa-)(dhūma-)(ādi-)(a-dṛṣṭivat* [-vat suff.])
Textual variant [Baudhabhāratī]: (svaccha-)
body.translated_text: 1938. And that [mental cognition] cannot be denied even when unseen, due to doubt; this [situation] would be like one with weak eyes not seeing faint smoke and the like.

body.text:
1939.
(api*)(āśritatve, n. 7th s.)(bhinna-)(deha-)(anukārataḥ* [-tas suff.])(viśeṣa-)(tat-)(sambaddham, n. 1st s.)(eka-)(santati-)(prācya-)(jñānam, n. 1st s.) (prabandhavat*)
body.translated_text: 1939. Moreover, even when dependent [on a body], knowledge connected with a different body follows the pattern of a single continuum, like a series linked to what is prior, due to the particular characteristics.

body.text:
1940.
(api*)(ca*)(sadyaḥ-)(janma-)(bhṛtām, m. 6th pl.)(abhilāṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pāna-ādau, 7th s.)(stana-)(udvegaḥ, m. 1st s.)(upaghāte, m. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 1940. Moreover, for those just born, there is desire for breast-feeding and the like, and distress upon being harmed.

body.text:
1941.
(asau, m. 1st s)(gamyate ”gam pass.)(rudira-)(pāna-)(stana-)(ādi)(sarvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(ātmā, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(vikalpa-)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(anuṣaṅga-vān, m. 1st s.)(nāma-)
body.translated_text: 1941. All that — blood-drinking, breast-sucking and the like — is understood [as evidence]; that self possessing conceptual cognition has the connection of naming.

body.text:
1942.
(vidyate ”vid pass.)(na*)(nāman-rūpam, n. 1st s.)(abhyastam, n. 1st s.)(asmin, n. 7th s.)(janmani, n. 7th s.)(teṣām, m. 6th pl.)(a-bhāve, m. 7th s.)(anya-)(bhava-)(prasajyate ”sañj pass.)(ucchedaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 1942. The name and form that is practiced is not found in this birth; in the absence of those [from this life], another existence is entailed, otherwise there would be annihilation of those [dispositions].

body.text:
1943.
(tat*)(asau, m. 1st s.)(bhāvī, m. 1st s.)(vāsanā-)(bala-)(abhyāsa-)(saṃstava-)(nāman-)(teṣām, 6th pl.)(rūpatvāt, n. 5th s.)(vikalpa-)
body.translated_text: 1943. Therefore, that [cognition] is future, having the nature of conceptual cognition, due to being of the nature of the names of those [dispositions] through the power of <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impressions), <s>abhyāsa</s> (habitual practice), and <s>saṃstava</s> (repeated association).

body.text:
1944.
(yat)(vikalpaḥ, m. 1st s.)(teṣām, m. 6th pl.)(vartate ”vṛt I C. Āt.)(jaḥ, m. 1st s.)(paripāka-)(vāsanā-)(abhyāsa-)(saṃstava-)(nāma-)(tat*)(antaram, n. 1st s.)(bhava-)(prasiddham, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1944. The conceptual cognition of those [beings] that operates, born from the ripening of <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impressions), <s>abhyāsa</s> (habitual practice), and <s>saṃstava</s> (repeated association) in terms of naming — that is well-established as [coming from] another existence.

body.text:
1945.
(teṣām, m. 6th s.)(pravartate ”vṛt I C. Āt.)(abhyāsa-balāt, m. 5th s.)(kim*)(smṛtiḥ, f. 1st s.)(vā*)(visphuṭāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(vācaḥ, f. 1st pl.)(vāggminām, m. 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 1945. Do their [cognitions] operate from the force of <s>abhyāsa</s> (habitual practice), or is it memory? The clear utterances of those gifted in speech [suggest the former].

body.text:
1946.
(āsām, f. 6th pl.)(iyam, f. 1st s.)(vṛttiḥ, f. 1st s.)(syāt)(na*)(paripāka-)(ākulatvataḥ* [-tas suff.])(paṭīyasā, m. 3rd s.)(upaghātena, m. 3rd s.)(iva*)(daśāsu, f. 7th s.)(sannipāta-)
body.translated_text: 1946. This activity of those [utterances] would not be [mere memory], due to the confusion caused by ripening; just as in states of acute illness (<s>sannipāta</s>), through a more powerful affliction.

body.text:
1947.
(mahā-ātmanām, m. 6th pl.)(yeṣām, m. 6th pl. )(su-alpīyān, m. 1st s.)(upaghātaḥ, m. 1st s.)(visphuṭāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(vācaḥ, f. 1st pl.)(śrūyante ”śru pass.)(ca*)(teṣām, m. 6th pl.)(sphuṭā, f. 1st s.)(smṛtiḥ, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1947. For great souls (<s>mahātmans</s>) whose affliction is very slight, clear utterances are heard, and their memory is vivid.

body.text:
1948.
(amī, m. 1st pl.)(rāga-)(dveṣa-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(paṭavaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(yogataḥ* [-tas suff.])(abhyāsa-)(bhavantaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(pariniścitāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(anvaya-)(vyatirekābhyām, m. 3rd d.)
body.translated_text: 1948. These <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), and the rest become strong through the practice of <s>abhyāsa</s> (habitual repetition); this is ascertained through positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>).

body.text:
1949.
(te, m. 1st pl.)(bhāvinaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(prathama-)(rahitāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(abhyāsa-)(ihatya-)(kaḥ, m. 1st s.)(hetuḥ-, m. 1st s.)(janmanaḥ, n. 6th s.)(yadi*)(syāt ”as II C. opt.)(na*)(antaram, n. 1st s.)(bhava-)(ye, m. 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 1949. If there were no other existence, those [afflictions] that are future, devoid of practice in this [present] life — what would be the cause of their arising in the first birth?

body.text:
1950.
(janma, n. 1st s.)(na*)(upapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(sānnidhyāt, n. 5th s.)(ālambana-)(api*)(tat-)(bhāve, m. 7th s.)(tat-)(a-)(udbhavāt, m. 5th s.)(sat-bhāve, m. 7th s.)(pratisaṅkhyāna-)
body.translated_text: 1950. Birth does not occur [merely] from the proximity of the object of support; moreover, even when that [object] is present, [if afflictions] do not arise from that, then in the presence of <s>pratisaṅkhyāna</s> (analytical meditation),

body.text:
1951.
(ca*)(pratisaṅkhyā-)(nivṛttau, f. 7th s.)(teṣām, m. 6th pl.)(darśanāt, n. 5th s.)(prābalya-)(api*)(naṣṭa-)(ajāte, m. 7th s.)(viṣaye, m. 7th s.)(viparyāsa-)(abhivṛddhitaḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 1951. and in the cessation [of afflictions] through <s>pratisaṅkhyā</s> (analytical meditation), since those [afflictions] are seen to increase even regarding a destroyed or unborn object, through the growth of <s>viparyāsa</s> (false conception),

body.text:
1952.
(rāga-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(pravartante ”vṛt I C. Āt. III p. pl.)(aṅganā-)(ādiṣu, m. 7th pl.)(samāropya ”ruh caus.*)(śubha-)(ātmīya-)(sthira-)(ādīn, m. 2nd pl.)(ca*)(viṣayāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(tat-)(rūpāḥ, m. 1st pl. [bv. cpd.])(na*)
body.translated_text: 1952. <s>Rāga</s> (attachment) and the rest operate regarding women and other [objects], by superimposing [qualities such as] auspiciousness, selfhood, permanence, and so forth; and the objects are not truly of that nature.

body.text:
1953.
(ihatyāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(vartante ”vṛt I C. Āt. III p. pl.)(eva*)(tat-an-ālambanāḥ, m. 1st pl. [bv. cpd.])(śaktitaḥ* [-tas suff.])(abhyāsa-)(sadṛśa-)(rāga-)(āditvāt, n. 5th s.)(yathā*)(uttare, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1953. [The afflictions] of this [life] indeed operate even without that [external] support, from the power of <s>abhyāsa</s> (habitual practice); because of being <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and the like of a similar kind, just as in subsequent [lives].

body.text:
1954.
(viṣaya-)(upanipāte, m. 7th s.)(tu*)(sukha-)(duḥkha-)(ādi-)(sambhavāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(tasmāt, 5th s.)(samāna-)(jātīya-)(vāsanā-)(paripāka-)(jāḥ, m. 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 1954. But upon the encounter with objects, the arising of pleasure, pain, and the like [occurs]; therefore, [these afflictions] are born from the ripening of <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions) of the same class.

body.text:
1955.
(rāga-)(dveṣa-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(kleśāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(pratisaṅkhyāna-)(vidviṣām, m. 6th pl.)(ayoniśo- [?])(manaskāra-)(vidheyānām, m. 6th pl.)(yathā-)(balam)
body.translated_text: 1955. <s>Rāga</s> (attachment), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), and the other <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), for those who oppose [them] through <s>pratisaṅkhyāna</s> (analytical meditation), [arise] in proportion to the strength of <s>ayoniśo-manaskāra</s> (improper mental attention) to which they are subject.

body.text:
1956.
(sākṣāt*)(viṣayāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(na*)(hetavaḥ m. 1st pl.)(rāga-)(dveṣa-)(ādi-)(ekaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kleśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(syāt ”as opt.)(sarveṣām, 6th pl.)(tatra*)(vat*)(bodha-)(tasya, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 1956. Objects such as <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), and the like are not directly the causes [of <s>kleśas</s>]; [otherwise] there would be one single <s>kleśa</s> (affliction) for all — [having] the same cognition of that [object].

body.text:
1957.
(iyam, f. 1st s.)(vṛttiḥ, f. 1st s.)(upalambhena, m. 3rd s.)(vṛtti-)(anya-)(vā*)(śravaṇena, n. 3rd s.)(parebhyaḥ, m. 5th pl.)(upalambhāt, m. 5th s.)(vyabhicāra-)
body.translated_text: 1957. This [particular] occurrence [of a kleśa arises] through perception or through hearing from others — [it is] different from [another's] occurrence; because of the deviation [that results] from [different] perceptions.

body.text:
1958.
(varāha-)(hariṇa-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(a-drṣṭa-)(a-śruta)(vṛtta-antāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(yānti ”yā II C. III p. pl.)(vikriyām, f. 2nd s.)(samparke, m. 7th s.)(sa-bhāga-gati-)
body.translated_text: 1958. Boars, deer, and the like — without [prior] seeing or hearing the events — undergo transformation upon contact with [beings of] similar kind.

body.text:
1959.
(dharmāḥ, m. 1st s.)(prajñā-)(śīla-)(kṛpā-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(anucitāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(saṃsāra-)(na*)(vartante ”vṛt I C. Āt. III p. pl.)(sva-rasena, m. 3rd s.)(vat*)(mada-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 1959. <s>Dharmas</s> (qualities) such as <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct), <s>kṛpā</s> (compassion), and the like, which are unsuitable [for] <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), do not operate spontaneously — like intoxication and the like.

body.text:
1960.
(samudbhavaḥ, m. 1st s.)(teṣām, m. 6th s.)(na*)(prabhāveṇa, m. 3rd s.)(balāsa-)(ādi-)(vat*)(pūrva-)(sarvathā* api*)(vyabhicārasya, m. 6th s.)(upalambhataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 1960. The arising of those [qualities] is not due to the influence of phlegm and the like in every respect; because of the apprehension of deviation in [its influence] from prior [conditions].

body.text:
1961.
(tasmāt, 5th s.)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(yat-abhyāsa-pūrvakāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(bhāvinaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(ādya-)(anya-)(bhavaḥ, m. 1st s.)(iti*)(siddhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(nāstitvatā, f. 1st s.)(hatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1961. Therefore, it is established that he [the being], whose future [births] are preceded by such habituation (<s>abhyāsa</s>), [arises in] another existence — [thus] the [view of] non-existence is defeated.

body.text:
1962.
(sādhye, n. 7th s.)(pūrvakatve, n. 1st s.)(abhyāsa-)(ihatya-)(bādhanam, n. 1st s.)(dṛṣṭa-)(iṣṭa-)(hetutve, n. 7th s.)(bhavāntarīya-)(nidarśanam, n. 1st s.)(śūnyam, n. 1st s.)(sādhya-)
body.translated_text: 1962. When the thing to be proven is the priority of habituation (<s>abhyāsa</s>), the refutation pertains to the present [life]; when the causality of what is seen and desired [is to be proven], the example [from] another existence is devoid of [proving] the thing to be proven.

body.text:
1963.
(sādhye, n. 7th s.)(aviśeṣeṇa, m. 3rd s.)(hetoḥ, m. 6th s.)(viruddhatā, f. 1st s.)(vinivartanāt, n. 5th s.)(hetutva-)(abhyāsa-)(anya-)(bhava-)(tathā*)(eva*)
body.translated_text: 1963. Because the reason is contradicted by [its] indiscriminate [application] to what is to be proven; [and] because, likewise, the cessation of the causality of habituation [in] another existence [follows].

body.text:
1964.
(sādhyatvam, n. 1st s.)(sāmānyena, n. 3rd s.)(na* ca*)(hetoḥ, m. 6th s.)(viruddhatā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(virodhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(asya, 6th s.)(tena, 3rd s.)(yena, 3rd s.)(vinivartayet ”vṛt caus. opt.)(tat, n. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 1964. The thing to be proven in general does not [entail] the contradictoriness of the reason; there is no contradiction of this [reason] by that which would [need to] refute it.

body.text:
1965.
(yadi*)(catuṣṭayam, n. 1st s.)(bhūta-)(na*)(asti ”as II C.)(atirekeṇa, m. 3rd s.)(jñāna-)(tat*)(kim*)(etat, n. 1st s.)(vichinnam, n. 1st s.)(vispaṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(avabhāsate ”bhās I C. Āt.)
body.translated_text: 1965. If [you say] the fourfold [set of] great elements (<s>bhūtas</s>) does not exist apart from cognition — what then is this that appears distinctly and clearly?

body.text:
1966.
(api*)(evam*)(pratibhāse, m. 7th s.)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(sati ”as II C., m. 7th s.)(upagame, m. 7th s.)(nāstitā-)(bhavatām, 6th pl.)(kim, n. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(pramāṇam, n. 1st s.)(astitve, n. 7th s.)(cittasya, n. 6th s.)(api*)
body.translated_text: 1966. Even so, when such an appearance exists and [its existence] is accepted — what would be the proof, for the proponents of non-existence, of the existence of consciousness as well?

body.text:
1967.
(bāhyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(arthaḥ, m. 1st s.)(bhāsamānaḥ ”bhās I C. Āt., m. 1st s.)(kim-)(ātmā, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(pratibhāsate ”bhās I C. Āt.)(kim*)(sva-bhāvaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(parama-aṇu-)(kim vā*)(lakṣaṇaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(avayavi-)
body.translated_text: 1967. As for the external object that appears — with what nature does it appear? Is it of the nature of <s>paramāṇus</s> (ultimate atoms), or of the nature of a <s>avayavin</s> (whole possessing parts)?

body.text:
1968.
(tāvat*)(ākāraḥ, m. 1st s.)(parama-)(aṇūnām, m. 6th pl.)(na*)(prativedyate ”vid caus. pass.)(pratyaya-)(a-prativedanāt, n. 5th s.)(aneka-)(niraṃśa-)(mūrttānām, m. 6th pl.)
Textual variant [Baudhabhāratī]: (mūrttābha-)
body.translated_text: 1968. First, the form of <s>paramāṇus</s> (ultimate atoms) is not perceived in cognition; because partless, formless entities that are multiple are not apprehended in experience.

body.text:
1969.
(parama-)(aṇavaḥ, m. 1st s.)(bhāseran ”bhās I C. Āt. Opt. III p. pl.)(vyapeta-)(bhedāḥ, m. 1st pl. [bv. cpd.])(bhāga-)(anyathā)(teṣām, m. 6th pl.)(na*)(adhyakṣatā, f. 1st s.)(a-samarpaṇāt, n. 5th s.)(ātman-)(ākāra-)
body.translated_text: 1969. If <s>paramāṇus</s> (ultimate atoms) were to appear without [their] part-distinctions — otherwise, they would not be objects of direct perception, because of [their] not presenting [their own] form.

body.text:
1970.
(api*)(jātāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(sāhityena, n. 3rd s.)(te, m. 1st s.)(bhāsinaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(sva-)(rūpeṇa, n. 3rd s.)(ca* ?)(tāsu, f. 7th pl.)(daśāsu, f. 7th pl.)(amī, m. 1st pl.)(na*)(tyajanti, ”tyaj I C. III p. pl.)(anaṃśa-)(rūpatvam, n. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 1970. Even if they arise together and are perceived collectively, [still] in those [collective] states, these [atoms] do not abandon their partless nature by [their] own form.

body.text:
1971.
(cet*)(teṣām, m. 6th pl.)(rūpam, n. 1st s.)(samasti ”as II C.)(labdha-)(paryantam, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(apacaya-)(nāma*)(katham*)(na*)(te, m. 1st pl.)(bhaveyuḥ ”bhu I C. Opt. III p. pl.)(a-mūrttāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(vat*)(vedana-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 1971. If [you say] their form, having reached [its] limit, is an aggregate — how then would they not become formless, like <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) and the like?

body.text:
1972.
(yathā*)(utpādāt, m. 5th s.)(tulya-)(apara-)(vibhramaḥ, m. 1st s.)(nityatva-)(cet*)(a-vicchinna-)(grahe, m. 7th s.)(sajātīya-)(vibhramaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sthūla-)
body.translated_text: 1972. Just as, because of equal production, [there would be] the error of permanence; if [you say that] in the apprehension of an uninterrupted [series of] homogeneous [moments there is] the error of grossness —

body.text:
1973.
(yadi*)(pratyakṣam, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(sva-)(vyāpāra-balena, n. 3rd s.)(na*)(janayet ”jan caus. Opt.)(parāmarśa-vijñānam, n. 2nd s.)(katham*)(te, m. 1st pl.)(gocarāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(adhyakṣa-)
body.translated_text: 1973. If direct perception itself does not generate, by [its] own operative power, a reflective cognition (<s>parāmarśa-vijñāna</s>) — how then would they [the atoms] be objects of direct perception?

body.text:
1974.
(iti*)(bhāvāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(kṣaṇikāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(niścīyante ”ci Pass. III p. pl.)(pramāṇataḥ* [-tas suff.])(tu*)(katham*)(aṇavaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(gamyante ”gam Pass. III p. pl.)(iti* ?)(sita-)(pīta-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 1974. Thus, entities are determined to be momentary by valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>); but how are atoms cognized? — [the question arises regarding] white, yellow, and the like.

body.text:
1975.
(iti* cet*)(ādya-)(cākṣuṣam, n. 1st s.)(pracaya-rūpam, n. 1st s.)(sūkṣma-)(sthūlatvāt, n. 5th s.)(vat*)(parvata- )(ādi-)(samasti ”as II C.)(eṣā, f. 1st s.)(anumā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1975. If [you say] 'the first visual [cognition is of] an aggregate-form' — [we reply:] this inference [follows] from the grossness of mountains and the like, like [the inference of] subtle [from gross].

body.text:
1976.
(sthūlatvam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(siddham, n. 1st s.)(dvaye, n. 7th s.)(dharmin-)(avayavī, m. 1st s.)(asti ”as II C.)(na*)(sthūlaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na* ca*)(aṇavaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(tathā-vidhāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(vastu-)(dharmaḥ)
body.translated_text: 1976. Grossness is not established in either of the two [alternatives] — the property-bearer [or the atoms]; a <s>avayavin</s> (whole) does not exist, nor are atoms of such a [gross] nature — [grossness] being a real property of substance.

body.text:
1977.
(atha*)(uditam, n. 1st s.)(tathā-)(sthita-)(rūpam, n. 1st s.)(vitānena, n. 3rd s.)(deśa-)(api*)(tathā*)(rūpeṇa, n. 3rd s.)(bhāsi-)(bhrānta-)(vijñāna-)(saṃśayaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1977. Now, if [you say] a form that is so constituted [appears] spread out over a spatial extension — even so, [there is] the doubt of an erroneous cognition appearing in that form.

body.text:
1978.
(cet*)(vaitathyāt, n. 5th s.)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(no*)(tathā*)(vyatireke, m. 7th s.)(a-prasādhite, m. 7th s.)(kaḥ, m. 1st s.)(atiśayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(asya, 6th s.)(tasmāt, 5th s.)(yadi*)(saṃvādanam, n. 1st s.)(kārya-)
body.translated_text: 1978. If [you say this doubt arises] from falsity — that is not so, when the distinction [between veridical and erroneous cognition] has not been established; what is the special [advantage]? Therefore, if [you assert] agreement with the effect —

body.text:
1979.
(ucyate ”vac Pass.)(saṃvāde, m. 7th s.)(vijñāna-)(avabhāsi-)(kārya-)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(sambhāvyate ”bhū Caus. Pass.)(anyathā*)(ca*)(hetoḥ, m. 5th s.)(sāmarthya-)(niyamāt, m. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 1979. [We reply:] in the case of agreement, that [cognition] — having the appearance [of its object] — is considered [valid]; and the efficacy of the effect is due to the restriction of the cause's capacity.

body.text:
1980.
(aṇūnām, m. 6th pl.)(dvaya-)(rūpatve, n. 7th s.)(yadā*)(tulyam, n. 1st s.)(rūpam, n. 1st s.)(grāhyam, n. 1st s.)(a-tulyam, n. 1st s.)(rūpam, n. 1st s.)(na* eva*)(gṛhyate ”grah Pass.)(tadā*)(kim, n. 1st s.)(na*)(upapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)
body.translated_text: 1980. When the atoms have a dual form — when the identical form is apprehended and the non-identical form is simply not grasped — what is not tenable [about this]?

body.text:
1981.
(sarva-)(vastunaḥ, n. 6th s.)(rūpatvāt, n. 5th s.)(sāmānya-)(viśeṣa-ātman-)(tat*)(aṇavaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(dvi-)(rūpāḥ, m. 1st pl. [bv. cpd.])(tulya-)(a-tulya-sva-rūpatvāt, n. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 1981. Because every entity has both general (<s>sāmānya</s>) and particular (<s>viśeṣa</s>) natures — those atoms have a dual form, because of [their] having both similar and dissimilar own-natures.

body.text:
1982.
(tatra*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(samānam, n. 1st s.)(rūpam, n. 1st s.)(yat, n. 1st s)(gocaram, n. 1st s. - emend to gocaraḥ, m. 1st s.)(akṣa-jñāna-)(ataḥ*)(eva*)(aṇuṣu, m. 7th pl.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(eka-)(ākāram, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])
body.translated_text: 1982. Therein, that identical form which is the object of sense-cognition — therefore, the cognition of atoms is of a single appearance.

body.text:
1983.

body.translated_text: 1983. The non-identical form is accepted [as the object of] yogic perception (<s>yogi-pratyakṣa</s>) — some confused thinkers fabricate this in a confounded [manner].

body.text:

(katham*)(yukte, n. 1st d.)(ekasya, n. 6th s.)(vastunaḥ, n. 6th s.)(dve, n. 1st d.)(rūpe, n. 1st d.)(tadā*)(prāpte, n. 1st d.)(dve, n. 1st d.)(vastunī, n. 1st d.)(ḥa-paraspara-)(rūpataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 1984. How can two forms belong to a single entity? Then two entities would follow, because of [their] mutually contradictory natures.

body.text:
1985.
(ātmatāyām, f. 7th s.)(paraspara-)(dvairūpyam, n. 1st s.)(virudhyate ”rudh Pass.)(ca*)(viśeṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(upalabhyeta ”labh Pass.)(cakṣuḥ-)(ādibhiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(indriyaiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 1985. The duality of form is contradicted in [what is of] a mutual [identical] nature; and the particular [form] should be perceived by the eye and other sense faculties.

body.text:
1986.
(katham*)(eka-)(rūpam, n. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(paraspara-)(viruddha-)(ātmanā, m. 3rd s.)(saṃvitteḥ, f. 5th s.)(na*)(a-sambhavaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ekasmin, 7th s.)(viruddhānām, 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 1986. How could a single form consist of mutually contradictory natures? There is no impossibility of contradictory [properties co-existing] in one [entity] from the standpoint of cognition.

body.text:
1987.
(iti*)(ekam, n. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(eka-)(ākāram, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(na*)(īśvara-)(bhāṣitam, n. 1st s.)(tathā* hi*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(upetavyam, n. 1st s.)(yathā* eva*)(yat, n. 1st s.)(upalabhyate ”labh Pass.)
body.translated_text: 1987. Thus, one [entity] would have a single appearance — [but] the word of <s>Īśvara</s> (God) [does not determine this]. For indeed, that [entity] must be accepted just as it is perceived.

body.text:
1988.
(tat, n. 1st s.)(na*)(saṃvitteḥ, f. 5th s.)(asataḥ, 6th s.)(api*)(vat*)(pīta-)(kambu-)(bhedasya, m. 6th s.)(tu*)(na*)(anyat, n. 1st s.)(lakṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(saṅgāt, m. 5th s.)(viruddha-)(dharma-)
body.translated_text: 1988. That [entity] is not [established merely] from cognition, [which apprehends] even non-existents; but there is no other defining characteristic [of the entity] apart from the contact of contradictory properties — as with a yellow conch.

body.text:
1989.
(siddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(mā*)(bhūt ”bhū Augmentless Aorist)(pramāṇataḥ* [-tas suff.])(astu ”as II C. Imp. 3p s.)(saṃśayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tu*)(katham*)(prekṣāvatām, m. 6th pl.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(niścayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(eṣām, m. 6th pl.)(a-bhāva-)
body.translated_text: 1989. Let there not be proof from valid means of knowledge — let there be doubt; but how could there be certainty of the non-existence of these [atoms] for the discerning?

body.text:

(saṃyuktam, n. 1st s.)(dūra-)(deśa-)(stham, n. 1st s.)(nairantarya-)(vyavasthitam, n. 1st s.)(eka-)(aṇu-)(abhimukham, n. 1st s.)(rūpam, n. 1st s.)(yat, n. 1st s.)(aṇoḥ, m. 6th s.)(madhya-)(vartinaḥ, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 1990. The form of an atom situated in the middle — [which is] conjoined, located at a distant place, established in contiguity — [and which is] facing a single [neighboring] atom —

body.text:
1991.
(aṇu-)(antara-)(ābhimukhyena, n. 3rd s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(yadi*)(kalpyate ”kḷp Caus. Pass.)(pracayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(bhū-dhara-)(ādīnām, m. 6th pl.)(evam*)(sati ”as II C., n. 7th s.)(na*)(yujyate ”yuj Pass.)
body.translated_text: 1991. If that very [form] is conceived through [its] facing toward an intervening atom — [then] the aggregation of mountains and the like, this being so, is not tenable.

body.text:
1992.
(cet*)(iṣyate, ”iṣ pass.)(ābhimukhyena, n. 3rd s.)(antara-)(aṇu-)(anyat, n. 1st s.)(rūpam, n. 1st s.)(tathā* sati ”as II C., n. 7th s.)(katham*)(parama-)(aṇuḥ, m. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(ekaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 1992. If a form other [than the atom's own form] is accepted through [its] facing toward an intervening atom — then, this being so, how could the <s>paramāṇu</s> (ultimate atom) be singular?

body.text:
1993.
(tatra*)(eva*)(iyam, f. 1st s.)(kṛtā, f. 1st s.)(cintā, f. 1st s.)(aṇuḥ, m. 1st s.)(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)(paraiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(apeta-)(bhedaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(bhāga-)(na*)(a-sambhavaḥ, m. 1st s.)(an-iṣṭa-)
body.translated_text: 1993. This very investigation has been made here: the atom that is accepted by the opponents as devoid of part-distinctions — [its] impossibility is not an undesired [consequence for us].

body.text:

body.translated_text: 1994. When they accept the ultimate-atom-nature of the parts, then inevitably the abandonment of their own thesis follows.

body.text:
1995.

body.translated_text: 1995. Here, [because the argument operates] by way of <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio ad absurdum), there is no unestablishedness of the substratum; for the oneness [of the atom] that is accepted by the opponent is refuted by the force of reasoning and the like.

body.text:
1996.

body.translated_text: 1996. Thus, in all positions, the self (<s>ātman</s>) having a single [nature] is not tenable — because of the impossibility of a single [entity]; nor is [it] possible [as] having a manifold essential nature.

body.text:
1997.

body.translated_text: 1997. Therefore, for the discerning, the ultimate atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>) is fit for the determination [that it is] of a non-existent essential nature — because of being devoid of oneness and multiplicity — like a sky-flower, water[-born lotus], and the like.

body.text:
1998.
(yataḥ*)(a-yogāt, m. 5th s.)(parama-aṇoḥ, m. 6th s.)(na*)(paraiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(upagamyate ”gam Pass.)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(ārabdhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(parama-aṇubhiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 1998. Since, because of the impossibility of the ultimate atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>), it is not accepted by the opponents — that [composite entity] which is composed of ultimate atoms [is also untenable].

body.text:

body.translated_text: 1999. A cognition that has no appearance, or one that has appearance, or one that has another's appearance — none of them cognizes an external object in any way whatsoever.

body.text:

body.translated_text: 2000. Consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) arises as excluded from insentient forms; that non-insentient nature which belongs to it — that is its self-awareness (<s>ātma-saṃvitti</s>).

body.text:
2001.

body.translated_text: 2001. [Objection:] its self-awareness is not [possible], because of the impossibility of the triple form of action, agent, and object [being present] in a single [entity] that is without parts.

body.text:

(tat*)(yuktam, n. 1st s.)(sva-vedanam, n. 1st s.)(rūpatvāt, n. 5th s.)(bodha-)(tena, 3rd s. tāvat*)(katham*)(saṃvedanam, n. 1st s.)(parasya, 6th s.)(rūpasya, n. 6th s.)(artha-)
body.translated_text: 2002. [Reply:] that self-awareness is justified, because of [its] nature as cognition; but then, how is the awareness of another — [that is,] of the form of an object — [possible]?

body.text:

(rūpam, n. 1st s.)(anyasya, 6th s.)(na*)(yena, 3rd s.)(tat-)(vedane, n. 7th s.)(param, n. 1st s.)(saṃvedyeta ”vid Caus. Pass. opt.)(parama-arthataḥ* [-tas suff.])(bhāvānām, m. 6th s.)(vibhinnatvāt, n. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 2003. [Consciousness] does not [possess] the form of another; whereby, in the awareness of that [other], another [thing] would be ultimately known — because of the distinctness of entities.

body.text:

body.translated_text: 2004. Cognition, which arises with the nature of cognition, is justifiably knowable; but the object, [which] has arisen [but] is not cognition — how is that cognized?

body.translated_text: 2005. In the thesis of [cognition] appearing in consciousness — even so, because of the difference between the two in reality — the awareness of the reflection (<s>pratibimba</s>) [of the object in consciousness] is [only] secondary, because of [the reflection's] conformity [to the original].

body.translated_text: 2006. By one who does not accept consciousness as having the coloring of the object-form — there is no [real] awareness of the object either; this [is indeed the correct] approach.

body.translated_text:
2007. [Objection:] the cognition [could still arise] — [for] swords, fire, and the like, even without being of the form of the thing to be cut or burned — [such as] an elephant and so forth — perform cutting, burning, and the like; so too would that [consciousness] and the like.

body.translated_text: 2008. This is unequal; because those [swords, fire, etc.], being existent, are established as causes of arising [of the effect]; but cognition is not a producer [of the object] in that way.

(vijñānasya, n. 6th s.)(rūpatvam, n. 1st s.)(pariccheda-)(upapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(yadi*)(paricchedaḥ, m. 1st s.)(grāhyasya, 6th s.)(sambhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(rūpaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(jñāna-)
body.translated_text: 2009. The nature of consciousness as determination (<s>pariccheda</s>) is tenable — if the determination of the apprehensible [object] were possible; [but this would require that consciousness] has the form of cognition.

body.text:
2010.
(anyathā*)(sphuṭam, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(vaktavyam, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(rūpam, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(pariccheda-)(na*)(nirdiṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(vedanam, n. 1st s.)(arthasya, m. 6th s.)(ittham*)
body.translated_text: 2010. Otherwise, it must be clearly stated: 'cognition has the form of determination' — [but] the awareness of the object has not been indicated thus.

body.text:

body.translated_text: 2011. [Objection:] 'who then is not subject to cross-examination?' [Reply:] that determination is the self of that [cognition] — like [the relation of] continuity and the like to pleasure and the like.

body.text:
2012.
(vedanāya, n. 4th s.)(sva-)(rūpa-)(vedakam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(vyapekṣate ”īkṣ I C. Āt.)(anyat, n. 2nd s.)(ca*)(idam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(a-viditam, n. 1st s.)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(arthaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sva-saṃvidaḥ, f. 6h s.)
body.translated_text: 2012. For self-awareness, [cognition] does not require another [cognition] to know its own form; and this meaning of self-awareness is not unknown.

body.text:
2013.
(vāpṛtam, n. 1st s.)(vittau, f. 7th s.)(artha-)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(ṛcchati ”r I C.)(ātmānam, m. 2nd s.)(tena, 3rd s.)(api*)(prakāśakatve, n. 7th s.)(pratīkṣate ”īkṣ I C. Āt.)(anyat, n. 2nd s.)(bodhāya, m. 4th s.)
body.translated_text: 2013. Cognition, [being] engaged in the awareness of the object, does not reach itself; therefore, even in [its] capacity as illuminator, it awaits another [cognition] for [its own] illumination.

body.text:
2014.
(vā*)(prakāśakatvam, n. 1st s.)(tasya n. 6th s.)(ātmakam, n. 1st s.)(anubhava-)(artha-)(ca*)(asti ”as II C.)(na*)(anubhavaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ātman-)(na*)(prakāśakam, n. 1st s.)(ātmanaḥ, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2014. Or, [if] its capacity as illuminator is of the nature of self-experience of the object — then there is no self-experience; and [an entity] without self [cannot be] an illuminator of itself.

body.text:
2015.
(yathā*)(cakṣuḥ-)(ādīnām, m. 6th pl.)(api*)(prakāśakatve, n. 7th s.)(dṛśyate ”dṛś Pass.)(vyavasthā, f. 1st s.)(rūpa-)(ādau, m. 7th s.)(tathā*)(bhaviṣyati ”bhū Future)(atra*)(api*)
body.translated_text: 2015. Just as even in the case of the eye and the like, in [their] capacity as illuminators, an arrangement regarding form and the like is seen — so too it will be here as well.

body.text:
2016.
(prakāśakatvam, n. 1st s.)(bāhye, m. 7th s.)(arthe, m. 7th s.)(na*)(ātmani, m. 7th s.)(a-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(śakti-)(ca*)(śaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(sarva-bhāvānām, m. 6th pl.)(na*)(paryanuyujyate ”yuj Pass.)
body.translated_text: 2016. The capacity of illumination is [directed] toward the external object, not toward itself — because of the absence of the capacity [to illuminate itself]; and the capacity of all entities is not subject to cross-examination.

body.text:
2017.
(saṃvittiḥ, f. 1st s.)(arthasya, m. 6th s.)(abhidhīyate ”dhā Pass.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(tasyām, f. 7th s.)(bhūtāyām, f. 7th s.)(tat-)(ātman-)(kaḥ, m. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(aparaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vyāpāraḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2017. Cognition is said to be the awareness of the object; when that [awareness] has occurred, [and cognition] is of the nature of that [awareness] — what further operation could there be?

body.text:
2018.
(anubhavaḥ, m. 1st s.)(rūpam, n. 1st s.)(arthasya, m. 6th s.)(yadi*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(ātmakam, n. 1st s.)(jñāna-)(yuktam, n. 1st s.)(jñāne, n. 7th s.)(ātmatvam, n. 1st s.)(anubhava-)(artha-)(ca*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(na*)
body.translated_text: 2018. If experience is the form of the object, and that is of the nature of cognition — [then] the nature of experience and of the object in cognition is tenable; and that [experience] is not [something separate from cognition].

body.text:
2019.
(prasaṅgāt, m. 5th s.)(parityāga-)(upeta-artha-)(tu*)(api*)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(jāte, n. 7th s.)(ātmatve n. 7th s.)(anubhava-)(prasiddhyati ”sidh Iv C.)(na*)(vittiḥ, f. 1st s.)(artha-)
body.translated_text: 2019. But even from the consequence of the abandonment of [the separate existence of] the object — when [the object] has attained the nature of experience — the awareness of the object is not established [as separate].

2020.

body.translated_text: 2020. [In the view of] the thesis of consciousness with form (<s>sākāra</s>) — the proximity of another [entity, i.e., the object,] is the basis [for cognition] there; [cognition bears] a reflection of the object.

body.text:

body.translated_text: 2021. If, because of [consciousness's] insentient nature by its own constitution, there is no self-experience — [then] because of the absence of awareness-cognition, the experience of another's object [would also not be possible].

2022.

body.translated_text: 2022. Cognition is indeed called the experience of the object; when [cognition] has the nature of non-establishment [of itself] — what further establishment of that [cognition] could there be?

body.translated_text: 2023. Without the experience of one's own cognition, the object is unestablished; when there is experience, that object would be established — [but] when would it again be established from the non-establishment of establishment?

body.translated_text: 2024. If [you say] 'in the arising of that cognition, [the object is] not established by self-awareness, [but] established by the awareness of another' — this is well-spoken.

(dvayam, n. 1st s.)(sādhyam, n. 1st s.)(bhinnam, n. 1st s.)(paraspareṇa, n. 3rd s.)(vat*)(rasa-)(ādi-)(ḥa-jñānāt, 5th s.)(aikya-)(rūpeṇa, n. 3rd s.)(vat*)(buddhi-)(antara-)(santāna-)
body.translated_text: [Verse 2066] Both [the apprehended and apprehender] are to be established as mutually distinct — like taste and the like; from the non-cognition of [their] unity — like [cognitions] in another continuum, in the form of [apparent] unity,

body.text:
2067.
(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(gṛhṇāti, IX C.)(aṃśam, m. 2nd s.)(sva-)(utpatteḥ, f. 5th s.)(jñāna-)(vat*)(sva-)(śakti-)(pratiṣedhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ca*)(grāhyatva-)(hi*)(vāsanā, f. 1st s.)(hīnā, f. 1st s.)(dvaya-)
body.translated_text: [Verse 2067] Knowledge does not grasp its own aspect — because of [its] own arising; like knowledge [itself]; and the denial of [its] own capacity — for <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression), devoid of the dual graspability,

body.text:
2068.
(caitra-)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(bodhakam, n. 1st s.)(grāhya-)(aṃśa-)(jñāna-)(udbhūta-)(tat-)(jñānatvāt, n. 5th s.)(yat-vat*)(udbhavam, n. 1st s.)(antara-)(deha-)
body.translated_text: [Verse 2068] <s>Caitra</s>'s knowledge is not the illuminator [of <s>Maitra</s>'s knowledge] — of the object-aspect of knowledge; because of being a knowledge arisen from that [particular knowledge] — just as that which arises in another body,

body.text:
2069.
(a-)(vedanāt, n. 5th s.)(pṛthak-)(pratipāditāt, 5th s.)(pūrvam, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(tat*)(paryanteṣu, m. 7th s.)(aparijñāna-)(aikarūpya-)(na*)(siddhatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: [Verse 2069] Because of non-experience separately from what was previously established — [and] because of the non-establishment of uniformity [arising from] non-comprehension in the final [stages]

body.text:
2070.
(nanu*)(ucyate ”vac Pass.)(anena, n. 3rd s.)(iti*)(sambaddhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(bahiḥ-)(deśa-)(saṃvitteḥ, f. 6th s.)(ākārasya, m. 6th s.)(grāhya-)(ṛte*)(anubhavāt, m. 5th s.)(grāhaka-)
body.translated_text: 2070. Surely, it is said by this — [the apprehender is] connected [with the apprehended]; apart from the experience of the apprehender, the form of the apprehended [and] the cognition of the external place —

body.text:
2071.
(ca*)(na*)(smarāmi ”smṛ I C. 1p s.)(iti*)(ko'pi, m. 1st s.)(arthaḥ, m. 1st s.)(gṛhītaḥ, m. 1st s.)(mayā, 3rd s.)(tadā*)(smaranti ”smṛ I C. III p. pl.)(utpādam, m. 2nd s.)(grāhaka-)(varjitam, m. 2nd s.)(grāhya-)(rūpa-)
body.translated_text: 2071. And 'I do not remember' — thus whatever object was grasped by me; at that time they remember the arising devoid of the apprehender — the form of the apprehended.

body.text:
2072.
(a-bhinnatāyām, f. 7th s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(smaraṇam, n. 1st s.)(grāhye, m. 7th s.)(api*)(sat-bhāve, m. 7th s.)(smṛti-)(grāhaka-)(tu*)(eṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(eva*)
body.translated_text: 2072. In the case of non-difference [between apprehender and apprehended], there would be remembering even when the apprehended exists; but this is indeed the memory of the apprehender.

body.text:
2073.
(evam*)(bhinnatā, f. 1st s.)(tayoḥ, n. 6th s.)(anvaya-)(vyatirekābhyām, m. 3rd s.)(evam* ca*)(api*)(ete, m. 1st pl)(hetavaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(prasiddhāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(sādhya-dharmiṇi, m. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 2073. Thus, the difference of those two [apprehender and apprehended is established] through positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>); and even so, these reasons are established in the subject that possesses the property to be proven.

body.text:
2074.
(prasidhyati ”sidh IV C.)(na*)(vittiḥ, f. 1st s.)(artha-)(a-prasiddha-)(upalambhasya, m. 6th s. [bv. cpd.])(tat*)(na*)(saṃvittiḥ, f. 1st s.)(grāhyasya, m. 6th s.)(ṛte*)(anubhavāt, m. 5th s.)(grāhaka-)
body.translated_text: 2074. The cognition of an object is not established for one whose apprehension [of it] is not established; therefore, there is no cognition of the apprehended apart from the experience of the apprehender.

body.text:
2075.
(pīta-)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(avekṣyate ”īkṣ Pass.)(a-sva-stha-)(locanaiḥ, m. 3rd pl. [bv. cpd.])(ca*)(na*)(saṃvedyam, n. 1st s.)(niṣkṛṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(aṃśāt, m. 5th s.)(grāhaka-)(tathā*)(param, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2075. Yellow and the like is perceived by unhealthy eyes; and what is cognized is not extracted from the apprehender aspect; so too the other [cases].

body.text:
2076.
(sā, f. 1st s.)(smṛtiḥ, f. 1st s.)(bāhya-)(rūpe, n. 7th s.)(viśeṣā, f. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(lakṣita-)(sā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(bhinna-rūpe, n. 7th s.)(sarvataḥ* [-tas suff.])(abhyāsa-)(ādi-)(a-sambhavāt, m. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 2076. That memory regarding an external form is characterized by particulars; it does not [arise] in a form that is completely different, because of the impossibility of practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>) and the like.

body.text:
2077.
(anyathā*)(evam*)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(na*)(smaraṇam, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(ko'pi, m. 1st s.)(gṛhītaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(ca*)(smaraṇam, n. 1st )(vedyate ”vid Caus. Pass.)(saṃkāśam, n. 1st s.)(śuddha-)(sphaṭika-)
body.translated_text: 2077. Otherwise, thus there would be no remembering — whatever was grasped; and remembering is not cognized as resembling pure crystal.

body.text:
2078.
(paścimayoḥ, m. 6th d.)(hetvoḥ, m. 6th d.)(vyaktam, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(anaikāntikatā, f. 1st s.)(vijñānaiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(pīta-)(kambu-)(ādi-)(eṣā, f. 1st s.)(dik, f. 1st s.)(anyatra*)(sādhane, n. 7th s.) also.
body.translated_text: 2078. In the last two reasons, there is clearly inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntikatā</s>) — [as shown] by the cognitions of yellow conch and the like; this is the direction regarding other proofs as well.

body.text:
2079.
(ataḥ*)(ārūḍham, n. 1st s.)(vivāda-āspadam, n. 1st s.)(matam, n. 1st s.)(a-dvayam, n. 1st s.)(viyogāt, m. 5th s.)(vedya-)(kartṛ-)(vijñānatvāt, n. 5th s.)(vat*)(pratibimba-).
body.translated_text: 2079. Therefore, what has risen to the arena of debate is the non-dual (<s>advaya</s>) doctrine, because of the separation of the cognizable and the agent [of cognition]; because of being consciousness — like a reflection.

body.text:
2080.
(pratibimbe, n. 7th s.)(api*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(matam, n. 1st s.)(sa-ālambanam, n. 1st s.)(hi*)(cakṣuḥ-)(raśmi-)(nivṛttau, f. 7th s.)(sva-)(mukha-)(ādeḥ, m. 6th s.)(īkṣaṇāt, n. 5th s.)(tathā*) in the reflection.
body.translated_text: 2080. Even regarding a reflection, cognition is held to have a support (<s>ālambana</s>); indeed, from the seeing of one's own face and the like upon the cessation of the eye's rays — so too in the reflection.

body.text:
2081.
(na*)(sva-)(mukha-)(ādeḥ, m. 6th s.)(īkṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(tathā*)(tat-)(dṛṣṭeḥ, f. 5th s.)(ābhimukhena, n. 3rd s.)(ca*)(dṛṣṭeḥ, f. 5th s.)(bheda-)(pramāṇa-)(deśa-)(ādi-)(vat*)(anya-)(pada-artha-).
body.translated_text: 2081. There is no seeing of one's own face and the like in that way; because [what is seen] is [only] through facing [the mirror]; and because of the proof of difference — place and the like — like another object.

body.text:
2082.
(vijñānatvam, n. 1st s.)(prakāśatvam, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(niḥ-āspadam, n. 1st s.)(grāhye, n. 7th s.)(a-yogena, m. 3rd s.)(a-nirbhāsa-)(ādi-)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(vyāptiḥ, f. 1st s.)(niścitā, f. 1st s.).
body.translated_text: 2082. The status of being consciousness and [its] illumination — that is without support regarding the apprehended, because of non-connection; non-appearance and the like — by that, the pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) is ascertained.

body.text:
2083.
(sthitiḥ, f. 1st s.)(viṣaya-)(grāhya-)(aṃśe, m. 7th s.)(śaktau, f. 7th s.)(an-antare, n. 7th s.)(jñāne, n. 7th s.)(na*)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)(asmābhiḥ, 3rd pl.)(tāttvikī, f. 1st s.)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(mānam, n. 1st s.)(samarthyate ”arth Pass.).
body.translated_text: 2083. The abiding in the aspect of the apprehended object — in [its] capacity — in the immediately following cognition — is not accepted by us as real; by that, the valid means [of cognition] is established.

body.text:
2084.
(vijñapti-)(mātratā-)(vimalīkṛtā, f. 1st s.)(siddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(dhīmadbhiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(asmābhiḥ, 3rd pl.)(yātam, n. 1st s.)(tat-)(diśā, f. 3rd s.)(viniścaye, m. 7th s.)(parama-artha-).
body.translated_text: 2084. The establishment of <s>vijñaptimātratā</s> (consciousness-only) has been made clear by us, the wise; [our discussion] has proceeded in that direction in the ascertainment of ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>).

body.text:
2085.
(anye, m. 1st pl.)(dhiyaḥ, m. 1st pl. [bv. cpd.])(malīmasa-)(a-jñāna-)(jaguḥ, ”gā Perf. III p. pl.)(punaḥ* iha*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(na*)(yujyate ”yuj pass.)(mātratayā, f. 3rd s.)(citta-)(bādhanāt, n. 5th s.)(śruti-).
body.translated_text: 2085. Others of impure intellect, [due to] ignorance, have declared again here [that consciousness alone exists]; this is not justified — by the mere [assertion of] mind — because of its contradiction by scripture (<s>śruti</s>).

body.text:
2086.
(sā, f. 1st s.)(sthitā, f. 1st s.)(pramāṇam, n. 1st s.)(sarveṣām, m. 1st s.)(akṛtatayā, f. 3rd s.)(nara-)(yataḥ*)(giraḥ, f. 1st pl.)(pauruṣeyyaḥ, f. 1st pl.)(vaitathyam, n. 2nd s. pratipadyante ”pad IV C. Āt. III p. pl.).
body.translated_text: 2086. That [scripture] stands as a valid means of cognition for all, because of not being man-made; since human words attain falsity.

body.text:
2087.
(vācyeṣu, n. 7th pl.)(pum-)(śaṅkyate ”śaṅk Pass.)(santi ”as II C. III p. pl.)(doṣāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(santi ”as II C. III p. pl.)(na*)(śrutau, f. 7th s.)(nu*)(a-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(kartuḥ, m. 6th s.)(naḥ, 6th pl.)(asti ”as II C.)(na*)(āśaṅkā, f. 1st s.)(doṣa-).
body.translated_text: 2087. In things to be expressed, faults [attributable to] a person are suspected to exist; they do not exist in scripture; indeed, because of the non-existence of an author, there is no suspicion of fault for us.

body.text:
2088.
(tāvat*)(kartā, m. 1st s.)(adṛṣṭaḥ, m. 1st s.)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)(iti*)(āsīt ”as II C. impf.)(kadā* api*)(sambandhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(adṛṣṭa-)(pūrva-)(hetukaḥ, m. 1st s.)(samprati*-)(ajñāna-); ...
body.translated_text: 2088. To begin with, the author is not seen; if it is accepted [that] there was [a connection] at some time — [this] connection, previously unseen, having ignorance as its cause at present —

body.text:
2089.
(api*)(parikalpyate ”kḷp Caus. Pass.)(iti*)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(asti ”as II C.)(vihīnaḥ, m. 1st s.)(anumāna-)(āgamaḥ, m. 1st s.)(api*)(na*)(siddhyai, f. 4th s.)(tat-)(na*)(asti ”as II C.)(-akṛtakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kṛtaka-).
body.translated_text: 2089. Even if it is imagined that he [the author] exists, [he is] devoid of [support from] inference and scripture; even for the establishment of that [authorship], there is no [proof]. [The <s>Veda</s> is] not uncreated [but] created.

body.text: 2090. Being itself (svayam* eva*)(apramāṇatvāt, n. 5th s.)(kṛtakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(bodhakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(asya, m. 6th s.)(api*)(satyatā, f. 1st s.)(vacanasya, n. 6th s.)(manu-)(ādi-)(kṛtā, f. 1st s.)(tat-)(eva*).
body.translated_text: 2090. Being itself not a valid means of cognition, [the <s>Veda</s> as] created is not revelatory; even the truth of this statement is made by <s>Manu</s> and the like — that alone [is the case].

body.text:
2091.
(tu*)(viśiṣṭaḥ, m. 1st s.)(asambaddhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(katham*)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(satya-vādī, m. 1st s.)(ataḥ*)(naḥ, 6th pl.)(asti ”as II C.)(na*)(āgamaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kartṛkaḥ, m. 1st s.)(api*)(anya-)(kāra-)(veda-).
body.translated_text: 2091. But how would [such an author be] distinguished, [being] unconnected [with the <s>Veda</s>], [yet] a truth-speaker? Therefore for us there is no scripture authored [by anyone] — even by another maker of the <s>Veda</s>.

body.text:
2092.
(yadi*)(kaścit, m. 1st s.)(dṛśyeta ”dṛś Pass. Opt.)(samprati*)(sadṛk, m. 1st s.)(kāra-)(veda-)(tataḥ*)(tena, m. 3rd s.)(upamānena, m. 3rd s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(upamā, f. 1st s.)(api*)(kartuḥ, m. 6th s.).
body.translated_text: 2092. If some [person] similar to the maker of the <s>Veda</s> were seen at present — then by that analogy, there would be a comparison even of the author.

body.text:
2093.
(yadi*)(kiñcit, n. 1st s.)(pramitam, n. 1st s.)(na siddhyet ”sidh IV C. Opt.)(ṛte*)(kārāt, m. 5th s.)(veda-)(tataḥ*)(kāraḥ, m. 1st s.)(veda-)(pratīyeta ”i Pass. Opt.)(artha-āpattyā, f. 3rd s.); ...
body.translated_text: 2093. If something known could not be established apart from the maker of the <s>Veda</s>, then the maker of the <s>Veda</s> would be understood through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption).

body.text:
2094.
(nanu*)(kiñcit, n. 1st s.)(vede, m. 7th s.)(yat, n. 1st s.)(na*)(upapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(vinā*)(tena, m. 3rd s.)(hi*)(sati, m. 7th s.)(asmin, m. 7th s.)(bahu, n. 1st s. eva*)(prāmāṇya-)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(na*)(siddhyati ”sidh IV C.).
body.translated_text: 2094. Surely, something in the <s>Veda</s> that is not possible without him [the author] — indeed, when this [is accepted], much — validity and the like — is not established.

body.text: 2095--Thus then, being not amenable (agamyatvāt)(pañcabhiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(gamyate ”gam Pass.)(eva*)(a-bhāvena, m. 3rd s.)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(asau, m. 1st s.)(bhāvaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(durlabha-)(bādhanāt, n. 5th s.)(a-bhāva-)(pramāṇa-)
body.translated_text: 2095. Therefore, being inaccessible by the five [means of cognition], he is apprehended only through non-existence; by that, the existence of that [author] is hard to find, because of the refutation of non-existence as a valid means of cognition.

body.text:
2096.
(vedasya, m. 6th s.)(apauruṣeyatā, f. 1st s.)(yā, f. 1st s.)(iṣṭā, f. 1st s.)(arthā, f. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(nivṛtti-)(aprāmāṇya-)(api* tu*)(avastutvāt, n. 5th s.)(sā, f. 1st s.)( na*)(sādhanīyā, f. 1st s.)(sādhanaiḥ, n. 3rd pl.).
body.translated_text: 2096. The authorlessness (<s>apauruṣeyatā</s>) of the <s>Veda</s> that is desired — [aimed at] the cessation of invalidity — but because of its non-reality, that is not to be established by proofs.

body.text:
2097.
(nirākaraṇat, n. 5th s.)(tat-)(nāma*)(sādhanam, n. 2nd s.)(pauruṣeyatva-)(yat, n. 2nd s.)(tārkikaḥ, m. 1st s.)(brūyāt ”brū II C. Opt.)(vedasya, m. 6th s.)(apauruṣeyatā, f. 1st s.)(siddhā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2097. From the refutation of that — the proof named [establishing] authorship — a logician would say: 'the authorlessness of the <s>Veda</s> is established.'

body.text:
2098.
(hi*)(yau, m. 1st d.)(vastu-bhūtau, m. 1st. d.)(pakṣau, m. 1st d.)(vat*)(pradhāna-)(parama-aṇu-)(anyatara-)(asiddhyā, f. 3rd s.)(itaraḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(siddhyati ”sidh IV C.)(svayam*).
body.translated_text: 2098. Indeed, the two positions that are real entities — like <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>) — by the non-establishment of one, the other is not established by itself.

body.text:
2099.
(api*)(sādhanam, n. 1st s.)(pradhāna-)(kāraṇatvasya, n. 6th s.)(nirākṛtasya, n. 6th s.)(jagat, n. 1st s.)(kṛtam, n. 1st s.)(parama-aṇu-)(sādhyam, n. 1st s.)(antaraiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(hetu-).
body.translated_text: 2099. Even the proof of the causality of <s>pradhāna</s> — when refuted — [does not establish that] the world is made of atoms; the thing to be proven [requires] other reasons.

body.text:
2100.
(tu*)(tasmin, n. 7th s.)(yat, n. 1st s.)(sādhanam, n. 1st s.)(ucyate ”vac Pass.)(prasiddhi-artham, m. 2nd s.)(bhāva-)(pakṣa-)(nirākṛte, n. 7th s.)(a-bhāvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(samyak*)(siddhyati ”sidh IV C.)(svayam*).
body.translated_text: 2100. But in that [case], when the proof is stated for the purpose of establishing the positive position — when [it] has been refuted — non-existence is properly established by itself.

body.text:
2101.
(yat, n. 1st s.)(paraiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(ucyate ”vac Pass.)(sādhanam, n. 1st s.)(pūrva-)(aparayoḥ, f. 6th d.)(koṭyoḥ, f. 6th d.)(vādinaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(veda-)(arthāḥ, m. 1st pl. [bv. cpd.])(kṛta-)(kṛtvā* ”kṛ nirākaraṇam, n. 2nd s.)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 2101. That which is stated by the opponents as a proof — of the first and latter alternatives — [those] proponents of the <s>Veda</s>, having made the refutation of that —

body.text:
2102.
(api*)(asādhayatām ”sidh Caus., m. 6th pl.)(tat, n. 2nd s.)(yat, n. 1st s.)(vastu-rūpam, n. 1st s.)(nityatvam, n. 1st s.)(tat-)(siddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(svayam*)(hate, n. 7th s.)(dvaye, n. 7th s.)(pūrva-pakṣa-)
body.translated_text: 2102. Even for those not proving that which is a real entity — the permanence — its establishment by itself [occurs] when both prior positions are defeated.

body.text:
2103.
(pūrvā, f. 1st s.)(koṭiḥ, f. 1st s.)(vedasya, m. 6th s.)(yā, f. 1st s. )(lakṣaṇā, f. 1st s.)(pauruṣeyatva-)(ca*)(parā, f. 1st s.)(rūpā, f. 1st s.)(vināśa-)(hi*)(a-bhāvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tat-)(nityatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2103. The first alternative regarding the <s>Veda</s>, which is characterized by authorship; and the latter, having the form of destruction — indeed, non-existence of those [constitutes its] permanence.

body.text:
2104.
(tat, n. 1st s. eva*)(nityatvam, n. 1st s.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(yat, n. 2nd s.)(vedaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(kriyate ”kṛ Pass.)(ādau, m. 7th s.)(na*)(eva*)(vinaśyati ”naś IV C.)(paścāt*)(cet*)(matam, n. 1st s.)(api*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(jñeyam, n. 1st s.)',...
body.translated_text: 2104. That very permanence of it [is this]: that the <s>Veda</s> is not created in the beginning, nor does it perish afterwards; if this view too [is held] — that should be known.

body.text:
2105.
(hi*)(nityatvam, n. 1st s.)(vivakṣitam, n. 1st s.)(akṛtatva)(avināśābhyām, m. 3rd d.)(ca*)(tau, m. 1st d.)(ātmakatvena, n. 3rd s.)(a-bhāva-)(na*)(apekṣete ”īkṣ I C. Āt. 3p d.)(sādhanam, n. 2nd s.)(sva-)
body.translated_text: 2105. Indeed, permanence (<s>nityatva</s>) is intended [to mean] uncreatedness and indestructibility; and those two, being of the nature of non-existence, do not require their own proof.

body.text:
2106.
(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vadati ”vad I C.)(mithyātvam, n. 2nd s.)(veda-)(vākya-)(artha-)(anumānataḥ* [-tas suff.])(tasya, m. 6th s.)(pakṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(nivartate ”vṛt I C. Āt.)(balāt, n. 5th s.)(vi-jñāna-)(vaidika-)
body.translated_text: 2106. He who states the falsity of <s>Vedic</s> statements and their meanings through inference — his position is overturned by the force of <s>Vedic</s> knowledge.

body.text:
2107.
(ca*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(vaidikam, n. 1st s.)(tulyatvāt, n. 5th s.)(pratyakṣa-)(balavattaram, n. 1st s.)(śakyam, n. 1st s.)(na* kathañcit* api*)(bādhitum* ”bādh)(anumānena, n. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 2107. And that Vedic [testimony], because of its equality [with inference], is stronger than direct perception; it cannot be refuted in any way whatsoever by inference.

body.text:
2108.
(yataḥ*)(śāstram, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(sthitam, n. 1st s.)(nikṣiptam, n. 1st s.)(pakṣa-)(pratyakṣa-)(balavattaram, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(etat, n. 1st s.)(bādhakam, n. 1st s.)(anumānasya, n. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2108. Since the scripture itself is established [and] placed in the thesis as stronger than direct perception — this [argument] is a refuter of inference.

body.text:
2109.
(lāghavam, n. 1st s.)(pramāṇatve, n. 7th s.)(āgamasya, m. 6th s.)(nirapekṣatvāt, n. 5th s.)(dṛṣṭānta-)(ca*)(a-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(doṣa-)(tādṛśam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(anumānasya, n. 6th s.).
body.translated_text: 2109. Lightness [of proof] — because of [scripture's] independence in [its] status as a means of knowledge, and because of the absence of an example — such a fault does not [belong] to inference.

body.text:
2110.
(tena, n. 3rd s.)(yatra*)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(saṃśayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(arthe, m. 7th s.)(āgama-)(anumānābhyām, n. 3rd d.)(nirṇayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kāryaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tatra*)(āgama-)(balīyastvāt, n. 5th s.)(eva*)(tena, m. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 2110. Therefore, wherever there is doubt regarding the meaning — [which should be resolved] by scripture (<s>āgama</s>) and inference — the determination should be made there; because of the superiority of scripture alone, by that [scripture].

body.text:
2111.
(api*)(vedaḥ, m. 1st s.)(bodhayan ”budh Caus., m. 1st s.)(artham, m. 2nd s.)(iti* evam*)(apramāṇam, n. 1st s.)(mama, 6th s.)(śakyate ”śak Pass.)(na*)(vaktum* ”vac)(satya-vādinā, m. 3rd s.)(mātreṇa, n. 3rd s.)(dveṣa-).
body.translated_text: 2111. Moreover, 'the <s>Veda</s> is not a means of knowledge for me, [even though it] makes the meaning known' — this cannot be said by a truth-speaker by mere hatred.

body.text:
2112.
(ca*)(na* syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(apramāṇatā, f. 1st s.)(dveṣāt, m. 5th s.)(a-sammatatvāt, n. 5th s.)(na*)(ca*)(avakalpyate ”kḷp Pass.)(pramāṇam, n. 1st s.)(prīti-)(anujñābhyām, f. 3rd d.)
body.translated_text: 2112. And there would not be invalidity from hatred; because of not being accepted [as valid merely] from affection and permission — nor is a means of knowledge [established] through these.

body.text:
2113.
(api*)(ye, m. 1st pl.)(dviṣantaḥ ”dviṣ I C., m. 1st pl.)(na*)(jalpanti ”jalp I C. III p. pl.)(kiñcit, n. 2nd s.)(kāraṇam, n. 2nd s.)(prāmāṇya-)(ete, m. 1st pl.)(na*)(bhaveyuḥ ”bhū I Cl. Opt. III p. pl.)(satya-vādinaḥ, m. 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 2113. Moreover, those who are hostile [and] do not state any reason for [the Veda's] validity — they would not be truth-speakers.

body.text:
2114.
(nitya-)(abhiyogibhiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(adhyayana-)(dhāraṇa-)(vyākhyā-)(karma-)(ajñātaḥ, m. 1st s.)(hetuḥ, m. 1st s.)(mithyātva-)(katham*)(jñāyate ”jñā Pass.)(sthaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(dūra-)
body.translated_text: 2114. By those constantly engaged [in] study, retention, and the work of exposition — the reason [for validity] is not [to be] known [as] false — how is it known by those who stand at a distance?

body.text:
2115.
(hi*)(ye, m. 1st pl.)(abhiyuktāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(yatra*)(prayojanāḥ, m. 1st pl. [bv. cpd.])(nibaddha-)(tat-)(te, m. 1st pl.)(jñāne, n. 7th s. adhikṛtāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(guṇa-)(doṣāṇām, m. 6th pl.)(tatratya-)
body.translated_text: 2115. For those who are devoted to a [particular subject] and have their purpose bound therein — they are qualified in the knowledge of the merits and faults pertaining to that [subject].

body.text:
2116.
(pāpāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(tu*)(ye, m. 1st pl.)(dviṣaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(brahma-)(dūram, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(bahiḥ-)(kṛtāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(vedāt, m. 5th s.)(katham*)(te, m. 1st pl.)(a-lajjitāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(jalpanti ”jalp I C. III p. pl.)(guṇa-)(doṣa-)(uktīḥ, f. 2nd pl.)(veda-)
body.translated_text: 2116. But those who are sinful [and] hostile to <s>Brahman</s> — who have been cast far outside the <s>Veda</s> — how do they, unashamed, speak of the merits and faults of the <s>Veda</s>?

body.text:
2117.
(kiñca*)(nityatvam, n. 1st s.)(vibhutvam, n. 1st s.)(śabdasya, m. 6th s.)(sthitam, n. 1st s.)(śrotra-ja-)(pratyabhijñayā, f. 3rd s.)(kaḥ, m. 1st s.)(adhyavasyet ”so IV C. Opt.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(viparyayam, m. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 2117. Furthermore, the permanence [and] all-pervasiveness of <s>śabda</s> (sound) is established through the recognition born from the ear; who would determine the opposite of that?

body.text:
2118.
(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(ekatā, f. 1st s.)(sarva-)(kāleṣu, m. 7th pl.)(ca*)(sarva-)(deśeṣu, m. 7th pl.)(prasiddhā, f. 1st s.)(pratyakṣa-)(pratyabhijñā-)(sā, f. 1st s.)(bādhikā, f. 1st s.)(asya, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2118. Therefore, its oneness in all times and in all places is well-established; that recognition, [being] perceptual, is the refuter of this [opponent's position].

body.text:
2119.
(cet*)(iti*)(ādeḥ, m. 6th s.)(jvālā-)(api*)(kṣaṇikatve, n. 7th s.)(pratyabhijñā, f. 1st s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(na*)(hi*)(pratijñeyam, n. 1st s.)(tatra*)(sāmānyam, n. 1st s.)(nityam, n. 1st s. eva*)(naḥ, 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 2119. [Objection:] 'If so, even of a flame and the like, recognition [would prove] permanence in momentariness.' [Reply:] That is not [a valid] thesis; for the universal there is indeed permanent for us.

body.text:
2120.
(yatra*)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(buddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(bheda-)(aṃśe, m. 7th s.)(kenacit, m. 3rd s.)(upādhinā, m. 3rd s.)(na*)(pratyabhijñānam, n. 1st s.)(tatra*)(avadhāritam, n. 1st s.)(buddhyā, f. 3rd s.)(bheda-)
body.translated_text: 2120. Wherever there would be a cognition of difference in the aspect of difference through some limiting condition — there, [when] the difference has been ascertained by the intellect, recognition [does] not [arise].

body.text:
2121.
(buddhayaḥ, f. 1st pl.)(vyakti-)(go-śabda-)(ca*)(bhinnāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(deśa-)(kāla-)(ādi-)(sarvāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(samāna-)(viṣayāḥ, m. 1st pl. [bv. cpd.])(vā*)(na*)(gocarāḥ, m. 1st pl. [bv. cpd.])(nānā-)(artha-)
body.translated_text: 2121. The cognitions of the word 'cow' [and] the individual [cow], differentiated by place, time, and the like — are all either having the same object, or not having diverse objects as their domain.

body.text:
2122.
