(utpadyamānatvāt, n. 5th s.)(iti*)(gauḥ, m. 1st s.)(vat*)(buddhi-)(utpanna-)(samprati-)(buddhyā, f. 3rd s.)(go-śabda-)(hyastanyā, f. 3rd s.)(prakāśitaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(go-śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2122. Because of arising [in the same way] — like a cow — the word 'cow' is illuminated by yesterday's cognition [and] the present cognition; this word 'cow' has arisen [identically].

body.text:
2123.
(viṣayatvena, n. 3rd s.)(go-śabda-)(eva*)(yathā*)(prasūtayā, f. 3rd s.)(adya*)(iyam, f. 1st s.)(vijānāti ”jñā IX C.)(tam, m. 2nd s.)(tat-)(hetoḥ, m. 5th s.)(vat*)(pūrva-)(buddhi-)
body.translated_text: 2123. Just as a [cow] that has given birth today recognizes it [the calf] as the object of the word 'cow' — because of that reason, like a prior cognition —

body.text:
2124.
(vā*)(ubhe, f. 1st du. api*)(bhavetām ”bhū I C. Opt 3p d.)(eka-)(viṣaye, f. 1st d.)(vat*)(eka-)(buddhi-)(samastāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(buddhayaḥ, f. 1st pl.)(gotva-)(bhinnāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(deśa-)(kāla-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 2124. Or, both [cognitions] would be [directed at] a single object, like [cognitions arising from] a single cognition; all the cognitions [of the word 'cow'], differentiated by place, time, and the like, [are distinguished] by <s>gotva</s> (cow-ness).

body.text:
2125.
(syuḥ ”as II C. Opt. III p. pl.)(janyāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(eka-)(go-śabda-)(dhītvāt, n. 5th s.)(go-)(vat*)(eka-)(buddhi-)(vāpi*)(go-śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(uccāraṇaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(hyastana-)(vidyate ”vid Pass.)(adya*)(api*)
body.translated_text: 2125. They would be produced [as cognitions] of a single word 'cow' — because of being cognitions of the word 'cow' — like a cow; or, the word 'cow' that was uttered yesterday also exists today, [as known] from a single cognition.

body.text:
2126.
(gamyatvāt, n. 5th s.)(jñāna-)(go-śabda-)(vat*)(śabda-)(uccārita-)(adya-)(ko'pi, m. 1st s.)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(gauḥ, m./f. 1st s. iti*)(śrūyamāṇaḥ ”śru Pass., m. 1st s.)(adya*)(śrutaḥ, m. 1st s.)(mayā, 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 2126. Because of being cognized — like a word 'cow' — like an uttered word; some word heard today as 'cow' — [the hearer says:] 'it was heard by me today.'

body.text:
2127.
(pūrva-uditāt, m. 5th s. eva*)(hetoḥ, m. 5th s.)(vat*)(śabda-)(uccārita-)(hyaḥ*)(vā*)(yāvān, m. 1st s.)(sthiraḥ, m. 1st s.)(vācakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(bhāk, m. 1st s.)(dīrgha-)(kāla-)
body.translated_text: 2127. Because of the very reason stated before — like an uttered word; or, that word which is stable [and] expressive, partaking of a long duration —

body.text:
2128.
(pravartanāt, n. 5th s.)(jñāna-)(jñeya-)(apekṣa- [bv. cpd.])(anubhava-)(sambandha-)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(īdṛk, m. 1st s.)(dṛṣṭaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sthiraḥ, m. 1st s.)(vat*)(sāmānya-)(bhāga-)(dhūma-)
body.translated_text: 2128. Because of the operation of [the relationship between] cognition and the object to be known — [and] the connection of experience requiring [both] — that which is seen as such, stable — like a part of the universal [nature] of smoke —

body.text:
2129.
(tu*)(avabodhakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(apekṣaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(jñāna-)(sambandha-)(na*)(a-sthiraḥ, m. 1st s.)(nimittatvāt, n. 5th s.)(tādātvika-)(vat*)(prakāśa-)(dīpa-)(vidyut-)
body.translated_text: 2129. But [what is merely] an illuminator, requiring the connection of cognition — [is] not stable; because of being a contemporaneous cause — like the light of a lamp or lightning.

body.text:
2130.
(ataḥ*)(pakṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(śabda-)(a-nityatva-)(virudhyate ”rudh Pass.)(sarvaiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(ebhiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(anumānaiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(siddhaiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(dṛḍhaiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(tataḥ*)(sthitāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(śabdāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(nityāḥ, m. 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 2130. Therefore, the thesis of the non-permanence of <s>śabda</s> (sound) is contradicted by all these [well-]established [and] firm inferences; therefore, sounds are permanent — [so] they stand.

body.text:
2131.
(ekatā-)(ghaṭa-)(ādi-)(āpattau, f. 7th s.)(iṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(jātyā, f. 3rd s.)(sādhanam, n. 1st s.)(siddha-)(cet*)(kuryāt ”kṛ VIII C. Opt.)(āpattim, f. 2nd s.)(vyaktīnām, f. 6th pl.)(ekatā-)(anayā, f. 3rd s.)(diśā, f. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 2131. [Objection:] 'In the occurrence of oneness with a pot and so forth, [is] the proof established by <s>jāti</s> (universal)?' If so, by this direction [of argument] one would bring about the oneness of individuals.

body.text:
2132.
(tathā*)(dṛṣṭa-)(viruddhatvam, n. 1st s.)(sarva-)(pramāṇakam, n. 1st s.)(vācyam, n. 1st s.)(yataḥ*)(bhedaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vyakti-)(su-)(niścitaḥ, m. 1st s.)(mānaiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(adhyakṣa-)(ādibhiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 2132. Likewise, the contradiction with what is observed is to be stated [as] supported by all means of knowledge; since the difference of individuals is well-ascertained by means of knowledge such as direct perception and the like.

body.text:
2133.
(ca*)(kṛtrimatve, n. 7th s.)(tat-)(prayoga-)(apavarjanāt, n. 5th s.)(sambandhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(niṣṭhatvāt, n. 5th s.)(tat-)(eka-)(vyakti-)(na*)(eva*)(sārvatrikaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2133. And in [the case of] artificiality — because of the exclusion of that [word's] usage — the relation, being fixed to a single individual, is not universal at all.

body.text:
2134.
(saṅkarāt, m. 5th s.)(pārthiva-)(dravya-)(sattva-)(lāṅgulatva)(ādi-)(avadhāraṇā, f. 1st s.)(gotva-)(vinā*)(bhūyastvam, n. 2nd s.)(prayoga-)
body.translated_text: 2134. Because of confusion — the ascertainment of <s>gotva</s> (cow-ness) without [the distinguishing features of] earthiness, substantiality, being, possession of a tail, and the like — [depends on] the preponderance of usage.

body.text:
2135.
(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(a-kṛtrimaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(kadācit*)(vinaśyati ”naś IV C.)(nitya-)(sambandhāt, m. 5th s.)(nityena, 3rd s.)(vat*)(ākāśa-)(parama-aṇu-)
body.translated_text: 2135. Therefore, <s>śabda</s> (sound) is uncreated [and] never perishes; because of the permanent connection — like <s>ākāśa</s> (space) [and] <s>paramāṇu</s> (ultimate atom) — with what is permanent.

body.text:
2136.
(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(go-)(śrutaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sakṛt*)(viṣayaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(an-eka-)(sāmānya-)(sammukha-)(na*)(prapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(sva-)(artha-vācitvam, n. 2nd s.)(niṣkṛṣṭam, n. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 2136. The word 'cow,' once heard, does not attain its pure denotative capacity [when it is] face-to-face with more than one universal as its object.

body.text: 2137-2138. --It (eṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pratipadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(niṣkṛṣṭa-)(vācitvam, n. 2nd s.)(gotva-)(cireṇa, m. 3rd s.)(bahubhiḥ, n. 3rd s.)(śravaṇaiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(varjayan ”vṛj Caus., m. 1st s.)(prāṇitva)(ādīni, n. 2nd pl.)(śukla-)(gamana-)(ādi, n. 2nd s.)(ca*)(sāsnā-lāṅgūlatā-)(ādi-)(vyaktīḥ, f. 2nd pl.)(śābaleya-)(ādi-)(akhaṇḍa-)(ādi-)(sva-)(sva-nibandhanāḥ, f. 2nd pl.)
body.translated_text: 2137-2138. It attains [its] pure denotative capacity for <s>gotva</s> (cow-ness) after a long time, through many hearings — excluding <s>prāṇitva</s> (animacy) and the like, whiteness, motion, and the like, [and] individuals such as <s>Śābaleya</s> (the spotted one) and the like — which are undivided [and] each having their own basis, such as dewlap-and-tail-ness and the like.

body.text:
2139.
(tāvat-kālam, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(sthiram, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(kaḥ, m. 1st s.)(nāśayiṣyati ”naś Caus. Fut.)(enam, m. 2nd s.)(paścāt*)(anyena, m. 3rd s.)(hetunā, m. 3rd s.)(na*)(sambhāvyate ”bhū Caus. Pass.)(asya, m. 6h s.)(nāśitvam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2139. Who will destroy it as stable for that duration? Afterwards, by another cause — the destructibility of this [sound] is not conceivable.

body.text:
2140.
(yathā*)(avagamyate ”gam Pass.)(iti*)(ghatā-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(naṅkṣyanti ”naś Fut. III p. pl.)(jarayā, f. 3rd s.)(vā*)(chedāt, m. 5th s.)(śastra-)(ādibhiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(asti ”as II C.)(na*)(evam*)(kāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(śabde, m. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 2140. As it is understood — pots and the like will perish by decay, or by cutting with weapons and the like; there is no such cause in [the case of] sound.

body.text:
2141.
(ca*)(api*)(bhede, m. 7th s.)(deśa-)(kāla-)(prayoktṝṇām, m. 6th pl.)(na*)(bhedavān, m. 1st s.)(varṇaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ga-)(ādi-)(yataḥ*)(pratyabhijñā, f. 1st s.)(tatra*)(parisphuṭā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2141. And moreover, even in the difference of place, time, and speakers — the phoneme 'ga' and the like is not differentiated; since recognition there is perfectly clear.

body.text:
2142.
Even (api*)(bhede, m. 7th s.)(vyaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(ga-)(niṣpannā, f. 1st s.)(sampratīyate ”i Pass.)(sphuṭā, f. 1st s.)(parā, f. 1st s.)(vicchinnā, f. 1st s.)(antara-)(vyakti-)(ga-)
body.translated_text: 2142. Even in [the case of] difference — the individual [instance of] 'ga' — [when] produced, is perceived as clear [and] supreme; [even when] interrupted by an intervening individual [instance of] 'ga' —

body.text:
2143.
(kāraḥ, m. 1st s.)(ga-)(na*)(vidyate ”vid Pass.)(niṣkṛṣṭa-)(ādhāraḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(gatva-)(a-nirūpyatvāt, n. 5th s.)(buddhi-)(anya-)(ga-)(vat*)(gatva-)(kalpita-)(anya-)
body.translated_text: 2143. The phoneme 'ga' does not exist [as a separate entity] — without a distinct substratum — because of the impossibility of determining <s>gatva</s> (ga-ness); like another [instance of] 'ga' imagined through <s>gatva</s>, like another [imagined through] cognition.

body.text:
2144.
(cāpi*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(sādhyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(varṇatvāt, n. 5th s.)(vat*)(kāra-)(kha-)(ādi)(ca*)(vyatirekasya, m. 6th s.)(na*)(dṛṣṭeḥ, f. 5th s.)(dṛṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(nivarttakam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2144. And moreover, this [ga-ness] is [itself] something to be established — because of being a phoneme — like the phoneme 'kha' and the like; and because the <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance) is not observed — the observed [evidence] is not a refuter.

body.text:
2145.
(tu*)(ātmā, m. 1st s.)(varṇa-)(siddhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(dvaya-)(ca*)(eva*)(yathā*)(nityatva-)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)(kalpitasya, 6th s.)(tat-vat*)(abhyupeyatām ”i Pass. Opt.)(siddhasya, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2145. But the self (<s>ātman</s>) is established through <s>varṇa</s> (phoneme) — and as to the two [properties], eternality and the like, which are accepted — let that which is established be accepted in the same way as that which is imagined.

body.text:
2146.
(tena, n. 3rd s.)(ekā, f. 1st s.)(buddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(upajāyate ”jan IV C. Āt.)(ekatvena, n. 3rd s.)(varṇasya, m. 6th s.)(sat-bhāvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(buddhi-)(viśeṣa-)(bhedataḥ* [-tas suff.])(vyañjaka-)
body.translated_text: 2146. By that [<s>varṇa</s>], a single cognition arises; the existence of the <s>varṇa</s> is [established] as one — [but] from the differentiation of particular cognitions, [there would need to be] a manifester (<s>vyañjaka</s>).

body.text:
2147.
(yasya, m. 1st s.)(dvayam, n. 1st s.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(dvayam, n. 1st s.)(buddhi-)(bhavataḥ, m. 6th s.)(tu*)(atīndriyatvāt, n. 5th s.)(katham*)(dhīḥ, f. 1st s.)(viśeṣa-)(nādaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 2147. For one who has two [properties], there would be two cognitions; but because of being beyond the senses (<s>atīndriya</s>), how could there be cognition through particular <s>nādas</s> (sound vibrations)?

body.text:
2148.
(kecit, m. 1st pl.)(pracakṣate ”cakṣ II C. Āt.)(yadā*)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pratīyate ”i Pass.)(śrotrāt, n. 5th s.)(saṃskṛtāt, n. 5th s.)(nādena, m. 3rd s.)(bodham, m. 2nd s.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(upaśleṣataḥ* [-tas suff.])(tat-)
body.translated_text: 2148. Some declare: when <s>śabda</s> (sound) is cognized from the ear that has been conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) by <s>nāda</s> (sound vibration), the apprehension of that [sound arises] from its contact with that [ear].

body.text:
2149.
(vā*)(na*)(grahaṇam, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(teṣām, m. 6th pl.)(tu*)(buddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(vaśāt, m. 5th s.)(tat-)(mahattva-)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(avabudhyate ”budh Pass.)(anukṛteḥ, f. 5th s.)(saṃskāra-)
body.translated_text: 2149. Or, there is no apprehension [of the eternal sound] at all; their cognition, however, [arises] from the force of [latent] impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) — magnitude and the like are apprehended through imitation (<s>anukṛti</s>).

body.text:
2150.
(yathā*)(cetasaḥ, m. 1st pl. [bv. cpd.])(bhrānta-)(doṣeṇa, m. 3rd s.)(pitta-)(gṛhṇanti ”grah IX C. III p. pl.)(madhuram, n. 2nd s.)(tikta-rūpeṇa, n. 3rd s.)(śvetam, n. 2nd s.)(pītatayā, f. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 2150. Just as those whose minds are deluded by the defect of bile (<s>pitta</s>) apprehend what is sweet as bitter in form, and what is white as yellow,

body.text:
2151.
(yathā*)(dhāvantaḥ ”dhāv I C., m. 1st pl.)(vegena, m. 3rd s. [adv.])(ca*)(ārūḍhāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(nau-)(bhrameṇa, m. 3rd s. [adv.])(prajānanti ”jñā IX C. III p. pl.)(parvata-)(ādīn, m. 2nd pl.)(gacchataḥ ”gam I C., m. 2nd pl.)(tān, m. 2nd pl.)(bhramataḥ ”bhram I C., m. 2nd pl.)
body.translated_text: 2151. Just as those running with speed, or those aboard [a boat] through the illusion of [its] motion, perceive mountains and the like as moving, as revolving,

body.text:
2152.
(akta-)(vasayā, f. 3rd s.)(maṇḍūka-)(akṣāḥ, m. 1st pl. [bv. cpd.])(vaṃśān, m. 2nd pl.)(buddhibhiḥ, f. 3rd pl.)(ura-ga-)(ca*)(mahattvābhyām, n. 3rd d.)(alpatva-)(vyakti-)(tat-)(āśrayam, m. 2nd s.).
body.translated_text: 2152. [Just as those with] frog-eyes [i.e., dice] anointed with grease [perceive] bamboo-stalks through [erroneous] cognitions as serpents — and [perceive] magnitude and smallness, manifestation, and their substrate.

body.text:
2153.
(yat-vat*)(gṛhṇanti ”grah IX C. III p. pl.)(etāni, n. 2nd pl.)(vinā*)(grahaṇāt, n. 5th s.)(nimitta-)(evam*)(ḥa-buddhvā* ”budh)(vyañjaka-stham, n. 2nd s.)(bhaviṣyati ”bhū Fut.)(bhrāntiḥ, f. 1st s.)(vyaṅgye, 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 2153. Just as they apprehend these without [any actual] apprehension of the cause — so too, having not [truly] cognized [the sound], there will be error (<s>bhrānti</s>) regarding what is manifested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) as residing in the manifester (<s>vyañjaka</s>).

body.text:
2154.
(tu*)(bhedaḥ, m. 1st s.)(hrasva-)(ādi-)(virudhyate ”rudh Pass.)(nityatva-)(ādeḥ, m. 6th s.)(katham*)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(yasya, m. 6th s.)(sat-bhāvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sarvadā*)(svayam*)(mātrikaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2154. But the difference of short [vowels] and the like contradicts eternality and the like; how can he whose existence is always self-measured (<s>mātrika</s>) [have such differences]?

body.text:
2155.
(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(uccāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(mātrā-)(kālam, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(vā*)(dvi-)(mātram, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(vā*)(tri-)(mātram, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(varṇaḥ, m. 1st s.)(svayam*)(na*)(mātrikaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2155. Therefore, [if] the pronunciation of that [<s>varṇa</s>] is of one <s>mātrā</s> (measure) duration, or of two <s>mātrās</s>, or of three <s>mātrās</s> — the <s>varṇa</s> itself is not self-measured.

body.text:
2156.
(nanu*)(abhivyaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(śabdasya, m. 6th s.)(nādaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(na*)(upapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(sā, f. 1st s.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(saṃskārāt, m. 5th s.)(śabda-)(indriyasya, n. 6th s.)(vā*)(ubhayasya, n. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2156. [The opponent says:] Surely, the manifestation (<s>abhivyakti</s>) of <s>śabda</s> (word) by <s>nādas</s> (sound vibrations) is not untenable; that [manifestation] would arise from the conditioning (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of the auditory organ (<s>śabdendriya</s>), or of both.

body.text:
2157.
(yadi*)(śabdaḥ)(saṃskriyate ”kṛ Pass.)(tataḥ*)(pratīyeta ”i Pass. Opt.)(sarvaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(nirbhāgasya, m. 6th s.)(vibhoḥ, m. 6th s.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(na*)(saṃskriyā, f. 1st s.)(eka-deśe, m. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 2157. If <s>śabda</s> (word) were conditioned, then it would be cognized by all; for [something] partless and all-pervading (<s>vibhu</s>), there can be no conditioning in one location.

body.text:
2158.
(na*)(ca*)(api*)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(niyamaḥ, m. 1st s.)(saṃskāra-)(bhedena, m. 3rd s.)(ādhāra-)(yataḥ*)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(nirādhāraḥ, m. 1st s.)(ca*)(eva*)(vat*)(vyoman-)(ātman-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 2158. Nor could there be a restriction [of conditioning] by difference of substrate (<s>ādhāra</s>), since <s>śabda</s> (word) is without substrate — like space (<s>vyoman</s>), the self (<s>ātman</s>), and the like.

body.text:
2159.
(api*)(atha*)(ākāśam, n. 1st s.)(ādhāraḥ, m. 1st s.)(tatra*)(sati ”as I C., n. 7th s.)(anavayave, n. 7th s.)(syāt ”as I C. Opt.)(na*)(saṃskāraḥ, m. 1st s.)(pradeśa-)(api*)(śabda-)(gateḥ, f. 5th s.)(kṛtsna-)
body.translated_text: 2159. Now, if space (<s>ākāśa</s>) is the substrate — [but] in that [space], which is without parts, there can be no conditioning of a location; also because of <s>śabda</s>'s pervading the entirety [of space].

body.text:
2160.
(hi*)(vyavasthitaḥ, m. 1st s.)(yāvat-)(vyoman-)(na*)(śakyate ”śak Pass.)(boddhum* ”budh)(sa-kalaḥ, m. 1st s.)(saṃskṛtaḥ, m. 1st s.)(eka-deśena, m. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 2160. Indeed, [<s>śabda</s>] is established as pervading all space; [so] it cannot be understood as conditioned in one location — [that is, as] a whole that has been conditioned by one part.

body.text:
2161.
(pakṣe, m. 7th s.)(śrotra-)(ākāśa-)(vibhutvāt, n. 5th s.)(tulyatā, f. 1st s.)(prāpti-)(iti*)(api*)(śabdānām, m. 6th pl.)(bhāve, m. 7th s.)(dūra-)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(prasajyeta ”sañj Pass.)
body.translated_text: 2161. In this position, because of the all-pervasiveness of the auditory organ and space, there would be the attainment of equality; also, cognition of distant <s>śabdas</s> (sounds) would absurdly follow when [sounds] exist.

body.text:
2162.
(evam*)(śrotrasya, n. 6th s.)(ca*)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(ekatvam, n. 1st s.)(sarva-)(prāṇa-bhṛtām, m. 6th pl.)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(velāyām, f. 7th s.)(eka-)(śruti-)(eva*)(sarve, m. 1st pl.)(te, m. 1st pl.)(śṛṇuyuḥ ”śru V C. Opt. III p. pl.)
body.translated_text: 2162. Likewise, the auditory organ of all living beings would be one; by that, at [any] time, all of them would hear with a single audition.

body.text:
2163.
(ca*)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(anavayavatvāt, n. 5th s.)(śrotram, n. 1st s.)(na*)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(deśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(nabhaḥ-)(saṃskṛtaḥ, m. 1st s.)(dharma-)(adharma-)(siddhaye, f. 4th s.)(dvaya-)(vyavasthā)
body.translated_text: 2163. And because of that [auditory organ's] partlessness, the ear would not have a [particular] location; [it would need to be] conditioned by space for the establishment of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> — [but] the arrangement of the two [is untenable].

body.text:
2164.
(ca*)(śrotram, n. 1st s.)(sakṛt*)(saṃskṛtam, n. 1st s.)(prabodhayet ”budh Caus. Opt.)(sarva-)(śabdān, m. 2nd pl.)(cakṣuḥ, n. 1st s.)(unmīlitam, n. 1st s.)(ghaṭāya, m. 4th s.)(na*)(na*)(buddhyate ”budh IV C. Āt.)(paṭam, m. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 2164. And [if] the ear, once conditioned, were to illuminate all sounds — [then] the eye, once opened, should not fail to cognize a cloth [as well as] a pot.

body.text:
2165.
(etat, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(prasaktavyam, n. 1st s.)(api*)(saṃsmṛtau, f. 7th s.)(viṣayasya, m. 6th s.)(saṃskārasya, m. 6th s.)(vṛttitvāt, n. 5th s.)(aviśeṣataḥ* [-tas suff.])(samāna-)(deśa-)
body.translated_text: 2165. This same [objection] is to be pressed also regarding memory (<s>saṃsmṛti</s>); because the impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) and the object occupy the same location, there being no difference [in their operation].

body.text:
2166.
(asya, m. 6th s.)(saṃskāraḥ, m. 1st s.)(bhavan ”bhū I C., m. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(upanītyā, f. 3rd s.)(sthira-)(vāyu-)(āvaraṇa-)(apāye, m. 7th s.)(upalambhanam, n. 1st s.)(stha-)(tat-)(deśa-)
body.translated_text: 2166. [If] the conditioning of this [ear] were to occur through the bringing [of the sound] — [but then] perception would arise at that very location when the obstruction of the steady air (<s>vāyu</s>) is removed.

body.text:
2167.
(śabda-)(ekatvena, n. 3rd s.)(na*)(siddhyataḥ ”sidh IV C. 3p d.)(saṃskṛta-)(asaṃskṛtatve, n. 1st d.)(ca*)(eka-)(avasthā-)(abhyupetau, f. 7th s.)(jñāyeta ”jñā Pass. Opt.)(sarvaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(vā*)(na*)
body.translated_text: 2167. Through the oneness of <s>śabda</s>, the [two states of] being conditioned and unconditioned are not [simultaneously] established; in the single state that is accepted, either all would know or none would.

body.text:
2168.
(doṣāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(abhihitāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(pratyeka-)(syuḥ ”as II C. Opt. III p. pl.)(saṃskṛtau, f. 7th s.)(api*)(dvayoḥ, n. 6th du)(ataḥ*)(na*)(kathañcit*)(api*)(vyañjakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(śabde, m. 7th s.).
body.translated_text: 2168. The faults that have been stated would apply to each [alternative] individually, even when both are conditioned; therefore, there is no manifester (<s>vyañjaka</s>) of <s>śabda</s> (sound) in any way whatsoever.

body.text:
2169.
(kāreṇa, m. 3rd s.)(bhāṣya-)(varṇitam, n. 1st s.)(uttaram, n. 1st s.)(saṃskārāt, m. 5th s.)(śrotra-)(ca*)(bhedaḥ, m. 1st s.)(śruti-)(vyavasthitaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pratiśrotṛ-)(bhedāt, m. 5th s.)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 2169. The reply set forth by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (commentator) [is]: the differentiation of hearing is established from the conditioning of the ear, [and] from the difference of each individual hearer.

body.text:
2170.
(yathā*)(dīpa-)(ādiḥ, m. 1st s.)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)(abhivyañjakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ghaṭasya, m. 6th s.)(eva*)(anugrahāt, m. 5th s.)(cakṣuṣaḥ, n. 6th s.)(dhvaniḥ, m. 1st s.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(saṃskṛteḥ, f. 5th s.)(śrotra-) --[ḥḥlokavārtika -- Eternality of Words, 42].
body.translated_text: 2170. Just as a lamp and the like are accepted as manifesters of a pot — likewise, by the grace of [conditioning] the auditory organ, <s>dhvani</s> (sound vibration) would arise from the conditioning of the ear — [thus says] the <s>Ślokavārttika</s> (Eternality of Words, 42).

body.text:
2171.
(na*)(ca*)(paryanuyogaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tatra*)(kena, m. 3rd s.)(prakāreṇa, m. 3rd s.)(saṃskṛtiḥ, f. 1st s.)(utpattau, f. 7th s.)(api*)(tatra*)(api*)(śaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(ati-indriyā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2171. But there is no objection there [to asking]: by what means does the conditioning arise? For even in [the theory of] origination, the capacity (<s>śakti</s>) [of causes] is beyond the senses.

body.text:
2172.
(kim*)(anuyujyate ”yuj Pass.)(śaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(nityam, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(anumeyā, f. 1st s)(kārya-)(pramāṇam, n. 1st s.)(tatra*)(gamyate ”gam Pass.)(bhāvitā-)(mātram, n. 1st s.)(bhāva-)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 2172. Why is [the question of] capacity objected to? The capacity is always to be inferred from [its] effect; the means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) there is the mere ripened state (<s>bhāvitā</s>) of the entity — [thus] it is understood.

body.text:
2173.
(ataḥ*)(ati-indriyayā, f. 3rd s.)(śaktyā, f. 3rd s.)(ete, m. 1st pl.)(ādadhānāḥ ”dhā III C. Āt., m. 1st pl.)(ati-indriyām, f. 2nd s.)(śaktim, f. 2nd s.)(indriyasya, n. 6th s.)(hi*)(sphuranti ”sphur I C. III p. pl.)(hetavaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(vyakti-)
body.translated_text: 2173. Therefore, these [<s>nādas</s>], possessing a supersensory capacity (<s>śakti</s>), bestow a supersensory capacity upon the sense organ; for the causes of manifestation (<s>vyakti</s>) indeed flash forth [their effects].

body.text:
2174.
(tu*)(yeṣām, m. 6th pl.)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(gṛhyate ”grah Pass.)(śrotreṇa, n. 3rd s.)(jātaḥ, m. 1st s.)(aprāptaḥ, m. 1st s.)(teṣām, m. 6th s.)(aprāpti-)(tulyatvāt, n. 5th s.)(dūra-)(vyavahita-)(ādiṣu, m. 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 2174. But for those [who hold that] <s>śabda</s> (sound) is apprehended by the ear [only when] it has arisen [and] has not reached [the ear] — for them, because of the equality of non-arrival, [there should be no cognition] in distant, obstructed, and other [cases].

body.text:
2175.
(grahaṇa-)(agrahaṇe, n. 1st d.)(tatra*)(stha-)(dūra-)(samīpa-)(syātām ”as II C. Opt. 3p d.)(same, n. 1st d.)(ca*)(na*)(kramaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na* api*)(tīvra-)(manda-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 2175. Apprehension and non-apprehension there of distant and nearby [objects] would be the same; and there would be no sequence, nor [any distinction of] intense, faint, and the like.

body.text:
2176.
(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(dṛṣṭyā, f. 3rd s.)(śrotriya-)(api*)(nirīkṣyatām ”īkṣ Pass. Opt.)(iyam, f. 1st s.)(kalpanā, f. 1st s.)(asaṃśayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(iti*)(vāyuḥ, m. 1st s.)(koṣṭhyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(abhihataḥ, m. 1st s.)(prayatna-)(yāti ”yā II C.)
body.translated_text: 2176. Therefore, let this contrivance (<s>kalpanā</s>) be examined from the perspective of the <s>Śrotriya</s> (Vedic ritualist) as well — [this is] without doubt. The air (<s>vāyu</s>) in the chest, struck by effort, moves forth,

body.text:
2177.
(ca*)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(anurudhyate ”rudh IV C. Āt.)(saṃyoga-)(vibhāgau, m. 2nd d.)(tālu-)(ādeḥ, m. 6th or 5th s.)(vegavattvāt, n. 5th s.)(avaśyam*)(pratiṣṭhate ”sthā I C. Āt.)(yāvat-vegam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])
body.translated_text: 2177. And it conforms to the conjunction and disjunction of the palate and the like; because of possessing velocity, it necessarily persists as long as [its] momentum [lasts].

body.text:
2178.
(dhruvam, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(gamanāt, n. 5th s.)(ātman-)(avayavānām, m. 6th pl.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(jāyate ”jan IV C. Āt. III p. pl.)(saṃyogāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(viprayogāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(stimitena, m. 3rd s.)(vāyunā, m. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 2178. Because of the definite movement of its own parts, conjunctions and disjunctions arise for that [air] with the still air (<s>vāyu</s>).

body.text:
2179.
(samprāptaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vyomani, n. 7th s.)(karṇa-)(niyacchati ”yam I. Cl.)(śaktim, f. 2nd s.)(śrotre, n. 7th s.)(ca*)(bodhāt, m. 5th s.)(śabda-)(tat-)(bhāve, m. 7th s.)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)(adṛṣṭaḥ, m. 1st s.)(saṃskāraḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2179. Having arrived in space, [the air] restrains [its] capacity in the ear; and from the cognition of <s>śabda</s> (sound) in that condition, an unseen (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) conditioning (<s>saṃskāra</s>) is postulated.

body.text:
2180.
(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(api*)(vat*)(śakti-)(utpatti-)(iti*)(naḥ, 6th pl.)(na*)(kiñcana, n. 1st s.)(adhikam, n. 1st s)(eva*)(tathā*)(tat-)(viśeṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(api*)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(viśeṣa-)(grahaṇāt, n. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 2180. That [conditioning] too, like the capacity, [has] origination — thus for us there is nothing additional [to explain]; likewise, there would be a particular [conditioning], because of the apprehension of [specific] distinctions.

body.text:
2181.
(api*)(pratibandhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kuḍya-)(yujyate ”yuj Pass.)(mātariśvanaḥ, m. 6th s.)(api*)(abhighātaḥ, m. 1st s.)(śrotra-deśa-)(tīvra-pravṛttinā, m. 3rd s. [bv. cpd.])(tena, m. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 2181. Also, the obstruction [of sound] by a wall is justified [in our view]; also, the impact upon the region of the ear by that [air] possessing intense motion [explains why the Mīmāṃsā view fails].

body.text:
2182.
(ca*)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(vṛttitvāt, n. 5th s.)(krama-)(kṣayi-)(sampadaḥ, m. 6th s. [bv. cpd.])(nimittatā, f. 1st s.)(krama-)(tīvratva-)(mandatā-)(saṃskāra-)
body.translated_text: 2182. And because of the successive operation of that [consciousness], which is of a perishing nature — the causality of the dispositions (<s>saṃskāras</s>) [is determined] by the intensity and weakness of the succession.

body.text:
2183.
(asmābhiḥ, 3rd pl.)(ca*)(na*)(avaśyam*)(abhyupeyate ”i Pass.)(śrotram, n. 1st s.)(ākāśam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(ca*)(vyoma, n. 1st s.)(anavayavam, n. 1st s.)(niṣedhataḥ* [-tas suff.])(jaina-)(sāṅkhya-)
body.translated_text: 2183. And by us, the organ of hearing is not necessarily accepted as space (<s>ākāśa</s>); nor is space without parts — from the negation by the <s>Jainas</s> and <s>Sāṅkhyas</s>.

body.text:
2184.
(tena, n. 3rd s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(śrotram, n. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(vā*)(eka-deśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ākāśa-)(yat-vā*)(antaram, n. 1st s.)(vastu-)(prati-naram*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(gamyam, n. 1st s.)(artha-āpatti-)(kārya-)
body.translated_text: 2184. Therefore, that organ of hearing would either be a portion of space, or rather an internal reality — apprehensible per individual person through inference from effects (<s>arthāpatti</s>).

body.text:
2185.
(api*)(yadi*)(ca*)(vyāpi, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(ekam, n. 1st s.)(tu*)(api*)(tathā*)(saṃskṛtiḥ, f. 1st s.)(dhvani-)(adhiṣṭhāne, n. 7th s.)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(pratipadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(śabdam, m. 2nd s.)(yasya, m. 6th s.)(sā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2185. Even if [space] is all-pervading and one — even so, the modification (<s>saṃskṛti</s>) [produced] by sound [occurs only] at the location [of sound]; he in whom that [modification occurs] apprehends the sound.

body.text:
2186.
(api*)(atha*)(saṃskāraḥ, m. 1st s.)(indriya-)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(api*)(deśataḥ* [-tas suff.])(adhiṣṭhāna-)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(śrotram, n. 1st s.)(śuṣkuli, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(asaṃskṛta-)(na*)(śroṣyati ”śru Fut.)(śabdam, m. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 2186. Now, if [you say] the modification is of the sense organ — that [modification] too [is limited] by the location of the [sound's] substrate; therefore, the ear-canal (<s>śuṣkuli</s>), [being] unmodified [by distant sound], will not hear the sound.

body.text:
2187.
(na*)(saṃskriyā, f. 1st s.)(śrotra-)(dhvaneḥ, m. 6th s.)(aprāpta-)(deśatvāt, n. 5th s.)(karṇa-)(ataḥ*)(niyamaḥ, m. 1st s.)(saṃskāra-)(sthitaḥ, m. 1st s.)(bhedena, m. 3rd s.)(adhiṣṭhāna-)
body.translated_text: 2187. The modification of the organ of hearing [does not occur from sound] that has not reached the location of the ear; therefore, the restriction [of hearing] is established by the distinction of the [sound's] substrate through modification.

body.text:
2188.
(nanu*)(labdha-)(saṃskāram, n. 1st s. -bv. cpd.)(ekasmin, n. 7th s.)(adhiṣṭhāne, n. 7th s.)(indriyam, n. 1st s.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(bodhakam, n. 1st s.)(sarva-)(deheṣu, m. 7th pl.)(vādinaḥ, m. 6th s.)(indriya-)(eka-)
body.translated_text: 2188. But surely, when the sense organ has received modification at a single substrate — [the proponent of] a single sense organ [for all beings] would [have to say] it would be a cognizer in all bodies.

body.text:
2189.
(utpattiḥ, f. 1st s.)(vijñāna-)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)(deha-pradeśeṣu, m. 7th pl.)(puṃsām, m. 6th pl.)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(pradhāna-)(vaideśyāt, n. 5th s.)(saṃskṛtiḥ, f. 1st s.)(śrotra-)(viguṇā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2189. The arising of consciousness is accepted [as occurring only] in the bodily regions of persons; therefore, because the principal [consciousness is] elsewhere [than where the modification occurs], the modification of the organ of hearing is defective.

body.text:
2190.
(ca*)(api*)(naḥ, 6th pl.)(ātmā, m. 1st s.)(niṣpradeśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ca*)(api*)(vidan ”vid II C., m. 1st s.)(kārtsnyena, n. 3rd s.)(gṛhṇāti ”grah IX C.)(śarīre, n. 7th s.)(eva*)(iti*)(evam-)(uktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(na*)(duṣyati ”duṣ IV C.)
body.translated_text: 2190. And even [if you say] that our self (<s>ātman</s>) is without spatial location, and [that] even so, it knows [and] grasps [objects] entirely within the body alone — such a statement is not faulty.

body.text:
2191.
--And( ca*)(etena, m. 3rd s.)(eva*)(hetunā, m. 3rd s.)(bādhirya-)(ādi-)(vyavasthānam, n. 1st s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(anyasya, m. 6th s.)(abhogyam, n. 1st s.)(avaśīkṛtam, n. 1st s.)(dharma-)(adharma-)
body.translated_text: 2191. And by this very reason, the arrangement of deafness and the like [is explained]; that [sense experience of one person] is not to be enjoyed by another — [it is] controlled by <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit).

body.text:
2192.
(yathā*)(avaropitaḥ, m. 1st s.)(svāmitvāt, n. 5th s.)(eva*)(bhavan ”bhū I C., m. 1st s.)(tatra*)(na*)(labhate ”labh I C. Āt.)(bhogam, m. 2nd s.)(tat-vat*)(badhiraḥ, m. 1st s.)(anyatra*)(śṛṇvati ”śru V C., m. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 2192. Just as one who has been displaced, by virtue of [another's] ownership alone, does not obtain enjoyment there — so too a deaf person, [does not hear] when another [person nearby] hears.

body.text:
2193.
(ca*)(śrotra-)(śabda-)(āśrayāṇām, m. 6th pl.)(svayam*)(nāma*)(na*)(avayavāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(ca*)(na*)(vṛttitvam, n. 1st s.)(eka-)(deśa-)(api*)(tathā*)(etat, n. 1st s.)(na*)(duṣyati ”duṣ IV C.)
body.translated_text: 2193. And [we say:] the parts of the substrates of sound and the organ of hearing are not themselves [identical]; and the occurrence of [hearing] in a single portion [of space] — even so, this is not faulty.

body.text:
2194.
(hi*)(vāyūnām, m. 6th pl.)(vyañjakānām, m. 6th pl.)(avayava-)(bhinna-)(deśatā, f. 1st s.)(ca*)(bhedaḥ, m. 1st s.)(jāti-)(evam*)(tena, 3rd s.)(saṃskāraḥ, m. 1st s.)(vyavatiṣṭhate ”sthā I C. Āt.)
body.translated_text: 2194. For the winds that manifest [sound] have [their] parts in different locations; and likewise, the distinction of the type [of sound] — by that [distinction], the modification is established.

body.text:
2195.
(yathā*)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(vāyuḥ, m. 1st s.)(preritaḥ, m. 1st s.)(artham, m. 2nd s.)(anya-)(na*)(karoti ”kṛ VIII C.)(tathā*)(śaktaḥ, m. 1st s.)(saṃskāra-)(anya-)(varṇa-)(na*)(kariṣyati ”kṛ Fut.)(anyam, m. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 2195. Just as the wind that has been impelled does not produce a different object, so too the modification by one phoneme (<s>varṇa</s>) will not produce another [phoneme].

body.text:
2196.
(yathā*)(anyaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(saṃyogaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(tālu-)(ādi-)(varṇaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(anyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tathā*)(sāribhiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(antara-)(dhvani-)(na*)(kṣepaḥ, m. 1st s.)(antara-)(dhvani-)
body.translated_text: 2196. Just as a phoneme is not [produced as] another through other conjunctions [of articulatory organs] such as the palate and the like — so too, another sound is not [produced] by the intermediate sounds, [nor is there] displacement of the intermediate sound.

body.text:
2197.
(tasmāt, m. 5th s.)(utpatti-)(abhivyaktibhyām, f. 3rd d.)(bhedaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sāmarthya-)(artha-āpattitaḥ* [-tas suff.])(kārya-)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(samaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sarvatra*)(prayatna-)(vivakṣayoḥ, f. 7th d.)
body.translated_text: 2197. Therefore, from origination and manifestation — through the difference of capacity — the inference from effects (<s>kārya-arthāpatti</s>) would be equal everywhere with respect to effort and the desire to express.

body.text:
2198.
(yat-vā*)(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(kāryā, f. 1st s.)(śrotratā-)(diś-)(anusāreṇa, m. 3rd s.)(veda-)(hi*)(na*)(kathañcana*)(vede, m. 7th s.)(uktam, n. 1st s.)(ātmakam, n. 1st s.)(ākāśa-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 2198. Or rather, the cognition [that] the organ of hearing is of the nature of direction (<s>diś</s>) is to be produced — for in no way is [the statement that it is] of the nature of space and the like stated in the <s>Veda</s>.

body.text:
2199.
(hi*)(pralayeṣu, m. 7th pl.)(etat, n. 1st s.)(abhidhīyate ”dhā Pass.)(iti*)(śrotram, n. 1st s.)(diśaḥ, f. 2nd pl.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(vacanam, n. 1st s.)(vat*)(cakṣuḥ-)(ādi-)(gāmitva-)(prakṛti-)
body.translated_text: 2199. For in the [cosmic] dissolutions, this is stated: 'the organ of hearing [returns] to the directions' — that statement is like [the statement that] the nature of the eye and the like is [to go toward] its source [light].

body.text:
2200.
(yathā*)(uktam, n. 1st s.)(asya, m. 6th s.)(cakṣuḥ, n. 1st s.)(gamayatāt ”gam Caus. Imperative 3p s.)(sūryam)(iti*)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(prakṛti-)(tejaḥ-)(tathā*)(śrotram, n. 1st s.)(ātmakam, n. 1st s.)(diś-)
body.translated_text: 2200. Just as it is said, 'let his eye lead [him] to the sun' — the consciousness whose nature is light — so too the organ of hearing is of the nature of direction (<s>diś</s>).

body.text:
2201.
(ca*)(dik, f. 1st s.)(ekā, f. 1st s.)(eva*)(sarva-gatā, f. 1st s.)(vyavasthitā, f. 1st s.)(yāvat)(vyoma, n. 2nd s.)(parichinnā, f. 1st s.)(randhra-)(karṇa-)(śrotram, n. 1st s.)(vat*)(deśa-)(ākāśa-)
body.translated_text: 2201. And direction is one, all-pervading, and established [everywhere]; as far as space [extends], it is delimited [only when associated with] the ear-canal — [in this capacity it serves as] the organ of hearing, like a local [portion of] space.

body.text:
2202.
(ca*)(yāvān, m. 1st s.)(kaścana, m. 1st s.)(nyāyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kalpane, n. 7th s.)(bhāga-)(nabhaḥ-)(asau, m. 1st s.)(samaḥ, m. 1st s.)(api* ca*)(bhāge, m. 7th s.)(diś-)(tu*)(viśiṣyate ”śiṣ Pass.)(āgamāt, m. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 2202. And whatever reasoning [there is] in the postulation of a portion of space — that is equal [in the case of direction] too, regarding a portion; but direction is distinguished [from space] by scriptural authority (<s>āgama</s>).

body.text:
2203.
(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(śrotram, n. 1st s.)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(bhāgaḥ, m. 1st s.)(dravya-)(diś-)(vaśīkṛtaḥ, m. 1st s.)(puṇya-)(apuṇya-)(parichinnaḥ, m. 1st s.)(randhra-)(karṇa-)(ca*)(saṃskriyate ”kṛ Pass.)
body.translated_text: 2203. Therefore, the organ of hearing is that portion of the directional substance (<s>diś-dravya</s>), delimited by the ear-canal, controlled by merit (<s>puṇya</s>) and demerit (<s>apuṇya</s>), and is modified [by sound].

body.text:
2204.
(api*)(saṃskāre, m. 7th s.)(viṣayasya, m. 6th s.)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(saṃskṛtiḥ, f. 1st s.)(ekasya, m. 6th s.)(eva*)(ca*)(bhedāt, m. 5th s.)(sāmarthya-)(na*)(avagamyate ”gam Pass.)(sarvaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 2204. Even when the object receives modification, the modification of a single [organ of hearing] by that [sound] — because of the difference of capacity — is not apprehended by all.

body.text:
2205.
(eva*)(yathā*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(utpadyamānaḥ, ”pad IV C. Āt., m. 1st s.)(api*)(bhavan ”bhū I C., m. 1st s.)(prati*)(sarvān, m. 2nd pl.)(na*)(avagamyate, ”gam Pass.)(sarvaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(vibhāgena, m. 3rd s.)(diś-)(deśa-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 2205. Just as this [sun], even while arising, does not become apprehended by all — in all [locations] — by the division of direction, place, and the like,

body.text: 2206. ... --in just (eva*)(tathā*)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(śrūyate ”śru Pass.)(eva*)(tena, m. 3rd s.)(yasya, m. 6th s.)(saṃskṛtiḥ, f. 1st s.)(samīpa-sthaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(nādaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(na*)(kathañcana*)(dūra-sthaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 2206. So too, sound is heard only by him whose [organ of hearing] receives modification from sounds that are nearby — [and] in no way from those that are far away.

body.text:
2207.
(utpatteḥ, f. 6th s.)(śabda-)(niṣiddhatvāt, n. 5th s.)(anupapatteḥ, f. 5th s.)(anyathā*)(dhvanibhyaḥ, m. 5th pl.)(janma, n. 1st s.)(viśiṣṭa-)(saṃskṛteḥ, f. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2207. Because the origination of sound [from ultimate atoms] has been refuted, and because it is otherwise untenable — the birth [of sound is] from [preceding] sounds, of a particular modification.

body.text:
2208.
(ca*)(atra*)(bhāvitā, f. 1st s.)(bhāva-)(tat-)(avabodhinī, f. 1st s.)(astitva-)(śakti-)(vat*)(śakti-)(śrotra-)(tatra*)(hi*)(buddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(iṣtā, f. 1st s.)(saṃhṛtā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2208. And here, the disposition that cognizes the nature of that [sound's] existence — [is] the capacity of the organ of hearing, like the capacity of existence; for [this] cognition is accepted as withdrawn [when the organ is impaired].

body.text:
2209.
(tu*)(pakṣe, m. 7th s.)(dvaya-)(saṃskāra-)(tat, n. 1st s.)(hi*)(dvayam, n. 1st s.)(doṣa-)(vṛthā*)(yena, n. 3rd s.)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(gamyate ”gam Pass.)(sarvaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(vaikalyāt, n. 5th s.)(anyatara-)
body.translated_text: 2209. But in the thesis of a twofold modification — that twofold [modification] is indeed a superfluous fault; by which [thesis], sound is not apprehended by all — because of the deficiency of one or the other [modification].

body.text:
2210.
(yathā*)(savitā, m. 1st s.)(api*)(ekaḥ, m. 1st s.)(īkṣyate ”īkṣ Pass.)(nānā-)(ātmā, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(jala-)(ādiṣu, m. 7th pl.)(yujapat*)(ca*)(na*)(asya, m. 6th s.)(bhedaḥ, m. 1st s.)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(api*)(tathā*)(gamyatām ”gam Pass. Imperative)
body.translated_text: 2210. Just as the sun, though one, is perceived as having manifold forms in water and the like simultaneously — and yet there is no [real] division of it — let sound too be understood thus.

body.text:
2211.
(hi*)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(gṛhyate ”grah Pass.)(tat-)(deśe, m. 7th s.)(adhīnatvāt, n. 5th s.)(dhvani-)(vyañjaka-)(ca*)(dhvanīnām, m. 6th pl.)(na*)(sāmarthyam, n. 1st s.)(vyāptum* ”āp)(nirantaram, n. 2nd s.)(vyoma, n. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 2211. For that [sound] is apprehended at the location of the manifesting sounds — because of [its apprehension] being dependent on the manifesting [winds]; and the sounds do not have the capacity to pervade space continuously.

body.text:
2212.
(tena, n. 3rd s.)(asau, m. 1st s.)(gamyate ”gam Pass.)(avicchinna-rūpeṇa, n. 3rd s.)(sarvatra*)(dhvanīnām, m. 6th pl.)(bhinna-)(deśatvāt, n. 5th s.)(śrutiḥ, f. 1st s.)(avarudhyate ”rudh Pass.)(tatra*)
body.translated_text: 2212. Therefore, that [sound] is apprehended everywhere in an unbroken form by [the manifesting] sounds; [but] because the sounds are in different locations, hearing is restricted there.

body.text:
2213.
(ca*)(antarālatvāt, n. 5th s.)(apūrita-)(avasīyate ”so Pass.)(vicchedaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ca*)(alpaka-)(deśatvāt, n. 5th s.)(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(śabde, m. 7th s.)(api*)(avibhutā-)
body.translated_text: 2213. And because of [the sound] being in an intermediate [location that is] unfilled, a break [in hearing] is ascertained; and because of [the manifesting sounds being in] a small [nearby] location, the cognition of [even a small] sound is also [possible, though] not fully manifest.

body.text:
2214.
(ca*)(gati-mat-)(vega-vattvābhyām, n. 3rd d.)(yataḥ* yataḥ*)(te, m. 1st pl.)(āyānti ”yā II C. III p. pl.)(śrotā, m. 1st s.)(manyate ”man IV C. Āt.)(śabdam, m. 2nd s.)(iva*)(āyāntam ”yā II C., m. 2nd s.)(tataḥ*)(tataḥ*)
body.translated_text: 2214. And because [the manifesting sounds] possess motion and velocity — from whichever direction they come — the hearer thinks the sound is as if coming from that direction.

body.text:
2215.
(āha ”ah Perf.)(kena, n. 3rd s.)(nimittena, n. 3rd s.)(bhinnāni, n. 1st pl.)(pratibimbāni, n. 1st pl.)(gṛhyante ”grah Pass. III p. pl.)(yugapattayā, f. 3rd s.)(pṛthak*)(pṛthak*)
body.translated_text: 2215. [Objection:] it has been said — for what reason are the separate reflections apprehended simultaneously, each distinctly?

body.text:
2216.
(brūmaḥ ”brū II C. 1p pl.)(atra*)(yadā*)(tāvat*)(tejaḥ, n. 1st s.)(cākṣuṣam, n. 1st s.)(pravarttitam, n. 1st s.)(pratisrotraḥ*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(tejasā, n. 3rd s.)(saurena, n. 3rd s.)(sphuratā ”sphur, n. 3rd s.)(jale, n. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 2216. We reply: here, when the visual radiance has been activated [and] the solar radiance is pulsating in the water,

body.text:
2217.
(gṛhṇāti ”grah IX C.)(savitāram, m. 2nd s.)(eva*)(sva-)(deśam, m. 2nd s.)(aneka-dhā*)(bhinna-)(mūrtiḥ, m. 1st s. - bv. cpd)(yathā-pātram*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(kutaḥ*)(tadā*)(anekatā, f. 1st s.)(asya, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2217. [The eye] apprehends the sun alone [as] its own object — [appearing] in multiple forms, variously in each vessel; whence then is there multiplicity of that [sun]?

body.text:
2218.
(yathā*)(api*)(ekaḥ, m. 1st s.)(gṛhyate ”grah Pass.)(pṛthak*)(īṣat-)(sammīlite, n.)(aṅgulyā, f. 3rd s.)(bhinnatvāt, n. 5th s.)(vṛtteḥ, f. 5th s.)(cakṣuḥ-)(eva*)(tathā*)(naḥ, 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 2218. Just as one [moon] is apprehended as separate [when seen] through a slightly closed [eye], by pressing with a finger — because of the difference of the visual operation — so too for us.

body.text:
2219.
(tu*)(anye, m. 1st pl.)(eṣiṇaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(pratibimba-)(udaya-)(codayanti ”cud Caus. III p. pl.)(atra*)(cet*)(eva*)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(pratīyeta ”i Pass. Opt.)(kasmāt, n. 5th s.)(na*)(dṛśyate ”dṛs Pass.)(upari*)
body.translated_text: 2219. But other seekers of the reflection-theory raise an objection here: if that very [sun] is cognized [in the reflection], why is it not seen above [in the sky as well]?

body.text:
2220.
(kutaḥ*)(īkṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(adhastāt*)(kūpa-)(ādiṣu, m. 7th pl.)(vinā*)(pratibimbāt, n. 5th s.)(katham*)(mukhaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(prāñc-)(paśyan ”dṛś VI C.,m. 1st s.)(darpaṇam, n. 2nd s.)(ca*)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(mukhaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(pratyañc-)
body.translated_text: 2220. Whence [comes] the seeing downward in wells and the like? Without a reflection, how could one looking forward with face [directed forward] — [and looking into] a mirror — be [simultaneously seeing as if] facing backward?

body.text:
2221.
(ap-)(sūrya-)(darśinām, m. 6th s.)(nityam, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(dvedhā*)(cakṣuḥ, n. 1st s.)(pravartate ”vṛt I C. Āt.)(ekam, n. 1st s.)(ūrdhvam*)(adhastāt*)(ca*)(tatra)(ūrdhva-)(aṃśu-)(prakāśitam, m. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 2221. For those who see the sun in water, the eye always operates in two directions: one [direction] upward and one downward; there, the [sun's image] illuminated by the upward rays —

body.text:
2222.
(adhiṣṭhāna-)(an-ṛjusthatvāt, n. 5th s.)(na*)(ātmā, m. 1st s.)(sūryam, m. 2nd s.)(prapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(pāramparya-)(arpitam, m. 2nd s.)(santam, m. 2nd s. [”as II C.])(avabudhyate ”budh IV C. Āt.)(avāñc-)(vṛttyā, f. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 2222. Because the substrate is not in a straight line — the self does not reach the sun; [rather, it] apprehends [the sun] as transmitted indirectly, through a downward operation.

body.text:
2223.
(ūrdhva-)(vṛttim, m. 2nd s. [bv. cpd.])(ekatvāt, n. 5th s.)(avāk*)(iva*)(ca*)(manyate ”man IV C. Āt.)(adhastāt*)(eva*)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(arkaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sa-antarālaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(pratīyate; prati-”i pass. Pr. III p. s.)
Textual variant [GOS]: (sūryam, m. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 2223. Because of the oneness [of the visual faculty] — having an upward operation — [the perceiver] thinks [of it] as if downward; therefore, the sun with an interval is perceived as being below alone.

body.text:
2224.
(evam*)(bhrāntyā, f. 3rd s.)(avagacchati ”gam I C.)(mukham, n. 2nd s.)(iti*)(pratyak*)(buddhyamānaḥ ”budh IV. C. Āt., m. 1st s.)(samarpitam, n. 2nd s.)(vṛttyā, f. 3rd s.)(natayā, f. 3rd s.)(prāñc-)(vṛtti-)(pratyañc-)
body.translated_text: 2224. Thus, through error one apprehends the face [in the mirror]; [the perceiver,] understanding [it as] directly [present, but in fact] presented through a bent operation — [the face being perceived] forward through a backward operation —

body.text:
2225.
(vā*)(api*)(pratibimbake, n. 7th s.)(sati ”as II C., n. 7th s.)(vṛttau, m. 7th s. [bv. cpd.])(aneka-)(deśa-)(vidyate ”vid Pass.)(na*)(nānātvam, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(gamyatvāt, n. 5th s.)(samāna-)(buddhi-)
body.translated_text: 2225. Or, even when a reflection exists, [and] the operation is in many directions — there is no multiplicity; because of being cognized as a single cognition.

body.text:
2226.
(ca*)(etat, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(bhinnatvam, n. 1st s.)(bhedena, m. 3rd s.)(deśa-)(ānumānikam, n. 1st s.)(tu*)(pratyayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(iti*)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(eva*)(pratyakṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(bādhakaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2226. And this — the differentness [inferred] from the difference of location is inferential; but the cognition [of unity] is perceptual — therefore, that [perceptual cognition] alone is the refuter.

body.text:
2227.
(ca*)(yathā*)(ekaḥ, m. 1st s.)(devadattaḥ, m. 1st s.)(api*)(vrajan ”vraj I C., m. 1st s.)(bhinna-)(deśān, m. 2nd pl.)(paryāyeṇa, m. 3rd s.)(na*)(bhidyate ”bhid Pass.)(tathā*)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(bhidyate ”bhid Pass.)
body.translated_text: 2227. And just as a single <s>Devadatta</s>, even [while] traveling to different places in succession, is not differentiated — so too, <s>śabda</s> (sound) is not differentiated.

body.text:
2228.
(ca*)(yathā*)(ekaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ekatvaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(jñāta-)(dṛśyamānaḥ, m. 1st s.)(punaḥ*)(punaḥ*)(na*)(bhinnaḥ, m. 1st s.)(bhedena, m. 3rd s.)(kāla-)(tathā*)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(deśataḥ)
body.translated_text: 2228. And just as a single [entity] that is one, [when] seen again and again as known, is not differentiated by the difference of time — so too, <s>śabda</s> (sound) [is not differentiated] by place.

body.text:
2229.
(cet*)(avirodhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(paryāyāt, m. 5th s.)(dṛśyatām ”dṛś Pass.)(api*)(vyāpitvāt, n. 5th s.)(hi*)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(dharmaḥ, m. 1st s.)(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(siddhyai, f. 4th s.)(dṛṣṭa-)(abhyupeyate ”i Pass.)(sarveṣām, 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 2229. [Objection:] 'If there is no contradiction because of [the sound being present] in succession — let it be observed: because of [its] pervasiveness, that <s>dharma</s> (property) which is adduced for the establishment of all [positions] —'

body.text:
2230.
(mṛdi, f. 7th s.)(khātāyām, f. 7th s.)(dhīḥ, f. 1st s.)(vyomni, n. 7th s.)(mahattva-)(vā*)(alpāyām, f. 7th s.)(dhīḥ, f. 1st s.)(alpa-)(evam*)(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(atyanta-)(akṛtake, m. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 2230. [Just as] in [the case of] earth that has been dug — the cognition [is directed at] space; or in a small [amount of earth] — the cognition of smallness — so too, the cognition [of space as small or large is] in what is utterly uncreated.

body.text:
2231.
(tena, n. 3rd s.)(evam*)(atra*)(bhramaḥ, m. 1st s.)(mati-)(vṛttau, f. 7th s.)(śabda-)(para-)(upādhi-)(ca*)(sthūlatva-)(sūkṣmatve, n. 1st d.)(na*)(lakṣyete ”lakṣ Pass. 3p d.)(vartinī, n. 1st d.)(śabda-)
body.translated_text: 2231. Therefore, thus there is error in cognition; in the operation of <s>śabda</s> (sound) — and the extrinsic limiting condition — grossness and subtlety, which abide in <s>śabda</s>, are not perceived.

body.text:
2232.
(kalpanā, f. 1st s.)(mahattva-)(alpatva-)(tīvratva-)(mandatve, n. 7th s.)(buddhi-)(ca*)(sarvadā*)(sā, f. 1st s.)(bhavati ”bhū I C.)(eva*)(paṭvī, f. 1st s.)(ghaṭa-)(ādau, m. 7th s.)(api*)(prakāśite, m. 7th s.)(mahā-)(tejaḥ-)(mandā, f. 1st s.)(prakāśite, m. 7th s.)(manda-)(evam*)(dīrgha-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(sarve, m. 1st pl.)(dharmāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(dhvani-)
body.translated_text: 2232-2233. The conceptual construction of magnitude, smallness, intensity, and faintness — the cognition [of these] is always sharp; even when a pot and the like are illuminated — [when illuminated] by a great light, [it is] faint [when illuminated] by a faint [light] — thus, all properties such as length and the like are [merely qualities of] <s>dhvani</s> (sound vibration).

body.text:
2234.
(na*)(ca*)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sambandhaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(artha-)(dṛṣṭa-)(bhavati ”bhū I C.)(vācakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(cet*)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(tathā*)(sarvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(api*)(apūrvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(prabodhayet ”budh Caus. Opt.)(sva-)(artham, m. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 2234. And <s>śabda</s> (sound) that has a connection with the object — is not observed to be a denoter; if [it were a denoter by nature], then every novel [sound] too would inform [one] of its own meaning.

body.text:
2235.
(darśanam, n. 1st s.)(sambandha-)(na*)(upapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(anityasya, m. 6th s.)(asya, m. 6th s.)(cet*)(jñāna-)(sambandha-)(siddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(dhruvam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(sthitiḥ, f. 1st s.)(antara-)(kāla-)
body.translated_text: 2235. The perception of the connection is not tenable for what is impermanent; if [the word-meaning connection is established through] the cognition of the connection — then certainly, stability [is established]; [there must be] an intermediate duration.

body.text:
2236.
(ca*)(na*)(anyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(bodhakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sambandhe, m. 7th s.)(jñāta-)(anyasmin, m. 7th s.)(hi*)(sambandhe, m. 7th s.)(jñāta-)(śabde, m. 7th s.)(go-)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(aśva-)(na*)(vācakaḥ)
body.translated_text: 2236. And no other [word] would be an informer; for when one connection is known — in another connection that is known — the word 'cow' is not a denoter of 'horse.'

body.text:
2237.
(atha*)(kaścit, m. 1st s.)(eva*)(anyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(api*)(avabodhakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sva-)(bhāvena, m. 3rd s.)(tatra*)(anibandhane, n. 7th s.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(na*)(viniścayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(iti*)(kaḥ, m. 1st s.)(asau, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2237. Now, if some other [word] too is an informer by its own nature — in that which has no [established] connection — there would be no certainty [of meaning]; who, then, is that [informer]?

body.text:
2238.
(vyavahāre, m. 7th s.)(prakalpite, m. 7th s.)(iti*)(yataḥ*)(pratyayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(api*)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(śrotṝṇām, m. 6th pl.)(tu*)(na*)(avakalpate ”kḷp I C. Āt.)(ittham*)(vaktṝṇām, m. 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 2238. Since, even when convention has been established — there might be a cognition [of meaning] for the speakers; but for the hearers, [the meaning] is not established in that way.

body.text:
2239.
(ajñātvā* ”jñā)(kam, m. 2nd s.)(śabdam, m. 2nd s.)(vivakṣatu ”vac Desid. Imperative 3p s.)(cet*)(jānāti ”jñā IX C.)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(avaśyam*)(avadhāritaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pūrvam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(eva*)
body.translated_text: 2239. Not having known which word [the speaker] wishes to express — if he does know, [then it is] necessarily already determined previously.

body.text:
2240.
(tejaḥ, n. 1st s.)(pratyakṣa-)(śeṣatvāt, n. 5th s.)(navatve, n. 7th s.)(prakāśakam, n. 1st s.)(api*)(ca*)(sadṛśatva-)(ḥa-pratīteḥ, f. 5th s.)(tat-)(dvāreṇa, n. 3rd s.)(api*)(a-vācakaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2240. Moreover, [a new sound], because of being the remainder after direct perception — even [when] illuminating [meaning] in its novelty — and because of the non-apprehension of similarity — even through that [similarity], it is not a denoter.

body.text:
2241.
(ca*)(kasya, m. 6th s.)(ekasya, m. 6th s.)(sādṛśyāt, n. 5th s.)(aparaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kalpyatām ”kalp Caus. Pass. Imperative 3p s.)(vācakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tadā*)(sarveṣām, m. 6th pl.)(tulyatā , f. 1st s.)(saṅgatitvena, n. 3rd s.)(adṛṣṭa-)
body.translated_text: 2241. And on the basis of the similarity with which single [word] should another be postulated as a denoter? Then there would be equality of all [words, making any word denote anything] — [the similarity] not having been observed as a connection.

body.text:
2242.
(cet*)(dṛṣṭaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pūrva-)(artha-vān, m. 1st s.)(kutaḥ*)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(etāvān, m. 1st s.)(kṣaṇaḥ, m. 1st s.)(hi*)(na*)(sampratīyate ”ī Pass.)(artha-vān, m. 1st s.)(upalabdhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(dviḥ-)(triḥ-vān, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2242. [Objection:] 'If [the word] was previously observed as meaningful — whence [the problem]?' [Reply:] For that [word], this momentary [existence] is [all there is]; it is not perceived [again] as meaningful — [for what is] apprehended twice or thrice [is a different instance].

body.text:
2243.
(apratīta-)(anya-)(śabdānām, m. 6th p. [bv. cpd.])(asau, m. 1st s.)(tat-)(kāle, m. 7th s.)(anarthakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(iti*)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(eva*)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(arthavān, m. 1st s.)(anya-)(śrutīnām, m. 6th pl. [bv. cpd.])(vismayaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2243. For those [hearers] who have not apprehended other words — that [word] is meaningless at that time; [the objection,] 'that very [word] would be meaningful for those who have heard other [instances]' — [this] is astonishing.

body.text:
2244.
(ca*)(tāvat*)(na*)(sambandha-)(karaṇam, n. 1st s.)(anuccārya* ”car)(śabdam, m. 2nd s.)(ca*)(naṣṭasya, m. 6th s.)(uccārita-)(na*)(prayojanam, n. 1st s.)(sambandhena, m. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 2244. And so much [is clear]: without having uttered the word, the establishment of [its] connection [with meaning cannot be made]; and for a [word that has] perished after being uttered — there is no purpose [served] by the connection.

body.text:
2245.
(tena, n. 3rd s.)(naṣṭatvāt, n. 5th s.)(asambandha-)(pūrvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tāvat*)(anarthakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(katham*)(uttaraḥ, m. 1st s.)(sambandhaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(akṛta-)(vijñāyeta ”jñā Pass. Opt.)(arthavān, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2245. Therefore, because of [its] having perished — that which is without a prior connection is meaningless so far; how would a subsequent [utterance], whose connection has not been made, be known as meaningful?

body.text:
2246.
(kaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kuryāt ”kṛ VIII C. Opt.)(kriyāḥ, f. 2nd p.)(uccāraṇa-)(śabda-)(karaṇa-)(sambandha-)(vyāvahārikīḥ, f. 2nd pl.)(sva-bhāvatvāt, n. 5th s.)(krama-)(yugapat*)(kvacit*)
body.translated_text: 2246. Who would perform the conventional acts — the utterance of the word, the making of the connection — [which are] practical? By [their] very nature, [they must occur] sequentially [and] simultaneously at some [point].

body.text:

(puṃsām, m. 6th pl.)(bhinnānām, m. 6th pl.)(kāla-)(deśa-)(ādi-)(pūrvam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(aśruteḥ, f. 5th s.)(antara-)(śabda-)(na*)(siddhyati ”sidh IV C.)(api*)(ekaḥ, m. 1st s.)(śabdah, m. 1st s.)(sambandhaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(kṛtrima-)
body.translated_text: 2247. For persons differentiated by place, time, and the like — because of not having been heard before — the intermediate word — not even a single artificially-connected word is established.

body.text:
2248.
(api*)(asya, m. 6th s.)(sambandha-)(kathane, n. 7th s.)(pratikriyā, f. 1st s.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(eva*)(eṣā, f. 1st s.)(hi*)(na*)(ākhyānasya, n. 6th s.)(sambhavaḥ, m. 1st s.)(naṣṭa-)(asat-)(vartamāneṣu, m. 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 2248. Moreover, even if [some] remedy were to exist in the narration of its connection — this [narration] is not possible for [words that have] perished, non-existent, [or] present [in some other form].

body.text:
2249.
(ca*)(kataraḥ, m. 1st s.)(vaktrā, m. 3rd s.)(kathyatām ”kath Pass.)(arthavān, m. 1st s.)(śrotuḥ, m. 6th s.)(yadā*)(asau, m. 1st s.)(na*)(śaknoti ”śak VII C.)(bhāṣitum* ”bhāṣ)(śabdam, m. 2nd s.)(pūrva-)(śrutam, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2249. And which one [of these words] is to be told by the speaker as meaningful? When that [speaker] is not able to utter the previously heard word to the hearer —

body.text:
2250.

body.translated_text: 2250. So much [is clear]: he does not speak the meaningful [word]; let him speak a similar one — [but] a similar word is not tenable as meaningful for the hearer —

body.text:
2251.
(a-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(grahaṇa-)(arthavat-)(ca*)(asau, m. 1st s.)(svayam*)(na*)(arthavān, m. 1st s.)(velāyām, f. 7th s.)(vaktuḥ, m. 6th s.)(śrotṛtva-)(eva*)(etat, n. 1st s.)(prasajyate ”sañj Pass.)
body.translated_text: 2251. Because of the absence of [its] apprehension as meaningful; and that [similar word] is not itself meaningful; at the time of the speaker — this [conclusion] of [the speaker] being [merely] a hearer absurdly follows.

body.text:
2252.
(tasmāt, 5th s.)(sambandhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(śabda-)(artha-)(abhyupeyatām ”i Pass. Imperative)(nityaḥ, m. 1st s.)(eva*)(tu*)(sāmayikaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(yuktaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tat-)(asambhavāt, m. 5th s.)(sarvathā*)
body.translated_text: 2252. Therefore, let the connection of word and meaning be accepted as permanent; but [if it is] conventional — that is not justified, because of the impossibility of that [convention] in every way.

body.text:
2253.
(śaktatvam, n. 1st s.)(svataḥ)(na*)(eva*)(asti ”as II C.)(mithaḥ*)(vācakayoḥ, m. 6th d.)(vācya-)(pratītiḥ, f. 1st s.)(puṃsām, m. 6th s.)(samayāt, m. 5th s.)(vat*)(nikoca-)(akṣa-)
body.translated_text: 2253. The capacity to denote does not exist inherently [or] mutually between the denoter and the denoted; the cognition of people [arises] from convention — like the contraction of the eye [conveys meaning by convention].

body.text:
2254.
(samayaḥ, m. 1sts.)(kriyate ”kṛ Pass.)(vā*)(prati-martyam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(vā*)(eva*)(prati-uccāraṇam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(vā*)(sakṛt*)(ādau, m. 7th s.)(jagat-)(kenacit, m. 3rd s.)(ekena, m. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 2254. Is the convention made for each person, or for each utterance, or once at the beginning [of creation] by some single [being] for [all] the world?

body.text:
2255.
(vā*)(sambandhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(api*)(bhidyeta ”bhid Pass. Opt.)(prati-ekam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(athavā*)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(ekaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ekatve, n. 7th s.)(na*)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(kṛtakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(cet*)(bhinnaḥ, m. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(dhīḥ, f. 1st s.)(bheda-)
body.translated_text: 2255. Or, would the connection also be differentiated for each individual? Or would it be one? If one, it would not be artificial; if different, there would be a differentiated cognition.

body.text:
2256.
(ca*)(bhedāt, m. 5th s.)(dhiyoḥ, f. 6th d.)(vaktṛ-)(śrotṛ-)(vyavahāraḥ, m. 1st s.)(duṣyati ”duṣ IV C.)(hi*)(sambandhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(buddhau, f. 7th s.)(vaktuḥ, m. 6th s.)(anyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tathā*)(śrotuḥ, m. 6th s.)(aparaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2256. And because of the difference of the two cognitions — of the speaker and the hearer — the convention (<s>vyavahāra</s>) is impaired; for the relation (<s>sambandha</s>) [established] in the cognition of the speaker is one, and that of the hearer is another.

body.text:
2257.
(vaktā, m. 1st s.)(pratipadyatām ”pad IV C. Āt. Imperative 3p s.)(kartum* ”kṛ)(sambandham, m. 2nd s.)(śrotuḥ, m. 6th s.)(hi*)(asau, m. 1st s.)(na*)(karoti ”kṛ VIII C.)(tam, m. 2nd s.)(śrotuḥ, m. 6th s.)(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tena, m. 3rd s.)(dṛṣṭaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pūrvam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])
body.translated_text: 2257. Let the speaker be acknowledged [as the one who] makes the relation; for he does not produce that [relation] for the hearer — [since] the one who was previously seen by the hearer,

body.text:

(navam, m. 2nd s.)(yam, m. 2nd s.)(karoti ”kṛ VIII C.)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(api*)(dṛṣṭa-)(pratipādakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(cet*)(tulyam, n. 1st s.)(ghaṭa-)(ādau, m. 7th s.)(api*)(na*)(sāmānya-)(prasiddhitaḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 2258. Even he who makes a new [relation] is a communicator of what was [already] seen; if [you say it is] the same in the case of pots and the like — [we reply:] not so, because of [not being] established through the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>).

body.text:

body.translated_text: 2259. Also, if the particular (<s>vyakti</s>), whose capacity has been seen, cannot be produced — and that [particular] which is produced has no ascertained capacity with regard to the effect,

body.text:
2260.
(api*)(tathā*)(uccāraṇa-)(ādiṣu, m. 7th pl.)(śaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(siddhā, f. 1st s.)(ākṛtitaḥ* [-tas suff.])(ca*)(tasyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(na*)(ādimattā, f. 1st s.)(tu*)(tava, 6th s.)(sambandhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ādimān, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2260. Even so, the capacity is established in pronunciation and the like from [its] form (<s>ākṛti</s>); and that [capacity] has no beginning — but your relation (<s>sambandha</s>) has a beginning.

body.text:
2261.
(yadi*)(abhyupagamyate ”gam Pass.)(nityam, n. 1st s.)(sāmānyam, n. 1st s.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(api*)(api*)(tathā*)(asmat-)(matam, n. 1st s.)(siddham, n. 1st s.)(tu*)(dvi-)(ākāra-)(na*)(sambhavaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2261. If the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) is accepted as eternal — even so, our position is established; but the existence of a twofold form is not possible.

body.text:
2262.
(hi*)(sambandhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(eva*)(śaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(ca*)(asyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(na*)(bhedaḥ, m. 1st s.)(dṛśyate ”dṛś Pass.)(anumeyatvāt, n. 5th s.)(kārya-)(sā, f. 1st s.)(anuvartate ”vṛt I C. Āt.)(bhedam, m. 2nd s.)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 2262. For the relation itself is the capacity (<s>śakti</s>), and no difference of this [capacity] is observed; because of being inferred from [its] effect, that [capacity] follows the differentiation of the effect.

body.text:
2263.
(ca*)(kalpanam, n. 1st s.)(sat-bhāva-)(śakti-)(anupapattyā, f. 3rd s.)(anyathā-)(ca*)(arthe, m. 7th s.)(siddhe, m. 7th s.)(ekayā, f. 3rd s.)(kalpanā, f. 1st s.)(bahvīnām, f. 6th pl.)(na*)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)
body.translated_text: 2263. And the postulation of [a separate] capacity, [given] the impossibility of the existence of [an independent] capacity — [is unnecessary]; and when the object is established by one [explanation], the postulation of many [explanations] is not accepted.

body.text:

body.translated_text: 2264. And at the time of declaring the relation — when the word 'cow' and the like is uttered — some understand the meaning through the relation by [their own] cognition; others do not [understand] in that way.

2265.
(tatra*)(sambandha-)(nāstitve, m. 7th s.)(na*)(sarvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(avadhārayet ”dhṛ Caus. Opt.)(artham, m. 2nd s.)(cet*)(astitve, n. 7th s.)(sarva-)(bodhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(anupagrahāt, m. 5th s.)(kaiścit, m. 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 2265. In that case, if the relation does not exist — not everyone would ascertain the meaning; if [the relation] does exist — [then] all [should] understand, [but they do] not — because of not being apprehended by some.

body.text:
2266.
(jñāpakatvāt, n. 5th s.)(sambandhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(apekṣate ”īkṣ I C. Āt.)(jñānam, n. 2nd s.)(sva-ātma-)(tena, 3rd s.)(api*)(vidyamānaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(prakāśakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(agṛhītaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2266. Because of being a notifier (<s>jñāpaka</s>), the relation requires knowledge of its own nature; even existing, [the relation is] not an illuminator when unapprehended.
