body.text:
2268.
(sat-)(asat-bhāvau, m. 1st d.)(viruddhau, m. 1st d.)(na*)(syātām ”as II C. Opt. 3p d.)(eka-)(vastuni, n. 7th s.)(ca*)(na*)(tulyam, n. 1st s.)(virodhitvam, n. 1st s.)(api*)(jñāta-)(ajñātatvayoḥ, n. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2268. Existence and non-existence, being contradictory, cannot obtain in a single entity; and the contradictoriness is not the same [in the case of] the states of being known and unknown.

body.text:
2269.
(hi*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(ādhāram, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(puruṣa-)(na*)(virduhyate ”rudh Pass.)(tat-)(bhedāt, m. 5th s.)(ca*)(ajñānam, n. 1st s.)(saṃstham, n. 1st s.)(antara-)(puruṣa-)(na*)(vāryate ”vṛ Caus. Pass.)
body.translated_text: 2269. For knowledge, which has a person as [its] substrate, is not contradicted by that difference [of knowers]; and ignorance, which abides in another person, is not prevented [either].

body.text:
2270.
(śuklaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sthaḥ, m. 1st s.)(samīpa-)(andha-)(anandha-)(na*)(avagamyate ”gam Pass.)(andhaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(ca*)(gamyate ”gam Pass.)(itaraiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(sat-)(sattve, n. 1st d.)(prati*)(tān, m. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 2270. [Consider] a white [object] situated nearby — [it is] not perceived by the blind, [but] is perceived by others who are not blind; [yet] the existence of that [object] obtains equally with respect to both of them.

body.text:
2271.
(tu*)(avirodhitā, f. 1st s.)(tatra*)(bhedāt, m. 5th s.)(śakti-)(aśaktyoḥ, f. 7th d.)(narāṇām, m. 6th s.)(hi*)(hi*)(atra*)(na*)(hetuḥ, m. 1st s.)(darśanasya, n. 6th s.)(anyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sambandhāt, m. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 2271. But there is no contradiction there, because of the difference between capacity and incapacity of the persons; for indeed, there is no cause of perception other than the relation.

body.text:
2272.
(eva*)(evam*)(upalambhanam, n. 1st s.)(vyavahāra-)(tulyam, n. 1st s.)(indriyaiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(tataḥ*)(te, m. 1st pl.)(yeṣām, m. 6th pl.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(avabudhyante ”budh IV C. Āt.)(artham, m. 2nd s.)((anye, m. 1st pl.)(na*)(vat*)(andha-)
body.translated_text: 2272. Just so, the apprehension [of meaning] through the convention [depends on] the sense organs — being equal; therefore, those for whom [the convention] exists understand the meaning; others do not — like the blind.

body.text:
2273.
(sarveṣām, m. 6th pl)(anabhijñānām, m. 6th pl.)(sambandhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(prasiddhitaḥ* [-tas suff.])(pūrva-pūrva-)(iti*)(evam*)(sambandhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(anādiḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2273. [The relation is established] for all those who are unfamiliar [with it] from the prior [establishment] of the relation [by their predecessors]; thus, the relation is beginningless.

body.text:
2274.
(pratyuccaraṇa-)(na*)(nirvṛttiḥ, f. 1st s.)(vyavahārataḥ* [-tas suff.])(ca*)(ādau, m. 7th s.)(sarga-)(na*)(kriyā, f. 1st s.)(hi*)(na*)(tādṛk, m. 1st s.)(kālaḥ, m. 1st s.)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)
body.translated_text: 2274. [There is] no cessation from [mere] re-utterance, nor from convention; and at the beginning of creation, there is no [creative] action — for no such time [of absolute beginning] is accepted.

body.text:
2275.
(hi*)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(jagat, n. 1st s.)(na*)(kadācit*)(anīdṛśam)(mahā-pralayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(jñāyate ”jñā Pass.)(pāramārthikaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2275. For the entire universe is accepted [as having] never been otherwise [than it is]; the great dissolution (<s>mahāpralaya</s>) [as] ultimate [annihilation] is not acknowledged.

body.text:
2276.
(vā*)(nāma*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(pralayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(rātriḥ, f. 1st s.)(līnatvāt, n. 5th s.)(sarva-)(karmaṇām, n. 6th s.)(ca*)(divasaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sañjñaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(sṛṣṭi-)(sarva-)(ceṣṭā-)(atisarjanāt, n. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 2276. Or, dissolution is [merely] called 'night' because of the cessation of all activities; and creation is designated 'day' because of the release of all actions.

body.text:
2277.
(vā*)(pralayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(rūpaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(utsāda-)(deśa-)(utsāda-)(kula-)(tu*)(hi*)(na*)(pramāṇam, n. 1st s.)(pralaye, m. 7th s.)(ātmake, m. 7th s.)(uccheda-)(sarva-)
body.translated_text: 2277. Or, dissolution would be in the form of [regional] destructions — of country, of family — but there is no valid means of cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) for a dissolution of the nature of total annihilation.

body.text:
2278.
(na*)(ca*)(kaścit, m. 1st s.)(sthiraḥ, m. 1st s.)(kārakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sṛṣṭi-)(saṃhāra-)(īśvara-)(ādiḥ, m. 1st s.)(yuktaḥ, m. 1st s.)(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(alupta-)(smṛtiḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(prakalpayet ”kḷp Caus. Opt.)(sambandham, m. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 2278. And there is no stable agent — such as <s>Īśvara</s> (God) — of creation and destruction, who, with unimpaired memory, could establish the relation [between words and meanings after dissolution].

body.text:
2279.
(nanu*)(ānupūrvī-)(anityatvāt, n. 5th s.)(vācakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(anityaḥ, m. 1st s.)(hi*)(iṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(vācakam, n. 1st s.)(padam, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(tat-)(adhīnā, f. 1st s.)(krama-)
body.translated_text: 2279. [Objection:] Surely, because the sequence (<s>ānupūrvī</s>) is non-eternal, the denoter is non-eternal; for the denoting word (<s>pada</s>) is accepted [as the unit], and the cognition depends on its sequence.

body.text:
2280.
(vaḥ, 6th pl.)(sarva-gatatvāt, n. 5th s.)(varṇāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(na*)(svataḥ* [-tas suff.])(vṛttayaḥ, m. 1st pl. [bv. cpd.])(krama-)(kramasya, m. 6th s.)(kāryatvāt, n. 5th s.)(anitya-)(dhvani-)(ataḥ*)(vināśitā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2280. Your <s>varṇas</s> (phonemes), being all-pervading, do not intrinsically have sequence; because sequence is a product — therefore [it has] the perishability of non-eternal <s>dhvani</s> (sound).

body.text:
2281.
(ca*)(asya, m. 6th s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(adhīnatā, f. 1st s.)(puruṣa-)(vaśāt, m. 5th s.)(tat-)(vivakṣā-)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(nityatā, f. 1st s.)(varṇānām, m. 6th s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(niṣphalā, f. 1st s.)(bhavatām, m. 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 2281. And its dependence on persons would follow from the force of the desire to express (<s>vivakṣā</s>); by that, the eternality of the <s>varṇas</s> would be fruitless for you.

body.text:
2282.
(ca*)(varṇāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(vinā*)(kramāt, m. 5th s.)(nirjñātāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(pratipādakāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(ca*)(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(evam*)(kramasya, m. 6th s.)(eva*)(prasajyate ”sañj Pass.)(padatvam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2282. And the <s>varṇas</s> without sequence are not known as communicators; therefore, wordhood (<s>padatva</s>) would thus pertain to the sequence itself.

body.text:
2283.
(tu*)(teṣām, m. 6th pl.)(eva*)(yeṣām, m. 6th pl.)(padam, n. 1st s.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(atiriktam, n. 1st s.)(varṇa-)(varjitam, n. 1st s.)(krama-)(eṣā, f. 1st s.)(kalpanā, f. 1st s.)(nityatva-)(śabda-)(arthavatī, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2283. But for those very [Mīmāṃsakas] for whom the word (<s>pada</s>) would be something over and above the <s>varṇas</s>, devoid of sequence — this contrivance of the eternality of <s>śabda</s> (word) would be meaningful.

body.text:
2284.
(ānupūrvasya, n. 6th s.)(padatvam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(prasajyate ”sañj Pass.)(naḥ, 6th pl.)(hi*)(etat, n. 1st s.)(ādhāram, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(vastu-)(antara-)(na*)(dṛṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(prakāśakam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2284. [Reply:] The wordhood of the sequence does not follow for us; for this [sequence], having no substrate as a separate entity, is not observed as a communicator.

body.text:
2285.
(idam, n. 1st s.)(mātram, n. 1st s.)(dharma-)(teṣām, n. 6th pl.)(na*)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)(antaram, n. 1st s.)(vastu-)(ittham*)(avabodhakāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(varṇāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(pratīyamānāḥ ”i Pass., m. 1st pl.)(tena, m. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 2285. Only this much is their property — no separate entity is accepted [for the sequence]; the <s>varṇas</s>, being apprehended thus [in sequence], are the communicators by that [arrangement].

body.text:
2286.
(ca*)(kramasya, m. 6th s.)(na*)(kāryatvam, n. 1st s.)(parigrahāt, m. 5th s.)(pūrva-)(siddha-)(hi*)(vaktā, m. 1st s.)(na*)(prapadyate ”pad IV C.)(kañcit, m. 2nd s.)(kramam, m. 2nd s.)(svātantryeṇa, n. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 2286. And the sequence is not a product, because of the acceptance of what is already established; for the speaker does not adopt any sequence independently,

body.text:
2287.
(vivakṣati ”vac Desid.)(enam, m. 2nd s.)(eva*)(tathā*)(eva*)(yathā*)(asya, m. 6th s.)(uktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(paraiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(api*)(paraḥ, m. 1st s.)(evam*)(ataḥ*)(asya, m. 6th s.)(anāditā, f. 1st s.)(vat*)(sambandha-)
body.translated_text: 2287. [But rather] desires to express this [word] in exactly the way in which its utterance [has been heard] from others; therefore, like the relation, this [sequence] is beginningless.

body.text:
2288.
(tena, n. 3rd s.)(akauṭasthye, n. 7th s.)(syāt ”as I C. Opt.)(iyam, f. 1st s.)(nityatā, f. 1st s.)(vyavahārāt, m. 5th s.)(naḥ, 6th pl.)(yatnataḥ* [-tas suff.])(pratiṣedhyā, f. 1st s.)(puruṣāṇām, m. 6th pl.)(svatantratā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2288. By that, even without absolute permanence (<s>kauṭasthya</s>), this eternality would [obtain] from convention; the independence of persons is to be carefully denied by us.

body.text:
2289.
(tu*)(evam*)(na*)(setsyati ”sidhi Future)(api*)(varṇānām, m. 6th pl.)(api*)(akauṭasthye, n. 7th s.)(varṇeṣu, m. 7th pl.)(satsu, m. 7th pl.)(nityeṣu, m. 7th pl.)(krama-)(udayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vyavahārāt, m. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 2289. But even so, [the eternality] will not succeed even for the <s>varṇas</s> without absolute permanence; [for] if the <s>varṇas</s> exist as eternal, the arising of sequence from convention [alone is untenable],

body.text:
2290.
(yat-vat*)(ghaṭa-)(ādi-)(racanā, f. 1st s.)(nityeṣu, m. 7th pl.)(parama-aṇuṣu, m. 7th pl.)(a-bhāve, m. 7th s.)(tat-)(racanā, f. 1st s.)(nirmūlā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(avadhāryate ”dhṛ Pass.)
body.translated_text: 2290. Just as the arrangement of pots and the like [is untenable] if the ultimate atoms (<s>paramāṇus</s>) are eternal; in the absence of that [arrangement], such an arrangement is baseless — [this] is not ascertainable.

body.text:
2291.
(ca*)(vivakṣā, f. 1st s.)(dhruvam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(īdṛśī, f. 1st s.)(iti*)(bravīmi ”brū II C. 1p pl.)(uktān, m. 2nd pl.)(pareṇa, m. 3rd s.)(ca*)(tathā*)(apattiḥ, f. 1st s.)(nityatā-)(na*)(asti ”as II C.)(na*)(anyat, n. 1st s.)(cihnam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2291. And [we say:] 'the desire to express is certainly of this kind' — this [is what] we declare; and by the opponent too, the same consequence [applies]; there is no [valid] mark of eternality, nor anything else.

body.text:
2292.
(yathā*)(ghaṭa-)(ādīnām, m. 6th pl.)(vyavahāra-)(upalakṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(tathā*)(ānupūrvya-)(ādeḥ, m. 6th s.)(setsyati ”sidh Future)(dvāreṇa, n. 3rd s.)(jāti-)
body.translated_text: 2292. Just as the conventional designation of pots and the like [is established] — so too, [the designation] of sequence and the like will be established through the medium of <s>jāti</s> (universal).

body.text:
2293.
(tāvat*)(jātayaḥ, f. 1st pl.)(tālu-)(ādi-)(vyavasthitāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(sarva-)(puṃsu, m. 7th pl.)(ca*)(upalakṣya* ”lakṣ)(tān, m. 2nd pl.)(dhvanīn, m. 2nd pl.)(tābhiḥ, f. 3rd pl.)(vaktā, m. 1st s.)(nirasyati ”as IV C.)
body.translated_text: 2293. So many universals [of phonemes] are established [as corresponding to] the palate and the like, and are observed in all persons; having identified those sounds through those [universals], the speaker utters them.

body.text:
2294.
(ca*)(bhinnāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(jātayaḥ, f. 1st pl.)(teṣām, m. 6th pl.)(hetavaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(abhivyakti-)(śabda-)(pravartante ”vṛt I C. ÄḥĀt. III p. pl.)(yāvat-)(varṇam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(vā*)(vyaktayaḥ, f. 1st pl.)(anvitāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 2294. And the different universals of those [sounds] are the causes of the manifestation of sound; they operate as far as each phoneme [extends], or [alternatively,] the individuals [of each phoneme type] are accompanied by those [universals].

body.text:
2295.
(tatra*)(ānupūrvyam, n. 1st s.)(dhvanīnām, m. 6th pl.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(pūrvakam, n. 1st s.)(krama-)(saṃyoga-)(vibhāga-)(tālu-)(ādi-)(ca*)(nityatā, f. 1st s.)(ubhaya-)(jātyā, f. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 2295. There, the sequence of sounds would be [determined by] the prior [element's] conjunction and disjunction with the palate and the like; and the eternality [of phonemes is established] by both universals.

body.text:
2296.
(eva*)(yathā*)(bhāgāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(bhramaṇa-)(ādīnām, m. 6th pl.)(lakṣitāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(jāti-)(ādi-)(krama-)(anuvṛttiḥ, f. 1st s.)(bhāk, f. 1st s.)(tālu-)(ādi-)(dhvani-)(varṇa-)
body.translated_text: 2296. Just as the parts of rotation and the like are identified [through universals] — [so too,] the recurrence of the sequence and the like [is established] through the universals of sound and phoneme — [which are associated with] the palate and the like.

body.text:
2297.
(vā*)(vyaktīnām, f. 6th pl.)(eva*)(saukṣmyāt, n. 5th s.)(avadhāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(dharma-)(jāti-)(ca*)(vaśena, m. 3rd s.)(tat-)(grahaḥ, m. 1st s.)(krama-)(varṇānām, m. 6th pl.)(api*)(vyāpitve, n. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 2297. Or rather, the ascertainment [is] of the individuals alone, because of [their] subtlety; and the apprehension of the property of universal [is made] by the force of that [individual]; even when phonemes are all-pervading, [the apprehension of] the sequence [is possible].

body.text:
2298.
(evam*)(varṇāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(anupatantaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(sarvān, m. 2nd pl.)(guṇān, m. 2nd pl.)(dhvani-)(vyavasthitān, m. 2nd pl.)(nityatvena, n. 3rd s.)(syuḥ ”as II C. Opt. III p. pl.)(avabodhinaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(bheda-)(artha-)
body.translated_text: 2298. Thus, the phonemes (<s>varṇas</s>), following [upon one another], [and] being cognizers of all the properties of sound that are established [in them] — would, by [their] eternality, be cognizers of the distinctions of meaning.

body.text:
2299.
(ca*)(ānupūrvī, f. 1st s.)(varṇānām, m. 6th pl.)(ca*)(hrasva-)(dīrgha-)(plutāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(ye, m. 1st pl.)(pravibhāgāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(kālasya, m. 6th s.)(te, m. 1st pl.)(upādhayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(dhvani-)
body.translated_text: 2299. And the sequence of phonemes, and the [distinctions of] short, long, and protracted [vowels] — those are the divisions of time; they are the qualifying conditions (<s>upādhis</s>) of sound.

body.text:
2300.
(ca*)(kālaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ekaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vibhuḥ, m. 1st s.)(nityaḥ, m. 1st s.)(api*)(gamyate ”gam Pass.)(pravibhaktaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sarva-)(bhāveṣu, m. 7th pl.)(vat*)(varṇa-)(vyajyate ”añj Pass.)(kenacit, n. 3rd s.)(kvacit*)
body.translated_text: 2300. And time is one, all-pervading, and eternal; even so, it is cognized as divided among all entities — like phonemes, [which though eternal,] are manifested by something somewhere.

body.text:
2301.
(vyajyamānasya ”añj Pass., m. 6th s.)(varṇeṣu, m. 7th pl.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(aṅgatā, f. 1st s.)(pratyāyana-)(tu*)(sat-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(anyatra*)(api*)(tat-)(sva-rūpasya, n. 6th s.)(nityatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2301. The [role of time] as an ancillary [factor] in the communication [of meaning] through phonemes that are being manifested — [is established] from the existence [of time]; and elsewhere too, its own form has eternality.

body.text:
2302.
(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(na*)(kaścit, m. 1st s.)(īdṛśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(dharmaḥ, m. 1st s.)(api*)(pada-)(vināśī, m. 1st s.)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(padam, n. 1st s.)(siddham, n. 1st s.)(nityam, n. 1st s.)(vādinām, m. 6th pl.)(nityatva-)(varṇa-)
body.translated_text: 2302. Therefore, no such property is perishable — not even the word (<s>pada</s>); thereby the word is established as eternal, for the proponents of the eternality of phonemes.

body.text:
2303.
(apica*)(dharme, m. 7th s.)(para-)(aṅgatvam, n. 1st s.)(vat*)(uktam, n. 1st s.)(java-)(ādi-)(aśva-)(ca*)(nityatāyām, f. 7th s.)(sarveṣām, 6th pl.)(pramāṇatā, f. 1st s.)(artha-āpatti-)
body.translated_text: 2303. Moreover, the [property of] being ancillary to another property — as stated [in the case of] speed and the like of a horse — and in [the case of] eternality [of all phonemes], the validity of inference from effects (<s>arthāpatti</s>) [applies] to all.

body.text:
2304.
(ca*)(virodhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sva-)(vākya-)(ādi-)(sādhane, n. 7th s.)(anityatva-)(śabda-)(sarvā, f. 1st s.)(pratijñā, f. 1st s.)(uccāryate ”car Caus. Pass.)(pratipattaye, f. 4th s.)(artha-)(sādhya-)
body.translated_text: 2304. And [there is] a contradiction with one's own statement and the like in proving the non-eternality of sound; every thesis is uttered for the sake of the apprehension of the object to be proven.

body.text:
2305.
(ca*)(upapāditam, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(anityā, f. 1st s.)(eṣā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(bravīti ”brū II C.)(sva-)(artham, m. 2nd s.)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(āpannāt, n. 5th s.)(pratyaya-)(artha-)(nityatvāt, n. 5th s.)(bādhanam, n. 1st s.)(nāśa-)
body.translated_text: 2305. And [if it is said] 'it has been demonstrated that this [word] is non-eternal' — [we reply:] it does not express its own meaning; therefore, from the eternality of the cognition produced by that [word], the refutation of destruction [follows].

body.text:
2306.
(naraḥ, m. 1st s.)(abhyupetya* ”i)(sāmarthyam, n. 2nd s.)(artha-)(abhidhāna-)(sādhayan ”sidh Caus., m. 1st s.)(bādhate ”bādh I C. Āt.)(nāśitvam, n. 2nd s.)(api*)(pūrva-)(abhyupagatena, n. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 2306. A person, having accepted the capacity for verbal designation, [and] while establishing [it], refutes the perishability [of sound] — by [the very capacity] previously accepted.

body.text:
2307.
(nāśitvam, n. 1st s.)(bādhyate ”bādh)(api*)(āgamena, m. 3rd s.)(sāmarthyaiḥ, n. 3rd s.)(pratīti-)(artha-)(upāśritaiḥ, n. 3rd s.)(prati-śāśtram*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])
body.translated_text: 2307. The perishability [of sound] is also refuted by scriptural tradition (<s>āgama</s>), and by the capacities [of words] dependent on the apprehension of meaning — [this applies] to each treatise.

body.text:
2308.
(ca*)(diśā, f. 3rd s.)(uktayā, f. 3rd s.)(pūrva-)(bādhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sarva-loka-)(prassiddhyā, f. 3rd s.)(virodhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(anumāna-)(api*)(hetunā, m. 3rd s.)(eva*)(uktena, m. 1st s.)(pūrva-)
body.translated_text: 2308. And the refutation [of non-eternality applies] by the previously stated method; and the contradiction [is established] by the well-known [practice] of the entire world; also by the previously stated reason of inference.

body.text:
2309.
(śrotra-)(ja-)(pratyabhijñānāt, n. 5th s.)(śabda-)(a-bheda-)(avasāyataḥ* [-tas suff.])(viruddhatvam, n. 1st s.)(pratyakṣeṇa, n. 3rd s.)(pratipāditam, n. 1st s.)(prāk*)(eva*)
body.translated_text: 2309. From the recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>) born of the organ of hearing — from the determination of the non-difference of sound — the contradictoriness [of the non-eternality thesis] has been demonstrated previously by direct perception.

body.text:
2310.
(ca*)(vaktavyam, n. 1st s.)(eṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sādhyate ”sidh Caus. Pass.)(vināśitvena, n. 3rd s.)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(tri-)(guṇaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(vā*)(paudgalaḥ, m. 1st s.)(athavā*)(guṇaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ākāśasya, n. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2310. And it must be stated: this sound is proven as perishable — [but is it] of three qualities (<s>guṇas</s>) [as the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s> hold], or material (<s>paudgala</s>) [as the <s>Jainas</s> hold], or a quality of space [as the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> hold]?

body.text:
2311.
(atha*)(ātmā, m. 1st s.)(nāda-)(varṇāt, m. 5th s.)(rūpam, n. 1st s. )(vāyu-)(avācakam, n. 1st s.)(sphoṭaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ātmakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pada-)(vākya-)(sārūpya-)(nivartane, n. 1st d.)(anya-)
body.translated_text: 2311. Or is [sound's] self the <s>nāda</s> (resonance), [its] form from the phoneme, [or] inexpressible by wind, [or] a <s>sphoṭa</s>, [or] of the nature of the word and sentence — [which] removes the resemblance with another?

body.text:
2312.
(eteṣām, n. 6th pl.)(astu ”as II C. Imper. 3p s.)(anityatvam, n. 1st s.)(asmākam, 6th pl.)(nityatā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(teṣu, n. 7th pl.)(viśeṣatvam, n. 1st s.)(aprasiddha-)(hetutā, f. 1st s.)(asiddha-)(āśraya-)
body.translated_text: 2312. Let the non-eternality of these [views] stand; [but] for us, there is no eternality [to refute] in those [views]; [the alleged] distinguishing feature [is based on] an unestablished [property], [and] the reason [suffers from] an unestablished substratum.

body.text:
2313.
(atha*)(pakṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(iṣṭaḥ, m. 1st s.)(asmat-)(dvayam, n. 1st s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(svayam*)(tava, 6th s.)(atha*)(mātram, n. 1st s.)(śabda-)(vaḥ, 6th pl.)(sati, n. 7th s.)(tathā*)(śabdatvam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2313. Now, if the thesis accepted [by you] were [to apply to] our pair [of views] — that [pair] is self-[refuting] for you; or if [the thesis is about] mere sound-ness (<s>śabdatva</s>) — [then] when sound-ness is [accepted as eternal],

body.text:
2314.
(anityam, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(virudhyate ”rudh Pass.)(sarveṣām, m. 6th pl.)(nityam, n. 1st s.)(iha*)(yatkiñcit, n. 1st s.)(sāmānyam, n. 1st s.)(kalpyate ”kḷp Pass.)(sarveṇa, m. 3rd s.)(nityam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2314. And that [sound-ness], being eternal, is contradicted [by your thesis]; if something is eternal here as a universal [of all sounds], it is posited as eternal by everyone.

body.text:
2315.
(ca*)(yadi*)(anityatvam, n. 1st s.)(ucyate ”vac Pass.)(nāśitvam, n. 1st s.)(tataḥ*)(prati*)(asmān, 2nd pl.)(pakṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(viśeṣaṇaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(a-prasiddha-)
body.translated_text: 2315. And if non-eternality is said to be perishability — then against us, the thesis would have an unestablished qualifier.

body.text:
2316.
(cet*)(iṣṭā, f. 1st s.)(yathākathañcit*)(vyapadeśyatā, f. 1st s.)(anitya-)(hi*)(sā, f. 1st s.)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)(anabhivyakti-)(avasthātaḥ* [-tas suff.])(vyakti-)(ātmatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2316. If the designability as 'non-eternal' is somehow accepted — for [we say:] that [designability as non-eternal] is accepted [by us only] from the standpoint of the state of non-manifestation; the nature of the individual [phoneme persists].

body.text:
2317.
(ca*)(hetau, m. 7th s.)(prakalpite, m. 7th s.)(atra*)(kevala-)(indriyakatve, n. 7th s.)(idānīm*)(pratīyate ”i Pass.)(vyabhicāraḥ, m. 1st s.)(jātyā, f. 3rd s.)(sādhitayā, f. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 2317. And when the reason is postulated here — in [the property of] being produced by the senses alone — then deviation is perceived now through the [previously] established <s>jāti</s> (universal).

body.text:
2318.
(eva*)(yathā*)(hetuḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(labhyate ”labh Pass.)(asiddhe, n. 7th s.)(dharmatve, n. 7th s.)(pakṣa-)(prativādinaḥ, m. 6th s.)(tat-vat*)(anvaya-)(vyatirekayoḥ, m. 7th d.)
body.translated_text: 2318. Just as the reason is not obtained when the property of the opponent's thesis (<s>pakṣa-dharmatva</s>) is unestablished — so too in [the case of] positive and negative concomitance.

body.text:
2319.
(tatra*)(api*)(yadi*)(jātiḥ, f. 1st s.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(asiddhā, f. 1st s.)(vādinaḥ, m. 6th s.)(sādhana-)(api*)(tathā*)(yāvat*)(ahetutvam, n. 1st s.)(tāvat*)(sā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(nirākrtā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2319. There too, if the <s>jāti</s> (universal) of the proponent is unestablished — even so, as long as [its] causelessness [is not demonstrated], that [universal] has not been refuted.

body.text:
2320.
(ca*)(indriyakatva-)(ādau, n. 7th s.)(sphuṭā, f. 1st s.)(nirūpaṇā. f. 1st s.)(kāryā, f. 1st s.)(iti*)(kim-vastu, n. 1st s.)(ananya-)(vyaktibhyaḥ, f. 5th pl.)(nānātva-)(bheda-)(abhedeṣu, m. 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 2320. And regarding [the property of] being produced by the senses and the like — a clear examination must be made: what [kind of] entity [is it that is] distinct from individuals — in the [contexts of] multiplicity, distinction, and non-distinction?

body.text:
2321.
(tatra*)(a-sādhāraṇa-)(a-siddha-)(sādhya-)(hīna-)(sapakṣatāḥ, f. 1st pl.)
(vikalpita-)(anusāreṇa, m. 3rd s.)(vaktavyā, f. 1st s.)(vādi-)(apekṣayā, f. 3rd s.)(api*)
Textual variants [Baudha Bhāratī]: (sapakṣatā, f. 1st s.)(ca*)(ādi-)
body.translated_text:
2321. There, the [faults of] uncommonness, unestablishedness, [being] devoid of the probandum, [and] deficient positive examples — are to be stated according to the [particular] alternative followed, from the standpoint of the proponent.
[Textual variants, Baudha Bhāratī: 'the positive example and the like.']

body.text:
2322.
(yat, n. 1st s.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(anantaram, n. 1 s.)(prayatna-)(sādhanam, n. 1st s.)(kṛtaka-)(anitya-)(tatra*)(api*)(asti ”as II C.)(anekāntaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vyatirekibhiḥ, 3rd pl.)(kṣaṇika-)
body.translated_text: 2322. The cognition that immediately follows effort — [that is] the proof of [being] produced [and therefore] non-eternal; there too, there is inconclusiveness (<s>anekānta</s>) with [respect to] what is distinguished by momentariness.

body.text:
2323.
(tribhiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(pratisaṅkhyā-)(apratisaṅkhyā-)(nirodha-)(vyomabhiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(hi*)(vināśe, m. 7th s.)(pūrva-)(buddhi-)(dhīḥ, f. 1st s.)(pratisaṅkhyā-)(nirodha-)
body.translated_text: 2323. By three [types of cessation] — <s>pratisaṅkhyā-nirodha</s> (analytical cessation), <s>apratisaṅkhyā-nirodha</s> (non-analytical cessation), and space (<s>vyoman</s>) — for in the case of destruction preceded by a prior cognition, [there is] <s>pratisaṅkhyā-nirodha</s> (cessation through analysis),

body.text:
2324.
(pūrvakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(abuddhi-)(apratisaṅkhyayā, f. 3rd s.)(nirodhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ca*)(api*)(dvau, m. 1st d.)(tau, m. 1st d.)(anāśitvāt, n. 5th s.)(iṣṭau, m. 1st d.)(akṛtakau, m. 1st d.)(api*)
body.translated_text: 2324. That [cessation] preceded by non-cognition [is] <s>apratisaṅkhyā-nirodha</s> (non-analytical cessation); and those two, even though they are not perishable, are also accepted as unproduced.

body.text:
2325.
(hi*)(te, m. 1st pl.)(āhuḥ ”ah Perf. III p. pl.)(vināśam, m. 2nd s.)(siddham, m. 2nd s.)(sva-bhāva-)(ahetukam, m. 2nd s.)(hi*)(kāṣṭhāt, n. 5th s.)(sambandhāt, n. 5th s. [bv. cpd.])(agni-)(bhavati ”bhū I C.)(santatiḥ, f. 1st s.)(aṅgāra-)
body.translated_text: 2325. For they declare destruction as self-established, essentiality-based, [and] without a [separate] cause; for from the connection with firewood, the continuum of charcoal arises from fire.

body.text:
2326.
(vināśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tu*)(svābhāvikaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pratiṣṭhitaḥ, m. 1st s.)(mātra-)(jāti-)(sūkṣmaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vṛtteḥ, f. 5th s.)(sadṛśa-)(santāna-)(anupalakṣitaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2326. But destruction is natural (<s>svābhāvika</s>), established [in things themselves]; [it is] subtle, merely of the type [of the entity], unobserved — because of the operation of a similar continuum.

body.text:
2327.
(yadā*)(vilakṣaṇaḥ, m. 1st s.)(hetuḥ, m. 1st s.)(patet ”pat I C. Opt.)(sadṛśa-)(santatau, f. 7th s.)(tadā*)(vilakṣaṇena, n. 3rd s.)(kāryeṇa, n. 3rd s.)(sthūlaḥ, m. 1st s.)(abhivyajyate ”añj Pass.)
body.translated_text: 2327. When a dissimilar cause falls upon the similar continuum, then it is manifested by the dissimilar effect as gross [destruction].

body.text:
2328.
(hetoḥ, m. 5th s.)(yataḥ, m. 5th s.)(asadṛśa-)(santānaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sañjāyate ”jan IV C. Āt.)(abhivyajyate ”añj Pass.)(sphuṭaḥ, m. 1st s.)(nāśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(akriyamāṇaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tena, m. 3rd s.)(eva*)
body.translated_text: 2328. Since from a dissimilar cause, a dissimilar continuum arises — the destruction, [which was already occurring] without being produced [by any external agent], is [now] clearly manifested by that [dissimilar cause] alone.

body.text:
2329.
(ataḥ*)(yasmāt, n. 5th s.)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(annantarīyakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(prayatna-)(prahāra-)(mudgara-)(ādi-)(dṛṣṭaḥ, m. 1st s.)(akṛtakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(hetuḥ, m. 1st s.)(vyabhicārī, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2329. Therefore, since that [destruction] is an inevitable consequence of [the blows of] effort, hammers, and the like — [and is] observed [to occur thus] — [the argument that destruction requires a cause] is an unproduced [and] deviant reason.

body.text:
2330.
(ākāśam, n. 1st s.)(api*)(sat, n. 1st s.)(nityam, n. 1st s.)(yadā*)(āvṛtam, n. 1st s.)(bhūmi-)(jala-)(vyajyate ”añj Pass.)(apohena, m. 3rd s.)(tat-)(khanana-)(ucchedana-)(ādibhiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 2330. Even if space (<s>ākāśa</s>) is existent and eternal, when it is covered by earth and water, it is manifested by the removal of those — through digging, cutting, and the like.

body.text:
2331.
(yadā*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(anantaram, n. 1st s.)(prayatna-)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(hetuḥ, m. 1st s.)(dṛśyate ”dṛś Pass.)(tatra*)(api*)(anaikāntikaḥ, m. 1st s.)(yat, n. 1st s.)(uktam, n. 1st s.)(darśanam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2331. When the cognition immediately [following] effort is seen as [having] a cause therein too — as for what has been said [about] perception, the [reason] is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>).

body.text:
2332.
(sapakṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(api*)(vikalpaḥ, m. 1st s.)(atra*)(śruti-)(arthe, m. 7th s.)(hīnatā, f. 1st s.)(sādhya-)(api*)(pakṣe, m. 7th s.)(lakṣaṇa-)(vyakti-)(kalpanā, f. 1st s.)(ananya-)(anya-)(jāti-)
body.translated_text: 2332. The positive example (<s>sapakṣa</s>) too is doubtful here; there is deficiency in the meaning of the scriptural [statement] regarding what is to be proven; and in the thesis, there is the fabrication of a defining characteristic [as belonging to] species (<s>jāti</s>) — whether non-different or different.

body.text:
2333.
(anyatve, n. 7th s.)(dharmin-)(asiddheḥ, f. 5th s.)(naḥ, 6th pl.)(api*)(ananyatve, n. 7th s.)(prati*)(parān, m. 2nd pl.)(api*)(aviśeṣe, m. 7th s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(vastu, n. 1st s.)(nityam, n. 1st s.)(anityam, n. 1st s.)(mama, 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2333. If [the <s>dharma</s> and its characteristic are] different, [there is] non-establishment of the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) for us; if non-different, [the same applies] against the opponents too. Without distinction, that entity is [both] eternal and non-eternal — in my [view],

body.text:
2334.
(hi*)(aṃśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(etasya, n. 6th s.)(ākhyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(jāti-)(nityaḥ, m. 1st s.)(itaraḥ, m. 1st s.)(mataḥ, m. 1st s.)(dhvaṃsī, m. 1st s.)(pratipāditam, n. 1st s.)(prāk*)(ekam, n. 1st s.)(vastu, n. 1st s.)(śabala-)(ākāram, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])
body.translated_text: 2334. For one aspect of this [entity], called <s>jāti</s> (universal), is eternal; the other is considered perishable. It has been previously demonstrated that a single entity has a variegated form.

body.text:
2335.
(evam*)(anityatā, f. 1st s.)(vikalpyā, f. 1st s.)(cet*)(nāśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(hīnatā, f. 1st s.)(sādhya-)(mama, 6th s.)(tu*)(anyasyām, f. 7th s.)(bhavatām, m. 6th pl.)(iti*)(eṣā, f. 1st s.)(dik, f. 1st s.)(ukti-)(dūṣaṇa-)
body.translated_text: 2335. If non-eternality is to be analyzed [alternatively as] destruction, [there is] deficiency in what is to be proven. But [we reply:] in [your] other [formulation], the same [applies] to you — this is the direction of the refutation of [your] statement.

body.text:
2336.
(vā*)(api*)(pada-)(artha-)(sambandha-)(sādhite, n. 7th s.)(nityatve, n. 7th s.)(ca*)(sidhyati ”sidh IV C.)(na*)(pramāṇatvam, n. 1st s.)(iha*)(prati*)(artham, m. 2nd s.)(vākya-)
body.translated_text: 2336. Or, even when eternality is established through the connection of word and meaning, the validity (<s>pramāṇatva</s>) of the sentence with respect to [its] object is not established here.

body.text:
2337.
(hi*)(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(arthaḥ, m. 1st s.)(api*)(san ”as II C., m. 1st s.)(niṣkāraṇaḥ, m. 1st s.)(parikalpitaḥ, m. 1st s.)(yājñikaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(samayāt, m. 5th s.)(puruṣāṇām, m. 6th pl.)(vat*)(guṇa-)(vṛddhi-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 2337. For understanding, even when the object exists, is [sometimes] fabricated without a [real] cause — by the ritualists (<s>yājñikas</s>) through convention — as with the increase of merit (<s>guṇa</s>) for persons and the like.

body.text:
2338.
(apica*)(tu*)(saṅghātāt, m. 5th s.)(asya, m. 6th s.)(pauruṣeyatā, f. 1st s.)(vat*)(kathā-)(ca*)(asti ”as II C.)(na*)(āptaḥ, m. 1st s.)(puruṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(atra*)(veda-)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(apramāṇatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2338. Moreover, because of [the <s>Veda</s>'s] being a composition, its human authorship [follows] — as with a story; and since there is no trustworthy person (<s>āpta</s>) here [as author] — therefore, the <s>Veda</s> lacks validity.

body.text:
2339.
(nityatā, f. 1st s.)(vākya-)(vaktavyā, f. 1st s.)(nyāyāt, m. 5th s.)(sambandha-)(akāraṇa-)(api*)(ādau, m. 7th s.)(vṛddhi-)(sambhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(vyavahāratvāt, n. 5th s.)(dṛṣṭa-)(artha-)
body.translated_text: 2339. The eternality of the sentence is to be stated on the ground of the [word-meaning] connection without a [human] cause; but if increase [of merit] were possible at the beginning, [that would be] because of being [merely] conventional usage with observed objects.

body.text:
2340.
(vede, m. 7th s.)(tu*)(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(sāmayikī, f. 1st s.)(na*)(yujyate ”yuj Pass.)(yataḥ*)(kena, m. 3rd s.)(sambandhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(svarga-)(yāga-)(atīndriyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(hi*)(dṛṣṭaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2340. But a conventional understanding regarding the <s>Veda</s> is not justified; because the connection between sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>) and heaven (<s>svarga</s>) is supersensory — by whom has it been seen?

body.text:
2341.
(ca*)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(na*)(anarthakatā, f. 1st s.)(pratyaya-)(tat-)(artha-)(udayāt, m. 5th s.)(saṅghatatvasya, n. 6th s.)(pratisādhanam, n. 1st s.)(vaktavyam, n. 1st s.)(īdṛśam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2341. And the [<s>Veda</s>'s] non-purposelessness [is established] from the arising of the cognition of that meaning; the counter-proof of [its] being a composition must be stated in this manner.

body.text:
2342.
(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(adhyayanam, n. 1st s.)(vedasya, m. 6th s.)(pūrvakam, n. 1st s.)(adhyayana-)(guru-)(vācyatvāt, n. 5th s.)(adhyayana-)(veda-)(yathā*)(adhyayanam, n. 1st s.)(adhunā*)
body.translated_text: 2342. All study of the <s>Veda</s> is preceded by [prior] study; because [the <s>Veda</s>] is to be recited by a teacher [who has studied it] — just as the study of the <s>Veda</s> [proceeds] now [by the same method].

body.text:
2343.
(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(evam*)(bhārate, n. 7th s.)(api*)(tu*)(bādhyate ”bādh Pass.)(smṛtyā, f. 3rd s.)(kartṛ-)(tu*)(yāpi, f. 1st s.)(smṛtiḥ, f. 1st s.)(vede, m. 7th s.)(sā, f. 1st s.)(nibandhanā, f. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(artha-vāda-)
body.translated_text: 2343. This being so, [the same argument] would [apply] in the <s>Bhārata</s> as well; but [it is] refuted by <s>smṛti</s> (tradition) [that attributes it] to an author. But whatever tradition [attributes authorship] in the <s>Veda</s> — that [tradition] has its basis in <s>arthavāda</s> (eulogistic passages).

body.text:
2344.
(atīta-)(anāgatau, m. 1st d.)(kālau, m. 1st d.)(viyoginau, m. 1st d.)(kāra-)(veda-)(kālatvāt, n. 5th s.)(tat-yathā*)(vartamānaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kālaḥ, m. 1st s.)(samīkṣyate ”īkṣ Pass.)
body.translated_text: 2344. Past and future — [these] two times are devoid of [the capacity of] producing the <s>Veda</s>; because of [their] nature as time, just as the present time is considered [incapable of authorship].

body.text:
2345.
(gamyatām ”gam Pass. Imper. 3p s.)(iti*)(brahman-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(kartāraḥ, m. 1st pl.)(vedānām, m. 6th pl.)(hetubhyaḥ, m. 5th pl.)(puruṣatva-)(ādi-)(yathā*)(prakṛtāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(narāḥ, m. 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 2345. Let it be understood that <s>Brahman</s> and the like are the authors of the <s>Vedas</s> — on the grounds of personhood and the like — just as ordinary men [are authors of their compositions].

body.text:
2346.
(ca*)(tataḥ*)(gamyatām ”gam Pass. Imper. 3p s.)(vyaktam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(vacaḥ, n. 1st s.)(vaidikam, n. 1st s.)(amṛṣā*)(sva-)(arthe, m. 7th s.)(anapekṣatvāt, n. 5th s.)(vaktṛ-)(vat*)(buddhi-)(pada-)(pada-arthe, m. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 2346. And from that, let it be understood clearly that Vedic speech is truthful regarding its own object; because of its independence from [any concern about] the speaker — like [the independence of] the cognition [produced by] words [from] word-meanings.

body.text:
2347.
(pratyayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kṛtaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tat-)(samyak*)(udbhavatvataḥ* [-tas suff.])(nitya-)(vākya-)(vat*)(buddhi-)(vākya-)(ca*)(etat, n. 1st s.)(siddham, n. 1st s.)(siddhitaḥ* [-tas suff.])(nityatva-)
body.translated_text: 2347. The cognition produced by that [Vedic speech] — because of [its] arising correctly — is like a cognition [produced by] an eternal sentence. And this [cognition's validity] is established from the establishment of the eternality [of the sentence].

body.text:
2348.

body.translated_text: 2348. The cognition generated by <s>codanā</s> (injunctive statement) is [considered] a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>); because of being produced by causes that are free from defects — like a cognition [produced by] inferential marks, statements of trustworthy persons (<s>āpta</s>), and the senses.

body.text:
2349.
(tathā*)(janyatvāt, n. 5th s.)(ukti-)(apraṇīta-)(anāpta-)(varjanāt, n. 5th s.)(bādha-)(bheda-)(ādau, m. 7th s.)(kāla-)(deśa-)(yathā*)(pratyayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ukti-)(āpta-)
body.translated_text: 2349. Likewise, because of being produced [by such causes], and because of the exclusion of untrustworthy and unauthorized [statements]; as with the cognition [produced by] a trustworthy person's statement — in [matters of] time, place, and the like, and in [cases of] contradiction and the like.

body.text:
2350.
(avasthite, n. 7th s.)(vede, m. 7th s.)(pramāṇe, n. 7th s.)(anādiḥ, f. 1st s.)(paramparā, f. 1st s.)(ācārya-)(śiṣya-)(api*)(kalpyamānā, f. 1st s.)(kalpate ”kḷp I C. Āt.)(na*)(doṣatvāya, n. 4th s.)
body.translated_text: 2350. When the <s>Veda</s> is established as a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), even though the beginningless succession of teachers and pupils is postulated, [this succession] does not amount to a fault.

body.text:
2351.
(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(pratighātaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vede, m. 7th s.)(cakṣuṣi, n. 7th s.)(sarva-)(laukika-)(anyeṣām, m. 6th pl.)(ulūkavat* [-vat suff.])(āloka-vat*)(kila*)(jaḥ, m. 1st s.)(adharma-)
body.translated_text: 2351. Therefore, the obstruction [felt by the unenlightened] regarding the <s>Veda</s> [is] like [the obstruction] of an owl regarding the eye [that perceives] all worldly [light]; for others [who see], light indeed [reveals], just as <s>adharma</s> (demerit) is born [of ignorance].

body.translated_text: 2352. All this is a false display of pride by the twice-born (<s>dvi-jāti</s>); nothing well-said [is found] herein — of these [Mīmāṃsakas], like the [accidental marks made by] wood-worms on syllables.

body.translated_text: 2353. For even in the absence of an author, this [<s>Veda</s>] would never attain truthfulness — because of the deficiency of the qualities of its cause; [it would be] like a false statement in the absence of [a speaker's] faults.

body.translated_text: 2354. [The Mīmāṃsaka says:] 'Faults are suspected in human-authored [works]' — [but] qualities exist [in the Veda too]; therefore, the purposelessness [of the Veda] is not established for us; and there is no suspicion regarding [its] qualities.

body.translated_text: 2355. Therefore, because of the non-existence of the causes — [namely] truthfulness and falsity, wisdom and lack of compassion, and the like — that pair [of truth and falsity] does not exist, nor [is there any basis] from [their] mutual dependence.

body.translated_text: 2356. Therefore, if purposelessness is established — as with sentences about six cakes and the like — [we reply:] the agents and actions are indeed comprehended —

body.translated_text: 2357. This [purposefulness] would [also follow] from the narrative of a person — as with the [story of] <s>Urvaśī</s> and the like; and of this [Veda], from [its] essential nature — when [the narrative] is not intended for that purpose, according to you.

body.translated_text: 2358. Even in the absence of faults, truthfulness is not established — because of the existence of other [possible explanations]; therefore, furthermore, there is an additional heap of purposelessness.

body.translated_text: 2359. Now [if you say] the <s>Veda</s> is inherently flawless and thus is regarded as truthful in meaning and free from doubt —

body.translated_text: 2360. If so, that cognition would always arise uninterruptedly — because of [its] being the cause [of cognition from an] ever-present [Veda]; just as at every moment that is accepted [as its occasion].

body.translated_text: 2362. After that, because of the exhaustion of the capacity to produce cognition, this <s>Veda</s> would not be eternal; or cognition would arise again [endlessly] when the capacity [is present].

body.translated_text: Therefore, even though this <s>apauruṣeyatā</s> (authorlessness) of the <s>Veda</s> exists, it is purposeless, for the result that is desired from it depends on knowledge.

body.translated_text: If this [Veda] is always capable [of conveying meaning] by itself, then why does it require anything else? But [if] knowledge is [needed], then in its presence, you would have a cause capable of only one [effect].

body.translated_text: And people, being independent, making interpretation of the <s>Veda</s> according to their own inclination, cannot be restrained by anyone whatsoever.

body.translated_text: Therefore, it is apprehended that those corrupted by faults such as delusion and pride might even produce a contrary interpretation of the <s>Śruti</s> (scripture).

body.translated_text: The <s>Veda</s>, being without expectation of its own, does not always speak its meaning; rather, it depends on a person for interpretation, which is equivalent to [depending on] a human — like a blind man grasped by a stick,

body.translated_text: And even if it were independently capable of generating knowledge, clearly its validity is not to be admitted, from the observation of human [dependence].

body.translated_text: When validity is thus not established, the beginningless succession of teacher and student that is postulated is also not tenable for [establishing] faultlessness.

body.translated_text: Since not even one among them is, according to their own doctrine, a perceiver of the supersensory, therefore this postulated beginningless succession is [merely] a succession of the blind.

body.translated_text: How could the <s>Veda</s>, producing that [cognition], not attain the status of a valid means of knowledge? For no one at all knows the doubtful object from [mere] statement; therefore,

body.text:
2389.
(na*)(evam*)(saṃśaya-)(sañjāteḥ, f. 5th s.)(vat*)(anya-)(vākya-)(viparīta-)(hi*)(prekṣāvantaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(na*)(paśyanti ”dṛś IV C. III p. pl.)(kañcana, m. 2nd s.)(bhedam, m. 2nd s.)(teṣām, n. 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: this is not so, for unlike the arising of doubt, [Vedic statements] are not like the statements of others that are contrary. Those who are discerning do not perceive any difference among them.

body.text:
2390.
(hi*)(at-indriye, m. 7th s.)(yjyete ”yuj Pass. 3p d.)(na*)(viniścayau, m. 1st d.)(sat-)(asattā-)(cet*)(niścayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(veda-)(vākyāt, n. 5th s.)(kim*)(na*)(anyādṛk, m. 1st s.)(anyataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: For regarding the supersensory, neither the determination of existence nor of non-existence is possible. If there is determination from a Vedic statement, why not a different [determination] from another [source]?

body.text:
2391.
(eṣā, f. 1st s.)(niṣkampyā, f. 1st s.)(buddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(upajāyate ”jan IV C. Āt.)(śrotriyāṇām, m. 6th pl.)(buddhīnām, m. 6th pl. [bv. cpd.])(vivaśa-)(śraddhā-)(sā, f. 1st s.)(samā, f. 1st s.)(anyeṣām, m. 6th pl.)(anyataḥ*)
body.translated_text: This unshakeable conviction arises in those learned in the <s>Vedas</s>, [but it is merely] an involuntary faith among the intelligent; that same [conviction] equally [arises] in others from other [sources].

body.text:
2392.
(tathāhi*)(akampyā, f. 1st s.)(dhīḥ, f. 1st s.)(upajāyate ”jan IV C. Āt.)(saugata-)(ādīnām, m. 6th pl.)(sambhūtiḥ, f. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(apāya-)(duḥkha-)(yāgāt, m. 5th s.)(anvitāt, m. 5th s.)(vadha-)(prāṇin-)
body.translated_text: For example, an unshakeable conviction arises in the followers of the <s>Sugata</s> (Buddha) and others [that] from sacrifice involving the killing of living beings, there arises suffering and destruction.

body.text:
2393.
(ca*)(asyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(dhiyaḥ, f. 6th s.)(na*)(dṛśyate ”dṛś Pass.)(kācit, f. 1st s.)(bādhā, f. 1st s.)(samprati*)(cet*)(śaṅkyā, f. 1st s.)(kadācit*)(kvacit*)(sā, f. 1st s.)(samā, f. 1st s.)(veda-)(vākye, n. 7th s.)(api*)
body.translated_text: And no refutation of this conviction is seen at present. If it is [said to be merely] suspected [of error] at some time or in some case, that same [suspicion] equally [applies] to Vedic statements as well.

body.text:
2394.
(yadi*)(vedaḥ, m. 1st s.)(prakāśayet ”kāś Caus. Opt.)(sva-)(artham, m. 2nd s.)(svayam*)(nirapekṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(saṅketa-)(adhīna-)(icchā-)(nara-)(tadā*)(yujyate ”yuj Pass.)(pramāṇam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: If the <s>Veda</s> were to illuminate its own meaning by itself, independent of the conventions, desires, and [interpretation of] humans, then it would be a valid means of knowledge.

body.text:
2395.
(hi*)(tadā*)(na*)(muñcati ”muc VI C.)(nijam, m. 2nd s.)(artham, m. 2nd s.)(api*)(ākhyāyamānaḥ ”khyā Pass., m. 1st s.)(anyathā*)(buddhibhiḥ, m. 3rd pl. [bv. cpd.])(moha-)(māna-)(ādi-)(doṣa-)
body.translated_text: For then it would not abandon its own meaning, even when being expounded otherwise by those whose intellects are [afflicted by] faults of delusion, pride, and the like.

2396.
(yasmāt, n. 5th s.)(aram*)(utpādayati ”pad Caus.)(dhiyam, f. 2nd s.)(tat-)(viṣayām, f. 2nd s. [bv. cpd.])(eva*)(tu*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(na*)(dyotayati ”dyut Caus.)(aparam, m. 2nd s.)(artham, m. 2nd s.)(iṣṭam, m. 2nd s.)(puruṣaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: Since it is fully capable of producing cognition pertaining to its own subject matter alone; but this [Veda] does not illuminate any other meaning desired by humans.

body.text:
2397.
(tu*)(apekṣāyām, f. 7th s.)(icchāyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(nara-)(na*)(bhidyate ”bhid Pass.)(pauruṣeyāt, n. 5th s.)(hi*)(dyotanam, n. 1st s.)(āyattam, n. 1st s.)(tat-)(api*)(sā, f. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(viparyastā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: But when there is dependence on the desire of humans, it does not differ from what is man-made. For the illumination is dependent on that [human desire]; and that [illumination] too may be erroneous.

body.text:
2398.
(apica*)(yathā*)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)(apauruṣeyasya, m. 6th s.)(prākṛtam, n. 1st s.)(arthatvam, n. 1st s.)(satya-)(kim*)(na*)(āśaṅkyate ”śaṅk Pass.)(evam*)(asatyatvam, n. 1sts.)
body.translated_text: Moreover, just as natural meaningfulness is claimed for what is authorless — in the same way, why is not untruthfulness also suspected?

body.text:
2399.
Indeed(hi*)(asya, m. 6th s.)(satyatā, f. 1st s.)(svataḥ* [-tas suff.])(hetutvāt, n. 5th s.)(bodhasya, m. 6th s.)(artha-)(satya-)(evam*)(śaṅkyate ”śaṅk Pass.)(svataḥ* [-tas suff.])(hetutvam, n. 1st s.)(bodhe, m. 7th s.)(api*)(mithyātva-)
body.translated_text: Indeed, if its truthfulness by its own nature is [claimed] on the ground that it is the cause of cognition of true meaning, then in the same way, its being the cause of cognition of false meaning is also suspected by its own nature.

body.text:
2400.
(kiñca*)(yadi*)(vaḥ, 6th pl.)(nirbandhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(veda-)(pramāṇatve, n. 7th s.)(tadā*)(yatnaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vidhīyatām ”dhā Pass. Imperative 3p s.)(kartṛkatva-)(nirdoṣa-)(ādau, m. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: Furthermore, if you insist on the <s>Veda</s> being a valid means of knowledge, then let effort be directed first toward [establishing] the flawlessness of the author.

body.text:
2401.
(kṛtaḥ, m. 1st s.)(nirdoṣeṇa, m. 3rd s.)(kartrā, m. 3rd s.)(ca*)(dyotyamānaḥ ”dyut Caus. Pass., m. 1st s.)(asmin, m. 7th s.)(loke, m. 7th s.)(adoṣaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(prakāśakaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(sādhanaḥ, m. 1st s.)(jñāna-)(bhūta-)(artha-)
body.translated_text: [A scripture] composed by a flawless author, and being illuminated in this world by faultless expositors, is a means [of knowledge] of true objects — [producing] knowledge of real things.

2402.
(hi*)(tathā*)(su-viniścitāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(sat-)(vācaḥ, f. 1st pl.)(yuktānām, m. 6th pl.)(prajñā-)(kṛpā-)(ādi-)(api*)(pauruṣeyyaḥ, f. 1st pl.)(hetavaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(yathā-artha-)(jñāna-)
body.translated_text: For thus the well-ascertained and true words of those endowed with wisdom, compassion, and the like — though man-made — are causes of knowledge that accords with reality.

body.text:
2403.
(tu*)(na*)(kāri, n. 1st s.)(yathā-artha-)(jñāna-)(eva*)(iti*)(akṛtam, n. 1st s.)(nara-)(hi*)(dṛṣṭā, f. 1st s.)(dāva-vahni-)(ādeḥ, m. 6th s.)(hetutā, f. 1st s.)(mithyā-)(jñāne, n. 7th s.)(api*)
body.translated_text: But [the objection that] what is man-made alone cannot produce knowledge that accords with reality — this is unfounded, for the capacity of a forest fire and the like to cause even false cognition has been observed.

(sati, m. 7th s.)(āloke, m. 7th s.)(vahni-)(nīla-)(saraḥ-jam, n. 1st s.)(raktam, n. 1st s.)(cet*)(vahni-)(ādiḥ, m. 1st s.)(upapadyate ”pad Pass.)(hetuḥ, m. 1st s.)(tat-)(kṛtakatvāt, n. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 2404. When there is firelight, a blue lotus appears red; if fire and the like are accepted as the cause of that, because of being produced —

(kim*)(vaikṛtakatvam, n. 1st s.)(arthānām, m. 6th pl.)(nibandhanam, n. 1st s.)(mithyā-)(jñāna-)(hi*)(evam*)(dhūmaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(eva*)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(yathāvat, n. 1st s.)(dyotakam, n. 1st s.)(agneḥ, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2405. Is the createdness of objects the basis of false cognition? Indeed, thus smoke would not be a proper indicator of fire.

body.translated_text: 2406. And even so, an authorless (<s>apauruṣeya</s>) <s>Veda</s> is not the basis of correct cognition; that contrivance of this [argument] is indeed in vain.

(ca*)(tataḥ*)(sādhanam, n. 1st s.)(apauruṣeyatva-)(vyakti-)(nityatva-)(nitya-)(yogaḥ, m. 1st s.)(śabda-)(artha-)(upavarṇitaḥ, m. 1st s.)(eva*)(vyarthaḥ, m. 1st s.)

(tena, m. 3rd s.)(eva*)(asmākam, 6th pl.)(na*)(guruḥ, m. 1st s.)(ādāraḥ, m. 1st s.)(pratikṣepe, m. 7th s.)(tat-)(hi*)(kaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kuryāt ”kṛ VIII C. Opt.)(niṣedhanam, n. 2nd s.)(upayogasya, m. 6th s. [bv. cpd.])(aprastuta-)

body.translated_text: 2415. But the inaccessibility [of the author] by all beings is doubtful; indeed, even what is suspected [to be inaccessible] — at some time, by some means of cognition, someone knows.

(tu*)(hi*)(tathā*)(agamyamānatvam, n. 1st s.)(svayam*)(vyabhicāri, n. 1st s.)(te, 6th s.)(antara-)(puruṣa-)(saṅkalpāt, m. 5th s.)(a-bhāvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tat-)(na*)(niścitaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2417. But indeed, such inaccessibility is itself deviant for you; because of the conjecture of another person, the non-existence of that [author] is not ascertained.

(ca*)(adhyakṣataḥ* [-tas suff.])(adhyetāraḥ, m. 1st pl.)(matāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(karttāraḥ, m. 1st pl.)(hi*)(na*)(yuktāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(te, m. 1st pl.)(vyañjakāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(vyakti-)(nityānām, n. 6th pl.)(asambhavāt, m. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 2418. And the reciters are held to be [merely] supervisors, [not] authors; indeed, they are not suitable [as] manifestors, because of the impossibility of permanent manifestations.

body.translated_text: 2419. The arising of those [sounds] whose nature is apprehensible — through their operation — even when they exist [permanently], apprehension follows even before [the operation].

body.translated_text: 2421. Because of having sequential form — like a drama, legend, and the like — of manifesting [sounds] — inference too comprehends the authorship (<s>pauruṣeyatva</s>) of the <s>Vedas</s>.

2422.

body.translated_text: 2422. Otherwise, because of permanence and from pervasion, there would be no sequential form; and there is no sequence; if manifestation [is claimed to be] permanent — because of the impossibility of manifestation.

body.translated_text: 2423. The validity as a means of cognition of scripture (<s>āgama</s>), analogy (<s>upamāna</s>), and <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) has been previously refuted; therefore, the presentation of those is not justified.

body.text:

body.translated_text: 2424. The authorlessness of the <s>Veda</s>, [aimed at] the cessation of invalidity, is desired to be meaningful; but that, because of being a real entity, is to be established by proofs.
