body.translated_text: [Verse 2471] For indeed, this entire establishment of word-meaning [relationship] has been demonstrated in detail previously [to be] disrupted — because of the impossibility of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion),

body.text:
2472.
(ca*)(nityam, n. 1st s.)(gotvam, n. 1st s.)(apāstam, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(sambandhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(api*)(kalpitaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ākāśa-)(aṇu-)(ādi-)(api*)(kṣiptam, n. 1st s.)(tat*)(hetu-)(udāharaṇe, n. 1st d.)(na*)
body.translated_text: [Verse 2472] And the eternal <s>gotva</s> (cow-universal) has been discarded, and the [word-meaning] connection too is [merely] imagined; [the theories of] <s>ākāśa</s> (space), <s>aṇu</s> (atom), and the like have also been rejected — [thus] the reason and example [of the opponent] are not [established],

body.text:
2473.
(cireṇa*, n. 3rd s. [adv.])(pratipadyatām ”pad IV C. Imperative Āt. 3p s.)(vācitvam, n. 2nd s.)(gotva-)(niṣkṛṣṭa-)(bhrāntaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(janaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(adhyavasāyataḥ* [-tas suff.])(eka-)(rūpatayā, f. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: [Verse 2473] Let [the opponent] eventually ascertain the expressiveness [of words] — [the notion of] cow-universal [has been] extracted [and refuted]; by deluded people, through determining [sounds] as having a single form,

body.text:
2474.
(tu*)(bhāvataḥ* [-tas suff.])(kṣaṇikatvāt, n. 5th s.)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(na*)(eva*)(sthiraḥ, m. 1st s.)(api*)(tāvat-)(kālam, m. 2nd s.)(iti*)(kim*)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(sthitiḥ, f. 1st s.)(paścāt*)(api*)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)
body.translated_text: [Verse 2474] But in reality, because of momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>), this [sound] is not stable even for that much time — then why is its persistence afterwards also accepted?

body.text:
2475.
(ghaṭa-)(ādau, m. 7th s.)(api*)(eva*)(na*)(kiñcit, n. 1st s.)(kāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(nāśasya, m. 6th s.)(iti*)(idam, n. 1st s.)(api*)(nirdiṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(kim*)(tat*)(bhaviṣyati ”bhū Future)(śabde, m. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: [Verse 2475] In [the case of] a pot and the like too, there is no cause of destruction whatsoever — this too has been stated [before]; how will that [apply] to sound?

body.text:
2476.
(viplave, m. 7th s.)(pratyabhijñāyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(upapāditaḥ, m. 1st s.)(purastāt*)(dharmaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vibhidyate ”bhid Pass.)(bhedāt, m. 5th s.)(deśa-)(kāla-)(prayoktṝṇām, m. 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: [Verse 2476] In the overthrow of recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>), [this] has been established previously — the property [of sound] is differentiated because of the difference of place, time, and speakers,

body.text:
2477.
(ṣaḍja-)(ṛṣabha-)(gāndhāra-)(pañcama-)(ādi-)(prabhedataḥ* [-tas suff.])(pratyakṣataḥ* [-tas suff.])(hi*)(vijñātā, f. 1st s.)(ga-)(vyaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(aparā, f. 1st s.)(sphuṭā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: [Verse 2477] Through the distinction of <s>ṣaḍja</s>, <s>ṛṣabha</s>, <s>gāndhāra</s>, <s>pañcama</s>, and the like — by direct perception, another distinct individual of the [sound] 'ga' is clearly known

body.text:
2478.
(eṣā, f. 1st s.)(saṃsthitiḥ, f. 1st s.)(bheda-)(yuktā, f. 1st s.)(bhedena, m. 3rd s.)(vyañjaka-)(iti*)(asti ”as II C.)(na*)(vyaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(nityeṣu, m. 7th s.)(abhidhāsyate ”dhā Future Pass.)(purastāt*)
body.translated_text: 2478. This arrangement, endowed with differentiation — [the opponent says:] 'through the differentiating manifester' — [but] there is no manifestation (<s>vyakti</s>) in eternal [entities]; this will be stated further on.

body.text:
2479.
(ca*)(sāmānyam, n. 1st s.)(gatvam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)(vāstavam, n. 1st s.)(vyatiriktam, n. 1st s.)(kāra-)(ga-)(ataḥ*)(sādhyatā-)(siddha-)(durvārā, f. 1st s.)(prayoge, m. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 2479. And the universal <s>gatva</s> (ga-ness) is not accepted as real [or] as distinct from the phoneme 'ga'; therefore, [the fault of] the provable being [already] established is unavoidable in practice.

body.text:
2480.
(cet*)(iti*)(samāśrayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(gatvasya, n. 6th s.)(na*)(ittham*)(eva*)(api*)(ātmakasya, n. 6th s.)(apoha-)(anya-)(na*)(evam*)(āptitaḥ* [-tas suff.])(āśraya-)(asiddhatā-)
body.translated_text: 2480. [Objection:] 'If thus, the basis [of the proof lies in] <s>gatva</s> (ga-ness)' — [Reply:] Not so; even for [<s>gatva</s>] that has this very nature — [which is] the exclusion of what is other (<s>apoha</s>) — [there is] no attainment from the basis — [hence] the unestablished basis [fallacy].

body.text:
2481.
(varṇa-)(ga-)(bhāvataḥ* [-tas suff.])(parāvṛtta-)(a-gakāra-)(kasya, m. 6th s.)(dharmiṇaḥ, m. 6th s.)(dharmaḥ, 1st s. m.)(a-nirūpyatvam, n. 1st s.)(buddhi-)(anya-)(ga-)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)
body.translated_text: 2481. [The property] of being undeterminable by a cognition of another [instance of] 'ga' — of which subject (<s>dharmin</s>) — that has turned away from being a non-ga-phoneme — [and turned away] from the nature of the <s>varṇa</s> (phoneme) 'ga' — could this <s>dharma</s> (property) [belong]?

body.text:
2482.
(ca*)(sarvā, f. 1st s.)(vāstavī, f. 1st s.)(anumā, f. 1st s.)(apekṣate ”īkṣ I C. Āt.)(dṛṣṭānta-)(ādi, n. 2nd s.)(siddham, n. 2nd s.)(dvaya-)(tataḥ*)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(dṛṣṭāntaḥ, m. 1st s.)(bhāk, m. 1st s.)(asiddhi-)(dharmin-)
body.translated_text: 2482. And every valid real inference requires an established example and the like — [established in] both [aspects]; therefore, by that [requirement], the example shares the unestablished subject [fallacy].

body.text:
2483.
(sarvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(prayatnaḥ, m. 1st s.)(te, 6th s.)(siddhaye, f. 4th s.)(ekatva-)(kāra-)(ga-)(ca*)(tatra*)(bādhā, f. 1st s.)(pratyakṣa-)(durnivārā, f. 1st s.)(uditā, f. 1st s.)(tava, 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2483. All this effort of yours is for the establishment of the oneness of the phoneme 'ga'; and therein, the refutation by direct perception, which has been stated, is irresistible for you.

body.text:
2484.
(ca*)(ime, m. 1st pl.)(pratyayāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(varṇa-)(ga-)(hyastana-)(adyatana-)(ādyāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(bhāvena, m. 3rd s.)(krama-)(na*)(eka-)(arthāḥ, m. 1st pl. [bv. cpd.])(vat*)(buddhi-)(rasa-)(rūpa-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 2484. And these cognitions — of yesterday's and today's phoneme 'ga' and the like — because of their sequential nature, do not have a single object — like cognitions of taste, form, and the like.

body.text:
2485.
(ataḥ*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(ekaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sadā*)(sthitaḥ, m. 1st s.)(varṇaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(siddhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(dvaya-)(nityatvam, n. 1st s.)(kalpitam, n. 1st s.)(asya, m. 6th s.)(eva*)(kalpitasya, m. 6th s.)(apopha-)
body.translated_text: 2485. Therefore, this single phoneme [as] always abiding is not established in both [aspects]; the permanence of this [phoneme], which is itself imagined, is [merely] imagined through <s>apoha</s> (exclusion).

body.text:
2486.
(velāyām, f. 7th s.)(śabda-)(upalambha-)(vāyavaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(vartinaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(paryanta-)(karṇa-)(kāriṇaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(saṃskāra-)(śrotra-)(na*)(avagamyante ”gam Pass III p. pl.)
body.translated_text: 2486. At the time of the apprehension of sound — the winds (<s>vāyus</s>) that abide at the periphery of the ear, which produce the conditioning of the auditory organ (<s>śrotra</s>) — are not perceived.

body.text:
2487.
(yadā*)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pratīyate ”ī Pass.)(śrotrāt, n. 5th s.)(saṃskṛtāt, n. 5th s.)(nādena, m. 3rd s.)(bodhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(upaśleṣataḥ* [-tas suff.])(tat-)(bādhyate ”bādh Pass.)(adhyakṣeṇa, n. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 2487. When sound is perceived from the ear that has been conditioned by <s>nāda</s> (sound vibration) — the knowledge of it [arises] from [its] contact — [yet] this is refuted by direct perception.

body.text:
2488.
(yat*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(rūpeṇa, n. 3rd s.)(tikta-)(ādi-)(pravṛttam, n. 1st s.)(madhura-)(ādiṣu, m. 7th pl.)(nirviṣayam, n. 1st s.)(tathā*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(śabda-)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)
body.translated_text: 2488. That cognition which operates with the form of bitter and the like in [things that are actually] sweet and the like — such cognition of sound would likewise be objectless.

body.text:
2489.
(hi*)(bhedāt, m. 5th s.)(druta-)(madya-)(ādi-)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(avabhāsate ”bhās I C. Āt.)(anyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ca*)(katham*)(na*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(tādrūpya-)(a-)(tat-)(rūpe, n. 7th s.)(nirviṣayam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2489. For, because of the difference [in sound-quality] from liquor and the like that are in a fluid state — the sound does not appear [the same]; and how is a cognition that has [the appearance of] that form [when directed at what] does not have that form — not objectless?

body.text:
2490.
(vacaḥ, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(vetti ”vid II C.)(tam, m. 2nd s.)(eva*)(artham, m. 2nd s.)(anyathā*)(vyāhatam, n. 1st s.)(saṃvittau, f. 7th s.)(anya-)(ākārasya, m. 6th s.)(katham*)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(hi*)(arthaḥ, m. 1st s.)(viditaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2490. [The opponent says:] '[The cognition] knows that very meaning as speech' — [but] otherwise, [this] is self-contradictory; in a cognition having another form — how is that meaning known?

body.text:
2491.
(jñāne, n. 7th s.)(nirākāre, n. 7th s.)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(te, 6th s.)(dhruvam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(bāhya-)(ākāraḥ, m. 1sts.)(ca*)(bāhyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(ātmā, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(tat-)(iti*)(tathā*)(katham*)(vidyate ”vid Pass.)
body.translated_text: 2491. In a formless cognition — for you — certainly the external form [is the object]; and [what is] external is not the self of that [cognition] — so how is it known?

body.text:
2492.
(api*)(pakṣe, m. 7th s.)(jñāna-)(sa-)(ākāra-)(jñāne, n. 7th s.)(sambhūtau, f. 7th s.)(nirbhāsa-)(anurūpataḥ* [-tas suff.])(bāhya-)(ākāra-)(arthaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ucyate ”vac Pass.)(viditaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2492. Also, in the position of cognition having form — when the manifestation [arises] in cognition — in conformity with the appearance — the object having an external form is said to be known.

body.text: 2493.--Here (iha*)(tu*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(pravarttate ”vṛt I C. Āt.)(anurūpeṇa, n. 3rd s.)(bāhya-)(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(sthitam, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(cittam, n. 1st s.)(bhrāntam, n. 1st s.)(nirviṣayam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2493. But here, the cognition does not operate in conformity with the external [object]; therefore, all [this] is established — [namely,] that consciousness is erroneous [and] objectless.

body.text:
2494.
(ca*)(na*)(yuktaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sat-bhāvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vyañjaka-)(viśeṣataḥ* [-tas suff.])(nitye, m. 7th s.)(ataḥ*)(na*)(bhinnāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(dhiyaḥ, f. 1st pl.)(dhanau, m. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 2494. And the existence of a manifester (<s>vyañjaka</s>) is not justified in [the case of what is] eternal, by [any] distinction; therefore, the cognitions are not differentiated in [what is like] a wealth [of uniformity].

body.text:
2495.
(hi*)(yathā*)(pradīpaḥ, m. 1st s.)(niyacchati ”yam I C.)(śaktim, f. 2nd s.)(artham, m. 2nd s.)(grahaṇa-)(ghaṭa-)(ādi-)(tathā*)(dhvaniḥ, m. 1st s.)(śrotre, n. 7th s.)(upalabdhaye, f. 4th s.)(śabda-)
body.translated_text: 2495. For just as a lamp bestows the capacity to apprehend objects such as a pot and the like — so too, <s>dhvani</s> (sound vibration) [serves] for the apprehension of <s>śabda</s> (sound) in the ear.

body.text:
2496.
(cet*)(saṃsthitaḥ, m. 1st s.)(prakṛti-)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(yogyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(upalabdhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(śrotra-)(tat*)(kim-artham*, m. 2nd s. [adv.])(na*)(upalabhyate ”labh Pass.)(api*)(śrotre, n. 7th s.)(asaṃskṛte, n. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 2496. [Objection:] 'If <s>śabda</s> (sound), established [as eternal] by its own nature, is suitable [for being] apprehended by the auditory organ — then why is it not apprehended even when the ear is unconditioned?'

body.text:
2497.
(yogya-)(kāraṇa-)(sat-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(upalambhanam, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(tat-)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(iva*)(velāyām, f. 7th s.)(sat-bhāva-)(saṃskṛta-)(śrotra-)
body.translated_text: 2497. Because of the existence of a suitable cause — there would indeed be apprehension of it — at the time when the ear has been conditioned — just as [there would be in] the existence of that [sound].

body.text:
2498.
(cet*)(na*)(yogyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(upalabdhau, f. 7th s.)(katham*)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(api*)(paścāt*)(ca*)(bhāve, m. 7th s.)(jñātaḥ, m. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(aparaḥ, m. 1st s.)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(yogī, m. 1st s.)(yogyatā-)
body.translated_text: 2498. If [the sound] is not suitable for apprehension — how could it be [apprehended] even later? And in [its mere] existence, another <s>śabda</s> (sound) that is known [later] would be [something different] — endowed with suitability —

body.text:
2499.
(tu*)(atha*)(api*)(paścāt*)(na*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(bhāvi, n. 1st s.)(tat-)(bala-)(tat*)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(utpādaḥ, m. 1st s.)(saṃskṛta-)(śravaṇa-)(ādibhyaḥ, m. 5th pl.)(varṇyate ”varṇ Pass.)
body.translated_text: 2499. But then, even later, the cognition having the force of that [conditioning] would not arise; the origination of that [cognition] from the conditioned auditory organ and the like is described [by you].

body.text:
2500.
(evam*)(śabdasya, m. 6th s.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(agrāhyatā, f. 1st s.)(anupayogataḥ* [-tas suff.])(tasmin, n. 7th s.)(evam*)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(na*)(asti ”as II C.)(kaścit, m. 1st s.)(viśeṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(rasa-)(ādibhyaḥ, m. 5th pl.)
body.translated_text: 2500. Thus, <s>śabda</s> (sound) would be ungraspable — because of [its] being useless; in that case, there is no distinction of this [sound] from taste and the like.

body.text:
2501.
(vā*)(nāma*)(idam, n. 1st s.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(sva-bhāvam, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(bodha-)(śabda-)(janitam, n. 1st s.)(taiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(saṃskṛta-)(śravaṇa-)(ādibhiḥ, m. 3rd s.)(nirāśaṃsaiḥ, m. 3rd s.)(śabda-)
body.translated_text: 2501. Or rather, this cognition — having the nature of informing about sound — [is] produced by those [elements]: the conditioned auditory organ and the like, which are indifferent to <s>śabda</s> (sound).

body.text:
2502.
(tu*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(rūpaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(jñeya-)(tat-)(jñāna-)(yathāpi*)(anuvarttate ”vṛt I C. Āt.)(iti*)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(anuvṛttiḥ, f. 1st s.)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(vijñānasya, n. 6th s.)(api*)(te, 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2502. But this [cognition], having the form of the knowable — [you say] it follows that [knowable] cognition; [and therefore] the sound would be [its object] — [but then] of your cognition too, there would be [such] conformity.

body.text:
2503.
(hi*)(anyathā*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(anuvṛttam, n. 1st s.)(tu*)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(anuvarttate ”vṛt I C. Āt.)(tat-)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(jñeyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(iti*)(evam*)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(parā*)(vyāhatiḥ, f. 1st s.)(tava, 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2503. For otherwise, the cognition has not [actually] conformed — but he [the opponent says] 'it conforms'; [if you say] 'therefore sound is the knowable [object]' — thus there would be a supreme self-contradiction for you.

body.text:
2504.
(tau, m. 1st d.)(sva-bhāvau, m. 1st du. [bv. cpd.])(jñāna-)(jñeya-)(hi*)(baddhau, m. 1st d.)(iva*)(śṛṅkhalayā, f. 3rd s.)(eka-)(bhāve, m. 7th s.)(dvitīyasya, m. 6th s.)(prāptiḥ, f. 1st s.)(avyabhicārataḥ [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 2504. For cognition and the knowable — having the nature of those two — [are] bound as if by a chain; in the existence of one, the attainment of the second [follows] without deviation.

body.text:
2505.
(eva*)(sambaddhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(jñāna-)(utpādya-)(saṃskṛta-)(śravaṇa-)(api*)(śrotra-)(asaṃskaraṇe, n. 7th s.)(iti*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(sphuṭam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(ākṣipyate ”kṣip Pass.)
body.translated_text: 2505. [Sound,] connected [with cognition] — to be produced by cognition — even when the ear has been conditioned by the auditory organ — in the absence of conditioning [of the ear] — the cognition is clearly rejected.

body.text:
2506.
(cet*)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(ātmā, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(jñeya-)(tat-)(vat*)(rasa-)(ādi-)(a-)(ātma-)(tat-)(sati, n. 7th s.)(tathā*)(śrotra-)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(sva-bhāvam, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(bodha-)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 2506. If <s>śabda</s> (sound) does not have the nature of the knowable — like taste and the like, which do not have that nature — in that case, even with the auditory organ, the cognition having the nature of informing [about sound] would not arise.

body.text:
2507.
(vā*)(kaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sambandhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(jñānasya, n. 6th s.)(śabdena, m. 3rd s.)(yataḥ*)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)(hi*)(rūpam, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(bodha-)(tat-)(śabda-)(na*)(tādātmyam, n. 1st s.)(vibhedataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 2507. Or, what connection of cognition with <s>śabda</s> (sound) is [thereby] accepted? For [the cognition] having the form of informing about sound — [there is] no identity [with sound], because of [their] difference.

body.text:
2508.
(na*)(ca*)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(utpattiḥ, f. 1st s.)(tat-)(śabdasya, m. 6th s.)(ajanakatvataḥ* [-tas suff.])(tat-)(utpattau, f. 7th s.)(niyamāt, m. 5th s.)(sā, f. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(bhāvinī, f. 1st s.)(sadā*)
body.translated_text: 2508. Nor is the origination of that [cognition] from that <s>śabda</s> (sound) — because of <s>śabda</s>'s being a non-producer; because of the restriction [that cognition arises only] from the origination of that [sound] — that [cognition] would always be present.

body.text:
2509.
(evam*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(viṣayam, n. 1st s.)(tat-)(vā*)(utpadyeta, ”pad IV C. Opt.Āt.)(sadā*)(vā*)(na*)(iti*)(sthite, n. 7th s.)(eka-ānte, m. 7th s.)(kalpanā, f. 1st s.)(saṃskāra-)(śrotra-)(vyarthā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2509. Thus, the cognition would either always arise having that [sound] as its object, or never — when one extreme is established, the conceptual construction of the conditioned ear is pointless.

body.text:
2510.
(hi*)(jñāna-)(sambhavaḥ, m. 1st s.)(eva*)(saṃskāre, m. 7th s.)(sat, m. 7th s.)(kādācitke, m. 7th s.)(parikalpanā, f. 1st s.)(saṃskāra-)(śobheta ”śubh I C. Opt. Āt.)(iti*)(kādācit*)
body.translated_text: 2510. For the origination of cognition is [only coherent] when the conditioning exists as occasional; the postulation of [occasional] conditioning would be appropriate [only] if [the cognition is also] occasional.

body.text:
2511.
(ca*)(saṃskāraḥ, m. 1st s.)(lakṣaṇaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(śakti-)(avaseyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kārya-)(jñāna-)(ca*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(a-bhāvi, n. 1st s.)(sadā*)(yadi* vā*)(bhāvi, n. 1st s.)(sarvadā*)
body.translated_text: 2511. And the conditioning, characterized by capacity (<s>śakti</s>), is to be inferred from its effect — cognition; and that cognition either never arises or always arises —

body.text:
2512.
(katham*)(nāma*)(sūcayet ”sūc X C. Opt.)(kādācitkam, m. 2nd s.)(saṃskāram, m. 2nd s.)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(ataḥ*)(uttaram, n. 1st s.)(saṃskārāt, m. 5th s.)(śrotra-)(na*)(sādhu*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(prakāśitam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2512. How then would it indicate an occasional conditioning? Therefore, [the thesis that cognition arises] from the conditioning of the ear is not well-established.

body.text:
2513.
(śaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(ādhīyate ”dhā Pass.)(śrotre, n. 7th s.)(ca*)(yadi*)(avyatirekiṇī, f. 1st s.)(tataḥ*)(nityatvam, n. 1st s.)(vyomnaḥ, n. 6th s.)(vā*)(diśaḥ, f. 6th s.)(hīyeta ”hā Pass. Opt.)(janmataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 2513. And if the capacity deposited in the ear is non-different [from the ear] — then, because of the permanence of space or the regions — it would fail [to explain occasional cognition] from [its very] origination.

body.text:
2514.
(ca*)(saṃskṛteḥ, f. 6th s.)(avyatiriktatvāt, n. 5th s.)(bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(nityatvam, n. 1st s.)(vat*)(bhāva-)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(janyam, n. 1st s.)(tat-)(sarvadā*)
body.translated_text: 2514. And because of the non-difference from the conditioning — because of [the ear's] existence [as permanent] — like the existence [of the ear], the permanence [of the conditioning would follow]; by that, the cognition that is to be produced from it would [arise] always.

body.text:
2515.
(tu*)(vyatireke, m. 7th s.)(upapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(na*)(sambandhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(iti*)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(ca*)(śrotrasya, n. 6th s.)(akārakatvam, n. 1st s.)(jñāna-)(samudbhavāt, m. 5th s.)(śakteḥ, f. 5th s.).
body.translated_text: 2515. But in the case of negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>), the relation is not tenable — thus; and the non-agenthood of that organ of hearing [is established] from the arising of knowledge from [its own] capacity.

body.text:
2516.
(pakṣa-)(antaram, n. 1st s.)(tataḥ*)(vinirmuktam, n. 1st s.)(bheda-)(abheda-)(vyastam, n. 1st s.)(uttaram, n. 1st s.)(saṃskārāt, m. 5th s.)(śrotra-)(ucyate ”vac Pass.)(asaṃskṛtatayā, f. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 2516. Another alternative (<s>pakṣa</s>) — freed from [the problems of] difference and non-difference — the reply [is]: it is said [that] from the conditioning (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of the ear, [and yet] by [its] unconditioned nature,

body.text:
2517.
(etena, n. 3rd s.)(eva*)(niṣeddhavyā, f. 1st s.)(saṃskṛtiḥ, f. 1st s.)(viṣaya-)(ubhaya-)(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(nirāspadā, f. 1st s.)(sartvathā*)(api*)(abhivyaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(nityeṣu, m. 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 2517. By this very [reasoning], the conditioning of both — the object and [the sense organ] — is to be rejected; therefore, manifestation (<s>abhivyakti</s>) in eternal [entities] is in every way without a basis.

body.text:
2518.
(ca*)(tataḥ*)(kecit, m. 1st pl.)(dīrgha-)(hrasva-)(krama-)(ādayaḥ)(ye, m. 1st pl.)(pravibhajyante ”bhaj Pass III p. pl.)(āśritya* ”śri)(vyaktim, f. 2nd s.)(api*)(sarve, m. 1st pl.)(te, m. 1st pl.)(nirāspadāḥ, m. 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 2518. And therefore, whatever [properties] — long, short, sequence, and the like — are distinguished by depending on manifestation — all of them too are without a basis.

body.text:
2519.
(api*)(mātra-)(aprāpti-)(sāmye, n. 7th s.)(grahaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sarvasya, m. 6th s.)(niyama-)(sāmarthya-)(sthiteḥ, f. 5th s.)(yathā*)(lohasya, m. 6th s.)(ayaḥ-kāntenam. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 2519. Also, [if] in the equality of non-arrival of the <s>mātrā</s> (measure), [there would be] apprehension of everything — from the fixed capacity of restriction — just as [the magnet attracts] iron by the lodestone.

body.text:
2520.
(yadi*)(tatra*)(api*)(ākarṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(prāptyā, f. 3rd s.)(prabhā-)(ayaḥ-kānta-)(nanu*)(na*)(iyam, f. 1st s.)(prabhā, f. 1st s.)(dṛśyā, f. 1st s.)(katham*)(gamyate ”gam Pass.)(iti*)(asti ”as II C.)
body.translated_text: 2520. If [you say] the attraction there also [occurs] through the reaching of the radiance (<s>prabhā</s>) of the lodestone — [we reply:] surely this radiance is not visible — how is [its existence] inferred?

body.text:
2521.
(kasmāt, n. 5th s.)(sā, f. 1st s.)(prabhā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(samākarṣati ”kṛṣ I C.)(kāṣṭha-)(ādi-)(āptam, n. 2nd s.)(cet*)(tat-)(śakti-)(niyatatvāt, n. 5th s.)(tat*)(samam, n. 1st s.)(aprāptau, f. 7th s.)(api*)
body.translated_text: 2521. Why does that radiance not attract wood and the like? If [you say] because of being restricted to that [particular] capacity — that is equal [to our position] even when there is no reaching.

body.text:
2522.
(gamyate ”gam Pass.)(dūra-)(madhya-)(samīpa-sthaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(akrameṇa, m. 3rd s.)(eva*)(sarveṣām, m. 6th s.)(jñāna-)(jātitaḥ* [-tas suff.])(anantaram*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(prayoga-)
body.translated_text: 2522. [Sound] is perceived by those situated at far, middle, and near [distances] — without sequence, immediately after the employment [of speech] — because of the nature of the cognition of all [hearers].

body.text:
2523.
(yathā*)(bhedena, m. 3rd s.)(dūra-)(āsanna-)(ādi-)(rūpam, n. 1st s.)(īkṣyate ”īkṣ Pass.)(aspaṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(spaṣṭa-)(eva*)(tathā*)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(vit, m. 1st s.)(manda-)(tīvra-)(ādi-)(śabde, m. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 2523. Just as a form at far, nearby, and other [distances] is seen as unclear or clear by [its] difference — so too there would be [cognition of] sound [as] faint, intense, and the like by one who knows.

body.text:
2524.
(katham*)(eka-)(ālambanatā, f. 1st s.)(matīnām, f. 6th pl.)(ābhānām, f. 6th pl.)(bhinna-)(cet*)(etat, n. 1st s.)(tulyam, n. 1st s.)(codyam, n. 1st s.)(dhiyām, f. 6th pl.)(rūpa-)(vādinām, m. 6th pl.)(bāhya-)(artha-)
body.translated_text: 2524. How can there be a single object (<s>ālambana</s>) for cognitions that have different appearances? If [you raise] this objection — the same objection [applies] to the proponents of external objects (<s>bāhyārtha</s>) regarding [their] cognitions of form.

body.text:
2525.
(tu*)(pakṣe, m. 7th s.)(grahaṇa-)(prāpti-)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(śabda-)(megha-)(ādike, m. 7th s.)(iti*)(na*)(vicchinnaḥ, m. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(vat*)(pakṣa-)(abhyantara-)(karṇa-)
body.translated_text: 2525. But in the position of [sound] reaching the ear — the cognition [would arise] regarding sound, clouds, and the like — thus, [sound] would not be interrupted, like [sound arriving] within the ear canal.

body.text:
2526.
(tat*)(janakatvāt, n. 5th s.)(jñāna-)(iti*)(vicchinnaḥ, m. 1st s.)(śrotram, n. 1st s.)(yathā*)(manaḥ, n. 1st s.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(kāri, n. 1st s.)(aprāpya-)(na*)(anyathā*)(vat*)(tvac-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 2526. Because [the ear] generates cognition of that [sound] — the ear would be interrupted [in its hearing], like the mind (<s>manas</s>); [if the ear were] an organ that operates without contact — [it would be] no different from touch and the like.

body.text:
2527.
(teṣām, m. 6th pl.)(ye, m. 1st pl.)(prāhuḥ ”ah Perfect III p. pl.)(iti*)(manaḥ, n. 1st s.)(api*)(kāri, n. 1st s.)(prāpya-)(na*)(yujyate ”yuj Pass.)(cetaḥ, n. 1st s.)(stham, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(dūratara-)(mātrataḥ* [-tas suff.])(kṣaṇa-)
body.translated_text: 2527. For those who declare that even the mind operates through contact — [that is] not tenable; [for] the mind, which abides in [a place] far more distant, [would then need to be in contact with its object] merely [within] a moment.

body.text:
2528.
(tu*)(sādhanam, n. 1st s.)(kāritva-)(prāpya-)(yat, n. 1st s.)(bāhya-)(indriyatva-)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(vyabhicāri, n. 1st s.)(vijātīyāt, m. 5th s.)(anya-)(dharma-)(virodhāt, m. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 2528. But the proof of [the ear's] operating through contact — [such as] being an external sense organ and the like — that [proof] is deviant (<s>vyabhicārin</s>); because of the contradiction with other properties of a different kind.

body.text:
2529.
And *ca*)(vyatirekiṇaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(saṃyoga-)(vibhāga-)(pūrvam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(vyastāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(ca*)(vāyoḥ, m. 6th s.)(akṣaṇikatvāt, n. 5th s.)(na*)(yuktāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(avyatirekiṇaḥ, m. 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 2529. And [for those who propose] that conjunction and disjunction [of air particles occur] prior [to sound reaching the ear] — [they are] separately [refuted]; and because of the non-momentariness of air (<s>vāyu</s>) — [those who hold that position] are not justified, [for they cannot maintain both] invariable [and] variable [concomitance].

body.text:
2530.
(eva*)(ataḥ*)(aviśeṣatvāt, n. 5th s.)(na*)(gatiḥ, f. 1st s.)(asya, m. 6th s.)(a-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(vega-)(asau, m. 1st s.)(ataḥ*)(na*)(pratiṣṭhate ”sthā I C. Āt.)(yāvat-)(vegam*, m. 2nd s. [adv.])
body.translated_text: 2530. Therefore, because of the absence of distinction — there is no motion of this [air]; because of the absence of velocity — therefore, that [air] does not persist as long as [its] momentum [lasts].

body.text:
2531.
(cet*)(samprāptaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vyomani, n. 7th s.)(karṇa-)(karoti ”kṛ VIII C.)(śaktim, f. 2nd s.)(śrotre, n. 7th s.)(tat*)(kasmāt, n. 5th s.)(na*)(gatiḥ, f. 1st s.)(tat-)(vittau, f. 7th s.)(śabda-)(vat*)(ghāta-)(kaśā-)
body.translated_text: 2531. If [you say the air] having reached the ear-space produces capacity in the organ of hearing — then why is there no motion in that [ear] when perceiving [sound], like [the motion produced by] a whip-blow?

body.text:
2532.
(tathā*)(ayuktam, n. 1st s.)(vidaḥ, m. 6th s.)(kaśā-ghāta-)(antara-)(iti*)(avadhānam, n. 1st s.)(śabda-)(pratibadhnāti ”bandh IX C.)(vedanām, f. 1st s.)(etasya, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2532. Likewise, [it is] unjustified [that] the awareness of the whip-blow and the like by the knower [is separate from the sound]; [rather,] the attention to the sound obstructs the sensation of that [blow].

body.text:
2533.
(adaḥ, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(bhrāntiḥ, f. 1st s.)(yugapat-)(lāghavāt, n. 5th s.)(api*)(krama-)(bhāve, m. 7th s.)(na* kiñcit, n. 1st s.)(asmin, m. 7th s.)(vāyoḥ, m. 6th s.)(anupalambhanāt, n. 5th s.)(sarvathā*)(api*)
body.translated_text: 2533. [The perception of] 'that [is a sound]' is an error — [arising] from the simultaneity [of sound and sensation] and from parsimony; even in [the case of] sequential [occurrence], there is nothing [to prove your point], because of the complete non-apprehension of the air [as a carrier of sound].

body.text:
2534.
(atha*)(vāyuḥ, m. 1st s.)(ati-indriyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(iva*)(varṇyate ”varṇ Pass.)(kāṇādaiḥ, m. 6th pl.)(api*)(yuṣmābhiḥ, 3rd pl.)(tatra*)(āptiḥ, f. 1st s.)(spṛṣṭi-)(bhāṣye, n. 7th s.)(kṛtā, f. 1st s.)(kim-)
body.translated_text: 2534. Now, if air is described as supersensory — as by the <s>Kāṇādas</s> (followers of <s>Kaṇāda</s>) and by you as well — then has the attainment [of sound by the ear] been accomplished in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> (commentary) through touch?

body.text:
2535.
(vā*)(vāyuḥ, m. 1st s.)(astu ”as II C. Imperative 3p s.)(ati-indriyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tu*)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(vid, f. 1st s.)(spraṣṭavyasya, m. 6th s.)(uṣṇa-)(śīta-)(itara-)(gatasya, m. 6th s.)(tat-)(tat-)(yogin-)(vat*)(anya-)
body.translated_text: 2535. Or, let the air be supersensory; but there would be the cognition of what is tangible — hot, cold, or otherwise — [when air is present], as with other [tangible things] associated with those [qualities], like a <s>yogin</s>.

body.text:
2536.
(api*)(atha*)(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(na*)(vid, f. 1st s.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(ayogāt, m. 5th s.)(karṇa-śaṣkulyā, f. 3rd s.)(katham*)(nu*)(etat, n. 1st s.)(matam, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(na*)(samprāptaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vyoma, n. 2nd s.)(karṇa-)
body.translated_text: 2536. Now, if [you say] the cognition is not [the cognition] of that [air], because of [its] non-contact with the ear-canal — how then is this view [that air carries sound to the ear] [tenable]? [For the air] has not reached the ear-space.

body.text:
2537.
(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(iyam, f. 1st s.)(kalpanā, f. 1st s.)(dṛṣṭā, f. 1st s.)(śrotriya-)(nirnibandhanā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(prītaye, f. 4th s.)(viduṣām, m. 6th pl.)(iti*)(rājate ”rāj I C. Āt.)(eva*)(śrotriyeṣu, m. 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 2537. Therefore, this contrivance of the <s>Śrotriyas</s> (Vedic ritualists) is seen to be without foundation; it shines [only] among the <s>Śrotriyas</s> [themselves] — [but] does not delight the learned.

body.text:
2538.
(te, m. 1st pl.)(doṣāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(prāk*)(udīritāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(prati*)(tān, m. 2nd pl.)(ye, m. 1st pl.)(prāhuḥ ”ah Perfect III p. pl.)(nabhaḥ, n. 2nd s.)(niraṃśam, n. 2nd s.)(jñeyāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(samāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(api*)(śrotratve, n. 7th s.)(eka-)(niraṃśa-)(diś-)
body.translated_text: 2538. For those who declare space (<s>nabhas</s>) to be partless — the faults previously stated against them are to be known as equal [even when applied to] the organ of hearing [as] a partless, single direction (<s>diś</s>).

body.text:
2539.
(pakṣe, m. 7th s.)(nabhaḥ-)(eka-)(vyāpin-)(prakalpyate ”kḷp Caus. Pass.)(na*)(vibhāgaḥ, m. 1st s.)(iti*)(āśrayam, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(saṃskṛta-)(ca*)(anyat, n. 1st s.)(hi*)(tat, n. 1st sa.)(nabhaḥ, n. 1st s.)(ekam, n. 1sts.)(eva*)
body.translated_text: 2539. In the position [that the ear is] a single, all-pervading space — no division is postulated; and the substrate of what is conditioned is another [thing]; for that space is one alone.

body.text:
2540.
(śrotram, n. 1st s.)(ātmakam, n. 1st s.)(eka-)(vyoman-)(na*)(asti ”as II C.)(śaṣkuli, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(asaṃskṛta-)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(niyamaḥ, m. 1st s.)(saṃskāra-)(bhedena, m. 3rd s.)(adhiṣṭhāna-)(asthitaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2540. The organ of hearing, having the nature of a single space, does not have the ear-canal [as its seat when it is] unconditioned; therefore, the restriction [of hearing] through the difference of conditioning [at different] substrates is untenable.

body.text:
2541.
(tena, n. 3rd s.)(indriyam, n. 1st s.)(labdha-)(saṃskāram, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(ekasmin, n. 7th s.)(adhiṣṭhāne, n. 7th s.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(bodhakam, n. 1st s.)(deheṣu, m. 7th po.)(sarva-)(vādinaḥ, m. 6th s.)(indriya-)(eka-)
body.translated_text: 2541. By that, the sense organ that has received conditioning at a single substrate would be a cognizer in all bodies — [this is the consequence] for the proponent of a single sense organ.

body.text:
2542.
(iṣyatām ”iṣ Pass Imperative 3p s.)(vijñāna-)(utpattiḥ, f. 1st s.)(pradeśeṣu, m. 7th po.)(deha-)(puṃsām, m. 6th pl.)(kintu*)(te, 6th s.)(na*)(vaideśyam, n. 1st s.)(pradhāna-)(nabhasaḥ, n. 6th s.)(ekatvāt, n. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 2542. Let the arising of consciousness be accepted [as occurring] at the bodily locations of persons; but for that [space], there is no being-elsewhere — because of the oneness of the principal space.

body.text:
2543.
(ukte, n. 7th s.)(evam-)(iti*)(naḥ, 6th pl.)(atmā, m. 1st s.)(api*)(niṣpradeśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ca*)(api*)(vidan ”vid II C., m. 1st s.)(kārtsnyena, n. 3rd s.)(gṛhṇāti ”gṛh IX C.)(śarīre, n. 7th s.)(eva*)(duṣyati ”duṣ IV C.)
body.translated_text: 2543. When this has been stated — [the reply is:] our self (<s>ātman</s>) too, though without spatial location, and though knowing, grasps entirely within the body alone — [this too] is faulty.

body.text:
2544.
(avyavasthānam, n. 1st s.)(bādhirya-)(ādi-)(ca*)(etena, m. 3rd s.)(eva*)(hetunā, m. 3rd s.)(yujyate ”yuj Pass.)(eva*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(abhogyam, n. 1st s.)(anyasya, m. 6th s.)(hi*)(aviśeṣāt, m. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 2544. And the arrangement of deafness and the like [is explained] by this very reason; that [sense experience] is indeed not to be enjoyed by another — because of no distinction [between the two positions].

body.text:
2545.
(hi*)(atyakta-)(pūrva-)(rūpam, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(viśeṣa-)(sati, m. 7th s.)(anudaye, m. 7th s.)(katham*)(nāma*)(te, 6th s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(śrotram, n. 1st s.)(abhogyam, n. 1st s.)(aparasya, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2545. For when a particular [quality] does not arise — [and the organ] has a form that has not been previously abandoned — how indeed could the organ of hearing of that [person] be not-enjoyable by another?

body.text:
2546.
(nityatvāt, n. 5th s.)(anapekṣatvāt, n. 5th s.)(nabhaḥ-)(śrotram, n. 1st s.)(avaśīkṛtam, n. 1st s.)(dharma-)(adharma-)(ca*)(prasajyate ”sañj Pass.)(sarva-)(sadā*)(eva*)
body.translated_text: 2546. Because of [space's] eternality and independence — the organ of hearing, being space (<s>nabhas</s>), is [always] controlled by <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit); and [the hearing of] all [persons] at all times would absurdly follow.

body.text:
2547.
(nabhaḥ, n. 1st s.)(na*)(kadācana*)(upakāryam, n. 1st s.)(dharma-)(adharma-)(nityatvāt, n. 5th s.)(ca*)(asya, n. 6th s.)(a-bhāve-)(kāryatā-)(kā, f. 1st s.)(iyam, f. 1st s.)(vaśīkriyā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2547. Space is never to be benefited by <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>; and because of its eternality — in the absence of [any] effect-nature — what is this subjugation?

body.text:
2548.
(punaḥ*)(katham*)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(bhogyam, n. 1st s.)(śaktyā, f. 3rd s.)(mantra-)(auṣadha-)(ādi-)(hi*)(nityatvāt, n. 5th s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(na*)(pratipadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(viśeṣam, m. 2nd s.)(tebhyaḥ, n. 5th pl.)
body.translated_text: 2548. Again, how could [the organ of hearing] become enjoyable through the capacity of <s>mantras</s> (sacred formulas), medicines, and the like? For because of [space's] eternality, that [organ] does not receive any modification from those [agents].

body.text:
2549.
(tu*)(cet*)(api*)(adhiṣṭhāne, n. 7th s.)(anitye, n. 7th s.)(anityatā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(kṣaṇikā, f. 1st s.)(tat*)(atiśaya-)(ayogāt, m. 5th s.)(ātman-)(bādhirya-)(ādiḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(yujyate ”yuj Pass.)
body.translated_text: 2549. But if [you say] even at a non-eternal substrate, [the space-ear] is not momentarily non-eternal — [then,] because of the impossibility of enhancement (<s>atiśaya</s>) in the self (<s>ātman</s>), deafness and the like are not tenable.

body.text:
2550.
(vā*)(atiśayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(astu ”as II C. Imperative 3p s.)(tasmin, n. 7th s.)(tu*)(eṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(vidyate ”vid Pass.)(vyomni, n. 7th s.)(ca*)(na*)(sambandhāt, m. 5th s.)(adhiṣṭhāna-)(nityatvāt, n. 5th s.)(anapekṣaṇāt, n. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 2550. Or, let there be enhancement in that [substrate]; but this [enhancement] is not found in space; and because of the relation with the substrate — [and] because of the eternality [of space, which entails] independence — [enhancement is impossible].

body.text:
2551.
(ataḥ*)(atra*)(bādhirya-)(ādiḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(yujyate ”yuj Pass.)(dvārakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tat-)(api*)(api*)(nabhasaḥ, n. 6th s.)(bhāgavattve, n. 7th s.)(samam, n. 1st s.)(idam, n. 1st s.)(nityatāyām, f. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 2551. Therefore, deafness and the like, which operate through that [organ], are not tenable here; also, even if space had parts, this [problem] would be the same [when] eternality [is maintained].

body.text:
2552.
(tatra*)(eva*)(api*)(bhavataḥ, m. 6th s.)(anapakarṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(svāmitva-)(na*)(yuktam, n. 1st s.)(yadi*)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(api*)(samasti ”as II C.)(na*)(kṣaṇikatvam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2552. Even there, the non-withdrawal of ownership is not justified for you — if that [sound] too does not have momentariness.

body.text:
2553.
(kaḥ, m. 1st s.)(atiśayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(utpannaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tasyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(paścāt*)(yataḥ*)(asau, m. 1st s.)(apakṛṣṭaḥ, m. 1st s.)(svāmitvāt, n. 5th s.)(na*)(āpnuyāt ”āp V C. Opt.)(punaḥ*)
body.translated_text: 2553. What excellence has arisen for that [organ of hearing] afterwards, such that this [person], having been withdrawn from ownership, would not [be able to] obtain [it] again?

body.text:
2554.
(ca*)(yadā*)(na*)(saṃskṛtiḥ, f. 1st s.)(yujyate ”yuj Pass.)(evam*)(śrotre, n. 7th s.)(ca*)(śabde, m. 7th s.)(saṃskāra-)(anupapattitaḥ* [-tas suff.])(vikalpena, m. 3rd s.)(bheda-)(abheda-)
body.translated_text: 2554. And when modification (<s>saṃskṛti</s>) is not justified thus — in the organ of hearing and in sound — because of the impossibility of <s>saṃskāra</s> (conditioning), [whether analyzed] through the alternative of difference or non-difference.

body.text:
2555.
(hi*)(saṃskāre, m. 7th s.)(vyatireke, m. 7th s.)(śrotra-)(śabdau, m. 1st d.)(na*)(syātām ”as II C. Opt. 3p d.)(saṃskṛtau, m. 1st d.)(ca*)(tābhyām, m. 3rd d.)(na*)(kaścana, m. 1st s.)(sambandhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(saṃskārasya, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2555. For if the <s>saṃskāra</s> (conditioning) is distinct [from the organ of hearing and sound], the organ of hearing and sound would not be modified; and if they are modified [by it], there would be no connection whatsoever of the <s>saṃskāra</s> with those two.

body.text:
2556.
(hi*)(vibhinnasya, m. 6th s.)(sambandhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(tā, f. 1st s.)(kāraṇa-)(kārya-)(ca*)(tasyām, f. 7th s.)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(eva*)(sarvadā*)(hetoḥ, m. 6th s.)(sthiteḥ, f. 5th s.)(sarvadā*)
body.translated_text: 2556. For the connection of [something] distinct would be [only] a cause-effect relationship; and in that [relationship], this [effect] would always arise — because the cause is always present.

body.text:
2557.
(api*)(pakṣe, m. 7th s.)(anartha-)(antara-)(asau, m. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(nityaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vat*)(tat-)(tat*)(aśakya-)(kriyaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(prasajyate ”sañj Pass.)(nityam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2557. Even in the alternative [of non-difference], that [saṃskāra] would be — like that [eternal sound itself] — permanent and incapable of [any new] action; therefore, the consequence [would be that] cognition is always [present] — a meaningless [result].

body.text:
2558.
(tat*)(niyamaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sāmarthya-)(vāyu-)(ādeḥ, m. 6th s.)(na*)(upapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(viṣaya-)(kartavya-)(ayoge, m. 7th s.)(sāmārthyasya, n. 6th s.)(api*)(ayogataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 2558. That restriction [of hearing to particular conditions] through the capacity of wind and the like is not tenable; because when there is no function to be performed regarding the object, the capacity too has no application.

body.text:
2559.
(ataḥ*)(abhivyakti-)(ayogena, m. 3rd s.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(śabda-)(idam-)(phalam, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(avinā-)(bhāvi, n. 1st s.)(utpāda-)(grāhya-)(vat*)(buddhi-)(vyakti-)(ghaṭa-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 2559. Therefore, because manifestation (<s>abhivyakti</s>) is untenable, this cognition having sound as [its] fruit is invariably [connected with] origination — like the cognition of a pot and the like, which is grasped [through] the manifestation of the intellect.

body.text:
2560.
(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(utpatti-)(abhivyaktyoḥ, f. 6th d.)(prayatna-)(vivakṣayoḥ, f. 5th d.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(samaḥ, m. 1st s.)(bhedaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sāmarthya-)(sarvatra*)(artha-āpattitaḥ* [-tas suff.])(kārya-) produced by them.
body.translated_text: 2560. Therefore, in [both] origination and manifestation — with respect to effort and the desire to express — the distinction [in] capacity would be equal everywhere, through inference from effects (<s>kārya-arthāpatti</s>).

body.text:
2561.
(ca*)(yāvān, m. 1st s.)(kaścana, m. 1st s.)(nyāyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(dūṣaṇe, n. 7th s.)(bhāgatva-)(nabhaḥ-)(samastaḥ, m. 1st s.)(asau, m. 1st s.)(vijñeyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(mati-śālibhiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(api*)(bhāge, m. 7th s.)(diś-)
body.translated_text: 2561. And whatever reasoning [there is] in the refutation of a portion of space — all that should be understood by the wise as [equally applicable] to a portion of direction (<s>diś</s>) as well.

body.text:
2562.
(api*)(saṃskāre, m. 7th s.)(viṣayasya, m. 6th s.)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(saṃskṛtiḥ, f. 1st s.)(ekasya, m. 6th s.)(eva*)(na*)(astatvāt, n. 5th s.)(śakti-)(niyateḥ, f. 5th s.)(ataḥ*)(na*)(saṃskṛtiḥ, f. 1st s.)(viṣaya-)
body.translated_text: 2562. Even when the object receives modification by that [sound], the modification of a single [organ] alone — because of the restriction of capacity — [is not tenable]; therefore, [universal] modification of the object [is not possible].

body.text:
2563.
(ayogyatve, n. 7th s.)(utpattau, f. 7th s.)(jñāna-)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(kadācana*)(gamyeta ”gam Pass. Opt.)(sarvaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(sarvatra*)(anupayogataḥ* [-tas suff.])(tat-)(jñāne, n. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 2563. If the origination of cognition [from sound] is untenable, this sound would never be cognized by anyone anywhere — because of [its] uselessness in the cognition of that [sound].

body.text:
2564.
(tu*)(sāmarthye, n. 7th s.)(utpattau, f. 7th s.)(jñāna-)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(avagamyeta ”gam Pass. Opt.)(sarvaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(sarvadā*)(sarvatra*)(sthiteḥ, f. 5th s.)(hetutayā, f. 3rd s.)(jñāna-)
body.translated_text: 2564. But if [you say] the origination of cognition [is due to the sound's] capacity — [then] this sound would be cognized by all, everywhere, at all times — because [it] always exists as a cause of cognition.

body.text:
2565.
(tam, m. 2nd s.)(sthitam, m. 2nd s.)(ātmani, m. 7th s.)(eva*)(prakṛtyā, f. 3rd s.)(śaktam, m. 2nd s.)(vā*)(aśaktam, m. 2nd s.)(kaḥ, m. 1st s.)(virodhī, m. 1st s.)(vā*)(sahakārī, m. 1st s.)(kṣamaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kṣapayitum* ”kṣap Caus.)(artham, m. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 2565. [Whether] that [sound], abiding in its own nature, [is] capable or incapable by [its] nature — who [or what] would be an opponent or a cooperating [condition] able to exhaust [its] purpose?

body.text:
2566.
(ca*)(yogyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(utpādana-)(jñāna-)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(bhavati ”bhū I C.)(prati*)(kāṃścit, m. 2nd pl.)(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(utpadyamānaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(na*)(avagamyate ”gam Pass.)(sarvaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 2566. And this [sound] is capable of producing cognition for some [persons only]; therefore, this [sound], being produced [anew], is not cognized by all.

body.text:
2567.
(athavā*)(kim*)(punaḥ*)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(śrūyate ”śru Pass.)(eva*)(taiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(yat*)(asya, m. 6th s.)(saṃskṛtiḥ, f. 1st s.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(nādaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(sthaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(samīpa-)(tu*)(na*)(sthaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(dūra-)
body.translated_text: 2567. Or rather, why is the sound heard only by those [nearby]? If [you say] its modification would occur through <s>nādas</s> (sound vibrations) that are nearby — but not through those that are far away —

body.text:
2568.
(api*)(sāmīpye, n. 7th s.)(saṃskāraḥ, m. 1st s.)(parikalpyate ”kḷp Caus. Pass.)(kāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(saṃskāraḥ, m. 1st s.)(samānaḥ, m. 1st s.)(teṣu, m. 7th pl.)(sthiteṣu, m. 7th s.)(dūra-)(api*)
body.translated_text: 2568. Even when proximity [is the condition], the <s>saṃskāra</s> (conditioning) is postulated [as the cause]; and [yet] the same <s>saṃskāra</s> as a cause exists even when those [sounds] are situated far away.

body.text:
2569.
(yadi*)(gamyate ”gam Pass.)(viśiṣṭa-)(saṃskṛteḥ, f. 6th s.)(janma, n. 1st s.)(dhvanibhyaḥ, m. 5th s.)(tadā*)(na*)(kenacit, m. 3rd s.)(śakyā, f. 1st s.)(pratikṣeptum* ”kṣip)(śabda-)(utpattiḥ, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2569. If [you say] the birth [of hearing] is from a particular modification produced by sounds — then no one can reject the origination of sound.

body.text:
2570.
(hi*)(sā, f. 1st s.)(viśiṣṭa-)(saṃskṛtiḥ, f. 1st s.)(na*)(vyatirekiṇī, f. 1st s.)(śabdāt, m. 5th s.)(śabdasya, m. 6th s.)(prāpteḥ, f. 5th s.)(ajñeyatā-)(tataḥ*)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(api*)(jāyate ”jan IV C. Āt.)
body.translated_text: 2570. For that particular modification is not distinct from the sound; because [if it were distinct from] the sound, the unknowability [of the sound would follow]; therefore, sound too is produced [anew].

body.text:
2571.
(ca*)(saṃskṛtaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ekadā*)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(jātucit*)(jahāti ”hā II C.)(tam, m. 2nd s.)(ātmānam, m. 2nd s.)(saṅgāt-)(anityatā-)(tat*)(upalabhyeta ”labh Pass. Opt.)(sadā*)
body.translated_text: 2571. And [if] the sound, once modified, never abandons that nature of [being modified] — then because of [its] permanent connection [with the modification], [its] non-eternality would always be perceived.

body.text:
2572.
(api*)(pakṣe, m. 7th s.)(saṃskāra-)(dvaya-)(vacaḥ, n. 1st s.)(dvaye, n. 7th s.)(doṣa-)(satyam, n. 1st s.)(yat*)(vaikalyam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(anyatara-)(prāktanasya, m. 6th s.)(anuvṛttitaḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 2572. Even in the thesis of a twofold <s>saṃskāra</s> (conditioning) — [the faults are stated] in two statements about defects; in truth, the deficiency [of hearing by others] is not [explained merely] by the continuation of one or the other [conditioning] from before.

body.text:
2573.
(hi*)(tathā*)(śrotra-)(varṇāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(ye, m. 1st pl.)(purā*)(saṃskṛtāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(vyañjakaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(m. 1st pl.)(na*)(naṣṭāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(cyuti-)(prāpteḥ, f. 5th s.)(tataḥ*)(śrutiḥ, f. 1st s.)(sarvaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(sarva-)
body.translated_text: 2573. For likewise, those phonemes (<s>varṇas</s>) of the organ of hearing that were previously modified by the manifesting [sounds] have not perished — because of [their] not having fallen away; therefore, all [persons] should hear all [sounds].

body.text:
2574.
(ca*)(cet*)(saṃskṛtau, m. 1st d.)(śrotra-)(śabdau, m. 1st d.)(yogyau, m. 1st d.)(śruti-)(niyata-)(tadā*)(punaḥ*)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(na*)(śravaṇam, n. 1st s.)(anya-)(prapattṝṇām, m. 6th pl.)(varṇa-)
body.translated_text: 2574. And if the organ of hearing and sound, [both] being modified, are capable [only] of producing a specific hearing — then there would be no hearing again for those who subsequently encounter those phonemes.

body.text:
2575.
(cet*)(saṃskṛtau, m. 1st d.)(punaḥ*)(yogyau, m. 1st d.)(vijñāna-)(tat-)(varṇa-)(nara-)(nanu*)(anuvṛttau, f. 7th s.)(tayoḥ, m. 6th d.)(eva*)(śrutiḥ, f. 1st s.)(api*)(tayoḥ, m. 6th d.)(syāt ”as Ii C. Opt.)
body.translated_text: 2575. If [you say] they are again capable [of producing] the cognition of those phonemes for those persons — [then we reply:] surely, when those two [earlier conditions] continue, the hearing of those two [sounds] should also continue.

body.text:
2576.
(vyāvṛttau, f. 7th s.)(katham*)(amī, m. 1st pl.)(anye, m. 1st pl.)(śrotra-)(varṇāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(na*)(prāpnuvanti ”āp V C. III p. pl.)(te, 6th s.)(tataḥ*)(āśā, f. 1st s.)(teṣu, m. 7th pl.)(nityatā-)(anibandhanā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2576. When [the earlier conditions] have ceased, how do these other phonemes of the organ of hearing not attain that [hearing]? Therefore, the hope for eternality [of sound] regarding those [phonemes] is without basis.

body.text:
2577.
(ca*)(jala-)(ādiṣu, m. 7th pl.)(na*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(ekaḥ, m. 1st s.)(savitā, m. 1st s.)(īkṣyate ”īkṣ Pass.)(nānā-)(ātmā, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(yat*)(dhiyaḥ, f. 1st pl.)(sarvāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(pratibima-)(sthitāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(nirālambanāḥ, f. 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 2577. And this one sun is not seen in water and the like as having manifold forms; because all cognitions of reflections are without a [real] support.

body.text:
2578.
(api*)(tvat-)(pakṣe, m. 7th s.)(sarvāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(dhiyaḥ, f. 1st pl.)(vyavasthitāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(nirākārāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(punaḥ*)(bāhyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pada-arthaḥ, m. 1st s.)(abhyupagamyate ”gam Pass.)(ākāravān, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2578. Moreover, in your thesis, all cognitions are established as formless (<s>nirākāra</s>); [and] yet an external word-meaning possessing form is accepted.

body.text:
2579.
( ca*)(idam, n. 1st s.)(pratibimbam, n. 1st s.)(samīkṣyate ”īkṣ Pass.)(antargatam, n. 1st s.)(jala-)(ādi-)(ca*)(sūrya-)(ādiḥ, m. 1st s.)(varttī, m. 1st s.)(tala-)(nabhaḥ-)(na*)(tathā*)(sthitaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2579. And this reflection is considered as internal to the water and the like; but the sun and the like, [which are] situated on the surface of the sky, are not so situated [within the water].

body.text: 2580.--How (katham*)(tat*)(bhāti ”bhā II C.)(evam*)(cet*)(bhrāntyā, f. 3rd s.)(ataḥ*)(eva*)(tu*)(spaṣṭam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(tat, n. 1st s.)(na*)(nirālambanam, n. 1st s.)(viyogataḥ* [-tas suff.])(artha-)(tat-)(rūpa-)
body.translated_text: 2580. How does it appear so? If [you say] through error — then precisely because of that, it is clear that that [reflection] is without a [real] support, because of [its] disconnection from the form of that object.

body.text:
2581.
(cet*)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(eva*)(pratipattiḥ, f. 1st s.)(anyathā*)(idam, n. 1st s.)(su-)(bhāṣitam, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(anyathā*)(kintu*)(evam*)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(vedakam, n. 1st s.)(sarva-)
body.translated_text: 2581. If [you say] there is the apprehension of that [object] itself, [but] in a different manner — [then] this is well said. But that [apprehension] too is in a different manner; therefore, everything would be a cognizer of everything.

body.text:
2582.
(pratipattiḥ, f. 1st s.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(eva*)(yadi*)(īkṣyeta ”īkṣ Pass. Opt.)(tathā-)(sthitam, n. 1st s.)(tu*)(upalabdhau, f. 7th s.)(anya-)(ākāra-)(katham*)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(dṛṣṭiḥ, f. 1st s.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2582. If the apprehension of that [object] itself were seen as so established — but when there is a perception of a different form, how could there be the [correct] vision of that [object]?

body.text:
2583.
(hi*)(api*)(vijñāne, n. 7th s.)(sākāre, n. 7th s.)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(yujyate ”yuj Pass.)(grāhakam, n. 1st s.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(ākāre, m. 7th s.)(sati, m. 7th s.)(avilakṣaṇe, m. 7th s.)(artha-)(jñāta-)
body.translated_text: 2583. For even in a cognition that possesses form, the cognition is justified as the apprehender of that [object] — when the form is not different from the object [already] known.

body.text:
2584.
(avabuddhyatām ”budh IV C. Imperative 3p s. Āt.)(ārvāñc-)(vṛttyā, f. 3rd s.)(santam, m. 2nd s.)(arpitam, m. 2nd s.)(pāramparya-)(api*)(ekatve, n. 7th s.)(kim*)(anumanyate ”man IV C. Āt.)(vṛttim, m. 2nd s. [bv. cpd.])(ūrdhva-)(arvāk*)(eva*)
body.translated_text: 2584. Let [the opponent] understand: [even one who is] placed in succession, by a backward-directed operation [of cognition] — even in [the case of] unity, does one accept [an operation that is] only upward and downward directed?

body.text:
2585.
(upapāditam, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(yadi*)(arkaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tathā*)(īkṣyeta ”īkṣ Pass. Opt.)(eva*)(yathā*)(asau, m. 1st s.)(avasthitaḥ, m. 1st s.)(prakalpyeta ”kḷp Caus. Pass. Opt.)(avabuddhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(anyathā*)
body.translated_text: 2585. If [you say] this has been demonstrated — [then] if the sun were seen just as it is situated, it would be conceived as [truly] cognized — and not otherwise.

body.text:
2586.
(evam*)(na*)(bhrāntyā, f. 3rd s.)(avagacchati ”gam I C.)(mukham, n. 2nd s.)(iti*)(pratyak*)(budhyamānaḥ IV C. Āt., m. 1st s.)(samarpitam, n. 2nd s.)(vṛtti-)(pratyañc-)(vṛttyā, f. 3rd s.)(prāñc-natayā, f. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 2586. Thus, [one who] perceives directly — cognizing 'this is not [apprehended] through error' — [sees] the face presented through a forward-directed operation, by the backward-directed operation [of cognition].

body.text:
2587.
(tat, n. 1st s.)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(pratibimbaka-)(na*)(sva-)(āsya-)(ādi-)(ālambanam, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(nirbhāsāt, m. 5th s.)(vilakṣaṇa-)(tat-)(vat*)(vitti-)(rasa-)(śabda-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 2587. That cognition of a reflection does not have one's own face and the like as [its real] object — because of [its] appearance being different from that [real object] — like [the cognition of] taste, sound, and the like.

body.text:
2588.
(hi*)(alpīyasi, n. 7th s.)(darpaṇe, n. 7th s.)(āsyam, n. 1st s.)(pratibhāti ”bhā II C.)(alpīyaḥ, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(vṛkṣa-)(ādiḥ, m. 1st s.)(pratīyate ”i Pass.)(viparyastaḥ, m. 1st s.)(magnaḥ, m. 1st s.)(jala-)
body.translated_text: 2588. For in a small mirror, the face appears smaller; and a tree and the like is perceived inverted [and] submerged in water.

body.text:
2589.
(bimbam, n. 1st s.)(abhimukham, n. 1st s.)(tu*)(na*)(evam*)(pratibimbakam, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(idam, n. 1st s.)(antargatam, n. 1st s.)(jala-)(ādi-)(tu*)(bimbam, n. 1st s.)(avasthitam, n. 1st s.)(ārāt*)
body.translated_text: 2589. But the original (<s>bimba</s>) is facing forward — the reflection (<s>pratibimba</s>) is not thus; and this [reflection] is inside the water and the like, while the original is situated afar.

body.text:
2590.
(pratibimbam, n. 1st s.)(bhedi, n. 1st s.)(sthūla-)(sūkṣma-)(ādi-)(anuvidhānena, n. 3rd s.)(āśraya-)(tu*)(na*)(bimbam, n. 1st s.)(ataḥ*)(hetoḥ, m. 6th s.)(na*)(asiddhatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2590. The reflection differs [from the original] by conforming to [the substrate's] gross, subtle, and other [features]; but the original [does not conform to] the substrate; therefore, there is no unestablishedness of this reason.

body.text:
2591.
(api*)(avabhāsena, m. 3rd s.)(vilakṣaṇa-)(sati, n. 7th s.)(saṃvedane, n. 7th s.)(artha-)(cittam, n. 1st s.)(rūpa-)(śabda-)(ādi-)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(gocaram, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(sarva-)(artha-)
body.translated_text: 2591. Even when there is an awareness with an appearance different [from the object] — the mind, [whose domain is] form, sound, and the like, would be the domain of all objects.

body.text:
2592.
(ca*)(yat*)(api*)(ekaḥ)(dṛśyate ”dṛś Pass.)(pṛthak*)(cakṣuṣi, n. 7th s.)(īṣat-)(sammīlite, n. 7th s.)(aṅgulyā, f. 3rd s.)(sā, f. 1st s.)(api*)(evam*)(matā, f. 1st s.)(bhrāntiḥ, f. 1st s.)(nirviṣayā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2592. And that which is seen separately when the eye is slightly closed by a finger — that too is regarded thus as an error, without [a real] object.

body.text:
2593.
(atra*)(tu*)(udayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pratibimba-)(vinivāritaḥ, m. 1st s.)(prāk*)(eva*)(dvaya-)(mūrtānām, m. 6th pl.)(ayogāt, m. 5th s.)(saha*)(ekatra*)(pratighātataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 2593. But here, the arising of reflections has already been refuted; because of the impossibility of two corporeal [entities existing] together in one [place], due to mutual obstruction.

body.text:
2594.
(vā*)(api*)(pratibimbake, n. 7th s.)(sati, n. 7th s.)(vṛttau, f. 7th s.)(aneka-)(deśa-)(bhedāt, m. 5th s.)(vat*)(sthūla-)(sūkṣma-)(ādi-)(na*)(eva*)(vidyate ”vid Pass.)(ekatvam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2594. Or even when the reflection exists, in the [theory of] manifold occurrence at different locations — because of [the reflection's conforming to] gross, subtle, and other [features of the substrate] — there is simply no oneness.

body.text:
2595.
(ca*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(adhyavasāyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pravarttate ”vṛt I C. Āt.)(puṃsām, m. 6th pl.)(iti*)(bhānuḥ, m. 1st s.)(sthitaḥ, m. 1st s.)(upari*)(mama, 6th s.)(niścitaḥ, m. 1st s.)(bhrāntaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2595. And this determination that arises in people — 'the sun is situated above me' — is certain [but] erroneous.

body.text:
2596.
(yasmāt, n. 5th s.)(sarve, m. 1st pl.)(prāṇa-bhṛtaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(paśyanti ”dṛś IV C. III p. pl.)(eva*)(ekam, m. 2nd s.)(divā-karam, m. 2nd s.)(yaugapadyena, n. 3rd s.)(na*)(kadācana*)(dvitīyam, m. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 2596. Because all living beings see only one sun simultaneously — [and] never a second one.

body.text:
2597.
(yasmāt, n. 5th s.)(iha*)(na*)(dvitīya-)(ādi-)(rāvam, n. 1st s.)(maṇḍalam, n. 1st s.)(vidyate ”vid Pass.)(dṛśya-)(adṛṣṭeḥ, f. 5th s.)(ca*)(ataḥ*)(viniścitaḥ, m. 1st s.)(eva*)(ekaḥ, m. 1st s.)(arkaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2597. Because there does not exist here a second disc [of the sun] or more — [this is established] from non-observation of [any] visible [second sun]; and therefore, the sun is certainly determined to be one.

body.text:
2598.
(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tu*)(na*)(niścitaḥ, m. 1st s.)(evam*)(ekatvena, m. 3rd s.)(kathañcana*)(krameṇa, m. 3rd s.)(ca*)(api*)(yugapad*)(tat-)(upalakṣaṇāt, n. 5th s.)(nānātva-)
body.translated_text: 2598. But sound is never determined as one in any way whatsoever; because of the characterization of its multiplicity — both successively and simultaneously.

body.text:
2599.
(yadā*)(bahavaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(vaktāraḥ, m. 1st pl.)(prayuñjate ”yuj VII C. Āt. III p. pl.)(varṇam, m. 2nd s.)(ga-)(ādikam, m. 2nd s.)(sakṛt*)(tadā*)(bhedaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vispaṣṭam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(upalabhyate ”labh Pass.)
body.translated_text: 2599. When many speakers utter the phoneme 'ga' and so forth at once, then difference [of the sounds] is clearly perceived.

body.text:
2600.
(asya, m. 6th s.)(prayoge, m. 7th s.)(krameṇa, m. 3rd s.)(bhedaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(kevalam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(avagamyate ”gam Pass.)(kintu*)(api*)(liṅgāt, n. 5th s.)(dhiyām, f. 6th pl.)(kramāt, m. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 2600. In its [i.e., sound's] use in succession, not merely is difference apprehended, but also from the inferential mark of the succession of cognitions.

body.text:
2601.
(bhavati ”bhū I C.)(upalambhanam, n. 1st s.)(asya, m. 6th s.)(adhīnam, n. 1st s.)(vyañjaka-)(dhvani-)(kintu*)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(grahaḥ, m. 1st s.)(yathā-)(avasthitasya, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2601. The apprehension of this [sound] is dependent on the manifesting sound (<s>dhvani</s>); but its apprehension would be [of it] as it actually exists.

body.text:
2602.
(anyathā*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(grahaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(tat-)(tat-)(rūpa-)(apratibhāsanāt, n. 5th s.)(hi*)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(prakāśate ”kāś I C. Āt.)(vyāpta-)(aśeṣa-)(nabhaḥ-)(bhāgaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])
body.translated_text: 2602. Otherwise, this apprehension [would be impossible] — because of the non-appearance of each and every form; for the sound, pervading the entire extent of space, does not manifest [itself fully].

body.text:
2603.
(kim*)(tat*)(śrutiḥ, f. 1st s.)(anurudhyate ”rudh IV C. Āt.)(bhinna-)(deśatvam, n. 2nd s.)(dhvaneḥ, m. 6th s.)(tu*)(vyaktaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pratibhāseta ”bhās I C. Opt. Āt.)(sva-ātmanā, m. 3rd s.)(vat*)(ghaṭa-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 2603. Why does hearing follow the different location of the sound? But the manifested [sound] would appear by its own nature — like a pot and the like.

body.text:
2604.
(ca*)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(idam, n. 1st s.)(uktam, n. 1st s.)(mātram, n. 1st s.)(prakriyā-)(na*)(kāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(asāmarthyam, n. 1st s.)(vyañjakānām, m. 6th pl.)(sādhitam, n. 1st s.)(ayogāt, m. 5th s.)(vyakti-)
body.translated_text: 2604. And all this that has been stated is a mere procedure — not a [valid] reason; the incapacity of the manifesters has been established because of the impossibility of manifestation.

body.text:
2605.
(pratyakṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pratyayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(iti*)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(eva*)(prāk*)(nirākṛtaḥ, m. 1st s.)(etat, n. 1st s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(abādhitam, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(bhedena, m. 3rd s.)(deśa-)(bhinnatvam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2605. [The objection based on] the perceptual cognition — that has already been refuted before; this [is] that [same objection], unrefuted — [namely,] the different location [established] through difference.

body.text:
2606.
(kaścit, m. 1st s.)(vrajan ”vraj I C., m. 1st s.)(bhinnāt, m. 5th s.)(deśāt, m. 5th s.)(bhidyate ”bhid Pass.)(kṣaṇa-bhaṅgitvāt, n. 5th s.)(anyathā*)(na*)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(gatimān, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2606. Someone moving from one place [to another] — [he] is differentiated because of momentariness (<s>kṣaṇa-bhaṅgitva</s>); otherwise, [he] would not have movement.

body.text:
2607.
(tasya, m. 6th s.)(sthairye, n. 7th s.)(sva-bhāvasya, m. 6th s.)(aviyuktasya, m. 6th s.)(pūrva-)(deśa-)(anuvarttanāt, n. 5th s.)(hi*)(upapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(na*)(prāptiḥ, f. 1st s.)(antara-)(deśa-)
body.translated_text: 2607. When its essential nature is stable [and] not separated from the previous location — because of [its] following the previous place — the attainment of another place is indeed not tenable.

body.text:
2608.
(nabhasaḥ, n. 6th s.)(nirupākhyāt, n. 5th s.)(prakalpyate ”kḷp Caus. Pass.)(na*)(abhivyaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(ca*)(tathā*)(atyakṣatvāt, n. 5th s.)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(khātāyām, f. 7th s.)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)(ālokaḥ, m. 1st s.).
Textual variant: atyakṣatvācca khātāyām ālokaḥ sa tatheṣyate.
body.translated_text:
2608. Manifestation is not postulated from featureless (<s>nirupākhya</s>) space; and likewise, because of [space] being beyond the senses — that [space] in a pit (<s>khātā</s>) is accepted as light.
[Textual variant: 'and because of being beyond the senses, that [space] in a pit is likewise accepted as light.']

body.text:
2609.
(kiñca*)(vat*)(śabda-)(ākāśe, n. 7th s.)(api*)(yujyate ”yuj Pass.)(na*)(abhivyaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(hi*)(abhivyaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(eṣā, f. 1st s.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(nityā, f. 1st s.)(hetu-)(sannidheḥ, f. 5th s.)
Textual variant: nityā (Baudha Bhāratī ed.) in place of nityaṃ.
body.translated_text:
2609. Moreover, manifestation is not tenable in space, as with sound; for this manifestation would be [the same as] cognition, and this [cognition] would be eternal — because of the [constant] proximity of the cause.
[Textual variant: 'eternal' (nityā, Baudha Bhāratī ed.) in place of 'eternally' (nityam).]

body.text:
2610.
(ca*)(yathā*)(prakalpyate ”kḷp Caus. Pass.)(vyañjakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kathañcit*)(śabde, m. 7th s.)(tat*)(na*)(atra*)(evam*)(vibhramaḥ, m. 1st s.)(mati-)(para-)(upādhiḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(buddhau, f. 7th s.)(śabda-)
body.translated_text: 2610. And just as a manifester of sound is postulated in some way — so too here, [there is] no such error; the qualifying condition of another's cognition is [applied] in the cognition, regarding sound.

body.text:
2611.
(ataḥ*)(sthitam, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(dīrgha-)(sarve, m. 1st pl.)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(na*)(dharmāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(dhvani-)(hi*)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(dhvanīnām, m. 6th pl.)(vyañjakatve, n. 7th s.)(ca*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(nirākṛtam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2611. Therefore, it is established that the long [vowels] and all the other properties of sound — [these] are not [eternal]; for if the sounds were [merely] manifesters, that [argument] has been refuted.

body.text:
2612.
(asakṛt*)(carcitam, n. 1st s.)(purā*)(iti*)(te, m. 1st pl.)(śabdāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(tat-)(arthāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(api*)(atyanta-)(bhedinaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(śaktāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(pratyavamarśane, n. 7th s.)(tulya-)
body.translated_text: 2612. [This has been] repeatedly discussed before; those sounds — [and] their meanings too — being utterly different, are capable of equal reflection.

body.text:
2613.
(ataḥ*)(na*)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(bhavati ”bhū I C.)(vācakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sambandhaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(artha-)(dṛṣṭa-)(tu*)(sādhitam, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(vastutaḥ* [-tas suff.])(eṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sva-vṛttyā, f. 3rd s.)(na*)(vācakaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2613. Therefore, sound is not an expresser [of meaning]; the connection with the object is observed — but as established [by convention] — in reality, [sound] is not an expresser by its own nature.

body.text:
2614.
(hi*)(ete, m. 1st pl.)(pratyayāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(nirmitāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(śabda-)(avabhāsinaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(mithyā-)(vācya-)(vācakatā-)(asthiteḥ, f. 5th s.)(jāti-)(sva-lakṣaṇa-)(ādīnām, m. 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 2614. For these cognitions [that appear as] illuminated by sound — are fabricated; because of the instability of the [relation of] expressible and expresser regarding <s>jāti</s> (universal), <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (unique particular), and the like.

body.text:
2615.
(api*)(vastutaḥ* [-tas suff.])(vailakṣaṇye, n. 7th s.)(vyavaharttāraḥ, m. 1st pl.)(bhrāntyā, f. 3rd s.)(tat-)(manyante ”man IV C. Āt. III p. pl.)(iti*)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(go-)(ekaḥ, m. 1st s.)(eva*)(buddhayaḥ, m. 1st pl. [bv. cpd.])(sama-)
body.translated_text: 2615. Even though there is real difference, the speakers, through error, think — 'the word for cow is one alone, [and] the cognitions are the same.'

body.text:
2616.
(tasmāt, m. 5th s.)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(n. 1st s.)(proktam, n. 1st s.)(puraskṛtya* ”kṛ)(bhedam, m. 2nd s.)(śabda-)(dvi-jātinā, m. 3rd s. [bv. cpd.])(bhāṣiṇā, m. 3red s.)(bahu-)(asambaddha-)(anāspadam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2616. Therefore, all that has been said — having put forward the distinction of sound, by the twice-born (<s>dvi-jāti</s>) speaker of many [words] — is unconnected and baseless.

body.text:
2617.
(tathāhi*)(kampa-)(hasta-)(ādeḥ, m. 6th s.)(na*)(ekatvam, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(buddhi-)(bhedataḥ* [-tas suff.])(bhedena, m. 3rd s.)(śīghra-)(manda-)(tat-)(vyaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(nirākṛtā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2617. For indeed, there is no oneness of a trembling hand and the like — because of the difference of cognitions; the manifestation [theory is refuted] by the distinction of fast and slow [motions].

body.text:
2618.
(ca*)(na*)(ekam, n. 1st s.)(sāmānyam, n. 1st s.)(upalakṣyate ”lakṣ Pass.)(anugāmi, n. 1st s.)(saṅketāt, m. 5th s.)(asau, m. 1st s.)(bhavati ”bhū I C.)(aṅgam, n. 1st s.)(gati-)(pratiṣedha-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 2618. And no single recurring universal is observed; from convention, that becomes an ancillary [factor] for the negation of movement and the like.

body.text:
2619.
(ca*)(proktam, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(śabdāh, m. 1st pl.)(na*)(gamayanti ”gam Caus. III p. pl.)(sākṣāt*)(vivekataḥ* [-tas suff.])(pratibandha-)(bāhya-)(artha-)(tu*)(amī, m. 1st pl.)(sūcakāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(vivakṣā-)
body.translated_text: 2619. And [it has been] stated that words do not directly convey the external object — from the exclusion of [any direct] connection; but rather, these [words] are indicators of the desire to express.

body.text:
2620.
(iti*)(te, m. 1st pl.)(hi*)(niścitāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(pratyakṣa-)(anupalambhataḥ* [-tas suff.])(kāryatayā, f. 3rd s.)(tasyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(atra*)(sphuṭā, f. 1st s.)(kārya-kāraṇatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2620. For these [words] are determined [as indicators] through direct perception and non-perception; because of being the effect of that [desire to express] — therefore, the cause-effect relation here is clear.

body.text:
2621.
(ca*)(yena, m. 3rd s.)(niścitaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kārya-kāraṇa-bhāvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(samayāt, m. 5th s.)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(prapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(śabdebhyaḥ, m. 5th pl.)(vivakṣām, f. 2nd s.)(vat*)(kampa-)(hasta-)
body.translated_text: 2621. And the one by whom the cause-effect relation has been determined from convention — he apprehends from words the desire to express, like a trembling hand [indicates intention].

body.text:
2622.
(samaye, m. 7th s.)(sati, m. 7th s.)(jāyate ”jan IV C. Āt.)(eṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kārya-kāraṇatā-ātmakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sambandhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(śabdānām, m. 6th pl.)(arthena, m. 3rd s.)(vartinā, m. 3rd s.)(vivakṣā-)
body.translated_text: 2622. When convention exists, this connection — having the nature of cause and effect — arises between words and the object that is the desire to express.

body.text:
2623.
(tena, n. 3rd s.)(proktaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sāmayikaḥ, m. 1st s.)(dyotanāt, n. 5th s.)(tena, m. 3rd s.)(ataḥ*)(teṣām, m. 6th pl.)(sambandhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ucyate ”vac Pass.)(samayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(api*)(na*)(tu*)(mukhyataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 2623. Therefore, [this connection] is called conventional (<s>sāmayika</s>), because of [its] illuminating [meaning] through that [convention]; therefore, the connection of those [words with their meanings] is said to be convention; but not [a connection that is] primary.

body.text:
2624.
(yogaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kāraṇa-)(kāryatā-)(na*)(eva*)(anyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vastubhyām, n. 5th d.)(bhūtābhyām, n, 5th d.)(kāraṇa-)(kārya-)(tu*)(te, n. 1st d.)(eva*)(udite, n. 1st d.)(tathā*)
body.translated_text: 2624. The connection of causality — [between cause and effect] — is not other than the two real things that have become cause and effect; but when those two have arisen, [the connection exists] accordingly.

body.text:
2625.
(te, n. 1st d.)(pratyekam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(gate, n. 1st d.)(jaḍaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(rūpatvena, n. 3rd s.)(eka-)(ātman-)(ataḥ*)(matā, f. 1st s.)(vyāptiḥ, f. 1st s.)(kāla-)(āpta-)(saṅketa-)(vyavahāra-)
body.translated_text: [Verse 2625] Those two [word and meaning], taken individually, are considered by the dull-witted to have a single essence in the form of [the word's] expressiveness; hence the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) [is established merely through] the conventional usage acquired over time,

body.text:
2626.
(tu*)(na*)(eva*)(yujyate ”yuj Pass.)(sambandhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vāstavaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ekaḥ, m. 1st s.)(arthānām, m. 6th pl.)(asaṅkīrṇatayā, f. 3rd s.)(bhede, m. 7th s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(a-sambandhatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: [Verse 2626] But a real connection — a single [unified relation] — is not at all justified; because of the unmixed [nature] of the objects, in [their] difference there would be disconnection,

body.text:
2627.
(ataḥ*)(iti*)(samayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ca*)(prati-martyam*, m. 2nd s. [adv.])(ca*)(eva*)(prati-uccāraṇam, n. 2nd s.)(ādi-)(uktam, n. 1st s.)(pareṇa, m. 3rd s.)(a-jānatā ”jñā IX C., m. 3rd s.)(para-)(nītim, f. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: [Verse 2627] Therefore, the convention [is established] for each person and indeed for each utterance and the like — [this] has been stated by the opponent who does not know the other's position,

body.text:
2628.
(hi*)(samayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sambandhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(tayoḥ, m. 6th d.)(dharmatayā, f. 3rd s.)(nara-)(tu*)(sambandhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(dyotakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(iti*)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(mukhyataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: [Verse 2628] For the convention is not a connection between those two [word and meaning] by [their own] nature; but a person is the illuminator of the connection — thus that [convention] would be primarily his,

body.text:
2629.
(ca*)(pare, m. 1st pl.)(na*)(pratijānate ”jñā IX C. Āt. III p. pl.)(enam, m. 2nd s.)(prati-uccāraṇam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(na*)(ca*)(kṛtam, m. 2nd s.)(īśa-)(ādeḥ, m. 6th s.)(ādau, m. 7th s.)(sarga-)(pratiṣiddhatvāt, n. 5th s.).
body.translated_text: [Verse 2629] And the opponents do not accept this [convention as established] for each utterance; nor was [it] made by <s>Īśvara</s> (God) and the like at the beginning of creation — because [creation by God] has been refuted,

body.text:
2630.
(ca*)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sambandhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(prati-ekam*, m. 2nd s. [adv.])(bhinnaḥ, m. 1st s.)(bhaṅgataḥ* [-tas suff.])(kṣaṇa-)(ca*)(pratyavamarśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tulya-)(na*)(virudhyate ”rudh VII C. pass.)(bhede, m. 7th s.)
Textual variant: sa bhinnaḥ (Baudha Bhāratī ed.) sambhinnaḥ.
body.translated_text: [Verse 2630] And that connection which is distinct for each [instance] — because of the momentary perishing — and the apprehension of similarity [across instances] — is not contradicted in [the context of] difference,
