body.text:
2708.
(api*)(anavabodhe, m. 7th s.)(saṅketa-)(api*)(aśrutau, f. 7th s.)(varṇānām, m. 6th pl.)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(artheṣu, m. 7th pl.)(bhāvi, n. 1st s.)(tat-)(śakta-)(kāraṇa-)(sannidheḥ, f. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 2708. Even without understanding the convention (<s>saṅketa</s>), and even when [the <s>varṇas</s>] have not been heard — the cognition of <s>varṇas</s> regarding [their] objects would [still] arise in the future — because of the proximity of the capable cause.

body.text:
2709.
(hi*)(tathā*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(sattvaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(nitya-)(ca*)(asya, m. 6th s.)(na*)(kācana, f. 1st s.)(apekṣā, f. 1st s.)(ca*)(na*)(api*)(vyaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(tat-)(dhvani-)(saṅketa-)(varṇaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(adarśanāt, n. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 2709. For this [<s>sphoṭa</s>] is thus of an eternally existent nature, and there is no requirement [for anything else]; and the manifestation by <s>dhvani</s> (sound), convention, and <s>varṇas</s> [would be superfluous] — because of [their] not being observed [as contributing anything].

body.text:
2710.
(hi*)(āhuḥ ”ah Perf. III p. pl.)(iti*)(vyaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(vidyate ”vid Pass.)(na*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(tat-)(tataḥ*)(kalpanā, f. 1st s.)(api*)(vyañjakasya, m. 6th s.)(asya, m. 6th s.)(eva*)(nirarthakā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2710. For they say: 'manifestation is cognition' — and [yet] no cognition of that [<s>sphoṭa</s>] exists; therefore, the postulation of a manifester for this [<s>sphoṭa</s>] is also purposeless.

body.text:
2711.
(nādena, m. 3rd s.)(āhita-)(bījāyām, f. 7th s. [bv. cpd.])(āvṛtta-)(paripākāyām, f. 7th s. [bv. cpd.])(saha*)(antyena, m. 3rd s.)(dhvaninā, m. 3rd s.)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(avabhāsate ”bhās I C. Āt.)(buddhau, f. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 2711. In [the cognition] wherein the seed has been deposited by <s>nāda</s> (sound vibration), [and] which has reached maturation through repetition — together with the final <s>dhvani</s> (sound), <s>śabda</s> (word) appears in the cognition.

body.text:
2712.
(tena, n. 3rd s.)(etat, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(prakalpitam, n. 1st s.)(atra*)(api*)(nirnimittam, n. 1st s.)(hi*)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(lakṣyate ”lakṣ Pass.)(api*)(tasyām, f. 7th s.)(anyaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2712. [The grammarian says:] 'that is why this [<s>sphoṭa</s>] has been postulated' — but even here [the postulation is] without cause; for no other <s>śabda</s> is observed in that [cognition].

body.text:
2713.
(janyatām ”jan Pass. Imperative 3p s.)(vā*)(vyajyatām ”añj Pass. Imperative 3p s.)(dhvanibhiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(bhāvibhiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(krama-)(kramaḥ, m. 1st s.)(viruddhyate ”rudh Pass.)(teṣām, m. 6th pl.)(ye, m. 1st pl.)(manyante ”man IV C. Āt. III p. pl.)(sphoṭasya, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2713. Whether [the <s>sphoṭa</s>] is produced or manifested by the successive <s>dhvanis</s> (sounds) — sequence is contradicted for those who think [it belongs to] the <s>sphoṭa</s>.

body.text:
2714.
(hi*)(niraṃśake, n. 7th s.)(na*)(yujyete ”yuj Pass. 3p d.)(vyaktī, f. 1st d.)(jāti-)(krameṇa, m. 3rd s.)(a-)(bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(bahiḥ-)(eka-)(rūpa-)(hi*)(te, f. 1st d.)(syātām ”as II C. Opt. 3p d.)(eva*)(sarvathā*).
body.translated_text: 2714. For in what is partless, two manifestations in sequence are not tenable — because of the absence of [an] external [difference]; for those two [manifestations] would in every way simply be of one form.

body.text:
2715.
(api*)(sāṃśatve, n. 7th s.)(yathā*)(varṇāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(pratipādakāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(krameṇa, m. 3rd s.)(kim*)(na*)(sphoṭa-aṃśāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(api*)(evam*)(kim*)(adṛṣṭāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(prakalpitāḥ, m. 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 2715. Even if [the <s>sphoṭa</s>] has parts — just as the <s>varṇas</s> are communicators through sequence — why are the parts of <s>sphoṭa</s> not [also communicators] in the same way? Why [are they] postulated as unseen?

body.text:
2716.
(cet*)(prayuñjate ”yuj VII Āt. III p. pl.)(anyān, m. 2nd pl.)(varṇān, m. 2nd pl.)(nitarām*)(artham, m. 2nd s.)(siddhi-)(vyakti-)(jātau, f. 7th s.)(vyaktau, f. 7th s.)(kṛtāyām, f. 7th s.)(sakṛt*)(ekena, m. 3rd s.)(dhvaninā, m. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 2716. If [the grammarians] employ other <s>varṇas</s> [to say that] the manifestation of the particular (<s>vyakti</s>) [within] the universal (<s>jāti</s>) is fully accomplished by a single <s>dhvani</s>,

body.text:
2717.
(yataḥ*)(sā, f. 1st s.)(asya, m. 6th s.)(prakṛtiḥ, f. 1st s.)(tathā*)(kṛtā, f. 1st s.)(duravadhārā, f. 1st s.)(vyajyate ”añj Pass.)(api*)(bhūyaḥ*)(paraiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(varṇaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(samāna-)(śaktikaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 2717. Because its nature (<s>prakṛti</s>) has been so made — [and is] difficult to ascertain — [the <s>sphoṭa</s>] is manifested further by other <s>varṇas</s> having equal capacity.

body.text:
2718.
(nanu*)(evam*)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(eva*)(vā*)(anyasya, m. 6th s.)(ekasya, m. 6th s.)(āvṛttau, f. 7th s.)(punaḥ*)(punaḥ*)(na*)(vyaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(āvartate ”vṛt I C. Āt.)(aviśeṣataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 2718. [Objection:] Surely, in that case, [whether] of that very [<s>sphoṭa</s>] or of another single [entity], upon repetition again and again — [we reply:] the manifestation of that [<s>sphoṭa</s>] does not recur, because of no distinction [between the repetitions].

body.text:
2719.
(ca*)(api*)(asya, m. 6th s.)(vyaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(rūpā, f. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(saṃskāra-)(viṣaya-)(indriya-)(cetasi, n. 7th s.)(ābhāse, n. 7th s. [bv. cpd.])(tat-)(pratiṣeddhavyā, f. 1st s.)(vat*)(varṇa-)
body.translated_text: 2719. And the manifestation of this [<s>sphoṭa</s>], whose form [depends on] impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>), object, sense organ, and mind — in [the cognition] having the appearance of that [<s>sphoṭa</s>] — is to be denied, as with the <s>varṇas</s>.

body.text:
2720.
(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(yat, n. 1st s.)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(samasta-)(varṇa-)(param, n. 1st s.)(pūrvam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(pratyakṣataḥ* [-tas suff.])(krama-)(jñāneṣu, n. 7th pl.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(kāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(jñāna-)(artha-)
body.translated_text: 2720. Therefore, the cognition [directed at] all <s>varṇas</s> collectively, which [arises] previously through direct perception — that is the cause of the cognition of the meaning, in [the series of] sequential cognitions.

body.text:
2721.
(hi*)(antya-)(varṇe, m. 7th s.)(vijñāte, m. 7th s.)(smaraṇam, n. 1st s.)(sarva-)(varṇeṣu, m. 7th pl.)(yaugapadyena, n. 3rd s.)(jāyate ”jan IV C. Āt.)(kāritam, n. 1st s.)(saṃskāra-)(sarva-)
body.translated_text: 2721. For when the final <s>varṇa</s> has been cognized, the memory of all <s>varṇas</s> arises simultaneously — produced by the <s>saṃskāra</s> (impression) of all [the preceding varṇas].

body.text:
2722.
(ca*)(sarva-)(vādinām, m. 6th pl.)(iṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(etat, n. 1st s.)(mānasam, n. 1st s.)(samuccaya-)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(sarveṣu, m. 7th pl.)(artheṣu, m. 7th pl.)(api*)(satsu ”as II C., m. 7th pl.)(jñāteṣu, m. 7th pl.)(krama-)
body.translated_text: 2722. And this mental cognition of the aggregate — [that] is accepted by the proponents of all [schools]; [it arises] even when all objects have been sequentially cognized.

body.text:
2723.
(cet*)(na*)(abhyupeyeta ”i Pass. Opt.)(hi*)(drṣṭeṣu, m. 7th pl.)(krama-)(na*)(eva*)(jāyeta ”jan IV C. Opt. Āt.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(samuccaya-)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(rūpam, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(śata-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 2723. If [this aggregate cognition] were not accepted — [then] for those [objects] seen sequentially, that aggregate cognition — having the form of a hundred and the like — would simply not arise.

body.text:
2724.
(tena, n. 3rd s.)(api*)(yadi*)(varṇeṣu, m. 7th pl.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(śrotra-)(manobhyām, n. 3rd d.)(pūrva-)(kramāt, m. 5th s.)(tu*)(parastāt*)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(smaraṇam, n. 1st s.)(yugapat*)
body.translated_text: 2724. Therefore, even if the cognition of <s>varṇas</s> is [first] by the ear and [then] by the mind — sequentially at first — afterwards there would be simultaneous memory.

body.text:
2725.
(tataḥ*)(varṇāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(āruḍhāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(tat-)(artha-)(avabodhanāt, n. 5th s.)(na-)(dūra-)(atha*)(laukikaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(abhidhīyate ”dhā Pass.)(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(śabdāt, m. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 2725. Then the <s>varṇas</s>, having been grasped [in that simultaneous memory], [produce] the understanding of meaning — [they are] not far [from conveying meaning]; now, the worldly people say: 'cognition [arises] from words.'

body.text:
2726.
(ca*)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(etat, n. 1st s.)(yujyate ”yuj Pass.)(vijñāne, n. 7th s.)(ākāravati, n. 7th s.)(hi*)(anyathā*)(katham*)(te, m. 1st pl.)(vinaṣṭāḥ, m. 1st plp.)(bhāseran ”bhās I C. Āt. III p. pl.)(smaraṇe, n. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 2726. And all this is tenable [only] in [the theory of] cognition possessing form (<s>sākāra-vijñāna</s>); for otherwise, how would those [varṇas], having perished, appear in memory?

body.text:
2727.
(atha*)(purā*)(viditāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(varṇāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(vyaktayaḥ, m. 1st pl. [bv. cpd.])(tirobhūta-)(smaryante ”smṛ Pass. III p. pl.)(avasthitāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(eva*)(na*)(prasaṅgataḥ* [-tas suff.])(spaṣṭa-)(ābha-)
body.translated_text: 2727. Now, [if you say] the <s>varṇas</s> previously known — [as] particulars whose manifestation has disappeared — are remembered as still existing — [we reply:] there is no occasion [for that], because of [their] clear appearance.

body.text:
2728.
(ca*)(sthitiḥ, f. 1st s.)(pūrvam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(apāstā, f. 1st s.)(tat-)(sthitau, f. 7th s.)(smaraṇam, n. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(kāle, m. 7th s.)(vijñāna-)(anubhava-)(varṇa-)(eka-)(hetutaḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 2728. And the persistence [of the varṇas] has been previously rejected; [and even if they] persisted, memory would [only] arise at [the time of] the experience of a single <s>varṇa</s> — from the cause of the [prior] cognition.

body.text:
2729.
(tu*)(asmābhiḥ, 3rd pl.)(na*)(eva*)(nivāryate ”vṛ Caus. Pass.)(eka-)(matitvam, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(gauḥ, f. 1st s.)(ca*)(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(ekatā-)(śabde, m. 7th s.)(grāhya-)(tat-)(eka-)(arthatābhyām, f. 3rd d.)
body.translated_text: 2729. But by us, the unity of cognition is not at all denied — [as in] 'this is a cow'; the cognition of unity regarding <s>śabda</s> (word) [arises] from the unity of the apprehended [object] and the unity of meaning.

body.text:
2730.
(api*)(sā, f. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(śabde, m. 7th s.)(go-)(śaighryāt, n. 5th s.)(ca*)(alpa-)(antaratvāt, n. 5th s.)(śabdeṣu, m. 7th pl.)(devadatta-)(ādi-)(bhedaḥ, m. 1st s.)(spaṣṭaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pratīyate ”i Pass.)
body.translated_text: 2730. That [unity of cognition] would also [obtain] regarding the word 'cow' — because of the rapidity [of cognition] and because of the small interval between the <s>śabdas</s> (sounds); [yet] the difference of [words like] <s>Devadatta</s> and the like is clearly perceived.

body.text:
2731.
(ca*)(eṣā, f. 1st s.)(dhīḥ, f. 1st s.)(artha-)(utthā, f. 1st s.)(varṇa-)(udbhavāt, m. 5th s.)(anantara-)(jñāna-)(tat-)(hi*)(sā, f. 1st s.)(yādṛśī, f. 1st s.)(utthā, f. 1st s.)(tat-)(iva*)(dhīḥ, f. 1st s.)(vahni-)(dhūma-)(ādeḥ, m. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 2731. And this cognition of meaning arises from <s>varṇas</s> — [specifically] from the cognition [that immediately follows] the arising of the meaning; for it is like [the cognition of] fire from smoke and the like — whatever [form of] cognition arises from that [source], the cognition [partakes of] that [form].

body.text:
2732.
(dhīḥ, f. 1st s.)(artha-)(na*)(vidyate ”vid Pass.)(bhāvinī, f. 1st s.)(anantara-)(jñāna-)(ābha-)(śabda-)(bhinna-)(varṇa-)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(na*)(anyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(śabdaḥ, m. 1st s.)(asti ”as II C.)(vācakaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2732. There is no cognition of meaning that would arise in the future from the appearance of a <s>śabda</s> [composed] of different <s>varṇas</s> — [that is, from a cognition immediately following another]; therefore, there is no other <s>śabda</s> (word) that is an expresser [beyond the varṇas themselves].

body.text:
2733.
(eva*)(sarvatra*)(anvaya-)(vyatirekau, m. 1st d.)(viniścitau, m. 1st d.)(aṅgam, n. 1st s.)(vyavahāra-)(kāryatā-)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(hi*)(vyāptiḥ, f. 1st s.)(niścitā, f. 1st s.)(iha*)
body.translated_text: 2733. Positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>) are ascertained everywhere; for by that [means], pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) is determined here — as a component of conventional practice and the [establishment of] effect-hood.

body.text:
2734.
(ca*)(prasādhite, n. 7th s.)(vācakatve, n. 7th s.)(eva*)(anityeṣu, m. 7th pl.)(varṇeṣu, m. 7th pl.)(pratyabhijñā-)(anumāne, n. 1st d.)(sādhane, n. 1st d.)(nitya-)(niraste, n. 1st d.)
body.translated_text: 2734. And when the denotative capacity [of words] has been established in non-eternal phonemes (<s>varṇas</s>) alone — [then] recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) and inference, [which serve as] proofs [of eternality], are both eliminated.

body.text:
2735.
(codanā, f. 1st s.)(kṛtā, f. 1st s.)(ajñānāt, n. 5th s.)(virodhānām, m. 6th pl.)(sva-)(vākya-)(ādi-)(tu*)(bhavanti ”bhū I C. III p. pl.)(sarve, m. 1st pl.)(te, m. 1st pl.)(bhavatām, m. 6th pl.)(pakṣe, m. 7th s.)(nitya-)(yataḥ*)
body.translated_text: 2735. The injunction (<s>codanā</s>) was made out of ignorance of the contradictions within one's own statements and the like; for all those [contradictions] exist in your position regarding the eternal [phonemes] — because —

body.text:
2736.
(upapāditam, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(vāk, f. 1st s.)(satī ”as II C., f. 1st s.)(nityā, f. 1st s.)(yuktā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(dyotikā, f. 1st s.)(ayogena, f. 3rd s.)(ānupūrvya-)(ādi-)(ca*)(anupalambhāt, m. 5th s.)(nityam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])
body.translated_text: 2736. Thus it has been demonstrated that speech, even if existent and eternal, is not suitable as an illuminator — because of the inapplicability of sequence (<s>ānupūrvya</s>) and the like, and because of the non-apprehension [of eternal sound] as permanent.

body.text:
2737.
(asiddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(āśraya-)(yā, f. 1st s.)(ucyate ”vac Pass.)(vikalpena, m. 3rd s.)(bheda-)(dharmin-)(sā, f. 1st s.)(ajñānāt, n. 5th s.)(lakṣaṇa-)(anumā-)(yataḥ*)(dharmitvam, n. 1st s.)(bhāsinaḥ, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2737. What is called the non-establishment of the locus (<s>āśraya-asiddhi</s>) — [that arises] from the alternative of the difference of the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) — [is refuted,] because that [non-establishment arises] from ignorance; since the inference of a defining characteristic [is valid], because the property-bearer-hood belongs to [what is] manifest.

body.text:
2738.
(arthaḥ, m. 1st s.)(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(avabhāsate ”bhās I C. Āt.)(jñāne, n. 7th s.)(prasiddhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(avicāra-)(api*)(śanaka-)(ādeḥ, m. 6th s.)(proktā, f. 1st s.)(tāvat-)(mātrasya, n. 6th s.)(dharmitā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2738. The object that appears in cognition — [which is] well-known even without examination — of <s>Śanaka</s> and the like — the property-bearer-hood of just that much [i.e., the appearing object] is stated.

body.text:
2739.
(hi*)(tatra*)(eva*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(vivādaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sampravṛttaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pravādinām, m. 6th pl.)(tu*)(asti ”as II C.)(na*)(vivādaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kasyacit, m. 6th s.)(bhede, m. 7th s.)(racita-)(icchā-)
body.translated_text: 2739. For the dispute of the debaters has arisen regarding that very [object]; but there is no dispute of anyone regarding [what is] different — [which is merely] a fabricated desire.

body.text:
2740.
(ataḥ*)(nirdiṣṭe, n. 7th s.)(aviśeṣa-)(vikalpanam, n. 1st s.)(viśeṣeṇa, m. 3rd s.)(pratibādhate ”bādh I C. Āt.)(pravṛttim, f. 2nd s.)(eva*)(sarvasya, n. 6th s.)(anumānasya, n. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2740. Therefore, when [the property-bearer] has been indicated without qualification, the supposition of a qualification obstructs the operation of all inference whatsoever.

body.text:
2741.
(api*)(iti*)(buddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(janitā, f. 1st s.)(codanā-)(pramāṇam, n. 1st s.)(janyamānatvāt, n. 5th s.)(kāraṇaiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(varjitaiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(doṣa-)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(vikalpyate ”kḷp Caus. Pass.)
body.translated_text: 2741. Moreover, [the thesis that] the cognition generated by <s>codanā</s> (injunctive statement) is a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), because of being produced by causes free from defects — and the like — is [itself] to be analyzed.

body.text:
2742.
(cet*)(pakṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(janitā, f. 1st s.)(codanā, f. 1st s.)(nitya-)(sambaddha-)(nitya-)(artha-)(anuṣajyate ”sañj Pass.)(āśraya-)(asiddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(prati*)(param, m. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 2742. If the thesis [is that] the cognition generated by <s>codanā</s> — [which is] eternally connected with eternal objects — [is valid, then] the [fault of] non-establishment of the locus applies against the opponent.

body.text:
2743.
(ca*)(nityatvam, n. 1st s.)(tādavasthyam, n. 1st s.)(anyatvam, n. 1st s.)(tat-)(anityatā, f. 1st s.)(tādavasthya-)(nivṛttau, f. 7th s.)(kim, n. 1st s.)(hi*)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)(avasthitam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2743. And eternality [means] remaining in the same state (<s>tādavasthya</s>); otherness [from that state means] non-eternality. When remaining in the same state has ceased — what indeed is accepted as [still] enduring?

body.text:
2744.
(ca*)(hetau, m. 7th s.)(prakalpite, n. 7th s.)(atra*)(kevala-)(aindriyakatve, n. 7th s.)(na*)(vyabhicāraḥ, m. 1st s.)(gamyate ”gam Pass.)(jātyā, f. 3rd s.)(pūrvam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(bādhitayā, f. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 2744. And when the reason is postulated here as [being] purely sensory — no deviation is cognized [from it]; for <s>jāti</s> (universal) has been previously refuted.

body.text:
2745.
(hetuḥ, m. 1st s.)(indriya-jñāna-)(nirbhāsin-)(sva-)(bhavet ”bhū Opt.)(aindriyakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ca*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(hi*)(prasādhitam, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(nitye, m. 7th s.)(na*)(asti ”as II C.)(hetutvam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2745. The reason [is]: that which appears in sense-cognition is of sensory origin (<s>aindriyaka</s>); and that [conclusion] has indeed been established. Therefore, in [the case of] the eternal [sound], there is no causality.

body.text:
2746.
(ca*)(iyam, f. 1st s.)(prasiddhā, f. 1st s.)(sarveṣām, m. 6th pl.)(īdṛk-)(arthasya, m. 6th s.)(hetutā, f. 1st s.)(anyathā*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(vikalpaḥ, m. 1st s.)(samaḥ, m. 1st s.)(api*)(sarvatra*)(dhūma-)(ādau, m. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 2746. And this [kind of] causality of such an object is well-known to all; otherwise, this doubt would be equal everywhere — regarding smoke and the like as well.

body.text:
2747.
(ca*)(pratisaṅkhyā-)(nirodha-)(ādeḥ, m. 6th s.)(na*)(siddhā, f. 1st s.)(ārambhakatā, f. 1st s.)(kārya-)(jñāna-)(anantara-)(prayatna-)(na*)(sāṃvṛtasya, m. 6th s.)(naḥ, 6th pl.).
N.B. read siddhā na instead of na siddhā.
body.translated_text: 2747. And the productive capacity of <s>pratisaṃkhyā-nirodha</s> (analytical cessation) and the like [as a cause of cognition] is not established — [since] effort immediately following cognition [is not established] for what is conventional (<s>sāṃvṛta</s>) in our [view].

body.text:
2748.
(ca*)(nirodhau, m. 1st d.)(na*)(iṣṭau, m. 1st d.)(ātmakau, m. 1st d.)(nāśa-)(yataḥ*)(pratisaṅkhyā-nirodhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(visaṃyogaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sāsravaiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(pṛthak-pṛthak*)
body.translated_text: 2748. And the two cessations (<s>nirodhas</s>) are not accepted [by us] as having the nature of destruction; because <s>pratisaṃkhyā-nirodha</s> (analytical cessation) is the disjunction from the defiled (<s>sāsrava</s>) [dharmas], separately.

body.text:
2749.
(anyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(nirodhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(apratisaṅkhyayā, f. 3rd s.)(atyanta-)(vighnaḥ, m. 1st s.)(utpāda-)(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(ajñāta-)(siddhāntāḥ, m. 1st pl. [bv. cpd.])(māninaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(alīka-)(plavante ”plu I C. Āt. III p. pl.)
body.translated_text: 2749. The other cessation — <s>apratisaṃkhyā-nirodha</s> (non-analytical cessation) — is the absolute obstruction of arising. Therefore, those who are ignorant of [our] established doctrine, [yet] prideful with false [claims], are [merely] floating [in confusion].

body.text:
2750.
(ca*)(kha-)(nāśau, m. 1st d.)(na*)(anantarīyakau, m. 1st d.)(prayatna-)(asva-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(nibandhanam, n. 1st s.)(jñāna-)(tathā-)(kapāla-)(rāśi-)(āloka-)(ādi, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2750. And space and destruction are not [effects] immediately following effort — because of not being of that nature; the basis [of cognition in those cases is rather] cognition itself — as with a heap of pot-sherds, light, and the like.

body.text:
2751.
(dvi-)(rūpatā, f. 1st s.)(ekasya, m. 6th s.)(artha-)(sva-bhāvasya, m. 6th s.)(parikṣiptā, f.1st s.)(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(ghaṭe, m. 7th s.)(na*)(ghaṭate ”ghaṭ I C. Āt.)(aṃśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ākhyaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(jāti-)(nityaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2751. The dual nature of a single entity — [having both] its own nature [and a universal] — has been rejected. Therefore, the aspect called <s>jāti</s> (universal) [that is supposed to be] eternal does not fit in the case of a pot.

body.text:
2752.
(ca*)(anityatā, f. 1sts.)(īpsitā, f. 1st s.)(mātram, n. 1st s.)(pratikṣepa-)(tādavasthya-)(sādhyatvena, n. 3rd s.)(pradīpa-)(ādiḥ, m. 1st s.)(sphuṭam, n. 1st s.)(udāharaṇam, n. 1st s.)(tatra*)
body.translated_text: 2752. And the desired non-eternality — [defined as] mere rejection of remaining in the same state — [is to be proven]; a lamp and the like is clearly the example therein.

body.text:
2753.
(tu*)(api*)(nāśitvam, n. 1st s.)(jvālā-)(ādeḥ, m. 6th s.)(prati-kṣaṇam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(na*)(asiddham)(tatra*)(laghavaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(avayavāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(yānti ”yā II C. III p. pl.)(antaram, n. 2nd s.)(deśa-)(laghu*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])
body.translated_text: 2753. But the destructibility of a flame and the like at every moment is not unestablished; therein, the light parts move to another location [and are replaced by new ones].

body.text:
2754.
(hi*)(prabhūtam, n. 1st s.)(piṇḍitam, n. 1st s.)(tejaḥ, n. 1st s.)(tiṣṭhati ”sthā I C.)(deśe, m. 7th s.)(varti-)(yāvat, n. 1st s.)(vrajati ”vraj I C.)(ūrdhvam*)(tāvat, n. 1st s.)(gamyate ”gam Pass.)(iti*)(jvālā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2754. For the abundant fire, gathered together, remains at the location of the wick; insofar as it moves upward, it is understood as 'flame.'

body.text:
2755.
(tat, n. 1st s.)(yat, n. 1st s.)(yāti ”yā II C.)(apakramya* ”kram)(api*)(tataḥ*)(ātmakam, n. 1st s.)(prabhā-)(tu*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(yat, n. 1st s.)(yāti ”yā II C.)(param, n. 2nd s.)(tataḥ*)(na*)(avadhāryate ”dhṛ Caus. Pass.)(saukṣmyāt, n. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 2755. That [fire] which moves away [from the wick] is of the nature of radiance (<s>prabhā</s>); but that which moves further from that [radiance] is not discerned — because of [its] subtlety.

body.text:
2756.
(ca*)(pūrve, m. 1st pl.)(na*)(yānti ”yā II C.)(uttara-)(avayavaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(ruddhaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(mārge, m. 7th s.)(yathā*)(pūrve, m. 1st pl.)(vimuñcanti ”muc VI C. III p. pl.)(tathā* tathā*)(uttare, m. 1st pl.)(yānti ”yā II C. III p. pl.)
body.translated_text: 2756. And the earlier [fire-particles] do not move — [being] obstructed by the later particles on the path; as the earlier ones release [their position], the later ones move [to take their place].

body.text:
2757.
(api*)(saṅkrāntau, f. 7th s.)(eteṣām, m. 6th pl.)(sambhavaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(vṛtti-)(tṛṇa-)(ādau, m. 7th s.)(tat*)(etat, n. 1st s.)(mātram, n. 1st s.)(kalpanā-)(pramāṇa-)(anabhidhānataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 2757. Even in the case of transference of these [fire-particles], their occurrence in grass and the like is not possible — that [claim] is a mere fabrication, [refuted] by [its] being unstated by valid means of knowledge.

body.text:
2758.
(kiñca*)(śaktīnām, m. 6th pl. [bv. cpd.])(avyāhata-)(saṅgatau, f. 7th s.)(tṛṇa-)(tūla-)(ādi-)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(prasaṅgaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vṛtti-)(dāha-)(na*)(nivartate ”vṛt I C. Āt.)(vat*)(pūrva-)
body.translated_text: 2758. Moreover, when the unimpeded capacities [of fire] come together with grass, cotton, and the like — this consequence of burning would not be averted — as before.

body.text:
2759.
(anyathā*)(tava, 6th s.)(kīdṛśī, f. 1st s.)(nitya-)(rūpā, f. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(sā, f. 1st s.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(teṣu, m. 7th pl.)(yadā*)(avasthitaḥ, m. 1st s.)(bhedaḥ, m. 1st s.)(śakta-)(aśakta-)(svabhāvasya, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2759. Otherwise, what would that [capacity] of yours look like — being of an eternal nature? When the distinction of capable and incapable natures is established among those [entities] —

body.text:
2760.
(sambandhasya, m. 6th s.)(ca*)(nityatvam, n. 1st s.)(pratiṣiddham, n. 1st s.)(purā*)(tataḥ*)(sambandha-)(a-kāraṇa-)(nyāyāt, m. 5th s.)(na*)(yuktā, f. 1st s.)(vākya-)(nityatā, f. 1st s.)
Textual variant: akāraṇa- in place of ākaraṇa-(typo)
body.translated_text: 2760. And the eternality of the connection [between word and meaning] has been previously refuted. Therefore, by the reasoning of there being no [eternal] cause of the connection — the eternality of the sentence is not justified.

body.text:
2761.
(ca*)(katamasya, n. 6th s.)(vākyasya, n. 6th s.)(upagamyate ”gam Pass.)(nityatvam, n. 1st s.)(ātmanaḥ, n. 6th s. [bv. cpd.])(mātra-)(varṇa-)(varṇa-)(kramasya, m. 6th s.)(atha*)(vibhedinaḥ, n. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2761. And of which sentence is the eternality accepted? Of [a sentence composed of] mere phonemes (<s>varṇas</s>) only? Or of the sequence of phonemes that is differentiated [into meaningful units]?

body.text:
2762.
(varṇānām, m. 6th pl.)(śḥr̥̄nyānām, m. 6th pl.)(krama-)(na*)(vidyate ”vid Pass.)(vācakatvam, n. 1st s.)(ataḥ*)(tādṛśāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(te, m. 1st pl.)(na*)(vākyam, n. 1st s.)(api*)(eṣām, m. 6th pl.)(na*)(vidyate ”vid Pass.)(kramaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2762. There is no denotative capacity in phonemes that are heard [in isolation]; therefore, those [isolated phonemes] are not such [as to constitute a sentence]; nor is there a sentence for these [phonemes] — [and] there is no sequence [for them either].

body.text:
2763.
(eṣām, m. 6th pl.)(vyāpteḥ, f. 5th s.)(ca*)(nityatayā, f. 3rd s.)(na*)(hi*)(upapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(kramaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kāla-)(deśa-)(vat*)(lipi-)(vat*)(phala-)(puṣpa-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 2763. And because of [their] pervasion by eternality, sequence is indeed not tenable for these [phonemes] — unlike [the sequence of] time, place, writing, and [the sequence of] fruits, flowers, and the like.

body.text:
2764.
(ca*)(krame, m. 7th s.)(svābhāvike, m. 7th s.)(eṣām, m. 6th pl.)(eva*)(sambhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(iti*)(tu*)(na*)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(iti*)(ādiḥ, m. 1st s.)(virodhataḥ* [-tas suff.])(krama-)(sthita-)
body.translated_text: 2764. And if [you say] the sequence of these [phonemes] is natural (<s>svābhāvika</s>) — [then] it would [always] obtain just so, and never otherwise — because of the contradiction with [any] established sequence.

body.text:
2765.
(ca*)(varṇāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(repha-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(sthitāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(ante, m. 7th s.)(na*)(eva*)(jāyante ”jan IV C. Āt.)(yoginaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(anya-)(krama-)(vāyutaḥ* [-tas suff.])(varṇitāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(ekatvena, n. 3rd s.)(nitya-)
body.translated_text: 2765. And the phonemes <s>repha</s> and the like, [which are] situated at the end, are simply not produced by the wind of another sequence; [yet they are] described as one [and the same] — [because they are supposed to be] eternal.

body.text:
2766.
(anyathā*)(pratyabhijñānam, n. 1st s.)(uktam, n. 1st s.)(tvayā, 3rd s.)(sādhanam, n. 1st s.)(nityatva-)(ekatva-)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(vyabhicāri, n. 1st s.)(vartanāt, n. 5th s.)(api*)(bhede, m. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 2766. Otherwise, the recognition [argument] stated by you as a proof of eternality and oneness would be deviant — because of [recognition] occurring even in [cases of] difference.

body.text:
2767.
(ca*)(kramaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vyakti-)(na*)(vākyam, n. 1st s.)(niṣedhanāt, n. 5th s.)(vyakti-)(nitye, n. 7th s.)(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(nityatvam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(upapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(yogataḥ* [-tas suff.])(vākyatā-)
body.translated_text: 2767. And the sequence [belongs to] the manifestation (<s>vyakti</s>), not [to] the sentence; because of the negation of manifestation — in [the case of] the eternal [phoneme]; therefore, eternality is not tenable — because of the connection with sentence-hood.

body.text:
2768.
(ca*)(yathā*)(śabdāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vṛddhi-)(arthakāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(viracita-)(icchā-)(eva*)(tathā*)(sambhāvyante ”bhū Caus. Pass. III p. pl.)(śabdāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(svarga-)(yāga-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 2768. And just as [words denoting] increase of merit (<s>vṛddhi</s>) and the like are fabricated by the desire [of speakers] — so too, words [denoting] sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>), heaven (<s>svarga</s>), and the like are [merely] imagined.

body.text:
2839.

body.translated_text: [Verse 2839] Moreover, [you have said:] 'validity is uncontested — [it is] the defining characteristic determinable by [the cognition's own] capacity — [it is established] by a means of valid cognition that is other [than the cognition itself]' — thus has been stated by you,

body.translated_text: [Verse 2840] Thus, the capacities of all entities — [which are] established by <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) — as means of establishing [their effects]: how is [validity] not established from an external source (<s>parataḥ</s>)?

body.text:

body.translated_text: [Verse 2841] Thus, the validity — which is of a partless nature — having been produced from its own cause and [being subject to] destruction — does not attain [establishment] through dependence on another, in [the context of] determination,

body.text:
2842.

body.translated_text: [Verse 2842] Another valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>) is not required for the production of that [validity's] own nature; but for the apprehension [of its validity], [another cognition] is required — regarding the object, in the determination of that [cognition's] own nature

body.text:

body.translated_text: 2843. Moreover, thus invalidity too would follow as intrinsic; indeed, of what is non-existent [as invalidity], the arising of that intrinsically from anywhere —

body.text:
2844.
(anapekṣatvam, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(ekam, n. 1st s.)(nibandhanam, n. 1st s.)(aprāmāṇya-)(iti*)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(hi*)(niḥśeṣam, n. 1st s.)(śakyate ”śak Pass.)(abhidhātum* ”dhā)(atra*)(api*)
body.translated_text: 2844. The non-dependence alone is the one basis of invalidity — thus and the like; indeed, all [the same arguments] can be stated here too.

body.text:
2845.
(tu*)(yathā*)(sāmarthyam, n. 1st s.)(avisaṃvādana-)(niśceyam, n. 1st s.)(anyataḥ* [-tas suff.])(tathā*)(sāmarthyam, n. 1st s.)(saṃvāda-)(ataḥ*)(sarvathā*)(dvayam, n. 1st s.)(samam, n. 1st s.)

body.translated_text: 2845. But just as the capacity for non-deception is to be ascertained from another [source], so too the capacity for accordance; therefore in every way the two are equal.

body.text: 2846.--Under the circumstances (tataḥ*)(kaḥ, m. 1st s.)(atiśayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(dṛṣṭaḥ, m. 1st s.)(prāmāṇyasya, n. 6th s.)(viparyayāt, m. 5th s.)(yena, m. 3rd s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(iṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(svataḥ* [-tas suff.])(tu*)(apramāṇatā, f. 1st s.)(parataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 2846. Under the circumstances, what superiority of validity is observed over its contrary, by which that alone is desired as intrinsic (<s>svataḥ</s>), but invalidity as extrinsic (<s>parataḥ</s>)?

body.text:
2847.
(tu*)(athāpi*)(asya, n. 6th s.)(prāmāṇyasya, n. 6th s.)(pramāṇānām, n. 6th pl.)(upavarṇanāt, n. 5th s.)(svataḥ* [-tas suff.])(abhimatā, f. 1st s.)(svataḥ* [-tas suff.])(vṛttiḥ, f. 1st s.)(sva-)(kārye, n. 7th s.)(jātānām, n. 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 2847. But moreover, regarding this validity — because of the description of the valid means — the operation that is desired as intrinsic is [the operation] of those [cognitions] that have arisen [operating] intrinsically in their own effect.

body.text:
2848.
(hi*)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)(lābhe, m. 7th s.)(ātman-)(bhāvānām, m. 6th pl.)(apekṣitā, f. 1st s.)(kāraṇa-)(tu*)(labda-)(ātmānaḥ, m. 1st pl [bv. cpd.])(vartante ”vṛt I C. Āt. III p. pl.)(eva*)(svayam*)(sva-)(kāryeṣu, n. 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 2848. Indeed, the dependence on causes is desired only for the attainment of self-existence [of entities]; but having obtained their selves, they operate indeed by themselves in their own effects.

body.text:
2849.
(ataḥ*)(jñānānām, n. 6th pl.)(asti ”as II C.)(vyapekṣā, f. 1st s.)(sva-)(hetuṣu, m. 7th pl.)(mātre, n. 7th s.)(utpatti-)(tu*)(na*)(janmani, n. 7th s.)(niścaya-)(sva-)(guṇeṣu, m. 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 2849. Therefore, cognitions have dependence only on their own causes for the sake of arising; but not at birth for the ascertainment [of their validity] in their own qualities.

body.text:
2850.
(hi*)(janane, n. 7th s.)(viniściteḥ, f. 6th s.)(prāmāṇya-)(artha-)(teṣām, n. 6th pl.)(svatantrāṇām, n. 6th pl.)(nirapekṣāṇām, n. 6th pl.)(sva-)(hetu-)(vṛttiḥ, f. 1st s.)(vat*)(ghaṭa-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 2850. Indeed, in the production of the ascertainment of the validity and meaning of those [cognitions] — they are independent, non-dependent — [operating] through their own causes — like a pot and the like.

body.text:
2851.
(janmani, n. 7th s.)(ghaṭaḥ, m. 1st s.)(apekṣate ”īkṣ I C. Āt.)(piṇḍa-)(mṛd-)(daṇḍa-)(cakra-)(ādi-)(tu*)(āharaṇe, n. 7th s.)(udaka-)(asya, m. 6th s.)(apekṣā, f. 1st s.)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 2851. A pot depends on a lump of clay, a staff, a wheel, and the like for its birth; but for carrying water, its dependence [on those causes is unnecessary].

body.text:
2852.
(ca*)(hi*)(ante, m. 7th s.)(eva*)(avaśyam*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(svataḥ-pramāṇatvam, n. 1st s.)(pramāṇatve, n. 7th s.)(adhīne, n. 7th s.)(para-)(prasajyate ”sañj Pass.)(anavasthā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2852. And indeed, at the end inevitably intrinsic validity (<s>svataḥ-prāmāṇya</s>) [must be accepted]; when validity is dependent on another, an infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>) follows.

body.text:
2853.
(cet*)(pramāṇatve, n. 7th s.)(maulike, n. 7th s.)(sādhyatā, f. 1st s.)(antara-)(pramāṇa-)(icchantaḥ ”iṣ I C., m. 1st pl.)(evam*)(tatra*)(labhemahi ”labh I C. Opt. 1p pl.)(na*)(vayvasthām, f. 2nd s.)(tava, 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2853. If, regarding the fundamental validity, the provability [is sought by] desiring another means of cognition — thus we would not obtain your [desired] stability.

body.text:
2854.
(hi*)(eva*)(yathā*)(prathamam, n. 1st s.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(apekṣate ”īkṣ I C. Āt.)(saṃvādam, m. 2nd s.)(tat-)(eva*)(tathā*)(punaḥ*)(mṛgyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(saṃvādaḥ, m. 1st s.)(saṃvādena, m. 3rd s.)(api*)
body.translated_text: 2854. Indeed, just as the first cognition requires accordance with its [object] — even so, again, accordance must be sought even through [further] accordance.

body.text:
2855.
(tu*)(yadi*)(kasyacit, n. 6th s.)(pramāṇatā, f. 1st s.)(iṣyeta ”iṣ Pass. Opt.)(eva*)(svataḥ* [-tas suff.])(kena, m. 3rd s.)(hetunā, m. 3rd s.)(pradveṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(prathamasya, n. 6th s.)(bhāve, m. 7th s.)(tathā*)
body.translated_text: 2855. But if the validity of some [cognition] is desired as intrinsic — by what reason is there hostility toward the first [cognition having such validity]?

body.text:
2856.

body.translated_text: 2856. If thus validity is dependent on perception and the like [as] a quality — and qualities never exist without a valid means [to establish them] —

2857.

body.translated_text: 2857. Then, the validity too of him who desires another valid means — which determines a quality — is dependent [on yet another] — whose quality is determined by another —

body.text:
2858.
(eva*)(yathā*)(ādye, n. 7th s.)(tathā*)(anyatra*)(iti*)(anavasthā, f. 1st s.)(vat*)(pūrva-)(evam*)(tatra*)(tatra*)(na*)(labhemahi ”labh I C. Opt. 1p pl.)(vyavasthām, f. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 2858. Just as in the first [case], so too elsewhere — thus an infinite regress as before; even so, there we would not obtain stability.

body.text:
2859.
(atha*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(guṇa-)(na*)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)(prāmāṇyam, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(āyatta-)(guṇa-)(ādyam, n. 1st s.)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(artha-)(api*)(na*)(apekṣeta ”īkṣ I C. Āt. Opt.)(pramām, f. 2nd s.)(guṇa-)
body.translated_text: 2859. Now, [if] cognition is not desired [to have] validity as a dependent quality — the first consciousness regarding an object too would not require a [separate] valid cognition as a quality.

body.text:
2860.

body.translated_text: 2860. Therefore, even having gone far — that which must necessarily be accepted — intrinsic validity (<s>svataḥ-prāmāṇya</s>) — somewhere — it is better that it be established right at the beginning.

body.text:
2861.
(vā*)(kena, m. 3rd s.)(abhyadhikena, m. 3rd s.)(saṃvāda-)(vijñāne, n. 1st d.)(guṇa-)(balena, n. 3rd s.)(yat-)(ādyasya, n. 6th s.)(adhīnatvam, n. 1st s.)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 2861. Or, by what superior force of the quality of the accordance-cognition — by which the dependence of the first [cognition on it] is [established] — that [is questionable].

body.text:
2862.
(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(prāmāṇyam, n. 1st s.)(sthitam, n. 1st s.)(svataḥ-)(sarvatra*)(autsargikam, n. 1st s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(apohyate ”ūh Pass.)(bādha-)(jñānābhyām, n. 3rd d.)(kāraṇa-)(duṣṭatva-)
body.translated_text: 2862. Therefore, validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) is established as intrinsic and universally applicable (<s>autsargika</s>) everywhere; that is removed by refuting cognition [arising from] defective causes.

body.text:
2863.

body.translated_text: 2863. And even when this [invalidity] is dependent on another, there is no infinite regress; indeed, this is dependent on a valid means; and that [valid means] is established intrinsically.

body.text:
2864.

body.translated_text: 2864. Indeed, just as a valid means is not established by another valid means — even so, invalidity is indeed not established from an invalid means.

2865.

body.translated_text: 2865. Indeed, when the support is of the same kind, non-establishment follows; but the firmly established root of a different kind — because of having a different cause —

2866.
(bādhaka-)(pratyayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tāvat*)(avadharaṇam, n. 1st s.)(artha-)(anyatva-)(anapekṣa-)(pramāṇatvāt, n. 5th s.)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(apohate ”ūh I C. Āt.)(pūrva-)(jñānam, n. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 2866. The refuting cognition (<s>bādhaka-pratyaya</s>) is, to begin with, the ascertainment of the otherness of the object; because of being a valid means that does not depend [on the prior cognition], it removes the prior cognition.

body.text:
2867.

body.translated_text: 2867. But again, there too there may be dependence [on checking] an exception — when somewhere a suspicion has arisen; that too is removed by the first [cognition] in a small [way].

body.text:
2868.
(yadi*)(antaram, n. 1st s.)(bādhaka-)(utpannam, n. 1st s.)(anvicchataḥ, m. 6th s.)(aparam*, n. 2st s. [adv.])(tataḥ*)(madhyama-)(bādhena, m. 3rd s.)(pramāṇatā, f. 1st s.)(pūrvasya, n. 6th s.)(eva*)
body.translated_text: 2868. If another refuting [cognition] has arisen, and one seeks yet another — then by the intermediate refutation, the validity is of the first [cognition] alone.

body.text:
2869.
(atha*)(samyañc-)(anveṣaṇe, n. 7th s.)(kṛte, n. 7th s.)(anurūpa-)(yatnena, m. 3rd s.)(na*)(bādhakam, n. 1st s.)(bādhaka-)(bhavet ”bhū Opt.)(vijñātam, n. 1st s.)(a-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(mūla-)
body.translated_text: 2869. Now, when a proper investigation has been made with appropriate effort — the refuter of the refuter is not found, because of the non-existence of a root [for it].

body.text:
2870.
(tataḥ*)(nirapavādatvāt, n. 5th s.)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(eva*)(balīyasā, n. 3rd s.)(bādhyate ”bādh Pass.)(ādyam, n. 1st s.)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(pramāṇatvam, n. 1st s.)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(eva*)(apohyate ”ūh Pass.)
body.translated_text: 2870. Then, because of being without exception, by that very stronger [cognition], the first is refuted; by that, the validity of that [first cognition] alone is removed.

body.text:
2871.
(evam*)(na*)(ativartate ”vṛt I C. Āt.)(tritayam, n. 2nd s.)(jñāna-)(parīkṣaka-)(ca*)(tataḥ*)(bādhena, m. 3rd s. [bv. cpd.])(a-jāta-)(punaḥ*)(āśaṅkyam, n. 1st s.)(bādhakam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2871. Thus, [the examination] does not exceed the triad of cognition-examiners; and therefore, when a refuter whose [own] refutation has not arisen — again a [further] refuter is to be suspected.

body.text:
2872.
(hi*)(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(mohāt, m. 5th s.)(utprekṣeta ”īkṣ I C. Opt. Āt.)(bādhakam, n. 2nd s.)(api*)(ajātam, n. 2nd s.)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(ātmā, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(saṃśaya-)(sarva-)(vyavahāreṣu, m. 7th pl.)(vrajet ”vraj I C. Opt.)(kṣayam, m. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 2872. Indeed, he who out of delusion would suspect a refuter that has not arisen — he, being of a doubtful nature, would go to destruction in all transactions.

body.text:
2873.
(ca*)(tathā*)(vāsudevena, m. 3rd s.)(ninditā, f. 1st s.)(saṃśaya-)(ātmatā, f. 1st s.)(iti*)(na*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(lokaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(paraḥ, m. 1st s.)(kaunteya, m. 1st s. vocative)(asti ”as II C.)(saṃśaya-)(ātmanaḥ, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2873. And thus, by <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the nature of doubt has been condemned: 'Neither this world nor the other, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, exists for the doubter.'

body.text:
2874.

body.translated_text: 2874. Therefore, regarding whichever opinion — as much exception as is possible — only to that extent, having been investigated, and when [the refuter] has not arisen with that nature —

body.text:
2875.
(pramātṛbhiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(kāmaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(ātman-)(na*)(sthātavyam, n. 1st s.)(utprekṣamāṇaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(bhūyaḥ*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(tatra*)(vastuni, n. 7th s.)(iti*)(api*)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(kadācit*)
body.translated_text: 2875. By cognizers who desire [truth], one should not remain imagining [further refuters]; for regarding that object — thus it may be [said] — at some time [a refuter may arise, but one should not wait indefinitely].

body.text:
2876.
(hi*)(ye, m. 1st pl.)(bhedāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(deśa-)(kāla-)(nara-)(avasthā-)(siddhāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(eva*)(yasmin, n. 7th s.)(saṃvyavahārataḥ* [-tas suff.])(arthinā, m. 3rd s.)(bādhaka-)(apekṣyāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(te, m. 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 2876. Indeed, those divisions [arising from] place, time, person, and condition — which are established in whichever [object] through conventional practice — by the seeker, refuters [of those types] are to be sought.

body.text:
2877.
(dūra-)(deśa-)(vyavasthānāt, n. 5th s.)(asamyañc-)(darśane, n. 7th s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(anya-)(āśaṅkā, f. 1st s.)(kvacit*)(tatra*)(samīpa-)(gati-)(mātrakam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2877. Because of being situated in a distant place, there may be an incorrect perception — another suspicion somewhere; there, merely going close [is sufficient to resolve it].

body.text:
2878.

body.translated_text: 2878. The limit of the exception regarding time, person, and condition — in another [case] — but no dependence exists there — like the cognition of a mirage and the like.

body.text:
2879.
(evam*)(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kāle, m. 7th s.)(santamase, n. 7th s.)(saṃśayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(gava-)(aśva-)(ādi-)(bhrānteḥ, f. 5th s.)(nirṇayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(avadhiḥ, m. 1st s.)(tatra*)(bhavana-)(prakāśī- [form with affix cvi])
body.translated_text: 2879. Thus, whatever doubt [arises] in time of deep darkness — [whether it is] a cow, horse, and the like — the limit of the ascertainment there from the confusion is light in the dwelling.

body.text:
2880.
(tathā*)(hi*)(candra-)(moha-)(diś-)(varṇa-)(svara-)(veda-)(ādiṣu, m. 7th s.)(anyathātve, n. 7th s.)(avadhāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(sampraśnāt, m. 5th s.)(antara-)(puruṣa-)
body.translated_text: 2880. Thus indeed, regarding the moon, delusion, direction, color, voice, the <s>Veda</s>, and the like — in [cases of] being otherwise — the ascertainment [comes] from questioning another person.

body.text:
2881.
(indriyaiḥ, m. 3rd pl. [bv. cpd.])(kṣata-)(rāga-)(dveṣa-)(mada-)(unmāda-)(kṣud-)(tṛṣṇā-)(ādi-)(durjñāne, n. 7th s.)(viparyayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(arthe, m. 7th s.)(jñāyamāne ”jñā Pass, m. 7th s.)(a-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 2881. When an object is being cognized by [one whose] senses are impaired — [through] passion, hatred, intoxication, madness, hunger, thirst, and so forth — there is error in [such] faulty cognition, because of the absence of that [valid cognition].

body.text:
2882.
(api*)(vyavahāre, m. 7th s.)(ṛṇa-)(ādi-)(vivadamānayoḥ ”vad I C. Āt., m. 7th d.)(dvayoḥ, m. 7th d.)(ekam, n. 1st s.)(vākyam, n. 1st s.)(prati-arthinaḥ, m. 6th s.)(dve, n. 1st d.)(vākye, n. 1st d.)(pūrva-vādinaḥ, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2882. Moreover, in [legal] proceedings — when two parties are disputing about debts and such — [there is] one statement of the defendant, and two statements of the plaintiff.

body.text:
2883.
(eva*)(bhayāt, m. 5th s.)(anavasthā-)(na*)(adhikam, n. 1st s.)(vākyam, n. 1st s.)(likhyate ”likh Pass.)(tu*)(tataḥ*)(svāmin-)(sākṣin-)(sabhā-sadaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(brūyuḥ ”bru II C. Opt. III p. pl.)(nirṇayam, m. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 2883. Out of fear of infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>), no additional statement is recorded; rather, the master, the witnesses, and the members of the assembly should pronounce the verdict.

body.text:
2884.
(evam*)(sarvatra*)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)(vikriyā, f. 1st s.)(trayasya, n. 6th s.)(jñāna-)(eva*)(ataḥ*)(eva*)(devānām, m. 6th pl.)(abhidhīyate ”dhā Pass.)(tri-satyatā, f. 1st s.)(api*)
body.translated_text: 2884. Thus, in all [such cases], a modification of only the triad of cognitions is accepted; and therefore, the 'triple truthfulness' (<s>tri-satyatā</s>) of the gods is declared.

body.text:
2885.
(tena, n. 3rd s.)(pramāṇatve, n. 7th s.)(svataḥ* [-tas suff.])(na*)(anavasthā, f. 1st s.)(api*)(ubhayoḥ, n. 6th d.)(ataḥ*)(pramāṇatva-)(apramāṇatve, n. 1st d.)(sthite, n. 1st d.)(yathā-yogam*, m. 2nd s. [adv.])
body.translated_text: 2885. Therefore, there is no infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>) in [establishing] validity (<s>pramāṇatva</s>) intrinsically (<s>svataḥ</s>); hence, validity and invalidity (<s>pramāṇatva</s> and <s>apramāṇatva</s>) of both [cognition and its object] are established, each in its proper manner.

body.text:
2886.
(tat, n. 1st s.)(vākyam, n. 1st s.)(yat, n. 1st s.)(avadhāryate ”dhṛ Caus. Pass.)(nityam, n. 1st s.)(vā*)(praṇītam, n. 1st s.)(āpta-)(na*)(api*)(manāk*)(dūṣyate ”duṣ Caus.
Pass.)
body.translated_text: 2886. That statement which is ascertained — whether eternal or composed by a trustworthy person (<s>āpta</s>) — is not vitiated even in the slightest.

body.text:
2887.
(eva*)(te, m. 1st pl.)(ye, m. 1st pl.)(vidyā-guravaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(ca*)(saha-adhyāyinaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(vārayantaḥ ”vṛ Caus., m. 1st pl.)(vināśam, m. 2nd s.)(tatra*)(kṣamāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(pālana-)(tādṛśām, n. 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 2887. Those who are teachers of knowledge (<s>vidyā-guru</s>) and fellow-students — [who are] capable of averting destruction — they are competent in the preservation of such [statements].

body.text:
2888.
(ataḥ*)(vākyam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(dūṣyate ”duṣ Caus. Pass.)(vā*)(doṣaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(niṣiddhaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(guṇa-)(yadvā*)(a-bhāve, m. 7th s.)(kartuḥ, m. 6th s.)(na*)(te, m. 1st pl.)(doṣāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(nirāśrayāḥ, m. 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 2888. Therefore, the statement is not vitiated — either by faults that have been prohibited, or by [the absence of] qualities; or, in the absence of an author, those faults are without any basis.

body.text:
2889.
(tatra*)(dvayam, n. 1st s.)(dṛṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(ukteḥ, f. 6th s.)(āpta-)(ātmakam, n. 1st s.)(a-bhāva-)(doṣa-)(guṇa-)(yathā*)(pramāṇatvam, n. 1st s.)(asti ”as II C.)(na*)(guṇebhyaḥ, m. 5th pl.)(tathā*)(uditam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2889. In that regard, two [aspects] are observed in a statement of a trustworthy person (<s>āpta</s>): the absence of faults and [the presence of] qualities. Just as validity (<s>pramāṇatva</s>) exists, so it has been stated — it does not [arise] from qualities [alone].

body.text:
2890.
(ataḥ*)(guṇavattvāt, n. 5th s.)(vaktuḥ, m. 6th s.)(na*)(doṣāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(nirākṛtāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(tat-)(ca*)(pramāṇam, n. 1st s.)(vākyam, n. 1st s.)(svataḥ* [-tas suff.])(upalakṣitam, n. 1st s.)(a-bhāva-)(doṣa-)
body.translated_text: 2890. Therefore, because the speaker possesses qualities, the faults are not thereby refuted; and that statement is a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) — recognized intrinsically (<s>svataḥ</s>) [as such] — [through] the absence of faults.

body.text:
2891.
(cet*)(a-bhāvah, m. 1st s.)(doṣa-)(vākyeṣu, n. 7th pl.)(āpta-)(gamyate ”gam Pass.)(guṇebhyaḥ, m. 5th pl.)(bhavet ”bhū II C. Opt.)(sā, f. 1st s.)(eva*)(anavasthā, f. 1st s.)(anugāminaḥ, m. 6th s.)(guṇavattva-)
body.translated_text: 2891. If the absence of faults in the statements of a trustworthy person (<s>āpta</s>) is known from [their] qualities, then that very same infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>) would follow — in [establishing] the possession of qualities.

body.text:
2892.
(eṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(doṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(guṇa-)(na*)(eva*)(apekṣyate ”īkṣ Pass.)(tadā*)(na*)(eva*)(jñāyamānatayā, f. 3rd s.)(guṇāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(upakāriṇaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(tatra*)
body.translated_text: 2892. This is not a fault — [for] cognition does not depend upon qualities [for its validity]; for qualities are not helpful there by virtue of being [themselves] cognized.

body.text:
2893.
(mātreṇa, n. 3rd s.)(sattā-)(te, m. 1st pl.)(sarve, m. 1st pl.)(kṣamāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(vyāvarttana-)(doṣa-)(teṣu, m. 7th pl.)(satsu, m. 7th pl.)(na*)(jāyate ”jan IV. C. Āt.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(viṣayam, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(doṣa-)(nṛ-)
body.translated_text: 2893. By the mere existence [of causes], all those [qualities] are capable of averting faults; when those [causes] are present, cognition does not arise [as] having faults and human [deficiencies] as its domain.

body.text:
2894.
(ca*)(jñāyamānatvāt, n. 5th s.)(doṣaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(na*)(apodyate ”vad Pass.)(prāmāṇyam, n. 1st s.)(siddham, n. 1st s.)(anapodita-)(tat, n. 1st s.)(sthitam, n. 1st s.)(svataḥ* [-tas suff.])(iha*)(api*)
body.translated_text: 2894. And because [cognition] is being cognized [as valid], its validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) is not refuted by faults; that [validity], being unrefuted, is established intrinsically (<s>svataḥ</s>) here as well.

body.text:
2895.
(tu*)(pauruṣeye, n. 7th s.)(śaṅkyate ”śaṅk Pass.)(iti*)(santi ”as II C. III p. pl.)(doṣāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(santi ”as II C. III p. pl.)(na*)(vede, m. 7th s.)(ca*)(a-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(kartuḥ, m. 6th s.)(asti ”as Ii C.)(eva*)(na*)(āśaṅkā, f. 1st s.)(naḥ, 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 2895. [Objection:] 'But in [a statement that is] of human origin (<s>pauruṣeya</s>), it is suspected: "there are faults" — but in the <s>Veda</s>, because of the absence of an author, there is indeed no such suspicion for us.'

body.text:
2896.
(ataḥ*)(yat*)(prāmāṇyam, n. 1st s.)(ucyate ”vac Pass.)(vede, m. 7th s.)(anapekṣatvāt, n. 5th s.)(tadā*)(sutarām*)(siddhyati ”sidh IV C.)(svataḥ* [-tas suff.])(praṇīte, n. 7th s.)(āptena, m. 3rd s.)(api*)
body.translated_text: 2896. [Reply:] Therefore, the validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) that is declared for the <s>Veda</s> — because it does not depend [on anything] — is all the more established intrinsically (<s>svataḥ</s>) even [in a text] composed by a trustworthy person (<s>āpta</s>).

body.text:
2897.
(tayā, f. 3rd s.)(eva*)(yā, f. 1st s.)(anya-)(pramāṇaiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(asaṅgatiḥ, f. 1st s.)(sarva-)(kālam*, m. 2nd s. [adv.])(arthe, m. 7th s.)(veda-)(asya, m. 6th s.)(pramāṇatvam, n. 1st s.)(anyathā*)(anuvādatvam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2897. By that very non-concordance (<s>asaṅgati</s>) with other <s>pramāṇa</s>s at all times — regarding an object — the <s>Veda</s>'s validity (<s>pramāṇatva</s>) [is established]; otherwise, it would be mere reiteration (<s>anuvāda</s>).

body.text:
2898.
(saṅgatiḥ, f. 1st s.)(na*)(eva*)(kāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(pramāṇatve, n. 7th s.)(anyasya, n. 6th s.)(api*)(hi*)(tulya-)(arthānām, n. 6th pl. [bv. cpd.])(vikalpena, m. 3rd s.)(pramāṇatā, f. 1st s.)(eva*)(ekasya, n. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2898. Concordance (<s>saṅgati</s>) is not at all the cause of the validity (<s>pramāṇatva</s>) of another [means of knowledge]; for, among [means] having the same objects, the validity of [only] one [is established] through distinction.

body.text:
2899.
(api*)(yatra*)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(paricchedaḥ, m. 1st s.)(punaḥ*)(uttaraiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(pramāṇaiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(nūnam*)(api*)(tatra*)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(arthaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(sphuṭam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(avadhṛtaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pūrveṇa, n. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 2899. Even where there might be ascertainment again by subsequent <s>pramāṇa</s>s — surely even there, that object was not clearly ascertained by the prior [<s>pramāṇa</s>].

body.text:
2900.
(na*)(pramāṇatā, f. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(arthe, m. 7th s.)(vinaṣṭe, n. 7th s.)(sakṛt-)(jāta-)(ca*)(śrautrā, f. 1st s.)(dhīḥ, f. 1st s.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(apramāṇam, n. 1st s.)(asaṅgatā, f. 1st s.)(netra-)(ādibhiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 2900. [If] the object has perished — [there] would be no validity (<s>pramāṇatā</s>); and the auditory cognition (<s>śrautrā dhīḥ</s>), once arisen, would be an invalid means of knowledge (<s>apramāṇa</s>) — [due to] non-concordance with the eyes and other [senses].

body.text:
2901.
(cet*)(pramāṇatā, f. 1st s.)(asyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(siddhā, f. 1st s.)(sambandhāt, m. 5th s.)(antareṇa, n. 3rd s.)(śrotra-)(jñāna-)(vede, m. 7th s.)(api*)(saṅgateḥ, f. 5th s.)(antara-)(vijñāna-)(janya-)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 2901. If the validity (<s>pramāṇatā</s>) of this [auditory cognition] is established independently of [its] relation with auditory cognition — then in the case of the <s>Veda</s> as well, [validity would follow] from concordance — [being] produced by an intermediate cognition.

body.text:
2902.
(tu*)(api*)(dvayoḥ, n. 6th d.)(buddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(asti ”as II C.)(na*)(janyā, f. 1st s.)(antara-)(sādhana-)(ataḥ*)(na*)(vāñchyate ”vāñch Pass.)(saṃvādaḥ, m. 1st s.)(jñāna-)(kṛta-)(antara-)(hetu-)
body.translated_text: 2902. But the cognition of both [parties] does not exist as produced by an intermediate means of proof; therefore, concordance (<s>saṃvāda</s>) is not sought — [being] caused by an intermediate cognition-produced ground.

body.text:
2903.
(tu*)(yathā*)(pratyakṣe, n. 7th s.)(kāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(saṅgatiḥ, f. 1st s.)(antara-)(vijñāna-)(adhīna-)(eka-)(indriya-)(tathā*)(kathyatām ”kath Pass. Imperative 3p s.)(kḷptā, f. 1st s.)(vede, m. 7th s.)(api*)
body.translated_text: 2903. But just as in perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), concordance with an intermediate cognition is the cause — [being] dependent on a single sense-faculty — let it be explained how [this] is established in the case of the <s>Veda</s> as well.

body.text:
2904.
(hi*)(labhyamāne ”labh Pass., n. 7th s.)(eva*)(ekena, n. 3rd s.)(vākyena, n. 3rd s.)(kāla-)(deśa-)(nara-)(ādiṣu, m. 7th pl.)(na*)(antaram, n. 1st s.)(kāraṇa-)(mṛgyam, n. 1st s.)(saṃvāde, m. 7th s.)(artha-)
body.translated_text: 2904. For when [the meaning] is obtained by a single statement alone — in [various] times, places, persons, and so forth — no additional cause need be sought when there is concordance regarding the object.

body.text:
2905.
(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(yat, n. 1st s.)(dṛḍham, n. 1st s.)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(utpannam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(visaṃvadet ”vad I C. Opt.)(vijñānaiḥ, n. 3rd s.)(antara-)(deśa-)(ādi-)(tat, n. 1st s.)(asaṃsayam, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(pramāṇam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2905. Therefore, whatever firm cognition (<s>vijñāna</s>) has arisen — [that which] would not be contradicted by cognitions [arising from] other places and so forth — that is undoubtedly a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>).

body.text:
2906.
(ca*)(pramāṇatā, f. 1st s.)(śabda-)(ādīnām, m. 6th pl.)(na*)(sādhyā, f. 1st s.)(anumānena, n. 3rd s.)(mā*)(aviśeṣataḥ* [-tas suff.])(sā, f. 1st s.)(pratyakṣasya, n. 6th s.)(api*)(bhūt ”bhū augmentless aorist)(sādhyā, f. 1st s.)(anumāna-)(eva*)
body.translated_text: 2906. And the validity (<s>pramāṇatā</s>) of verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) and the rest is not to be established by inference (<s>anumāna</s>) — lest, without distinction, that [validity] of perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) too would become something to be established by <s>anumāna</s> alone.

body.text:
2907.
(yena, n. 3rd s.)(pramāṇatvam, n. 1st s.)(pramāṇānām, n. 6th pl.)(sādhyate ”sidh Caus. Pass.)(anyena, n. 3rd s.)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(api*)(sādhyatvāt, n. 5th s.)(anyena, n. 3rd s.)(prasajyate ”sañj Pass.)(anavasthā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2907. By whatever [means] the validity (<s>pramāṇatva</s>) of the <s>pramāṇa</s>s is established — since the validity of that [means] too must be established by yet another — an infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>) follows.

body.text:
2908.
(cet*)(pramāṇatā, f. 1st s.)(sādhakasya, n. 6th s.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(asādhitā, f. 1st s.)(anyena, n. 3rd s.)(sā, f. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(siddhā, f. 1st s.)(eva*)(tat-vat*)(api*)(sādhyānām, n. 6th pl.)(tataḥ*)
body.translated_text: 2908. If the validity (<s>pramāṇatā</s>) of the proving [cognition] were unestablished by another, then that [validity] would [already] be established [by itself]; and likewise, [the validity] of those to be proved would then [also be established].

body.text:
2909.
(nanu*)(pratyakṣa-)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(na*)(gṛhyate ”gṛh Pass.)(evam*)(iti*)(pramāṇam, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(ittham*)(agṛhītena, n. 3rd s.)(na*)(vyavahāraḥ, m. 1st s.)(avakalpyate ”kḷp Caus. Pass.)
body.translated_text: 2909. [Objection:] 'But perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) and the rest are not apprehended as "this is a <s>pramāṇa</s>" — and with [a <s>pramāṇa</s> that is] thus unapprehended, practical activity (<s>vyavahāra</s>) cannot be conceived.'

body.text:
2910.
(pūrvam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(grahaṇāt)(pramāṇam, n. 1st s.)(pratiṣṭhitam, n. 1st s.)(sva-)(rūpeṇa, n. 3rd s.)(ca*)(tat-)(sva-)(arthe, m. 7th s.)(nirapekṣam, n. 1st s.)(pramite, m. 7th s.)(mīyate ”mā Pass.)(paraiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 2910. [Reply:] Prior to [such explicit] apprehension, a <s>pramāṇa</s> is established by its own nature; and regarding its own object, it is independent [of external confirmation] — [only] when [the object is already] measured is it [re-]measured by others.

body.text:
2911.
(ca*)(yathā*)(sarve, m. 1st pl.)(viṣayāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(gṛhyante ”grah Pass. III p. pl.)(cakṣuḥ-)(ādibhiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(indriyaiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(eva*)(aviditaiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(tathā*)(te, m. 1st pl.)(pramāṇaiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(api*)
body.translated_text: 2911. And just as all objects are apprehended by the sense-faculties such as the eyes — even though those [faculties themselves] are unknown — so too [are objects apprehended] by the <s>pramāṇa</s>s.

body.text:
2912.
(tena, n. 3rd s.)(jñāyamānatvam, n. 1st s.)(atra*)(na*)(upayujyate ”yuj Pass.)(prāmāṇye, n. 7th s.)(anubhavaḥ, m. 1st s.)(viṣaya-)(api*)(labhyate ”labh Pass.)(asmāt, n. 5th s.)(eva*)(ajñātāt, n. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 2912. Therefore, [the <s>pramāṇa</s>] being [itself] cognized is not required here for [establishing] validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>); experience (<s>anubhava</s>) of the object is also obtained from this very [<s>pramāṇa</s>], even though it is [itself] unknown.

body.text:
2913.
(iva*)(pramāṇam, n. 1st s.)(apramāṇam, n. 1st s.)(punaḥ*)(sthitam, n. 1st s.)(sva-)(arthe, m. 7th s.)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(mithyātvam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(gṛhyeta ”grah Pass. Opt.)(ṛte*)(antarāt, n. 5th s.)(pramāṇa-)
body.translated_text: 2913. Just as an invalid means of knowledge (<s>apramāṇa</s>), again, is established in its own object — its falsity (<s>mithyātva</s>) would not be apprehended without a [subsequent] <s>pramāṇa</s>.

body.text:
2914.
(hi*)(anyathā-)(bhāvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(arthasya, m. 6th s.)(na*)(āttaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pūrveṇa, n. 3rd s.)(vat*)(tathātva-)(tat*)(atra*)(api*)(dhīḥ, f. 1st s.)(bhāve, m. 7th s.)(anyathā-)(yat-vā*)(kāraṇe, n. 7th s.)(duṣṭa-)
body.translated_text: 2914. For the otherness of the object — not grasped by the prior [cognition] — like that [prior cognition's] being-such (<s>tathātva</s>) — here too, [one would need] a cognition; or, when there is a defective cause [producing] an otherwise [cognition] —

body.text:
2915.
(eva*)(tāvatā, n. 3rd s.)(mithyātvam, n. 1st s.)(gṛhyate ”grah Pass.)(na*)(anya-)(hetukam, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(avastham, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(utpatti-)(idam, n. 1st s.)(mīyate ”mā Pass.)(iti*)(pramāṇam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2915. By just that much, the falsity (<s>mithyātva</s>) is apprehended — not [as] caused by another [means]; this <s>pramāṇa</s>, [having] the nature of its origination, is measured as 'this [cognition is valid].'

body.text:
2916.
(ataḥ*)(api*)(yatra*)(mithyātvam, n. 1st s.)(pratipādyate ”pad Caus. Pass.)(parebhyaḥ, m. 4th pl.)(tatra*)(api*)(etat, n. 1st s.)(dvayam, n. 1st s.)(vācyam, n. 1st s.)(tu*)(na*)(mātṛkam, n. 1st s.)(sādharmya-)
body.translated_text: 2916. Therefore, even where falsity (<s>mithyātva</s>) is demonstrated to others — even there, these two [aspects] are to be stated; but [it is] not [established] merely by [invoking] the authority [of another] — [rather] by similarity of properties (<s>sādharmya</s>).

body.text:

body.translated_text: Those who are undiscerning, who resort to mere similarity to establish the invalidity of all <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid cognition),

2918.
(teṣām, m. 6th pl.)(tādṛk, n. 1st s.)(sādhana-kalpanam, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(ātman-)(vadhāya, m. 4th s.)(parasya, m. 6th s.)(api*)(utpadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(tādṛśam, n. 1st s.)(pratibimbena, n. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: For them, such a formulation of proof serves only for self-destruction; and for the opponent too, such [a counter-argument] arises through reflection,

body.text:
2919.
(ca*)(pratiṣiddhatvāt, n. 5th s.)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(sādhanam, n. 1st s.)(a-yathā-bhūta-)(na*)(kṣamam, n. 1st s.)(bādhitum* ”bādh)(codanām, f. 2nd s.)(autsargika-)(pramāṇatvāt, n. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: And since it has been refuted by that, a proof that is contrary to reality is not capable of invalidating <s>codanā</s> (Vedic injunction), because it has general validity as a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition).

body.text:
2920.
(atra*)(abhidhīyate ”dhā Pass.)(tu*)(nanu*)(eṣā, f. 1st s.)(vyavasthā, f. 1st s.)(sa-)(nibandhanā, f. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(teṣām, n. 6th pl.)(bhāvānām, m. 6th pl.)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)(sthitiḥ, f. 1st s.)

body.translated_text: But here it is replied: Is not this arrangement held to be well-founded? The persistence of those entities is accepted.

body.text:
2921.
(lābhe, m. 7th s.)(ātman-)(ādīnām, m. 6th pl.)(ghaṭa-)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)(apekṣitā, f. 1st s.)(kāraṇa-)(labdha-)(ātmanām, m. 6th pl. [bv. cpd.])(pravṛttiḥ, f. 1st s.)(eva*)(svayam*)(sva-)(kāryeṣu, n. 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: Upon the attainment of the self and other [conditions], the operation of those that have obtained their nature through [requisite] causes is accepted as proceeding spontaneously toward their own effects, like a pot.

body.text:
2922.
(tu*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(yat, n. 1st s.)(tvayā, 3rd s.)(api*)(iṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(asthiram, n. 1st s.)(anantaram*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(janma-)(asataḥ, n. 6th s.)(paścāt*)(labda-)(ātmanaḥ, n. 6th s. [bv. cpd.])(kīdṛśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vyāpāraḥ, m. 1st s.)(tasya, n. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: But the cognition which is also accepted by you as impermanent — what kind of activity can it have, since it is non-existent immediately after its birth, having obtained its nature [only momentarily]?

body.text:
2923.
(hi*)(vyāpāraḥ, m. 1st s.)(kāraṇānām, n. 6th pl.)(dṛṣṭaḥ, m. 1st s.)(atirekataḥ* [-tas suff.])(janman-)(janma, n. 1st s.)(vivakṣyate ”vac Desiderative Pass.)(iti*)(mā*)(bhūt ”bhū augmentless Aorist)(tathā*)(pramāṇe, n. 7th s.)(api*)
body.translated_text: For the activity of causes is observed to go beyond [mere] birth. Lest it be intended that birth [itself constitutes activity] — even in the case of a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition),

body.text:
2924.
(hi*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(na*)(āste ”ās Ii C. Āt.)(api*)(kṣaṇam, n. 2nd s.)(vā*)(jāyate ”jan IV C. Āt.)(ātmakam, n. 1st s.)(apramā-)(yena, n. 3rd s.)(vyāpriyeta ”pṛ Pass. Opt.)(paścāt*)(grahaṇe, n. 7th s.)(artha-)(vat*)(indriya-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: For that does not remain even for a moment, or else it arises with the nature of non-valid cognition, by which it would operate subsequently in the apprehension of objects, like the senses and so forth.

body.text:
2925.
(api*)(atha*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(abhyupagamyate ”gam Pass.)(akṣaṇikam, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(nityam, n. 1st s.)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(virodhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(abhyupeta-)(evam*)(avabādhanam, n. 1st s.)(yuktyā, f. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: Now, if cognition is accepted as non-momentary and permanent, this contradiction is already acknowledged; such refutation has been established through reasoning,

body.text:
2926.
(sādhita-)(sa-vistaram, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(vastu, n. 1st s.)(bhaṅgam, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(kṣaṇa-)(ca*)(nityam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(janyate ”jan Pass.)(iti*)(kā, f. 1st s.)(apekṣitā, f. 1st s.)(asya, n. 6th s.)(kāraṇa-)
body.translated_text: All reality has been demonstrated in detail to be momentary; and what is permanent is not produced — so what need is there for a cause of this?

body.text:
2927.
(ca*)(ataḥ*)(śakyate ”śak Pass.)(vaktum* ”vac)(eva*)(svataḥ* [-tas suff.])(na*)(vartate ”vṛ I C. Āt.)(pramā, f. 1st s.)(paścāt*)(sva-)(kāryeṣu, n. 7th pl.)(nairūpyāt, n. 5th s.)(vat*)(gagana-abja-)
body.translated_text: And therefore it can indeed be said: valid cognition does not operate intrinsically toward its own effects subsequently, because of the absence of its own form, like a sky-flower.

body.text:
2928.
(vā*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(astu ”as II C. Imperative 3p s.)(akṣaṇkam, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(svataḥ* [-tas suff.])(pravartate ”vṛt I C. Āt.)(viniścityai, f. 4th s.)(sva-)(prāmāṇya-)(tat*)(kim*)(saṃśaya-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: Or let cognition be non-momentary; it operates intrinsically — then what [role do] doubt and the rest [play] in the ascertainment of its own validity?

body.text:
2929.
(yasmāt, n. 5th s.)(niścayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(prāmāṇya-)(bhāvikaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tatra*)(tat-)(mātra-)(tasmin, m. 7th s.)(jāte, m. 7th s.)(anāspadau, m. 1st d.)(sandeha-)(viparyāsau, m. 1st d.)
body.translated_text: Since certainty is inherent in validity, when that alone arises, doubt and error have no basis therein.

body.text:
2930.
(hi*)(manasoḥ, n. 6th d.)(niścaya-)(āropa-)(bhāvataḥ* [-tas suff.])(bādhaka-)(bādhya-)(samāropa-)(viveke, m. 7th s.)(niścayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vartate ”vṛt I C. Āt.)(akhilaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: For certainty operates in the discrimination of what is to be sublated and the superimposition of the sublator, from the existence of the superimposition of certainty upon both minds.

body.text:
2931.
(ca*)(tataḥ*)(siddhaye, f. 4th s.)(prāmāṇya-)(mati-)(janya-)(codanā-)(yuktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(uttha-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(hetu-)(varjita-)(doṣa-)(apārthikā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: And therefore, the reasoning born of cognition for establishing the validity of <s>codanā</s> (Vedic injunction) is purposeless, since it arises from a cause devoid of defects.

body.text:
2932.
(yadi*)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)(svataḥ-pramāṇatve, n. 7th s.)(sā, f. 1st s.)(nivāriṇī, f. 1st s.)(apavāda-)(api*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(na*)(evam*)(asambhavāt, m. 5th s.)(āśaṅkāyāḥ, f. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: If in [the theory of] intrinsic validity, that [reasoning] is held to be a remover of exceptions, that is not so, because such an apprehension is impossible.

body.text:
2933.
(sā, f. 1st s.)(āśaṅkā, f. 1st s.)(tāvat*)(eva*)(yāvat*)(niścayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(udeti ”i II C.)(niścaye, m. 7th s.)(gate, m. 7th s.)(tat-)(kutaḥ*)(nu*)(iyam, f. 1st s.)(aprāmāṇye, n. 7th s.)(tasmin, n. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: That apprehension lasts only so long as certainty does not arise; when certainty has come, then whence this [apprehension] regarding invalidity?

body.text:
2934.
(yena, n. 3rd s.)(yatnaḥ, m. 1st s.)(artham*, m. 2nd s. [adv.])(vinivṛtti-)(tat-)(vrajet ”vraj I C. Opt.)(sārthakatām, f. 2nd s.)(hi*)(niścita-tādātmyaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(sthāṇau, m. 7th s.)(na*)(śaṅkate ”śaṅk I C. Āt.)(anyathātvam, n. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: For one whose identity has been ascertained with certainty does not doubt the otherness of a post; the effort for the removal of that [doubt] would achieve its purpose,

body.text:
2935,
When a firm conviction (niścayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(jāyate ”jan IV C. Āt.)(yat-)(rūpa-)(yatra*)(vastuni, n. 7th s.)(yasmāt, n. 5th s.)(śaṅkāyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(viparyaya-)(tat-)(nivartanam, n. 1st s.)(tataḥ*)(eva*)
body.translated_text: When a firm conviction arises regarding the nature of whatever object, then the cessation of contrary doubt follows from that alone.

body.text:
2936.
(yathā*)(astitā-)(pāvaka-)(ādi-)(gatau, f. 7th s.)(liṅgebhyaḥ, n. 5th pl.)(ādi-)(dhūma-)(nāstitā-)(tat-)(upapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(vyavacchedaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tataḥ*)(eva*)
body.translated_text: Just as the existence of fire and the like is [established] from inferential marks such as smoke, and the non-existence of that [is established otherwise], the exclusion is established from that alone.

body.text:
2937.
(evam*)(iṣyatām ”iṣ Pass. Imperative 3p s.)(vyavacchedaḥ, m. 1st s.)(aprāmāṇya-)(eva*)(svataḥ* [-tas suff.])(ataḥ*)(nivṛttaye, f. 4th s.)(aprāmāṇya-)(na*)(sādhanam, n. 1st s.)(yuktam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: Thus let it be accepted: the exclusion of invalidity alone [is established] intrinsically; therefore, for the removal of invalidity, no [separate] means of proof is appropriate.

body.text:
2938.
(tu*)(yadi*)(vartteta ”vṛt I C. Opt. Āt.)(āśaṅkā, f. 1st s.)(dvaya-)(apramāṇa-)(tatra*)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(na*)(niścayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(prāmāṇya-)(kṛteḥ, f. 5th s.)(viṣayī- [form with affix cvi])(bhrāntyā, f. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: But if doubt were to persist regarding both [validity and invalidity], there would be no certainty, because [one would be] deceived regarding the validity of an invalid [cognition] through error.

body.text:
2939.
(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kṛtaḥ, m. 1st s.)(viṣayī- [form with affix cvi])(pratyayaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(sandeha-)(viparyāsa-)(hi*)(tatra*)(tadā*)(na*)(niścayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(rūpa-)(tat-)(vat*)(sthāṇu-)
body.translated_text: For one who has been made the object [of doubt] by cognitions of doubt and error — there, then, there is no certainty of that nature, like a post.

2940.
(yathā*)(sthāṇu-)(tejaḥ-)(apramāṇa-)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(vyavasīyate ”so Pass.)(parebhyaḥ, n. 5th pl.)(pratyayaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(bali-bhuj-)(dhūma-)(doṣa-)(uttha-)(kāraṇa-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: Just as a post, fire, invalidity, and the like are ascertained through extrinsic cognitions — [arising from] smoke, defective causes, and the like,

body.text:
2941.
(yat*)(gatam, n. 1st s.)(viṣayatvam, n. 1st s.)(sandeha-)(viparyāsa-)(gamyatām ”gam Pass. Imperative 3p s.)(niścayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(pramāṇatvasya, n. 6th s.)(parataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: Let it be accepted that whatever has become the object of doubt and error — the certainty of its validity is [established] from extrinsic [sources].

body.text:
2942.
(ca*)(bhavatām, m. 6th pl.)(pakṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vākye, n. 7th s.)(yatra*)(nañaḥ, n. 6th s.)(śrutiḥ, f. 1st s.)(tatra*)(eva*)(vyavacchedaḥ, m. 1st s.)(anya-)(anyatra*)(sva-ātmā, m. 1st s.)(eva*)(gamyate ”gam Pass.)
body.translated_text: And your position is: where the negative particle is heard in a sentence, there alone is exclusion; elsewhere, the inherent nature itself is understood.

body.text:
2943.
(ca*)(iha*)(iti*)(buddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(janitā, f. 1st s.)(codanā-)(pramāṇam, n. 1st s.)(nañaḥ, n. 6th s.)(na*)(asti ”as II C.)(prayogaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(na*)(nivarttanam, n. 1st s.)(aprāmāṇya-)
body.translated_text: And here, the cognition generated [by <s>codanā</s>] is: '<s>codanā</s> (Vedic injunction) is a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition)'; there is no employment of the negative particle; therefore there is no removal of invalidity [by it].

body.text:

(kiñca*)(yadi*)(prāmāṇyam, n. 1st s.)(sarva-)(pramāṇānām, n. 6th pl.)(niścitam, n. 1st s.)(svataḥ* [-tas suff.])(eva*)(tadā*)(kasmāt, n. 5th s.)(bhedaḥ, m. 1st s.)(mata-)(pravādinām, m. 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: Moreover, if the validity of all <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid cognition) is ascertained intrinsically alone, then why is there disagreement among proponents of different doctrines?

body.translated_text: Some earlier [thinkers] say: 'It is exclusively intrinsic'; while others hold an irregular [view]: 'Some [validity is] intrinsic and some from other [sources].'

(yasmāt, n. 5th s.)(vivādaḥ, m. 1st s.)(bhrāntitaḥ* [-tas suff.])(ca*)(sā, f. 1st s.)(bādhitā, f. 1st s.)(niścaya-)(tataḥ*)(vādinaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(niścinvantaḥ ”ci V C., m. 1st pl.)(tattvam, n. 2nd s.)(na*)(vivaderan ”vad I C. Opt. Āt. III p. pl.)
body.translated_text: Since the dispute arises from error, and that [error] is sublated by certainty, therefore those who ascertain the truth would not dispute.

body.text:

(viniścaye, m. 7th s.)(svataḥ* [-tas suff.])(prāmāṇyasya, n. 6th s.)(sarva-)(pramāṇānām, n. 6th pl.)(vṛttitaḥ* [-tas suff.])(niścaya-)(na*)(kaścit, m. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(bhāk, m. 1st s.)(visaṃvāda-)
body.translated_text: If the validity of all <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid cognition) is intrinsically ascertained, then no one who has actually experienced [them] would partake of non-deception,

body.text:
2948.
(vṛttaḥ, m. 1st s.)(apramāṇe, n. 7th s.)(buddhyā, f. 3rd s.)(pramaṇatva-)(vañcyate ”vañc Caus. Pass.)(tu*)(bodhāt, m. 5th s.)(svataḥ-prāmāṇya-)(na*)(kaścit, m. 1st s.)(viparītaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: But one who has engaged with what is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> is deceived by the intellect regarding its validity; through the cognition of intrinsic validity, no one is mistaken.

body.text:

(nanu*)(vṛttaḥ, m. 1st s.)(apramāṇataḥ* [-tas suff.])(samaśnute ”aś V Āt.)(visaṃvādam, m. 2nd s.)(niścayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(mataḥ, m. 1st s.)(parataḥ* [-tas suff.])(bādhakāt, m. 5th s.)(pratyayāt, m. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: Objection: One who has engaged with what is not a valid means of cognition experiences non-deception; the certainty of that [invalidity] is held to be from extrinsic [sources], from a sublating cognition.

body.text:
2950.
(tu*)(pravṛttaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pramāṇataḥ* [-tas suff.])(na*)(samaśnute ”aś V Āt.)(visaṃvādam, m. 2nd s.)(ca*)(asmābhiḥ, 3rd pl.)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)(niścayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(eva*)(asya, n. 6th s.)(prāmāṇya-)(sva-taḥ-)
body.translated_text: But one who has engaged with a valid means of cognition does not experience non-deception [i.e., is not disappointed]; and by us, the certainty of its validity is accepted as intrinsic.

body.translated_text: What is intended here in the ascertainment of the validity of all <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid cognition) is not [derived] from non-recognition of the [speaker's] intention.

(yatra*)(eva*)(na*)(niścayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(svataḥ-prāmāṇya-)(pratīyate ”i Pass.)(tasmin, n. 7th s.)(balāt, n. 5th s.)(pāriśeṣya-)(aprāmāṇyam, n. 1st s.)

body.translated_text: Therefore, error is not consistent with validity; hence indeed no one would engage [in action] based on the course of what is non-deceptive.

body.translated_text: 2958. [Objection:] 'But what is the superiority of that [cognition] over the previous one, by which it [the later cognition] is not accepted — like a prior cognition?'

body.translated_text: 2960. And the cognition that has the appearance of purposeful activity — [that appearance] is clearly experienced; and it is determined by the mind that possesses [that] mere reflective awareness.
