body.translated_text: 2961. Therefore, from the correct determination of its intrinsic validity (<s>svataḥ-prāmāṇya</s>) — a subsequent cognition for the attainment of purposeful activity is not required.

body.text:
2962.
(ca*)(tasmin, m. 7th s.)(pramāṇa-bhāve, m. 7th s.)(jñāna-)(api*)(prathame, m. 7th s.)(pratyaye, m. 7th s.)(avabhāsini, m. 7th s.)(kārya-)(asmāt, m. 5th s.)(hetoḥ, m. 5th s.)(prāmāṇya-)(niścayaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2962. And in [the establishment of] that validity as a means of knowledge — even in the first cognition that manifests the effect — from this very reason, the determination of validity [is established].

body.text:
2963.
(hi*)(ādye, n. 7th s.)(viṣaye, n. 7th s. [bv. cpd.])(avastu-)(dvitīyam, n. 1st s.)(lakṣaṇam, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(saṃvāda-)(vastu-)(pravarteta ”vṛt I C. Āt.)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(hetoḥ, m. 6th s.)(asambhavāt, m. 5th s.)
N.B.: read tasya, not yasya, before hetoḥ.
body.translated_text: 2963. For in the first [cognition] whose object is a non-entity — the second [cognition], whose characteristic is concordance with reality — would not arise, because of the impossibility of its cause.

body.text:
2964.
(adhyavasāyinaḥ, m. 6th s.)(pāvaka-)(stabaka-)(aśoka-)(ādau, m. 7th s.)(na*)(jātu*)(jāyate ”jan IV C. Āt.)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(nirbhāsi, n. 1st s.)(dāha-)(pāka-)
body.translated_text: 2964. For one who determinatively cognizes an <s>aśoka</s> (tree) cluster as fire — the cognition that manifests burning and cooking never arises.

body.text:
2965.
(vā*)(jātau, f. 7th s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(prasajyate ”sañj Pass.)(na*)(vijātīyam, n. 1st s.)(jvalanāt, n. 5th s.)(vibhāvasoḥ, m. 6th s.)(lakṣaṇatvāt, n. 5th s.)(mātra-)(yogyatā-)(tat-)(kārya-)
body.translated_text: 2965. Or, when [such a cognition] does arise in [the case of an actual] fire — it is not of a heterogeneous object; because of [fire's] being characterized [as having] the mere suitability for its effect — [fire is understood] from [the nature of] fire.

body.text:
2966.
(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(yāvat*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(ābhāsam, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(artha-)(kriyā*)(na*)(jāyate ”jan IV C. Āt.)(tāvat*)(āśaṅkā, f. 1st s.)(ādye, n. 7th s.)(apramā-)(hetutaḥ* [-tas suff.])(bhrānti-)
body.translated_text: 2966. Therefore, as long as a cognition manifesting purposeful activity (<s>arthakriyā</s>) does not arise — so long, the suspicion [remains] in the first [cognition] that [it may be] invalid, on account of error.

body.text:
2967.
(ca*)(atra*)(kāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(bhrānti-)(adṛṣṭiḥ, f. 1st s.)(phala-)(anantaram*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(upalambhanam, n. 1st s.)(sādṛśyasya, n. 6th s.)(a-paṭutā, f. 1st s.)(mateḥ, f. 6th s.)(iti-ādi, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2967. And the cause of error therein [is]: the non-seeing of the fruit immediately [after the cognition]; the dullness of the intellect regarding the similarity [between cognition and object] — and the like.

body.text:
2968.
(tu*)(jāte, n. 7th s.)(vijñāne, n. 7th s.)(avabhāsin-)(kārya-)(vidyate ”vid Pass.)(na*)(etat, n. 1st s.)(sākṣāt*)(prativedanāt, n. 5th s.)(kriyāyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(nibaddhāyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(vastu-)
body.translated_text: 2968. But when a cognition manifesting the effect has arisen — this [doubt] does not exist; because of the direct experience of the [purposeful] activity that is connected with reality.

body.text:
2969.
(tu*)(ādye, n. 7th s.)(api*)(phale, n. 7th s.)(aprāpte, n. 7th s.)(abhyāsavatyām, f. 7th s.)(vṛttau, f. 7th s.)(vailakṣaṇyam, n. 1st s.)(pratīyate ”i Pass.)(jñānāt, n. 5th s.)(atat-)(viṣayataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 2969. But even in the first [cognition, when] the fruit has not [yet] been attained — in the [cognizer's] practiced operation — a distinctiveness is perceived — from [his] cognition, because of [the cognition] not having a non-corresponding object.

body.text:
2970.
(vailakṣaṇya-)(a-pratītau, f. 7th s.)(tu*)(vijātīya-)(artha-)(śaṅkayā, f. 3rd s.)(kārya-)(avabhāsin-)(vijñānāt, n. 5th s.)(ṛte*)(māna-)(a-viniścayaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2970. But when the distinctiveness is not perceived — because of the suspicion of a heterogeneous object — without a cognition that manifests the effect — there is no determination of [the cognition's status as a] means of valid knowledge.

body.text:
2971.
(tasmin, n. 7th s.)(api*)(mānatvam, n. 1st s.)(sat ”as II C., n. 1st s.)(śakyate ”śak Pass.)(na*)(viniścetum* ”ci)(tat, n. 1st s.)(pratīyate ”i)(kevalam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(uttara-)(jñānāt, n. 5th s.)(ādya-)(kriyā-)
body.translated_text: 2971. Even in that [effect-manifesting cognition], the validity, [though] existing, cannot be determined [by itself]; that [validity] is perceived only from the prior [purposeful-activity] cognition — [which is] first [and] without requiring [further confirmation].

body.text:
2972.
(ca*)(ataḥ*)(prathamam, n. 1st s.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(apekṣate ”īkṣ I C. Āt.)(tat-)(saṃvādam, m. 2nd s.)(eva*)(tathā*)(na*)(mṛgyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(punaḥ*)(saṃvādaḥ, m. 1st s.)(saṃvādena, m. 3rd s.)(api*)
body.translated_text: 2972. And therefore, the first cognition requires precisely its concordance [with reality]; thus, concordance is not to be sought again by [yet another] concordance.

body.text:
2973.
(tasya, n. 6th s.)(pramāṇatā, f. 1st s.)(svataḥ* [-tas suff.])(asat-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(hetoḥ, m. 6th s.)(bhrānti-)(prathamasya, n. 6th s.)(pradeśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(bhāve, m. 7th s.)(tathā-)(sambhavāt, m. 5th s.)(bhrānti-)
N.B.: read tathābhāve rather than tadābhāve.
body.translated_text: 2973. Its validity [is established] intrinsically — because of the non-existence of a cause of error; and there is scope for [error] when such [a cause of error] exists, because of the possibility [of error in those circumstances].

body.text:
2974.
(nanu*)(pramāṇatve, n. 7th s.)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(vijñānasya, n. 6th s.)(aviniścite, n. 7th s.)(katham*)(prekṣā-vān, m. 1st s.)(pravartteta ”vṛt I C. Opt. Āt.)(tatra*)(īpsita-)(agateḥ, f. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 2974. [Objection:] 'But when the validity of that cognition has not been determined — how would a discerning person engage [in action], because of the non-attainment of [what is] desired?'

body.text:
2975.
(ucyate ”vac Pass.)(saṃśayena, m. 3rd s.)(eva*)(asau, m. 1st s.)(vicakṣaṇaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vartate ”vṛt I C. Āt.)(ca*)(kṣatiḥ, f. 1st s.)(vaicakṣaṇya-)(na*)(anuṣajyate ”sañj Pass.)(evam*)
body.translated_text: 2975. [Reply:] It is said — that discerning person engages [in action] even with [mere] doubt; and there is no harm to [his] discernment in this way.

body.text:
2976.
(yataḥ*)(vṛtteḥ, f. 5th s.)(saṃśayena, m. 3rd s.)(viniścaye, m. 7th s.)(tat-)(prāmāṇya-)(upāyatā, f. 1st s.)(niścita-)(ca*)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(sā, f. 1st s.)(api*)(sati ”as II C., m. 7th s.)(saṃśaye, m. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 2976. Since from the [doubtful] operation, [when followed by] the determination of its validity — the means of [attaining the desired end] is determined; and that [means is applicable] even when doubt exists.

body.text:
2977.
(yadi*)(me, 6th s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(prāptiḥ, f. 1st s.)(phala-)(pravṛttau, f. 7th s.)(sandehena, m. 3rd s.)(niścayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(prāmāṇya-)(tatra*)(eva*)(jñātaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2977. 'If I would attain the fruit' — in [his] engagement through doubt — the determination of validity is [thereby] known; [he acts] precisely in that [way],

body.text:
2978.
(na*)(anyathā*)(cāpi*)(iti*)(yuktimān, m. 1st s.)(evam*)(anuyogaḥ, m. 1st s.)(atra*)(iti*)(kasmāt, n. 5th s.)(varttate ”vṛt I C. Āt.)(upāye, m. 7th s.)(hi*)(na*)(anyathā-)(gatiḥ, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2978. And not otherwise — thus [reasons] the one endowed with reasoning; what [objection] is there here? For there is no alternative to the means [of attaining the goal] — [so the question] 'why does he engage?' [is answered].

body.text:
2979.
(hi*)(vinā*)(upāyāt, m. 5th s.)(na*)(kaścit, m. 1st s.)(pratipadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(upeyam, n. 2nd s.)(iti*)(api*)(vṛttaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(jahāti ”hā II C.)(prekṣāvattām, f. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 2979. For without a means, no one attains the goal; even one who has engaged [in action] does not abandon [his] discernment.

body.text:
2980.
(ca*)(nanu*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(ābhāsi, n. 1st s.)(artha-)(kriyā-)(vidyate ”vid Pass.)(svapne, m. 7th s.)(api*)(ca*)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(na*)(pramāṇatvam, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(tat-)(hetoḥ, m. 6th s.)(prathamasya, n. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 2980. [Objection:] 'But surely, the cognition manifesting purposeful activity exists even in dreams; and yet that [dream cognition] is not a valid means of knowledge; and therefore, the first [cognition] too [is not valid] for that reason.'

body.text:
2981.
(na*)(evam*)(hi*)(sarvā, f. 1st s.)(sā, f. 1st s.)(avasthā, f. 1st s.)(bhrāntā, f. 1st s.)(anibandhanā, f. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(bāhya-)(tāsu, f. 7th pl.)(avasthāsu, f. 7th pl.)(na*)(saṃvādaḥ, m. 1st s.)(bāhya-)(vastu-)
body.translated_text: 2981. [Reply:] Not so — for all those states [of dreaming] are erroneous, without an external basis; in those states, there is no concordance with external reality.

body.text:
2982.
(ca*)(saṃvidita-)(sva-)(rūpāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(avilakṣaṇāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(citta-)(caitta-)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(bhedaḥ, m. 1st s.)(dvaya-)(avasthā-)(api*)(spaṣṭam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(pratīyate ”i Pass.)
body.translated_text: 2982. And [the two states of waking and dreaming], having their own forms perceived [and] not being undifferentiated — [the states of] mind (<s>citta</s>) and mental factors (<s>caitta</s>) — by that, the distinction of the two states is clearly perceived.

body.text:
2983.
(matam, n. 1st s.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(viniścaye, m. 7th s.)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(prāmāṇyasya, n. 6th s.)(parataḥ* [-tas suff.])(prasajyate ”sañj Pass.)(prameyatvam, n. 1st s.)(nanu*)(avirodhi, n. 1st s.)(adaḥ, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2983. [Objection:] 'If [it is] your view that the determination of its validity [is] extrinsic (<s>parataḥ</s>) — the status of being a provable [absurdly] follows.' [Reply:] Surely, this [objection] is not contradictory.

body.text:
2984.
(hi*)(prāmāṇyam, n. 1st s.)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(gīyate ”gā Pass.)(apekṣam, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(vastu-)(grāhya-)(tat-)(avagateḥ, f. 5th s.)(parataḥ* [-tas suff.])(tasya, n. 6th s.)(vyavasthitiḥ, f. 1st s.)(prameyatva-)
body.translated_text: 2984. For the validity of that [cognition] is declared [to be] dependent on the graspable object of reality; because of the ascertainment from the other [i.e., the object] — its establishment of the status of being provable [is not a fault].

body.text:
2985.
(ca*)(na*)(virudhyate ”rudh Pass.)(evam*)(vyavasthā, f. 1st s.)(pramāṇatva-)(prameyatva-)(bhedataḥ* [-tas suff.])(apekṣā-)(vat*)(kāraṇatā-)(kārya-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 2985. And this arrangement — [based on] the distinction of validity and provability — is not contradicted; like the [arrangement of] causality and effecthood, which depends on [mutual] requirement.

body.text:
2986.
(evam*)(sthitam, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(pramāṇatva-)(viniścaye, m. 7th s.)(jñānāt, n. 5th s.)(artha-)(kriyā-)(na*)(anavasthā, f. 1st s.)(para-)(ākāṅkṣā-)(nivṛtteḥ, f. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 2986. When it is thus established — in the determination of validity from the cognition of purposeful activity (<s>arthakriyā</s>) — there is no infinite regress, because of the cessation of [further] requirement of another [cognition].

body.text:
2987.
(api*)(vijñāne, n. 5th s.)(samutpanne, n. 5th s.)(na*)(avadhāryate ”dhṛ Caus. Pass.)(yāvat* na*)(śuddhatvam, n. 1st s.)(kāraṇa-)(gatam, n. 1st s.)(antarāt, n. 5th s.)(pramāṇa-)
body.translated_text: 2987. Moreover, even when a cognition has arisen, the purity of the cause is not determined from within — so long as [the cognition] is not [confirmed as] a valid means of knowledge.

body.text:
2988.
(api*)(su-dhiyaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(āhuḥ ”ah Perf. III p. pl.)(atra*)(iti*)(na*)(anavasthā, f. 1st s.)(yena, n. 3rd s.)(sā, f. 1st s.)(śuddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(pratīyate ”i Pass.)(jñānāt, n. 5th s.)(saṃvādinaḥ, n. 5th s.)(anapekṣāt, n. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 2988. Even [those of] keen intellect say this — therefore there is no infinite regress; for that purity is perceived from a concordant cognition — without requiring [anything further].

body.text:
2989.
(hi*)(saṃvāda-)(kārya-)(dṛṣṭitaḥ* [-tas suff.])(viṣaye, m. 7th s.)(sannikṛṣṭe, m. 7th s.)(gamyate ”gam Pass.)(viśuddhatvam, n. 1st s.)(kāraṇānam, n. 6th pl.)(ayatnena, m. 3rd s.)(eva*)
body.translated_text: 2989. For from the observation of concordant effects — in a proximate object — the purity of the causes is understood effortlessly.

body.text:
2990.
(hi*)(viṣaye, m. 7th s.)(viprakṛṣṭe, m. 7th s.)(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(udbhūtā, f. 1st s.)(tat-)(pramā, f. 1st s.)(janyatvāt, n. 5th s.)(tat-)(eva*)(yathā*)(iyam, f. 1st s.)(gocarā, f. 1st s.)(artha-)(sannikṛṣṭa-)
body.translated_text: 2990. For [when] a cognition has arisen regarding a distant object — that [cognition] is valid — because of being produced by that [valid cause] — just as this [cognition that has] a proximate object as its domain.

body.text:
2991.
(yathā*)(śaṅkhe, m. 7th s.)(puraḥ-sthite, m. 7th s.)(avāptyā, f. 3rd s.)(kriyā-)(sādhya-)(sita-)(gamyate ”gam Pass.)(iti*)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(uttham, n. 1st s.)(netra-)(ākrānta-)(kāmala-)
body.translated_text: 2991. Just as, when a conch-shell is present before [one] — its whiteness is understood through the attainment of the intended [action]; the cognition [that it is yellow] does not arise from an eye afflicted by <s>kāmala</s> (jaundice).

body.text:
2992.
(saṃśuddhau, f. 7th s.)(kāraṇa-)(ittham*)(pratītāyām, f. 7th s.)(yā, f. 1st s.)(eva*)(tadā*)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(ākāra-)(pīta-)(śaṅkhe, m. 7th s.)(maye, m. 7th s.)(śātakumbha-)
body.translated_text: 2992. When the purity of the cause is thus perceived — whatever cognition would then arise — [even] in a conch-shell made of gold — with a yellow appearance —

body.text:
2993.
(tu*)(utpādāt, m. 5th s.)(viśuddha-)(kāraṇa-)(niścayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(prāmāṇya-)(asyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(iva*)(mateḥ, f. 6th s.)(ākāra-)(sita-)(kambau, m. 7th s.)(niṣpādita-)(kriye, m. 7th s. [bv. cpd.])
body.translated_text: 2993. But the certainty of validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) of this cognition [arises] from [its] origination from a pure cause — as with a cognition [having] a white [appearance] regarding a conch — in [a case where] the action has been accomplished.

body.text:
2994.
(kāraḥ, m. 1st s.)(bhāṣya-)(api*)(uktavān, m. 1st s.)(idam, n. 2nd s.)(vacanāt, n. 5th s.)(anupaghāta-)(ādi-)(kṣud-)(ādi-)(ataḥ*)(mohāt, m. 5th s.)(anavasthā, f. 1st s.)(codyate ”cud Pass.)(iha*)
body.translated_text: 2994. The author of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> (commentary) too has stated this: because of the statement of non-injury and the like [being a criterion], and because of hunger and the like [being causes of error] — therefore, from delusion, an infinite regress is charged here.

body.text:
2995.
(mānatā, f. 1st s.)(ādyasya, n. 6th s.)(na*)(adhigamyate ”gam Pass.)(śaṅkayā, f. 3rd s.)(janyatva-)(duṣṭa-)(kāraṇa-)(tat*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(śuddhi-)(matam, n. 1st s.)(abhyadhikam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2995. The validity (<s>mānatā</s>) of the first [cognition] is not ascertained — because of the suspicion [that its cause may be] defective; that cognition whose purity of cause is [independently] established is [considered] superior.

body.text:
2996.
(ca*)(evam*)(śuddhi-)(hetu-)(viniścitau, f. 7th s.)(jñānāt, n. 5th s.)(artha-)(kriyā-)(arthe, m. 7th s.)(artha-)(kriye, m. 7th s. [bv. cpd.])(akṛta-)(vṛttiḥ, f. 1st s.)(upapadyate ”pad Pass.)(avācyā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 2996. And thus, when the purity of the cause has been determined, the operation [of cognition] in the object of efficacious action (<s>arthakriyā</s>) — [which is] inexpressible [yet] accomplished — is tenable, [proceeding] from the cognition [of the object].

body.text:
2997.
(yadi*)(svataḥ-pramāṇatvam, n. 1st s.)(sthitam, n. 1st s.)(autsargikam, n. 1st s.)(sarvatra*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(apodyate ”vad Pass.)(bādha-)(jñānābhyām, n. 3rd d.)(kāraṇa)(duṣṭatva-)
body.translated_text: 2997. If <s>svataḥ-prāmāṇyam</s> (intrinsic validity) is established as a general rule everywhere — that is refuted by two [means]: the cognition of a defeater (<s>bādhaka</s>) and [the cognition of] defective causes.

body.text:
2998.
(pramāṇatā, f. 1st s.)(prāptā, f. 1st s.)(a-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(bādha-)(jñāna-)(kāraṇa-)(duṣṭatva-)(ca*)(te, 6th s.)(evam*)(niścayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(prāmāṇya-)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(parasmāt, n. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 2998. Validity is obtained because of the absence of a defeater-cognition and of defective causes; and thus, the certainty of validity for you would be from another [source, i.e., extrinsic].

body.text:
2999.
(hi*)(tathā*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(a-bhāvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tat-)(antaram, n. 1st s.)(pramā-)(ākhyam, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(a-bhāva-)(tvat-)(pakṣe, m. 7th s.)(anumānam, n. 1st s.)(ākhyam, n. 1st s.)(anupalambha-)(mat-)(pakṣe, m. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 2999. For thus, this absence [of a defeater] — which is called a further valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>) — [constitutes] the absence [of a defeater]; in your position, [this is known through] what is called inference (<s>anumāna</s>), [namely] through non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>); in our position [likewise].

body.text:
3000.
(anayā, f. 3rd s.)(eva*)(upapattyā, f. 3rd s.)(aprāmāṇyam, n. 1st s.)(api*)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(svataḥ* [-tas suff.])(yasmāt, n. 5th s.)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(nyāyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(śakyate ”śak Pass.)(vaktum* ”vac)(īdṛśaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3000. By this very reasoning, invalidity (<s>aprāmāṇya</s>) too could be intrinsic (<s>svataḥ</s>); since this reasoning can be stated in such [a symmetrical] manner.

body.text:
3001.
(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(svataḥ-)(apramāṇatvam, n. 1st s.)(sthitam, n. 1st s.)(autsargikam, n. 1st s.)(sarvatra*)(apodyate ”vad Pass.)(a-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(bādha-)(jñāna-)(kāraṇa-)(duṣṭatva-)
body.translated_text: 3001. Therefore, intrinsic invalidity (<s>svataḥ-aprāmāṇyam</s>) is established as a general rule everywhere; [it is] refuted by [the establishment of] the absence of a defeater-cognition and of defective causes.

body.text:
3002.
(tathā*)(apramāṇatā, f. 1st s.)(buddheḥ, f. 6th s.)(prāptā, f. 1st s.)(ātmakatvena, n. 3rd s.)(bodha-)(apodyate ”vad Pass.)(jñāna-)(yathā-)(artha-)(jñānāt, n. 5th s.)(guṇa-)(uttha-)(hetu-)
body.translated_text: 3002. Likewise, the invalidity of cognition is obtained — [being] of the nature of apprehension (<s>bodha</s>); [it is] refuted by the cognition [arising] from the cause of qualities — [namely] from a cognition [that corresponds to] the object as it is.

body.text:
3003.
(aprāmāṇye, n. 7th s.)(āyatte, n. 7th s.)(para-)(eva*)(bhavati ”bhū I C.)(anavasthitiḥ, f. 1st s.)(hi*)(etat, n. 1st s.)(adhīnam, n. 1st s.)(pramāṇa-)(ca*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(svataḥ* [-tas suff.])(apratiṣṭhitam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3003. When invalidity depends on another [source for its removal], there is an infinite regress; for this [validity] too is dependent on a [further] valid cognition — and that [further valid cognition] is itself not intrinsically established.

body.text:
3004.
(tathāhi*)(bhavatā, m. 3rd s.)(ucyate ”vac Pass.)(prāmāṇyam, n. 1st s.)(a-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(bādhaka-)(a-bhāvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(bādha-)(api*)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)(antaram, n. 1st s.)(pramāṇa-)(ākhyam, n. 1st s.)(a-bhāva-)
body.translated_text: 3004. For indeed, by you it is said: validity [is established] from the absence of a defeater; the absence of a defeater is also accepted [as established from] a further [cognition] called the absence of [a defeater] — [which is itself] a valid cognition.

body.text:
3005.
(prāmāṇyam, n. 1st s.)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(api*)(abhidhīyate ”dhā Pass.)(a-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(bādhaka-)(icchāyām, f. 7th s.)(tatra*)(tatra*)(evam*)(upalabhyate ”labh Pass.)(na*)(vyavasthā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3005. The validity of that [further cognition] too is stated [to be established] from the absence of a defeater; [but] when [the absence of a defeater is sought] in each and every [case], no [final] determination is found.

body.text:
3006.
(yataḥ*)(pramāṇatvam, n. 1st s.)(bādhaka-)(pratyaye, m. 7th s.)(anapekṣa-)(na*)(siddham, n. 1st s.)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(na*)(eva*)(apohate ”ūh I C. Āt.)(pūrva-)(jñānam, n. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 3006. Because the validity of a defeater-cognition, [being itself] independent [of further verification], is not established — therefore, this [defeater-cognition] does not in fact refute the previous cognition.

body.text:
3007.
(athāpi*)(prāmāṇyam, n. 1st s.)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)(kvacit*)(vinā*)(a-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(bādhaka-)(tathā-bhāve, m. 7th s.)(kim-nimittakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pradveṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ādye, n. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 3007. But if validity is accepted sometimes without [needing] the absence of a defeater — then what is the basis of the hostility in the first [case, i.e., for ordinary cognitions]?

body.text:
3008.
(ca*)(yadi*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(bādhakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pratyayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(apohate ”ūh I C. Āt.)(pūrva-)(jñānam, n. 2nd s.)(pramāṇatvāt, n. 5th s.)(anapekṣa-)(kim*)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(śaṅkā, f. 1st s.)(atra*)
body.translated_text: 3008. And if this defeater-cognition refutes the previous cognition — [being itself valid] because of [its own] independent validity — what suspicion could there be here?

body.text:
3009.
(ca*)(śaṅkyate ”śaṅk Pass.)(atra*)(bādhakam, n. 1st s.)(anapekṣya-)(pramāṇatvam, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(etat, n. 1st s.)(hi*)(āśaṅkā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(jāyate ”jan IV Cl. Āt.)(niścite, n. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 3009. And [if you say] doubt is raised here without examining the defeater — [but then,] for [a cognition] whose independent validity [is established], this suspicion simply does not arise when [validity] has been determined.

body.text:
3010.
(api*)(pakṣe, m. 7th s.)(svataḥ-prāmāṇya-)(niścayāt, m. 5th s.)(sva-)(rasena, m. 3rd s.)(kasmāt, n. 5th s.)(yatnaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vidhīyate ”dhā Pass.)(siddhau, f. 7th s.)(sat-bhāva-)(bādhaka-)
body.translated_text: 3010. Moreover, in the position of <s>svataḥ-prāmāṇya</s> (intrinsic validity), from the [intrinsic] determination [of validity] — why is effort spontaneously directed toward [establishing] the existence of a defeater?

body.text:
3011.
(yasmin, n. 7th s.)(māna-)(na*)(niścayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(eva*)(sva-rasena, m. 3rd s.)(tatra*)(bādhakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(api*)(niścīyate ”ci Pass.)(ayatnena, m. 3rd s.)(sāmarthyāt, n. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 3011. In [the case] where there is no determination of validity even spontaneously — there, [the existence of] a defeater too is determined effortlessly, by [its own] capacity.

body.text:
3012.
(ataḥ*)(kim*)(ucyate ”vac Pass.)(trayam, n. 1st s.)(jñāna-)(atra*)(parīkṣaka-)(asti ”as Ii C.)(na*)(avakāśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(api*)(ekasya, n. 6th s.)(niścayataḥ* [-tas suff.])(tasmin, n. 7th s.)(svataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 3012. Therefore, what is [the point of] saying [there are] three examining cognitions here? There is no room even for a single one, since [validity is supposed to be] determined intrinsically in that [cognition].

body.text:
3013.
(ca*)(yadi*)(api*)(anupalambhe, m. 7th s.)(utpadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(śaṅkā, f. 1st s.)(saṃśayāt, m. 5th s.)(yasmāt, n. 5th s.)(anupalambhanam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(avinā-bhūtam, n. 1st s.)(bādhā-)(a-bhāva-)
body.translated_text: 3013. And even if suspicion arises upon non-apprehension [of a defeater] — because of doubt — since non-apprehension is not invariably concomitant with the absence of a defeater —

body.text:
3014.
(sati ”as II C., n. 7th s.)(kasmāt, n. 5th s.)(tvayā, 3rd s.)(kṛtaḥ, m. 1st s.)(paritoṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(traye, n. 7th s.)(hi*)(api*)(adṛṣṭau, f. 7th s.)(vat*)(pūrva-)(bādhā, f. 1st s.)(śaṅkyeta ”śaṅk Pass.)(atra*)
body.translated_text: 3014. [Then] why have you been satisfied with [just] three [examining cognitions]? For even in [the case of] three [cognitions], a defeater may be suspected here — as when a prior [defeater was] unseen.

body.text:
3015.
(yataḥ*)(yāvat*)(na*)(saṃvādaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kārya-)(tāvat*)(śaṅkā, f. 1st s.)(bādhā-)(na*)(vinivarttate ”vṛt I C. Āt.)(niyamaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tasmin, n. 7th s.)(tritaye, n. 7th s.)(a-phalaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3015. For as long as there is no agreement with the effect — so long the suspicion of a defeater does not cease; the restriction to those three [cognitions] is without result.

body.text:
3016.
(ca*)(tataḥ*)(bādhakam, n. 1st s.)(punaḥ*)(āśaṅkyam, n. 1st s.)(chalena, n. 3rd s.)(na*)(jātu*)(avatiṣṭhate ”sthā I C. Āt.)(tattvam, n. 1st s.)(vastunaḥ, n. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 3016. And thereafter, a defeater is again to be suspected; the truth of an entity never comes to rest through [mere] pretext.

body.text:
3017.
(samutpannam, n. 1st s.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(śaṅkhe, m. 7th s.)(nibham, n. 1st s.)(pīta-)(varjitam, n. 1st s.)(bādha-)(pratyaya-)(ā*)(jīvitāt, n. 5th s.)(na*)(hi*)(jāyate ”jan IV C. Āt)(pramāṇam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3017. A cognition that arises regarding a conch as having the appearance of yellow — [when] devoid of a defeater-cognition — does not become a valid means of knowledge for [the entire duration of one's] life.

body.text:
3018.
(bādhakam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(upajāyeta ”jan IV C. Opt. Āt.)(kāraṇa-)(viśuddhi-)(a-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(vā*)(anyena, ns. 3rd s.)(nimittena, n. 3rd s.)(ataḥ*)(śaṅkā, f. 1st s.)(na*)(nivarttate ”vṛt I C. Āt.)
body.translated_text: 3018. [Because] a defeater may not arise — either because of the absence of the purity of [its] causes, or because of some other reason — therefore, the suspicion does not cease.

body.text:
3019.
(tena, n. 3rd s.)(yatra*)(iyam, f. 1st s.)(āśaṅkā, f. 1st s.)(mohataḥ* [-tas suff.])(eva*)(sa-nimittā, f. 1st s.)(tu*)(dṛṣṭau, f. 7th s.)(śuddhi-)(saṃvāda-)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(na*)(āśaṅkā, f. 1st s.)(su-dhiyaḥ, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 3019. Therefore, wherever this suspicion [arises] — [it is] motivated merely by delusion; but when the purity [of the cause] and agreement [with the effect] have been observed, the suspicion would not [arise] for the wise.

body.text:
3020.
(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(jāyate ”jan IV C. Āt.)(ātmā, m. 1st s.)(saṃśaya-)(sarva-)(vyavahāreṣu, m. 7th pl.)(hi*)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(dhīḥ, f. 1st s.)(niḥ-saṃśayā, f. 1st s.)(darśane, n. 7th s.)(śuddhi-)(saṃvāda-)
body.translated_text: 3020. For the [wise person] — the nature of doubt does not arise in all [his] dealings; for his cognition is free from doubt, upon observing the purity [of the cause] and agreement [with the effect].

body.text:
3021.
(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(api*)(atra*)(kaścit, m. 1st s.)(jaḍaḥ, m. 1st s.)(prakurute ”kṛ VIII C. Āt.)(śaṅkām, f. 2nd s.)(manye ”man IV C. Āt. 1p. s.)(prati*)(tam, m. 2nd s.)(saṃśaya-)(ātmakatā, f. 1st s.)(ninditā, f. 1st s.)(ajena, m. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 3021. And whoever, being dull, raises a suspicion here — against him, I think, the [charge of having] the nature of doubt — condemned by [the sage] <s>Aja</s> — [applies].

body.text:
3022.
(niścaye, m. 7th s.)(prāmāṇya-)(prakalpite, m. 7th s.)(apekṣā-)(bheda-)(deśa-)(kāla-)(nara-)(avasthā-)(vyaktam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(niścitiḥ, f. 1st s.)(prāmāṇya-)(anyasmāt, n. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 3022. When the certainty of validity has been postulated [to depend on] the distinction of person, place, time, and condition — clearly the determination of validity [comes] from another [source].

body.text:
3023.
(deśa-)(kāla-)(ādau, m. 7th s.)(su-)(niścitau, f. 7th s.)(a-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(bādhā-)(niścayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(prāmāṇya-)(prāñce, n. 7th s.)(jñāne, n. 7th s.)(antarataḥ* [-tas suff.])(pramāṇa-)
body.translated_text: 3023. When [place, time, and the like] have been well determined, the certainty of validity [arises] from the absence of a defeater; in [the case of] a prior cognition, [the certainty arises] from within, [through] a [further] valid cognition.

body.text:
3024.
(tu*)(vyavahāraḥ, m. 1st s.)(ṛṇa-)(ādi-)(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(yogya-vān, m. 1st s.)(traya-)(vākya-)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(ātmā, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(tādṛśa-)(sthala-)(eva*)(na*)(udāhāryaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sthitau, f. 7th s.)(pramā-)
body.translated_text: 3024. But the conventional practice regarding debts and the like — that which possesses the [relevant] three sentences — [which is] of such a nature and pertains to such a context — [that] is not to be cited as an example when the [intrinsic] establishment of valid cognition [is at stake].

body.text:
3025.
(tatra*)(vastuni, n. 7th s.)(arthi-)(pratyarthinau, m. 1st d.)(smṛtvā* ”smṛ)(smṛtvā* ”smṛ)(parisphuṭam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(labhete ”labh I C. 3p. d.)(kartum* ”kṛ)(sūkṣma-)(īkṣikām, f. 2nd s.)(tatra*)(vastuni, n. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 3025. Therein, both the plaintiff and the defendant, having recalled [the matter] clearly regarding the object in question, are able to make a subtle examination regarding that object.

body.text:
3026.
(tu*)(pramāṇam, n. 1st s.)(vyavasthāpyam, n. 1st s.)(sthityā, f. 3rd s.)(vastu-)(tu*)(na*)(chalāt, n. 5th s.)(ataḥ*)(vyavahāraḥ, m. 1st s.)(udāhṛtaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pratirūpaḥ, m. 1st s.)(prākṛta-)
body.translated_text: 3026. But the valid means of knowledge is to be established by the stability of the real entity — not by pretext; therefore, the ordinary conventional practice has been cited as an appropriate [analogy].

body.text:
3027.
(api*)(devānām, m. 6th pl.)(tri-satya-tā, f. 1st s.)(eva*)(kāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(niściti-)(niściti-)(asat-bhāve, m. 7th s.)(ādyāt, n. 5th s.)(asau, f. 1st s.)(parataḥ* [-tas suff.])(api*)
body.translated_text: 3027. Even of the gods, the thrice-truthful nature is indeed the cause of the determination [of validity]; in the absence of the determination [from] the first [cognition], that [further determination] is [needed] from another [source] as well.

body.text:
3028.
(yena, n. 3rd s.)(idam, n. 1st s.)(uttaram, n. 1st s.)(dvayam, n. 1st s.)(vacana-)(tadīyam, n. 1st s.)(a-bhāve, m. 7th s.)(pratyaya-)(ādye, n. 7th s.)(tat-)(kaḥ, m. 1st s.)(viśeṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(anyayoḥ, n. 6th d.)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 3028. Since these two subsequent [determinations] — [which are] the words of that [deity] — [depend on] the absence of the first cognition — what distinction is there between the other two [and the first]?

body.text:
3029.
(ataḥ*)(yuktyā, f. 3rd s.)(uktayā, f. 3rd s.)(pūrva-)(anavasthitiḥ, f. 1st s.)(tvat-)(pakṣe, m. 7th s.)(api*)(ataḥ*)(pramāṇatva-)(pramāṇatve, n. 1st d.)(sthite, n. 1st d.)(yathā-yogam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])
body.translated_text: 3029. Therefore, by the reasoning previously stated, there is an infinite regress in your position too; therefore, when validity and the means of valid cognition have been established — as appropriate —

body.text:
3030.
(nityam, n. 1st s.)(vākyam, n. 1st s.)(nirākṛtam, n. 1st s.)(asmābhiḥ, 3rd pl.)(purā*)(vistareṇa, m. 3rd s.)(ca*)(bhavatām, m. 6th pl.)(mate, n. 7th s.)(asti ”as II C.)(na*)(āptaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kṣīṇa-)(aśeṣa-)(doṣaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])
body.translated_text: 3030. The eternal sentence has been refuted by us previously in detail; and in your [Mīmāṃsā] view, there is no trustworthy person (<s>āpta</s>) who has exhausted all faults.

body.text:
3031.
(tu*)(kīdṛk, m. 1st s.)(bhaviṣyati ”bhū Fut.)(āptaḥ, m. 1st s.)(rāśiḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(āvṛti-)(akṣīṇa-)(yataḥ*)(doṣāt, m. 5th s.)(sambhāvyate ”bhū Caus. Pass.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(vacaḥ, n. 1st s.)(api*)(anyathā*)
body.translated_text: 3031. But what kind of trustworthy person (<s>āpta</s>) will there be — one whose mass of defects is inexhaustible? Because [even] his speech is suspected of being otherwise, due to [the possibility of] faults.

body.text:
3032.
(api*)(āpte, m. 7th s.)(jāte, m. 7th s.)(kena, m. 3rd s.)(śakyate ”śak Pass.)(jñātum* ”jñā)(asau, m. 1st s.)(oghaḥ, m. 1st s.)(guṇa-)(yataḥ*)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(avadhāraṇam, n. 1st s.)(vākye, n. 7th s.)(praṇīte, n. 7th s.)(āpta-)
body.translated_text: 3032. Even when a trustworthy person has arisen, by whom can he be known? [Only by one who possesses] a flood of [discerning] qualities — whence the ascertainment would be [possible] regarding a statement composed by a trustworthy person.

body.text:
3033.
(api*)(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(atīndriya-)(dṛk, m. 1st s.)(paśyet ”dṛś IV C. Opt.)(tadīya-)(sampadam, f. 2nd s.)(guṇa-)(kim, n. 1st s.)(prayojanam, n. 1st s.)(api*)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(vacasā, n. 3rd s.)(praṇītena, n. 3rd s.)(āpta-)
body.translated_text: 3033. Even one who has supersensory vision, and could see that person's wealth of qualities — what purpose [would be served] for him by the statement composed by the trustworthy person?

body.text:
3034.
(hi*)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(svayam*)(prapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(artham, m. 2nd s.)(nirāśaṃsaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vākya-)(api*)(anyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(aparijñānāt, n. 5th s.)(āpta-)(na*)(avagacchati ”gam I C.)(artham, m. 2nd s.)(tataḥ*)
body.translated_text: 3034. For he himself would directly attain the object, being free from expectation [of another's words]; and another, because of not fully knowing [the trustworthy person's qualities], does not understand the object from that [person's statement].

body.text:
3035.
(ca*)(vāde, m. 7th s.)(sva-taḥ-)(prāmāṇya-)(niścaya-)(jātitaḥ* [-tas suff.])(svataḥ* [-tas suff.])(ayogāt, m. 5th s.)(sambhava-)(vināśa-)(kimartham*, m. 2nd s. [adv.])(vinivāraṇam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3035. And in the doctrine of <s>svataḥ-prāmāṇya</s> (intrinsic validity) — because of the impossibility of ascertaining [validity] intrinsically [in all cases], due to [the possibility of] origination and destruction — why [is there any need for] the prevention [of doubt]?

body.text:
3036.
(vākyam, n. 1st s.)(nāma*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(na*)(dūṣyate ”duṣ Pass.)(doṣaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(nirākṛtaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(guṇa-)(tu*)(aniścayataḥ* [-tas suff.])(guṇa-)(tat, n. 1st s.)(śakyate ”śak Pass.)(na*)(viniścetum* ”ci)
body.translated_text: 3036. A statement, indeed, is not vitiated by faults that have been negated [in the speaker]; but because of the non-ascertainment of [the speaker's] qualities, that [statement's validity] cannot be definitively determined.

body.text:
3037.
(ca*)(vākyasya, n. 6th s.)(akartṛkatvam, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(prāk*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(vinivāritam, n. 1st s.)(ataḥ*)(na*)(a-bhāvena, m. 3rd s.)(kartuḥ, m. 6th s.)(syuḥ ”as II C. III p. pl.)(na*)(doṣāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(nirāśrayāḥ, m. 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 3037. And the authorlessness of the statement (<s>vākya</s>) has already been refuted previously; therefore, faults — [which would be] without a substrate in the absence of an author — would not exist.

body.text:
3038.
(ca*)(yathā*)(pramāṇatvam, n. 1st s.)(yuktam, n. 1st s.)(guṇebhyaḥ, m. 5th pl.)(tathā*)(uditam, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(guṇānām, m. 6th s.)(aparijñāne, n. 7th s.)(a-bhāvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(doṣāṇām, m. 6th pl.)(na*)(lakṣyate ”lakṣ Pass.)
body.translated_text: 3038. And just as validity (<s>pramāṇatva</s>) is justified [as arising] from [the speaker's] qualities — so has been stated; and when the qualities are not fully known, the absence of faults is not observed.

body.text:
3039.
(tat*)(na*)(yuktam, n. 1st s.)(vākyam, n. 1st s.)(pramāṇam, n. 1st s.)(svataḥ* [-tas suff.])(upalakṣitam, n. 1st s.)(a-bhāva-)(doṣa-)(hi*)(aparijñānāt, n. 5th s.)(a-bhāvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(doṣa-)(alakṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3039. Therefore, [it is] not justified [that] the statement is a valid means of knowledge intrinsically ascertained — [merely] from the absence of faults; for because of the non-cognition of the absence of faults, [that] is a non-characteristic of the absence of faults.

body.text:
3040.
(hi*)(puṃsām, m. 6th pl.)(aparijñāne, n. 7th s.)(daṇḍa-)(na*)(lakṣyate ”lakṣ Pass.)(iti*)(daṇḍī, m. 1st s.)(etat, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(mānam, n. 1st s.)(lakṣitam, n. 1st s.)(tat-)(absence of defects)(svataḥ* [-tas suff.])(parāhatam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3040. For when a stick is not cognized by people, [the stick] is not observed — [yet] the one who has a stick [still exists]; this [claim that] the intrinsic validity is ascertained [by the absence of observed faults] — that is refuted by its own [logic].

body.text:
3041.
(a-bhāvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(doṣa-)(yuktam, n. 1st s.)(lakṣaṇam, n. 1st s.)(vākyasya, n. 6th s.)(niścita-ātmakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pramāṇāt, n. 5th s.)(pramā-abhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(ataḥ*)(sthitiḥ, f. 1st s.)(pramā-)(parataḥ* [-tas suff.])
body.translated_text: 3041. The absence of faults is the justified characteristic of the statement — [only when it has been] ascertained by a valid means of cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>); because of the absence of valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>), therefore the status of valid cognition [is established] from an external source (<s>parataḥ</s>).

body.text:
3042.
(teṣu, m. 7th pl.)(satsu, m. 7th pl.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(viṣayam, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(doṣa-)(nṛ-)(upajāyate ”jan IV C. Āt.)(tu*)(ajñāne, n. 7th s.)(guṇa-)(katham*)(nāma*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(a-bhāve, m. 7th s.)(doṣa-)
body.translated_text: 3042. When those [faults] exist, a cognition having [those faults as its] object arises in people; but in the ignorance of qualities — how indeed could there be cognition in the absence of faults?

body.text:
3043.
(doṣāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(dveṣa-)(moha-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(bādhitāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(kṛpā-)(prajñā-)(ādi-)(hi*)(aniścaye, m. 7th s.)(dayā-)(ādi-)(katham*)(gatam, n. 1st s.)(asattvam, n. 1st s.)(teṣām, m. 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 3043. Faults [are] hatred, delusion, and the like — [which are] obstructed [by] compassion, wisdom, and the like; but when [it is] uncertain [whether] compassion and the like [are present] — how has the non-existence of those [faults] been ascertained?

body.text:
3044.
(tu*)(tadā*)(guṇāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(na*)(vyāpriyante ”pṛ Pass.)(jñāyamānatayā, f. 3rd s.)(mātra-)(sattā-)(upakāriṇaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(vijñeye, m. 7th s.)(a-bhāve, m. 7th s.)(doṣa-)
body.translated_text: 3044. But then [one might say:] the qualities are not active [in producing knowledge] — [they are] merely helpful by their [mere] existence as known; [yet] in the absence of faults regarding the object to be known,

body.text:
3045.
(yadi*)(evam*)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(na*)(saṃśayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tathā*)(viparyastā, f. 1st s.)(matiḥ, f. 1st s.)(sammate, m. 7th s.)(āpta-)(iti*)(santi ”as II C. 3p. pl.)(doṣāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(asya, m. 6th s.)(vā*)(no*)(iti*)(santi ”as II C. III p. pl.)(eva*)
body.translated_text: 3045. If this were so, there would be no doubt; [but] the cognition is reversed [in the case of] one accepted as trustworthy (<s>āpta</s>) — [for one wonders:] 'do faults exist in him, or not?' — [the faults] indeed exist.

body.text:
3046.
(ca*)(bhavataḥ ”bhū I C. 3p. d.)(tat-)(sandeha-)(viparyāsau, m. 1st d.)(atra*)(kasyacit, m. 6th s.)(yāvat*)(na*)(avagamyate ”gam Pass.)(iti*)(asau, m. 1st s.)(ādhāraḥ, m. 1st s.)(gaṇa-)(guṇa-)
body.translated_text: 3046. And doubt and error regarding that [speaker] arise in someone — as long as the group of qualities is not understood — that is the basis [of the problem].

body.text:
3047.
(atha*)(niścayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sva-taḥ-)(prāmāṇya-)(api*)(ajñāne, n. 7th s.)(a-bhāve, m. 7th s.)(doṣa-)(api*)(tathā*)(tatra*)(vaktari, m. 7th s.)(na*)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(vimatiḥ, f. 1st s.)(vat*)(pūrva-)
body.translated_text: 3047. Now, [if you say] the ascertainment of <s>svataḥ-prāmāṇya</s> (intrinsic validity) [obtains] even in ignorance [and] in the absence of faults — even so, there would be no doubt regarding the speaker there — as before.

body.text:
3048.
(ca*)(ajñānāt, n. 5th s.)(a-bhāvasya, m. 6th s.)(doṣa-)(katham*)(pratīyate ”i Pass.)(nāstitā, f. 1st s.)(dvaya-)(pramā-)(yena, n. 3rd s.)(niścayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(prāmāṇya-)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)
body.translated_text: 3048. And from the ignorance of the absence of faults — how is the non-existence [of faults] ascertained? By which the ascertainment of both [absence of faults and absence of error] — the ascertainment of validity — would [be established].

body.text:
3049.
(atha*)(api*)(apratītau, f. 7th s.)(asattā-)(dvaya-)(apramā-)(eva*)(svataḥ* [-tas suff.])(prāmāṇyam, n. 1st s.)(gamyate ”gam Pass.)(evam*)(vat*)(pūrva-)(na*)(vimatiḥ, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3049. Now, even when [the two —] the non-existence [of faults] and the non-erroneousness — are not cognized, [if you say] <s>svataḥ-prāmāṇya</s> (intrinsic validity) is understood — then, as before, there would be no doubt.

body.text:
3050.
(kim* - interrogative)(asya, m. 6th s.)(vacanam, n. 1st s.)(mānam, n. 1st s.)(kim* - interrogative)(vā*)(amānam, n. 1st s.)(atha*)(api*)(adaḥ, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(amānam, n. 1st s.)(niścayāt, m. 5th s.)(sarveṣām, n. 6th pl.)(prāmāṇya-)(sva-taḥ-)
body.translated_text: 3050. Is this person's statement a valid means of knowledge, or is it not? Now, if that [statement] alone is not a valid means — [then] because of the intrinsic validity of all [cognitions], [that determination is impossible].

body.text:
3051.
(ataḥ*)(avaśya-)(abhyupagantavyā, f. 1st s.)(niyamāt, m. 5th s.)(pratītiḥ, f. 1st s.)(triṣu, m. 7th pl.)(a-bhāva-)(doṣa-)(a-bhāva-)(apramā-)(bhāveṣu, m. 7th pl.)(guṇa-)
body.translated_text: 3051. Therefore, the cognition [of validity] must necessarily be accepted — [as arising] from the restriction [of validity to cases where there is] the presence of qualities, the absence of faults, and the absence of error in the three [respects].

body.text:
3052.
(eṣām, m. 6th pl.)(evam*)(vikalpyate ”kḷp Pass.)(iti*)(sā, f. 1st s.)(pramāṇam, n. 1st s.)(vā*)(apramāṇam, n. 1st s.)(katham*)(apramāṇam, n. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(aṅgam, n. 1st s.)(yathā-artha-)(niścayāya, m. 4th s.)
body.translated_text: 3052. [The validity] of these is thus deliberated: is that [cognition of validity] a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) or not? How could it be not a valid means? [It is] an ancillary [factor] for the ascertainment of [correspondence with] the real object.

body.text:
3053.
(tat-)(viniścayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(prāmāṇya-)(prāmāṇye, n. 7th s.)(prāpteḥ, f. 5th s.)(parataḥ* [-tas suff.])(katham*)(vā*)(gamyate ”gam Pass.)(tasyāḥ, f. 6th s.)(pratīteḥ, f. 6th s.)(sā, f. 1st s.)(pramā-ātmatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3053. When the validity [of that ancillary cognition] is attained from an external source (<s>parataḥ</s>) — the ascertainment of [its] validity — or how else is the status of being valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>) of that cognition understood?

body.text:
3054.
(cet*)(iti*)(a-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(pratyaya-)(bādhaka-)(kim* - interrogative)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(api*)(pramā, f. 1st s.)(vā*)(na*)(iti*)(api*)(sarvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(doṣaḥ, m. 1st s.)(anuvartate ”vṛt I C. Āt.)(atra*)(punaḥ*)
body.translated_text: 3054. If [you say] because of the absence of a sublating cognition (<s>bādhaka-pratyaya</s>) — [we ask:] is that [absence] too a valid cognition or not? All the faults recur here again.

body.text:
3055.
(pramāṇatā, f. 1st s.)(prastutasya, n. 6th s.)(prāptā, f. 1st s.)(prāmāṇye, n. 7th s.)(parataḥ* [-tas suff.])(vā*)(kutaḥ*)(apramāṇasya, n. 6th s.)(hetutvam, n. 1st s.)(yathā-artha-)(jñāna-)
body.translated_text: 3055. The validity of what is under discussion — [if it is] attained from an external source — or whence [does it come]? [For] what is not a valid means of knowledge — how [can it have] the status of being a cause of cognition of the real object?

body.text:
3056.
(cintyate ”cint Pass.)(iti*)(kena, n. 3rd s.)(prāmāṇyam, n. 1st s.)(asya, n. 6th s.)(api*)(gamyate ”gam Pass.)(asattvāt, n. 5th s.)(pratyaya-)(bādhaka-)(iti*)(prasajyate ”sañj Pass.)(aniṣṭā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3056. [If one says] 'by that [very cognition] the validity of this [statement] is also understood' — [we reply:] because of the non-existence of a sublating cognition — thus an undesired [consequence] follows.

body.text:
3057.
(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(guṇebhyaḥ, m. 5th pl.)(a-bhāvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(doṣāṇām, m. 6th pl.)(tat-)(a-bhāvataḥ* [-tas suff.])(asattvam, n. 1st s.)(dvaya-)(apramāṇa-)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(utsargaḥ, m. 1st s.)(anapoditaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3057. Therefore, the absence of faults [is established] from [the presence of] qualities; [and] from the absence of those [faults], the non-existence of the two [—non-validity and error]; by that, the general rule [of validity] is unrefuted.

body.text:
3058.
(cet*)(pramāṇatvam, n. 1st s.)(sarvatra*)(niścitam, n. 1st s.)(evam*)(iha*)(api*)(asau, m. 1st s.)(pūrva-uditaḥ, m. 1st s.)(gaṇaḥ, m. 1st s.)(doṣa-)(ca*)(prasaktā, f. 1st s.)(anavasthitiḥ, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3058. If validity is ascertained everywhere in this manner — even here, the previously stated group of faults [applies]; and an infinite regress (<s>anavasthiti</s>) is entailed.

body.text:
3059.
(idam, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(sattvam, n. 1st s.)(pramā-)(a-bhāve, m. 7th s.)(doṣa-)(niṣedhanam, n. 1st s.)(yadi*)(kalpyeta ”kḷp Pass. Opt.)(kevalam, n. 1st s.)(tat-)(sambhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(na*)(eva*)(siddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3059. If, in the absence of faults, the negation [of faults] is postulated as [having] the nature of valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>) alone — [then] there would indeed be no establishment [of validity].

body.text:
3060.
(tat-)(avakalpyate ”kḷp Pass.)(na*)(siddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(upalambhena, m. 3rd s.)(a-bhāvāt, m. 5th s.)(ca*)(na*)(yuktā, f. 1st s.)(anupalambhataḥ* [-tas suff.])(doṣāt, m. 5th s.)(anavasthiti-)
body.translated_text: 3060. That [negation of faults] is not established by apprehension, and from [its] absence [it is] also not justified; from [the fault of] non-apprehension of faults — an infinite regress [follows].

body.text:
3061.
(asattā, f. 1st s.)(doṣa-)(dvaya-)(apramā-)(gamyate ”gam Pass.)(anupalambhataḥ* [-tas suff.])(nāstitvam, n. 1st s.)(upalambhasya, m. 6th s.)(anyena, m. 3rd s.)(iti*)(anavasthitiḥ, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3061. The non-existence of faults and the non-erroneousness of the two are understood from non-apprehension; the non-existence of the apprehension [is established] by another [cognition] — thus [there is] an infinite regress.

body.translated_text: 3062. If [you say non-apprehension is] of the nature of [a cognition that is] an exclusion of other [possibilities] — [then] because of seeing [the presence of faults] as distinct [from their absence], the non-cognition of the absence of faults would have the nature of [cognizing] the [presence of] qualities.

body.text:

body.translated_text: 3063. And [the cognition's] own form — intended as valid cognition — [would absurdly] follow; and the cognition [that establishes] the non-existence of the two [faults] and the non-erroneousness — [being] exclusive of those [faults] —

body.text:
3064.
(athavā*)(asattve, n. 7th s.)(dvitaya-)(apramā-)(jñāte, n. 7th s.)(svātantryataḥ* [-tas suff.])(kutaḥ*)(bhavataḥ, m. 6th s.)(niścayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(iti*)(pariśiṣṭaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pramā-ātmā, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])
body.translated_text: 3064. Or rather, when the non-existence of the two [faults] and the non-erroneousness have been known [first] — whence, independently, does your ascertainment [arise] — [namely,] that the remainder has the nature of valid cognition (<s>pramā</s>)?

body.translated_text: 3065. If [you say] the ascertainment would arise from the impossibility of being otherwise — [that is,] from presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>) — or even from inference (<s>anumāna</s>) — [then] even so, it would be from an external source (<s>anyataḥ</s>).

body.translated_text: 3066. Therefore, by this very reasoning, the invalidity too is entailed as [established] intrinsically (<s>svataḥ</s>) for you; since that [invalidity] can clearly be stated there [in the same way].

body.translated_text: 3179. The statements of the son of <s>Śuddhodana</s> do not have validity because of [their] dependence [on an authority]; even so, [the son of] <s>Śuddhodana</s>, who himself sees the <s>Dharma</s> —

body.translated_text: 3180. The beginninglessness of such <s>pudgalas</s> (persons), even when imagined — because of the fixity of the position — does not surpass the invalidity of the statements; therefore [this argument fails].

body.translated_text: 3181. Therefore, by those [Mīmāṃsakas] who are examining [this], it is stated — [just as] the beginninglessness of the students of the <s>Veda</s> [is postulated], likewise [the beginninglessness] in general of the <s>Buddhas</s> [is postulated].

body.translated_text: 3182. Because of the particularity of that [Buddhist] knowledge, it does not reach equality with theirs [the Mīmāṃsakas']; validity and invalidity — these two would thus be beginningless.

body.translated_text: 3183. For those virtues of valid means of knowledge, and those faults — and their semblances — are beginningless; not all of them reach equality merely by [their shared] beginninglessness.

body.translated_text: 3184. Just as genuine gold, which is the instrument of transactions, [is] without beginning and end — [but the question] 'is illusory gold also [without beginning]?' — what [does it matter]? [The two are not equal] for that reason.

body.translated_text: 3185. And those who declare the omniscience [of the Buddha] and the permanence of the <s>Veda</s> to them — these two [claims] are equivalent.

body.translated_text: 3186. Indeed, no omniscient being is seen [by us] at present; nor is there any mark — partial or [otherwise] — that would lead [one] to infer [an omniscient being].
