body.text:
3188.
(atha*)(sarva-jñaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pratīyate ”i Pass.)(anyaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(eva*)(tat-)(vacanena, n. 3rd s.)(katham*)(prakalpyate ”kḷp Caus. Pass.)(siddhiḥ, f. 1st s.)(anyonya-)(āśrayayoḥ, m. 6th du. -bv. cpd.)(tayoḥ, m. 6th d.)
body.translated_text: 3188. Now, if the omniscient being is known through the very statements of others — how is the establishment [achieved] when those two [the omniscient being and the statements] are mutually dependent?

body.text:
3189.
(vākyam, n. 1st s.)(satyam, n. 1st s.)(uktatayā, f. 3rd s.)(sarva-jña-)(tat-)(astitā, f. 1st s.)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(katham*)(ubhayam, n. 1st s.)(tat-)(siddhyet ”sidh IV C. Opt.)(ṛte*)(antarāt, n. 5th s.)(siddhāt, n. 5th s.)(mūla-)
body.translated_text: 3189. The statement [is declared] true because [it was] spoken by an omniscient being — [and] the existence of that [omniscient being is established] by that [statement]; how could both be established without a root [that is] established from within?

body.text:
3190.
(tu*)(avagacchantaḥ ”gam I C., m. 1st pl.)(sarva-jñam, m. 2nd s.)(vacanāt, n. 5th s.)(praṇītāt, n. 5th s.)(a-sarvajña-)(kim*)(na*)(jānate ”jñā IX C. 3p. pl. Āt.)(sva-)(vākyāt, n. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 3190. But [we who] understand the omniscient being from [his] well-composed statements — do not those who are not omniscient know [anything] from their own statements?

body.text:
3191.
(ca*)(siddhaye, f. 4th s.)(eka-)(sarva-jña-)(kalpyāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(bahavaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(sarva-jñāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(api*)(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(eva*)(ekaḥ, m. 1st s.)(asarvajñaḥ, m. 1st s.)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(budhyate ”budh IV C. Āt.)(sarva-jñam, m. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 3191. And for the establishment of a single omniscient being — many omniscient beings must be postulated; [but] even a single non-omniscient person does not know the omniscient being.

body.text:
3192.
(evam*)(hi*)(api*)(boddhṛbhiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(kālaiḥ, m. 3rd pl. [bv. cpd.])(tat-)(śakyate ”śak Pass.)(na*)(jñātum* ”jñā)(iti*)(ayam, m. 1st s.)(sarva-jñaḥ)(śūnyaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(vi-jñāna-)(jñeya-)(jñāna-)(tat-)
body.translated_text: 3192. For even by cognizers [existing at] those times — this omniscient being, devoid of [any criterion for determining] the knowable, [its] knowledge, and that [knowledge's validity] — cannot be known.

body.text:
3193.
(ca*)(sarva-jñaḥ, m. 1st s.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(na*)(avabuddhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(eva*)(yena, m. 3rd s.)(prati*)(tam, m. 2nd s.)(vākyānām, n. 6th pl.)(tat-)(na*)(pramāṇatvam, n. 1st s.)(mūla-)(ajñāne, n. 7th s.)(vat*)(vākya-)(anya-)
body.translated_text: 3193. And [if] the omniscient being were not [actually] known — by the one with respect to whom [the statements are supposed to be valid] — then the statements would have no validity for that [person]; like the statements of another, when the root is unknown.

body.text:
3194.
(api*)(saṃvādayan ”vad Caus., m. 1st s.)(arthān, m. 2nd pl.)(jñātān, m. 2nd pl.)(sarva-)(śiṣyaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(na*)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(sarva-jñaḥ, m. 1st s.)(varjanāt, n. 5th s.)(artha-)(jñāta-)(loka-)(anya-)
body.translated_text: 3194. Moreover, even one who demonstrates concordance [between his words and] all objects that are known by [his] disciples — would not be omniscient; because of the exclusion of objects that are unknown to the world and otherwise [inaccessible].

body.text:
3195.
(na*)(ca*)(sarva-)(nara-)(jñāta-)(jñeya-)(saṃvāda-)(sambhavaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kāla-)(traya-)(tri-)(loka-)(sthaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(naraiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(na*)(ca*)(samāgamaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3195. And it is not possible that all things known to all people [could be concordant with the teacher's statements]; for there is no meeting with people [situated] in the three times and the three worlds.

body.text:
3196.
(hi*)(jñaḥ, m. 1st s.)(api*)(kiñcit-)(śaknoti ”śak V C.)(bhramayitum* ”bhram Caus.)(stokān, m. 2nd pl.)(narān, m. 2nd pl.)(yena, n. 3rd s.)(cetasaḥ, m. 1st pl. [bv. cpd.])(bhrānta-)(bhakti-)(te, m. 1st pl.)(gṛhnīyuḥ ”grah IX C. Opt. III p. pl.)(sarva-jñam, m. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 3196. For even one who knows something is capable of deceiving a few people; by which [deception], those whose devotion is deluded would accept [him as] an omniscient being.

body.text:
3197.
(vijñānaiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(kuhaka-)(kecit, m. 1st pl.)(kṣamāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(saṃvādana-)(bhukta-)(cintita-)(dravya-)(stha-)(muṣṭi-)(varjitāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(jñāna-)(dharma-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 3197. Some [who are] capable of concordance through jugglery and conjuring — [such as knowing] objects that have been eaten, thought of, [or placed] in a closed fist — [are people] devoid of [actual] knowledge of <s>Dharma</s> and the like.

body.text:
3198.
(tathā*)(kecit, m. 1st pl.)(kuśalāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(māyā-)(indra-jālā-)(ādi-)(bhrāmayanti ”bhram Caus. III p. pl.)(ajñakam, m. 2nd s.)(janam, m. 2nd s.)(yena, n. 3rd s.)(te, m. 1st pl.)(pratibhānti ”bhā II C. III p. pl.)(sarva-jñāḥ, m. 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 3198. Likewise, some [who are] skilled in <s>māyā</s> (illusion), <s>indrajāla</s> (magic), and the like — delude ignorant people; by which [deception], they appear [to be] omniscient beings.

body.text:
3199.
(api*)(kīrtitam, n. 1st s.)(itihāsa-)(purāṇeṣu, n. 7th pl.)(iti*)(brahma-)(ādiḥ, m. 1st s.)(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sarva-vit, m. 1st s.)(yasya, m. 6th s.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(vairāgyam, n. 1st s.)(apratigham, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3199. Moreover, in the <s>Itihāsas</s> (epics) and <s>Purāṇas</s>, it is proclaimed that [the one] beginning with <s>Brahmā</s> is omniscient — he whose knowledge and dispassion are unobstructed.

body.text:
3200.
(api*)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(vaktavyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(eva*)(gauṇatvena, n. 3rd s.)(vat*)(artha-vāda-)(mantra-)(yadvā*)(apratighatā, f. 1st s.)(ucyate ”vac Pass.)(jñānāt, n. 5th s.)(dharma-)(ādi-)(prakṛta-)
body.translated_text: 3200. Moreover, he [Brahmā] is to be spoken of [as omniscient] only in a secondary sense (<s>gauṇa</s>) — like <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passage) and <s>mantra</s>; or, the unobstructedness is said [to refer only to knowledge] of <s>Dharma</s> and the like that are the subject-matter.

body.text:
3201.
(tasya, m. 6th s.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(api*)(caturṣu, m. 7th pl.)(prakṛteṣu, m. 7th pl.)(dharma-)(artha-)(kāma-)(mokṣeṣu, m. 7th pl.)(apratigham, n. 1st s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(na-)(gocaram, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(sarva-)(artha-)
body.translated_text: 3201. His knowledge too — in the four subject-matters: <s>Dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>Artha</s> (wealth), <s>Kāma</s> (desire), and <s>Mokṣa</s> (liberation) — is unobstructed; that [knowledge] does not have all objects as its domain.

body.text:
3202.
(hi*)(apratighatā-)(mātrāt, n. 5th s.)(na*)(ucyate ”vac Pass.)(sarva-)(gocaratā, f. 1st s.)(hi*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(bhavati ”bhū I C.)(apratigham, n. 1st s.)(apratīghātāt, m. 5th s.)(api*)(sva-)(artheṣu, m. 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 3202. For merely from unobstructedness, omniscience is not declared; for that [knowledge] is unobstructed because of [its] non-obstruction even in [its] own objects [alone].

body.text:
3203.
(ca*)(etat, n. 1st s.)(yāvat*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(gocaram, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(dharma-)(ādi-)(phala-da)(tu*)(na* ... kiñcit, n. 1st s.)(prayojanam, n. 1st s.)(sarvaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(vṛkṣa-)(ādibhiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(jñātaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 3203. And this much [is clear] — knowledge that has [only] <s>Dharma</s> and the like as its domain is fruit-bearing; but there is no purpose whatsoever [served] by knowing all things — trees and the like.

body.text:
3204.
(yāvat*)(aupayika-)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(ca*)(jñāna-)(pratihanyate ”han Pass.)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(apratigha-)(vyapadeśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(asya, n. 6th s.)(labhyate ”labh Pass.)
Textual variant (Baudhabhāratī): etat in place of jñāna-.
body.translated_text: 3204. As much knowledge as is useful — [such] knowledge is not obstructed; by that, the designation 'unobstructed' is obtained for it.

body.text:
3205.
(yadvā*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(ātmani, m. 7th s.)(pravartitam, n. 1st s.)(abhyāsa-)(dhyāna-)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(eva*)(apratighātena, m. 3rd s.)(jñāna-)(ucyate ”vac Pass.)(apratighatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3205. Or, that very knowledge which has been cultivated through practice and meditation in oneself — because of the non-obstruction of that very knowledge, its unobstructedness is declared.

body.text:
3206.
(api*)(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(śaṅkaraḥ, m. 1st s.)(śrūyate ”sru Pass.)(daśa-)(avyayaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(iti*)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(vairāgyam, n. 1st s.)(aiśvaryam, n. 1st s.)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(api*)(jñānavān, m. 1st s.)(vittayā, f. 3rd s.)(ātman-)
body.translated_text: 3206. Moreover, <s>Śaṅkara</s> [i.e., <s>Śiva</s>], who is heard [described as] possessed of the ten [qualities] — imperishable — knowledge, dispassion, sovereignty — even he is knowledgeable [only] through self-knowledge.

body.text:
3207.
(etat, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(tat-)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(yat, n. 1st s.)(darśanam, n. 1st s.)(viśuddha-)(ātman-)(ca*)(yat, n. 1st s.)(nimitte, n. 7th s.)(tat-)(a-śuddhe, n. 7th s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(ucyate ”vac Pass.)(ajñānam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3207. This very [self-]knowledge of his is the vision of the purified self; and that which [arises] from an impure cause — that is declared to be ignorance.

body.text:
3208.
(api*)(atha*)(brahman-)(viṣṇu-)(maheśvarāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(dehatvāt, n. 5th s.)(veda-)(vedāt, m. 5th s.)(mayāt, m. 5th s.)(jñāna-)(sarva-)(sarva-jñāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(kim*)(mānuṣasya, m. 6th s.)
body.translated_text: 3208. Now then, if <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s> are omniscient — because of [their] embodiment — [and their omniscience comes] from the <s>Veda</s>, composed of all knowledge — what [does this prove] for a human being?

body.text:
3209.
(ca*)(kva*)(martyāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(buddha-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(ca*)(kva*)(trayam, n. 1st s.)(uttama-)(deva-)(yena, n. 3rd s.)(dṛk, f. 1st s.)(iti*)(te, m. 1st pl.)(spardhayā, f. 3rd s.)(tat-)(api*)(sarva-jñāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(moha-)
body.translated_text: 3209. And where [stand] mortals — the <s>Buddha</s> and the like — and where [stands] the supreme triad of gods? Thus, [if] they too [are declared] omniscient out of deluded rivalry with those [gods] —

body.text:
3210.
(apica*)(kīrtanam, n. 1st s.)(traya-)(brahman-)(ādi-)(vede, m. 7th s.)(nitye, m. 7th s.)(āgame, m. 7th s.)(ca*)(nityatvam, n. 1st s.)(vedānām, m. 6th pl.)(na*)(vihanyate ”han Pass.)(tat-)(nityatvāt, n. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 3210. Furthermore, the mention of the triad beginning with <s>Brahmā</s> — in the <s>Veda</s>, which is a permanent scripture — [does not establish their omniscience]; nor is the permanence of the <s>Vedas</s> invalidated — because of their [the Vedas'] permanence.

body.text:
3211.
(hi*)(te, m. 1st pl.)(samanvitāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(nityaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(guṇaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(nitya-)(karmabhiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(na*)(virodhinaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(sambhavāt, m. 5th s.)(abhidhāyitva-)(nitya-)(veda-)
body.translated_text: 3211. For they [the Vedas] are endowed with permanent qualities [and] permanent actions; because of the possibility of being eternal articulators [of meaning] — they are not contradictory to the permanence of the <s>Veda</s>.

body.text:
3212.
(tu*)(buddha-)(ādeḥ, m. 6th s.)(anityasya, m. 6th s.)(na*)(gamyatā, f. 1st s.)(āgama-)(ca*)(āgamasya, m. 6th s.)(iṣṭe, n. 7th s.)(nityatve, n. 7th s.)(kalpanā, f. 1st s.)(sarva-jña-)(vṛthā*)
body.translated_text: 3212. But for the <s>Buddha</s> and the like, who are non-eternal — the scriptural authority (<s>āgama</s>) is not tenable; and when the permanence of the scripture is accepted [as sufficient] — the conceptual construction of an omniscient being is pointless.

body.text:
3213.
(sarva-jña-)(jñāpanāt, n. 5th s.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)
(varam, n. 1st s.)(dharma-)(avabodhanam, n. 1st s.)(veda-)(bodhita-)(sarva-jña-)(jñānāt, n. 5th s.)(dharmāt, m. 5th s.)(tirohitāt, m. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 3213. Rather than [establishing validity] from the declaration of that omniscient being — better is the understanding of <s>Dharma</s> directly from the <s>Veda</s>; from the knowledge of the omniscient being taught by the <s>Veda</s> — [Dharma itself is] concealed by [that detour through] <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text:
3214.
(atirohita-)(dharma-)(ādi-)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(viśeṣyate ”śiṣ Caus. Pass.)(evam*)(āgama-)(gamyatvam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(sarva-jñasya, m 6th s.)(labhyate ”labh Pass.)
Textual variant: (Baudha Bhāratī) -dharmādijñānam eva for (GOS) -dharmavijñānam eva.
body.translated_text: 3214. [Direct] knowledge of <s>Dharma</s> and the like, which is not concealed — is indeed superior; thus, the knowability [of omniscience] through scripture is not obtained for the omniscient being.

body.text:
3215.
(yadi*)(kaścit, m. 1st s.)(sadṛśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sarva-jña-)(dṛśyeta ”dṛś Pass. Opt.)(samprati*)(tadā*)(sat-bhāvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sarva-jña-)(gamyeta ”gam Pass. Opt.)(balāt, n. 5th s.)(upamā-)
body.translated_text: 3215. If some [being] similar to an omniscient being were observed at present — then the existence of [past] omniscient beings could be understood forcefully — from analogy (<s>upamā</s>).

body.text:
3216.
(tu*)(dṛṣṭvā* ”dṛś)(eva*)(sarvān, m. 2nd pl.)(narān, m. 2nd pl.)(adhunātanān, m. 2nd pl.)(asarvajñān, m. 2nd pl.)(niścayaḥ, m. 1st s.)(upamānena, n. 3rd s.)(sādṛśyasya, n. 6th s.)(śeṣa-)(a-sarvajña-)
body.translated_text: 3216. But having seen all present-day men [to be] non-omniscient — the certainty of the non-omniscience of the remaining [beings is established] through analogy (<s>upamāna</s>), by [their] similarity.

body.text:
3217.
(upadeśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(hi*)(buddha-)(ādeḥ, m. 6th s.)(dharma-)(adharma-)(ādi-)(gocaraḥ, m. 1st s.)(anyathā*)(na*)(upapadyate ”pad IV Āt.)(sarva-jñaḥ, m. 1st s.)(yadi*)(no*)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)
body.translated_text: 3217. For the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s> and the like concerns the domain of <s>dharma</s> (merit), <s>adharma</s> (demerit), and the like; [such teaching] is not tenable otherwise — unless [the teacher] were omniscient.

body.text:
3218.
(pratyakṣa-)(ādau, m. 7th s.)(niṣiddhe, m. 7th s.)(api*)(sarva-jña-)(pratipādake, m. 7th s.)(artha-)(āpattyā, f. 3rd s.)(eva*)(sarva-jñam, m. 2nd s.)(ittham*)(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pratipadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)
body.translated_text: 3218. Even when direct perception and the like, [which would serve as] proofs of [the existence of] an omniscient [being], have been rejected — one who thus ascertains the omniscient [being] through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) alone —

body.text:
3219.
(yadvā*)(sādhanam, n. 1st s.)(pravṛttam, n. 1st s.)(iha*)(sarva-jñasya, m. 6th s.)(ucyate ”vac Pass.)(sāmānyataḥ-dṛṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(anyatra*)(darśanāt, n. 5th s.)(pūrvatva-)(jñāna-)
body.translated_text: 3219. Or alternatively, the proof that is put forward here for [the existence of] an omniscient [being] is said [to be] an inference based on general observation (<s>sāmānyato-dṛṣṭa</s>) — from the observation elsewhere of [the principle that] knowledge precedes [teaching].

body.text:
3220.
(hi*)(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kaścit, m. 1st s.)(upadeśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sarvaḥ, m. 1st s.)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(pūrvakaḥ, m. 1st s.)(jñāna-)(yathā*)(upadeśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(śaktīnām, f. 6th pl.)(abhayā-)(ādi-)(tathā-vidhaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3220. For whatever teaching [there is] — all of it is preceded by knowledge; just as the teaching of the capacities of <s>abhayā</s> (Terminalia chebula) and the like is of such a nature.

body.text:
3221.
(ayam, m. 1st s.)(upadeśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(dharma-)(adharma-)(ca*)(upadeśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kṛtaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tat-)(tasmāt,)(anumīyate ”mā Pass.)(asya, m. 6th s.)(pūrvakatvam, n. 1st s.)(jñāna-)(tadīya-)
body.translated_text: 3221. This is a teaching, and a teaching of <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit) has been made by him; therefore, it is inferred that his [teaching] was preceded by the knowledge of those [subjects].

body.text:
3222.
(upapannatvāt, n. 5th s.)(api*)(anyathā*)(iyam, f. 1st s.)(artha-āpattiḥ, f. 1st s.)(na*)(kṣamā, f. 1st s.)(ataḥ*)(eva*)(eṣā, f. 1st s.)(anumā, f. 1st s.)(vyavatiṣṭhate ”sthā I C. Āt.)(na*)(sādhvī, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3222. Because [the teaching] is tenable even otherwise, this <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) is not competent; and precisely for this reason, this inference too does not stand as valid.

body.text:
3223.
(hi*)(upadeśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(buddha-)(ādeḥ, m. 6th s.)(upapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(anyathā*)(api*)(vyāmohāt, m. 5th s.)(dṛṣṭa-)(svapna-)(ādi-)(vā*)(vedāt, m. 5th s.)(avitatha-)(śrutāt)
body.translated_text: 3223. For the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s> and the like is tenable even otherwise — through delusion, or from dreams and the like, or from the <s>Veda</s> that has been heard truthfully.

body.text:
3224.
(hi*)(tāvat*)(ye, m. 1st pl.)(a-veda-jñāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(asambhavaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vedāt, m. 5th s.)(upadeśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kṛtaḥ, m. 1st s.)(taiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(eva*)(kevalāt, m. 5th s.)(vyāmohāt, m. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 3224. For first, those who do not know the <s>Veda</s> — [their] teaching is impossible from the <s>Veda</s>; that which was taught by them was [done] merely from delusion alone.

body.text:
3225.
(loke, m. 7th s.)(upadeśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(duṣṭa-)(upadeṣṭṝṇām, m. 6th pl.)(pravarttate ”vṛ I C. Āt.)(vā*)(vyāmohāt, m. 5th s.)(a-tat-āśrayāt, m. 5th s. [bv. cpd.])(vā*)(artham*, m. 2nd s. [adv.])(vyāmohana-)(śiṣya-)
body.translated_text: 3225. In the world, the teaching of deluded teachers proceeds — either from delusion, or from a basis that is not that [true knowledge], or for the purpose of deluding the disciples.

body.text:
3226.
(tu*)(yadi*)(asau, m. 1st s.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(mūlaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(veda-)(tathā*)(prayaccheyuḥ ”yam I C. Opt. III p. pl.)(upadeśam, m. 2nd s.)(eva*)(veda-)(vādibhyaḥ, m. 4th pl.)(yathā*)(manu-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 3226. But if that [teaching of the Buddha] had the <s>Veda</s> as its root — then they would give their teaching to the proponents of the <s>Veda</s> — just as <s>Manu</s> and the others [do].

body.text:
3227.
(yataḥ*)(tu*)(taiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(upadeśanam, n. 1st s.)(jñāyate ”jñā Pass.)(kṛtam, n. 1st s.)(mūrkha-)(śūdrebhyaḥ, m. 4th pl.)(tena, n. 3rd s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(duṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(sāṃvṛtam, n. 1st s.)(vat*)(karman-)(kūṭa-)
body.translated_text: 3227. Since their teaching is known to have been given to fools and <s>Śūdras</s> — therefore, that [teaching] is corrupt, like a fraudulent conventional act (<s>kūṭa-karman</s>).

body.text:
3228.
(tu*)(manu-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(ye, m. 1st s.)(siddhāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(prādhānyena, n. 3rd s.)(trayī-)(vidām, m. 6th pl.)(granthāḥ, m. 1st pl. [bv. cpd.])(āśrita-)(trayī-)(vid-)(te, m. 1st pl.)(uktayaḥ, m. 1st pl [bv. cpd.])(prabhava-)(veda-)
body.translated_text: 3228. But those [sages] such as <s>Manu</s> and the like, who are established preeminently among the knowers of the three [<s>Vedas</s>] — [their] treatises are based on the three [<s>Vedas</s>]; their utterances have the <s>Veda</s> as [their] source.

body.text:
3229.
(na*)(upapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(praṇayanam, n. 1st s.)(grantha-)(ca*)(arpaṇam, n. 1st s.)(teṣām, m. 6th pl.)(adṛṣṭvā* ”dṛś)(vā*)(a-pradarśya* ”dṛś Caus.)(śiṣyebhyaḥ, m. 4th pl.)(veda-)(vākyāni, n. 2nd pl.)
body.translated_text: 3229. And the composition of [their] treatises and the transmission of those [teachings] to disciples is not tenable without having seen or shown the Vedic sentences [as their basis].

body.text:
3230.
(api*)(yat, n. 1st s.)(sādhanam, n. 1st s.)(prayujyate ”yuj Pass.)(iti*)(kopi, m. 1st s.)(naraḥ, m. 1st s.)(asti ”as II C.)(sarva-jñaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(sarva-jñatvam, n. 1st s.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(nyūnam, n. 1st s.)(pratijñā-)
body.translated_text: 3230. Moreover, the proof that is employed — 'some person is omniscient' — that [proposition of] omniscience is itself deficient as a thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>).

body.text:
3231.
(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(arthaḥ, m. 1st s.)(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sisādhayiṣitaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(abhidhīyate ”dhā Pass.)(anayā, f. 3rd s.)(tu*)(asti ”as II C.)(na*)(kiñcit, n. 1st s.)(prayojanam, n. 1st s.)(siddhau, f. 7th s.)(tat-)(yat, n. 1st s.)(ucyate ”vac Pass.)
body.translated_text: 3231. The object that is desired to be proven is not [properly] stated [by that thesis]; and by this [formulation], there is simply no purpose served in the proof of that [omniscience].

body.text:
3232.
(mātreṇa, n. 3rd s.)(siddhi-)(sarva-jña)(sāmānya-)(labhyate ”labh Pass.)(sā, f. 1st s.)(sarva-jñatā, f. 1st s.)(ucyate ”vac Pass.)(siddhyai, f. 4th s.)(satyatā-)(yadīya-)(āgama-)
body.translated_text: 3232. By [merely proving the existence of] an omniscient [being] in general, that omniscience is obtained [but only abstractly]; [however,] the omniscience [that needs to be proven] is said [to be] for the purpose of establishing the truthfulness of his (<s>tadīya</s>) scripture (<s>āgama</s>).

body.text:
3233.
(yāvat*)(buddhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(sarva-jñaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tāvat*)(tat-)(vacanam, n. 1st s.)(mṛṣā*)(kutaḥ*)(satyatā, f 1st s.)(tat-)(siddhe, m. 7th s.)(yatra kvacana*)(sarva-jñe, m. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 3233. As long as the <s>Buddha</s> is not [proven to be] omniscient, so long his statement is false; whence [could there be] truthfulness [of his statement] if any omniscient [being] whatsoever were established?

body.text:
3234.
(hi*)(sarva-jñe, m. 7th s.)(anyasmin, m. 7th s.)(satyatā, f. 1st s.)(vacasaḥ, n. 6th s.)(anyasya, m. 6th s.)(hi*)(tayoḥ, n. 6th d.)(sāmānādhikaraṇye, n. 7th s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(aṅga-aṅgitā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3234. For if [the omniscience belongs to] another omniscient [being], the truthfulness of another's speech [would follow]; and for those two [the omniscient being and the Buddha], in [the case of] co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>), there would be a principal-subsidiary relationship.

body.text:
3235.
(nāma*)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(yat, n. 1st s.)(asmin, m. 7th s.)(loke, m. 7th s.)(pratyakṣam, n. 1st s.)(kasyacit, m. 6th s.)(vastutvaiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(prameya-)(jñeya-)(vat*)(dadhi-)(rūpa-)(rasa-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 3235. Indeed, whatever in this world is directly perceived by anyone — [having the nature of] an object of valid knowledge and a knowable — like the form, taste, and the like of curds —

body.text:
3236.
(api*)(mātre, n. 7th s.)(jñāna-)(nirdiṣṭe, n. 7th s.)(āpatet ”pat I C. Opt.)(nyūnatvam, n. 1st s.)(pakṣa-)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(iti*)(sarva-jñaḥ, m. 1st s.)(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(abhīṣṭaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(pratipāditaḥ, m. 1st s.)(ittham*)
body.translated_text: 3236. Even when [the thesis is] indicated as mere knowledge [of some things], the deficiency of the thesis would follow — [for] the omniscient [being] that is desired [to be proven] has not been thus demonstrated.

body.text:
3237.
(yadi*)(kaścit, m. 1st s.)(anyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(atiriktaḥ, m. 1st s.)(buddha-)(gataḥ, m. 1st s.)(sarvajñatām, f. 2nd s.)(kva*)(upayujyate ”yuj Pass.)(tat, n. 1st s.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(pramāṇatve, n. 7th s.)(vākya-)(buddha-)
body.translated_text: 3237. If some other, additional [quality] pertaining to the <s>Buddha</s> reaches the status of omniscience — where is that knowledge employed in the validity of the <s>Buddha</s>'s statement?

body.text:
3238.
(ca*)(asau, m. 1st s.)(gataḥ, m. 1st s.)(daśan-)(bhūmi-)(sarva-)(rāga-)(ādi-)(saṅkṣaye, m. 7th s.)(buddhyate ”budh Pass.)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(jñānena, n. 3rd s.)(tulyena, n. 3rd s.)(śuddha-)(sphaṭika-)
body.translated_text: 3238. And he, having gone through [all] ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages), upon the exhaustion of all <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and the like — knows everything through cognition that is like a pure crystal.

body.text:
3239.
(ca*)(āpannaḥ, m. 1st s.)(dhyāna-)(dadhat ”dhā III C., m. 1st s.)(dhāraṇām, f. 2nd s.)(sarva-)(viṣayām, f. 2nd s. [bv. cpd.])(ca*)(tathā*)(vyāptaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sarva-)(arthaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(na*)(eva*)(śaktaḥ, m. 1st s.)(upadeśane, n. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 3239. And having attained <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), [and] holding <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) that encompasses all objects — and thus pervaded by all objects — [he is] indeed not capable [merely] of [ordinary] teaching.

body.text:
3240.
(ca*)(yadā*)(upadiśet ”diś VI C. Opt.)(kiñcit, n. 2nd s.)(vat*)(sāmānya-)(vaktṛ-)(syāt ”as II C.)(gītam, n. 1st s.)(eka-deśa-)(jña-)(na*)(tat, n. 1st s.)(bhāṣitam, n. 1st s.)(sarva-jña-)
body.translated_text: 3240. And when he would teach something, like an ordinary speaker, [the teaching] would be [only] of one part [of reality] — [the speech] of a knower of one portion; that [speech] would not be the utterance of an omniscient [being].

body.text:
3241.
(tasmin, m. 7th s.)(samāpanne, m. 7th s.)(dhyāna-)(āsthite, m. 7th s.)(-vat*)(cintā-)(ratna-)(deśanāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(niścaranti ”car I C. III p. pl.)(yathā-kāmam*, m. 2nd s. as adv.)(api*)(kuḍya-)(ādibhyaḥ, m. 5th pl.)
body.translated_text: 3241. When he has entered into <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and is absorbed [therein] — teachings, like [those proceeding from] wish-fulfilling gems (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>), issue forth at will even from walls and the like.

body.text:
3242.
(tābhiḥ, f. 3rd pl.)(mānavāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(jānanti ”jñā IX C. III p. pl.)(sarvān, m. 2nd pl.)(arthān, m. 2nd pl.)(jijñāsitān, m. 2nd pl.)(ca*)(te, m. 1st pl.)(kṣipram, n. 2nd s. [adverb])(yathā-bhavyam, n. 2nd s. [adverb])(āsadayanti ”sad Caus. III p. pl.)(hitāni, n. 2nd pl.)
body.translated_text: 3242. Through those [teachings], human beings know all the objects they desire to know; and they quickly attain beneficial [results] as is fitting.

body.text:
3243.
(iti*)(ādi, n. 1st s.)(kīrtyamānam ”kīrt Pass., n. 1 s.)(śobhate ”śubh I C. Āt.)(śrad-dadhāneṣu, ”dhā III C., m. 7th pl.)(vayam, 1st pl.)(tu*)(ye, m. 1st pl.)(aśrad-dadhānāḥ, ”dhā III C., m. 1st pl.)(prārthayāmahe ”arth X C. Āt/)(yuktīḥ, f. 2nd pl.)
body.translated_text: 3243. Such and other [claims] being proclaimed are appealing to [those who have] faith; but we who are without faith request [logical] reasonings.

body.text:
3244.
(ca*)(niḥsṛtānām, f. 6th pl.)(kuḍya-)(na*)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(upadiṣṭatā, f. 1st s.)(āpta-)(ca*)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(na*)(viśvāsaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tāsu, f. 7th pl.)(iti*)(kena, m. 3rd s.)(imāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(kīrtitāḥ, f. 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 3244. And [regarding teachings] that have issued from walls — there would be no status as [teachings of] a trustworthy person (<s>āpta</s>); and there would be no confidence in them [either] — by whom [then] have these [teachings] been proclaimed?

body.text:
3245.
(tu*)(kim*)(syuḥ ”as II C. Opt. III p. pl.)(praṇītāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(buddha-)(tu*)(kim*)(vañcakaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(brāhmaṇa-)(syuḥ ”as II C. Opt. III p. pl.)(upadiṣṭāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(krīḍadbhiḥ ”krīḍ VI C., m. 3rd pl.)(dūrastha-)(pratiśabdakaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 3245. Were they composed by the <s>Buddha</s>? Or were they taught by deceitful <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>? Or [uttered] by those playing [the trick of] distant echoes?

body.text:
3246.
(kiṃvā*)(kṣudra-)(eva*)(adṛṣṭaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(piśāca-)(ādyaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(mānibhiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(prājña-)(kartavyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(viśvāsaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tāsu, f. 7th pl.)
body.translated_text: 3246. Or perhaps [they were uttered] by unseen petty [beings such as] <s>piśācas</s> (demons) and the like? Therefore, confidence should not be placed in them by the wise who [rightly] esteem [reason].

body.text:
3247.
(evam*)(nirāspadā, f. 1st s.)(sarva-jñatā, f. 1st s.)(puṃsām, m. 6th pl.)(svātantryeṇa, n. 3rd s.)(ca*)(cintyate ”cint Pass.)(idam, n. 1st s.)(katham*)(sarva-darśī, m. 1st s.)(bhūyaḥ*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(mataḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3247. Thus, the omniscience of persons is without basis even when considered independently; [and we ask:] how is [this person] regarded as all-seeing? — yet again —

body.text:
3248.
(jānan ”jñā IX C., m. 1st s.)(yugapad*)(vā*)(paripāṭyā*, f. 3rd s. [adv.])(ca*)(sarvam, n. 2nd s.)(eka-)(sva-bhāvataḥ*)(vā*)(yathā-pradhānam*, n. 2nd s. [adv.])(vā*)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)(sarva-vit, m. 1st s.)(śaktyā, f. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 3248. Does [the omniscient being] know everything simultaneously, or in sequence? [Is omniscience accepted as] of a single nature, or as according to [what is] principal, or through capacity?

body.text:
3249.
(na*)(kvacit*)(dṛṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(eka-)(dhiyā, f. 3rd s.)(jñānam, n. 1st s.)(virodhinām, m. 6th pl.)(sva-bhāvānām, m. 6th pl.)(śuci-)(aśuci-)(ādi-)(vā*)(bhinnāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(gatayaḥ, f. 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 3249. Nowhere is it observed that contradictory natures — such as pure and impure, and the like — [are known] by a single cognition; or [such things would require] distinct operations [of cognition].

body.text:
3250.
(kaḥ, m. 1st s.)(śaknuyāt ”śak V C. Opt.)(boddhum* ”budh)(api*)(śataiḥ, n. 3rd pl.)(vatsarāṇām, m. 6th pl.)(krameṇa, m. 3rd s.)(anantam, n. 2nd s.)(vastu, n. 2nd s.)(bhūtam, n. 2nd s.)(bhavat, n. 2nd s.)(ca*)(bhaviṣyat, n. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 3250. Who could know — even in hundreds of years — through sequence, the infinite reality — [what] has been, [what] is, and [what] will be?

body.text:
3251.
(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sva-)(avibhaktena, m. 3rd s.)(bhāvena, m. 3rd s.)(avabudhyate ”budh IV C. Āt.)(sarvam, n. 2nd s.)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(budhyate ”budh IV C. Āt.)(sva-lakṣaṇāni, n. 2nd pl.)(sarveṣām, m. 6th pl.)(bhāvānām, m. 6th pl.)
body.translated_text: 3251. He who knows everything through an undifferentiated state [of cognition] — he does not know the unique particulars (<s>sva-lakṣaṇas</s>) of all entities.

body.text:
3252.
(kim, n. 1st s.)(api*)(tena, m. 3rd s.)(sarva-jñena, m. 3rd s.)(boddhā, m. 1st s.)(sāmānya-)(rūpasya, n. 6th s.)(vastu, n. 2nd s.)(na*)(avagamyate ”gam Pass.)(anya-)(rūpeṇa, n. 3rd s.)(bodhena, m. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 3252. Is anything at all not understood by that omniscient being? The entity [that has] the form of the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) is not apprehended by a cognition of another form.

body.text:
3253.
(tat, n. 1st s.)(eka-ākāra-)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(samyak*)(vā*)(api*)(mithyā*)(samyaktve, n. 7th s.)(bādhā, f. 1st s.)(dṛṣṭa-)(evam*)(prasaktam, n. 1st s.)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)(advayam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3253. That cognition of a single form — would it be correct or false? If correct — sublation [by other cognitions] is observed; [and] thus all [that follows] is entailed — [namely,] non-duality (<s>advaya</s>).

body.text:
3254.
(ca*)(tataḥ*)(vaḥ, 6th pl.)(syuḥ ”as II C. Opt. III p. pl.)(na*)(śiṣya-)(sarva-jña-)(dharma-)(adharma-)(uktayaḥ, f. 1st pl.)(tat-)(sva-bhāva-)(anavadhāraṇāt, n. 5th s.)(bhinna-)(rūpatve, n. 7th s.)
body.translated_text: 3254. And therefore, for you, the declarations of the omniscient [being regarding] teacher, disciple, <s>dharma</s>, and <s>adharma</s> would not exist — because of the non-ascertainment of their distinct natures.

body.text:
3255.
(tu*)(mṛṣātve, n. 7th s.)(sarva-vit, m. 1st s.)(prāpnoti ”āp V C.)(bhrāntaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(śraddheyam, n. 1st s.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(vacaḥ, n. 1st s.)(tadā*)(vat*)(vākya-)(unmatta-)(ādi-)
body.translated_text: 3255. But if [the cognition of a single form is] false — the omniscient one turns out to be deluded; the speech of that [deluded person] is not to be trusted then — like the speech of a madman and the like.

body.text:
3256.
(yadi*)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(sarva-jñaḥ, m. 1st s.)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)(yaḥ, m. 1st s.)(jānāti ”jñā IX C.)(sakalam, n. 2nd s.)(karma, n. 2nd s.)(sa-hetu, n. 2nd s.)(alaukikena, n. 3rd s.)(jñānena, n. 3rd s.)(jena, n. 3rd s.)(samādhi-)
body.translated_text: 3256. If that [person] is accepted as omniscient (<s>sarvajña</s>) who knows all actions (<s>karma</s>) together with [their] causes through a supramundane knowledge born of <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration),

body.text:
3257.
(tat*)(asti ”as II C.)(na*)(pramāṇam, n. 1sts.)(asya, m. 6th s.)(sat-bhāve, m. 7th s.)(pratyakṣam, n. 1st s.)(vā*)(anumānam, n. 1st s.)(vā*)(śābdam, n. 1st s.)(kṛtam, n. 1st s.)(atat-)(iti*)(īdṛśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(asti ”as II C.)
body.translated_text: 3257. Then — there is no valid means of cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) for his existence; neither perception, nor inference, nor verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) — such [a being] does not exist — thus [is our position].

body.text:
3258.
(yugapad*)(vā*)(paripāṭyā, f. 3rd s.)(katham*)(anumā, f. 1st s.)(vinā*)(kāryāt, n. 5th s.)(api*)(na*)(sāmarthyam, n. 1st s.)(eva*)(vā*)(samarthe, m. 7th s.)(eva*)(sarvam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3258. How [could there be] inference — whether simultaneously or successively — without [an observable] effect? Or, if [you say there is] the capacity itself [as evidence] — [then] everything [would obtain] even in one who is [merely] capable.

body.text:
3259.
(ca*)(sarve, m. 1st pl.)(kṣetra-jñāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(prabhaviṣṇavaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(avabodhe, m. 7th s.)(sarva-)(tu*)(vikalatvāt, n. 5th s.)(upāya-)(te, m. 1st pl.)(na*)(budhyante ”budh IV C. III p. pl.)(nikhilam, n. 2nd s.)
body.translated_text: 3259. And all conscious beings (<s>kṣetrajñas</s>) are capable of apprehending everything; but because of the deficiency of the means (<s>upāya</s>), they do not cognize everything.

body.text:
3260.
(evam*)(iti*)(ekaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tatra*)(labdha-)(asādhāraṇa-)(upāyaḥ, m. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(vilakṣaṇaḥ, m. 1st s.)(aśeṣa-)(puṃsām, m. 6th pl.)(vit, m. 1st s.)(sarva-)(niṣpramāṇakam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3260. Thus, one [being] there — who has obtained an extraordinary means — [is] distinguished from all persons; [he is] the knower of all — [but this is] without [independent] proof.

body.text:
3261.
(ittham*)(yadā*)(na*)(sarva-jñaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kaścidapi, m. 1st s.)(upapadyate ”pad IV C. Āt.)(tadā*)(pauruṣeyam, n. 1st s.)(vacaḥ, n. 1st s.)(hetuḥ, m. 1st s.)(adhigame, m. 7th s.)(dharma-)
body.translated_text: 3261. When, in this way, no omniscient being (<s>sarvajña</s>) whatsoever is tenable — then human speech [alone] is the means [of knowing] <s>dharma</s> (duty) —

body.text:
3262.
(iti*)(mīmāṃsakāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(prāhuḥ ”ah Perf. III p. pl.)(lālāsāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(svatantra-)(śruti-)(ca*)(sādhitā, f. 1st s.)(vistareṇa, m. 3rd s.)(vedānām, m. 6th pl.)(pauruṣeyatā, f. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3262. Thus the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> declare, [being] desirous [of establishing] the independence of <s>śruti</s> (scripture); but the human authorship (<s>pauruṣeyatā</s>) of the <s>Vedas</s> has been established at length.

body.text:
3263.
(tasmāt, n. 5th s.)(vidyate ”vid Pass.)(sākṣāt-)(draṣṭā, m. 1st s.)(atīndriya-)(arthānām, m. 6th pl.)(tu*)(na*)(kaścit, m. 1st s.)(paśyati ”dṛś IV C.)(nityena, n. 3rd s.)(vacasā, n. 3rd s.)(asambhavāt, m. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 3263. Therefore, there does exist a direct seer (<s>sākṣāt-draṣṭā</s>) of supersensory objects; but no one sees [them] through an eternal speech — because of [its] impossibility.

body.text:
3264.
(nityasya, n. 6th s.)(vacasaḥ, n. 6th s.)(na*)(samutpadyate ”pad IV C.)(śaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(jñāne, n. 7th s.)(sva-)(artha-)(svataḥ*)(vā*)(api*)(anyataḥ*)(avirodhataḥ*)(akrama-)(krama-)
body.translated_text: 3264. An eternal speech does not produce the capacity for the cognition of its own object — neither intrinsically nor from an external source — [whether] without sequence or with sequence — without contradiction.

body.text:
3265.
(svarga-)(yāga-)(ādayaḥ, m. 1st pl.)(prakāśitāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(jñātvā* ”jñā)(svataḥ*)(tava, 6th s.)(api*)(kāraḥ, m. 1st s.)(veda-)(asti ”as II C.)(tādṛśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(dṛk, m. 1st s.)(atīndriya-)(artha-)
body.translated_text: 3265. Heaven (<s>svarga</s>), sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>), and the like have been illuminated [only] through being known [by someone] independently — even according to you, there is [in effect] a Vedic author — [one who is] a seer of supersensory objects.

body.text:

body.translated_text: 3267. But by the acceptance gained through presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>) [of the existence] of one who knows <s>dharma</s> — this negation [of omniscience] made by you at length is refuted.

body.translated_text: 3269. Because there might be someone whose [cognition of] all entities has been illuminated by a pure, unwavering lamp of knowledge — [the objection] stated here is not a valid refutation.

body.translated_text: 3270. And merely from the non-perception [of the omniscient being], the ascertainment of his non-existence [is untenable] — because of the impossibility of [establishing] the non-existence of what is perceived — [namely,] the pervasion of causality in [all] entities.

body.translated_text: As long as the stream of qualities flows favorably in this mind-continuum, to that extent it becomes ever more luminous.

body.translated_text: This <s>citta</s> (mind), whose nature is perception of reality, is <s>prabhāsvara</s> (luminous) by its very nature and stable; but the impurities are considered <s>āgantuka</s> (adventitious).

body.translated_text: For if the mind were necessarily oriented toward self-awareness alone, then cognition of objects would not be possible, since apprehension would be unestablished.

body.translated_text: Therefore, the mind has a self-nature, as evidenced by <s>sva-saṃvedana</s> (self-awareness); this <s>sva-saṃvitti</s> (self-cognition) is established as having a nature that is unsuperimposed.

body.translated_text: And because the path that destroys all impurities leads to their complete eradication, there is no loss; without effort there is no effort, but from perceiving the qualities, effort arises.

body.translated_text: 3440. Therefore, the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror), adorned with a mass of stainless [and] unwavering virtues — [having] a nature unshakable by the wind of faults — is understood [to be] omniscient.

body.translated_text: 3441. Furthermore, whatever objects are cultivated [in meditation] — all of them shine forth perfectly clearly at the culmination [of practice]; just as the objects of desire and the like [become vivid] through meditation.

body.translated_text: 3442. And all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) are cultivated by great beings for a long time, in manifold ways, in their true form — [as] <s>śūnya</s> (empty), <s>anātman</s> (selfless), and the like.

body.translated_text: 3443. And the [quality of] being amenable to cultivation in [their] true form — [as] <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), <s>anātman</s> (selflessness), and the like — has been established for form and the like; therefore, because of the arising of cultivation [directed at] actual reality — that [cognition] is accepted as a valid means of knowledge.

body.translated_text: 3444. [It is] direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) — because of manifesting clearly [its object]; [it is] a valid means of knowledge — because of [its] concordance with reality; like the appearance of blue and the like that have arisen [and] are based on the eye and the like.

body.translated_text: 3445. And the clear manifestation of all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) at once in a single cognition is possible; and therefore, let it be thus understood.

body.translated_text: 3446. Because of being cultivated in that way — like [the meditation on] a son, a thief, or a woman — the cultivation too [of all dharmas] is not difficult [to attain]; [it requires] merely the wish [directed toward] a primary [object of meditation].

body.translated_text: 3447. body.translated_text: 3460-3461. Just as one who has directly perceived water and the like is a teacher [of its location to others] — the supreme sage, that excellent being, spoke from [his] own definitive knowledge — [about] the supersensory meaning — unheard, uninferred — the capacity, characterized by <s>kalpas</s> (ritual procedures), <s>mudrās</s> (gestures), <s>maṇḍalas</s> (diagrams), and the like — [which was] unknown to others.

body.translated_text: 3463. The direct perception that operates for one who stands in a single room — the capacity [would be limited] precisely to that [room]; indeed, [it does] not [extend] to the space outside that room.

body.translated_text: 3472. And when that [omniscient being] is [thus] conceived — this rule is established: <s>Dharma</s> is known through the independent <s>Veda</s> alone.

body.text:
3473.

body.translated_text: 3473. And the capacity of direct perception regarding the knowable that has not yet come — would likewise obtain for <s>yogins</s>; that has been stated in [the chapter on] the examination of the three times.

body.text:
3474.
(yadivā*)(sāmarthyāt, n. 5th s.)(yoga-)(mānasam, n. 1st s.)(yoginām, m. 6th pl.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(sphuṭam, n. 1st s.)(nibham, n. 1st s.)(bhūta-)(ajāta-)(nirāśaṃsam, n. 1st s.)(liṅga-)(āgama-)
body.translated_text: 3474. Or, through the capacity of <s>yoga</s> — the mental [cognition] of <s>yogins</s> would be clear — resembling what has been and what has not yet been — without requiring inferential marks or scripture.

body.text:
3475.
(saṃvitteḥ, f. 5th s.)(sva-)(ātman-)(avabhāsa-)(tat, n. 1st s.)(gocaram, n. 1st s. [bv. cpd.])(sva-lakṣaṇa-)(ca*)(saṃvedanāt, n. 5th s.)(spaṣṭa-)(avabhāsa-)(tat, n. 1st s.)(iṣyate ”iṣ Pass.)(pratyakṣam, n. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3475. Because of [its] awareness being the self-manifestation of [its own] cognition — it has [its own] unique particular (<s>sva-lakṣaṇa</s>) as [its] domain; and because of clearly manifesting experience — it is accepted as direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>).

body.translated_text: 3476. Therefore, there does indeed exist a seer of supersensory objects — directly; because of the non-existence of permanent speech, no one sees by that [permanent speech].

body.translated_text: 3477. Those of keen intellect declare that the cognition of the sage [is known] regarding supersensory objects — from inference — [based on what was] previously stated; but not otherwise — from scripture that has been [artificially] composed.

body.translated_text: 3553. 'But [the omniscience of <s>Śiva</s> and others] is not accepted by us' — [the opponent says, claiming that] those [<s>Śaivas</s> and others] are omniscient too, out of rivalry. For who would fabricate a rivalry with sky-flowers [i.e., non-existent things] against real [entities]?

body.text:

body.translated_text: 3554. For it has been established that eternal [beings], by [their] separation from all capacities, are devoid of all power; therefore, <s>Tryambaka</s> (three-eyed <s>Śiva</s>) and the like, accepted by the opponents, do not exist.

body.translated_text: 3555. Moreover, the knowledge of those [rival claimants to omniscience] is erroneous — as is seen from [their assertions of] a self (<s>ātman</s>) and the like; but [the knowledge] of the <s>Buddhas</s> has been demonstrated at length to be non-erroneous.

body.translated_text: 3556. Therefore, there is no rivalry with them in reality — the distance [between the two] is vast. For who would create a rivalry with those afflicted by eye-disease (<s>taimirikas</s>), when one's own vision is sound?

body.translated_text: 3576-3577. And all [beings] here, without distinction, could be of that [distinguished] lineage; they would be supports of [the mastery of] qualities and the like — those whose every impurity has been exhausted; if they have that [noble lineage] as their basis, they become distinguished. But distinction [comes] not otherwise — like [the distinction claimed by] a hunter [who happens to be born in] a twice-born caste.

body.text:
3578.

body.translated_text: 3578. And the well-known practices that begin with the birth-rite (<s>jāta-karman</s>) and the like — those are [merely] conventional; for those [practices] are future [in character] — like those of others — and even in artificial [ritual contexts].

body.translated_text: 3579. And much time has passed, and [given] the excessive fickleness of women — the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-hood even of a person [of your community] cannot be ascertained.

body.translated_text: 3580. There is no knower of supersensory objects among you; and the eternal <s>Veda</s> too has not proclaimed the purity of your lineage.

body.translated_text: 3581. Therefore, <s>Manu</s> and the others too — whose twice-born [status] is unknown — they should not give instruction to the twice-born, because of the uncertainty regarding that [status].

body.translated_text: 3582-3583. Surely, I suspect, [the reason why] <s>Manu</s> and the others [taught] from some [supposed] Vedic derivation regarding [a particular] matter — [was their] inability to demonstrate [that derivation] in themselves. The <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are dull — [merely] having studied the <s>Veda</s> — [and] incapable of critical examination; therefore, the instruction was given by them to the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> alone.

body.text:

(purāṇam, n. 1st s.)(dharmaḥ, m. 1st s.)(mānavaḥ, m. 1st s.)(vedaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sāṅgaḥ, m. 1st s.)(cikitsitam, n. 1st s.)(catvāri, n. 1st pl.)(siddhāni, n. 1st pl.)(ājñā-)(na*)(hantavyāni, n. 1st pl.)(hetubhiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)
body.translated_text: 3584. 'The <s>Purāṇa</s>, the law of <s>Manu</s>, the <s>Veda</s> with its auxiliary [sciences], and medicine — these four authoritative [works] should not be attacked with [mere] reasons' — [thus they say].

body.translated_text: 3585. This [dictum], I think, was an intimidation given by them to the dull-witted; for by that [dictum] alone — how could there be established validity, from a mere command, elsewhere [than in the command itself]?

body.translated_text: 3586. But those great souls, by whom the correctness of meaning in their own utterances has been clearly determined — and the capacity to make others understand that [meaning] —

body.translated_text: 3587. Those [<s>Buddhas</s>], whose every fear has been set at rest, roar the lion's roar — [which] produces weariness in the <s>kutīrthyas</s> (false teachers), [who are like] elephants intoxicated with the madness of pride.

(bhikṣavaḥ, m. 1st pl. as vocative [sambuddhau])(mat-)(vacaḥ, n. 1st s.)(grāhyam, n. 1st s.)(paṇḍitaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(parīkṣya* ”īkṣ)(tu*)(na*)(gauravāt, n. 5th s.)(iva*)(suvarṇam, n. 1st s.)(tāpāt, m. 5th s.)(chedāt, m. 5th s.)(nikaṣāt, m. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 3588. O <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), my words should be accepted by the wise only after examination — not out of [mere] reverence — just as gold [is tested] by heating, cutting, and rubbing on a touchstone.

body.text:
3589.
(ca*)(ye, m. 1st s.)(brāhmaṇāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(pāramārthikāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(vāhita-)(pāpatvāt, n. 5th s.)(abhyasta-)(amala-)(nairātmyāḥ, m. 1st pl [bv. cpd.])(te, m. 1st pl.)(śāsane, n. 7th s.)(muneḥ, m. 6th s.)(eva*)
body.translated_text: 3589. And those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who are [truly] ultimate — because of having cast off evil, [and being] practiced in the stainless [doctrine of] <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness) — they are [followers] of the teaching of the <s>Muni</s> (Sage, i.e., the <s>Buddha</s>) alone.

body.text:
3590.
(tena, n. 3rd s.)(iha*)(eva*)(śramaṇaḥ, m. 1st s.)(parikīrtyate ”kīrt Pass.)(śramaṇaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(tathā*)(brāhmaṇaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(caturdhā*)(hi*)(pravādāḥ, m. 1st pl.)(para-)(śūnyāḥ, m. 1st pl.)
body.translated_text: 3590. Therefore, herein [the <s>Buddha</s>] alone is proclaimed as the [true] <s>śramaṇa</s> (ascetic) — by [genuine] <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> alike; for the four [types of] assertions [of other teachers] are devoid of the other [i.e., valid reasoning].

body.text:

body.translated_text: 3591. [Thus] the proof has been established — [namely,] that there exists some person [who is] omniscient; the thesis [involving the negation of] deficiency and the like is also not faulty.

body.translated_text: 3592. For formerly — [so say] the wise <s>Saugatas</s> (Buddhists) — they made effort in [attaining] the complete knowledge of all objects — [which is] without remainder; even [though the effort may seem] fruitless at first,

body.translated_text: 3593. But here, [what has been] sung [is]: 'the knower of a portion [of reality] — [his] speech would not be [the speech of an] omniscient [being] — [for it was] formerly declared' — because of the connection with all knowledge.

body.translated_text: 3594. Just as an ordinary person (<s>alpa-darśana</s>) — having experienced desired objects and the like — projects [them] onto consciousness and afterwards speaks [of] the substrates of experience,

body.translated_text: 3595. And that speech [of the ordinary person] is not [a source of valid knowledge] — [for] the birth of the knowledge of those objects would not be [thereby established]; so too, the speech of the omniscient [being] differs — because of the difference of the cause.

body.text:

(gatam, n. 1st s.)(kāraṇatām, f. 2nd s.)(asya, n. 6th s.)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(samasta-)(vastu-)(tu*)(nimittam, n. 1st s.)(tasya, n. 6th s.)(vijñānam, n. 1st s.)(mātra-)(kiñcit-)(artha-)
body.translated_text: 3596. The cognition of all entities has attained causality for this [omniscient speech]; but the cause of that [ordinary person's speech] is a cognition of merely some objects.

body.translated_text: 3597. [Objection:] Surely, in [the case of] the impossibility of conceptual thought (<s>vikalpa</s>) [for the omniscient being] — what kind of desire to express (<s>vivakṣā</s>) [could] that [being have]? For because of [his] having abandoned [all habitual] conduct, conceptual thought does not operate in him.

body.text:
3598.
(na*)(evam*)(hi*)(saṅkalpaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kliṣṭaḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(asti ”as II C.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(āvṛtti-)(kṣayāt, m. 5th s.)(tu*)(anukūlaḥ, m. 1st s.)(jagat-)(hita-)(kuśalaḥ, m. 1st s.)(kena, m. 3rd s.)(vāryate ”vṛ Caus. Pass.)
body.translated_text: 3598. [Reply:] Not so — for afflicted conceptualization (<s>kliṣṭa-saṅkalpa</s>) does not exist in him, because of the exhaustion of [afflictive] coverings (<s>āvṛtti</s>); but the [conceptualization that is] favorable [and] conducive to the welfare of the world — by what [reason] is it prevented?

body.text:

(ca*)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(na*)(avasyati ”syo IV C.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(vikalpasya, m. 6th s.)(arthavattām, f. 2nd s.)(hi*)(vetti ”vit II C.)(tam, m. 2nd s.)(nirālamabanam, m. 2nd s.)(hi*)(asau, m. 1st s.)(samaḥ, m. 1st s.)(māyā-kāra-)
body.translated_text: 3599. And he does not cling to the substantiality of that conceptual thought; for he knows it as without [a real] object; for he is like a magician (<s>māyākāra</s>) — equanimous [toward his own mental constructs].

body.translated_text: 3600. Just as a certain magician knows [his] mind [to have] a determined object — [that the horses and the like] beginning with horses are objectless — by that [knowledge], he is not deluded.

body.translated_text: 3601. But [the claim] 'this and that' [about the twice-born] and the like — shines [only] when proclaimed to the faithful; this [counter-argument] has not been stated in accordance with the subject at hand.

3602.
(ca*)(prakṛtam, n. 1st s.)(atra*)(hi*)(etat, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(tathā-)(avyāptaḥ, m. 1st s.)(sarva-)(arthaiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(na*)(śaktaḥ, m. 1st s.)(upadeśane, n. 7th s.)(ca*)(tatra*)(mahā-dhiyaḥ, m. 1st pl. [bv. cpd.])(āhuḥ ”ah Perf. 3p pl.)
body.translated_text: 3602. And the subject here is indeed this: [that one who is] not pervaded by all objects is not capable of instruction; and regarding that, the great-minded [scholars] say:

body.text:
3603.
(cet*)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(syāt ”as II C. Opt.)(na*)(śaktiḥ, f. 1st s.)(upadeśane, n. 7th s.)(kim, n. 1st s.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(tadā*)(tataḥ*)(bhavadbhiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(vaktavyam, n. 1st s.)(iti*)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(na*)(āgamaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3603. If he had no capacity for instruction — what would happen then? [You] should say [it would follow that] there would be no scripture (<s>āgama</s>).

body.text:

(api*)(tatra*)(āhuḥ ”ah Perf. 3p pl.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(evam*)(tvayā, 3rd s.)(dṛṣṭaḥ, m. 1st s.)(asau, m. 1st s.)(vadan ”vad I C., m. 1st s.)(kim*)(yadi*)(codyate ”cud Pass.)(idam, n. 1st s.)(aniṣṭam, n. 1st s.)(prasaṅga-sādhanena, n. 3rd s.)
body.translated_text: 3604. Regarding that too, they say: [even] so it would be — was he seen by you speaking [thus]? If this undesired [consequence] is raised through a <s>prasaṅga</s>-proof (reductio ad absurdum),

body.text:

(cet*)(vaktṛtvam, n. 1st s.)(na*)(iṣyeta ”iṣ Pass. Opt.)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(na*)(upagamaḥ, m. 1st s.)(āgama-)(tu*)(āgama-)(praṇīta-)(tat-)(iṣṭau, f. 7th s.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(vaktṛtvam, n. 1st s.)(iṣyatām ”iṣ Pass. Imperative 3p s.)
body.translated_text: 3605. If his speakership were not accepted — there would be no acceptance of the scripture; but [given] the acceptance of the scripture composed by that [being] — let his speakership be accepted.

body.text:

(yadi*)(evam*)(īdṛśaḥ, m. 1st s.)(nyāyaḥ, m. 1st s.)(prasiddhaḥ, m. 1st s.)(nyāya-vādinām, m. 6th pl.)(prasaṅga-sādhane, n. 7th s.)(dharmaḥ, m. 1st s.)(mataḥ, m. 1st s.)(paraiḥ, m. 3rd pl.)(mātrāt, n. 5th s.)(śraddhā-)
body.translated_text: 3606. If such is the reasoning well-known to the logicians — [that] <s>dharma</s> is accepted by others merely out of faith — through the <s>prasaṅga</s>-proof,

body.text:
3607.
(ca*)(prasiddhatāyām, f. 7th s.)(yukti-)(bhavet ”bhū I C. Opt.)(svatantram, n. 1st s.)(sādhanam, n. 1st s.)(ca*)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(āgamaḥ, m. 1st s.)(iṣṭaḥ, m. 1st s.)(pareṇa, m. 3rd s.)(praṇītaḥ, m. 1st s.)(tat-)(īdṛśaḥ, m. 1st s.)
body.translated_text: 3607. And when the logical reasoning is well-established, there would be an independent proof [of the Buddha's speakership]; and that scripture — accepted [and] composed by that [being] — is of such a nature.

body.text:
3608.
(avedhataḥ* [-tas suff.])(sambhāra-)(deśanāḥ, f. 1st pl.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(puṃsaḥ, m. 6th s.)(niḥsaranti ”sṛ I C. 3p pl.)(yathā-kāmam*)(api*)(kuḍya-)(ādibhyaḥ, m. 5th pl.)(cintā-maṇeḥ, m. 5th s.)
body.translated_text: 3608. The teachings of that person issue forth, without [deliberate] composition, from walls and the like — at will — like [the emanations of] a wish-fulfilling gem (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>).

body.text:
3609.
(ataḥ*)(prapattyā, f. 3rd s.)(ādhipatya-)(saḥ, m. 1st s.)(abhidhīyate ”dhā Pass.)(praṇetā, m. 1st s.)(tasya, m. 6th s.)(vaktṛtvam, n. 1st s.)(prasajyate ”sañj Pass.)(na*)(anugatam, n. 1st s.)(vikalpa-)
body.translated_text: 3609. Therefore, by virtue of [his] sovereign mastery, he is called the author; [but] his speakership is not accompanied by conceptual thought — [this] is entailed.

body.translated_text: 3611. And why is there no status as [teachings of] a trustworthy person (<s>āpta</s>) for [teachings] that have issued from walls and the like? When their promulgation is by virtue of that [being's] sovereignty.

body.translated_text: 3612. And how would those [teachings] — which are devoid of incoherent speech, violence, and other contemptible purposes — be [regarded as] authored by playful <s>piśācas</s> (demons) and the like?
